index 000000000..1649a40b6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/persistence.mli
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+(** {1 Tensor checkpoint persistence: save, load, and restore.}
+
+    Checkpoint files use an S-expression header for metadata followed by contiguous
+    binary payloads in native precision format. *)
+
+val save : appending:bool -> Ocannl_tensor.Tensor.tn_set -> string -> unit
+(** [save ~appending t_set path] writes tensor data to a checkpoint file.
+
+    When [~appending:false], creates a fresh checkpoint (overwriting any existing file).
+    When [~appending:true] and the file exists, replaces tensors with matching IDs
+    and keeps non-overlapping entries from the existing file.
+
+    Raises if any tnode in [t_set] has no hosted array (e.g., virtual or local tnodes).
+    Calls [Tnode.do_read] on each tnode to sync device-to-host before saving. *)
+
+val load : ?prefix_namespace:string -> string -> Ocannl_tensor.Tensor.tn_set
+(** [load ?prefix_namespace path] reads tensors from a checkpoint file, creates new
+    tnodes, registers them, and returns the resulting set.
+
+    Raises if any loaded tensor ID clashes with an existing tnode in the registry.
+    After loading, bumps the session ID floor so that subsequently created tensors
+    get IDs strictly above any loaded ID.
+
+    [?prefix_namespace] is reserved for future namespace support (#372). Currently,
+    only [None] or [Some ""] are accepted; any non-empty prefix raises an error. *)
+
+val restore : Ocannl_tensor.Tensor.tn_set -> string -> unit
+(** [restore t_set path] updates existing tensor buffers from a checkpoint file.
+
+    For each tnode in [t_set], finds its data in the file by ID and overwrites
+    the hosted buffer. After restoring, clears [prepare_read] (to prevent stale
+    device-to-host transfers) and calls [do_write] (to mark all devices as stale
+    so the next device access re-transfers from host).
+
+    Raises if:
+    - A tensor in [t_set] is missing from the file
+    - Precision or dimensions don't match between live tensor and file *)

index 00000000..31fcade4

+++ b/test/operations/test_tensor_persistence.ml
@@ -0,0 +1,255 @@
+open Base
+module Tn = Ir.Tnode
+module Nd = Ir.Ndarray
+module Ops = Ir.Ops
+module Tensor = Ocannl_tensor.Tensor
+module Persistence = Ocannl.Persistence
+
+(* Self-checking tensor checkpoint persistence tests. Each case prints a
+   [PASS] <id> <name> or [FAIL] <id> <name> record; the process exits with a
+   non-zero status if any case fails. *)
+
+let failures = ref 0
+
+let report id name ok =
+  if ok then Stdio.printf "[PASS] %d %s\n%!" id name
+  else begin
+    Int.incr failures;
+    Stdio.printf "[FAIL] %d %s\n%!" id name
+  end
+
+let tmp_dir = Stdlib.Filename.get_temp_dir_name ()
+let tmp_file name = Stdlib.Filename.concat tmp_dir ("test_persistence_" ^ name ^ ".ckpt")
+
+let cleanup name =
+  let path = tmp_file name in
+  if Stdlib.Sys.file_exists path then Stdlib.Sys.remove path
+
+(** Create a tnode with given values for testing. *)
+let make_tn ~id ~label prec dims values =
+  let padding = None in
+  let nd = Nd.create_array ~debug:"test" prec ~dims ~padding in
+  Nd.set_flat_values nd values;
+  Tn.create_from_padded ~id ~label ~ndarray:nd ~padding ()
+
+let get_values tn =
+  match Lazy.force tn.Tn.array with
+  | Some nd -> Nd.retrieve_flat_values nd
+  | None -> [||]
+
+let values_match tn expected =
+  let vals = get_values tn in
+  Array.length vals = Array.length expected
+  && Array.for_alli vals ~f:(fun i a -> Float.(abs (a - expected.(i)) < 1e-4))
+
+
+
+let with_error_check f =
+  try
+    f ();
+    false
+  with _ -> true
+
+(* Test 9: Loading with an empty prefix_namespace behaves like a plain load. *)
+let test_empty_prefix () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "w" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 4.; 5. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "emptyprefix" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn1 ]) path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load ~prefix_namespace:"" path in
+  let ok =
+    Set.length loaded = 1
+    && (match Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 0) with
+       | Some tn -> values_match tn [| 4.; 5. |]
+       | None -> false)
+  in
+  cleanup "emptyprefix";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 10: Loading with a non-empty prefix_namespace raises or yields tensors
+   carrying the namespace prefix, without clashing with pre-existing tensors. *)
+let test_prefix_namespace () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "w" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 6.; 7. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "prefix" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn1 ]) path;
+  let ok =
+    try
+      let loaded = Persistence.load ~prefix_namespace:"ns" path in
+      Set.length loaded = 1
+    with _ -> true
+  in
+  cleanup "prefix";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 11: Saving with ~appending:false discards prior checkpoint contents. *)
+let test_fresh_clears () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn_a = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "a" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 1.; 2. |] in
+  let tn_b = make_tn ~id:1 ~label:[ "b" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 3.; 4. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "fresh" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_a; tn_b ]) path;
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_a ]) path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load path in
+  let ok =
+    Set.length loaded = 1
+    && (match Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 0) with
+       | Some tn -> values_match tn [| 1.; 2. |]
+       | None -> false)
+  in
+  cleanup "fresh";
+  ok
+(* Test 1: Round-trip save/load preserves ids, labels and values. *)
+let test_round_trip () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "weights" ] Ops.single [| 2; 3 |] [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4.; 5.; 6. |] in
+  let tn2 = make_tn ~id:1 ~label:[ "bias" ] Ops.double [| 3 |] [| 10.; 20.; 30. |] in
+  let t_set = Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn1; tn2 ] in
+  let path = tmp_file "roundtrip" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false t_set path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load path in
+  let l0 = Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 0) in
+  let l1 = Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 1) in
+  let ok =
+    Set.length loaded = 2
+    && (match l0 with
+       | Some tn ->
+           List.equal String.equal tn.Tn.label [ "weights" ]
+           && values_match tn [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4.; 5.; 6. |]
+       | None -> false)
+    && (match l1 with
+       | Some tn ->
+           List.equal String.equal tn.Tn.label [ "bias" ] && values_match tn [| 10.; 20.; 30. |]
+       | None -> false)
+  in
+  cleanup "roundtrip";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 2: Restore overwrites the hosted buffer with stored values. *)
+let test_restore () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "w" ] Ops.single [| 2; 2 |] [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4. |] in
+  let t_set = Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn1 ] in
+  let path = tmp_file "restore" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false t_set path;
+  let nd = Option.value_exn (Lazy.force tn1.Tn.array) in
+  Nd.set_flat_values nd [| 99.; 99.; 99.; 99. |];
+  Persistence.restore t_set path;
+  let ok = values_match tn1 [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4. |] in
+  cleanup "restore";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 3: Append mode with a disjoint set keeps existing entries. *)
+let test_append_disjoint () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn_a = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "a" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 1.; 2. |] in
+  let tn_b = make_tn ~id:1 ~label:[ "b" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 3.; 4. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "append" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_a ]) path;
+  Persistence.save ~appending:true (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_b ]) path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load path in
+  let ok =
+    Set.length loaded = 2
+    && (match Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 0) with
+       | Some tn -> values_match tn [| 1.; 2. |]
+       | None -> false)
+    && (match Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 1) with
+       | Some tn -> values_match tn [| 3.; 4. |]
+       | None -> false)
+  in
+  cleanup "append";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 4: Append mode replaces overlapping tensors. *)
+let test_append_overwrite () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn_a = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "a" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 1.; 2. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "overwrite" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_a ]) path;
+  let tn_a2 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "a" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 77.; 88. |] in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:true (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_a2 ]) path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load path in
+  let ok =
+    Set.length loaded = 1
+    && (match Set.find loaded ~f:(fun tn -> tn.Tn.id = 0) with
+       | Some tn -> values_match tn [| 77.; 88. |]
+       | None -> false)
+  in
+  cleanup "overwrite";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 5: Saving/restoring an empty set works. *)
+let test_empty () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let empty = Set.empty (module Tn) in
+  let path = tmp_file "empty" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false empty path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let loaded = Persistence.load path in
+  Persistence.restore empty path;
+  let ok = Set.length loaded = 0 in
+  cleanup "empty";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 6: Restore raises when a tensor is missing from the checkpoint. *)
+let test_missing_on_restore () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "present" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 1.; 2. |] in
+  let tn2 = make_tn ~id:1 ~label:[ "absent" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 3.; 4. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "missing" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn1 ]) path;
+  let ok =
+    with_error_check (fun () -> Persistence.restore (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn2 ]) path)
+  in
+  cleanup "missing";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 7: Restore raises on dimension mismatch. *)
+let test_dim_mismatch () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn_save = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "d" ] Ops.single [| 2; 3 |] [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4.; 5.; 6. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "dimfail" in
+  Persistence.save ~appending:false (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_save ]) path;
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn_wrong = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "d" ] Ops.single [| 3; 2 |] [| 1.; 2.; 3.; 4.; 5.; 6. |] in
+  let ok =
+    with_error_check (fun () -> Persistence.restore (Set.of_list (module Tn) [ tn_wrong ]) path)
+  in
+  cleanup "dimfail";
+  ok
+
+(* Test 8: Load raises when a loaded tensor id clashes with the registry. *)
+let test_id_clash () =
+  Tensor.unsafe_reinitialize ();
+  let tn1 = make_tn ~id:0 ~label:[ "x" ] Ops.single [| 2 |] [| 1.; 2. |] in
+  let path = tmp_file "clash" in

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Test-only wrapper for the tensor-persistence benchmark tests.
+#
+# Builds and runs the self-checking persistence test executable and emits a
+# stable, individually parseable "[PASS] <id> <name>" / "[FAIL] <id> <name>"
+# record per assertion. The underlying per-test exit status is preserved: the
+# wrapper exits non-zero if the test target fails to build or reports a failed
+# assertion.
+#
+# Usage: run_persistence_tests.sh [results-file]
+set -u
+
+RESULTS="${1:-/tmp/rebench-test-results.txt}"
+: >"$RESULTS"
+
+# Deterministic, colorless, per-test verbose output.
+export OCANNL_BACKEND="${OCANNL_BACKEND:-sync_cc}"
+export DUNE_NO_COLOR=1
+
+overall=0
+
+exe="test/operations/test_tensor_persistence.exe"
+name="test_tensor_persistence"
+
+if ! dune build "$exe" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  # The requested behavior is not implemented: the test cannot even build.
+  echo "[FAIL] 0 ${name} (build)" | tee -a "$RESULTS"
+  exit 1
+fi
+built="_build/default/$exe"
+run_dir="$(dirname "$built")"
+# Run from the build directory holding the test's ocannl_config so the
+# per-assertion records are cleanly parseable.
+base="$(basename "$exe")"
+out="$(cd "$run_dir" && OCANNL_BACKEND="$OCANNL_BACKEND" "./$base" 2>/dev/null)"
+status=$?
+# Re-emit the test's own per-assertion records.
+printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E '^\[(PASS|FAIL)\] ' | tee -a "$RESULTS"
+if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
+  overall=1
+fi
+# Ensure at least one record was emitted for this target.
+if ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '^\[(PASS|FAIL)\] '; then
+  echo "[FAIL] 0 ${name} (no results)" | tee -a "$RESULTS"
+  overall=1
+fi
+
+echo "---- results ----"
+exit "$overall"

problem_statement:
Implement product between two `AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix`
Implement the method `*(A::AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix, B::AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix)` efficiently. Perhaps just between matrices of the same format, like CSC-CSC, CSR-CSR and COO-COO.

It should also include methods between Transpose or Adjoint, ad done for `*(A:: AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix, B::DenseMatrix)` or `+(A::AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix, B::AbstractDeviceSparseMatrix)`.

### Additional contract requirements

# Sparse-sparse matrix multiplication contract

Sparse-sparse multiplication is supported for pairs of device sparse matrices with
the same concrete storage format: CSC with CSC, CSR with CSR, or COO with COO.
Transpose and adjoint wrappers of those operands are supported in the same pairs.
Mixed storage-format pairs are not part of this interface.

The operands must be on the same backend and have compatible matrix dimensions.
A backend mismatch raises `ArgumentError`; incompatible inner dimensions raise
`DimensionMismatch`. Compatible empty dimensions, including an `m×0` matrix
multiplied by a `0×n` matrix, are supported.

Operand value element types may differ when their multiplication is defined. The
result has the promoted value element type, the ordinary matrix-product values and
shape, and is returned as a device sparse matrix in the operands' concrete storage
format. The result representation is sparse; this contract specifies no portable
timing threshold or intermediate-storage policy.

+"""
+    *(A::DeviceSparseMatrixCOO, B::DeviceSparseMatrixCOO)
+
+Multiply two sparse matrices in COO format. Both matrices must have compatible dimensions
+(number of columns of A equals number of rows of B) and be on the same backend (device).
+
+The multiplication converts to CSC format, performs the multiplication with GPU-compatible
+kernels, and converts back to COO format. This approach is used for all cases including
+transpose/adjoint since COO doesn't have an efficient direct multiplication algorithm.
+
+# Examples
+```jldoctest
+julia> using DeviceSparseArrays, SparseArrays
+
+julia> A = DeviceSparseMatrixCOO(sparse([1, 2], [1, 2], [2.0, 3.0], 2, 2));
+
+julia> B = DeviceSparseMatrixCOO(sparse([1, 2], [1, 2], [4.0, 5.0], 2, 2));
+
+julia> C = A * B;
+
+julia> collect(C)
+2×2 Matrix{Float64}:
+ 8.0   0.0
+ 0.0  15.0
+```
+"""
+function Base.:(*)(A::DeviceSparseMatrixCOO, B::DeviceSparseMatrixCOO)
+    size(A, 2) == size(B, 1) || throw(
+        DimensionMismatch(
+            "second dimension of A, $(size(A,2)), does not match first dimension of B, $(size(B,1))",
+        ),
+    )
+
+    backend_A = get_backend(A)
+    backend_B = get_backend(B)
+    backend_A == backend_B ||
+        throw(ArgumentError("Both matrices must have the same backend"))
+
+    # Convert to CSC, multiply, convert back to COO
+    # This is acceptable as COO doesn't have an efficient direct multiplication algorithm
+    # and CSC provides the sorted structure needed for efficient SpGEMM
+    A_csc = DeviceSparseMatrixCSC(A)
+    B_csc = DeviceSparseMatrixCSC(B)
+    C_csc = A_csc * B_csc
+    return DeviceSparseMatrixCOO(C_csc)
+end
+
+# Multiplication with transpose/adjoint support - all cases use the same approach
+for (wrapa, transa, conja, unwrapa, whereT1) in trans_adj_wrappers(:DeviceSparseMatrixCOO)
+    for (wrapb, transb, conjb, unwrapb, whereT2) in
+        trans_adj_wrappers(:DeviceSparseMatrixCOO)
+        # Skip the case where both are not transposed (already handled above)
+        (transa == false && transb == false) && continue
+
+        TypeA = wrapa(:(T1))
+        TypeB = wrapb(:(T2))
+
+        @eval function Base.:(*)(
+            A::$TypeA,
+            B::$TypeB,
+        ) where {$(whereT1(:T1)),$(whereT2(:T2))}
+            size(A, 2) == size(B, 1) || throw(
+                DimensionMismatch(
+                    "second dimension of A, $(size(A,2)), does not match first dimension of B, $(size(B,1))",
+                ),
+            )
+
+            backend_A = get_backend($(unwrapa(:A)))
+            backend_B = get_backend($(unwrapb(:B)))
+            backend_A == backend_B ||
+                throw(ArgumentError("Both matrices must have the same backend"))
+
+            # Convert to CSC (handles transpose/adjoint), multiply, convert back to COO
+            # Same approach as the base case since COO doesn't have an efficient
+            # direct multiplication algorithm
+            A_csc = DeviceSparseMatrixCSC(A)
+            B_csc = DeviceSparseMatrixCSC(B)
+            C_csc = A_csc * B_csc
+            return DeviceSparseMatrixCOO(C_csc)
+        end
+    end
+end

problem_statement:
in assess tidy district-wide results should use same school_code
`school_code == '000'` and `school_code == ''` (empty string) both code for district-level results.  fix that.

### Additional contract requirements

In the tidy output of the legacy NJ assessment pipeline (NJASK, HSPA, and GEPA), district-level (district-aggregate) rows are identified by a missing school code: their `school_code` value is `NA` (`NA_character_`).

Both raw encodings of district-level rows documented for these files — the empty string `""` and the literal sentinel `"000"` — are normalized to this single missing value in tidy output. Consequently:

- Tidy output contains no `school_code == "000"` values and no blank or whitespace-only `school_code` values.
- `is.na(school_code)` is the single, complete test for "this row is not a school-level row"; all district rows flagged as district rows have `NA` school codes, and no other rows do.
- Every genuine school code (the zero-padded codes `"001"` through `"999"`) is preserved unchanged as a 3-character string through the tidy pipeline; no real school code is collapsed to `NA` or otherwise altered.
- This convention is consistent with the PARCC tidy output, in which district-aggregate rows likewise carry a missing school identifier.

+#' @title canonicalize school_code in tidy legacy assessment output
+#'
+#' @description Collapses the multiple "no school here" encodings emitted
+#' by the raw NJ DOE NJASK/HSPA/GEPA files into a single canonical value
+#' (\code{NA_character_}).
+#'
+#' Issue #26 documents that the raw fixed-width layouts use two different
+#' encodings for district-aggregate rows in the same column:
+#' \itemize{
+#'   \item \code{""} (whitespace-only, after trimming the padded field)
+#'   \item \code{"000"} (a literal three-digit zero sentinel)
+#' }
+#' Both mean "this row is not a school." Without normalization,
+#' downstream filters silently disagree:
+#' \code{filter(school_code == "000")} drops the blank-encoded rows,
+#' \code{filter(is.na(school_code))} drops the "000"-encoded rows, and
+#' neither filter returns the full set of district-aggregate rows.
+#'
+#' After this function runs, \code{is.na(school_code)} is the single,
+#' correct test for "not a school." Real school codes
+#' (\code{"001"}..\code{"999"} per layout_njask) are preserved unchanged.
+#'
+#' The function is idempotent: applying it twice yields the same result.
+#'
+#' @param df a tidied NJASK/HSPA/GEPA data frame (must have a
+#'   \code{school_code} column).
+#' @return \code{df} with \code{school_code} normalized.
+#' @keywords internal
+canonicalize_legacy_assess_school_code <- function(df) {
+  if (!"school_code" %in% names(df)) return(df)
+
+  sc <- as.character(df$school_code)
+  sc_trim <- trimws(sc)
+
+  # Treat both whitespace-only and "000" as district-aggregate sentinels.
+  district_aggregate <- !is.na(sc) & (sc_trim == "" | sc_trim == "000")
+  sc[district_aggregate] <- NA_character_
+
+  df$school_code <- sc
+  df
+}
+

+# is.na(school_code) is the single correct test for "not a school."

+# All tests below exercise the PUBLIC tidy_nj_assess() pipeline on a
+# process_nj_assess()-shaped fixture whose raw School_Code column contains

+    ),

problem_statement:
Spotless config is using heavily discouraged wildcards
https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/issues/111#issuecomment-652081184

Maintainer of spotless says

> Just a bump that `src/*/java/**/*.java` will perform far better than `**/*.java`. We heavily discourage `**/blah wildcards`.

Meanwhile NIA uses the heavily discouraged wildcards 

such as
```
            kotlin {
                target("**/*.kt")
                targetExclude("**/build/**/*.kt")
                ktlint(ktlintVersion).editorConfigOverride(
                    mapOf(
                        "android" to "true",
                    ),
                )
                licenseHeaderFile(rootProject.file("spotless/copyright.kt"))
            }
```

### Additional contract requirements

Spotless target and target-exclusion patterns that select Kotlin (`.kt`), Kotlin-script
(`.kts`), or XML (`.xml`) files must not start with the `**/` path segment. Use bounded
patterns rooted at known project directories instead.

+package com.google.samples.apps.nowinandroid
+
+import com.diffplug.gradle.spotless.SpotlessExtension
+import org.gradle.api.Project
+import org.gradle.kotlin.dsl.apply
+import org.gradle.kotlin.dsl.configure
+
+internal fun Project.configureSpotlessForAndroid() {
+    configureSpotlessCommon()
+    extensions.configure<SpotlessExtension> {
+        format("xml") {
+            target("src/**/*.xml")
+            // Look for the first XML tag that isn't a comment (<!--) or the xml declaration (<?xml)
+            licenseHeaderFile(rootDir.resolve("spotless/copyright.xml"), "(<[^!?])")
+            endWithNewline()
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+internal fun Project.configureSpotlessForJvm() {
+    configureSpotlessCommon()
+}
+
+internal fun Project.configureSpotlessForRootProject() {
+    apply(plugin = "com.diffplug.spotless")
+    extensions.configure<SpotlessExtension> {
+        kotlin {
+            target("build-logic/convention/src/**/*.kt")
+            ktlint(libs.findVersion("ktlint").get().requiredVersion).editorConfigOverride(
+                mapOf("android" to "true"),
+            )
+            licenseHeaderFile(rootDir.resolve("spotless/copyright.kt"))
+            endWithNewline()
+        }
+        format("kts") {
+            target("*.kts")
+            target("build-logic/*.kts")
+            target("build-logic/convention/*.kts")
+            // Look for the first line that doesn't have a block comment (assumed to be the license)
+            licenseHeaderFile(rootDir.resolve("spotless/copyright.kts"), "(^(?![\\/ ]\\*).*$)")
+            endWithNewline()
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun Project.configureSpotlessCommon() {
+    apply(plugin = "com.diffplug.spotless")
+    extensions.configure<SpotlessExtension> {
+        kotlin {
+            target("src/**/*.kt")
+            ktlint(libs.findVersion("ktlint").get().requiredVersion).editorConfigOverride(
+                mapOf("android" to "true"),
+            )
+            licenseHeaderFile(rootDir.resolve("spotless/copyright.kt"))
+            endWithNewline()
+        }
+        format("kts") {
+            target("*.kts")
+            // Look for the first line that doesn't have a block comment (assumed to be the license)
+            licenseHeaderFile(rootDir.resolve("spotless/copyright.kts"), "(^(?![\\/ ]\\*).*$)")
+            endWithNewline()
+        }
+    }
+}

+package com.google.samples.apps.nowinandroid
+
+import java.io.File
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+import java.nio.file.Files
+import java.util.Base64
+import kotlin.test.Test
+import kotlin.test.assertEquals
+import kotlin.test.assertTrue
+
+/** Checks resolved Spotless patterns without depending on custom format names. */
+class SpotlessWildcardTest {
+    private val rootDir = File(System.getProperty("user.dir")).parentFile.parentFile
+
+    @Test
+    fun spotlessTargetsDoNotUseDiscouragedLeadingWildcards() {
+        val offenders =
+            resolvedFormats()
+                .filter(::formatsRelevantSourceFiles)
+                .flatMap { format ->
+                    (format.includes + format.excludes)
+                        .filter { it.startsWith("**/") }
+                        .map { "${format.projectPath}:${format.name}(\"$it\")" }
+                }
+
+        assertTrue(
+            offenders.isEmpty(),
+            "Active Spotless patterns for Kotlin, Kotlin-script, or XML files must not begin with \"**/\":\n" +
+                offenders.joinToString("\n"),
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun formatsAreClassifiedByResolvedFilesRatherThanTheirNames() {
+        val renamedFormat = Format(
+            projectPath = ":sample",
+            name = "companySources",
+            includes = listOf("src/**/*.kt"),
+            excludes = emptyList(),
+            files = setOf(File("src/main/kotlin/Sample.kt")),
+        )
+        val unrelatedFormat = Format(
+            projectPath = ":sample",
+            name = "documentation",
+            includes = listOf("docs/**/*.md"),
+            excludes = emptyList(),
+            files = setOf(File("docs/README.md")),
+        )
+
+        assertTrue(formatsRelevantSourceFiles(renamedFormat))
+        assertTrue(!formatsRelevantSourceFiles(unrelatedFormat))
+    }
+
+    private fun formatsRelevantSourceFiles(format: Format): Boolean =
+        format.files.any { it.extension in SourceExtensions } ||
+            (format.includes + format.excludes).any { pattern ->
+                SourceExtensions.any { extension -> pattern.endsWith(".$extension") }
+            }
+
+    private fun resolvedFormats(): List<Format> {
+        val report = Files.createTempFile("spotless-contract", ".txt").toFile()
+        val probe = Files.createTempFile("spotless-contract", ".init.gradle.kts").toFile()
+        try {
+            probe.writeText(probeScript(report))
+            val command = mutableListOf(
+                rootDir.resolve("gradlew").absolutePath,
+                "spotlessCheck",
+                "--dry-run",
+            )
+            val legacyInitScript = rootDir.resolve("gradle/init.gradle.kts")
+            if (legacyInitScript.isFile) {
+                command += listOf("--init-script", legacyInitScript.absolutePath)
+            }
+            command += listOf(
+                "--init-script",
+                probe.absolutePath,
+                "--no-configuration-cache",
+                "--console=plain",
+            )
+            val process = ProcessBuilder(command).directory(rootDir).redirectErrorStream(true).start()
+            val output = process.inputStream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
+            assertEquals(0, process.waitFor(), "Unable to resolve active Spotless formats:\n$output")
+            return report.readLines().filter { it.isNotBlank() }.map(::parseFormat)
+        } finally {
+            report.delete()
+            probe.delete()
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun parseFormat(line: String): Format {
+        val parts = line.split('|')
+        require(parts.size == 6 && parts.first() == "SPOTLESS_CONTRACT") {
+            "Invalid Spotless probe output: $line"
+        }
+        return Format(
+            projectPath = decode(parts[1]),
+            name = decode(parts[2]),
+            includes = decodeList(parts[3]),
+            excludes = decodeList(parts[4]),
+            files = decodeList(parts[5]).map(::File).toSet(),
+        )
+    }
+
+    private fun decode(value: String): String =
+        String(Base64.getDecoder().decode(value), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+
+    private fun decodeList(value: String): List<String> =
+        decode(value).split('\u0000').filter(String::isNotEmpty)
+
+    private fun probeScript(report: File): String =
+        """
+        import java.io.File
+        import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+        import java.util.Base64
+
+        fun fields(type: Class<*>): Sequence<java.lang.reflect.Field> = sequence {
+            yieldAll(type.declaredFields.asSequence())
+            type.superclass?.let { yieldAll(fields(it)) }
+        }
+
+        fun fieldValue(instance: Any, name: String): Any? =
+            fields(instance.javaClass).firstOrNull { it.name == name }?.let {
+                it.trySetAccessible()
+                it.get(instance)
+            }
+
+        fun encode(value: String): String =
+            Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(value.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
+
+        fun fileTreePatterns(value: Any?, name: String): List<String> {
+            val patterns =
+                value?.javaClass?.methods?.firstOrNull { it.name == name && it.parameterCount == 0 }
+                    ?.invoke(value) as? Iterable<*> ?: return emptyList()
+            return patterns.map { it.toString() }
+        }
+
+        gradle.projectsEvaluated {
+            allprojects {
+                val project = this
+                gradle.taskGraph.whenReady {
+                    val extension = project.extensions.findByName("spotless") ?: return@whenReady
+                    val formats = fieldValue(extension, "formats") as? Map<*, *> ?: return@whenReady
+                    formats.forEach { (formatName, format) ->
+                        if (format == null) return@forEach
+                        val target = fieldValue(format, "target") ?: return@forEach
+                        val files = (target as? org.gradle.api.file.FileCollection)?.files.orEmpty()
+                        val targetExclude = fieldValue(format, "targetExclude")
+                        val record = listOf(
+                            "SPOTLESS_CONTRACT",
+                            encode(project.path),
+                            encode(formatName.toString()),
+                            encode(fileTreePatterns(target, "getIncludes").joinToString("\u0000")),
+                            encode(
+                                (
+                                    fileTreePatterns(target, "getExcludes") +
+                                        fileTreePatterns(targetExclude, "getIncludes")
+                                ).joinToString("\u0000"),
+                            ),
+                            encode(files.map(File::getCanonicalPath).joinToString("\u0000")),
+                        ).joinToString("|")
+                        File("${report.absolutePath.replace("\\", "\\\\")}").appendText(record + "\n")
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        """.trimIndent()
+
+    private data class Format(
+        val projectPath: String,
+        val name: String,
+        val includes: List<String>,
+        val excludes: List<String>,
+        val files: Set<File>,
+    )
+
+    private companion object {
+        val SourceExtensions = setOf("kt", "kts", "xml")
+    }
+}

## Project identity requirements

The package/project name must be changed from `acx` to `casbin` throughout the project. In particular, the following identities must hold:

- The publishable package metadata must name the package `casbin` (this is the name used when publishing to Hex).

contract_addendum:
## Project identity requirements

The package/project name must be changed from `acx` to `casbin` throughout the project. In particular, the following identities must hold:

- The Mix build must produce the OTP application named `:casbin`.
- The publishable package metadata must name the package `casbin` (this is the name used when publishing to Hex).
- The OTP application must be configured to start with the root `Casbin` application module.
- The root module of the library must be `Casbin`, and all public modules must live under the `Casbin` namespace (for example `Casbin.Enforcer`).
- The old `Acx` namespace is retired: it is no longer part of the public API contract, and backwards-compatible `Acx` aliases, shims, or duplicate modules are not required or expected.

+defmodule Casbin.ProjectIdentityTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case
+
+  test "the Mix project build is the :casbin application" do
+    assert Mix.Project.config()[:app] == :casbin
+  end
+
+  test "the package metadata publishes the project as casbin" do
+    assert get_in(Mix.Project.config(), [:package, :name]) == "casbin"
+  end
+
+  test "the :casbin OTP application is wired to the Casbin application module" do
+    assert Application.spec(:casbin, :mod) == {Casbin, []}
+  end
+
+  test "the Casbin module implements the OTP application behaviour" do
+    Code.ensure_loaded!(Casbin)
+    assert function_exported?(Casbin, :start, 2)
+  end
+
+  test "the Casbin module is defined" do
+    assert Code.ensure_loaded?(Casbin)
+  end
+
+  test "the root Casbin module is a public API module" do
+    assert Code.ensure_loaded?(Casbin.Enforcer)
+  end
+
+  test "the retired Acx root namespace is not defined" do
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Enforcer)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.EnforcerServer)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.EnforcerSupervisor)
+  end
+
+  test "the retired Acx model namespace is not defined" do
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.Config)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.Matcher)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.Policy)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.PolicyDefinition)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.PolicyEffect)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.Request)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Model.RequestDefinition)
+  end
+
+  test "the retired Acx persist namespace is not defined" do
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Persist.EctoAdapter)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Persist.PersistAdapter)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Persist.ReadonlyFileAdapter)
+  end
+
+  test "the retired Acx internal namespace is not defined" do
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.Digraph)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.Helpers)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.Operator)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.Parser)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.PartialRange)
+    refute Code.ensure_loaded?(Acx.Internal.RoleGroup)
+  end
+
+  test "the published library source layout has no retired acx paths" do
+    assert Path.wildcard("lib/acx*") == []
+  end
+
+  test "the README does not direct consumers to the retired package or namespace" do
+    readme = File.read!("README.md")
+
+    refute readme =~ ~r/\bAcx\b/
+    refute readme =~ ~r/\bacx\b/
+  end
+end

problem_statement:
AlsoTo should support configurable downstream failure propagation
### Motivation

`alsoTo` uses `Broadcast[Out](2, eagerCancel = true)` internally. When the side sink fails or cancels, the entire stream is terminated. Users cannot isolate the side sink â for example, a fire-and-forget logging sink should not kill the main business stream when the logging destination is temporarily unavailable.

### Current behavior

`Flow.scala:4014-4020`:
```scala
protected def alsoToGraph[M](that: Graph[SinkShape[Out], M]): Graph[FlowShape[Out @uncheckedVariance, Out], M] =
  GraphDSL.createGraph(that) { implicit b => r =>
    import GraphDSL.Implicits._
    val bcast = b.add(Broadcast[Out](2, eagerCancel = true))
    bcast.out(1) ~> r
    FlowShape(bcast.in, bcast.out(0))
  }
```

With `eagerCancel = true`, any cancellation from the side sink immediately cancels the entire stream.

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

`alsoTo` gains a configurable cancellation-propagation variant in both the Scala and Java DSLs. In addition to the pre-existing single-argument `alsoTo(that)`, there is a two-argument overload `alsoTo(that, propagateCancellation)` where `that` is the attached side sink graph and `propagateCancellation` is a Boolean.

- When `propagateCancellation` is `false`, cancellation or failure of the attached sink does not terminate the main stream; elements continue to flow to the main downstream only. When `propagateCancellation` is `true`, or when the single-argument form is used, the behavior is identical to the classic `alsoTo`: cancellation or failure of the attached sink terminates the main stream.
- The attached sink still backpressures the main stream while it has no demand. Failure of the upstream terminates the main stream regardless of the setting.

In the Scala DSL, this two-argument overload is available on `Flow`, `Source`, `SubFlow`, and `SubSource` (and on any `FlowOps`-supporting type), returning the same self type. A materialized-value variant `alsoToMat(that, propagateCancellation)(matF)` is available on operations that support materialized values, combining this operator's materialized value with the attached sink's materialized value using the supplied combiner function.

The Java DSL exposes matching two-argument `alsoTo` overloads on `Flow`, `Source`, `SubFlow`, and `SubSource`, and three-argument materialized-value `alsoToMat` overloads (taking `that`, `propagateCancellation`, and a combiner function) on `Flow` and `Source`.

`Broadcast` gains a per-output cancellation configuration. A new Scala factory `Broadcast(outputPorts: Int, eagerCancel: Boolean, nonEagerCancelOutputs: Set[Int])` creates a broadcast where outputs whose port indices appear in `nonEagerCancelOutputs` are removed from the broadcast on cancellation without cancelling upstream, while cancellation of the remaining outputs preserves the broadcast's normal cancellation semantics. The configured set of such output indices is observable via the `Broadcast.nonEagerCancelOutputs: Set[Int]` accessor; it is empty for the pre-existing factories. The Java DSL exposes a matching factory `Broadcast.create(outputCount, eagerCancel, nonEagerCancelOutputs)` accepting a `java.util.Set[java.lang.Integer]` of output indices.

The three-argument Scala factory and the matching Java factory must reject invalid configurations: when `eagerCancel` is `false`, `nonEagerCancelOutputs` must be empty, and every configured index must be a valid output index between `0` and `outputPorts - 1`. Construction with an invalid configuration must fail.

+@nowarn("cat=unused")
+class FlowAlsoToSpec extends StreamSpec("""
+    pekko.stream.materializer.initial-input-buffer-size = 2
+  """) {
+
+  "alsoTo with configurable cancellation propagation" must {
+
+    "expose a two-argument alsoTo overload accepting propagateCancellation" in {
+      val sink: Graph[SinkShape[Int], NotUsed] = Sink.ignore.mapMaterializedValue(_ => NotUsed)
+
+      // The two-argument overload must exist with the documented signature on
+      // every declared Scala DSL receiver type.
+      def flowCheck(flow: Flow[Int, Int, NotUsed]): Flow[Int, Int, NotUsed] =
+        flow.alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)
+
+      def sourceCheck(source: Source[Int, NotUsed]): Source[Int, NotUsed] =
+        source.alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)
+
+      def subFlowCheck[F[+_], C](subFlow: SubFlow[Int, NotUsed, F, C]): SubFlow[Int, NotUsed, F, C] =
+        subFlow.alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)
+
+      def subSourceCheck(subSource: SubFlow[Int, NotUsed, Source[Int, NotUsed]#Repr, ?]): Any =
+        subSource.alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)
+
+      val results: Seq[Any] = List(
+        flowCheck(Flow[Int].alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)),
+        sourceCheck(Source.single(1).alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)),
+        subFlowCheck(Flow[Int].groupBy(2, _ % 2).alsoTo(sink, propagateCancellation = false)),
+        subSourceCheck(Source.single(1).groupBy(2, _ % 2)))
+
+      results should have size 4
+    }
+
+    "not cancel the main stream when the side sink cancels with propagateCancellation=false" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (sideProbe, sideSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      src.alsoTo(sideSink, propagateCancellation = false).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(3)
+      sideProbe.request(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(2)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(2)
+
+      // Cancelling the best-effort side sink must not kill the main stream.
+      sideProbe.cancel()
+
+      pub.sendNext(3)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(3)
+
+      pub.sendComplete()
+      mainProbe.expectComplete()
+    }
+
+    "still propagate side sink cancellation when propagateCancellation=true" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (sideProbe, sideSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      // The pre-existing single-argument alsoTo keeps the default (eager)
+      // cancellation propagation behavior.
+      src.alsoTo(sideSink).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(2)
+      sideProbe.request(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      sideProbe.cancel()
+      pub.expectCancellation()
+    }
+
+    "propagate side sink cancellation through the new overload when propagateCancellation=true" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (sideProbe, sideSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      // Explicitly opting in to cancellation propagation through the
+      // two-argument overload must behave like the classic alsoTo.
+      src.alsoTo(sideSink, propagateCancellation = true).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(3)
+      sideProbe.request(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(2)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(2)
+
+      sideProbe.cancel()
+      pub.expectCancellation()
+    }
+
+    "continue the main stream when the side sink fails with propagateCancellation=false" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      val failingSideSink = Flow[Int].map { elem =>
+        if (elem == 1) throw new RuntimeException("side sink failure")
+        elem
+      }.to(Sink.ignore)
+
+      src.alsoTo(failingSideSink, propagateCancellation = false).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(3)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(3)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(3)
+

+
+      val failingSideSink = Flow[Int].map { elem =>

+      src.alsoTo(failingSideSink, propagateCancellation = true).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(3)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      // Side-sink failure must tear down the whole stream when propagation is enabled.
+      mainProbe.expectError()
+    }
+
+    "backpressure on the main stream while the side sink backpressures with propagateCancellation=false" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (sideProbe, sideSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      src.alsoTo(sideSink, propagateCancellation = false).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(2)
+
+      // The side sink signals no demand, so no element may reach the main
+      // downstream even though the main downstream requested.
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNoMessage()
+
+      sideProbe.request(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      // Once the side sink is gone, the main stream flows freely.
+      sideProbe.cancel()
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(2)
+
+      pub.sendComplete()
+      mainProbe.expectComplete()
+    }
+
+    "fail the main stream when upstream fails with propagateCancellation=false" in {
+      val (mainProbe, mainSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (sideProbe, sideSink) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      src.alsoTo(sideSink, propagateCancellation = false).runWith(mainSink)
+
+      mainProbe.request(2)
+      sideProbe.request(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      mainProbe.expectNext(1)
+      sideProbe.expectNext(1)
+
+      val failure = new RuntimeException("upstream failure")
+      pub.sendError(failure)
+      mainProbe.expectError() shouldBe failure
+    }
+  }
+
+  "alsoToMat with configurable cancellation propagation" must {
+
+    "expose and combine materialized values through the propagateCancellation variant" in {
+      // Distinct observable materialized values for the upstream part and for
+      // the attached side sink, so that any implementation that forwards one
+      // of them unchanged, or that ignores the supplied combiner, is detected.
+      val upstreamMat = "upstream-result"
+      val sideMat = "side-result"
+
+      val sideSink: Graph[SinkShape[Int], String] = Sink.ignore.mapMaterializedValue(_ => sideMat)
+
+      // The propagateCancellation variant of alsoToMat must exist with the
+      // documented signature on Flow and Source and must combine the
+      // materialized values of the operator and of the attached side sink
+      // with the supplied combiner function.
+      val withFlowMat: Flow[Int, Int, String] =
+        Flow[Int]
+          .mapMaterializedValue(_ => upstreamMat)
+          .alsoToMat(sideSink, propagateCancellation = false)(_ + "+" + _)
+
+      val withSourceMat: Source[Int, String] =
+        Source
+          .single(1)
+          .mapMaterializedValue(_ => upstreamMat)
+          .alsoToMat(sideSink, propagateCancellation = false)(_ + "+" + _)
+
+      val flowMat: String =
+        Source
+          .single(1)
+          .viaMat(withFlowMat)(Keep.right)
+          .toMat(Sink.ignore)(Keep.left)
+          .run()
+      flowMat shouldBe "upstream-result+side-result"
+
+      val sourceMat: String = withSourceMat.to(Sink.ignore).run()
+      sourceMat shouldBe "upstream-result+side-result"
+    }
+  }
+
+  "Broadcast with non-eager cancellation outputs" must {
+
+    "accept a configured set of non-eager cancellation outputs" in {
+      // Both the pre-existing factories and the factory accepting a set of
+      // output indices whose cancellation must not cancel upstream must exist.
+      val defaultPorts: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed] = Broadcast[Int](2)
+      val defaultEager: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed] =
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true)
+      val configured: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed] =
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(1))
+
+      List[Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed]](defaultPorts, defaultEager, configured) should have size 3
+    }
+
+    "expose the configured non-eager cancellation outputs" in {
+      // The set of output indices whose cancellation must not cancel upstream
+      // given at construction must be observable through the accessor.
+      val defaultOutputs: Broadcast[Int] = Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true)
+      defaultOutputs.nonEagerCancelOutputs shouldBe empty
+
+      val configuredBroadcast: Broadcast[Int] =
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(1))
+      configuredBroadcast.nonEagerCancelOutputs shouldBe immutable.Set(1)
+    }
+
+    "not cancel upstream when a non-eager cancellation output cancels" in {
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeA, sinkA) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeB, sinkB) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      val bcastGraph: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed] =
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(1))
+
+      RunnableGraph
+        .fromGraph(GraphDSL.createGraph(bcastGraph, sinkA, sinkB)((_, _, _)) { implicit b => (bcast, a, bsink) =>
+          import GraphDSL.Implicits._
+          src ~> bcast.in
+          bcast.out(0) ~> a
+          bcast.out(1) ~> bsink
+          ClosedShape
+        })
+        .run()
+
+      probeA.request(3)
+      probeB.request(2)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      probeA.expectNext(1)
+      probeB.expectNext(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      probeA.expectNext(2)
+      probeB.expectNext(2)
+
+      // Output 1 is declared non-eager: its cancellation must leave the rest
+      // of the broadcast running.
+      probeB.cancel()
+
+      pub.sendNext(3)
+      probeA.expectNext(3)
+
+      pub.sendComplete()
+      probeA.expectComplete()
+    }
+
+    "still cancel upstream when an eager cancellation output cancels" in {
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeA, sinkA) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeB, sinkB) = TestSink[Int]().preMaterialize()
+
+      val bcastGraph: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[Int, Int], NotUsed] =
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(1))
+
+      RunnableGraph
+        .fromGraph(GraphDSL.createGraph(bcastGraph, sinkA, sinkB)((_, _, _)) { implicit b => (bcast, a, bsink) =>
+          import GraphDSL.Implicits._
+          src ~> bcast.in
+          bcast.out(0) ~> a
+          bcast.out(1) ~> bsink
+          ClosedShape
+        })
+        .run()
+
+      probeA.request(1)
+      probeB.request(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      probeA.expectNext(1)
+      probeB.expectNext(1)
+
+      // Output 0 was not declared non-eager: its cancellation must retain the
+      // classic eager behaviour and cancel upstream.
+      probeA.cancel()
+      pub.expectCancellation()
+    }
+
+    "honour non-eager cancellation outputs configured through the Java factory" in {
+      val (pub, src) = TestSource[java.lang.Integer]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeA, sinkA) = TestSink[java.lang.Integer]().preMaterialize()
+      val (probeB, sinkB) = TestSink[java.lang.Integer]().preMaterialize()
+
+      // A broadcast created through the Java factory with a configured set of
+      // non-eager cancellation outputs must behave the same as one created
+      // through the Scala factory: the configured set must not be ignored.
+      val bcastGraph: Graph[UniformFanOutShape[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer], NotUsed] =
+        javadsl.Broadcast.create[java.lang.Integer](2, true, javaSet(1))
+
+      RunnableGraph
+        .fromGraph(GraphDSL.createGraph(bcastGraph, sinkA, sinkB)((_, _, _)) { implicit b => (bcast, a, bsink) =>
+          import GraphDSL.Implicits._
+          src ~> bcast.in
+          bcast.out(0) ~> a
+          bcast.out(1) ~> bsink
+          ClosedShape
+        })
+        .run()
+
+      probeA.request(2)
+      probeB.request(1)
+
+      pub.sendNext(1)
+      probeA.expectNext(1)
+      probeB.expectNext(1)
+
+      // Output 1 was declared non-eager through the Java factory: its
+      // cancellation must leave the remaining output and upstream running.
+      probeB.cancel()
+
+      pub.sendNext(2)
+      probeA.expectNext(2)
+
+      pub.sendComplete()
+      probeA.expectComplete()
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs with a negative output index" in {
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(0, -1))
+      }
+
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(-1))
+      }
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs with a negative output index through the Java factory" in {
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        javadsl.Broadcast.create[java.lang.Integer](2, true, javaSet(0, -1))
+      }
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs when eagerCancel is false" in {
+      // A nonempty set of non-eager cancellation outputs is only meaningful
+      // when the broadcast otherwise cancels eagerly.
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = false, immutable.Set(1))
+      }
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs that are not valid output indices" in {
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        Broadcast[Int](2, eagerCancel = true, immutable.Set(0, 2))
+      }
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs when eagerCancel is false through the Java factory" in {
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        javadsl.Broadcast.create[java.lang.Integer](2, false, javaSet(1))
+      }
+    }
+
+    "reject non-eager cancellation outputs that are not valid output indices through the Java factory" in {
+      a[RuntimeException] shouldBe thrownBy {
+        javadsl.Broadcast.create[java.lang.Integer](2, true, javaSet(0, 2))
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  "Java DSL API compatibility wrappers" must {
+
+    "compile the matching javadsl signatures" in {
+      // These wrappers call the Java DSL variants of the new APIs; their
+      // bodies only compile when the documented overloads exist. The
+      // behavioral coverage for cancellation propagation lives in the
+      // corresponding Scala DSL cases above.
+      new JavaDslCompatibility().references() should have size 7
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def javaSet(indices: Int*): java.util.Set[java.lang.Integer] = {
+    val set = new java.util.HashSet[java.lang.Integer]()
+    indices.foreach(index => set.add(java.lang.Integer.valueOf(index)))
+    set
+  }
+}
+
+final class JavaDslCompatibility {
+  def flowTo(flow: javadsl.Flow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.Flow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    flow.alsoTo(javadslSink, false)
+
+  def sourceTo(source: javadsl.Source[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.Source[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    source.alsoTo(javadslSink, false)
+
+  def subFlowTo(subFlow: javadsl.SubFlow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.SubFlow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    subFlow.alsoTo(javadslSink, false)
+
+  def subSourceTo(subSource: javadsl.SubSource[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.SubSource[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    subSource.alsoTo(javadslSink, false)
+
+  def flowToMat(flow: javadsl.Flow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.Flow[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    flow.alsoToMat(javadslSink, false, keepLeft)
+
+  def sourceToMat(source: javadsl.Source[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed])
+      : javadsl.Source[java.lang.Integer, NotUsed] =
+    source.alsoToMat(javadslSink, false, keepLeft)
+
+  def fanOut(indices: java.util.Set[java.lang.Integer])
+      : Graph[UniformFanOutShape[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer], NotUsed] =
+    javadsl.Broadcast.create[java.lang.Integer](2, true, indices)
+
+  def javadslSink: Graph[SinkShape[java.lang.Integer], NotUsed] =
+    javadsl.Sink.ignore().asScala.mapMaterializedValue(_ => NotUsed)
+
+  def keepLeft: pekko.japi.function.Function2[NotUsed, NotUsed, NotUsed] =
+    new pekko.japi.function.Function2[NotUsed, NotUsed, NotUsed] {
+      override def apply(left: NotUsed, right: NotUsed): NotUsed = left
+    }
+
+  def references(): Seq[Any] = {
+    val nonEagerIndices = new java.util.HashSet[java.lang.Integer]()
+    nonEagerIndices.add(java.lang.Integer.valueOf(1))
+
+    val keyed = new pekko.japi.function.Function[java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Integer] {
+      override def apply(element: java.lang.Integer): java.lang.Integer = element
+    }
+
+    Seq[Any](
+      flowTo(javadsl.Flow.of(classOf[java.lang.Integer])),
+      sourceTo(javadsl.Source.single(java.lang.Integer.valueOf(1))),
+      subFlowTo(javadsl.Flow.of(classOf[java.lang.Integer]).groupBy(2, keyed)),
+      subSourceTo(javadsl.Source.single(java.lang.Integer.valueOf(1)).groupBy(2, keyed)),
+      flowToMat(javadsl.Flow.of(classOf[java.lang.Integer])),
+      sourceToMat(javadsl.Source.single(java.lang.Integer.valueOf(1))),
+      fanOut(nonEagerIndices))
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
[build] Update to kotlin 2.x and openai-kotlin 4.x

### Additional contract requirements

The project must build and its offline test suites must pass with Kotlin 2.x and openai-kotlin 4.x. The root Maven build configuration must configure a 2.x Kotlin version, and the OpenAI client module must resolve a compatible 2.x Kotlin version for compilation and a 4.x OpenAI client-library version. These versions may be declared directly or through build properties; the contract does not require particular property names.

As part of this upgrade, the Gemini model catalogs bundled with each Gemini module must be refreshed:

- `gemini-embedding-001` must be included in supported embedding-model listings and overall model-id listings.
- `text-embedding-004` must no longer be listed as a supported embedding model.
- Current model ids such as `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` must remain available.
- Chat, multimodal, and vision-language listings must remain non-empty and consistent.

All evaluated checks are offline and deterministic; network-backed checks are excluded from the evaluation scope.

problem_statement:
Adding Error to log functions
There was a slightly similar issue ([Simplify logging Error types #267](https://github.com/apple/swift-log/issues/267)) but I would like to give this another twist.

Basically all advanced logging systems accept a textual message and allow to add additional values to better describe the log event.
And also many system allow to explicitly log an Error, not just as part of the message or metadata. Examples: Sentry, Datadog
These service do handle explicit errors in special ways like automated grouping, warning thresholds, incident management...
It's more complex to train these systems to analyze/filter/map the metadata of log events and perform the same routines as with explicit errors.

So I would like to propose to [HIDDEN] that then can be send to log services.
Manual extraction of key values from an error, in it's simplest form `error.localizedDescription` or more complex, is not sufficient to leverage the potential of log services.

### Given
```swift
let error: Error? = ...
let logger = Logger(label: "com.example")
```

### Expected behavior
```swift
logger.error("message", error)
```
and a [HIDDEN]
```swift
func log(
        level: Logging.Logger.Level,
        message: Logging.Logger.Message,
        error: Error?, // <<<<<<<<<< new line here
        metadata: Logging.Logger.Metadata?,
        source: String,
        file: String,
        function: String,
        line: UInt
    )
```

### Actual behavior
The given log functions `.log(...)` or explicit like `.error(...)` on a logger instance only accept a message and metadata where metadata is a String, or array/dictionary hierarchy where terminal elements are again String.

### SwiftLog version/commit hash
v1.5.4

### Additional contract requirements

Error-bearing logging is part of the public `Logger` API. Loggers accept an `Error?` value
and forward it unchanged to the installed log handler together with the emitted log event.

The dynamic call surface includes `log(level:_:error:metadata:source:file:function:line:)`:
`level` is labeled, the message is unlabeled, and `error` is labeled, accepts an `Error?`,
and defaults to the absence of an error. Its metadata argument defaults to `nil`, its source
argument defaults to `nil`, and its file, function, and line arguments default to the caller
location.

Each level convenience method—`trace`, `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`, and
`critical`—must provide an error-bearing overload with the spelling
`level(_:error:metadata:source:file:function:line:)`. The message is the first, unlabeled
argument; `error` is the second, labeled argument, accepts an `Error?`, and defaults to the
absence of an error; metadata, source, file, function, and line have the same labels and
caller-location defaults as the dynamic call. The pre-existing error-free dynamic and level
convenience calls, including their source-bearing forms, remain source-compatible.

When a log call is filtered out, its lazy message, error, and metadata arguments must not be
evaluated.

The built-in in-memory log handler records each received event as an entry, and on an
error-bearing event the entry exposes the associated error: it preserves explicitly provided
nonempty metadata on that entry, and it retains the identical error instance that was passed
to the log call.

The error-bearing APIs preserve the logger's existing sendability guarantees.

The given log functions `.log(...)` or explicit like `.error(...)` on a logger instance only accept a message and metadata where metadata is a String, or array/dictionary hierarchy where terminal elements are again String.

contract_addendum:
Error-bearing logging is part of the public `Logger` API. Loggers accept an `Error?` value
and forward it unchanged to the installed log handler together with the emitted log event.

The dynamic call surface includes `log(level:_:error:metadata:source:file:function:line:)`:
`level` is labeled, the message is unlabeled, and `error` is labeled, accepts an `Error?`,
and defaults to the absence of an error. Its metadata argument defaults to `nil`, its source
argument defaults to `nil`, and its file, function, and line arguments default to the caller
location.

Each level convenience method—`trace`, `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`, and
`critical`—must provide an error-bearing overload with the spelling
`level(_:error:metadata:source:file:function:line:)`. The message is the first, unlabeled
argument; `error` is the second, labeled argument, accepts an `Error?`, and defaults to the
absence of an error; metadata, source, file, function, and line have the same labels and
caller-location defaults as the dynamic call. The pre-existing error-free dynamic and level
convenience calls, including their source-bearing forms, remain source-compatible.

When a log call is filtered out, its lazy message, error, and metadata arguments must not be
evaluated.

The built-in in-memory log handler records each received event as an entry, and on an
error-bearing event the entry exposes the associated error: it preserves explicitly provided
nonempty metadata on that entry, and it retains the identical error instance that was passed
to the log call.

The error-bearing APIs preserve the logger's existing sendability guarantees.

problem_statement:
Adding support for privacy level in string interpolation
On macOS, the (Apple’s) Logger object uses a custom `OSLogMessage` object which allows it to have a custom string interpolation with support for format arguments privacy levels.

Would it be possible to add support for said string interpolation so we could finally have an efficient and fully feature-compatible OSLog `Logger` for `swift-log`?

Thanks!

### Additional contract requirements

## Attributed metadata values

To support privacy-aware logging on top of `swift-log`, `swift-log` must let callers attach
*attributes* (such as a privacy or sensitivity level) to individual metadata values, so that a
logging backend can render or redact them appropriately.

### Requirements

* `Logger` exposes a public, `Sendable`, `Equatable` value type `MetadataValueAttributes`.
* `MetadataValueAttributes` declares a public protocol `MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute`.
  A type conforms to it to define a custom attribute kind. Conforming types are `Sendable` and
  `RawRepresentable` with a raw value of type `Int64`. The concrete conforming type itself acts
  as the key by which a stored attribute is identified.
* `MetadataValueAttributes` can be constructed empty (`init()`) and from an array literal of
  attribute values.
* A value set in `MetadataValueAttributes` can be read, replaced, and removed through a typed
  subscript keyed by the attribute's concrete type:
  `subscript<T: MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute>(attribute: T.Type) -> T?`.
  Assigning `nil` removes the attribute. Reading an attribute that was never set returns `nil`.
  Two `MetadataValueAttributes` values are equal when they contain the same set of attributes,
  independent of insertion order.
* `Logger.MetadataValue` string interpolation gains an `attributes:` form. Within
  `\(value, attributes: ...)`, the caller supplies attributes either as an
  `inout MetadataValueAttributes -> Void` closure that mutates the attributes, or as an already
  constructed `MetadataValueAttributes` value.
* A metadata value constructed with the `attributes:` interpolation form produces the same
  textual representation (`description`) as the plain interpolation of the same value, and the
  attached attributes are observable. A metadata value constructed without any attribute (plain
  interpolation, `.string`, `.stringConvertible`, `.array`, or `.dictionary`) carries no attributes.
* `Logger.MetadataValue` exposes a read-only computed property
  `attributes: MetadataValueAttributes` that returns the attributes attached to that value, or an
  empty `MetadataValueAttributes` when none were attached.
* Attributes travel with the metadata value: they are preserved when the value is stored in a
  `Logger`'s metadata (via `logger[metadataKey:]`), when it is emitted as statement metadata on a
  log call, when it appears on a `LogEvent`'s `metadata`, and when an event is forwarded through a
  `MultiplexLogHandler` to each of its target handlers. A `LogHandler` observing an event's metadata
  can read the attached attributes of each value.

### Notes

* Only the observable behavior described above is part of the contract; the concrete storage
  strategy for attributes is an implementation detail.
* The set of meaningful attribute kinds is defined by each adopter. `swift-log` defines the
  container and reading API; it does not prescribe a particular privacy taxonomy.

+#### Reading metadata attributes in LogHandlers
+
+Metadata values can carry attributes alongside their string representation. Attributes are embedded inside
+`MetadataValue` via the `.stringConvertible` case and are accessible through the `value.attributes` property. This
+enables features like sensitivity annotations without any changes to your handler's protocol conformance.
+
+To read attributes in your log handler:
+
+```swift
+public func log(event: LogEvent) {
+    // Merge handler metadata, provider metadata, and event metadata as usual
+    var merged = self.metadata
+
+    if let provider = self.metadataProvider {
+        merged.merge(provider.get(), uniquingKeysWith: { _, rhs in rhs })
+    }
+
+    if let eventMetadata = event.metadata {
+        merged.merge(eventMetadata, uniquingKeysWith: { _, rhs in rhs })
+    }
+
+    // Read attributes from individual values:
+    for (key, value) in merged {
+        let attributes = value.attributes    // Empty if the value carries no attributes
+
+        // Process based on your handler's needs
+        // For example, check for a custom attribute:
+        // if attributes[MyAttribute.self] == .flagged { ... }
+    }
+}
+```
+
+**Key considerations:**
+
+- **Opt-in inspection**: Attributes are invisible unless you call `value.attributes`. Handlers that do not care about
+  attributes work without any changes.
+
+- **No new protocol requirements**: Reading attributes does not require implementing any new `LogHandler` properties
+  or subscripts. The `metadata` property and `metadataKey` subscript work exactly as before.
+
+- **Attributes flow through metadata**: Attributed values flow naturally through metadata merging, `MetadataProvider`,
+  and `MultiplexLogHandler` — no special handling needed.
+
 ### Performance considerations
 
 1. **Avoid blocking**: Don't block the calling thread for I/O operations.

+// MARK: - MetadataValueAttributes storage
+
+extension Logger {
+    /// Attributes that can be associated with metadata values.
+    public struct MetadataValueAttributes: Sendable {
+        /// A protocol for defining custom metadata attributes.
+        ///
+        /// Conform to this protocol to define a custom attribute that can be stored in
+        /// ``MetadataValueAttributes``. Each conforming type acts as both the key (identified
+        /// by its metatype) and the value.
+        ///
+        /// This protocol is designed for **small, fixed-vocabulary attributes**.
+        /// Each attribute value is stored as an `Int64` raw value, so attributes occupy minimal
+        /// space (one inline slot without heap allocation for the common single-attribute case).
+        ///
+        /// ## Examples
+        ///
+        /// ```swift
+        /// public enum Priority: Int64, Sendable, Logger.MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute {
+        ///     case low = 1
+        ///     case high = 2
+        /// }
+        /// ```
+        ///
+        /// ```swift
+        /// public struct Priority: Sendable, Hashable, Logger.MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute {
+        ///     public let rawValue: Int64
+        ///     public init(rawValue: Int64) {
+        ///         self.rawValue = rawValue
+        ///     }
+        ///     public static let low = Priority(rawValue: 1)
+        ///     public static let high = Priority(rawValue: 2)
+        /// }
+        /// ```
+        public protocol Attribute: Sendable, RawRepresentable where RawValue == Int64 {}
+
+        /// An entry in the metadata attributes storage.
+        @usableFromInline
+        internal struct Entry: Sendable, Equatable {
+            @usableFromInline
+            internal var key: ObjectIdentifier
+
+            @usableFromInline
+            internal var value: Int64
+
+            @inlinable
+            internal init(key: ObjectIdentifier, value: Int64) {
+                self.key = key
+                self.value = value
+            }
+        }
+
+        @usableFromInline
+        internal var _inline: Entry?
+
+        @usableFromInline
+        internal var _overflow: [Entry]?
+
+        /// Create empty metadata value attributes.
+        @inlinable
+        public init() {}
+
+        /// Get or set a custom attribute by its type.
+        ///
+        /// - Parameter attribute: The metatype of the attribute to access.
+        /// - Returns: The attribute value, or `nil` if not set.
+        @inlinable
+        public subscript<Attr: Attribute>(attribute: Attr.Type) -> Attr? {
+            get {
+                let id = ObjectIdentifier(Attr.self)
+                if let inline = self._inline, inline.key == id { return Attr(rawValue: inline.value) }
+                if let overflow = self._overflow {
+                    for entry in overflow {
+                        if entry.key == id { return Attr(rawValue: entry.value) }
+                    }
+                }
+                return nil
+            }
+            set {
+                let id = ObjectIdentifier(Attr.self)
+                if let v = newValue {
+                    self._upsert(key: id, value: v.rawValue)
+                } else {
+                    self._remove(key: id)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        @inlinable
+        internal mutating func _upsert(key id: ObjectIdentifier, value: Int64) {
+            let entry = Entry(key: id, value: value)
+            if let inline = self._inline, inline.key == id {
+                self._inline = entry
+                return
+            }
+            if let idx = self._overflow?.firstIndex(where: { $0.key == id }) {
+                self._overflow?[idx] = entry
+                return
+            }
+            if self._inline == nil {
+                self._inline = entry
+            } else {
+                if self._overflow == nil {
+                    self._overflow = [entry]
+                } else {
+                    self._overflow?.append(entry)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        @inlinable
+        internal mutating func _remove(key id: ObjectIdentifier) {
+            if let inline = self._inline, inline.key == id {
+                if var overflow = self._overflow, !overflow.isEmpty {
+                    self._inline = overflow.removeLast()
+                    self._overflow = overflow.isEmpty ? nil : overflow
+                } else {
+                    self._inline = nil
+                }
+                return
+            }
+            if let idx = self._overflow?.firstIndex(where: { $0.key == id }) {
+                self._overflow?.remove(at: idx)
+                if self._overflow?.isEmpty == true {
+                    self._overflow = nil
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        @inlinable
+        internal mutating func _merge(from other: Self) {
+            if let inline = other._inline {
+                self._upsert(key: inline.key, value: inline.value)
+            }
+            if let overflow = other._overflow {
+                for entry in overflow {
+                    self._upsert(key: entry.key, value: entry.value)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        /// Compare all entries as an unordered set.
+        ///
+        /// The inline slot and overflow array may hold the same logical entries in different
+        /// positions depending on insertion order. This method checks set equality by
+        /// verifying that every entry on one side exists on the other. O(n²) but n is
+        /// typically 1–2.
+        @inlinable
+        internal func _isEqual(to other: Self) -> Bool {
+            let lhsOverflowCount = self._overflow?.count ?? 0
+            let rhsOverflowCount = other._overflow?.count ?? 0
+            let lhsCount = (self._inline != nil ? 1 : 0) + lhsOverflowCount
+            let rhsCount = (other._inline != nil ? 1 : 0) + rhsOverflowCount
+            guard lhsCount == rhsCount else { return false }
+            guard lhsCount > 0 else { return true }
+

+        }

+        }

+        }

+            _ value: T
+        ) {
+            self.output.append(String(describing: value))
+        }
+    }

+                    metadataAttributes: stringInterpolation.attributes
+                )
+            )

+        }

+import Testing
