+/// Tests for attaching attributes to metadata values via string interpolation
+/// and observing them via the `attributes` API.
+struct MetadataAttributesTests {
+
+    // MARK: - Attributes via string interpolation
+
+    @Test func metadataValueInterpolationWithClosureRecordsAttribute() {
+        let value: Logger.MetadataValue = "\("secret", attributes: { $0[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked })"
+
+        #expect(value.description == "secret")
+        #expect(value.attributes[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+    }
+
+    @Test func metadataValueInterpolationWithClosureRecordsMultipleAttributes() {
+        let setBoth: @Sendable (inout Logger.MetadataValueAttributes) -> Void = { attrs in
+            attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+            attrs[TestPriority.self] = .high
+        }
+        let value: Logger.MetadataValue = "\("secret", attributes: setBoth)"
+
+        #expect(value.description == "secret")
+        #expect(value.attributes[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+        #expect(value.attributes[TestPriority.self] == .high)
+    }
+
+    @Test func metadataValuePlainInterpolationCarriesNoAttributes() {
+        let value: Logger.MetadataValue = "\("plain")"
+
+        #expect(value.description == "plain")
+        #expect(value.attributes[TestSensitivity.self] == nil)
+        #expect(value.attributes == Logger.MetadataValueAttributes())
+    }
+
+    @Test func metadataValueInterpolationWithEmptyClosureCarriesNoAttributes() {
+        let value: Logger.MetadataValue = "\("plain", attributes: { _ in })"
+
+        #expect(value.description == "plain")
+        #expect(value.attributes == Logger.MetadataValueAttributes())
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - MetadataValue.attributes on un-attributed values
+
+    @Test func metadataValueAttributesAreEmptyForUnattributedValues() {
+        let values: [Logger.MetadataValue] = [
+            .string("test"),
+            .stringConvertible(42),
+            .array(["a", "b"]),
+            .dictionary(["k": "v"]),
+        ]
+        for value in values {
+            #expect(value.attributes == Logger.MetadataValueAttributes())
+        }
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - MetadataValueAttributes typed subscript
+
+    @Test func attributesSubscriptRoundTrip() {
+        var attrs = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == nil)
+
+        attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+
+        attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = .plain
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == .plain)
+    }
+
+    @Test func attributesSubscriptNilRemovesValue() {
+        var attrs = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+
+        attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = nil
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == nil)
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - MetadataValueAttributes array literal construction
+
+    @Test func attributesCanBeConstructedFromArrayLiteral() {
+        let attrs: Logger.MetadataValueAttributes = [TestSensitivity.masked, TestPriority.high]
+
+        #expect(attrs[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+        #expect(attrs[TestPriority.self] == .high)
+    }
+
+    @Test func attributesArrayLiteralMatchesSubscriptMutation() {
+        let literal: Logger.MetadataValueAttributes = [TestSensitivity.masked]
+        var subscripted = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        subscripted[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+
+        #expect(literal == subscripted)
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - MetadataValueAttributes equality is independent of insertion order
+
+    @Test func attributesEqualityIgnoresInsertionOrder() {
+        var first = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        first[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+        first[TestPriority.self] = .high
+
+        var second = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        second[TestPriority.self] = .high
+        second[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+
+        #expect(first == second)
+
+        let literalForward: Logger.MetadataValueAttributes = [TestSensitivity.masked, TestPriority.high]
+        let literalReverse: Logger.MetadataValueAttributes = [TestPriority.high, TestSensitivity.masked]
+
+        #expect(literalForward == literalReverse)
+        #expect(first == literalForward)
+    }
+
+    @Test func attributesEqualityDetectsDifferences() {
+        var first = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        first[TestSensitivity.self] = .masked
+
+        var second = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        second[TestSensitivity.self] = .plain
+        #expect(first != second)
+
+        second[TestPriority.self] = .high
+        #expect(first != second)
+
+        let empty = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        #expect(first != empty)
+        #expect(empty == Logger.MetadataValueAttributes())
+    }
+
+    // MARK: - Convenience factory for attributed values
+
+    @Test func attributedFactoryProducesDescribedValueWithAttributes() {
+        let value: Logger.MetadataValue = .attributed("hello", attributes: .masked)
+
+        #expect(value.description == "hello")
+        #expect(value.attributes[TestSensitivity.self] == .masked)
+    }
+}
+
+// MARK: - Test-local attribute keys
+
+private enum TestSensitivity: Int64, Logger.MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute {
+    case plain = 1
+    case masked = 2
+}
+
+private enum TestPriority: Int64, Logger.MetadataValueAttributes.Attribute {
+    case low = 1
+    case high = 2
+}
+
+// Convenience initializer used only by these tests: builds an attributed value
+// through the same prebuilt-attributes interpolation form as any other attribute.
+extension Logger.MetadataValue {
+    fileprivate static func attributed(_ value: String, attributes: TestSensitivity) -> Logger.MetadataValue {
+        var attrs = Logger.MetadataValueAttributes()
+        attrs[TestSensitivity.self] = attributes
+        return "\(value, attributes: attrs)"
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
`binary:split/3` `trim` and `trim_all` options
`split(subject, pattern, options)` accepts `trim` and `trim_all` options. This is used in Popcorn.

### Additional contract requirements

# Additional contract notes

`binary:split/2,3` behaves as follows:

- The subject and the pattern must be binaries; any other subject or pattern
  type raises an `error:badarg` exception. Passing a list of binaries as the
  pattern is outside the scope of this task.
- Without options, `binary:split/3` splits at the first occurrence of the
  pattern only, returning a two-element list ([Part1, Part2]), or a
  one-element list with the original binary when the pattern does not occur.
- With the `global` option, the subject is split at every occurrence of the
  pattern. Occurrences at the start, in the middle, or at the end of the
  subject produce empty (`<<>>`) segments in the result list.
- With the `trim` option, trailing empty segments are removed from the result
  list; in particular, if every segment is empty the result is the empty
  list. This applies both with and without `global`, including when the
  pattern does not occur in the subject.
- With the `trim_all` option, all empty segments are removed from the result
  list, both with and without `global`, including when the pattern does not
  occur in the subject.
- When both `trim` and `trim_all` are supplied (in any order), `trim_all`
  takes precedence: all empty segments are removed.
- When trimming applies, consecutive occurrences of the pattern yield a
  single separator segment in the result rather than one segment per
  occurrence.
- Option list handling matches BEAM semantics: any option atom other than
  `global`, `trim`, or `trim_all` raises an `error:badarg` exception, and an
  improper list tail after a valid proper prefix of option atoms (for example
  `[global | foo]`) is ignored rather than raising an error.

### Additional contract requirements

## Additional contract requirements

The following observable behaviors are required in addition to the base
problem statement. They describe only externally visible behavior; how they
are achieved internally is unconstrained.

### Bounded automatic relay selection

When the user does not explicitly supply a relay, automatic relay selection
must always complete within a bounded time — it must never hang
indefinitely and must not surface an unhandled timeout error to the caller.

- The wait for each candidate relay to answer its address (connection
  details) request is individually bounded. Candidate relays that fail to
  respond, or whose response carries no usable connection details, are
  excluded from selection; if every candidate is excluded, selection fails
  with an error instead of hanging.

- If usable device-reported relay latencies are unavailable — because the
  device sends no response, its response cannot be interpreted, or the
  request toward the device cannot be settled — selection falls back to
  choosing among the client-reachable candidate relays using client-side
  latencies alone. The overall automatic-selection wait is bounded well
  within half a minute (the base behavior that motivated this change — an
  unbounded wait — is fixed by giving each phase a finite completion
  window); the specific value is an implementation choice.

- In every failure mode above, selection completes by returning one of the
  client-reachable candidate relays; it neither hangs nor surfaces an
  unhandled timeout or format error to the caller.

- Selection never chooses a relay that is unreachable from the client. If
  no reachable relay remains, selection fails with an error.

- When multiple candidate relays are equally good (for example a latency
  tie), any of them may be returned.

### Latency measurement

Client-side latency measurement reports, for every requested candidate
relay, either a non-negative measured latency or a sentinel indicating that
the relay is unreachable; entries with missing connection details are
treated as unreachable.

### Daemon handling of relay-latency requests

When the device daemon receives a relay-latency request it responds, for
each requested relay, with either a non-negative measured latency or the
unreachable sentinel. A request with a missing or malformed payload is
ignored — the daemon sends no response and does not crash. A request with
an empty set of relays is answered with an empty result.

problem_statement:
The x-popover does not always render above other views
    Context

     When x-popover is inside an element that creates a CSS stacking context (e.g., x-navbar with position: sticky + backdrop-filter: blur()), the panel
     renders behind content below the navbar. Neither z-index nor position: fixed can escape this trap. The panel must physically leave the stacking
     context.

     x-context-menu already solves this with a portal pattern (overlay root at document level). This plan adds an opt-in portal attribute to x-popover that
     uses the same approach, while keeping the default behavior unchanged.

     Approach

     Add a portal boolean attribute. When set, the panel renders in a document-level overlay layer instead of inside the shadow DOM. User's light DOM
     content is moved (not cloned) to preserve event listeners, and moved back on close.

### Additional contract requirements

### Popover portal mode

When a popover carries the opt-in `portal` boolean attribute (also exposed as a
reflecting `portal` boolean property), opening it renders its panel in a
document-level overlay instead of inside the host's own rendering tree, so the
panel is not contained by — and therefore cannot be clipped or covered by — any
ancestor that creates a CSS stacking context. Without the attribute, the
existing rendering behavior is unchanged and no document-level overlay is
created.

While open in portal mode, the user's light-DOM content nodes are moved (not
cloned) into the document-level panel: node identity and registered event
listeners are preserved, and the same nodes are moved back into the host element
on close.

The documented popover lifecycle is retained in portal mode: `show()`, `hide()`,
and `toggle()` behave as documented; a `disabled` popover does not open; the
cancelable toggle event fires with an `open`-reporting detail and preventing its
default keeps the popover closed; pressing Escape or clicking outside the panel
closes an open portal popover.

+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+;; Portal mode
+;;
+;; The `portal` attribute is an opt-in: when set, opening the popover renders
+;; the panel in a document-level overlay so it escapes ancestor CSS stacking
+;; contexts. Light-DOM content is moved (not cloned) so that node identity
+;; and event listeners are preserved, and the same nodes are moved back on
+;; close. Without the attribute, the existing rendering behavior is unchanged.
+;; These tests assert only that observable contract; they do not depend on
+;; any particular overlay element names, ids, or internal DOM topology.
+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+(defn ^js find-moved-container
+  "Returns the first ancestor of el (walking up to the document root) whose
+   subtree, light DOM or any nested shadow root, excluding the el subtree
+   itself, contains node. Returns nil when node is not found anywhere
+   outside el, i.e. when no document-level overlay adopted it."
+  [^js el ^js node]
+  (letfn [(contains-node? [^js root]
+            (loop [^js child (.-firstElementChild root)]
+              (cond
+                (nil? child)
+                false
+
+                (identical? child el)
+                (recur (.-nextElementSibling child))
+
+                (identical? child node)
+                true
+
+                (or (contains-node? child)
+                    (when-let [^js s (.-shadowRoot child)]
+                      (contains-node? s)))
+                true
+
+                :else
+                (recur (.-nextElementSibling child)))))]
+    (loop [^js current (.-parentElement el)]
+      (cond
+        (nil? current)         nil
+        (contains-node? current) current
+        :else                  (recur (.-parentElement current))))))
+
+(deftest portal-attribute-renders-document-level-panel-test
+  (async done
+    (let [^js el     (make-el)
+          ^js marker (.createElement js/document "div")]
+      (set! (.-textContent marker) "Portalled content")
+      (.appendChild el marker)
+      (.setAttribute el "portal" "")
+      (append! el)
+      (.show el)
+      (js/setTimeout
+       (fn []
+         (let [^js host (find-moved-container el marker)]
+           (is (some? host)
+               "opening with the portal attribute should move light-DOM content into a document-level overlay")
+           (is (not (or (identical? host el)
+                        (.contains el host)))
+               "the portal panel must live outside the host element, at document level"))
+         (.hide el)
+         (done))
+       50))))
+
+(deftest portal-panel-escapes-stacking-context-ancestors-test

+    (let [^js wrapper (.createElement js/document "div")]
+      ;; An ancestor that creates a CSS stacking context
+      (set! (.. wrapper -style -position) "sticky")

+           (let [^js host (find-moved-container el marker)]

+                 "the portal panel must not be contained by a stacking-context ancestor"))
+           (.hide el)
+           (.remove wrapper)
+           (done))
+         50)))))
+
+(deftest portal-content-moved-not-cloned-test
+  (async done
+    (let [^js el  (make-el)
+          ^js div (.createElement js/document "div")
+          seen    (atom false)]
+      (set! (.-textContent div) "Cart content")
+      ;; An event listener on the light-DOM node proves identity is kept:

+      (.show el)

+         (is @seen
+             "event listeners on light-DOM content must survive the move (no cloning)")
+         (.hide el)
+         (is (.contains el div)
+             "the same node should be moved back into the host on close")
+         (done))
+       50))))

+         (.hide el)
+         (done))
+       50))))
+
+(deftest portal-cancel-prevents-open-test
+  (let [^js el (append! (make-el))]
+    (.setAttribute el "portal" "")
+    (.addEventListener el "x-popover-toggle"
+                       (fn [^js e] (.preventDefault e)))
+    (.show el)
+    (is (not (.hasAttribute el "open"))

+(deftest portal-escape-closes-test
+  (async done
+    (let [^js el (append! (make-el))]
+      (.setAttribute el "portal" "")
+      (.show el)
+      (js/setTimeout
+       (fn []
+         (.dispatchEvent js/document

+          (fn []
+            (is (not (.hasAttribute el "open"))
+                "Escape should close an open portal popover")
+            (done))
+          50))
+       50))))
+
+(deftest portal-outside-click-closes-test
+  (async done
+    (let [^js el     (append! (make-el))
+          ^js marker (.createElement js/document "div")]
+      (.appendChild el marker)
+      (.setAttribute el "portal" "")
+      (.show el)
+      (js/setTimeout
+       (fn []
+         (is (some? (find-moved-container el marker))

+         (.dispatchEvent (.-body js/document)

+         (js/setTimeout
+          (fn []
+            (is (not (.hasAttribute el "open"))

+            (done))
+          50))
+       50))))
+
+(deftest default-mode-renders-panel-inside-host-test
+  (async done
+    (let [^js el     (append! (make-el))
+          ^js marker (.createElement js/document "div")]
+      ;; No portal attribute: default behavior is unchanged
+      (.appendChild el marker)

problem_statement:
Report direction of lumped elements for simulation configuration
The SolidModel (or SolidModel + Schematic) should be able to report port orientations so that they can be automatically configured for simulation. Note that Palace allows lumped ports with arbitrary orientation, so any solution should accommodate that.

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

- Any geometry entity can be annotated with an orientation using the exported
  `WithDirection` style, as in `WithDirection(angle)(entity)`. The angle is the
  direction counterclockwise from the +X axis in the entity's local coordinate
  frame. `WithDirection()` defaults to `0°`; a bare numeric (non-angle) argument
  is interpreted as radians and is stored as the equivalent angle in degrees
  (so `WithDirection(pi / 4)` stores a direction of approximately `45°`). The
  annotated direction is available in the style's `direction` field and is not
  automatically normalized to `[0°, 360°)`. Calling the style on an entity
  with an optional direction argument also works, with the direction defaulted
  when omitted.
- `extract_direction` is exported. Given a (possibly nested) styled entity, it
  recovers, at the point where the entity is placed, the stored local direction
  angle of the outermost `WithDirection` wrapper in the style chain (other
  styles such as mesh-sizing or optionality wrappers may appear inside or
  outside it), and returns `nothing` when no `WithDirection` wrapper is
  present.
- The annotated direction transforms together with the entity: rotating the
  style rotates its direction by the same amount, and reflecting the style
  reflects its direction. The annotation has no effect on rendered geometry;
  styling an entity with `WithDirection` produces the same polygons as the
  unstyled entity.
- `ExamplePDK.port_directions(sch, ly)` returns a `Dict` mapping the positive
  integer layer index of every indexed entity on schematic layer `ly` that
  carries a `WithDirection` annotation to a simulation-configuration value
  describing that annotation's globally transformed orientation.
- Global orientation is the local annotated angle composed with the transforms
  of all references along the placement chain, including reflections, so an
  entity reached through a rotated or reflected reference reports the rotated
  or reflected orientation.
- Calling `port_directions` for a layer whose entities have not been indexed
  raises an `ErrorException`; in such a call the untransformed entities still
  carry their default positive indices, and the failure is the documented
  repeated-index error raised when two annotated entities report the same
  index. `port_directions` performs no separate unindexed-layer validation, and
  indexing a schematic layer itself (via `index_layer!`) does not perform its
  own validation of pre-existing positive indices. Entities on `ly` without a
  `WithDirection` annotation are omitted from the result; when nothing
  qualifies, the result is an empty `Dict`.
- Orientations within `1e-3` degrees of a cardinal direction normalize (modulo
  360°) to one of the strings `"+X"`, `"+Y"`, `"-X"`, or `"-Y"`.
- Any other orientation is reported as a floating-point unit vector
  `[dx, dy, 0.0]`, whose components equal the cosine and sine of the globally
  transformed orientation angle.

+"""
+    port_directions(sch::Schematic, ly::Symbol) -> Dict{Int, Union{String, Vector{Float64}}}
+
+For every entity on layer `ly` in `sch.coordinate_system` that has been indexed
+(i.e., `layerindex(metadata) != 0`) AND carries a [`WithDirection`](@ref) style in
+its wrapper chain, return a dictionary mapping `layerindex(metadata) -> direction config value` suitable for Palace's `LumpedPort`/`WavePort` `Direction` field.
+
+Direction config value is a string `"+X"`, `"-X"`, `"+Y"`, or `"-Y"` for axis-aligned orientations
+(within `atol=1e-3` degrees of the nearest axis), or a unit vector `[dx, dy, 0.0]::Vector{Float64}`
+for arbitrary orientations.
+
+Must be called AFTER indexing has run. Typical usage is after `render!(sm, sch, target)` or `Cell(sch, target)` for a target whose `indexed_layers(target)`
+includes `ly`. If no entities on `ly` are indexed or none carry `WithDirection`,
+returns an empty `Dict`. This function does NOT call `index_layer!` itself.
+
+# Example
+
+```julia
+render!(sm, sch, target)
+dirs = port_directions(sch, :lumped_element)
+# Dict(1 => "+Y", 2 => "-X")
+```
+
+See also: [`WithDirection`](@ref).
+"""
+function port_directions(sch::Schematic, ly::Symbol)
+    dirs = Dict{Int, Union{String, Vector{Float64}}}()
+    # Traverse all reachable coordinate systems in the schematic (the schematic's
+    # own `coordinate_system` plus every reference descendant). `index_layer!`
+    # places indexed entities onto per-node coordsyses, recording the node for
+    # each index in `sch.index_dict[ly]` and setting in-component indices to 0.
+    # Each `(cs, trans)` pair includes the accumulated reference transform;
+    # applying it makes the returned direction reflect the entity's global orientation.
+    for (cs, trans) in DeviceLayout.traversal(sch.coordinate_system)
+        for (el, m) in zip(elements(cs), element_metadata(cs))
+            layer(m) == ly || continue
+            idx = layerindex(m)
+            idx == 0 && continue
+            dir = DeviceLayout.extract_direction(el)
+            dir === nothing && continue
+            haskey(dirs, idx) &&
+                error("Repeated index $idx. Before calling `port_directions`, \
+layer $ly should be indexed by rendering with a target whose `indexed_layers` \
+include $ly (or indexed directly with `index_layer!`)")
+            dirs[idx] = _direction_config(rotated_direction(dir, trans))
+        end
+    end
+    return dirs
+end
+
+# Format a direction angle (CCW from +X, in degrees) as a Palace-compatible
+# `Direction` config value. Axis-aligned directions return one of "+X", "-X", "+Y",
+# "-Y"; off-axis returns a unit-vector [dx, dy, 0.0]. Input is normalized modulo 360°.
+function _direction_config(angle; atol=1e-3)
+    a_deg = mod(DeviceLayout.ustrip(°, angle), 360.0)
+    abs(a_deg - 0.0) < atol && return "+X"
+    abs(a_deg - 90.0) < atol && return "+Y"
+    abs(a_deg - 180.0) < atol && return "-X"
+    abs(a_deg - 270.0) < atol && return "-Y"
+    abs(a_deg - 360.0) < atol && return "+X"
+    return [cos(angle), sin(angle), 0.0]
+end

+
+"""
+    struct WithDirection <: GeometryEntityStyle
+        direction::typeof(1.0°)
+    end
+    WithDirection(direction=0°)
+
+Style that annotates a `GeometryEntity` with a direction angle (CCW from the +X axis
+in the entity's local frame) for use in simulation configuration. For example, a
+lumped-port rectangle can carry its electrical orientation so that Palace's
+`LumpedPort`/`WavePort` `Direction` field can be populated after rendering.
+
+Rendering is unaffected: `to_polygons` and `to_primitives` pass through to the underlying entity.
+The direction transforms with the entity under rotation or reflection via
+`transform(sty::WithDirection, f::Transformation) = WithDirection(rotated_direction(sty.direction, f))`,
+so after `plan!`/`build!`/`index_layer!` the carried angle describes the global
+orientation.
+
+If an angle is given without units, it is assumed to be in radians.
+The stored angle is **not** automatically normalized to `[0°, 360°)`.
+"""
+struct WithDirection <: GeometryEntityStyle
+    direction::typeof(1.0°)
+    # Constrain the inner constructor to a Number so WithDirection(::GeometryEntity)
+    # routes via the generic `(T::Type{<:GeometryEntityStyle})(x::GeometryEntity, args...)`
+    # fallback instead of colliding with this constructor (silences Aqua).
+    WithDirection(direction::Number) = new(uconvert(°, direction))
+end
+# Default constructor — no-arg form is unambiguous.
+WithDirection() = WithDirection(0°)
+
+to_polygons(ent::GeometryEntity, ::WithDirection; kwargs...) = to_polygons(ent; kwargs...)
+
+transform(sty::WithDirection, f::Transformation) =
+    WithDirection(rotated_direction(sty.direction, f))
+
+# Walk through any nesting of StyledEntity wrappers and return the `direction`
+# angle of the first `WithDirection` style encountered (from outside in), or `nothing` if no
+# `WithDirection` is present. Handles nesting like
+# WithDirection(MeshSized(only_simulated(rect))) and the reverse.
+extract_direction(::DeviceLayout.GeometryEntity) = nothing
+function extract_direction(ent::DeviceLayout.StyledEntity)
+    return extract_direction(ent.ent)
+end
+function extract_direction(
+    ent::DeviceLayout.StyledEntity{T, U, WithDirection}
+) where {T, U <: GeometryEntity{T}}
+    return ent.sty.direction
+end

problem_statement:
[core] cleanup workaround using NIOLockedValueBox instead of Mutex
Due to 
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/issues/80036
https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/issues/78048

we use `NIOLockedValueBox` instead of `Mutex` in `LambdaRuntime.swift`

This issue to is keep track of that and to not forget remove `NIOLockedValueBox` when 6.0.x will fix this or when we will not support 6.0 anymore (at the release of 6.3 in 2026)

### Additional contract requirements

Its synchronization may use any facility available on the supported toolchains, without changing its externally observable single-consumption semantics: one retrieval succeeds and every later retrieval throws. When retrievals race, exactly one may succeed.

No storage property name, visibility, concrete replacement type, or locking method is part of this contract, and non-executable commentary such as comments or documentation therefore does not count as using the retired workaround. No new public logging interface or structured-log fields are required; existing logging, byte-writing, pool, and cancellation checks are regression coverage only.

problem_statement:
Consider having `--no-foo` trigger a validation error for non boolean options
## Currently 
It's nice that bb cli supports `--no-foo`:

```clojure
(cli/parse-opts ["--foo"])
;; => {:foo true}

(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"])
;; => {:foo false}

(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :boolean}}})
;; => {:foo false}
```

## But what if foo is not a boolean?

When `false` is coercible, it doesn't fail...
```clojure
(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :symbol}}})
;; => {:foo false}

(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :string}}})
;; => {:foo "false"}

(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :keyword}}})
;; => {:foo :false}
```
But since this makes no sense, I'm thinking specifying `--no-foo` here merits an error.

We do get an error when `false` is not coercible...
```clojure
(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :long}}})
;; => Execution error (ExceptionInfo) at babashka.cli/->error-fn$fn (cli.cljc:263).
;;    Invalid value for option --no-foo: cannot transform input "false" to long
```
But the error message is not the user-friendliest.

## Proposal
Generate a helpful error message when `--no-` is applied to a non-boolean option.

[HIDDEN]

## Out of scope
I think the `:negatable` option is still fine as it is.
It only affects generated help.
If a developer slaps this on a non-boolean option, that's a developer error.

### Additional contract requirements

## Contract addendum: option negation with non-boolean coercions

### Supported negation token forms

- An option may be negated with either the `--no-<name>` long-option form or the
  `:no-<name>` keyword-option form (e.g. `--no-foo` and `:no-foo`).

### Applicable coercion declarations

- The negation rejection rule applies whenever the target option has an
  explicitly declared, non-boolean coercion. Both supported ways of declaring
  that coercion are covered:
  - the top-level `:coerce` map (e.g. `{:coerce {:foo :long}}`), and
  - the option's `:coerce` entry inside `:spec` (e.g. `{:spec {:foo {:coerce :long}}}`).
- A collection-wrapped coercion (e.g. `{:coerce {:foo [:long]}}`) whose element
  coercion is non-boolean is likewise non-boolean for the purposes of this rule.
- Both `:boolean` and `:bool` (and collection-wrapped variants of them) count as
  boolean coercions and continue to accept negation.

### Behavior and compatibility expectations

- Applying a negated token to an option with an explicitly declared non-boolean
  coercion signals an error; it does not silently treat the negated value as a
  value to coerce to the option's type.
- The following existing behaviors are preserved:
  - a negated token for an option with no declared coercion yields `false`
    (e.g. parsing `["--no-option"]` yields `{:option false}`, also through
    `parse-args`);
  - a negated token for an option with a `:boolean`/`:bool` coercion yields `false`;
  - a negated token for an option whose declared coercion is boolean via `:spec`
    yields `false`;
  - a negated token whose remaining name does not match any declared option
    still parses as its own option with value `true`;
  - the `:negatable` option remains a help-formatting concern only and does not
    change this parsing behavior.

### Error guarantee

- The error raised for a rejected negation is descriptive: its message contains
  the offending token exactly as it appeared on the command line (for example,
  the text `--no-foo` when `--no-foo` was used, or `:no-foo` when `:no-foo` was
  used). No other error wording, error type, or error-data fields are
  guaranteed by this contract.

problem_statement:
Should boolean flags coerce to `:edn`?
While working on #166, I noticed that boolean flags coerce to `:edn`:

```clojure
(require '[babashka.cli :as cli])

(cli/parse-opts ["--foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :edn}}})
;; => {:foo true}

(cli/parse-opts ["--no-foo"] {:spec {:foo {:coerce :edn}}})
;; => {:foo false}
```

I'm not sure about expected behaviour; there's not much said about the `:edn` coercer in the docs.

problem_statement:
Bitstring generators in comprehensions
Client-side comprehensions support enumerable generators, filters, and the `:into`, `:uniq`, and `:reduce` options, but bitstring generators are not handled:

```elixir
for <<r::8, g::8, b::8 <- pixels>>, do: {r, g, b}
```

The compiler has no transformation for them, so they currently produce invalid client code.

Add bitstring generator support across the compiler and the client runtime with server-identical semantics, including stepwise prefix matching, silent termination on mismatch, leftover-bit discarding, and `{:bad_generator, term}` errors for non-bitstring sources.

This completes comprehension parity with the Elixir server runtime.

### Additional contract requirements

- Client-side comprehensions must support bitstring generators (`for <<segment_pattern <- bitstring_source>>`) with semantics identical to the Elixir server runtime.
- A bitstring generator iterates its source stepwise: at each step the leading bits of the remaining source must match the full segment pattern (all specified segments, sizes, and prefixes). Iteration terminates silently at the first position where the pattern does not match; items after the first non-matching prefix are not produced. The terminating prefix does not raise.
- Bits left over at the end of the source that cannot fill a complete pattern are silently discarded; they must not raise and must not produce a partial item.
- An empty source yields an empty result.
- A source that is not a bitstring must raise an `ErlangError` whose message is `Erlang error: {:bad_generator, <source>}` where `<source>` is the inspected source term (for example `{:bad_generator, [1, 2]}`).
- Segment patterns may bind multiple variables per step and may match segments narrower than a byte (for example `x::4`), and variable bindings produced by bitstring generators, enumerable generators, filters, the `:uniq` option, and `:reduce` accumulators must compose exactly as they do on the Elixir server runtime.
- These semantics must hold in both the synchronous and the asynchronous client execution modes.

Set navigation view pane to compact mode 3. Add a `PaneItemExpander` and children 4. Press pane item expander on the sidebar. **Expected behavior** Same as left-to-right. **Screenshots** **Additional context** n/a ### Additional contract requirements ## Regression coverage addendum ### Covered behavior `test/navigation_view_test.dart` now covers the reported compact-pane flyout issue: when a `NavigationView` uses `PaneDisplayMode.compact` and its pane contains a `PaneItemExpander`, tapping the expander opens a `MenuFlyout` whose observable behavior must be the same in right-to-left directionality as in left-to-right directionality. The tests verify, using only publicly observable widget geometry: 1. **Equal usable dimensions** — the flyout opened in RTL directionality has the same width and height as the equivalent flyout opened in LTR directionality (so it must not be squeezed into the compact pane's width). 2. **Logical placement** — in each directionality the flyout opens on the logical outer side of the compact pane: to the right of the pane in LTR and to the left of the pane in RTL, while remaining vertically aligned with the expander in the same way in both directions. All pre-existing `NavigationView` tests remain part of the contract and must continue to pass unchanged.

## Regression coverage addendum

### Covered behavior

`test/navigation_view_test.dart` now covers the reported compact-pane flyout
issue: when a `NavigationView` uses `PaneDisplayMode.compact` and its pane
contains a `PaneItemExpander`, tapping the expander opens a `MenuFlyout` whose
observable behavior must be the same in right-to-left directionality as in
left-to-right directionality.

The tests verify, using only publicly observable widget geometry:

1. **Equal usable dimensions** — the flyout opened in RTL directionality has
   the same width and height as the equivalent flyout opened in LTR
   directionality (so it must not be squeezed into the compact pane's width).
2. **Logical placement** — in each directionality the flyout opens on the
   logical outer side of the compact pane: to the right of the pane in LTR and
   to the left of the pane in RTL, while remaining vertically aligned with the
   expander in the same way in both directions.

All pre-existing `NavigationView` tests remain part of the contract and must
continue to pass unchanged.

       },

+
+  group('Issue - NavigationView compact pane flyout in RTL directionality', () {
+    const paneKey = ValueKey('rtl-compact-pane');
+
+    NavigationPane makePane(String directionTag) {
+      return NavigationPane(
+        key: paneKey,
+        selected: 0,
+        displayMode: PaneDisplayMode.compact,
+        items: [
+          PaneItemExpander(
+            key: ValueKey('expander-$directionTag'),
+            icon: const Icon(FluentIcons.folder),
+            title: const Text('Files'),
+            body: const Center(child: Text('Files Page')),
+            items: [
+              PaneItem(
+                icon: const Icon(FluentIcons.document),
+                title: const Text('Documents'),
+                body: const Center(child: Text('Documents Page')),
+              ),
+              PaneItem(
+                icon: const Icon(FluentIcons.picture_fill),
+                title: const Text('Pictures'),
+                body: const Center(child: Text('Pictures Page')),
+              ),
+              PaneItem(
+                icon: const Icon(FluentIcons.music_note),
+                title: const Text('Music'),
+                body: const Center(child: Text('Music Page')),
+              ),
+            ],
+          ),
+        ],
+      );
+    }
+
+    /// Pumps a compact [NavigationView] wrapped in the given [direction],
+    /// opens the [PaneItemExpander] flyout and returns the flyout's global
+    /// rect together with the compact pane's global rect.
+    Future<(Rect flyoutRect, Rect paneRect)> openFlyout(
+      WidgetTester tester,
+      TextDirection direction,
+    ) async {
+      // Key the whole subtree on the direction so each scenario starts from
+      // a freshly-created expander state.
+      await tester.pumpWidget(
+        KeyedSubtree(
+          key: ValueKey(direction),
+          child: FluentApp(
+            home: Directionality(
+              textDirection: direction,
+              child: SizedBox(
+                width: 1200,
+                height: 800,
+                child: NavigationView(pane: makePane(direction.name)),
+              ),
+            ),
+          ),
+        ),
+      );
+      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+      // Tap the PaneItemExpander icon to open the flyout.
+      await tester.tap(find.byIcon(FluentIcons.folder), warnIfMissed: false);
+      await tester.pumpAndSettle();
+
+      expect(
+        find.byType(MenuFlyout),
+        findsOneWidget,
+        reason: 'The PaneItemExpander flyout should open in compact mode',
+      );
+      return (
+        tester.getRect(find.byType(MenuFlyout)),
+        tester.getRect(find.byKey(paneKey)),
+      );
+    }
+
+    testWidgets(
+      'PaneItemExpander flyout has the same usable dimensions in RTL as LTR',
+      (tester) async {
+        final (ltrRect, _) = await openFlyout(tester, TextDirection.ltr);
+        final (rtlRect, _) = await openFlyout(tester, TextDirection.rtl);
+
+        expect(
+          rtlRect.width,
+          moreOrLessEquals(ltrRect.width, epsilon: 1.0),
+          reason:
+              'The RTL flyout should be as wide as the LTR flyout, not '
+              'squeezed into the $kCompactNavigationPaneWidth px compact pane '
+              '(LTR: $ltrRect, RTL: $rtlRect)',
+        );
+        expect(
+          rtlRect.height,
+          moreOrLessEquals(ltrRect.height, epsilon: 1.0),
+          reason:
+              'The RTL flyout should be as tall as the LTR flyout '
+              '(LTR: $ltrRect, RTL: $rtlRect)',
+        );
+      },
+    );
+
+    testWidgets(
+      'PaneItemExpander flyout opens on the logical outer side of the pane',
+      (tester) async {
+        final (ltrRect, ltrPaneRect) = await openFlyout(
+          tester,
+          TextDirection.ltr,
+        );
+        expect(
+          ltrRect.left,
+          greaterThanOrEqualTo(ltrPaneRect.right - 1.0),
+          reason:
+              'In LTR, the flyout should open to the right of the compact '
+              'pane (pane: $ltrPaneRect, flyout: $ltrRect)',
+        );
+
+        final (rtlRect, rtlPaneRect) = await openFlyout(
+          tester,
+          TextDirection.rtl,
+        );
+        expect(
+          rtlRect.right,
+          lessThanOrEqualTo(rtlPaneRect.left + 1.0),
+          reason:
+              'In RTL, the flyout should open to the left of the compact '
+              'pane (pane: $rtlPaneRect, flyout: $rtlRect)',
+        );
+        expect(
+          rtlRect.top,
+          moreOrLessEquals(ltrRect.top, epsilon: 1.0),
+          reason:
+              'In RTL, the flyout should be vertically aligned with the '
+              'expander the same way as in LTR (LTR: $ltrRect, RTL: $rtlRect)',
+        );
+      },

👍 ## 🤖 Model Performance False Positives: Frequent but expected in current model stage Especially during: - Background noise - Phone handling noise - Some >70% confidence despite being incorrect Hope this helps :octocat: ### Additional contract requirements ## Contract addendum: confirmed-detections flag This task implements the high-priority **"Confirm detections"** request from the feature table: a way for a reviewer to mark a detection as verified (visual/audio verification). The observable contract is: ### Confirmation state on detection records - Every detection starts out **unconfirmed**; confirmation is opt-in. - The current state is observable on the detection record through a boolean `isConfirmed` accessor. - The confirmation state is backed by per-detection confirmation data exposed through a `confirmedAt` member on the record: - it can be passed to the record constructor, and - it can be changed on an existing record to mark the detection confirmed or to undo that confirmation (this mirrors the tap-to-toggle review action). - Toggling works repeatedly: confirming, unconfirming, and confirming again each update the observable `isConfirmed` state accordingly. ### Persistence - The confirmation state is part of a detection's saved session data: it survives serializing a record to JSON and loading it back, together with the record's other fields. - Sessions saved before this feature existed (record JSON without any confirmation information) still load, and every such detection is treated as unconfirmed. ### Exports - When a detection has been marked confirmed, that fact must be perceptible in every export that lists detections (Raven selection table, CSV, JSON, and GPX), so a confirmed detection can be told apart from an otherwise identical unconfirmed one. - The concrete representation (dedicated column or field, marker element, or equivalent note) is an implementation choice. - A detection that was never confirmed must never appear as confirmed in any export. ### Out of scope for judging - The exact names of export columns/fields/elements, the exact presence or text format of confirmation timestamps inside exports, and column ordering are **not** required beyond the observable distinctions above. - UI presentation details (icon placement, badge styling, map overlays) are free implementation choices.

contract_addendum:
## Contract addendum: confirmed-detections flag

This task implements the high-priority **"Confirm detections"** request from
the feature table: a way for a reviewer to mark a detection as verified
(visual/audio verification). The observable contract is:

### Confirmation state on detection records

- Every detection starts out **unconfirmed**; confirmation is opt-in.
- The current state is observable on the detection record through a boolean
  `isConfirmed` accessor.
- The confirmation state is backed by per-detection confirmation data exposed
  through a `confirmedAt` member on the record:
  - it can be passed to the record constructor, and
  - it can be changed on an existing record to mark the detection confirmed
    or to undo that confirmation (this mirrors the tap-to-toggle review
    action).
- Toggling works repeatedly: confirming, unconfirming, and confirming again
  each update the observable `isConfirmed` state accordingly.

### Persistence

- The confirmation state is part of a detection's saved session data: it
  survives serializing a record to JSON and loading it back, together with
  the record's other fields.
- Sessions saved before this feature existed (record JSON without any
  confirmation information) still load, and every such detection is treated
  as unconfirmed.

### Exports

- When a detection has been marked confirmed, that fact must be perceptible
  in every export that lists detections (Raven selection table, CSV, JSON,
  and GPX), so a confirmed detection can be told apart from an otherwise
  identical unconfirmed one.
- The concrete representation (dedicated column or field, marker element, or
  equivalent note) is an implementation choice.
- A detection that was never confirmed must never appear as confirmed in any
  export.

### Out of scope for judging

- The exact names of export columns/fields/elements, the exact presence or
  text format of confirmation timestamps inside exports, and column ordering
  are **not** required beyond the observable distinctions above.
- UI presentation details (icon placement, badge styling, map overlays) are
  free implementation choices.

problem_statement:
TASK-009: Video save-as Bug — "Page is not yet closed"
## Problem

Calling `(spel/finish-video-recording {:save-as "/path/to/output.webm"})` throws `"Page is not yet closed"`. Playwright requires page/context to be closed before `video.saveAs()` can be called.

## Reproduction

```bash
spel --eval '(do (spel/navigate "https://example.com") (spel/start-video-recording) (Thread/sleep 2000) (spel/finish-video-recording {:save-as "/tmp/test.webm"}))'
# Error: "Page is not yet closed"
```

## Workaround

```clojure
(let [path (spel/video-path)]
  (spel/finish-video-recording) ;; no save-as
  (Thread/sleep 500)
  ;; then cp the file manually)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `(spel/finish-video-recording {:save-as "/tmp/out.webm"})` successfully saves
2. No "Page is not yet closed" error
3. Function blocks until file is fully written
4. Clear error if path not writable
5. Works from both `--eval` and library API

## Type
🐛 Bug — Documented API option doesn't work

## Priority
🟠 P2 — Medium. Workaround exists but is unintuitive.

## Effort/Impact
20% effort / 30% impact — Medium ROI

**Linear:** https://linear.app/blockether/issue/BLO-141

### Additional contract requirements

When `finish-video-recording` is called with a `:save-as` destination:

- The call succeeds without raising a "Page is not yet closed" error and, on success, returns a result that reports the recording as stopped.
- The call blocks until the requested destination file is completely written: when the call returns, the destination file exists and contains the recorded (non-empty) video.
- If the destination cannot be written, the call must not silently claim success: it raises an error with a clear, non-empty message or returns a result that does not report a successful stop. The unwritable destination file must not be created.
- This behavior applies when the function is invoked through `spel --eval` or through the library evaluation API, since both go through the same `spel/finish-video-recording` entry point.
- This requirement does not prescribe any destination-specific convention for the `:video-path` value in the result of `:save-as` calls; the observable contract is the existence and completed content of the requested destination file.

 (ns com.blockether.spel.sci-eval-video-test
   "Tests for video recording through SCI eval."
   (:require
+   [clojure.string :as str]
    [com.blockether.spel.sci-env :as sut]
    [com.blockether.spel.allure :refer [defdescribe describe expect it]]))
 
+(defn- reset-sci-atoms!
+  "Resets the SCI session atoms so each scenario starts fresh."
+  []
+  (reset! sut/!pw nil) (reset! sut/!browser nil)
+  (reset! sut/!context nil) (reset! sut/!page nil)
+  (reset! sut/!daemon-mode? false))
+
+(defn- eval-recording-fixture-code
+  "Evaluates the script start! -> start-video-recording -> about:blank -> wait
+   in one `eval-string' form, mirroring what `spel --eval' (and the library
+   evaluation API) send through the same `eval-string' entry point. Uses the
+   built-in `about:blank' page so the fixture needs no network access; a live
+   https navigation would make the whole scenario fail outright in a
+   network-restricted evaluator."
+  [ctx]
+  (sut/eval-string ctx
+    (str "(do (spel/start!)"
+         "    (spel/start-video-recording {:video-dir \"test-videos-sci\"})"
+         "    (spel/navigate \"about:blank\")"
+         "    (spel/wait-for-timeout 500))")))
+
+(defn- wait-for-file!
+  "Blocks until `file` exists with non-empty content (up to ~5s), then
+   returns it. Mirrors the documented contract that a successful finish
+   call blocks until the destination file is completely written: on a
+   correct implementation the file is already fully written when the call
+   returns, so this normally returns on the first iteration. The short
+   wait only absorbs asynchronous filesystem/encoder visibility slack so
+   the size assertion below never flakes."
+  [^java.io.File file]
+  (loop [attempts 50]
+    (if (and (.exists file) (pos? (.length file)))
+      file
+      (when (pos? attempts)
+        (Thread/sleep 100)
+        (recur (dec attempts))))))
+
 (defdescribe sci-video-recording-test
   "Video recording via SCI eval"
 
   (describe "start and finish video recording"
     (it "records and produces a video file"
-      ;; Reset SCI atoms
-      (reset! sut/!pw nil) (reset! sut/!browser nil)
-      (reset! sut/!context nil) (reset! sut/!page nil)
-      (reset! sut/!daemon-mode? false)
+      (reset-sci-atoms!)
       (let [ctx (sut/create-sci-ctx)]

           ;; Start browser
@@ -24,8 +59,9 @@

-          ;; Navigate to generate some video content

+(defdescribe sci-video-save-as-primary-test
+  "Video recording with :save-as via SCI eval (the `spel/finish-video-recording' entry point)"
+
+  (describe "finish-video-recording with :save-as"
+    (it "successfully saves and completely writes the requested destination file"
+      (reset-sci-atoms!)
+      (let [ctx       (sut/create-sci-ctx)
+            save-path "test-videos-sci/save-as-copy.webm"
+            file      (java.io.File. save-path)]
+        (when (.exists file) (.delete file))
+        (try
+          (eval-recording-fixture-code ctx)
+
+          ;; Finish with :save-as — must succeed without throwing
+          ;; (in particular, no "Page is not yet closed" error) and report
+          ;; the recording as stopped.
+          (let [result (sut/eval-string ctx
+                         (str "(spel/finish-video-recording {:save-as \"" save-path "\"})"))]
+            (expect (map? result))
+            (expect (= "stopped" (:status result)))
+            ;; The call blocks until the destination file is fully written:
+            ;; once it returns, the destination exists and contains the
+            ;; recorded (non-empty) video. This asserts only the observable
+            ;; destination file, not any particular :video-path convention.
+            (wait-for-file! file)
+            (expect (.exists file))
+            (expect (> (.length file) 0)))
+
+          (finally
+            (try (sut/eval-string ctx "(spel/stop!)")
+                 (catch Exception _))
+            (when (.exists file) (.delete file))))))))
+
+(defdescribe sci-video-save-as-error-reporting-test
+  "Error reporting of finish-video-recording :save-as via SCI eval"
+
+  (describe "finish-video-recording with :save-as"
+    (it "reports a clear error when the destination is not writable"
+      (reset-sci-atoms!)
+      (let [ctx (sut/create-sci-ctx)
+            ;; Build a destination that is guaranteed unwritable on every
+            ;; host, platform and user (root included), without depending
+            ;; on any particular system path or permission bits: a regular
+            ;; file is placed where the destination's parent "directory"
+            ;; would be, so any attempt to create the destination
+            ;; directory or file underneath it must fail
+            ;; (NotDirectoryException / DirectoryNotFoundException /
+            ;; FileSystemException — the exact subtype is not asserted).
+            ;; All paths live inside an independent, per-scenario temp
+            ;; directory so the recording's own video directory can never
+            ;; collide with (or be confused for) the blocker location.
+            root      (.toFile
+                        (java.nio.file.Files/createTempDirectory
+                          "spel-save-as-error" (into-array java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute [])))
+            blocker   (.toFile
+                        (java.nio.file.Files/createFile
+                          (.toPath (java.io.File. root "spel-blocker"))
+                          (into-array java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute [])))
+            bad-path  (str (.getPath blocker) java.io.File/separator "save-as-copy.webm")
+            bad-file  (java.io.File. bad-path)]
+        (try
+          (eval-recording-fixture-code ctx)
+
+          ;; Sanity-check the fixture invariant before triggering the save:
+          ;; the blocker is an existing regular file and the destination
+          ;; cannot exist.
+          (expect (.isFile blocker))
+          (expect (not (.exists bad-file)))
+
+          ;; Exercise only the public `eval-string' entry point on a
+          ;; normal, still-open recording session — no internal session
+          ;; state is touched, exactly as a user calling
+          ;; `spel/finish-video-recording' would. The destination is
+          ;; unwritable, so any correct implementation must report a
+          ;; non-silent failure here.
+          (let [outcome (try
+                          (sut/eval-string ctx
+                            (str "(spel/finish-video-recording {:save-as \"" bad-path "\"})"))
+                          (catch Exception e
+                            {:ex/message (ex-message e)}))]
+            (if-let [msg (:ex/message outcome)]
+              ;; A clear error message was raised, and it must actually be
+              ;; the destination-writability error: the generic
+              ;; "Page is not yet closed" Playwright state error means the
+              ;; implementation never closed the recording page before
+              ;; saving (the masking defect), so the unwritable destination
+              ;; was never exercised and this result does not count as
+              ;; reported.
+              (let [msg (str msg)]
+                (expect (not (str/blank? msg)))
+                (expect (not (re-find #"(?i)page is not yet closed" msg))))
+              ;; Otherwise the result must not claim success —
+              ;; and it must not be the silent no-op nil.
+              (do
+                (expect (some? outcome))
+                (expect (not= "stopped" (:status outcome))))))
+
+          ;; The unwritable destination must not have been created. The
+          ;; blocker is a real file, so `bad-path` can only ever exist if
+          ;; the implementation deleted the blocker — never acceptable.
+          (expect (.isFile blocker))
+          (expect (not (.exists bad-file)))
+
+          (finally
+            (try (sut/eval-string ctx "(spel/stop!)")
+                 (catch Exception _))

problem_statement:
Bash post-tool clears neo-tree markers globally, wiping concurrent Bash command markers
## Summary

When an agent issues **multiple separate Bash commands** that touch files (e.g. several `rm`/delete commands, or shell writes), accepting the **first** command clears the neo-tree markers for **all** of them, and the remaining commands stay unmarked.

Surfaces often with OpenCode (and any agent that emits multiple shell commands as a batch), but it is **backend-agnostic and not Windows-specific**.

## Repro

1. Ask the agent to delete several files; the agent emits them as separate Bash commands.
2. Each command's PreToolUse marks its file(s) in neo-tree (`deleted`). All files appear marked.
3. Accept the first command.
4. **Observed:** every `deleted`/`bash_*` marker disappears, not just the accepted command's file. The remaining (still-pending) commands' markers are gone.
5. **Expected:** accepting one command clears only that command's file markers; the rest stay marked until accepted.

## Root cause

`lua/code-preview/post_tool.lua` (Bash branch):

```lua
if tool_name == "Bash" then
  changes.clear_by_statuses({ "deleted", "bash_modified", "bash_created" })
  ...
```

The Bash post-tool clears by **status, globally**, rather than by the specific files in *that* command. It was written to avoid clobbering `modified` markers from concurrent Edit/Write, but it doesn't account for concurrent **Bash** commands clobbering each other.

## Proposed fix

[HIDDEN]

Scoped clear, no global wipe; helps every backend.

## Scope
Small, standalone fix. Add a regression spec (two Bash deletes pending â accept first â only its marker clears).

+    -- Clear only THIS command's files, not every bash-owned marker: a global
+    -- status sweep wiped the still-pending markers of concurrent Bash commands
+    -- (issue #83). Detection is deterministic, so re-running it on the post
+    -- payload yields exactly the paths pre_tool marked â mirroring how the
+    -- ApplyPatch branch closes specific files via patch_paths. This also keeps
+    -- concurrent Edit/Write `modified`/`created` markers untouched, since those
+    -- paths never appear in a shell command's detection.
+    local cmd = input.tool_input and input.tool_input.command or ""
+    local detected = shell_detect.detect(cmd, input.cwd or "")
+    for _, p in ipairs(detected.rm_paths)    do changes.clear(p) end

problem_statement:
Propagate cancellation token instead of defining cancelAfter
**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'd like to reuse a cancellation token instead of defining the [cancelAfter](https://github.com/CaptnCodr/Fli?tab=readme-ov-file#builder-operations) information at the CE level.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

-

**Additional context**

-

### Additional contract requirements

## Cancellation token support for asynchronous execution

`Command.executeAsync` accepts an optional caller-provided
`System.Threading.CancellationToken` for both `ShellContext` and `ExecContext`:

```fsharp
open System.Threading

use cts = new CancellationTokenSource(1000)

cli {
    Shell BASH
    Command "some long-running command"
}
|> fun context -> Command.executeAsync (context, cts.Token)
```

When a token is supplied, asynchronous execution observes that token. If it is
cancelled before a long-running command completes, awaiting execution ends with
cancellation rather than a successful command result. Implementations may
surface this as `OperationCanceledException` (including derived cancellation
exceptions) or as an `AggregateException` containing only cancellation
exceptions.

A caller-provided token takes precedence over a `CancelAfter` value configured
on the context. Calling `Command.executeAsync` with only the context remains
supported and continues to use the context's existing cancellation behavior.

diff --git a/src/Fli.Tests/ExecContext/ExecCommandExecuteUnixTests.fs b/src/Fli.Tests/ExecContext/ExecCommandExecuteUnixTests.fs
index 8401b00..41be5b8 100644
--- a/src/Fli.Tests/ExecContext/ExecCommandExecuteUnixTests.fs
+++ b/src/Fli.Tests/ExecContext/ExecCommandExecuteUnixTests.fs
@@ -5,6 +5,8 @@ open FsUnit
 open Fli
 open System
 open System.Text
+open System.Diagnostics
+open System.Threading
 
 [<Test>]
 [<Platform("Linux,Unix,MacOsX")>]
@@ -104,3 +106,103 @@ let ``Testing input on unix systems`` () =
     |> Command.execute
     |> Output.toText
     |> should equal "{"
+
+let private isCancellationExn (ex: exn) =
+    match ex with
+    | :? OperationCanceledException -> true
+    | :? AggregateException as agg when
+        agg.InnerExceptions
+        |> Seq.forall (fun ie ->
+            match box ie with
+            | :? OperationCanceledException -> true
+            | _ -> false)
+        ->
+        true
+    | _ -> false
+
+[<Test>]
+[<Platform("Linux,Unix,MacOsX")>]
+let ``Executing program async with CancellationToken`` () =
+    async {
+        use cts = new CancellationTokenSource(1000)
+
+        let stopwatch = new Stopwatch()
+        stopwatch.Start()
+
+        let! wasCancelled =
+            async {
+                try
+                    let! _ =
+                        cli {
+                            Exec "sleep"
+                            Arguments "5"
+                        }
+                        |> fun c -> Command.executeAsync (c, cts.Token)
+
+                    return false
+                with e when isCancellationExn e -> return true
+            }
+
+        stopwatch.Stop()
+        wasCancelled |> should be True
+        stopwatch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds |> should be (greaterThanOrEqualTo 0.9)
+        stopwatch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds |> should be (lessThan 3.0)
+    }
+
+[<Test>]
+[<Platform("Linux,Unix,MacOsX")>]
+let ``Executing program async CancellationToken takes precedence over CancelAfter`` () =
+    async {
+        use cts = new CancellationTokenSource(3000)
+
+        let stopwatch = new Stopwatch()
+        stopwatch.Start()
+
+        let! wasCancelled =
+            async {
+                try
+                    let! _ =
+                        cli {
+                            Exec "sleep"
+                            Arguments "30"
+                            CancelAfter 500
+                        }
+                        |> fun c -> Command.executeAsync (c, cts.Token)
+
+                    return false
+                with e when isCancellationExn e -> return true

### Additional contract requirements

The chat widget supports two window layouts, selectable through the
user configuration under the `windows` section:

- The layout is controlled by setting `windows.position` to `"right"`
  or `"bottom"`. The default value is `"right"`.
- The default layout is the pre-existing vertical sidebar: when no
  layout option is configured, the widget keeps its previous behavior —
  the chat window opens as a sidebar next to the current window, and
  the prompt input plus the dynamic panels (code, referenced files,
  todos) stack vertically with it.
- Enabling the horizontal layout opens the widget as a bottom panel
  docked below the editor: the chat panel occupies the left side of the
  widget area, and the prompt input plus the dynamic panels (code,
  referenced files, todos) stack in a column to the right of the chat
  panel. Dynamic panels appear only while their buffers have content
  and disappear again when emptied.

Both layouts apply to the `show`/`hide` toggle commands and to the
automatic window management (opening, resizing, and closing of dynamic
panels) documented in the README.

Layout sizing:

- `windows.height` controls the panel height used by the horizontal
  layout. The default is `"30%"`.
- `windows.width` continues to control the sidebar width in the default
  vertical layout. Its default stays `"40%"`.

Both sizing settings accept the same value shapes: a percentage string
(e.g. `"40%"`), a decimal fraction between 0 and 1 (e.g. `0.4`), or an
absolute cell count (e.g. `40`). Any other value is invalid and falls
back to the documented default proportion for that dimension.

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..17e37b36
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lua/agentic/ui/widget_layout.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,467 @@
+local Config = require("agentic.config")
+local BufHelpers = require("agentic.utils.buf_helpers")
+local WindowDecoration = require("agentic.ui.window_decoration")
+local Logger = require("agentic.utils.logger")
+
+--- @class agentic.ui.WidgetLayout.Params
+--- @field tab_page_id integer
+--- @field buf_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.BufNrs
+--- @field win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+--- @field focus_prompt? boolean
+
+--- @class agentic.ui.WidgetLayout
+local WidgetLayout = {}
+
+local function get_layout_state(tab_page_id)
+    if
+        not tab_page_id
+        or not vim.api.nvim_tabpage_is_valid(tab_page_id)
+        or not vim.t[tab_page_id]
+    then
+        return nil
+    end
+    local layout_state = vim.t[tab_page_id].agentic_layout_state
+    return layout_state
+end
+
+local function set_layout_state(tab_page_id, position)
+    if
+        not tab_page_id
+        or not vim.api.nvim_tabpage_is_valid(tab_page_id)
+        or not vim.t[tab_page_id]
+    then
+        return
+    end
+    vim.t[tab_page_id].agentic_layout_state = { position = position }
+end
+
+--- @param tab_page_id integer
+--- @return boolean
+function WidgetLayout.needs_rebuild(tab_page_id)
+    local state = get_layout_state(tab_page_id)
+    if not state then
+        return false
+    end
+    return state.position ~= Config.windows.position
+end
+
+--- @param size number|string
+--- @param max_dimension integer
+--- @param default_percentage number
+--- @return integer
+local function calculate_dimension(size, max_dimension, default_percentage)
+    local is_percentage_string = type(size) == "string"
+        and string.sub(size, -1) == "%"
+    local value
+    local is_percentage
+
+    if is_percentage_string then
+        local value_num = tonumber(string.sub(size, 1, #size - 1))
+        if value_num then
+            value = value_num / 100
+            is_percentage = true
+        end
+    else
+        value = tonumber(size)
+        if value then
+            is_percentage = value > 0 and value < 1
+        end
+    end
+
+    if not value then
+        value = default_percentage
+        is_percentage = true
+    end
+
+    if is_percentage then
+        return math.max(1, math.floor(max_dimension * value))
+    end
+
+    return math.max(1, math.floor(value))
+end
+
+--- @param size number|string
+--- @return integer
+function WidgetLayout.calculate_width(size)
+    return calculate_dimension(size, vim.o.columns, 0.4)
+end
+
+--- @param size number|string
+--- @return integer
+function WidgetLayout.calculate_height(size)
+    return calculate_dimension(size, vim.o.lines, 0.3)
+end
+
+--- @param bufnr integer
+--- @param max_height integer
+--- @return integer
+local function calculate_dynamic_height(bufnr, max_height)
+    max_height = math.max(1, max_height)
+    local line_count = vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(bufnr)
+    return math.min(line_count + 1, max_height)
+end
+
+--- @param position "right"|"bottom"
+--- @return table<string, any>
+local function get_chat_window_opts(position)
+    --- @type table<string, any>
+    local win_opts = {
+        scrolloff = 4,
+    }
+
+    if position == "bottom" then
+        win_opts.winfixheight = true
+    else
+        win_opts.winfixheight = false
+    end
+
+    return win_opts
+end
+
+--- @param bufnr integer
+--- @param enter boolean
+--- @param opts vim.api.keyset.win_config
+--- @param window_name agentic.ui.ChatWidget.PanelNames
+--- @param win_opts table<string, any>
+--- @return integer
+local function open_win(bufnr, enter, opts, window_name, win_opts)
+    --- @type vim.api.keyset.win_config
+    local default_opts = {
+        split = "right",
+        win = -1,
+        noautocmd = true,
+        style = "minimal",
+    }
+
+    local config = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", default_opts, opts)
+
+    local winid = vim.api.nvim_open_win(bufnr, enter, config)
+
+    local window_config = Config.windows[window_name] or {}
+    local config_win_opts = window_config.win_opts or {}
+
+    local merged_win_opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", {
+        wrap = true,
+        linebreak = true,
+        winfixbuf = true,
+        winfixheight = true,
+    }, win_opts or {}, config_win_opts)
+
+    for name, value in pairs(merged_win_opts) do
+        vim.api.nvim_set_option_value(name, value, { win = winid })
+    end
+
+    return winid
+end
+
+--- @param win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+--- @param panel_name string
+--- @param bufnr integer
+--- @param enter boolean
+--- @param open_opts vim.api.keyset.win_config
+--- @param win_opts table<string, any>
+--- @return integer
+local function get_or_create_window(
+    win_nrs,
+    panel_name,
+    bufnr,
+    enter,
+    open_opts,
+    win_opts
+)
+    local cached_winid = win_nrs[panel_name]
+    if cached_winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(cached_winid) then
+        return cached_winid
+    end
+
+    local new_winid =
+        open_win(bufnr, enter, open_opts, panel_name, win_opts or {})
+    win_nrs[panel_name] = new_winid
+    WindowDecoration.render_header(bufnr, panel_name)
+    return new_winid
+end
+
+--- @param buf_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.BufNrs
+--- @param win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+--- @param window_name agentic.ui.ChatWidget.PanelNames
+--- @param open_win_opts vim.api.keyset.win_config
+--- @param max_height integer
+--- @param should_display boolean|nil
+local function open_or_resize_dynamic_window(
+    buf_nrs,
+    win_nrs,
+    window_name,
+    open_win_opts,
+    max_height,
+    should_display
+)
+    if should_display == nil then
+        should_display = true
+    end
+
+    local bufnr = buf_nrs[window_name]
+    local winid = win_nrs[window_name]
+
+    if not should_display then
+        if winid then
+            pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, winid, true)
+        end
+        win_nrs[window_name] = nil
+        return
+    end
+
+    if BufHelpers.is_buffer_empty(bufnr) then
+        if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+            pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, winid, true)
+        end
+        win_nrs[window_name] = nil
+        return
+    end
+
+    local height = calculate_dynamic_height(bufnr, max_height)
+
+    if not winid or not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+        open_win_opts.height = height
+        win_nrs[window_name] =
+            open_win(bufnr, false, open_win_opts, window_name, {})
+        WindowDecoration.render_header(bufnr, window_name)
+    else
+        vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(winid, { height = height })
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param params agentic.ui.WidgetLayout.Params
+local function show_right_layout(params)
+    local should_focus = (
+        params.focus_prompt == nil and true or params.focus_prompt
+    ) == true
+
+    get_or_create_window(params.win_nrs, "chat", params.buf_nrs.chat, false, {
+        width = WidgetLayout.calculate_width(Config.windows.width),
+    }, get_chat_window_opts("right"))
+
+    get_or_create_window(
+        params.win_nrs,
+        "input",
+        params.buf_nrs.input,
+        should_focus,
+        {
+            win = params.win_nrs.chat,
+            split = "below",
+            height = Config.windows.input.height,
+            fixed = true,
+        },
+        {}
+    )
+
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "code", {
+        win = params.win_nrs.chat,
+        split = "below",
+    }, Config.windows.code.max_height)
+
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "files", {
+        win = params.win_nrs.input,
+        split = "above",
+    }, Config.windows.files.max_height)
+
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "todos", {
+        win = params.win_nrs.chat,
+        split = "below",
+    }, Config.windows.todos.max_height, Config.windows.todos.display)
+
+    if should_focus then
+        local winid = params.win_nrs.input
+        vim.schedule(function()
+            if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+                local target_tabpage = vim.api.nvim_win_get_tabpage(winid)
+                local current_tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+                if target_tabpage == current_tabpage then
+                    vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(winid)
+                    BufHelpers.start_insert_on_last_char()
+                end
+            end
+        end)
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param params agentic.ui.WidgetLayout.Params
+local function show_bottom_layout(params)
+    local should_focus = (
+        params.focus_prompt == nil and true or params.focus_prompt
+    ) == true
+
+    get_or_create_window(params.win_nrs, "chat", params.buf_nrs.chat, false, {
+        split = "below",
+        win = -1,
+        height = WidgetLayout.calculate_height(Config.windows.height),
+    }, get_chat_window_opts("bottom"))
+
+    local chat_width = vim.api.nvim_win_get_width(params.win_nrs.chat)
+    local ratio = tonumber(Config.windows.stack_width_ratio) or 0.4
+    local raw_width = math.floor(chat_width * ratio)
+    local stack_width = math.max(1, math.min(raw_width, chat_width - 1))
+
+    get_or_create_window(
+        params.win_nrs,
+        "input",
+        params.buf_nrs.input,
+        should_focus,
+        {
+            win = params.win_nrs.chat,
+            split = "right",
+            width = stack_width,
+            fixed = true,
+        },
+        {}
+    )
+
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "code", {
+        win = params.win_nrs.input,
+        split = "below",
+    }, Config.windows.code.max_height)
+
+    local ref_win = params.win_nrs.code or params.win_nrs.input
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "files", {
+        win = ref_win,
+        split = "below",
+    }, Config.windows.files.max_height)
+
+    ref_win = params.win_nrs.files
+        or params.win_nrs.code
+        or params.win_nrs.input
+    open_or_resize_dynamic_window(params.buf_nrs, params.win_nrs, "todos", {
+        win = ref_win,
+        split = "below",
+    }, Config.windows.todos.max_height, Config.windows.todos.display)
+
+    if should_focus then
+        local winid = params.win_nrs.input
+        vim.schedule(function()
+            if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+                local target_tabpage = vim.api.nvim_win_get_tabpage(winid)
+                local current_tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+                if target_tabpage == current_tabpage then
+                    vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(winid)
+                    BufHelpers.start_insert_on_last_char()
+                end
+            end
+        end)
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param params agentic.ui.WidgetLayout.Params
+function WidgetLayout.open(params)
+    if
+        not params.tab_page_id
+        or not vim.api.nvim_tabpage_is_valid(params.tab_page_id)
+    then
+        Logger.notify(
+            "Invalid tab_page_id in WidgetLayout.open: "
+                .. tostring(params.tab_page_id),
+            vim.log.levels.ERROR
+        )
+        return
+    end
+
+    local current_position = Config.windows.position
+    local saved_tabpage = vim.api.nvim_get_current_tabpage()
+    local is_same_tabpage = saved_tabpage == params.tab_page_id
+
+    if not is_same_tabpage then
+        vim.api.nvim_set_current_tabpage(params.tab_page_id)
+    end
+
+    local layout_fns = {
+        right = show_right_layout,
+        bottom = show_bottom_layout,
+    }
+    local layout_fn = layout_fns[current_position]
+
+    local success
+    if layout_fn then
+        local ok, err = pcall(layout_fn, params)
+        if not ok then
+            Logger.notify(
+                string.format(
+                    "Failed to show %s layout (tab: %d): %s",
+                    current_position,
+                    params.tab_page_id,
+                    tostring(err)
+                ),
+                vim.log.levels.ERROR
+            )
+        end
+        success = ok
+    else
+        Logger.notify(
+            "Invalid windows.position config: "
+                .. tostring(Config.windows.position),
+            vim.log.levels.ERROR
+        )
+        success = false
+    end
+
+    if not is_same_tabpage then
+        vim.api.nvim_set_current_tabpage(saved_tabpage)
+    end
+
+    if success then
+        set_layout_state(params.tab_page_id, current_position)
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+function WidgetLayout.close(win_nrs)
+    for name, winid in pairs(win_nrs) do
+        win_nrs[name] = nil
+        local ok = pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, winid, true)
+        if not ok then
+            Logger.debug(
+                string.format(
+                    "Failed to close window '%s' with id: %d",
+                    name,
+                    winid
+                )
+            )
+        end
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param buf_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.BufNrs
+--- @param win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+--- @param window_name agentic.ui.ChatWidget.PanelNames
+function WidgetLayout.resize_dynamic_window(buf_nrs, win_nrs, window_name)
+    local bufnr = buf_nrs[window_name]
+    local winid = win_nrs[window_name]
+
+    if BufHelpers.is_buffer_empty(bufnr) then
+        if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+            vim.api.nvim_win_close(winid, true)
+        end
+        win_nrs[window_name] = nil
+        return
+    end
+
+    if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+        local window_config = Config.windows[window_name] or {}
+        local max_height = window_config.max_height or 10
+
+        local new_height = calculate_dynamic_height(bufnr, max_height)
+
+        vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(winid, {
+            height = new_height,
+        })
+    end
+end
+
+--- @param win_nrs agentic.ui.ChatWidget.WinNrs
+--- @param window_name agentic.ui.ChatWidget.PanelNames
+function WidgetLayout.close_optional_window(win_nrs, window_name)
+    local winid = win_nrs[window_name]
+    if winid and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(winid) then
+        pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_close, winid, true)
+    end
+    win_nrs[window_name] = nil
+end
+
+return WidgetLayout

+--- Integration tests for the documented window layout configuration.
+--- These tests exercise the public, user-observable contract only:
+--- the plugin exposes an optional window layout/position setting that
+--- selects between the default vertical sidebar and a horizontal
+--- (stacked below the editor) arrangement, plus sizing settings that
+--- accept percentage strings, decimal fractions, and absolute counts.

+-- before their own declarations below.
