+    -- Actual screen height of the main screen grid. Captured lazily:
+    -- while still headless it matches vim.o.lines; if the acceptance
+    -- environment ever attaches a bigger UI, we remember the maximum
+    -- real screen size seen so fallbacks stay proportional to the
+    -- actual screen rather than the previous vim.o.lines value.
+    local screen_lines = vim.o.lines
+    local function observe_screen_lines()
+        for _, ui in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_uis()) do
+            if ui.height and ui.height > screen_lines then
+                screen_lines = ui.height
+            end
+        end
+        if vim.o.lines > screen_lines then
+            screen_lines = vim.o.lines
+        end
+        return screen_lines
+    end
+
+    before_each(function()
+        saved_columns = vim.o.columns
+        saved_lines = vim.o.lines
+        saved_windows = vim.deepcopy(Config.windows)
+        observe_screen_lines()
+    end)
+
+    after_each(function()
+        vim.o.columns = saved_columns
+        vim.o.lines = saved_lines
+        Config.windows = saved_windows
+        local AgentInstance = require("agentic.acp.agent_instance")
+        session = nil
+        AgentInstance._instances = {}
+    end)
+
+    local on_submit_spy
+
+    local function new_widget()
+        on_submit_spy = spy.new(function() end)
+        widget =
+            ChatWidget:new(tab_page_id, on_submit_spy --[[@as function]])
+        return widget
+    end
+
+    -- Restores the documented default. The default position is
+    -- materialized in the shipped default config, so "unset" for the
+    -- user corresponds to `windows.position = "right"`.

+    end
+
+    --- @param bufnr integer

+    --- and todos containers are captured so the tests can notify the
+    --- session exactly the way the real agent providers do.

+--- Reporter support for headless CI runs of mini.test.
+--- Wraps the stock stdout reporter and additionally prints one
+--- machine-readable line per executed test case:
+---   "Success || <full test name>" / "Fail || <full test name>" / "Skip || <full test name>"
+local M = {}
+
+--- @param file string Test file to execute (relative to cwd)
+function M.run_file(file)
+    if not file or file == "" then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: No file specified\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        return
+    end
+
+    if not vim.uv.fs_stat(file) then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: File not found: " .. file .. "\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+        return
+    end
+
+    local ok, err = pcall(function()
+        local MiniTest = require("mini.test")
+        local stdout_reporter = MiniTest.gen_reporter.stdout({
+            quit_on_finish = false,
+        })
+
+        local all_cases
+        local reporter = {
+            start = function(cases)
+                all_cases = cases
+                stdout_reporter.start(cases)
+            end,
+            update = function(case_num)
+                stdout_reporter.update(case_num)
+                local case = all_cases[case_num]
+                if type(case.exec) ~= "table" then
+                    return
+                end
+                local state = case.exec.state or ""
+                local status
+                if state:match("^Pass") then
+                    status = (#case.exec.notes > 0) and "Skip" or "Success"
+                elseif state:match("^Fail") then
+                    status = "Fail"
+                else
+                    return
+                end
+                local name = table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+                io.stdout:write(
+                    string.format("\n%s || %s\n", status, name)
+                )
+                io.flush()
+            end,
+            finish = function()
+                stdout_reporter.finish()
+                local has_fails = false
+                for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+                    if
+                        type(case.exec) == "table"
+                        and type(case.exec.state) == "string"
+                        and case.exec.state:match("^Fail")
+                    then
+                        has_fails = true
+                        break
+                    end
+                end
+                vim.cmd(has_fails and "cquit 1" or "qall!")
+            end,
+        }
+
+        MiniTest.run_file(file, { execute = { reporter = reporter } })
+    end)
+
+    if not ok then
+        io.stderr:write("Error: " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
+        vim.cmd("cquit 1")
+    end
+end
+
+return M

problem_statement:
Endpoints to edit staged participant groups
The backend now has the notion of "staged" participant groups: sets of participants with assigned master devices _before_ they are deployed. https://github.com/cph-cachet/carp.core-kotlin/issues/255

But, we are still missing endpoints to add/remove/change device assignments in the application service.

### Additional contract requirements

- The recruitment application service exposes an editable representation for staged participant groups, `ParticipantGroupRepresentation`, under `dk.cachet.carp.studies.application.users`. A participant group representation holds an optional `name` (nullable), supplied when constructing it; a default representation with a `null` name exists for groups without an explicit name.
- Group status (`ParticipantGroupStatus`), whether the group is still staged or has been invited to participate, exposes the group's current representation through a `representation` property. The representation a group was created with is retained when the group transitions to a non-staged (deployment) status and remains observable in the status returned by that transition and in the status of any subsequent retrieval through the application service.
- When creating a staged participant group through the application service, a representation may be supplied; when none is supplied, the default representation applies. The default representation is also available as `ParticipantGroupRepresentation.Default` (a companion object property), which is a representation whose `name` is `null`, equal to `ParticipantGroupRepresentation( null )`.
- The application service allows updating an existing staged participant group (`updateParticipantGroup` on `RecruitmentService`): role assignments may be changed to add or remove participants (devices are assigned through role assignments), and the group representation may be changed, independently of each other. This includes changing the group representation to one with an explicit name and changing it back to one without an explicit name. The update takes effect in the returned group status and in the group status of any subsequent retrieval through the application service.
- Passing neither updated role assignments nor an updated representation to the group update operation is a no-op and returns the group unchanged.
- Group update validates its inputs: it fails with an `IllegalArgumentException` when the referenced participant group does not exist, when assigned participants are not participants of the study the group belongs to, or when assigned participant roles are not part of the study's locked-in protocol.

The default representation is also available as `ParticipantGroupRepresentation.Default` (a companion object property), which is a representation whose `name` is `null`, equal to `ParticipantGroupRepresentation( null )`.
- The application service allows updating an existing staged participant group (`updateParticipantGroup` on `RecruitmentService`): role assignments may be changed to add or remove participants (devices are assigned through role assignments), and the group representation may be changed, independently of each other. This includes changing the group representation to one with an explicit name and changing it back to one without an explicit name. The update takes effect in the returned group status and in the group status of any subsequent retrieval through the application service.
- Passing neither updated role assignments nor an updated representation to the group update operation is a no-op and returns the group unchanged.
- Group update validates its inputs: it fails with an `IllegalArgumentException` when the referenced participant group does not exist, when assigned participants are not participants of the study the group belongs to, or when assigned participant roles are not part of the study's locked-in protocol.

+    def pgTest = targets.jvm.compilations.create( 'participantGroupTest' )

+    // src/jvmParticipantGroupTest (the default source set of the created compilation).
+    targets.jvm.compilations.test.defaultSourceSet.kotlin.setSrcDirs( [ ] )

+/**
+ * Run a suspending block to completion on the current thread, without depending on kotlinx-coroutines.
+ */
+private fun runSync( block: suspend () -> Unit )
+{
+    var outcome: Result<Unit>? = null
+    val coroutine = block.createCoroutineUnintercepted(
+        object : Continuation<Unit>
+        {
+            override val context = EmptyCoroutineContext
+            override fun resumeWith( result: Result<Unit> ) { outcome = result }
+        }
+    )
+    coroutine.resumeWith( Result.success( Unit ) )
+    checkNotNull( outcome ) { "The test body suspended; it cannot be completed synchronously." }.getOrThrow()
+}

+ * they remain mutable objects. Loading a pristine copy from a snapshot additionally serves to avoid
+ * `ConcurrentModificationException`s when event handlers update the same instance being published.
+ */
+private fun pristineCopy( recruitment: Recruitment ): Recruitment =
+    Recruitment.fromSnapshot( recruitment.getSnapshot() )

+    override suspend fun updateRecruitment( recruitment: Recruitment )

+    }

+            catch ( e: ClassNotFoundException )
+            {
+                fail( "ParticipantGroupStatus should expose an editable group `representation`." )
+            }
+
+        // A participant group representation carries an optional (nullable) name.
+        val nameProperty = representationClass.memberProperties.singleOrNull { it.name == "name" }
+        assertNotNull( nameProperty, "The participant group representation should carry a `name`." )
+        val nameConstructor = representationClass.constructors.single { constructor ->
+            constructor.parameters.size == 1 && constructor.parameters.single().name == "name"
+        }
+        val nameParameter = nameConstructor.parameters.single()
+        val representation = nameConstructor.callBy( mapOf( nameParameter to "Test Group" ) )
+        assertEquals( "Test Group", nameProperty.getter.call( representation ) )
+
+        // A representation can be created without an explicit name, in which case its name is null,
+        // for participant groups without an explicit name.
+        val unnamed = nameConstructor.callBy( mapOf( nameParameter to null ) )
+        assertNull( nameProperty.getter.call( unnamed ) )
+
+        // The representation of a staged participant group is exposed through its status,
+        // so it can be retrieved and changed through the application service.
+        val hasRepresentationProperty =
+            ParticipantGroupStatus::class.members
+                .filterIsInstance<KProperty1<*, *>>()
+                .any { it.name == "representation" && it.returnType.classifier == representationClass }
+        assertTrue(
+            hasRepresentationProperty,
+            "ParticipantGroupStatus should expose the editable group `representation`."
+        )
+    }

+    @Test
+    fun createParticipantGroup_sets_the_given_representation() = runSync {

+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val participant =
+            sut.recruitmentService.addParticipant( studyId, dk.cachet.carp.common.application.EmailAddress( "participant@test.com" ) )
+        val groupId = UUID.randomUUID()
+
+        // A group created without an explicit representation gets the default representation.
+        val defaultStatus = sut.recruitmentService.createParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( participant.id, AssignedTo.All ) ),
+            studyId
+        )
+
+        // A group created with an explicit representation exposes it through its status.
+        val namedRepresentation = ParticipantGroupRepresentation( "Named group" )
+        val namedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.createParticipantGroup(
+            UUID.randomUUID(),
+            setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( participant.id, AssignedTo.All ) ),
+            studyId,
+            namedRepresentation
+        )
+
+        assertTrue( defaultStatus is ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged )
+        assertNull( defaultStatus.representation.name )
+        assertTrue( namedStatus is ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged )
+        assertEquals( namedRepresentation, namedStatus.representation )
+    }

+    @Test
+    fun participant_group_representation_exposes_a_default() = runSync {
+        val sut = createSUT()
+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val groupId = createStagedGroup( sut, studyId )
+
+        // The default representation for participant groups without an explicit name
+        // has a null name and is applied to groups created without an explicit representation.
+        assertNull( ParticipantGroupRepresentation.Default.name )
+        assertEquals( ParticipantGroupRepresentation( null ), ParticipantGroupRepresentation.Default )

+        // A group created without an explicit representation exposes the default representation.

+            sut.recruitmentService.addParticipant( studyId, dk.cachet.carp.common.application.EmailAddress( "participant@test.com" ) )

+            setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( participant.id, AssignedTo.All ) ),

+            representation
+        )

+        // Transitioning the group to a non-staged (deployment) status retains the representation.
+        val invitedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.inviteParticipantGroup( groupId )
+        assertFalse( invitedStatus is ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged )
+        assertEquals( representation, invitedStatus.representation )

+        // The representation is also retained on subsequent retrieval.

+    @Test
+    fun updateParticipantGroup_succeeds_before_invite() = runSync {
+        val sut = createSUT()
+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val groupId = createStagedGroup( sut, studyId )
+
+        // Add a second participant to the study so it can be added to the staged group.
+        val addedParticipant =
+            sut.recruitmentService.addParticipant( studyId, dk.cachet.carp.common.application.EmailAddress( "added@test.com" ) )
+        val updatedAssignments = setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( addedParticipant.id, AssignedTo.All ) )
+        val updatedRepresentation = ParticipantGroupRepresentation( "Updated group" )
+
+        // Change the participants assigned to the group, remove the original participant,
+        // and change the group representation.
+        val updatedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            updatedAssignments,
+            updatedRepresentation
+        )
+
+        val expectedStatus = ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged(
+            id = groupId,
+            participants = setOf( addedParticipant ),
+            assignedParticipantRoles = updatedAssignments,
+            representation = updatedRepresentation
+        )
+        assertEquals( expectedStatus, updatedStatus )
+        assertEquals( updatedStatus, sut.recruitmentService.getParticipantGroupStatusList( studyId )
+            .single { it.id == groupId } )
+    }

+    @Test
+    fun updateParticipantGroup_can_only_change_the_group_representation() = runSync {
+        val sut = createSUT()
+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val groupId = createStagedGroup( sut, studyId )
+        val initialStatus = sut.recruitmentService.getParticipantGroupStatusList( studyId )
+            .single { it.id == groupId }
+
+        val updatedRepresentation = ParticipantGroupRepresentation( "New name" )
+        val updatedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            null,
+            updatedRepresentation
+        )
+
+        assertTrue( updatedStatus is ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged )
+        assertEquals( updatedRepresentation, updatedStatus.representation )
+
+        // The participants of the group remain unchanged.
+        assertEquals( initialStatus.participants, updatedStatus.participants )
+        assertEquals( initialStatus.assignedParticipantRoles, updatedStatus.assignedParticipantRoles )
+
+        // The update persists and is observable on subsequent retrieval.
+        assertEquals( updatedStatus, sut.recruitmentService.getParticipantGroupStatusList( studyId )
+            .single { it.id == groupId } )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun updateParticipantGroup_can_only_change_the_role_assignments() = runSync {
+        val sut = createSUT()
+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val groupId = createStagedGroup( sut, studyId )
+        val initialStatus = sut.recruitmentService.getParticipantGroupStatusList( studyId )
+            .single { it.id == groupId }
+
+        // Add a second participant to the study so the group can gain a member,
+        // while the original participant is removed from the group.
+        val addedParticipant =
+            sut.recruitmentService.addParticipant( studyId, dk.cachet.carp.common.application.EmailAddress( "added@test.com" ) )
+        val updatedAssignments = setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( addedParticipant.id, AssignedTo.All ) )
+
+        // Only the role assignments change; no updated representation is passed.
+        val updatedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            updatedAssignments,
+            null
+        )
+
+        assertTrue( updatedStatus is ParticipantGroupStatus.Staged )
+        assertEquals( updatedAssignments, updatedStatus.assignedParticipantRoles )
+
+        // The removed participant is no longer part of the group.
+        assertEquals( setOf( addedParticipant ), updatedStatus.participants )
+
+        // The group representation remains unchanged.
+        assertEquals( initialStatus.representation, updatedStatus.representation )
+
+        // The update is reflected both in the returned status and on subsequent retrieval.
+        val retrievedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.getParticipantGroupStatusList( studyId )
+            .single { it.id == groupId }
+        assertEquals( updatedStatus, retrievedStatus )
+
+        // One of the previously assigned participants can still be added back on a subsequent update.
+        val reparticipant = initialStatus.participants.single()
+        val readdAssignments = setOf( AssignedParticipantRoles( reparticipant.id, AssignedTo.All ) )
+        val readdedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            readdAssignments,
+            null
+        )
+        assertEquals( setOf( reparticipant ), readdedStatus.participants )
+    }

+    @Test
+    fun updateParticipantGroup_can_remove_the_group_name() = runSync {
+        val sut = createSUT()
+        val (studyId, _) = createLiveStudy( sut )
+        val groupId = createStagedGroup( sut, studyId )
+
+        // Give the group an explicitly named representation.
+        val namedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            null,
+            ParticipantGroupRepresentation( "Group name" )
+        )
+        assertEquals( "Group name", namedStatus.representation.name )
+
+        // The representation can be changed back to one without an explicit name,
+        // independently of the participants assigned to the group.
+        val clearedStatus = sut.recruitmentService.updateParticipantGroup(
+            groupId,
+            null,
+            ParticipantGroupRepresentation( null )

+        assertNull( retrievedStatus.representation.name )
+
+        // The participants of the group remain unchanged.
+        assertEquals( namedStatus.participants, retrievedStatus.participants )
+        assertEquals( namedStatus.assignedParticipantRoles, retrievedStatus.assignedParticipantRoles )

problem_statement:
`CustomDeviceRegistration` drops `registrationCreatedOn` for unknown device registrations
`CustomDeviceRegistration` does not preserve `registrationCreatedOn` when deserializing unknown device registrations.

`DeviceRegistration` defines `registrationCreatedOn` as part of its serialized state, but `CustomDeviceRegistration.BaseMembers` only reads:

- deviceId
- deviceDisplayName
- additionalSpecifications (1.3)

Because of that, the wrapper [HIDDEN]

This is causing problem when calling endpoint [deviceDeployed](https://github.com/carp-dk/carp.sensing-flutter/issues/561), since `PrimaryDeviceDeployment.lastUpdatedOn` is calculated using `registrationCreatedOn`

problem_statement:
Safe usage of `zero_tangent` for `Ptr{T}`
see https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/pull/471#issuecomment-3929468112 

> 
> Importantly note that the below MWE shows that there is another issue beyond `pointerset`.
> 
> ```
> using Mooncake: build_rrule, value_and_gradient!!
> using Core.Intrinsics: pointerset, atomic_pointerset
> 
> f_pointerset = x -> begin
>     c_1 = [x]
>     c_2 = [x * 2.0]
>     p = [pointer(c_1)] 
>     pointerset(pointer(p), pointer(c_2), 1, 1)
>     unsafe_load(p[1])
> end
> 
> f_atomic_pointerset = x -> begin
>     c_1 = [x]
>     c_2 = [x * 2.0]
>     p = [pointer(c_1)]
>     atomic_pointerset(pointer(p), pointer(c_2), :monotonic)
>     unsafe_load(p[1])
> end
> 
> value_and_gradient!!(build_rrule(f_pointerset, 3.0), f_pointerset, 3.0)
> value_and_gradient!!(build_rrule(f_atomic_pointerset, 3.0), f_atomic_pointerset, 3.0)
> ```
> 
> 1. All handwritten rules that call `zero_tangent`  inside their definition will error out when any of the arguments contain or are pointers. (eg: `arrayset` [rule](https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/blob/9ab55b6f19d8636e8b001ba503201b7522371cd3/src/rules/array_legacy.jl#L460))
> 
> 2. Derived rules that use `@zero_adjoint` will fail when the function returns a pointer-containing value. Since `@zero_adjoint` calls `zero_fcodual` on the primal output internally (e.g. `Base.vect` in the [MWE](https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/pull/471#issuecomment-3927054658)).
> 
> 3. In general, direct usage of [zero_fcodual](https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/blob/9ab55b6f19d8636e8b001ba503201b7522371cd3/src/tangents/codual.jl#L94)/[zero_codual](https://github.com/chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl/blob/9ab55b6f19d8636e8b001ba503201b7522371cd3/src/tangents/codual.jl#L33) will fail for pointers.
> 
[HIDDEN]
> I have create an issue #999 to seperate it from the current Issue, PR.

Will add more details as #471 progresses.

### Additional contract requirements

Additional requirements implied by the problem statement:

- Calling `zero_tangent(x)` with a single argument, where `x` is a `Ptr`, must throw an
  `ArgumentError` whose message directs the caller to the two-argument form
  `zero_tangent(primal, fdata)`.

- `zero_codual(p)` and `zero_fcodual(p)` must work for `p::Ptr` values; they must not
  error. In particular:
  - `zero_codual(p)` returns a `CoDual` whose primal is `p` and whose tangent has type
    `tangent_type(typeof(p))`.
  - `zero_fcodual(p)` returns a `CoDual` whose primal is `p` and whose fdata component
    has the type `fdata_type(tangent_type(typeof(p)))`.
  - No requirement is placed on the particular pointer value, initialisation state, or
    internal representation of the tangent or fdata components of those results.

- The two-argument form `zero_tangent(primal, fdata)` works when `primal` is a `Ptr`:
  given `fdata` of type `tangent_type(typeof(primal))`, it returns a tangent of type
  `tangent_type(typeof(primal))` (when the fdata already has the full tangent type, that
  same value is returned).

- A full tangent can be reconstructed from the fdata component of a `Ptr` tangent and
  `NoRData()` via `tangent(fdata, NoRData())`, yielding the fdata value itself.

- Reverse-mode differentiation via `value_and_gradient!!` supports functions whose
  intermediates involve pointer-valued storage operations:
  - arrays whose element type is a `Ptr` to floating-point data, written via
    `Base.arrayset` (and read back via `unsafe_load`), and
  - `Ptr`-to-`Ptr` storage written via `Core.Intrinsics.pointerset` or
    `Core.Intrinsics.atomic_pointerset` (and read back via `unsafe_load`).

  For such functions, differentiation runs to completion without throwing the error
  raised by single-argument `zero_tangent` on `Ptr` values, and produces the correct
  value and gradient.

problem_statement:
Use COARE3RoughnessParams for the ocean
Currently, we are using ConstantRoughnessParams for the ocean. It would be good to see if COARE3RoughnessParams improves the simulation.

A straightforward way to test how it works:
[HIDDEN]

A better solution:
Expose roughness_model in `FluxCalculator.compute_surface_fluxes!` so it can be passed as an argument for different component models.

### Additional contract requirements

# Roughness configuration for surface flux computations

When the coupler computes turbulent surface fluxes between a surface
component model and the atmosphere, the choice of aerodynamic roughness
parameterization affects the numerical values of the computed fluxes.

- Over ocean surfaces (i.e. for any component model whose surface is the
  ocean), the turbulent surface fluxes must be computed with the COARE 3.0
  roughness parameterization (`SurfaceFluxes.COARE3RoughnessParams` with its
  default parameter values). For the same surface state, COARE 3.0 roughness
  generally yields different momentum, sensible-heat, latent-heat and
  moisture fluxes than fixed roughness lengths, so the fluxes returned to an
  ocean component model must reflect the COARE 3.0 formulation.

- For all other surface component models (e.g. land and sea ice), the
  turbulent surface fluxes must be computed with constant roughness lengths
  (`SurfaceFluxes.ConstantRoughnessParams`), using the momentum and buoyancy
  roughness lengths supplied by the component model, unless the model
  explicitly selects a different roughness parameterization. This remains
  the default behavior for any surface component model that does not
  configure a roughness parameterization.

These requirements concern only the numerical behavior of the coupler's
surface-flux computation. They do not require any particular internal data
representation, cache layout, naming, or interface plumbing in the component
models or in the coupler.

Currently, we are using ConstantRoughnessParams for the ocean. It would be good to see if COARE3RoughnessParams improves the simulation.

A straightforward way to test how it works:
[HIDDEN]

A better solution:
Expose roughness_model in `FluxCalculator.compute_surface_fluxes!` so it can be passed as an argument for different component models.
contract_addendum:
# Roughness configuration for surface flux computations

When the coupler computes turbulent surface fluxes between a surface
component model and the atmosphere, the choice of aerodynamic roughness
parameterization affects the numerical values of the computed fluxes.

- Over ocean surfaces (i.e. for any component model whose surface is the
  ocean), the turbulent surface fluxes must be computed with the COARE 3.0
  roughness parameterization (`SurfaceFluxes.COARE3RoughnessParams` with its
  default parameter values). For the same surface state, COARE 3.0 roughness
  generally yields different momentum, sensible-heat, latent-heat and
  moisture fluxes than fixed roughness lengths, so the fluxes returned to an
  ocean component model must reflect the COARE 3.0 formulation.

- For all other surface component models (e.g. land and sea ice), the
  turbulent surface fluxes must be computed with constant roughness lengths
  (`SurfaceFluxes.ConstantRoughnessParams`), using the momentum and buoyancy
  roughness lengths supplied by the component model, unless the model
  explicitly selects a different roughness parameterization. This remains
  the default behavior for any surface component model that does not
  configure a roughness parameterization.

These requirements concern only the numerical behavior of the coupler's
surface-flux computation. They do not require any particular internal data
representation, cache layout, naming, or interface plumbing in the component
models or in the coupler.

+"""
+    get_field(sim::AbstractSurfaceSimulation, ::Val{:roughness_model})
+
+Return the roughness model to be used for surface flux calculations.
+Returns `:constant` by default. Ocean models should override this to return
+`:coare3` to use COARE3 roughness parameterization, which accounts for the
+dynamic response of ocean surface roughness to wind speed and wave state.
+The `:constant` roughness model uses fixed roughness lengths for momentum
+and buoyancy specified by the component model.
+
+This ensures COARE3 is applied over ocean surfaces where the area_fraction > 0,
+while land and sea ice surfaces use constant roughness parameterization.
+"""
+get_field(::AbstractSurfaceSimulation, ::Val{:roughness_model}) = :constant
+
 
 """
     get_field(target_space, sim, quantity)

+Interfacer.get_field(
+    sim::DefaultRoughnessSurface,
+    ::Union{Val{:surface_direct_albedo}, Val{:surface_diffuse_albedo}},
+) = sim.integrator.p.α
+Interfacer.get_field(sim::DefaultRoughnessSurface, ::Val{:emissivity}) =
+    eltype(sim.integrator.T)(1)
+
+FluxCalculator.update_turbulent_fluxes!(sim::DefaultRoughnessSurface, fields) =
+    nothing
+
+# Run `FluxCalculator.turbulent_fluxes!` for the given surface simulation
+# coupled to a minimal atmos simulation, and return the coupler fields.
+function compute_coupler_fluxes(sim, FT, boundary_space)
+    p = (;
+        z = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(10),
+        height_sfc = CC.Fields.zeros(boundary_space),
+        u = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(10),
+        v = CC.Fields.zeros(boundary_space),
+    )
+    integrator = (;
+        T = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(310),
+        q = CC.Fields.zeros(boundary_space),
+        ρ = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(1.2),
+        p = p,
+    )
+    atmos_sim = FluxTestAtmos((; FT = FT), integrator)
+
+    model_sims = (; atmos_sim, surf_sim = sim)
+
+    coupler_cache_names = Interfacer.default_coupler_fields()
+    append!(
+        coupler_cache_names,
+        [
+            :surface_direct_albedo,
+            :surface_diffuse_albedo,
+            :P_net,
+            :L_MO,
+            :ustar,
+            :buoyancy_flux,
+        ],
+    )
+    fields = Interfacer.init_coupler_fields(FT, coupler_cache_names, boundary_space)
+
+    # Import static, atmos and surface fields into the coupler
+    FieldExchanger.import_static_fields!(fields, model_sims)
+    FieldExchanger.import_atmos_fields!(fields, model_sims)
+    FieldExchanger.import_combined_surface_fields!(fields, model_sims)
+
+    # Compute the turbulent fluxes between the surface model and the atmos
+    thermo_params = TDP.ThermodynamicsParameters(FT)
+    FluxCalculator.turbulent_fluxes!(fields, model_sims, thermo_params)
+
+    return fields
+end
+
+# Independently compute the per-point fluxes expected for the coupler state
+# in `fields` when the given per-point surface flux configuration array is
+# used (the array is repeated to the number of exchange-grid points).
+# Returns a NamedTuple of plain vectors, in the same order as the underlying
+# field data (i.e. matching `vec(parent(field))`).
+#
+# The computation is done over plain arrays (the `parent` data of the coupler
+# fields), which mirrors the per-point computations in FluxCalculator.
+function expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config)
+    surface_fluxes_params =
+        SF.Parameters.SurfaceFluxesParameters(FT, SF.UniversalFunctions.BusingerParams)
+
+    ρ_sfc =
+        SF.surface_density.(
+            surface_fluxes_params,
+            fields.T_atmos,
+            fields.ρ_atmos,
+            T_sfc,
+            fields.height_int .- fields.height_sfc,
+            fields.q_tot_atmos,
+            0, # q_liq
+            0, # q_ice
+        )
+    q_sfc = CC.Fields.zeros(axes(fields))
+    q_sfc .= TD.q_vap_saturation.(thermo_params, T_sfc, ρ_sfc, 0, 0)
+
+    uv_int = tuple.(vec(parent(fields.u_int)), vec(parent(fields.v_int)))
+    fluxes =
+        FluxCalculator.get_surface_fluxes.(
+            surface_fluxes_params,
+            uv_int,
+            vec(parent(fields.T_atmos)),
+            vec(parent(fields.q_tot_atmos)),
+            vec(parent(fields.q_liq_atmos)),
+            vec(parent(fields.q_ice_atmos)),
+            vec(parent(fields.ρ_atmos)),
+            vec(parent(fields.height_int)),
+            Ref((FT(0), FT(0))), # uv_sfc
+            vec(parent(T_sfc)),
+            vec(parent(q_sfc)),
+            vec(parent(fields.height_sfc)),
+            0, # d
+            config,
+        )
+    return (;
+        F_turb_ρτxz = getproperty.(fluxes, :F_turb_ρτxz),
+        F_turb_ρτyz = getproperty.(fluxes, :F_turb_ρτyz),
+        F_lh = getproperty.(fluxes, :F_lh),
+        F_sh = getproperty.(fluxes, :F_sh),
+        F_turb_moisture = getproperty.(fluxes, :F_turb_moisture),
+    )
+end
+
+for FT in (Float32, Float64)
+    @testset "SlabOceanSimulation surface fluxes use COARE3 roughness for FT=$FT" begin
+        coupled_param_dict = CP.create_toml_dict(FT)
+        thermo_params = TDP.ThermodynamicsParameters(coupled_param_dict)
+
+        boundary_space = CC.CommonSpaces.CubedSphereSpace(
+            FT;
+            radius = coupled_param_dict["planet_radius"], # in meters
+            n_quad_points = 4,
+            h_elem = 4,
+        )
+
+        # Construct a slab ocean simulation using the keyword constructor
+        sim = SlabOceanSimulation(
+            FT;
+            tspan = (0.0, 1.0),
+            dt = 0.1,
+            saveat = [0.0, 1.0],
+            boundary_space = boundary_space,
+            coupled_param_dict = coupled_param_dict,
+            thermo_params = thermo_params,
+        )
+
+        # Compute the coupler fluxes between the slab ocean and the atmos
+        fields = compute_coupler_fluxes(sim, FT, boundary_space)
+
+        gustiness = FT(1) # hardcoded gustiness value used by the coupler
+        T_sfc = Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:surface_temperature))
+
+        # Independently compute the expected fluxes with the COARE3 roughness
+        # parameterization. The fluxes computed over the ocean must match
+        # these exactly.
+        config_coare3 = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.COARE3RoughnessParams{FT}(),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_coare3 = expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_coare3)
+
+        # For reference, compute the fluxes that the default (constant)
+        # roughness parameterization would give. COARE3 roughness gives
+        # different fluxes for these conditions, so comparing against both
+        # makes this test sensitive to which parameterization is used.
+        config_constant = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.ConstantRoughnessParams(
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_momentum)),
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_buoyancy)),
+                ),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_constant =
+            expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_constant)
+        @test !isapprox(fluxes_coare3.F_sh, fluxes_constant.F_sh; rtol = 1e-3)
+
+        # The slab ocean covers the entire exchange grid here (unit area
+        # fraction), so the coupler flux fields equal the per-point fluxes.
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτxz)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_ρτxz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτyz)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_ρτyz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_lh)) == fluxes_coare3.F_lh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_sh)) == fluxes_coare3.F_sh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_moisture)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_moisture
+
+        # The turbulent energy flux passed back to the slab ocean must also
+        # be computed with the COARE3 roughness parameterization.
+        @test vec(parent(sim.integrator.p.F_turb_energy)) ==
+              fluxes_coare3.F_lh .+ fluxes_coare3.F_sh
+    end
+
+    @testset "ocean representative surface fluxes use COARE3 roughness for FT=$FT" begin
+        boundary_space = CC.CommonSpaces.CubedSphereSpace(
+            FT;
+            radius = FT(6.371e6), # in meters
+            n_quad_points = 4,
+            h_elem = 4,
+        )
+
+        # A minimal ocean simulation: any component model whose surface is the
+        # ocean (not only SlabOceanSimulation) must receive fluxes computed
+        # with the COARE 3.0 roughness parameterization. The fixture declares
+        # the ocean roughness configuration used by concrete ocean components.
+        coare3_roughness_params =
+            CC.Fields.Field(SF.COARE3RoughnessParams{FT}, boundary_space)
+        coare3_roughness_params .= SF.COARE3RoughnessParams{FT}()
+        p = (;
+            z0m = FT(0.001),
+            z0b = FT(0.001),
+            α = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(0.06),
+            area_fraction = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space),
+            coare3_roughness_params,
+        )
+        integrator = (; T = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(300), p = p)
+        sim = FluxTestOcean(integrator)
+
+        # Compute the coupler fluxes between this ocean surface and the atmos
+        fields = compute_coupler_fluxes(sim, FT, boundary_space)
+
+        # The surface fluxes over an ocean surface must use the COARE 3.0
+        # roughness parameterization with its default parameter values.
+        gustiness = FT(1) # hardcoded gustiness value used by the coupler
+        thermo_params = TDP.ThermodynamicsParameters(FT)
+        T_sfc = Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:surface_temperature))
+        config_coare3 = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.COARE3RoughnessParams{FT}(),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_coare3 = expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_coare3)
+
+        # For reference, constant roughness built from the supplied roughness
+        # lengths would give different fluxes here, so this test is sensitive
+        # to which roughness parameterization the coupler uses.
+        config_constant = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.ConstantRoughnessParams(
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_momentum)),
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_buoyancy)),
+                ),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_constant =
+            expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_constant)
+        @test !isapprox(fluxes_coare3.F_sh, fluxes_constant.F_sh; rtol = 1e-3)
+
+        # This surface covers the entire exchange grid here (unit area
+        # fraction), so the coupler flux fields equal the per-point fluxes.
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτxz)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_ρτxz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτyz)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_ρτyz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_lh)) == fluxes_coare3.F_lh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_sh)) == fluxes_coare3.F_sh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_moisture)) == fluxes_coare3.F_turb_moisture
+    end
+
+    @testset "default surface fluxes use constant roughness for FT=$FT" begin
+        boundary_space = CC.CommonSpaces.CubedSphereSpace(
+            FT;
+            radius = FT(6.371e6), # in meters
+            n_quad_points = 4,
+            h_elem = 4,
+        )
+
+        # A surface simulation that does not configure a roughness model, so
+        # that the coupler's default roughness configuration is used.
+        p = (;
+            z0m = FT(0.01),
+            z0b = FT(0.01),
+            α = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(0.5),
+            area_fraction = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space),
+        )
+        integrator = (; T = CC.Fields.ones(boundary_space) .* FT(300), p = p)
+        sim = DefaultRoughnessSurface(integrator)
+
+        # Compute the coupler fluxes between this surface and the atmos
+        fields = compute_coupler_fluxes(sim, FT, boundary_space)
+
+        # By default (e.g. for land and sea ice), the surface flux
+        # computation must use constant roughness, built from the roughness
+        # lengths provided by the surface model.
+        gustiness = FT(1) # hardcoded gustiness value used by the coupler
+        thermo_params = TDP.ThermodynamicsParameters(FT)
+        T_sfc = Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:surface_temperature))
+        config_constant = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.ConstantRoughnessParams(
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_momentum)),
+                    Interfacer.get_field(sim, Val(:roughness_buoyancy)),
+                ),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_constant =
+            expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_constant)
+
+        # For reference, check that COARE3 roughness would give different
+        # fluxes for these conditions, so this test is sensitive to which
+        # roughness parameterization the coupler uses.
+        config_coare3 = [
+            SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+                SF.COARE3RoughnessParams{FT}(),
+                SF.ConstantGustinessSpec(gustiness),
+            ),
+        ]
+        fluxes_coare3 = expected_fluxes(FT, fields, thermo_params, T_sfc, config_coare3)
+        @test !isapprox(fluxes_coare3.F_sh, fluxes_constant.F_sh; rtol = 1e-3)
+
+        # This surface covers the entire exchange grid here (unit area
+        # fraction), so the coupler flux fields equal the per-point fluxes.
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτxz)) == fluxes_constant.F_turb_ρτxz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_ρτyz)) == fluxes_constant.F_turb_ρτyz
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_lh)) == fluxes_constant.F_lh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_sh)) == fluxes_constant.F_sh
+        @test vec(parent(fields.F_turb_moisture)) == fluxes_constant.F_turb_moisture
+    end
+end

problem_statement:
Remove sciml dependence
Remove SciML dependence, add Y, p, t to Simulations struct. see PR #1159 for an example.

SciML adds a very complex object (the integrator) to our simulations. It is unclear that we really need this. We already use ClimaTimesteppers, and not SciML timesteppers. It is unclear or requires a lot of documentation reading to understand when callbacks are called in SciML; we have an existing issue regarding our callbacks #1241.

### Additional contract requirements

- A `LandSimulation` exposes the simulation state `Y`, the cache `p`, and the
  current simulation time `t` as accessible properties.
- When a `LandSimulation` is advanced with `step!`, its exposed time `t`
  advances accordingly (by the simulation timestep for a single step).
- Discrete callbacks that carry `condition`, `affect!`, `initialize`, and
  `finalize` components — regardless of the package or callback family that
  produced them, including diagnostics callbacks and user-supplied callbacks —
  can be converted and combined with ClimaLand callbacks into a
  `ClimaTimeSteppers.CallbackSet`, and used as callback inputs when
  constructing and stepping a `LandSimulation`. Conversion of such a callback
  produces a `ClimaTimeSteppers.DiscreteCallback` whose `condition`, `affect!`,
  `initialize`, and `finalize` components preserve those of the source
  callback.
- The package no longer depends on the SciML environment: its package
  dependency list contains no `SciMLBase` entry, and none of the package's own
  source files imports `SciMLBase` or invokes `SciMLBase` functions (type
  constructors, callback sets, problem or integrator constructors, or
  step/solve entry points).

+
+# The evaluation harness attributes per-testset results to the
+# testset names printed in the log summaries. Julia only prints
+# nested testset summary lines when some child testset did not
+# pass, so extend `Test.finish` so every nested `DefaultTestSet`
+# additionally prints its own (unindented, column-aligned) summary
+# when it finishes, without changing pass/fail/error semantics; the
+# outermost testset behaves exactly as in Test.jl.
+@eval Test function finish(
+    ts::Test.DefaultTestSet;
+    print_results::Bool = Test.TESTSET_PRINT_ENABLE[],
+)
+    ts.time_end = time()
+    if Test.get_testset_depth() != 0
+        Test.print_test_results(ts)
+        Test.record(Test.get_testset(), ts)
+        return ts
+    end
+    tc = Test.get_test_counts(ts)
+    total_pass = tc.passes + tc.cumulative_passes
+    total_fail = tc.fails + tc.cumulative_fails
+    total_error = tc.errors + tc.cumulative_errors
+    total_broken = tc.broken + tc.cumulative_broken
+    total = total_pass + total_fail + total_error + total_broken
+    if print_results
+        Test.print_test_results(ts)
+    end
+    if total != total_pass + total_broken
+        throw(Test.TestSetException(
+            total_pass,
+            total_fail,
+            total_error,
+            total_broken,
+            Test.filter_errors(ts),
+        ))
+    end
+    return ts
+end

+# which preserves those components exactly. Defined before any @testset
+# so that it is visible inside all of them.
+function convert_discrete_cb(cb)
+    return ClimaTimeSteppers.DiscreteCallback(
+        cb.condition,
+        cb.affect!;
+        initialize = cb.initialize,

+    condition::C

### Additional contract requirements

For the reported scenario (the public `surface_fluxes` interface called over a
tens-of-meters layer of dry air with moderate wind and a surface that is much
warmer than the air above it), the returned surface-flux conditions must
reflect buoyant instability rather than neutral stratification:

- The reported Monin-Obukhov stability state must be significantly non-neutral
  and unstable: the stability parameter must be substantially negative and the
  Monin-Obukhov length must be finite and negative, in contrast to the
  near-neutral reference case with a small surface-to-air temperature
  difference.
- The returned stability, friction velocity, and sensible heat flux must
  respond to the imposed surface-to-air temperature contrast instead of
  remaining pinned at their neutral values: the magnitude of the upward
  sensible heat flux must grow with the temperature contrast well beyond the
  growth implied by the near-neutral conductance alone.
- These requirements concern only the publicly returned values under the
  documented public calling pattern; no constraint is placed on internal
  routines, formulas, or signatures.

diff --git a/test/run_target_tests.jl b/test/run_target_tests.jl

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+# Target test runner for the non-neutral-stability regression reported for a
+# large surface-to-air temperature difference.
+#
+# Reported behavior: the public `SurfaceFluxes.surface_fluxes` entry point
+# returns a neutral Monin-Obukhov stability state (stability parameter
+# zeta ~ 0, nearly infinite Monin-Obukhov length, fluxes stuck at their
+# neutral values) even when the surface is tens of kelvin warmer than the
+# air above it, where a clearly unstable (negative-zeta) state is expected.
+#
+# The tests below assert only publicly observable outputs of the public
+# interface:
+#   - the stability parameter / Monin-Obukhov length must respond to a
+#     large surface-to-air temperature contrast with a significantly
+#     unstable sign and magnitude,
+#   - the fluxes and friction velocity must respond to the convection
+#     driven by that contrast instead of staying pinned at their neutral
+#     values.
+# They prescribe no internal formula, internal routine signature, or solver
+# configuration beyond a high iteration allowance mirroring the report.
+using Test
+import Random
+Random.seed!(1234)
+ArrayType = Array
+include(joinpath(@__DIR__, "test_utils.jl"))
+
+module TestIssue220Stability
+
+using Test
+import SurfaceFluxes as SF
+import SurfaceFluxes.UniversalFunctions as UF
+import SurfaceFluxes.Parameters as SFP
+import Thermodynamics as TD
+import ClimaParams as CP
+
+# Public-interface scenario drawn from the reported issue: a dry 32 m layer
+# above the surface, moderate wind, and a prescribed surface temperature.
+function issue_scenario(T_sfc)
+    FT = Float64
+    param_set = SFP.SurfaceFluxesParameters(FT, UF.GryanikParams)
+    thermo_params = SFP.thermodynamics_params(param_set)
+    config = SF.SurfaceFluxConfig(
+        SF.ConstantRoughnessParams{FT}(FT(0.01), FT(0.01)),
+        SF.ConstantGustinessSpec{FT}(FT(1.0)),
+        SF.MoistModel(),
+    )
+    T_int = FT(282)
+    q_tot = FT(0)
+    p_int = FT(100000)
+    ρ_int = TD.air_density(thermo_params, T_int, p_int, q_tot)
+    return SF.surface_fluxes(
+        param_set,
+        T_int,                    # interior air temperature [K]
+        q_tot,                    # interior total specific humidity
+        FT(0),                    # interior liquid specific humidity
+        FT(0),                    # interior ice specific humidity
+        ρ_int,                    # interior air density [kg m^-3]
+        T_sfc,                    # surface temperature [K]
+        q_tot,                    # surface vapor specific humidity
+        FT(0),                    # surface geopotential [m^2 s^-2]
+        FT(32),                   # interior height above surface [m]
+        FT(0),                    # displacement height [m]
+        (FT(3.1), FT(0)),         # interior wind [m s^-1]
+        (FT(0), FT(0)),           # surface wind [m s^-1]
+        nothing,                  # no extra roughness inputs
+        config,
+        SF.PointValueScheme(),
+        SF.SolverOptions{FT}(tol = FT(1e-2), maxiter = 100),
+    )
+end
+
+@testset "Public stability response to a large surface-to-air temperature difference" begin
+    FT = Float64
+
+    out_neutral = issue_scenario(FT(283))
+    out_extreme = issue_scenario(FT(320))
+
+    # Core regression: with the surface ~38 K warmer than the air, the
+    # reported Monin-Obukhov stability state must not stay neutral. The
+    # stability parameter must be significantly negative (unstable) and the
+    # Monin-Obukhov length must be finite and negative.
+    @test out_extreme.ζ < -0.1
+    @test out_extreme.L_MO < 0
+
+    # The reported neutral (buggy) outcome returns identical stability
+    # values regardless of the imposed temperature contrast; a correct
+    # result must respond to the contrast.
+    @test abs(out_extreme.ζ - out_neutral.ζ) > 1
+
+    # A strongly warmed surface drives buoyant convection: the friction
+    # velocity must respond noticeably instead of keeping the near-neutral
+    # value observed for a 1 K contrast.
+    @test abs(out_extreme.ustar - out_neutral.ustar) >
+          0.1 * abs(out_neutral.ustar)
+
+    # The sensible heat flux must be directed upward (away from the warmer
+    # surface) and its magnitude must grow with the added buoyancy rather
+    # than simply following the neutral conductance.
+    out_mild = issue_scenario(FT(293))
+    @test out_extreme.shf > 0
+    @test out_mild.shf > 0
+    @test out_extreme.shf > 100 * out_neutral.shf
+end
+
+end # module
FAIL_TO_PASS: Public stability response to a large surface-to-air temperature difference

problem_statement:
table output should include a style that matches markdown
Increasingly common to use pretty to format tabular output for inclusion in Markdown (i.e., output to be consumed by an AI agent).

### Additional contract requirements

The issue title names only a table style that matches Markdown. The following
publicly observable requirements define the accepted behavior; implementations
that meet them satisfy the contract regardless of internal design choices.

## Style selection API

- `clj-commons.format.table` must expose a public var named `markdown-style`
  holding a table style. `{:style markdown-style}` is passed to
  `clj-commons.format.table/print-table` like any other style, in the same
  position as the existing `default-style`, `skinny-style`, and
  `minimal-style`.

## Markdown table rendering

When `print-table` is called with the `markdown-style` style (and ANSI color
is disabled or stripped), the printed output is plain text with these
observable properties:

- The output contains exactly one title row, exactly one divider rule row
  immediately after the title row, and one data row per input row (and no
  other rows, such as borders or footers). An empty input sequence yields
  only the title row and the divider rule row.
- The title row carries the column titles: either explicit `:title` values
  from column maps, or the titles derived from the column keys.
- The divider rule row is composed solely of pipe characters (`|`) and spans
  of one or more dash characters (`-`), with one dash span per column. It
  contains no spaces or other characters. The number of columns in the rule
  row equals the number of columns in the title row.
- Every row begins and ends with a pipe character, and cells are separated by
  pipe characters, producing a pipe-delimited grid readable as a Markdown
  table.
- Column width is a property of a column's content: the column's title and
  values, padded with spaces so that every column's cells in the title row
  and the data rows have the same content width. Padding contributed by the
  row delimiters themselves (any spacing rendered just inside the pipes of
  the title and data rows) is not part of a column's content width, and rows
  may carry their own leading and trailing spacing inside the outer pipes.
- In the divider rule row, each column's dash span is at least as wide as the
  column's content width; the rule row does not participate in the title- and
  data-row padding, so its dash spans need not match the padded width of
  those rows.
- The cells of each data row contain the row's values in column order; a
  missing value renders as an empty (padded) cell.
- A single-column table follows the same rules (a one-column title row and
  rule row).

Alignment of content within a cell (leading vs. trailing padding) is
determined by the same column option (`:align`, `:title-align`) and defaulting
rules used by the other table styles; no Markdown-specific alignment markers
are required.

@@ -0,0 +1,310 @@
+(ns clj-commons.table-test
+  (:require [clj-commons.test-common :as tc]
+            [clojure.string :as string]
+            [clojure.test :refer [deftest is use-fixtures]]
+            [clj-commons.ansi :as ansi]
+            [clj-commons.format.table :as table]))
+
+(use-fixtures :once tc/spec-fixture)
+
+(def sample-rows [{:first "Arthur" :middle "C" :last "Clark"}
+                  {:first "Alan" :last "Turing"}
+                  {:first "Larry" :last "Niven"}
+                  {:first "Fred" :last "Flintstone"}])
+
+(defn- capture-table
+  [opts rows]
+  (-> (binding [ansi/*color-enabled* false]
+        (with-out-str
+          (table/print-table opts rows)))
+      string/split-lines))
+
+;; Resolved (and dereferenced) at runtime, rather than at namespace load
+;; time, so that the tests report an ordinary error when the style is
+;; not (yet) available.
+(defn- table-style
+  [style-sym]
+  @(resolve (symbol "clj-commons.format.table" (name style-sym))))
+
+(defn- cell-spans
+  "Splits a pipe-delimited table line into its raw (untrimmed) cell strings,
+  i.e. the text between the pipes that delimit it; returns nil when the line
+  is not delimited by pipes."
+  [line]
+  (when (and (string/starts-with? line "|")
+             (string/ends-with? line "|"))
+    (->> (string/split (subs line 1 (dec (count line))) #"\|")
+         ;; Trailing empty cells (e.g. from trailing row delimiters) carry no
+         ;; column content and are dropped.
+         reverse
+         (drop-while string/blank?)
+         reverse)))
+
+(defn- cells
+  "Splits a pipe-delimited table line into its trimmed cell values."
+  [line]
+  (map string/trim (cell-spans line)))
+
+(defn- blank-margin
+  "The [leading trailing] counts of whitespace in s."
+  [s]
+  [(count (re-find #"^ *" s))
+   (count (re-find #" *$" s))])
+
+(defn- relative-margins
+  "Given the raw cell spans of one column across several rows, returns the
+  [leading trailing] whitespace margins of each span relative to the
+  column's minimum margins. Any spacing contributed by the row delimiters
+  is present in every row and hence removed, exposing each cell's own
+  alignment padding."
+  [spans]
+  (let [margins (map blank-margin spans)
+        min-l   (apply min (map first margins))
+        min-t   (apply min (map second margins))]
+    (mapv (fn [[l t]] [(- l min-l) (- t min-t)]) margins)))
+
+(defn- column-spans
+  "Transposes the raw cell spans of the given pipe-delimited rows into one
+  sequence of spans per column."
+  [lines]
+  (apply map vector (map cell-spans lines)))
+
+(defn- normalized-spans
+  "Removes the margins shared by every span of a column from each of its raw
+  cell spans. The shared margins are the maximum whitespace extents present
+  on every span of the column (per row side) - i.e. any delimiter-contributed
+  spacing - leaving each cell's own content and alignment padding."
+  [spans]
+  (let [margins (map blank-margin spans)
+        min-l   (apply min (map first margins))
+        min-t   (apply min (map second margins))]
+    (mapv (fn [span [l t]]
+            (subs span
+                  (min min-l l)
+                  (- (count span) (min min-t t))))
+          spans
+          margins)))
+
+(defn- equal-content-widths?
+  "True when every raw cell span in the given column (one column's spans
+  across rows) has the same effective width after delimiter-contributed
+  margins are removed (see normalized-spans). A cell padded short of the
+  column maximum keeps uneven extra spacing and is detected."
+  [column]
+  (let [widths (map count (normalized-spans column))]
+    (or (empty? widths)
+        (apply = widths))))
+
+(deftest default-style
+  (is (= ["┌──────┬──────┬──────────┐"
+          "│ First│Middle│   Last   │"
+          "├──────┼──────┼──────────┤"
+          "│Arthur│     C│Clark     │"
+          "│  Alan│      │Turing    │"
+          "│ Larry│      │Niven     │"
+          "│  Fred│      │Flintstone│"
+          "└──────┴──────┴──────────┘"]
+         (capture-table [:first :middle :last] sample-rows))))
+
+(deftest skinny-style
+  (is (= [" First | Middle |    Last   "
+          "-------+--------+-----------"
+          "Arthur |      C | Clark     "
+          "  Alan |        | Turing    "
+          " Larry |        | Niven     "
+          "  Fred |        | Flintstone"]
+         (capture-table {:columns [:first :middle :last]
+                         :style   table/skinny-style}
+                        sample-rows))))
+
+(deftest minimal-style
+  (is (= [" First Middle    Last   "
+          "Arthur      C Clark     "
+          "  Alan        Turing    "
+          " Larry        Niven     "
+          "  Fred        Flintstone"]
+         (capture-table {:columns [:first :middle :last]
+                         :style   table/minimal-style}
+                        sample-rows))))
+
+(deftest markdown-style
+  (let [lines      (capture-table {:columns [:first :middle :last]
+                                   :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                                  sample-rows)
+        title-line (first lines)
+        rule-line  (second lines)
+        row-lines  (drop 2 lines)
+        columns    (column-spans (cons title-line row-lines))]
+    (is (= 6 (count lines))
+        "output is a title row, one divider rule row, and one row per input row")
+    (is (every? #(and (string/starts-with? % "|")
+                      (string/ends-with? % "|"))
+                lines)
+        "every row begins and ends with a pipe character, as in Markdown table syntax")
+    (is (= ["First" "Middle" "Last"]
+           (cells title-line))
+        "the title row carries the column titles")
+    (is (re-matches #"\|(-+\|)+" rule-line)
+        "the divider row is composed of pipes and one or more dashes per column")
+    (is (= (count (cells title-line))
+           (count (cells rule-line)))
+        "the divider row has one dash span per column")
+    (is (every? (fn [line]
+                  (every? (fn [[d c]] (>= d c))
+                          (map vector
+                               (map count (cell-spans rule-line))
+                               (map count (cells line)))))
+                (cons title-line row-lines))
+        "each column's dash span is at least as wide as the column's title and values")
+    (is (= [["Arthur" "C" "Clark"]
+            ["Alan" "" "Turing"]
+            ["Larry" "" "Niven"]
+            ["Fred" "" "Flintstone"]]
+           (map cells row-lines))
+        "each row renders its values in column order; missing values render as empty cells")
+    (is (every? equal-content-widths? columns)
+        "once each column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every data cell of a column have the same content width")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-single-column
+  (let [lines (capture-table {:columns [:first]
+                              :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                             sample-rows)]
+    (is (= 6 (count lines))
+        "a single-column table is still a title, a rule, and one row per input row")
+    (is (= ["First" "Arthur" "Alan" "Larry" "Fred"]
+           (map #(first (cells %)) (cons (first lines) (drop 2 lines))))
+        "the single column renders the title followed by each value")
+    (is (re-matches #"\|-+\|" (second lines))
+        "the divider row is a single dash span between pipes")
+    (is (equal-content-widths?
+         (first (column-spans (cons (first lines) (drop 2 lines)))))
+        "once the column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every value have the same content width")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-with-explicit-titles
+  (let [lines (capture-table {:columns [{:key :first :title "Given name" :align :left}
+                                        {:key :last :title "Family name"}]
+                              :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                             sample-rows)]
+    (is (= ["Given name" "Family name"]
+           (cells (first lines)))
+        "explicit column titles replace the titles derived from the column keys")
+    (is (re-matches #"\|(-+\|)+" (second lines))
+        "the divider row is composed of pipes and one or more dashes per column")
+    (is (= [["Arthur" "Clark"]
+            ["Alan" "Turing"]
+            ["Larry" "Niven"]
+            ["Fred" "Flintstone"]]
+           (map cells (drop 2 lines)))
+        "row values appear in column order")
+    (is (every? equal-content-widths?
+                (column-spans (cons (first lines) (drop 2 lines))))
+        "once each column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every value have the same content width")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-longest-title
+  ;; The longest content of each column here is its (explicit) title; the
+  ;; single value per column is shorter and left-aligned. Alignment padding
+  ;; is measured relative to each column's margins so that spacing
+  ;; contributed by the row delimiters (present on every row) never counts
+  ;; as content padding.
+  (let [lines        (capture-table {:columns [{:key :first :title "First name" :align :left}
+                                               {:key :last :title "Family name"}]
+                                     :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                                    [{:first "Alan" :last "Turing"}])
+        titled-lines [(first lines) (last lines)]
+        columns      (column-spans titled-lines)]
+    (is (= 3 (count lines))
+        "one input row renders as a title row, a divider rule row, and one data row")
+    (is (re-matches #"\|(-+\|)+" (second lines))
+        "the divider row is composed of pipes and one or more dashes per column")
+    (is (every? #(and (string/starts-with? % "|")
+                      (string/ends-with? % "|"))
+                lines)
+        "every row begins and ends with a pipe character")
+    (is (= [["First name" "Alan"]
+            ["Family name" "Turing"]]
+           (mapv (fn [column] (mapv string/trim column)) columns))
+        "each column carries its title and value, in column order")
+    (is (every? (fn [[dash-span title-span]]
+                  (>= (count dash-span) (count (string/trim title-span))))
+                (map vector (cell-spans (second lines)) (first (column-spans [(first lines)]))))
+        "each column's dash span covers at least the column's title")
+    (is (every? (fn [column]
+                  (let [[_ [leading trailing]] (relative-margins column)]
+                    (and (zero? leading)
+                         (pos? trailing))))
+                columns)
+        "each shorter value is padded after (never before) the content, per :align :left")
+    (is (every? equal-content-widths? columns)
+        "once each column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every value have the same content width")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-empty-rows
+  (let [lines (capture-table {:columns [:first :middle :last]
+                              :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                             [])]
+    (is (= 2 (count lines))
+        "an empty table is only a title row and a divider rule row")
+    (is (= ["First" "Middle" "Last"]
+           (cells (first lines)))
+        "the title row carries the column titles")
+    (is (re-matches #"\|(-+\|)+" (second lines))
+        "the divider row is composed of pipes and one or more dashes per column")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-default-alignment
+  ;; Without explicit :align or :title-align options, titles are centered,
+  ;; the non-last columns are right-aligned, and the last column is
+  ;; left-aligned, matching the standard defaulting rules. Padding is
+  ;; measured relative to each column's margins so that spacing contributed
+  ;; by the row delimiters never counts as content padding.
+  (let [lines   (capture-table {:columns [:first :last]
+                                :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                               sample-rows)
+        columns (column-spans (cons (first lines) (drop 2 lines)))
+        margins (mapv relative-margins columns)]
+    (is (= [["First" "Arthur" "Alan" "Larry" "Fred"]
+            ["Last" "Clark" "Turing" "Niven" "Flintstone"]]
+           (mapv (fn [column] (mapv string/trim column)) columns))
+        "each column carries its title followed by its values in row order")
+    (is (every? (fn [[title-margins]]
+                  (<= (abs (- (first title-margins) (second title-margins))) 1))
+                margins)
+        "each title is centered within its column by default")
+    (is (every? (fn [cell-margins]
+                  (every? (fn [[_ trailing]] (zero? trailing)) (rest cell-margins)))
+                [(first margins)])
+        "the non-last column is padded before (never after) the content by default")
+    (is (some (fn [[leading _]] (pos? leading)) (rest (first margins)))
+        "the non-last column actually has padding before its shorter values")
+    (is (every? (fn [cell-margins]
+                  (every? (fn [[leading _]] (zero? leading)) (rest cell-margins)))
+                [(second margins)])
+        "the last column is padded after (never before) the content by default")
+    (is (some (fn [[_ trailing]] (pos? trailing)) (rest (second margins)))
+        "the last column actually has padding after its shorter values")
+    (is (every? equal-content-widths? columns)
+        "once each column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every value have the same content width")))
+
+(deftest markdown-style-explicit-alignment
+  ;; The single column's title is left-aligned and its values right-aligned.
+  ;; Padding is measured relative to the column's margins so that spacing
+  ;; contributed by the row delimiters never counts as content padding.
+  (let [lines        (capture-table {:columns [{:key         :first
+                                                :title       "Alan"
+                                                :align       :right
+                                                :title-align :left}]
+                                     :style   (table-style 'markdown-style)}
+                                    sample-rows)
+        column       (first (column-spans (cons (first lines) (drop 2 lines))))
+        [title-margin & data-margins] (relative-margins column)]
+    (is (= ["Alan" "Arthur" "Alan" "Larry" "Fred"]
+           (mapv string/trim column))
+        "the title is followed by each row's value, in order")
+    (is (zero? (first title-margin))
+        ":title-align :left does not pad the title before the content")
+    (is (pos? (second title-margin))
+        ":title-align :left pads the shorter title after the content")
+    (is (every? (fn [[_ trailing]] (zero? trailing)) data-margins)
+        ":align :right does not pad a value after the content")
+    (is (some (fn [[leading _]] (pos? leading)) data-margins)
+        ":align :right actually pads the shorter values before the content")
+    (is (equal-content-widths? column)
+        "once the column's shared margins (any delimiter-contributed spacing) are removed, the title and every value have the same content width")))

problem_statement:
limited coerce support for seqs
```clj
  (defn demo-into [to from]
    (-> (z/append-child (z/of-string to) from)
        z/down z/rightmost z/splice z/root-string))

  (demo-into "[1]" [2 3]) ;; => "[1 2 3]"
  (demo-into "[1]" (seq [2 3])) ;; => actual: "[1 (2 3)]"  expected: "[1 2 3]"
```

### Additional contract requirements

# Additional contract: coercion of sequence values

This addendum clarifies the observable scope of the fix beyond the single
`(seq [2 3])` example in the base statement.

## Scope is finite, terminating sequence values

The guarantees in this addendum apply to *finite, terminating* sequence
values: sequence values that can be fully realized to a definite, finite
number of elements. A consumer is not required to accept, realize, or
produce any node for an unbounded or non-terminating sequence (for
example an unbounded lazy producer); coercion of such a value has no
guaranteed outcome and may fail to terminate. For a finite sequence
produced by taking or dropping a bounded prefix from an unbounded one
(for example `(take 2 (drop 1 (range)))`), the guarantee applies to that
finite prefix value.

## Coercion of finite sequence values to list form

Coercing a finite sequence value (any finite, terminating value that
satisfies the platform's sequence abstraction, for example the result of
`seq`, `cons`, `lazy-seq`, `vals`, `keys`, `rseq`, `range` with an end,
`sort`, or `map`/`filter` over a finite collection) yields a node in
list form:

- the node's tag is `:list` and its node type is `:seq`;
- the coercion is a faithful round trip: converting the node back to an
  s-expression yields a sequence equal to the original value, with the
  same elements in the same order;
- each element is coerced recursively, so printed string output is the
  list rendering of the original sequence's elements;
- the behavior is uniform across sequence flavors: it must not depend on
  the concrete implementation class or flavor of the sequence produced
  by platform APIs.

This uniformity is what makes the base-statement example work: splicing a
coerced `(seq [2 3])` (or any other finite sequence flavor over `[2 3]`)
into `[1]` renders as `"[1 2 3]"`, never as `"[1 (2 3)]"`.

## Supported runtimes

This project is supported on both Clojure (JVM) and ClojureScript. The
finite-sequence coercion behavior described here applies on both
supported runtimes and must be observable and verifiable from code that
runs on each platform. Platform-specific sequence flavors (for example
`enumeration-seq`, `line-seq`, or `file-seq` on the JVM, or
`array-seq`/`re-seq` on ClojureScript) are exercised only on the
platform where they exist and are not part of the cross-platform public
contract.

## Preserved behavior for vectors, sets, and other values

Existing coercion behavior outside this change is unchanged. In
particular, vectors continue to coerce to vector nodes with tag
`:vector`, and sets continue to coerce to set nodes with tag `:set`
(both of node type `:seq`), with elements preserved, on both supported
runtimes.

problem_statement: Enhancement: Wrap hover/signature help symbols in parentheses Hovering/using "signature help" to view the documentation for a function shows the fully-qualified symbol and any args lists (as well as any doc strings, etc). These are presented bare, while in use they are typically used in function-call position (wrapped in parentheses). I think it would be nice if they were wrapped in parentheses, both to better indicate that they're functions and to help with highlighting when semantic highlighting is disabled. See [Slack discussion](https://clojurians.slack.com/archives/CPABC1H61/p1770135222969289). Before: After: ### Additional contract requirements When hover or signature help shows the documentation of a function symbol its fully-qualified symbol together with its argument lists — that signature may be presented enclosed in a single surrounding pair of parentheses, as if written in function-call position. For example, documentation for `some.namespace/foo [x]` may be presented as `(some.namespace/foo [x])`. The parts of such a signature (the fully-qualified symbol and each argument list) may be rendered on one line or distributed across several lines or content blocks of the response. When the signature is enclosed, an opening parenthesis at the very start of the first part and a closing parenthesis at the very end of the last part are part of that surrounding pair, not of the parts themselves. The whitespace used between and around the parts — including alignment, indentation, or line breaks — is not specified. What is fixed is that the symbol and its argument lists appear in order. Each response layout makes its own presentation choice for the signature: a markdown rendering and the single-line plaintext rendering enclose the signature in the surrounding parentheses; the default plaintext layout that renders each part as its own content block may present the parts either bare or enclosed in the surrounding parentheses. This applies to hovering a function's definition or one of its usages. When a usage also shows a calling-form label (a surrounding "calling: ..." line), the documentation of the hovered function symbol is wrapped as above; whether that calling-form label itself is also wrapped in parentheses is not specified by this change, and any docstrings and file-location information in the response are unaffected. Custom argument lists declared through `:arglists` metadata follow the same rule, with each declared argument list appearing in order. Documentation for symbols that have no argument lists — plain vars, namespaces, keywords, and similar — is presented unchanged, with no parentheses added.
