+(defn ^:private signature-blocks
+  "The pieces of a plaintext hover response that render the documentation
+  of the hovered symbol: every language-tagged content block, in response
+  order."
+  [contents]
+  (into [] (comp (filter map?) (map :value)) contents))
+
+(defn ^:private markdown-text
+  "The textual content of a markdown hover response, whatever its concrete
+  presentation (fences, language tags, rules, and other markdown markup are
+  presentation details that are not specified)."
+  [contents]
+  (or (:value contents) ""))
+
+(defn ^:private whitespace-insensitive-regex
+  "A regex matching its `literal` text exactly, except that each run of
+  whitespace contained in the text matches any amount and kind of whitespace."
+  [literal]
+  (re-pattern (str "\\s*"
+                   (string/join "\\s+"
+                                (map #(java.util.regex.Pattern/quote %)
+                                     (string/split (string/trim literal) #"\s+")))
+                   "\\s*")))
+
+(defn ^:private signature-blocks-text
+  "A single whitespace-normalized string for a rendering of a symbol's
+  documentation, whether the rendering is one string or is distributed
+  across several lines or content blocks."
+  [rendering]
+  (-> (if (sequential? rendering)
+        (string/join " " (signature-blocks rendering))
+        (or rendering ""))
+      (string/replace #"\s+" " ")
+      string/trim))
+
+(defn ^:private paren-stripped-block
+  "The content of a language-tagged content block presenting `form` with
+  nothing but (optionally) one wrapping parenthesis, or `nil` when the
+  block presents anything else. An opening parenthesis at the very start
+  or a closing parenthesis at the very end of the block is part of the
+  signature's surrounding pair, not of `form` itself."
+  [block form]
+  (cond (= block form)
+        block
+
+        (and (string/starts-with? block "(")
+             (= form (subs block 1)))
+        (subs block 1)
+
+        (and (string/ends-with? block ")")
+             (= form (subs block 0 (dec (count block)))))
+        (subs block 0 (dec (count block)))
+
+        :else nil))
+
+(defn ^:private stripped-signature-blocks-text
+  "A single string for the language-tagged content blocks of a plaintext
+  hover response, keeping each of the signature's forms exactly while
+  moving any surrounding-pair parenthesis outside them: the blocks
+  present `sym` and each of `arglists` in order when the stripped forms
+  are joined with single spaces."
+  [rendering sym arglists]
+  (when (sequential? rendering)
+    (let [blocks (signature-blocks rendering)
+          stripped (keep-indexed (fn [idx block]
+                                   (paren-stripped-block block (nth (cons sym arglists) idx "")))
+                                 blocks)]
+      (when (and (= (count blocks) (count stripped))
+                 (every? some? stripped))
+        (let [first-block (first blocks)
+              last-block (last blocks)]
+          (str (when (and (string/starts-with? first-block "(")
+                          (not= first-block (first stripped)))
+                 "(")
+               (string/join " " stripped)
+               (when (and (string/ends-with? last-block ")")
+                          (not= last-block (last stripped)))
+                 ")")))))))
+
+(defn ^:private parenthesized-contents?
+  "True when `text` presents each of `forms` exactly and in order, all
+  enclosed in one surrounding pair of parentheses: any amount and kind of
+  whitespace is accepted between and around the parts, and, apart from the
+  outer pair of parentheses, no opening or closing parenthesis occurs in
+  the presentation."
+  [text forms]
+  (boolean
+    (re-matches (re-pattern (str "^\\("
+                                 (string/join "" (map whitespace-insensitive-regex forms))
+                                 "\\)$"))
+                text)))
+
+(defn ^:private signature-context
+  "The elements of a plaintext hover response besides the signature
+  itself: any calling-form label, docstring, edit warning, and file
+  location, in response order. Every language-tagged content block is
+  part of the signature: the first block presents the symbol (possibly
+  with the surrounding pair's opening parenthesis at its very start) and
+  the last presents the final argument list (possibly with the closing
+  parenthesis at its very end)."
+  [contents sym]
+  (let [before (take-while string? contents)
+        after (->> (drop (count before) contents)
+                   (drop-while map?)
+                   (filter string?)
+                   (remove #(= % sym)))]
+    (vec (concat before after))))
+
+(defn ^:private complete-signature?
+  "True when `rendering` (one string, or the whole contents of a plaintext
+  hover response) presents the symbol's documentation as exactly the
+  fully-qualified `sym` followed by each of `arglists` in order, all
+  enclosed in one surrounding pair of parentheses. The parts may be
+  rendered on one line or split across several lines or content blocks:
+  the pair of parentheses is distributed across the content blocks that
+  present the parts -- an opening parenthesis at the very start of the
+  block presenting `sym` and a closing parenthesis at the very end of the
+  block presenting the last argument list are part of the signature's
+  surrounding pair, not of the parts themselves. Any amount and kind of
+  whitespace is accepted between and around the parts, and no part is
+  presented outside the surrounding pair."
+  [rendering sym arglists]
+  (parenthesized-contents? (or (stripped-signature-blocks-text rendering sym arglists)
+                               (signature-blocks-text rendering))
+                           (cons sym arglists)))
+
+(defn ^:private bare-signature?
+  "True when the language-tagged content blocks of a plaintext hover
+  response are exactly `sym` followed by each of `arglists` in order,
+  with no wrapping parenthesis anywhere."
+  [contents sym arglists]
+  (let [blocks (signature-blocks contents)]
+    (boolean
+      (and (= (inc (count arglists)) (count blocks))
+           (= (seq (cons sym arglists)) (seq blocks))
+           (every? (fn [block]
+                     (not (or (string/starts-with? block "(")
+                              (string/ends-with? block ")"))))
+                   blocks)))))
+
+(defn ^:private default-multiline-signature?
+  "True when the default (each part on its own content block) plaintext
+  hover response presents the documentation of the hovered symbol as the
+  fully-qualified `sym` followed by each of `arglists` in order: either
+  enclosed in one surrounding pair of parentheses distributed across the
+  content blocks, or bare."
+  [contents sym arglists]
+  (or (complete-signature? contents sym arglists)
+      (bare-signature? contents sym arglists)))
+
+(defn ^:private enclosed-args?
+  "True when the textual content `text` contains the fully-qualified `sym`
+  and each of `arglists` in order, enclosed together in one surrounding
+  pair of parentheses, starting at or after `open-idx`."
+  [text open-idx sym arglists]
+  (let [pattern (re-pattern (str "\\("
+                                 (string/join ""
+                                              (map whitespace-insensitive-regex
+                                                   (cons sym arglists)))
+                                 "\\)"))]
+    (let [start (max 0 (- open-idx 8))
+          end (min (count text)
+                   (+ open-idx (count sym) (apply + (map count arglists)) 64))]
+      (boolean (re-find pattern (subs text start end))))))
+
+(defn ^:private markdown-signature?
+  "True when the textual content of a markdown hover response presents
+  the symbol's documentation as the fully-qualified `sym` followed by
+  each of `arglists` in order, all enclosed in one surrounding pair of
+  parentheses. Fences, language tags, rules, and other markdown markup
+  are presentation details that are not specified, so the whole enclosed
+  signature may appear anywhere in the textual content."
+  [contents sym arglists]
+  (let [markdown (markdown-text contents)]
+    (boolean
+      (some #(enclosed-args? markdown % sym arglists)
+            (keep-indexed (fn [idx ch] (when (= ch (char 40)) idx))
+                          markdown)))))
+
+(defn ^:private markdown-includes?
+  "True when the textual content of a markdown hover response contains
+  `text`. Whitespace, fences, markup, and the layout of the surrounding
+  markdown are presentation details that are not specified, so `text`
+  may appear anywhere in the textual content."
+  [contents text]
+  (string/includes? (markdown-text contents) text))
+
+(def ^:private calling-label-prefix "calling: ")
+
+(defn ^:private calling-form-label
+  "The call named by the calling-form label of `contents` (the part of a
+  calling-label element after the prefix), or `nil` when the response
+  has no calling-form label."
+  [contents]
+  (some (fn [element]
+          (when (and (string? element)
+                     (string/starts-with? element calling-label-prefix))
+            (subs element (count calling-label-prefix))))
+        contents))
+
+(defn ^:private calling-label?
+  "True when `contents` contains a calling-form label for `call` (for
+  example \"calling: clojure.core/->>\"). The label may be presented bare
+  or wrapped in one pair of parentheses."
+  [contents call]
+  (= call (calling-form-label contents)))
+
+(defn ^:private parenthesized-calling-label?
+  "True when `contents` contains a calling-form label for `call` wrapped
+  in one surrounding pair of parentheses (for example
+  \"calling: (clojure.core/->>)\")."
+  [contents call]
+  (= (str "(" call ")") (calling-form-label contents)))
+
+(defn ^:private accepting-calling-label?
+  "True when `contents` contains a calling-form label for `call`, whether
+  the label is presented bare or wrapped in one pair of parentheses. The
+  documentation of the hovered function symbol is wrapped in parentheses;
+  whether the surrounding calling-form label also is wrapped is not
+  specified by this test."
+  [contents call]
+  (or (calling-label? contents call)
+      (parenthesized-calling-label? contents call)))
+

problem_statement:
cyclic-dependencies is over-zealous #1 in comment forms
**Describe the bug**
If you have a `(require ..)` in a `comment` form, used for dev/REPL work, this should **not** contribute to a cyclic dependency.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a simple ns, add a `comment` form, containing a `(require .. :reload)` of that same ns
2. LSP will flag this as a cyclic dependency

**Expected behavior**
`require` inside `comment` should not contribute to a cyclic dependency.

**User details (please complete the following information):**
 - Version: [2025.08.15-15.37.37](https://github.com/clojure-lsp/clojure-lsp/releases/tag/2025.08.15-15.37.37)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

+(defn ^:private comment-form-bounds
+  "Var-usages of `comment` define regions of code that are not
+   evaluated. Returns those usages from a single uri's analysis."
+  [var-usages]
+  (filter (fn [{:keys [to name]}]
+            (and (or (fast= 'clojure.core to) (fast= 'cljs.core to))
+                 (fast= 'comment name)))
+          var-usages))
+
+(defn ^:private decrement-dep-edge [dep-graph from to]
+  (let [path [from :dependencies to]]
+    (if (<= (or (get-in dep-graph path) 0) 1)
+      (update-in dep-graph [from :dependencies] dissoc to)
+      (update-in dep-graph path dec))))
+
+(defn ^:private remove-comment-form-deps
+  "Remove dep-graph edges that originate from a (require ...) (or similar) call
+   inside a (comment ...) form, so they don't participate in cycle detection."
+  [dep-graph analysis]
+  (reduce-kv
+    (fn [graph _uri {:keys [namespace-usages var-usages]}]
+      (let [bounds (comment-form-bounds var-usages)]
+        (if (empty? bounds)
+          graph
+          (reduce
+            (fn [g {:keys [from name] :as usage}]
+              (cond-> g
+                (some #(shared/inside? usage %) bounds)
+                (decrement-dep-edge from name)))
+            graph namespace-usages))))
+    dep-graph analysis))

problem_statement:
cyclic-dependencies is over-zealous #2 about :as-alias
**Describe the bug**
A ns that is required `:as-alias` should not contribute to a cyclic dependency since it does not load the ns (indeed, there doesn't even need to be a real ns behind such a require.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create two nses, `a` and `b`; have `a` require `b`; have `b` require `a` with `:as-alias`
2. This is flagged (incorrectly) as a cyclic dependency

**Expected behavior**
`:as-alias` should not contribute to a cyclic dependency.

**User details (please complete the following information):**
 - Version: [2025.08.15-15.37.37](https://github.com/clojure-lsp/clojure-lsp/releases/tag/2025.08.15-15.37.37)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

### Additional contract requirements

The `clojure-lsp/cyclic-dependencies` linter must treat a namespace required with `:as-alias` as not contributing a dependency edge, since such a require does not load the namespace; a namespace reached only through `:as-alias` requires must not produce cyclic-dependency diagnostics, whether the `:as-alias` libspec is written on a single line or split across multiple lines. A namespace required normally must still contribute a dependency edge, including when the same target namespace is also required with `:as-alias` in an additional libspec; in that case the cycle diagnostics must still be reported.

+(defn ^:private text-between-name-and-alias
+  [text {:keys [name-end-row name-end-col alias-row alias-col]}]
+  (when (and text name-end-row name-end-col alias-row alias-col)
+    (let [lines (string/split text #"\r\n|\n|\r" -1)]
+      (if (= name-end-row alias-row)
+        (subs (nth lines (dec name-end-row))
+              (dec name-end-col)
+              (dec alias-col))
+        (str
+          (subs (nth lines (dec name-end-row)) (dec name-end-col))
+          "\n"
+          (string/join
+            "\n"
+            (subvec lines name-end-row (dec alias-row)))
+          "\n"
+          (subs (nth lines (dec alias-row)) 0 (dec alias-col)))))))
+
+(defn ^:private as-alias-usage? [documents {:keys [uri alias] :as usage}]
+  (when alias
+    (some-> (text-between-name-and-alias (get-in documents [uri :text]) usage)
+            (string/includes? ":as-alias"))))
+
 (defn ^:private remove-comment-form-deps
   "Remove dep-graph edges that originate from a (require ...) (or similar) call
    inside a (comment ...) form, so they don't participate in cycle detection."
@@ -317,13 +339,29 @@
             graph namespace-usages))))
     dep-graph analysis))
 
+(defn ^:private remove-as-alias-deps
+  "Remove dep-graph edges from :as-alias requires. They create aliases without
+   loading the target namespace, so they do not participate in cycle detection."
+  [dep-graph analysis documents]
+  (reduce-kv
+    (fn [graph _uri {:keys [namespace-usages]}]
+      (reduce
+        (fn [g {:keys [from name] :as usage}]
+          (cond-> g
+            (as-alias-usage? documents usage)
+            (decrement-dep-edge from name)))
+        graph namespace-usages))
+    dep-graph analysis))
+
 (defn ^:private cyclic-dependencies
   "Detects cyclic dependencies and generates diagnostics for each namespace in a cycle."
   [narrowed-db project-db settings]
   (let [level (get-in settings [:linters :clojure-lsp/cyclic-dependencies :level] :off)]
     (when-not (identical? :off level)
-      (let [dep-graph (remove-comment-form-deps
-                        (:dep-graph narrowed-db) (:analysis project-db))
+      (let [dep-graph (-> (:dep-graph narrowed-db)
+                          (remove-comment-form-deps (:analysis project-db))
+                          (remove-as-alias-deps
+                            (:analysis project-db) (:documents project-db)))
             cycles (find-dependency-cycles dep-graph)
             exclude-namespaces (set (get-in settings [:linters :clojure-lsp/cyclic-dependencies :exclude-namespaces] #{}))

problem_statement:
[BUG] Two tables with connected clients
I'm not sure if it's a bug or if I just don't understand the implementation, but the current ws server has two tables with connected clients:
1. https://github.com/coder/claudecode.nvim/blob/70fa226d51f07ee465b8750be698e5a7f7825395/lua/claudecode/server/init.lua#L15
2. https://github.com/coder/claudecode.nvim/blob/70fa226d51f07ee465b8750be698e5a7f7825395/lua/claudecode/server/tcp.lua#L11

It seems like they store the same thing, but they are pretty much out of sync most of the time.

What I see:
- when I open CC terminal, both receive a new client connection (identical)
- when I hit `Ctrl-C` in CC terminal (exit session), its client connection is removed from both tables, but immediately after, a new connection appears in `server/init`, but not in `server/tcp`. `server/init` constantly grows with these phantom connections that appear after each terminated session. I can't figure out what initiates this connection and why it stays in the `server/init` clients table.

Is this by design? What initiates this second connection after the session termination?

### Additional contract requirements

Client session termination must not leave or accumulate stale entries in the
server's connected-client bookkeeping:

- When a client session terminates (for example, exiting the client terminal),
  the terminated client is removed from the server's connected clients and the
  server notifies the disconnect through its disconnect callback exactly once
  per termination.

- This invariant holds for every way a session can terminate: the abrupt end
  of the connection (EOF), transport-level read errors, protocol-level close
  or error conditions, and prolonged inactivity on a terminated connection.

- This invariant holds across repeated connect/termination cycles: after any
  number of connected clients terminate, no stale or duplicate entries are
  retained and the connected-client count returns to zero.

- If a terminated client's connection later delivers an overlapping or
  repeated terminal signal, it must not produce an additional disconnect
  notification or resurrect or retain any connected-client entry.

+-- Custom busted output handler that prints one machine-readable line per test.
+-- Format (unindented, one per test):  "Success || <name>" / "Fail || <name>" / "Skip || <name>"
+-- It still reflects real outcomes and lets busted exit nonzero on failure.
+local io_write = io.write
+local io_flush = io.flush
+local string_format = string.format
+
+return function(options)
+  local busted = require("busted")
+  local handler = require("busted.outputHandlers.base")()
+
+  local function full_name(element)
+    local ok, name = pcall(handler.getFullName, element)
+    if ok and type(name) == "string" and name ~= "" then
+      return name
+    end
+    return tostring(element and (element.name or element.descriptor) or "unknown")
+  end
+
+  handler.testEnd = function(element, parent, status, debug)
+    local name = full_name(element)
+    if status == "success" then
+      io_write(string_format("Success || %s\n", name))
+    elseif status == "pending" then
+      io_write(string_format("Skip || %s\n", name))
+    else
+      -- "failure" is a failed assertion; "error" is an unexpected error.
+      io_write(string_format("Fail || %s\n", name))
+    end
+    io_flush()
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  handler.suiteEnd = function()
+    io_write(
+      string_format(
+        "%d successes / %d failures / %d errors / %d pending\n",
+        handler.successesCount,
+        handler.failuresCount,
+        handler.errorsCount,
+        handler.pendingsCount
+      )
+    )
+    io_flush()
+    return nil, true
+  end
+
+  busted.subscribe({ "test", "end" }, handler.testEnd, { predicate = handler.cancelOnPending })
+  busted.subscribe({ "suite", "end" }, handler.suiteEnd)
+
+  return handler
+end

+++ b/tests/unit/server/tcp_spec.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,334 @@
+-- Regression coverage for the reported "phantom clients" bug: when a client
+-- session terminates, the server must drop the client from its connected
+-- clients and notify the disconnect through its disconnect callback, so that
+-- higher-level bookkeeping stays in sync -- and this must hold no matter how
+-- many sessions are started and terminated in a row.
+require("tests.busted_setup")
+
+describe("client session termination", function()
+  local saved_now
+  local server
+  local config = {
+    port_range = {
+      min = 10000,
+      max = 65535,
+    },
+  }
+
+  before_each(function()
+    server = require("claudecode.server.init")
+  end)
+
+  after_each(function()
+    pcall(function()
+      server.stop()
+    end)
+    -- Extra safety: reset the module table itself between tests
+    package.loaded["claudecode.server.init"] = nil
+  end)
+
+  -- The dead-connection inactivity scenario overrides the mocked wall clock;
+  -- restore the original clock once all scenarios have run.
+  teardown(function()
+    if saved_now then
+      vim.loop.now = saved_now
+      saved_now = nil
+    end
+  end)
+
+  local function client_count()
+    local count = 0
+    for _ in pairs(server.state.server.clients) do
+      count = count + 1
+    end
+    return count
+  end
+
+  -- Simulates an incoming connection accepted by the running server and
+  -- returns the connected client object.
+  local function simulate_client_connect()
+    local listen_cb = server.state.server.server._listen_cb
+    assert.is_function(listen_cb)
+    listen_cb(nil)
+    local client = server.state.server.clients[next(server.state.server.clients)]
+    assert.is_table(client)
+    assert.is_table(client.tcp_handle)
+    assert.is_function(client.tcp_handle._read_cb)
+    return client
+  end
+
+  -- Simulates the client's connection terminating abruptly (EOF), as happens
+  -- when a session is exited (e.g. Ctrl-C in the client terminal).
+  local function simulate_client_termination(client)
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, nil)
+  end
+
+  -- Wraps the server's disconnect notification so the test can observe it.
+  local function observe_disconnects()
+    local notifications = {}
+    local original = server.state.server.on_disconnect
+    server.state.server.on_disconnect = function(client, ...)
+      notifications[#notifications + 1] = client
+      return original(client, ...)
+    end
+    return notifications
+  end
+
+  -- Collects every timer callback that has been scheduled on the running
+  -- server's periodic timers, so a test can drive the server's periodic
+  -- activity checks deterministically.
+  local function collect_timer_callbacks()
+    local callbacks = {}
+    local ping_timer = server.state.ping_timer
+    if ping_timer then
+      for _, cb in ipairs(ping_timer.timer_callbacks) do
+        callbacks[#callbacks + 1] = cb
+      end
+    end
+    return callbacks
+  end
+
+  -- A minimal but valid WebSocket upgrade request used to complete a session
+  -- handshake in protocol-level scenarios.
+  local HANDSHAKE_REQUEST = table.concat({
+    "GET / HTTP/1.1",
+    "Host: 127.0.0.1",
+    "Upgrade: websocket",
+    "Connection: Upgrade",
+    "Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==",
+    "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13",
+    "",
+    "",
+  }, "\r\n")
+
+  -- Builds a masked WebSocket frame as a client would send it.
+  local function build_client_frame(opcode, payload)
+    local mask = { 0x12, 0x34, 0x36, 0x78 }
+    local bytes = { string.char(0x80 + opcode, 0x80 + #payload) }
+    for _, b in ipairs(mask) do
+      bytes[#bytes + 1] = string.char(b)
+    end
+    for i = 1, #payload do
+      bytes[#bytes + 1] = string.char(bit.bxor(payload:byte(i), mask[((i - 1) % 4) + 1]))
+    end
+    return table.concat(bytes)
+  end
+
+
+  it("should not keep any client after a terminated session", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    simulate_client_termination(client)
+
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once, got " .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+
+  it("should not accumulate clients across repeated connect/termination cycles", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    for cycle = 1, 3 do
+      local client = simulate_client_connect()
+      assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+      simulate_client_termination(client)
+
+      assert(
+        #notifications == cycle,
+        "expected one disconnect notification per terminated session, got "
+          .. #notifications
+          .. " after cycle "
+          .. cycle
+      )
+
+      local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+      assert(
+        count_after_disconnect == 0,
+        "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+      )
+    end
+
+    server.stop()
+  end)
+
+  it("should notify the disconnect at most once when a terminated client receives an extra terminal signal", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    -- A session's connection may deliver overlapping terminal signals of
+    -- different kinds: here the client requests a protocol-level close, and
+    -- the connection then reports its transport-level end as well.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, HANDSHAKE_REQUEST)
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, build_client_frame(0x8, ""))
+
+    -- The overlapping follow-up signal must not produce a second disconnect
+    -- notification or resurrect/keep any connected-client entry.
+    simulate_client_termination(client)
+
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once despite an extra terminal signal, got "
+        .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+
+  -- The remaining scenarios exercise each other observable termination
+  -- signal -- a transport read error, a protocol-level close, a
+  -- protocol-level error, and long inactivity on a terminated connection --
+  -- and assert only the observable invariant: the terminated client is
+  -- removed from the connected clients and the disconnect is notified
+  -- exactly once per terminated session.
+
+  it("should terminate the client on a transport read error", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    -- A transport read error terminates the session just like EOF does.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb("read failed", nil)
+
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once, got " .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+
+  it("should terminate the client on a protocol-level close", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    -- Complete the handshake so the session reaches the connected state.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, HANDSHAKE_REQUEST)
+
+    -- The client closes the session with a protocol close frame.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, build_client_frame(0x8, ""))
+
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once, got " .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+
+  it("should terminate the client on a protocol-level error", function()
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    -- Complete the handshake so the session reaches the connected state.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, HANDSHAKE_REQUEST)
+
+    -- A frame the session protocol cannot handle is a protocol error that
+    -- terminates the session.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, build_client_frame(0x0, ""))
+
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once, got " .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+
+  it("should terminate the client when the session stays inactive on a dead connection", function()
+    -- Take control of the mocked wall clock so the session's inactivity can
+    -- be exaggerated deterministically and restored afterwards.
+    saved_now = saved_now or vim.loop.now
+    local current_time = saved_now()
+    vim.loop.now = function()
+      return current_time
+    end
+
+    assert(server.start(config))
+    local notifications = observe_disconnects()
+
+    local client = simulate_client_connect()
+    assert(client_count() == 1)
+
+    -- Complete the handshake so the session reaches the connected state.
+    client.tcp_handle._read_cb(nil, HANDSHAKE_REQUEST)
+
+    -- Drive the server's periodic activity checks by invoking the callbacks
+    -- captured by the scheduled timers. Each invocation advances the mocked
+    -- clock by less than one timer interval, so no single wake-up can be
+    -- mistaken for the system having slept; repeated wake-ups while the
+    -- session stays silent let its inactivity accumulate until the server
+    -- gives up on the dead connection.
+    local timer_callbacks = collect_timer_callbacks()
+    assert(#timer_callbacks > 0, "expected the running server to have scheduled periodic activity checks")

+    while client_count() > 0 and step < 100 do
+      step = step + 1
+      current_time = current_time + 5000

+      end
+    end
+

+      step < 100,
+      "expected the server to terminate the long-inactive session on its dead connection after enough activity checks"
+    )
+    assert(
+      #notifications == 1,
+      "expected the server to notify the client disconnect exactly once, got " .. #notifications
+    )
+    assert(notifications[1] == client)
+
+    local count_after_disconnect = client_count()
+    assert(
+      count_after_disconnect == 0,
+      "expected no connected clients after the session terminated, got " .. tostring(count_after_disconnect)
+    )
+  end)
+end)

problem_statement:
Cannot create monitoring client (CloudWatch)
In a blank folder i create a deps.edn file with the following content:

```
{:deps {org.clojure/clojure          {:mvn/version "1.12.4"}
        com.cognitect.aws/api        {:mvn/version "0.8.774"}
        com.cognitect.aws/endpoints  {:mvn/version "871.2.41.2"}
        com.cognitect.aws/monitoring {:mvn/version "871.2.40.9"}}}
```

I start a repl and have the following interaction:

```
user> (require '[cognitect.aws.client.api :as aws])
nil

user> (def monitoring-client
        (aws/client {:api :monitoring}))
Execution error (FileNotFoundException) [HIDDEN].
Could not locate cognitect/aws/protocols/smithy_rpc_v2_cbor__init.class, cognitect/aws/protocols/smithy_rpc_v2_cbor.clj or cognitect/aws/protocols/smithy_rpc_v2_cbor.cljc on classpath. Please check that namespaces with dashes use underscores in the Clojure file name.
```

What am I missing?

### Additional contract requirements

An AWS service descriptor states which wire protocol(s) the service speaks in
two places:

* the legacy single-value `:metadata` `:protocol` key; and
* the newer `:metadata` `:protocols` collection, which lists the protocols
  the service supports in the service's preferred order.

Not every advertised value names a protocol this library can use for a
client. When a client is created, the protocol for that client is determined
as follows:

1. The values in the `:protocols` collection are considered in their
   advertised order, and the first value that names a protocol this library
   can use is selected.
2. If no advertised value names a usable protocol, the legacy `:protocol`
   value is used when it names a usable protocol.
3. If neither source yields a usable protocol, creating the client fails
   with a `clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo` that carries additional data
   (accessible via `ex-data`).

A descriptor that contains only the legacy `:protocol` key keeps working
exactly as before when its value names a usable protocol, and it fails as
described in rule 3 when it does not.

Observable through the public client API (`cognitect.aws.client.api`):

* Creating a client for the CloudWatch monitoring API,
  `(cognitect.aws.client.api/client {:api :monitoring ...})`, succeeds. The
  monitoring descriptor advertises a preferred protocol this library does
  not use, followed by protocols it does, so the client is created instead
  of failing.
* Operations invoked on a created client (`cognitect.aws.client.api/invoke`)
  are carried out according to the protocol determined for the client:
  request serialization, protocol-specific request headers, and response
  deserialization all follow that single determined protocol, so invocation
  behaves exactly as it would for a service whose descriptor simply
  declared that protocol.

exactly as before when its value names a usable protocol, and it fails as
described in rule 3 when it does not.

  `(cognitect.aws.client.api/client {:api :monitoring ...})`, succeeds. The

  of failing.

  request serialization, protocol-specific request headers, and response
  deserialization all follow that single determined protocol, so invocation
  behaves exactly as it would for a service whose descriptor simply
  declared that protocol.

+  "Return the best protocol that aws-api supports for the given service."
+  [service]

+            [cognitect.aws.client.api :as aws]
+            [cognitect.aws.credentials :as credentials]
+            [cognitect.aws.http :as http]
+            [cognitect.aws.service :as service]
+            [cognitect.aws.util :as util])
+  (:import [java.time Instant ZoneOffset]
+           [java.util UUID]))
+
+(set! *warn-on-reflection* false)
+

+;; of real AWS service descriptors, including the CloudWatch monitoring
+;; descriptor that motivated https://github.com/cognitect-labs/aws-api/issues/291.
+

+  {:metadata   {:uid              "sample-service-2026-01-01"
+                :protocol         "smithy-rpc-v2-cbor"
+                :protocols        ["smithy-rpc-v2-cbor" "json"]
+                :endpointPrefix   "monitoring"
+                :jsonVersion      "1.0"
+                :targetPrefix     "SampleService"
+                :signatureVersion "v4"}

+                          :input  {:shape "DoThingInput"}
+                          :output {:shape "DoThingOutput"}}}
+   :shapes     {:DoThingInput  {:type "structure" :members {}}
+                :DoThingOutput {:type    "structure"
+                                :members {:Greeting {:shape "Greeting"}}}
+                :Greeting      {:type "string"}}})
+

+  ;; Multiple usable entries in :protocols, and a legacy :protocol value
+  ;; that is usable but conflicts with the first usable advertised entry.

+                :protocol         "json"
+                :protocols        ["smithy-rpc-v2-cbor" "query" "json"]
+                :endpointPrefix   "monitoring"
+                :apiVersion       "2026-01-01"
+                :jsonVersion      "1.0"
+                :targetPrefix     "SampleService"
+                :signatureVersion "v4"}
+   :operations {:DoThing {:name   "DoThing"
+                          :input  {:shape "DoThingInput"}
+                          :output {:shape "DoThingOutput"}}}
+   :shapes     {:DoThingInput  {:type "structure" :members {}}
+                :DoThingOutput {:type          "structure"
+                                :resultWrapper "DoThingResult"

+                :protocols        ["smithy-rpc-v2-cbor" "json" "query"]
+                :endpointPrefix   "monitoring"

+                              :input  {:shape "ListMetricsInput"}
+                              :output {:shape "ListMetricsOutput"}}}

+                :ListMetricsOutput {:type "structure"

+                                  :credentials-provider stub-credentials-provider
+                                  :http-client          (stub-http-client
+                                                         request-bodies
+                                                         {:status  200
+                                                          :headers {}
+                                                          :body    (util/->bbuf body)})})]
+          (is (= {:Greeting greeting}
+                 (aws/invoke client {:op :DoThing :request {}}))
+              "responses must be parsed with the first usable advertised protocol (query here), not with the legacy :protocol value (json)")
+          (is (= ["Action=DoThing&Version=2026-01-01"] @request-bodies)
+              "requests must be serialized with the first usable advertised protocol (query here)"))))))
+
+(deftest monitoring-client-creation-regression-test
+  (with-redefs [service/service-description (fn [_] (monitoring-descriptor))]
+    (testing "creating a CloudWatch monitoring client no longer fails"
+      (is (some? (aws/client {:api :monitoring :region "us-east-1"}))
+          "the monitoring descriptor advertises an unusable preferred protocol; client creation must fall back to a usable advertised protocol instead of failing"))
+
+    (testing "monitoring operations run with a usable advertised protocol"
+      (let [request-bodies (atom [])]
+        (let [client (aws/client {:api                  :monitoring
+                                  :region               "us-east-1"
+                                  :credentials-provider stub-credentials-provider
+                                  :http-client          (stub-http-client
+                                                         request-bodies
+                                                         {:status  200
+                                                          :headers {}
+                                                          :body    (util/->bbuf "{\"Metrics\":[]}")})})]
+          (is (= {:Metrics []}
+                 (aws/invoke client {:op :ListMetrics :request {}}))
+              "ListMetrics responses must be parsed with a usable advertised protocol (json)")
+          (is (= ["{}"] @request-bodies)
+              "ListMetrics requests must be serialized with a usable advertised protocol (json)"))))))

problem_statement:
Feature request: Expose WebAuthn Signal API (signalUnknownCredential / signalAllAcceptedCredentials)
### Problem
                                                                                                 
This is a follow-up to #172, which described the situation where a passkey credential is deleted server-side but remains on the device. The user then picks the stale credential from the OS passkey picker, authentication fails, and there's no way for the app to clean it up programmatically.

That issue was closed with the conclusion that the platform doesn't support programmatic deletion — which is true for *direct* deletion, but the **WebAuthn Signal API** is a different and more appropriate mechanism that wasn't mentioned there.

### The Signal API

WebAuthn Level 3 introduced methods specifically for this problem that allow a relying party to signal to the platform that a credential is no longer valid, so it can be removed from autofill suggestions:

  - **`signalUnknownCredential(rpId, credentialId)`** — tells the platform that a specific credential is not recognized by the relying party
  - **`signalAllAcceptedCredentials(rpId, userId, allAcceptedCredentialIds)`** — tells the platform the full set of valid credentials for a user, allowing it to prune any others
  - **`signalCurrentUserDetails(rpId, userId, name, displayName)`** — updates user display info on stored credentials

Both Android and Apple platforms support this:

  - **Android:** [`SignalUnknownCredentialRequest` / `SignalAllAcceptedCredentialIdsRequest`](https://developer.android.com/identity/credential-manager/signal-api-rp) via `CredentialManager`
  (`androidx.credentials` 1.6.0-beta03+, Android 15+)
  - **iOS/macOS:** [`ASCredentialUpdater.reportUnknownPublicKeyCredential` /
  `reportAllAcceptedPublicKeyCredentials`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/authenticationservices/ascredentialupdater) (note: `ASCredentialUpdater` is deprecated as of iOS/macOS 26.2 in favour of `ASCredentialDataManager`, so both should ideally be supported)

### Requested Addition

New methods on `PasskeyAuthenticator` (or a separate utility class):

```dart
Future<void> signalUnknownCredential({
  required String rpId,
  required String credentialId,
});

Future<void> signalAllAcceptedCredentials({
  required String rpId,
  required String userId,
  required List<String> allAcceptedCredentialIds,
});
```

### Use Case

After a relying party returns an error indicating that a credential is not recognized, the app could call `signalUnknownCredential` to hint to the OS to remove the stale entry, preventing it from accumulating in the picker over repeated login attempts.

### Additional contract requirements

## WebAuthn Signal API support

The feature adds two signal calls that let a relying party send WebAuthn
Signal API hints to the platform so stale or superseded passkeys can be
pruned from the OS credential picker and autofill suggestions:

- **signalUnknownCredential** — tells the platform that a single credential,
  identified by its relying-party ID and credential ID, is no longer
  recognized by the relying party.
- **signalAllAcceptedCredentials** — tells the platform the relying-party ID,
  the user ID, and the complete list of credential IDs the relying party
  still accepts for that user, so any other credentials can be pruned.

### Public API

The public `PasskeyAuthenticator` facade gains two asynchronous signal
methods, each taking a single positional typed request object:

```dart
Future<void> signalUnknownCredential(
  SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType request,
);

Future<void> signalAllAcceptedCredentials(
  SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType request,
);
```

The request types are the same `SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType` and
`SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType` types described in the
platform-interface contract below, so the feature request's illustrative
named-argument shape is replaced by these typed request calls.

### Parameter semantics

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `relyingPartyId` | The relying-party identifier the credential(s) belong to. |
| `credentialId` | The Base64URL-encoded ID of the single credential that is no longer recognized by the relying party. |
| `userId` | The Base64URL-encoded ID of the user the credentials belong to. |
| `allAcceptedCredentialIds` | The Base64URL-encoded IDs of every credential still accepted by the relying party for that user. |

Every value supplied by the caller is delivered to the platform unchanged:
the relying-party identifier, and for `signalUnknownCredential` the single
credential identifier, or for `signalAllAcceptedCredentials` the user
identifier together with the complete list of accepted credential identifiers
in the caller-supplied order.

### Platform behavior

- Where the platform supports the WebAuthn Signal API, the hint is delivered
  to the underlying platform API with the supplied values so stale
  credentials can be removed from the passkey picker and autofill
  suggestions. The Android and Darwin platform packages deliver each of the
  supplied values, unchanged and in the caller-supplied order, to the
  host side over the plugin's Dart-to-host messenger. This contract is stated
  only in terms of the values delivered to the host side; it does not require
  any particular transport technology or generated API shape.
- On any platform or OS version without Signal API support, both calls
  complete normally without throwing and without any other effect; they are
  best-effort no-ops there.

### Platform-interface contract

So that platform implementations can deliver the hints, the shared passkeys
platform interface (`package:passkeys_platform_interface`) exposes the two
corresponding signal entry points:

```dart
Future<void> signalUnknownCredential(
  SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType request,
);

Future<void> signalAllAcceptedCredentials(
  SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType request,
);
```

Each entry point takes a single positional typed request object exported from
the platform-interface types library:

- `SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType` — immutable, with a `const`
  constructor taking named parameters `relyingPartyId` (`String`) and
  `credentialId` (`String`), exposed as fields with the same names.
- `SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType` — immutable, with a `const`
  constructor taking named parameters `relyingPartyId` (`String`), `userId`
  (`String`), and `allAcceptedCredentialIds` (`List<String>`), exposed as
  fields with the same names.

The public `PasskeyAuthenticator` signal methods must deliver the caller's
values to these platform-interface entry points exactly as supplied: the
relying-party ID becomes `relyingPartyId`, and the credential ID, user ID,
and accepted credential IDs become `credentialId`, `userId`, and
`allAcceptedCredentialIds` respectively, every value passed through unchanged
and in the caller-supplied order.

Overriding these entry points is optional for platform implementations: their
default behavior on the shared platform interface is a no-op that completes
normally, so platform implementations without Signal API support inherit the
best-effort no-op behavior for free. Platform implementations that do
override them must pass every request value through unchanged to the
platform.

### Delivery boundary of the Android and Darwin plugins

The observable boundary between Dart and the underlying platform API is the
plugin's Dart-to-host messenger. Every signal call must reach the host side
of that messenger unchanged and in the caller-supplied order. For the Android
and Darwin packages this boundary is exercised at the generated
transport-API surface as follows:

- For `signalUnknownCredential` the host receives, on the channel named
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_android.PasskeysApi.signalUnknownCredential`
  for Android and
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_darwin.PasskeysApi.signalUnknownCredential`
  for Darwin, a single message whose decoded payload is the ordered values
  `relyingPartyId`, then `credentialId`.
- For `signalAllAcceptedCredentials` the host receives, on the channel named
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_android.PasskeysApi.signalAllAcceptedCredentials`
  for Android and
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_darwin.PasskeysApi.signalAllAcceptedCredentials`
  for Darwin, a single message whose decoded payload is the ordered values
  `relyingPartyId`, then `userId`, then `allAcceptedCredentialIds`.

These conformance points document only how the host is invoked along the
existing messenger-based boundary; they do not require any particular
transport technology or generated API shape beyond the boundary defined here,
and they do not constrain how the host side forwards the values to the
underlying platform API.

Existing registration and authentication behavior is unchanged.

## WebAuthn Signal API support

The feature adds two signal calls that let a relying party send WebAuthn
Signal API hints to the platform so stale or superseded passkeys can be
pruned from the OS credential picker and autofill suggestions:

- **signalUnknownCredential** — tells the platform that a single credential,
  identified by its relying-party ID and credential ID, is no longer
  recognized by the relying party.
- **signalAllAcceptedCredentials** — tells the platform the relying-party ID,
  the user ID, and the complete list of credential IDs the relying party
  still accepts for that user, so any other credentials can be pruned.

### Public API

The public `PasskeyAuthenticator` facade gains two asynchronous signal
methods, each taking a single positional typed request object:

```dart
Future<void> signalUnknownCredential(
  SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType request,
);

Future<void> signalAllAcceptedCredentials(
  SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType request,
);
```

The request types are the same `SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType` and
`SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType` types described in the
platform-interface contract below, so the feature request's illustrative
named-argument shape is replaced by these typed request calls.

### Parameter semantics

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `relyingPartyId` | The relying-party identifier the credential(s) belong to. |
| `credentialId` | The Base64URL-encoded ID of the single credential that is no longer recognized by the relying party. |
| `userId` | The Base64URL-encoded ID of the user the credentials belong to. |
| `allAcceptedCredentialIds` | The Base64URL-encoded IDs of every credential still accepted by the relying party for that user. |

Every value supplied by the caller is delivered to the platform unchanged:
the relying-party identifier, and for `signalUnknownCredential` the single
credential identifier, or for `signalAllAcceptedCredentials` the user
identifier together with the complete list of accepted credential identifiers
in the caller-supplied order.

### Platform behavior

- Where the platform supports the WebAuthn Signal API, the hint is delivered
  to the underlying platform API with the supplied values so stale
  credentials can be removed from the passkey picker and autofill
  suggestions. The Android and Darwin platform packages deliver each of the
  supplied values, unchanged and in the caller-supplied order, to the
  host side over the plugin's Dart-to-host messenger. This contract is stated
  only in terms of the values delivered to the host side; it does not require
  any particular transport technology or generated API shape.
- On any platform or OS version without Signal API support, both calls
  complete normally without throwing and without any other effect; they are
  best-effort no-ops there.

### Platform-interface contract

So that platform implementations can deliver the hints, the shared passkeys
platform interface (`package:passkeys_platform_interface`) exposes the two
corresponding signal entry points:

```dart
Future<void> signalUnknownCredential(
  SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType request,
);

Future<void> signalAllAcceptedCredentials(
  SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType request,
);
```

Each entry point takes a single positional typed request object exported from
the platform-interface types library:

- `SignalUnknownCredentialRequestType` — immutable, with a `const`
  constructor taking named parameters `relyingPartyId` (`String`) and
  `credentialId` (`String`), exposed as fields with the same names.
- `SignalAllAcceptedCredentialsRequestType` — immutable, with a `const`
  constructor taking named parameters `relyingPartyId` (`String`), `userId`
  (`String`), and `allAcceptedCredentialIds` (`List<String>`), exposed as
  fields with the same names.

The public `PasskeyAuthenticator` signal methods must deliver the caller's
values to these platform-interface entry points exactly as supplied: the
relying-party ID becomes `relyingPartyId`, and the credential ID, user ID,
and accepted credential IDs become `credentialId`, `userId`, and
`allAcceptedCredentialIds` respectively, every value passed through unchanged
and in the caller-supplied order.

Overriding these entry points is optional for platform implementations: their
default behavior on the shared platform interface is a no-op that completes
normally, so platform implementations without Signal API support inherit the
best-effort no-op behavior for free. Platform implementations that do
override them must pass every request value through unchanged to the
platform.

### Delivery boundary of the Android and Darwin plugins

The observable boundary between Dart and the underlying platform API is the
plugin's Dart-to-host messenger. Every signal call must reach the host side
of that messenger unchanged and in the caller-supplied order. For the Android
and Darwin packages this boundary is exercised at the generated
transport-API surface as follows:

- For `signalUnknownCredential` the host receives, on the channel named
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_android.PasskeysApi.signalUnknownCredential`
  for Android and
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_darwin.PasskeysApi.signalUnknownCredential`
  for Darwin, a single message whose decoded payload is the ordered values
  `relyingPartyId`, then `credentialId`.
- For `signalAllAcceptedCredentials` the host receives, on the channel named
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_android.PasskeysApi.signalAllAcceptedCredentials`
  for Android and
  `dev.flutter.pigeon.passkeys_darwin.PasskeysApi.signalAllAcceptedCredentials`
  for Darwin, a single message whose decoded payload is the ordered values
  `relyingPartyId`, then `userId`, then `allAcceptedCredentialIds`.

These conformance points document only how the host is invoked along the
existing messenger-based boundary; they do not require any particular
transport technology or generated API shape beyond the boundary defined here,
and they do not constrain how the host side forwards the values to the
underlying platform API.

Existing registration and authentication behavior is unchanged.

problem_statement:
De-brand Crow from RadiusMethod
Sweep out remaining RadiusMethod ties. The repo already moved to `corveil/crow`, but several identity strings, the shipped bundle, and docs still reference RadiusMethod. Group the work into three tiers.

## Tier 1 — Hard identity ties (baked into the shipped app / project identity)
- **Bundle ID `com.radiusmethod.crow`** — `scripts/bundle.sh:81` (`CFBundleIdentifier`). The same reverse-DNS prefix is reused for internal GCD queue labels: `Packages/CrowIPC/Sources/CrowIPC/SocketServer.swift:23` (`com.radiusmethod.crow.socket`) and `Packages/CrowTelemetry/Sources/CrowTelemetry/Receiver/OTLPReceiver.swift:13` (`com.radiusmethod.crow.otlp-receiver`). Pick the new reverse-DNS [HIDDEN] and update all three. **Note:** changing `CFBundleIdentifier` affects notarization, macOS keychain/entitlement scoping, and defaults storage — treat as the one behavior-affecting change.
- **About-window copyright** — `Sources/Crow/App/AboutView.swift:48` renders `© <year> Radius Method`.
- **Signing-identity example** — `scripts/sign-and-notarize.sh:5` example string `Developer ID Application: Radius Method (TEAMID)` (comment/example only; the real Team ID is a CI secret).

## Tier 2 — Contact + repo-home references (docs)
- **Contact emails `security@radiusmethod.com`** — `SECURITY.md:7`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:40`.
- **`github.com/radiusmethod/crow` URLs** (now `corveil/crow`) — `README.md` (clone + releases), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/terminal-runtime-research.md`.

## Tier 3 — Placeholder/example strings (cosmetic sweep for consistency)
- `RadiusMethod` as the stock example workspace name (paired with fictional `acme-api`) and `RadiusMethod/crow` example issue URLs in: `skills/crow-workspace/SKILL.md`, `skills/crow-batch-workspace/SKILL.md`, the matching `Resources/*.template` files, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- Test fixtures hard-coding `radiusmethod/crow` / `radiusmethod/corveil` slugs in `Packages/CrowProvider/Tests/.../ProviderManagerTests.swift`, `Tests/CrowTests/IssueTrackerDedupTests.swift`, `Packages/CrowCore/Tests/.../AssignedIssueTests.swift`, `Packages/CrowGit/Tests/.../GitManagerTests.swift`. Pure test data — update for consistency, low risk.

## Acceptance
- `rg -i 'radius[ ._-]?method'` over the repo (excluding `.git`/`.build`/`vendor`) returns no hits.
- App builds, tests pass, and the bundle ID change is applied consistently across `bundle.sh` + both queue labels.

Decision to confirm during implementation: the replacement reverse-DNS / org name [HIDDEN].

[🐦‍⬛ Created with Crow via Cursor](https://github.com/radiusmethod/crow)

### Additional contract requirements

De-branding identity choices (public contract clarifications):

- The replacement organization and reverse-DNS identity for all "RadiusMethod" / `radiusmethod` / `com.radiusmethod` references is the Corveil organization:
  - GitHub organization / owner slug: `corveil` (canonical repository home: `https://github.com/corveil/crow`). All `github.com/radiusmethod/crow` links in documentation, attribution strings, and examples resolve to `https://github.com/corveil/crow`.
  - Reverse-DNS prefix: `com.corveil`. This applies uniformly to the shipped bundle identifier (new value: `com.corveil.crow`) and to every internal queue label previously using the `com.radiusmethod.crow.*` prefix (now `com.corveil.crow.*`).
  - The stock example workspace/owner name in documentation, skill files, and templates is `Corveil` (paired with the fictional `acme-api` repository), replacing `RadiusMethod` and `RadiusMethod/crow` example issue URLs.

- The replacement security/contact destination is private vulnerability reporting through the repository: `https://github.com/corveil/crow/security/advisories/new` (linked from `SECURITY.md` and `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`), replacing the `security@radiusmethod.com` contact email.

- Repo-wide sweep: outside of test fixtures and synthetic test data, and excluding the version-control checkout, build output, and vendored content (`.git`, `.build`, `vendor`), no `radiusmethod` / `radius-method` / `radius_method` / `radius.method` / `Radius Method` spelling of the previous organization identity remains anywhere in the repository.

problem_statement:
Rename `--ide` option to `--agent`, but keep `--ide` as an alias.
All internal APIs should also be renamed to match.

### Additional contract requirements

## Clarifications on the `--ide` → `--agent` rename

- The command-line flag is renamed to `--agent`. The legacy flag `--ide`
  remains usable as a command-line alias and behaves exactly like `--agent`.

- All library (internal/package) APIs that previously carried IDE-oriented
  names are renamed to their agent-oriented equivalents; there are no
  IDE-named compatibility aliases on library APIs. For example, across the
  agent model, agent detection, agent adapter/factory, skill installer, skill
  manifest, and command support APIs, the former enum, classes, methods,
  parameters, and helpers named `Ide`/`ide`/`ForIde` are renamed to
  `Agent`/`agent`/`ForAgent`.

+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
+
+/// Supported agents for skill installation.
+///
+/// The "generic" agent uses `.agents/skills/`. Antigravity, Codex, and generic are
+/// separate CLI options that all map here; only "generic" is stored in
+/// skills_config.
+enum Agent {
+  cursor('cursor', '.cursor/skills'),
+  generic('generic', '.agents/skills'),
+  claude('claude', '.claude/skills'),
+  copilot('copilot', '.github/skills'),
+  cline('cline', '.cline/skills'),
+  opencode('opencode', '.opencode/skills');
+
+  final String cliName;
+
+  /// Relative path from project root to the agent's skills/rules directory.
+  final String skillsRelativePath;
+
+  const Agent(this.cliName, this.skillsRelativePath);
+
+  /// Aliases that map to this agent in the CLI (e.g. antigravity, codex → generic).
+  List<String> get cliAliases => switch (this) {
+    Agent.generic => ['antigravity', 'codex'],
+    _ => [],
+  };
+
+  /// Returns the absolute skills directory path for this agent within [projectPath].
+  String skillsPath(String projectPath) =>
+      p.join(projectPath, skillsRelativePath);
+
+  /// Whether this agent is detected in the project at [projectPath].
+  ///
+  /// Copilot is excluded from auto-detection because its `.github/` marker
+  /// directory is commonly used for CI/CD and other purposes. Use `--agent
+  /// copilot` to install explicitly.
+  bool isDetected(String projectPath) {
+    return switch (this) {
+      Agent.cursor => Directory(p.join(projectPath, '.cursor')).existsSync(),
+      Agent.generic => Directory(p.join(projectPath, '.agents')).existsSync(),
+      Agent.claude => Directory(p.join(projectPath, '.claude')).existsSync(),
+      Agent.cline =>
+        Directory(p.join(projectPath, '.cline')).existsSync() ||
+            Directory(p.join(projectPath, '.clinerules')).existsSync(),
+      Agent.copilot => false,
+      Agent.opencode => Directory(
+        p.join(projectPath, '.opencode'),
+      ).existsSync(),
+    };
+  }
+
+  /// Parses a CLI name string into an [Agent].
+  /// Accepts canonical names and aliases (e.g. antigravity, codex → generic).
+  static Agent? fromCliName(String name) {
+    final lower = name.toLowerCase();
+    for (final agent in Agent.values) {
+      if (agent.cliName == lower) return agent;
+      if (agent.cliAliases.contains(lower)) return agent;
+    }
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  /// All valid CLI names (canonical + aliases) for --agent and help.
+  /// Sorted alphabetically with "generic" last.
+  static List<String> get cliNames {
+    final all = Agent.values
+        .expand((e) => [e.cliName, ...e.cliAliases])
+        .toList();
+    all.sort((a, b) {
+      if (a == 'generic') return 1;
+      if (b == 'generic') return -1;
+      return a.compareTo(b);
+    });
+    return all;
+  }
+
+  /// All valid CLI names as a comma-separated string.
+  static String get validNames => cliNames.join(', ');
+}
+
+/// Detects which agent is being used based on project directory markers.
+class AgentDetector {
+  const AgentDetector();
+
+  /// Auto-detects a single agent from project directory markers.
+  ///
+  /// Returns null if no agent or multiple agents are detected.
+  Agent? detect(String projectPath) {
+    final detected = detectAll(projectPath);
+    if (detected.length == 1) return detected.first;
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  /// Detects all agents present in the project based on directory markers.
+  List<Agent> detectAll(String projectPath) {
+    return Agent.values
+        .where((agent) => agent.isDetected(projectPath))
+        .toList();
+  }
+}

contract_addendum:
## Separated recording collections in the JSON format

This addendum makes the observable serialized representation of recorded
uses precise for `package:record_use`.

### Top-level shape

- Recordings of recorded uses are grouped under a single top-level
  object property named `uses`.
- The top-level `uses` property itself is optional: a document without
  any recorded uses either omits `uses` entirely or carries a `uses`
  object with no recordings; both represent zero recordings and are
  valid.
- The `uses` object has exactly two permitted properties, and no other
  property may appear on it:
  - `static_calls`: an array holding recordings of static calls.
  - `instances`: an array holding recordings of const instances.
  Both properties are optional: a document may record both kinds, only
  one kind, or no recordings at all.
- There is no combined `recordings` collection, and a consumer is not
  required to accept one. The separation between static calls and const
  instances is observable at every level: the two kinds of uses never
  appear in the same list.

### Recording entries

- Every entry of `static_calls` and of `instances` has an integer
  `definition_index` identifying the recorded definition, and a `uses`
  array listing the recorded uses of that definition.
- Both `definition_index` and `uses` are required on every entry, and
  `uses` must contain at least one recorded use.
- Each recording entry is closed: no other properties are permitted on
  it. In particular, legacy per-entry collection names such as `calls`,
  `instances`, or `static_calls` are not valid on a recording entry;
  they must be rejected as unallowed additional properties.
- The two entry kinds are exclusive: an entry in `static_calls` records
  only static calls to the definition, and an entry in `instances`
  records only const instances of the definition. A recording entry
  never carries the use fields of the other kind.

### Parsing zero recordings

- Parsing a document whose top-level `uses` object carries no
  recordings (an empty `uses` object) succeeds and yields zero
  recordings.
- Parsing a document with no top-level `uses` property at all likewise
  succeeds and yields zero recordings.
- The two zero-recordings representations are interchangeable: both

  whose `uses` object contains a non-empty `instances` collection.
- Serializing recordings with no recorded uses produces a document that
  represents zero recordings as described above.

  round-trip: the static-call recordings and instance recordings
  obtained after a JSON encode/decode cycle are equal to the original

problem_statement:
Failing to download files from volume if the file name contains a space
## Description

If a file in a volume contains a space in the name (e.g. `/Volume/catalog/schema/default/my custom report.txt`) then the function `db_volume_download_dir` will fail with either a HTTP2 error or a `curl_parse_url()` error.

 13.             Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂfailure_realm %||% url_parse(req$url)$hostname

 15.               Ã¢ÂÂÃ¢ÂÂcurl::curl_parse_url(url, baseurl = base_url)
Run rlang::last_trace(drop = FALSE) to see 4 hidden frames.
```

## Potential Root Cause

Spaces in volume paths should be encoded as `%20` as part of the request url. 

The output of `db_volume_list_files_recursive` is the standard file path like `/Volume/catalog/schema/default/my custom report.txt`.  This is used to create the request URLs against the files api. problem_statement:
HTML error responses break error message parsing
The Databricks REST API normally returns JSON errors, but gateways, proxies, and auth redirects can return empty, plain string, or HTML bodies instead. In the Databricks Python SDK, the response is run through an ordered chain of deserializers (empty, standard JSON, string, HTML) and falls back to the HTTP status when none match, so a non-JSON body never masks the real failure. This might be useful here as well since I've seen gateway errors where the error parsing has failed due to sending HTML instead.

### Additional contract requirements

## Error message handling requirements

When a Databricks REST request fails, the error body behavior is:

- For a standard JSON error body containing `error_code` and `message` fields,
  the reported error body is formatted as `{error_code}: {message}`.
- For a non-JSON error body (for example, an HTML or plain-text body returned
  by a gateway, proxy, or authentication redirect), the raw body text is
  reported as the error message.
- For an empty or unreadable error body, the reported error message falls back
  to the human-readable HTTP status description (for example, an empty body
  with status 504 reports `Gateway Timeout`).

When `dbConnect()` validation of the warehouse credentials fails, the error
raised to the caller must begin with a message identifying the failed
connection (including the warehouse ID) and must preserve the full details of
the underlying validation query failure, including both the HTTP status text
and any error-code detail contained in the original error message.

problem_statement:
[bug] joins with incorrect names should error out, not OUTER JOIN.
Pretty sure `join`s are buggy.

1. Load up Titanic dataset, call it`df`
2. Try the following: `df |> rightJoin ["Cats"] df`
3. Expected: `Column not found "Cats"`. But instead, got a successful join with 793881 rows. (This is equal to 891 * 891, with 891 being the number of rows in Titanic)
4. This leads me to believe that the columns are being full outer joined if the column doesn't exist.

PS - I think that this should be a beginner-friendly task so please farm it out!

### Additional contract requirements

For the join functions `innerJoin`, `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, and `fullOuterJoin`:

- When both inputs are non-empty (have at least one row), every requested join key must exist in both inputs. If any requested key is absent from either input, evaluating the join must raise an error that identifies an absent requested key; evaluating it must not return a join result. This holds whether the key is absent from both inputs or from only one input, and also when other requested keys do exist.

- `innerJoin` must report an absent requested key even when its left input has no rows.

- When at least one input is empty, `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, and `fullOuterJoin` must keep producing their established empty-input results even when a requested key is absent: left and right joins return the input on their preserved side, and full outer join returns the non-empty input.

- When all requested keys exist, existing join results are unchanged.

problem_statement:
Approach to universal constants? Dividing by units?
For example, in Unitful:
```julia
u"R"
```
(the gas constant) yields
```
8.31446261815324 J K^-1 mol^-1
```

With FlexUnits, I can similarly do
```
register_unit("R", 8.314ud"J/mol/K")
```
but if I _then_ try to divide by this, I find
```julia
julia> 10u"K" / u"R"
```
```
ERROR: promotion of types StaticDims{K} and StaticUnits{(m² kg)/(s² K mol), AffineTransform{Float64}} failed to change any arguments
Stacktrace:
 [1] error(::String, ::String, ::String)
   @ Base .\error.jl:54
 [2] sametype_error(input::Tuple{StaticDims{K}, StaticUnits{(m² kg)/(s² K mol), AffineTransform{Float64}}})
   @ Base .\promotion.jl:428
 [3] not_sametype(x::Tuple{StaticDims{…}, StaticUnits{…}}, y::Tuple{StaticDims{…}, StaticUnits{…}})
   @ Base .\promotion.jl:422
 [4] promote
   @ .\promotion.jl:405 [inlined]
 [5] /(u1::StaticDims{K}, u2::StaticUnits{(m² kg)/(s² K mol), AffineTransform{Float64}})
   @ FlexUnits C:\Users\iwheeler\.julia\packages\FlexUnits\gN0km\src\math.jl:205
 [6] /(q::Quantity{Float64, StaticDims{K}}, u::StaticUnits{(m² kg)/(s² K mol), AffineTransform{Float64}})
   @ FlexUnits C:\Users\iwheeler\.julia\packages\FlexUnits\gN0km\src\math.jl:183
 [7] top-level scope
   @ REPL[27]:1
 [8] top-level scope
   @ REPL:1
Some type information was truncated. Use `show(err)` to see complete types.
```

That case can be resolved by a judicious use of `q"R"` instead of `u"R"`, but the error message does not make that obvious. And going further, is the lack of a divide method for units a deliberate design decision, or just an oversight? This is something that "just works" with Unitful so it will almost certainly affect other people than just me.

### Additional contract requirements

This contract adds the following observable requirements, beyond the base problem statement.

## Regression: dividing by a registered scalar unit

After registering a scalar unit whose value carries a non-identity scaled
conversion to base dimensions — for example a gas constant registered as a
multiple of an energy-per-amount-per-temperature unit — the library must support
division by that unit without raising a promotion error:

* Dividing a quantity with static dimensions/units by such a registered unit must
  succeed and return a quantity whose value, reduced to base dimensions, equals the
  numerator's value divided by the registered unit's scale.
* Dividing a bare static dimension or unit by such a registered unit must succeed and
  return a unit whose dimension and scale match the corresponding quotient. This
  includes quotients whose numerator is itself a scaled static unit.
* Dividing by the registered unit must agree with multiplying by its inverse, and must
  produce an equivalent result whether the registered unit is referenced in static or
  dynamic form.

These requirements concern only observable values and dimensions; they impose no
constraint on the internal representation of units.

## Internal representation is not part of the contract

The hidden tests intentionally do not fix the concrete representation of static units
or static dimensions. In particular, they must not require:

* any specific concrete type, constructor, or helper for static units,
* `constructorof` on a static unit to return a specific concrete unit type,
* dimension queries to return values whose type matches a particular static/dynamic
  representation, or
* any specific internal string representation for unit or dimension concrete types.

Identities, conversions, equality/promotion behavior, and dimensions are asserted only

Approach to universal constants? Dividing by units?

u"R"
```

contract_addendum:
This contract adds the following observable requirements, beyond the base problem statement.

## Regression: dividing by a registered scalar unit

After registering a scalar unit whose value carries a non-identity scaled
conversion to base dimensions — for example a gas constant registered as a
multiple of an energy-per-amount-per-temperature unit — the library must support
division by that unit without raising a promotion error:

* Dividing a quantity with static dimensions/units by such a registered unit must
  succeed and return a quantity whose value, reduced to base dimensions, equals the
  numerator's value divided by the registered unit's scale.
* Dividing a bare static dimension or unit by such a registered unit must succeed and
  return a unit whose dimension and scale match the corresponding quotient. This
  includes quotients whose numerator is itself a scaled static unit.
* Dividing by the registered unit must agree with multiplying by its inverse, and must
  produce an equivalent result whether the registered unit is referenced in static or
  dynamic form.

These requirements concern only observable values and dimensions; they impose no
constraint on the internal representation of units.

## Internal representation is not part of the contract

The hidden tests intentionally do not fix the concrete representation of static units
or static dimensions. In particular, they must not require:

* any specific concrete type, constructor, or helper for static units,
* `constructorof` on a static unit to return a specific concrete unit type,
* dimension queries to return values whose type matches a particular static/dynamic
  representation, or
* any specific internal string representation for unit or dimension concrete types.

Identities, conversions, equality/promotion behavior, and dimensions are asserted only
through representation-independent observable results where possible.

problem_statement:
Add the tableIdentifier in the UCClient#getCommits API to support both uc client and uc delta client.
I left a comment in here https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6780/changes#r3243137766

Let's paste  here for the task: 

> This is wrong,  we shouldn't maintain a `concurrentHashMap` to cache the `tableId -> tableIdentifier` mapping. 

> but it's also exposing a serious problem for us, which is: the current `getCommits` API actually does not have the required tableIdentifier for uc delta client api,  so we will need to have a separate PR to add a `tableIdentifier` like the `commit` API where  we did in this PR https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6776. 

> So for this PR,  I will remove the entire implementation for the `getCommits` API, and make it unsupported directly. 

> Let's file a separate PR to focus on widening the `getCommits` to 

```java
public GetCommitsResponse getCommits(
      String tableId,
      TableIdentifier tableIdentifier,
      URI tableUri,
      Optional<Long> startVersion,
      Optional<Long> endVersion) throws IOException, UCCommitCoordinatorException {
```

The task is to add a `TableIdentifier` field in the `getCommits` to support both uc client and uc delta client.

### Additional contract requirements

The commit-coordinator REST client interface (`UCClient` in the storage module) exposes its
commit-history lookup through the `getCommits` API. That API must be widened from four
arguments to exactly five arguments, adding a table identifier of type
`io.delta.storage.commit.TableIdentifier`, in this parameter order: the table ID (String),
the table URI (`java.net.URI`), the table identifier, the start version
(`Optional<Long>`), and the end version (`Optional<Long>`). Exactly one such five-argument
overload must be exposed, and the table identifier must be the third argument — after the
table URI, mirroring the argument placement already used by the `commit` API.

The interface may additionally keep the previous four-argument overload as a bridging
default that delegates to the widened one, so existing consumers and implementors remain
source-compatible.

A caller may pass null for the table identifier when no identifier is available.

The token-based client used by the Unity Catalog client flow must return its commit data
through the widened API exactly as it did before.

The commit-coordinator client, when asked for the commits of a table whose table descriptor
carries an identifier, must forward that identifier — preserving the full two-segment
namespace and the table name — together with the Unity Catalog table ID stored in the
descriptor's configuration, rather than dropping the identifier or substituting null.

The delta-oriented token-based client variant must treat `getCommits` as not yet supported:
invoking it through the widened API with a non-null identifier must throw an
`UnsupportedOperationException` whose message contains the text
"getCommits is not yet supported".

All behavior already covered through the existing call path — successful commit retrieval,
required-parameter validation, and HTTP 404 target-table error handling — must behave the
same once the widened API is present.
