+// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Friedrich von Never <friedrich@fornever.me>
+//
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+module Generaptor.Tests.JobTimeoutTestSupport
+
+open System
+open System.Diagnostics
+open System.IO
+open System.Threading.Tasks
+open Generaptor
+open Generaptor.GitHubActions
+open TruePath
+open Xunit
+
+let private workflow = """# This file is auto-generated.
+on: {}
+jobs:
+  main:
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+"""
+
+let private RunScript(root: string, scriptPath: string): unit =
+    let startInfo = ProcessStartInfo()
+    startInfo.FileName <- "dotnet"
+    startInfo.WorkingDirectory <- root
+    startInfo.RedirectStandardOutput <- true
+    startInfo.RedirectStandardError <- true
+    startInfo.UseShellExecute <- false
+    startInfo.ArgumentList.Add "fsi"
+    startInfo.ArgumentList.Add scriptPath
+    startInfo.ArgumentList.Add "verify"
+
+    use process = new Process(StartInfo = startInfo)
+    Assert.True(process.Start(), "The regenerated script could not be started.")
+    let standardOutput = process.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()
+    let standardError = process.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync()
+    process.WaitForExit()
+    Task.WaitAll [| standardOutput :> Task; standardError :> Task |]
+    Assert.True(
+        process.ExitCode = 0,
+        $"The regenerated script did not verify the original workflow.\nstdout:\n{standardOutput.Result}\nstderr:\n{standardError.Result}"
+    )
+
+/// Regenerate a script from a workflow and verify that executing it reproduces that workflow.
+/// The test deliberately depends only on the YAML contract, not on a generated DSL member name.
+let AssertJobTimeoutRoundTrips(): unit =
+    let root = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), Path.GetRandomFileName())
+    let workflowDirectory = Path.Combine(root, ".github", "workflows")
+    Directory.CreateDirectory workflowDirectory |> ignore
+    try
+        let yamlPath = Path.Combine(workflowDirectory, "1.yml")
+        File.WriteAllText(yamlPath, workflow)
+
+        let generatedScript = ScriptGenerator.GenerateFrom(LocalPath workflowDirectory)
+        let packageReference = $"#r \"nuget: Generaptor.Library, {ScriptGenerator.PackageVersion()}\""
+        let assemblyPath = typeof<Workflow>.Assembly.Location.Replace("\\", "\\\\")
+        let localReference = $"#r \"{assemblyPath}\""
+        Assert.Contains(packageReference, generatedScript)
+
+        let scriptPath = Path.Combine(root, "regenerated.fsx")
+        File.WriteAllText(scriptPath, generatedScript.Replace(packageReference, localReference))
+        RunScript(root, scriptPath)
+    finally
+        if Directory.Exists root then Directory.Delete(root, true)

 """
     ]
     DoTest files
+
+let private IsFilteredTriggerCommand(command: string): bool =
+    command.StartsWith "onPushTo "
+    || command.StartsWith "onPushTags "
+    || command.StartsWith "onPullRequestTo "
+
+let private GeneratedTriggerCommands(workflowId: string, script: string): string list =
+    let startMarker = $"workflow \"{workflowId}\" ["
+    let rec skipUntilWorkflow (remaining: string list): string list =
+        match remaining with
+        | [] -> failwithf $"Workflow \"{workflowId}\" is not declared in the generated script."
+        | line :: rest when line.Trim() = startMarker -> rest
+        | _ :: rest -> skipUntilWorkflow rest
+
+    script.Split "\n"
+    |> Array.toList
+    |> skipUntilWorkflow
+    |> List.takeWhile(fun line -> line.StartsWith "        ")
+    |> List.choose(fun line ->
+        if line.StartsWith "            " then
+            None // inside a job body, not a workflow-level command
+        else
+            let command = line.Trim()
+            if command = "" || command = "[" || command = "]" || command = "[|" || command = "|]"
+               || command.StartsWith "job " then None
+            else Some command
+    )
+
+let private ReconstructedTriggerCommand(command: string): TriggerCreationCommand =
+    let argument(prefix: string) =
+        command.Substring(prefix.Length).Trim().Trim('"').Replace("\\\"", "\"").Replace("\\n", "\n")
+    match command with
+    | c when c.StartsWith "onPushTo " -> OnPushBranches [argument "onPushTo "]
+    | c when c.StartsWith "onPushTags " -> OnPushTags [argument "onPushTags "]
+    | c when c.StartsWith "onPullRequestTo " -> OnPullRequestToBranches [argument "onPullRequestTo "]
+    | c when c.StartsWith "onSchedule " -> OnSchedule(argument "onSchedule ")
+    | "onWorkflowDispatch" -> OnWorkflowDispatch
+    | _ ->
+        // Unfiltered triggers may be declared using any DSL shape: resolve the commands whose names
+        // correspond to parameterless cases of the TriggerCreationCommand union.
+        let commandName = (command.Split([| ' '; '(' |], StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries))[0]
+        let case =
+            FSharpType.GetUnionCases typeof<TriggerCreationCommand>
+            |> Seq.tryFind(fun case ->
+                (case.Name.Equals(commandName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
+                 || ("on" + case.Name).Equals(commandName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
+                && Seq.isEmpty(case.GetFields()))
+        match case with
+        | Some case -> FSharpValue.MakeUnion(case, [||]) :?> TriggerCreationCommand
+        | None -> failwithf $"Unrecognized trigger command in the generated script: \"{command}\"."
+
+let private RegeneratedWorkflowYaml(workflowId: string, triggerCommands: string seq): Dictionary<obj, obj> =
+    let wf = workflow workflowId [
+        for command in triggerCommands -> AddTrigger(ReconstructedTriggerCommand command)
+    ]
+    let yaml = Serializers.Stringify wf Map.empty TestFramework.MockActionsClient
+    DeserializerBuilder().Build().Deserialize<Dictionary<obj, obj>> yaml
+
+let private AssertUnfilteredTrigger(yaml: Dictionary<obj, obj>, expectedTriggerKey: string): unit =
+    Assert.True(yaml.ContainsKey "on", "The resulting workflow YAML must contain an 'on' section.")
+    let onSection =
+        match yaml["on"] with
+        | :? Dictionary<obj, obj> as section -> section
+        | other -> failwithf $"The 'on' section of the resulting workflow YAML must be a mapping, got: %A{other}"
+    Assert.True(onSection.ContainsKey expectedTriggerKey,
+                $"The resulting workflow YAML must contain the '{expectedTriggerKey}' trigger.")
+    match onSection[expectedTriggerKey] with
+    | null -> ()
+    | :? Dictionary<obj, obj> as filters -> Assert.Empty filters
+    | other -> failwithf $"The '{expectedTriggerKey}' trigger must not define filters, got: %A{other}"
+
+let private DoTriggerBehavioralTest(workflowId: string, expectedTriggerKey: string, files: (string * string) seq): unit =
+    let tempDir =
+        let path = Path.GetTempFileName()
+        File.Delete path
+        Directory.CreateDirectory path |> ignore
+        AbsolutePath path
+    try
+        for fileName, fileContent in files do
+            let filePath = tempDir / fileName
+            File.WriteAllText(filePath.Value, fileContent)
+
+        // Regeneration must complete successfully.
+        let script = ScriptGenerator.GenerateFrom(LocalPath tempDir)
+
+        // The regenerated script must not drop the trigger: the workflow must declare exactly one
+        // trigger command, and it must not impose any branch or tag filters.
+        let triggerCommands = GeneratedTriggerCommands(workflowId, script)
+        Assert.True(triggerCommands.Length = 1,
+                    $"Expected exactly 1 trigger command in the regenerated workflow, got {triggerCommands.Length}: %A{triggerCommands}")
+        Assert.False(IsFilteredTriggerCommand triggerCommands[0],
+                     $"Expected an unfiltered trigger command, got \"{triggerCommands[0]}\".")
+
+        // Executing the workflow declared by the regenerated script must result in workflow YAML where
+        // the expected trigger key is present without filters.
+        let yaml = RegeneratedWorkflowYaml(workflowId, triggerCommands)
+        AssertUnfilteredTrigger(yaml, expectedTriggerKey)
+    finally
+        Directory.Delete(tempDir.Value, true)
+
+[<Fact>]
+let PullRequestWithoutBranches(): unit =
+    DoTriggerBehavioralTest("1", "pull_request", [
+        "1.yml", """
+on:
+  pull_request:
+jobs:
+  main:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+"""
+    ])
+
+[<Fact>]
+let PushWithoutBranches(): unit =
+    DoTriggerBehavioralTest("1", "push", [
+        "1.yml", """

+  push:
+jobs:
+  main:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+"""
+    ])

problem_statement:
Cross-Validator: projection consistency and dual consistency checks
## Summary

Extend the cross-format validator with projection consistency checks and session type dual consistency verification.

Split from #105 (multi-party session amendments). Builds on completed work in #91/#112 (cross-format validator).

## Projection Consistency

When role definitions are present, verify that per-role projected ALPS profiles are consistent with the global SCXML and role definitions:

- Every transition in a projected profile exists in the global SCXML
- Every transition in the global SCXML appears in at least one role's projection (no orphaned transitions)
- Guard annotations in projected profiles match SCXML guard definitions
- SHACL shapes referenced by projected transitions correspond to shapes defined in Frank.Validation

## Dual Consistency (Wadler)

Verify that derived client duals are consistent with server projections:

- Every `must-select` obligation in a client dual corresponds to at least one available transition in the server's projected profile
- Every `session-complete` annotation appears only at final states in the global SCXML
- Client duals for complementary roles (e.g., PlayerX and PlayerO) are compatible — their interaction does not deadlock (subsumes #108 progress analysis with a stronger, type-theoretic check)

## Algebraic Law Verification

Verify composition laws from #124:

- Guard monoid laws: `compose identity g = g`, `compose g identity = g`, associativity
- TransitionResult functor laws: `map id = id`, `map (f >> g) = map f >> map g`

Checkable via property-based testing (FsCheck/Hedgehog):

```
frank validate --check-dual game.scxml --roles roles.json
frank validate --check-laws
```

## Dependencies

- #106 (Role Definition Schema)
- #107 (Projection Operator) — for projection consistency
- #124 (Foundation — algebraic composition) — for law verification
- #125 (Dual Derivation Engine) — for dual consistency

## Related

- #108 (Progress Analysis) — dual consistency subsumes deadlock detection
- #126 WP3 (session type duality integration for Validator)

### Additional contract requirements

# Projection-consistency validation contract

For this task, the required behavior is limited to projection-consistency
validation of role-annotated extracted statecharts. This scope replaces the
broader SCXML/ALPS artifact, client-dual, session-completion, SHACL, and
algebraic-law requirements in the original issue; those areas are not part of
this contract.

## Public surface

The `Frank.Statecharts` library exposes the public F# module
`Frank.Statecharts.Analysis.ProjectionValidator` with these types:

```fsharp
type Severity = Error | Warning

type ProjectionCheckKind =
    | Connectedness
    | MixedChoice
    | Completeness
    | Deadlock

type ProjectionIssue =
    { Check: ProjectionCheckKind
      Severity: Severity
      Message: string }

type ProjectionCheckResult =
    { Issues: ProjectionIssue list
      ChecksRun: int
      ResourceRoute: string }
```

`Severity` cases are qualified as `Severity.Error` and `Severity.Warning`.
The module provides these operations:

```fsharp
checkConnectedness: ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkMixedChoice: ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkCompleteness:
    Map<string, ExtractedStatechart> -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkDeadlock:
    Map<string, ExtractedStatechart> -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
validateProjection: string -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionCheckResult
```

The string supplied to `validateProjection` is returned as `ResourceRoute`.
A chart with no declared roles is outside projection validation and returns no
issues with `ChecksRun = 0`. A chart with roles runs all four checks and returns
`ChecksRun = 4`.

## Checks

1. **Connectedness** is a pre-projection check over every transition. An empty
   `RestrictedTo` list is an error because no role can trigger that transition.
   Every name in a non-empty restriction must name a declared role; each
   undeclared name is an error. An issue identifies the event, source, and
   target, and an undeclared-role issue also identifies that role.

2. **Mixed choice** examines restricted outgoing transitions grouped by source
   state. If those transitions collectively name two or more distinct roles,
   one warning identifies the source and roles. Unrestricted transitions do
   not contribute to the set of roles and do not suppress the warning.

3. **Completeness** compares a reachable global chart with its per-role
   projections. Every global transition absent from all supplied projections
   is an error identifying the event, source, and target.

4. **Deadlock** compares a reachable global chart with its per-role
   projections. A non-final state absent from the union of projection
   transition sources produces a warning naming the state. Final states are
   exempt.

`validateProjection` computes all role projections, prunes unreachable states
before the completeness and deadlock checks, and combines the issues from all
four checks. Connectedness and mixed choice remain pre-projection checks over
the original chart. Every issue records its check, uses the severity specified
above, and has a human-readable message.

## Dual Consistency (Wadler)

Verify that derived client duals are consistent with server projections:

- Every `must-select` obligation in a client dual corresponds to at least one available transition in the server's projected profile
- Every `session-complete` annotation appears only at final states in the global SCXML
- Client duals for complementary roles (e.g., PlayerX and PlayerO) are compatible — their interaction does not deadlock (subsumes #108 progress analysis with a stronger, type-theoretic check)

## Algebraic Law Verification

Verify composition laws from #124:

- Guard monoid laws: `compose identity g = g`, `compose g identity = g`, associativity
- TransitionResult functor laws: `map id = id`, `map (f >> g) = map f >> map g`

Checkable via property-based testing (FsCheck/Hedgehog):

```
frank validate --check-dual game.scxml --roles roles.json
frank validate --check-laws
```

## Dependencies

- #106 (Role Definition Schema)
- #107 (Projection Operator) — for projection consistency
- #124 (Foundation — algebraic composition) — for law verification
- #125 (Dual Derivation Engine) — for dual consistency

## Related

- #108 (Progress Analysis) — dual consistency subsumes deadlock detection
- #126 WP3 (session type duality integration for Validator)

# Projection-consistency validation contract

For this task, the required behavior is limited to projection-consistency
validation of role-annotated extracted statecharts. This scope replaces the
broader SCXML/ALPS artifact, client-dual, session-completion, SHACL, and
algebraic-law requirements in the original issue; those areas are not part of
this contract.

## Public surface

The `Frank.Statecharts` library exposes the public F# module
`Frank.Statecharts.Analysis.ProjectionValidator` with these types:

```fsharp
type Severity = Error | Warning

type ProjectionCheckKind =
    | Connectedness
    | MixedChoice
    | Completeness
    | Deadlock

type ProjectionIssue =
    { Check: ProjectionCheckKind
      Severity: Severity
      Message: string }

type ProjectionCheckResult =
    { Issues: ProjectionIssue list
      ChecksRun: int
      ResourceRoute: string }
```

`Severity` cases are qualified as `Severity.Error` and `Severity.Warning`.
The module provides these operations:

```fsharp
checkConnectedness: ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkMixedChoice: ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkCompleteness:
    Map<string, ExtractedStatechart> -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
checkDeadlock:
    Map<string, ExtractedStatechart> -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionIssue list
validateProjection: string -> ExtractedStatechart -> ProjectionCheckResult
```

The string supplied to `validateProjection` is returned as `ResourceRoute`.
A chart with no declared roles is outside projection validation and returns no
issues with `ChecksRun = 0`. A chart with roles runs all four checks and returns
`ChecksRun = 4`.

## Checks

1. **Connectedness** is a pre-projection check over every transition. An empty
   `RestrictedTo` list is an error because no role can trigger that transition.
   Every name in a non-empty restriction must name a declared role; each
   undeclared name is an error. An issue identifies the event, source, and
   target, and an undeclared-role issue also identifies that role.

2. **Mixed choice** examines restricted outgoing transitions grouped by source
   state. If those transitions collectively name two or more distinct roles,
   one warning identifies the source and roles. Unrestricted transitions do
   not contribute to the set of roles and do not suppress the warning.

3. **Completeness** compares a reachable global chart with its per-role
   projections. Every global transition absent from all supplied projections
   is an error identifying the event, source, and target.

4. **Deadlock** compares a reachable global chart with its per-role
   projections. A non-final state absent from the union of projection
   transition sources produces a warning naming the state. Final states are
   exempt.

`validateProjection` computes all role projections, prunes unreachable states
before the completeness and deadlock checks, and combines the issues from all
four checks. Connectedness and mixed choice remain pre-projection checks over
the original chart. Every issue records its check, uses the severity specified
above, and has a human-readable message.

+++ b/src/Frank.Cli.Core/Commands/UnifiedValidateCommand.fs
@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+module Frank.Cli.Core.Commands.UnifiedValidateCommand
+
+open System.IO
+open Frank.Resources.Model
+open Frank.Statecharts.Analysis.ProjectionValidator
+open Frank.Cli.Core.Unified
+open Frank.Cli.Core.Statechart.StatechartError
+
+type UnifiedValidateResult =
+    { ProjectionResults: ProjectionCheckResult list
+      TotalIssues: int
+      TotalErrors: int
+      TotalWarnings: int
+      ResourcesChecked: int
+      FromCache: bool }
+
+let private buildResult (fromCache: bool) (resources: UnifiedResource list) : UnifiedValidateResult =
+    let withRoles =
+        resources
+        |> List.choose (fun r ->
+            r.Statechart
+            |> Option.bind (fun sc -> if sc.Roles.IsEmpty then None else Some(r.RouteTemplate, sc)))
+
+    let results = withRoles |> List.map (fun (route, sc) -> validateProjection route sc)
+
+    let totalIssues = results |> List.sumBy (fun r -> r.Issues.Length)
+
+    let totalErrors =
+        results
+        |> List.sumBy (fun r -> r.Issues |> List.filter (fun i -> i.Severity = Severity.Error) |> List.length)
+
+    let totalWarnings =
+        results
+        |> List.sumBy (fun r -> r.Issues |> List.filter (fun i -> i.Severity = Severity.Warning) |> List.length)
+
+    { ProjectionResults = results
+      TotalIssues = totalIssues
+      TotalErrors = totalErrors
+      TotalWarnings = totalWarnings
+      ResourcesChecked = withRoles.Length
+      FromCache = fromCache }
+
+let execute (projectPath: string) (force: bool) : Async<Result<UnifiedValidateResult, StatechartError>> =
+    async {
+        if not (File.Exists projectPath) then
+            return Error(FileNotFound projectPath)
+        else
+            let projectDir = Path.GetDirectoryName(Path.GetFullPath(projectPath))
+
+            match UnifiedCache.tryLoadFresh projectDir force with
+            | Ok state -> return Ok(buildResult true state.Resources)
+            | Error _ ->
+                match! UnifiedExtractor.extract projectPath with
+                | Error e -> return Error e
+                | Ok resources -> return Ok(buildResult false resources)
+    }

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/Frank.Statecharts/Analysis/ProjectionValidator.fs
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+module Frank.Statecharts.Analysis.ProjectionValidator
+
+open Frank.Resources.Model
+
+[<RequireQualifiedAccess>]
+type Severity =
+    | Error
+    | Warning
+
+type ProjectionCheckKind =
+    | Connectedness
+    | MixedChoice
+    | Completeness
+    | Deadlock
+
+module ProjectionCheckKind =
+    let toString =
+        function
+        | Connectedness -> "connectedness"
+        | MixedChoice -> "mixed-choice"
+        | Completeness -> "completeness"
+        | Deadlock -> "deadlock"
+
+type ProjectionIssue =
+    { Check: ProjectionCheckKind
+      Severity: Severity
+      Message: string }
+
+type ProjectionCheckResult =
+    { Issues: ProjectionIssue list
+      ChecksRun: int
+      ResourceRoute: string }
+
+/// Pre-projection: every transition must be reachable by at least one role.
+/// RestrictedTo [] means no role can trigger it; stale role names are flagged.
+let checkConnectedness (statechart: ExtractedStatechart) : ProjectionIssue list =
+    let knownRoles = statechart.Roles |> List.map _.Name |> Set.ofList
+
+    statechart.Transitions
+    |> List.collect (fun t ->
+        match t.Constraint with
+        | Unrestricted -> []
+        | RestrictedTo [] ->
+            [ { Check = Connectedness
+                Severity = Severity.Error
+                Message =
+                  $"Transition '%s{t.Event}' (%s{t.Source} -> %s{t.Target}) has no role assignment (RestrictedTo [])" } ]
+        | RestrictedTo roles ->
+            roles
+            |> List.choose (fun role ->
+                if Set.contains role knownRoles then
+                    None
+                else
+                    Some
+                        { Check = Connectedness
+                          Severity = Severity.Error
+                          Message =
+                            $"Transition '%s{t.Event}' (%s{t.Source} -> %s{t.Target}) references unknown role '%s{role}'" }))
+
+/// Pre-projection: warn when different roles have exclusive transitions from the same state.
+/// Only RestrictedTo transitions contribute; Unrestricted transitions are fine.
+let checkMixedChoice (statechart: ExtractedStatechart) : ProjectionIssue list =
+    statechart.Transitions
+    |> List.choose (fun t ->
+        match t.Constraint with
+        | RestrictedTo roles when not roles.IsEmpty -> Some(t.Source, roles)
+        | _ -> None)
+    |> List.groupBy fst
+    |> List.collect (fun (source, entries) ->
+        let distinctRoles = entries |> List.collect snd |> List.distinct
+
+        if distinctRoles.Length > 1 then
+            let roleNames = String.concat ", " distinctRoles
+
+            [ { Check = MixedChoice
+                Severity = Severity.Warning
+                Message = $"State '%s{source}' has restricted transitions from multiple roles: %s{roleNames}" } ]
+        else
+            [])
+
+/// Post-projection: every pruned global transition must appear in at least one role's projection.
+let checkCompleteness
+    (projections: Map<string, ExtractedStatechart>)
+    (pruned: ExtractedStatechart)
+    : ProjectionIssue list =
+    let orphans = Projection.findOrphanedTransitions pruned projections
+
+    orphans
+    |> List.map (fun t ->
+        { Check = Completeness
+          Severity = Severity.Error
+          Message = $"Transition '%s{t.Event}' (%s{t.Source} -> %s{t.Target}) is not covered by any role's projection" })
+
+/// Post-projection: warn when a reachable non-final state has no outgoing transitions
+/// in any role's projection. This checks whether *any* role can advance the state machine
+/// (sufficient for HTTP where state is server-side), not per-role progress (which is #108).
+let checkDeadlock (projections: Map<string, ExtractedStatechart>) (pruned: ExtractedStatechart) : ProjectionIssue list =
+    let isFinal state =
+        pruned.StateMetadata
+        |> Map.tryFind state
+        |> Option.map _.IsFinal
+        |> Option.defaultValue false
+
+    let roleOutgoing =
+        projections
+        |> Map.values
+        |> Seq.collect _.Transitions
+        |> Seq.map _.Source
+        |> Set.ofSeq
+
+    pruned.StateNames
+    |> List.choose (fun state ->
+        if isFinal state then
+            None
+        elif Set.contains state roleOutgoing then
+            None
+        else
+            Some
+                { Check = Deadlock
+                  Severity = Severity.Warning
+                  Message = $"State '%s{state}' is reachable but no role has outgoing transitions from it" })
+
+/// Run all 4 projection checks. Returns 0 checks if statechart has no roles.
+let validateProjection (resourceRoute: string) (statechart: ExtractedStatechart) : ProjectionCheckResult =
+    if statechart.Roles.IsEmpty then
+        { Issues = []
+          ChecksRun = 0
+          ResourceRoute = resourceRoute }
+    else
+        let projections = Projection.projectAll statechart
+        let pruned = Projection.pruneUnreachableStates statechart
+
+        let issues =
+            [ yield! checkConnectedness statechart
+              yield! checkMixedChoice statechart
+              yield! checkCompleteness projections pruned
+              yield! checkDeadlock projections pruned ]
+
+        { Issues = issues
+          ChecksRun = 4
+          ResourceRoute = resourceRoute }

+module Frank.Statecharts.Tests.Analysis.ProjectionValidatorContractTests
+
+open System
+open System.Collections
+open System.Reflection
+open Expecto
+open Frank.Resources.Model
+
+let private transition event source target constraint' : TransitionSpec =
+    { Event = event
+      Source = source
+      Target = target
+      Guard = None
+      Constraint = constraint' }
+
+let private state isFinal : StateInfo =
+    { AllowedMethods = [ "GET" ]
+      IsFinal = isFinal
+      Description = None }
+
+let private chart states initial roles transitions : ExtractedStatechart =
+    { RouteTemplate = "/contract"
+      StateNames = states |> List.map fst
+      InitialStateKey = initial
+      GuardNames = []
+      StateMetadata = states |> Map.ofList
+      Roles = roles |> List.map (fun name -> { Name = name; Description = None })
+      Transitions = transitions }
+
+// Reflection lets the same executable suite describe a missing public API as a
+// normal failing test on the base revision, rather than failing test discovery
+// at compile time. All asserted names and shapes are part of the addendum.
+let private validatorType () =
+    let assembly = Assembly.Load("Frank.Statecharts")
+    let result = assembly.GetType("Frank.Statecharts.Analysis.ProjectionValidator", false)
+    Expect.isNotNull result "The public projection-validator module must be available"
+    result
+
+let private methodNamed name =
+    let result =
+        (validatorType ()).GetMethod(name, BindingFlags.Public ||| BindingFlags.Static)
+
+    Expect.isNotNull result $"ProjectionValidator must expose '{name}'"
+    result
+
+let private invoke name (arguments: obj array) =
+    try
+        (methodNamed name).Invoke(null, arguments)
+    with
+    | :? TargetInvocationException as ex when not (isNull ex.InnerException) ->
+        raise ex.InnerException
+
+let private property name (value: obj) =
+    let result = value.GetType().GetProperty(name, BindingFlags.Public ||| BindingFlags.Instance)
+    Expect.isNotNull result $"{value.GetType().FullName} must expose '{name}'"
+    result.GetValue(value)
+
+let private items (value: obj) =
+    (value :?> IEnumerable) |> Seq.cast<obj> |> Seq.toList
+
+let private issues result = property "Issues" result |> items
+let private intProperty name value = property name value :?> int
+let private stringProperty name value = property name value :?> string
+
+let private expectIssue check severity fragments issue =
+    Expect.equal (property "Check" issue |> string) check "Issue identifies its check"
+    Expect.equal (property "Severity" issue |> string) severity "Issue has the required severity"
+    let message = stringProperty "Message" issue
+    for fragment in fragments do
+        Expect.stringContains message fragment $"Issue message should contain '{fragment}'"
+
+[<Tests>]
+let tests =
+    testList
+        "ProjectionValidator public contract"
+        [ testCase "public module exposes the five validation operations"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              [ "checkConnectedness"
+                "checkMixedChoice"
+                "checkCompleteness"
+                "checkDeadlock"
+                "validateProjection" ]
+              |> List.iter (methodNamed >> ignore)
+
+          testCase "a chart without roles runs no projection checks"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input = chart [ "Only", state false ] "Only" [] []
+              let result = invoke "validateProjection" [| box "/no-roles"; box input |]
+              Expect.equal (intProperty "ChecksRun" result) 0 "No-role charts are out of scope"
+              Expect.equal (issues result) [] "No-role charts report no issues"
+              Expect.equal (stringProperty "ResourceRoute" result) "/no-roles" "Result identifies the resource"
+
+          testCase "a valid role chart runs all four checks without issues"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Open", state false ]
+                      "Open"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "refresh" "Open" "Open" (RestrictedTo [ "Admin" ]) ]
+
+              let result = invoke "validateProjection" [| box "/clean"; box input |]
+              Expect.equal (intProperty "ChecksRun" result) 4 "Role charts run exactly four checks"
+              Expect.equal (issues result) [] "A covered, progressing chart is valid"
+
+          testCase "connectedness reports an empty role restriction with transition context"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Active", state false; "Archived", state true ]
+                      "Active"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "archive" "Active" "Archived" (RestrictedTo []) ]
+
+              let found = invoke "checkConnectedness" [| box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 1 "The dead transition yields one connectedness issue"
+              expectIssue "Connectedness" "Error" [ "archive"; "Active"; "Archived" ] found.Head
+
+          testCase "connectedness reports every undeclared role name"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Active", state false; "Archived", state true ]
+                      "Active"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "archive" "Active" "Archived" (RestrictedTo [ "Admin"; "Ghost" ]) ]
+
+              let found = invoke "checkConnectedness" [| box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 1 "Only the undeclared role yields an issue"
+              expectIssue "Connectedness" "Error" [ "archive"; "Active"; "Archived"; "Ghost" ] found.Head
+
+          testCase "connectedness reports each undeclared role name separately"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Active", state false; "Archived", state true; "Removed", state true ]
+                      "Active"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "archive" "Active" "Archived" (RestrictedTo [ "Admin"; "Ghost"; "Phantom" ])
+                        transition "purge" "Active" "Removed" (RestrictedTo [ "Specter" ]) ]
+
+              let found = invoke "checkConnectedness" [| box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 3 "Every undeclared name in every transition yields its own issue"
+
+              for issue in found do
+                  Expect.equal (property "Check" issue |> string) "Connectedness" "Issue identifies its check"
+                  Expect.equal (property "Severity" issue |> string) "Error" "Issue has the required severity"
+
+              for (event, role) in [ "archive", "Ghost"; "archive", "Phantom"; "purge", "Specter" ] do
+                  Expect.exists
+                      found
+                      (fun issue ->
+                          let message = stringProperty "Message" issue
+                          message.Contains(event) && message.Contains(role))
+                      $"An issue identifies both '{event}' and '{role}'"
+
+          testCase "mixed choice warns for distinct roles at one source"
+          <| fun _ ->

+                      "Pending"
+                      [ "Manager"; "Clerk" ]
+                      [ transition "approve" "Pending" "Approved" (RestrictedTo [ "Manager" ])
+                        transition "reject" "Pending" "Rejected" (RestrictedTo [ "Clerk" ])
+                        transition "view" "Pending" "Pending" Unrestricted ]
+
+              let found = invoke "checkMixedChoice" [| box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 1 "Distinct restricted roles yield one warning per source"
+              expectIssue "MixedChoice" "Warning" [ "Pending"; "Manager"; "Clerk" ] found.Head
+
+          testCase "completeness reports a reachable transition omitted from every projection"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Active", state false; "Archived", state true ]
+                      "Active"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "archive" "Active" "Archived" (RestrictedTo []) ]
+
+              let projections = Map.empty<string, ExtractedStatechart>
+              let found = invoke "checkCompleteness" [| box projections; box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 1 "The orphaned transition yields one issue"
+              expectIssue "Completeness" "Error" [ "archive"; "Active"; "Archived" ] found.Head
+
+          testCase "completeness reports only the transitions missing from the projection union"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Open", state false; "Closed", state false; "Archived", state true ]
+                      "Open"
+                      [ "Admin"; "Auditor" ]
+                      [ transition "close" "Open" "Closed" (RestrictedTo [ "Admin" ])
+                        transition "archive" "Closed" "Archived" (RestrictedTo []) ]
+
+              let coveringProjection = { input with Transitions = [ input.Transitions.Head ] }
+
+              let projections =
+                  Map.ofList<string, ExtractedStatechart> [ "Admin", coveringProjection ]
+
+              let found = invoke "checkCompleteness" [| box projections; box input |] |> items
+              Expect.equal found.Length 1 "Only the uncovered transition is reported"
+              expectIssue "Completeness" "Error" [ "archive"; "Closed"; "Archived" ] found.Head
+
+          testCase "aggregate post-projection checks ignore unreachable states"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let input =
+                  chart
+                      [ "Start", state false; "Hidden", state false ]
+                      "Start"
+                      [ "Admin" ]
+                      [ transition "stay" "Start" "Start" (RestrictedTo [ "Admin" ])
+                        transition "hidden" "Hidden" "Hidden" (RestrictedTo []) ]
+
+              let result = invoke "validateProjection" [| box "/unreachable"; box input |]

+              expectIssue "Connectedness" "Error" [ "hidden"; "Hidden" ] found.Head
+

+
+              let completenessFound = byExpectedCheck "Completeness"

+              expectIssue "Completeness" "Error" [ "enter"; "Start"; "Idle" ] completenessFound.Head
+
+              let deadlockFound = byExpectedCheck "Deadlock"
+              Expect.equal deadlockFound.Length 2 "Every reachable non-final state without role progress is named"
+
+              for state in [ "Start"; "Idle" ] do
+                  Expect.exists

+              for issue in deadlockFound do

+
+          testCase "deadlock warns for a reachable non-final state with no role progress"

problem_statement:
Frank.LinkedData: projected content negotiation for multi-party sessions
## Summary

Extend Frank.LinkedData's content negotiation to support **role-projected ALPS profiles** — returning per-role filtered ALPS profiles based on the authenticated user's claims and the resource's current state.

Split from #105 (multi-party session amendments). Builds on completed work in #75 (Frank.LinkedData).

## Projected Content Negotiation

When role definitions are present on a `statefulResource` (#106), content negotiation for ALPS profiles should support **projection**:

- An authenticated request for `Accept: application/alps+json` evaluates the user's `ClaimsPrincipal` against the resource's role definitions
- The response contains only the ALPS descriptors available to the user's role(s) in the current state
- `ext` elements annotate the response with `projectedRole` and `protocolState`
- Unauthenticated or admin requests receive the global (unprojected) ALPS profile

[HIDDEN]

## Client Dual Content Negotiation

When an agent requests `Accept: application/alps+json` with a `Prefer: return=dual` header, serve the **client dual** — annotations that tell the client not just what it *can* do but what it *should* do:

- `clientObligation`: `must-select` (client must act to advance), `may-poll` (client can observe), `session-complete` (terminal state)
- Each `unsafe`/`idempotent` descriptor annotated with whether it **advances** the protocol or is a side-channel action

This extends the projected ALPS profile with additional duality annotations.

### Platform notes
- **CloudflareFS** (#121): Dual cached at edge per `(role, state)` pair since it's deterministic
- **BEAM** (#122): GenServer computes dual inline, no external state fetch

## Dependencies

- #106 (Role Definition Schema)
- #107 (Projection Operator)
- #125 (Dual Derivation Engine) — for client dual support

## Related

- #126 WP1 (session type duality integration for LinkedData)
- #124 (ALPS duality vocabulary)

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum refines the base problem statement. Where the two conflict, this addendum takes precedence.

## Role-projected ALPS profile selection uses Link headers

The evaluated feature is hypermedia-driven profile **selection**, not ALPS body
projection. ALPS profiles are served as separate resources at their own URLs; the
per-request resource response body is unchanged. The ALPS body-projection and
`Prefer: return=dual` client-dual descriptions in the base statement are **not**
part of the evaluated contract, and they place no observable requirements on the
implementation under test.

- When a global ALPS profile would be advertised for a resource
  that has role-specific ALPS profile projections, the response instead selects
  the `rel="profile"` entry of the `Link` header appropriate to the requesting
  user:
  - If the user has resolved roles (see below) and at least one resolved role
    has a profile projection for that resource's route, the `rel="profile"`
    entry of the `Link` header is replaced with the role-specific profile URL.
    The remaining Link entries are preserved unchanged, and when several
    resolved roles match, the first matching role (alphabetical order) wins.
  - If the user has no resolved roles, is unauthenticated, has no matching
    role projection for that route, or the response carries no `Link` header,
    the response is unchanged apart from the `Vary` header described below.
- Role names are matched case-insensitively.
- Every response for a route that has role projections includes a `Vary`
  header containing `Authorization` (RFC 7234 §4.1), whether or not the
  Link header was actually swapped.

## Resolved roles

Request-time role selection is driven by the user's **resolved roles**, a set of
role names exposed per request through the existing role-resolution mechanism
(`HttpContext` role feature, e.g. `GetRoles`/`SetRoles`). A typical pipeline
resolves roles from the authenticated user's `ClaimsPrincipal`, but the
implementation under test consumes resolved roles rather than claims directly.

## Role profile lookup

Role-specific profile links are pre-computed at startup from the loaded runtime
state:

- Each role-specific ALPS profile is keyed by a slug of the form
  `<resource slug>-<role name>` and is matched to a resource when its slug
  starts with that resource's slug followed by a hyphen; the remainder is the
  role name. Slugs that match no known resource are ignored, and when there are
  no role projections the lookup is empty.
- The selected profile entry is an RFC 8288 Link value of the form
  `<base-URI-trimmed-of-trailing-slash/role-slug>; rel="profile"`.

## Registration

Two web-host builder custom operations must exist:

- `useProjectedProfilesWith` registers the profile-selection middleware using
  an explicitly supplied runtime state. When the supplied state has no role
  projections, registration is a no-op.
- `useProjectedProfiles` auto-loads the runtime state from the entry assembly's
  embedded `model.bin`. When the entry assembly is unavailable or `model.bin`
  is missing or unreadable, registration silently degrades to a no-op (with a
  log message) and never throws.

The profile-selection middleware runs after the affordance middleware (which
supplies the base `Link` headers) and always invokes the rest of the pipeline.
problem_statement_base:
Frank.LinkedData: projected content negotiation for multi-party sessions
## Summary

Extend Frank.LinkedData's content negotiation to support **role-projected ALPS profiles** — returning per-role filtered ALPS profiles based on the authenticated user's claims and the resource's current state.

Split from #105 (multi-party session amendments). Builds on completed work in #75 (Frank.LinkedData).

## Projected Content Negotiation

When role definitions are present on a `statefulResource` (#106), content negotiation for ALPS profiles should support **projection**:

- An authenticated request for `Accept: application/alps+json` evaluates the user's `ClaimsPrincipal` against the resource's role definitions
- The response contains only the ALPS descriptors available to the user's role(s) in the current state
- `ext` elements annotate the response with `projectedRole` and `protocolState`
- Unauthenticated or admin requests receive the global (unprojected) ALPS profile

[HIDDEN]

## Client Dual Content Negotiation

When an agent requests `Accept: application/alps+json` with a `Prefer: return=dual` header, serve the **client dual** — annotations that tell the client not just what it *can* do but what it *should* do:

- `clientObligation`: `must-select` (client must act to advance), `may-poll` (client can observe), `session-complete` (terminal state)
- Each `unsafe`/`idempotent` descriptor annotated with whether it **advances** the protocol or is a side-channel action

This extends the projected ALPS profile with additional duality annotations.

### Platform notes
- **CloudflareFS** (#121): Dual cached at edge per `(role, state)` pair since it's deterministic
- **BEAM** (#122): GenServer computes dual inline, no external state fetch

## Dependencies

- #106 (Role Definition Schema)
- #107 (Projection Operator)
- #125 (Dual Derivation Engine) — for client dual support

## Related

- #126 WP1 (session type duality integration for LinkedData)
- #124 (ALPS duality vocabulary)

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/Frank.Statecharts/Affordances/ProjectedProfileMiddleware.fs

+namespace Frank.Affordances
+
+open System.Threading.Tasks
+open Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http
+open Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing
+open Microsoft.Extensions.Primitives
+open Frank.Statecharts
+
+/// Replaces the profile entry in a Link header StringValues with a role-specific value.
+/// Returns the original values unchanged if no profile entry is found.
+module LinkHeaderRewriter =
+
+    let private profileMarker = "rel=\"profile\""
+
+    let replaceProfileLink (existing: StringValues) (replacement: string) : StringValues =
+        let count = existing.Count
+
+        if count = 0 then
+            existing
+        elif count = 1 then
+            if existing.[0].Contains(profileMarker) then
+                StringValues(replacement)
+            else
+                existing
+        else
+            // Find the index of the profile entry using StringValues indexer
+            // (avoids ToArray which returns the backing array reference, not a copy)
+            let mutable profileIdx = -1
+
+            for i in 0 .. count - 1 do
+                if profileIdx = -1 && existing.[i].Contains(profileMarker) then
+                    profileIdx <- i
+
+            if profileIdx = -1 then
+                existing
+            else
+                let result =
+                    Array.init count (fun i -> if i = profileIdx then replacement else existing.[i])
+
+                StringValues(result)
+
+/// Appends a value to the Vary header without overwriting existing entries.
+module VaryHeader =
+
+    let append (ctx: HttpContext) (value: string) =
+        let existing = ctx.Response.Headers["Vary"]
+
+        if existing.Count = 0 then
+            ctx.Response.Headers["Vary"] <- StringValues(value)
+        else
+            let current = existing.ToString()
+
+            if not (current.Contains(value)) then
+                ctx.Response.Headers["Vary"] <- StringValues(current + ", " + value)
+
+/// ASP.NET Core convention-based middleware that replaces the global ALPS profile
+/// Link header with a role-specific one when the authenticated user has resolved roles.
+///
+/// Runs after AffordanceMiddleware (which sets the base Link headers).
+/// Additive: always calls next regardless of whether headers were modified.
+type ProjectedProfileMiddleware(next: RequestDelegate, roleLookup: RoleProfileLookup) =
+
+    member _.InvokeAsync(ctx: HttpContext) : Task =
+        let endpoint = ctx.GetEndpoint()
+
+        if not (isNull endpoint) then
+            let routeTemplate =
+                match endpoint with
+                | :? RouteEndpoint as re -> re.RoutePattern.RawText
+                | _ -> null
+
+            if not (isNull routeTemplate) then
+                match roleLookup.TryGetValue(routeTemplate) with
+                | true, roleMap ->
+                    // This route has role projections — Vary: Authorization applies to all
+                    // responses (RFC 7234 §4.1: Vary describes the selection algorithm,
+                    // not whether this specific response was affected).
+                    VaryHeader.append ctx "Authorization"
+
+                    let roles = ctx.GetRoles()
+
+                    if not (Set.isEmpty roles) then
+                        // First match wins; Set iteration order is alphabetical.
+                        let profileLinkValue =
+                            roles
+                            |> Seq.tryPick (fun role ->
+                                match roleMap.TryGetValue(role) with
+                                | true, v -> Some v
+                                | _ -> None)
+
+                        match profileLinkValue with
+                        | Some linkValue ->
+                            let existingLinks = ctx.Response.Headers["Link"]
+
+                            if existingLinks.Count > 0 then
+                                ctx.Response.Headers["Link"] <-
+                                    LinkHeaderRewriter.replaceProfileLink existingLinks linkValue
+                        | None -> ()
+                | _ -> ()
+
+        next.Invoke(ctx)

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+namespace Frank.Affordances
+
+open System
+open System.Collections.Generic
+open Frank.Resources.Model
+
+/// Pre-computed lookup for role-specific ALPS profile Link header values.
+/// Outer key: route template (e.g., "/games/{gameId}")
+/// Inner key: role name (case-insensitive via OrdinalIgnoreCase comparer)
+/// Value: formatted Link header value (e.g., "<https://example.com/alps/games-playerx>; rel=\"profile\"")
+type RoleProfileLookup = Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>>
+
+module RoleProfileOverlay =
+
+    /// Build a profile URL from base URI and slug, reusing the same format as AffordanceMap.profileUrl.
+    let private profileUrl (baseUri: string) (slug: string) : string =
+        let trimmed = baseUri.TrimEnd('/')
+        sprintf "%s/%s" trimmed slug
+
+    /// Build a role profile overlay from runtime state.
+    /// Returns a lookup mapping route templates to per-role profile Link values.
+    let build (state: RuntimeState) : RoleProfileLookup =
+        let lookup = RoleProfileLookup(StringComparer.Ordinal)
+
+        if Map.isEmpty state.Profiles.RoleAlpsProfiles then
+            lookup
+        else
+            // Build resourceSlug → routeTemplate(s) index
+            let slugToRoutes = Dictionary<string, ResizeArray<string>>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
+
+            for resource in state.Resources do
+                match slugToRoutes.TryGetValue(resource.ResourceSlug) with
+                | true, routes -> routes.Add(resource.RouteTemplate)
+                | false, _ ->
+                    let routes = ResizeArray<string>()
+                    routes.Add(resource.RouteTemplate)
+                    slugToRoutes.[resource.ResourceSlug] <- routes
+
+            // Match role slug keys against known resource slugs using prefix matching.
+            // Handles hyphenated resource slugs correctly (e.g., "tic-tac-toe-playerx"
+            // matched against known slug "tic-tac-toe" → role "playerx").
+            for roleSlugKey in state.Profiles.RoleAlpsProfiles |> Map.toSeq |> Seq.map fst do
+                let mutable matched = false
+
+                for slug, routes in slugToRoutes |> Seq.map (fun kv -> kv.Key, kv.Value) do
+                    if
+                        not matched
+                        && roleSlugKey.Length > slug.Length + 1
+                        && roleSlugKey.StartsWith(slug, StringComparison.Ordinal)
+                        && roleSlugKey.[slug.Length] = '-'
+                    then
+                        let roleName = roleSlugKey.Substring(slug.Length + 1)
+                        let url = profileUrl state.BaseUri roleSlugKey
+                        let linkValue = AffordancePreCompute.formatLinkValue url "profile"
+
+                        for routeTemplate in routes do
+                            match lookup.TryGetValue(routeTemplate) with
+                            | true, roleMap -> roleMap.[roleName] <- linkValue
+                            | false, _ ->
+                                let roleMap = Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
+                                roleMap.[roleName] <- linkValue
+                                lookup.[routeTemplate] <- roleMap
+
+                        matched <- true
+
+            lookup

+module Frank.Affordances.Tests.AffordanceTestHelpers

+/// Build a pre-computed affordance lookup dictionary for test scenarios.
+let buildAffordanceLookup (entries: (string * PreComputedAffordance) list) =
+    let dict = Dictionary<string, PreComputedAffordance>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
+
+    for key, value in entries do
+        dict.[key] <- value
+
+    dict
+
+/// Get a header value from the response, checking both response and content headers.
+let getHeaderValues (response: HttpResponseMessage) (name: string) : string list =
+    let mutable values = Seq.empty
+
+    if response.Headers.TryGetValues(name, &values) then
+        values |> Seq.toList
+    elif not (isNull response.Content) && response.Content.Headers.TryGetValues(name, &values) then
+        values |> Seq.toList
+    else
+        []
+
+/// Check whether a header exists in either response or content headers.
+let hasHeader (response: HttpResponseMessage) (name: string) : bool =
+    getHeaderValues response name |> List.isEmpty |> not
+
+/// Shared test affordance fixtures.
+let xTurnAffordance =
+    { AllowHeaderValue = StringValues("GET, POST")
+      LinkHeaderValues =
+        StringValues(
+            [| "<https://example.com/alps/games>; rel=\"profile\""
+               "</games/123/move>; rel=\"makeMove\"" |]
+        ) }
+
+let wonAffordance =
+    { AllowHeaderValue = StringValues("GET")
+      LinkHeaderValues = StringValues([| "<https://example.com/alps/games>; rel=\"profile\"" |]) }
+
+let healthAffordance =
+    { AllowHeaderValue = StringValues("GET")
+      LinkHeaderValues = StringValues([| "<https://example.com/alps/health>; rel=\"profile\"" |]) }
+
+/// Run a test against a configured test server with AffordanceMiddleware,
+/// disposing all resources on completion.
+let withAffordanceServer
+    (lookup: Dictionary<string, PreComputedAffordance>)
+    (featureSetter: HttpContext -> unit)
+    (configureEndpoints: IEndpointRouteBuilder -> unit)
+    (f: HttpClient -> Task)
+    =
+    task {
+        let builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder([||])
+        builder.WebHost.UseTestServer() |> ignore
+        builder.Services.AddRouting() |> ignore
+        let app = builder.Build()
+
+        app.UseRouting() |> ignore
+
+        (app :> IApplicationBuilder)
+            .Use(fun ctx (next: Func<Task>) ->
+                featureSetter ctx
+                next.Invoke())
+        |> ignore
+
+        (app :> IApplicationBuilder).UseMiddleware<AffordanceMiddleware>(lookup)
+        |> ignore
+
+        app.UseEndpoints(configureEndpoints) |> ignore
+
+        app.Start()
+        let server = app.GetTestServer()
+        let client = server.CreateClient()
+
+        try
+            do! f client
+        finally
+            client.Dispose()
+            server.Dispose()
+            (app :> IDisposable).Dispose()
+    }
+    :> Task
+
+/// Default test endpoints: /games/{gameId} and /health.
+let defaultEndpoints (endpoints: IEndpointRouteBuilder) =
+    endpoints.MapGet(
+        "/games/{gameId}",
+        RequestDelegate(fun ctx -> ctx.Response.WriteAsync("OK"))
+    )
+    |> ignore
+
+    endpoints.MapGet(
+        "/health",
+        RequestDelegate(fun ctx -> ctx.Response.WriteAsync("healthy"))
+    )
+    |> ignore

+/// Start a test server from a WebHostSpec. This exercises only the public
+/// WebHostBuilder registration operations and observes the resulting HTTP response.
+let private withSpecServer (spec: WebHostSpec) (featureSetter: HttpContext -> unit) (f: HttpClient -> Task) =
+    task {
+        let builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder([||])
+        builder.WebHost.UseTestServer() |> ignore
+        builder.Services.AddRouting() |> ignore
+        spec.Services(builder.Services) |> ignore
+        let app = builder.Build()
+
+        (app :> IApplicationBuilder)
+        |> spec.BeforeRoutingMiddleware
+        |> fun pipeline -> pipeline.UseRouting()
+        |> fun pipeline ->
+            pipeline.Use(fun ctx (next: Func<Task>) ->
+                featureSetter ctx
+                next.Invoke())
+        |> spec.Middleware
+        |> ignore
+
+        (app :> Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.IEndpointRouteBuilder)
+            .DataSources
+            .Add(TestEndpointDataSource(spec.Endpoints))
+
+        app.Start()
+        let client = app.GetTestClient()
+
+        try
+            do! f client
+        finally
+            client.Dispose()
+            (app :> IDisposable).Dispose()
+    }
+    :> Task
+
+let private buildSpec (state: RuntimeState) includeAffordances includeRoutes =
+    let ceBuilder = WebHostBuilder([||])
+    let initial = ceBuilder.Yield()
+
+    let withAffordances =
+        if includeAffordances then
+            ceBuilder.UseAffordancesWith(initial, AffordanceMap.fromRuntimeState state)
+        else
+            initial
+
+    let withProjection = ceBuilder.UseProjectedProfilesWith(withAffordances, state)
+
+    includeRoutes
+    |> List.fold
+        (fun spec routeTemplate ->
+            let endpoint =
+                resource routeTemplate {
+                    get (RequestDelegate(fun ctx -> ctx.Response.WriteAsync("OK")))
+                }
+
+            ceBuilder.Resource(spec, endpoint))
+        withProjection
+
+/// Split a header field value on top-level commas, ignoring commas inside
+/// angle brackets or quoted strings (RFC 8288 link-value lists).
+let private splitTopLevelCommas (value: string) : string list =
+    let segments = ResizeArray<string>()
+    let current = System.Text.StringBuilder()
+    let mutable inAngleBrackets = false
+    let mutable inQuotes = false
+
+    for ch in value do
+        if ch = '<' && not inQuotes then
+            inAngleBrackets <- true
+            current.Append(ch) |> ignore
+        elif ch = '>' && not inQuotes then
+            inAngleBrackets <- false
+            current.Append(ch) |> ignore
+        elif ch = '"' && not inAngleBrackets then
+            inQuotes <- not inQuotes
+            current.Append(ch) |> ignore
+        elif ch = ',' && not inAngleBrackets && not inQuotes then
+            segments.Add(current.ToString())
+            current.Clear() |> ignore
+        else
+            current.Append(ch) |> ignore
+
+    segments.Add(current.ToString())
+    segments |> Seq.toList
+
+/// RFC 8288 link-values carried by the response, whether they are exposed as
+/// separate header elements or combined into a single comma-separated field value.
+let private linkValues (response: HttpResponseMessage) : string list =
+    match response.Headers.TryGetValues("Link") with
+    | true, values ->
+        values |> Seq.collect splitTopLevelCommas |> Seq.map (fun value -> value.Trim()) |> Seq.toList
+    | _ -> []
+
+/// Vary field-names normalized to invariant lowercase, because HTTP field names
+/// in Vary values are matched case-insensitively.
+let private varyTokens (response: HttpResponseMessage) : string list =
+    match response.Headers.TryGetValues("Vary") with
+    | true, values ->
+        values
+        |> Seq.collect splitTopLevelCommas
+        |> Seq.map (fun value -> value.Trim().ToLowerInvariant())
+        |> Seq.filter (fun value -> value.Length > 0)
+        |> Seq.toList
+    | _ -> []
+
+let private get (path: string) (spec: WebHostSpec) featureSetter (assertion: HttpResponseMessage -> Task) =
+    withSpecServer spec featureSetter (fun client ->
+        task {
+            let! response = client.GetAsync(path)
+            Expect.equal response.StatusCode HttpStatusCode.OK "The resource should respond"
+            do! assertion response
+        })
+
+let private varyOnAuthorization =
+    "authorization"

problem_statement:
Improve type design: FoundStatefulResource, ProjectedArtifact, ProjectResult
## Context

Expert review of PR #182 (@7sharp9, Syme) identified type design improvements that can be done in one pass.

### 1. `FoundStatefulResource` DU → record carrier

The DU case now has 4 positional tuple fields, making pattern matches unwieldy (`FoundStatefulResource(route, _, _, _)`). The private `SyntaxStatefulResource` record already has the same shape.

**Change:** `FoundStatefulResource of SyntaxStatefulResource` — adding future fields won't break match sites.

### 2. `ProjectedArtifact` type refinements

- `Slug` is ambiguous (resource slug vs role slug) — rename to `ProfileSlug`
- Add `ResourceSlug: string` for provenance tracking
- Replace `IsGlobalOverride: bool` with `ArtifactKind` DU (`RoleProfile of roleName | GlobalOverride`)

### 3. `ProjectResult` naming

Name reads as "result of loading a project" — consider `RoleProjectionResult` or `ProjectCommandResult`.

All are type refactors with no behavioral change. One pass through extractor + command + tests.

### Additional contract requirements

The CLI's projection command must return a type named `RoleProjectionResult`; the previous result-type name for the projection command is replaced by `RoleProjectionResult`. This is an immutable, behavior-preserving rename: its fields and their meanings are unchanged (projected artifacts, orphan warnings, errors, output directory, cache-provenance flag).

Each projected artifact produced by the projection command exposes:

- `ProfileSlug: string` — the slug identifying the generated profile (replaces the former ambiguous `Slug`).
- `ResourceSlug: string` — the slug of the source resource, for provenance tracking. Every emitted artifact records the slug of its source resource.
- `Content: string` — the generated profile content.
- `FilePath: string option` — where the artifact was written, if written.
- `Kind` — a two-case artifact-kind classification replacing the former boolean override flag. One case, a role-profile kind, carries the role name (a string) for the role whose profile was projected; the other case, a global-override kind, carries no role name.

Behavior of the projection command's emitted artifacts:

- For a stateful resource that declares one or more roles, the projection emits one role-profile artifact per declared role and one global-override artifact for the resource. Each role-profile artifact's `Kind` carries that role's name, and its `ProfileSlug` is distinct per role. Every emitted artifact's `ResourceSlug` equals the source resource's slug.
- For a resource with no roles or no transitions (a global-only projection), the projection emits no artifacts.

Within the unified extractor, a syntax finding for a `statefulResource` computation expression is represented as a single record carrier value rather than four positional tuple fields. The carrier exposes the same information through named fields: the route template, the optional machine name, the state handlers (each with a case name and a list of HTTP methods), and the role names in declaration order.

All of the above are type-level and presentation-preserving refactors: behavior, output content, and observable results are otherwise unchanged.

problem_statement:
Consider sub-DUs for AlpsRole and AlpsDuality id fields
## Context

PR #135 introduced `AlpsRole of id: string * value: string` and `AlpsDuality of id: string * value: string` where the `id` field has a fixed set of legal values:

- `AlpsRole`: `"projectedRole"` or `"protocolState"`
- `AlpsDuality`: `"clientObligation"`, `"advancesProtocol"`, `"dualOf"`, or `"cutPoint"`

## Problem

Consumers must string-match on the `id` field to distinguish semantically different concepts, defeating the purpose of typed classification. A string with a fixed set of values is a DU trying to escape.

## Source

[SYME-IMPORTANT] and [AMUNDSEN-IMPORTANT] from expert review of #135.

## Recommendation

If the extension vocabulary grows, consider:

```fsharp
type AlpsRoleKind = ProjectedRole | ProtocolState
| AlpsRole of kind: AlpsRoleKind * value: string

type AlpsDualityKind = ClientObligation | AdvancesProtocol | DualOf | CutPoint
| AlpsDuality of kind: AlpsDualityKind * value: string
```

This preserves category grouping while giving consumers exhaustive matching on sub-kinds. The `[<Literal>]` constants in `Classification.fs` would map to these sub-DUs, and `getExtAnnotations` would map them back to string IDs for serialization.


-----

## v7.4.0 Implementation Plan

**Wave:** 1 (independent — no v7.4.0 dependencies)
**Dependencies within v7.4.0:** None
**Blocks:** #124 (foundation layer should build on typed sub-DU structure)
**Estimated scope:** Small

### Implementation approach

1. Define typed sub-DUs in `Frank.Statecharts.Core` AST types:
   ```fsharp
   type AlpsRoleKind = ProjectedRole | ProtocolState
   type AlpsDualityKind = ClientObligation | AdvancesProtocol | DualOf | CutPoint
   ```
2. Update `AlpsRole` and `AlpsDuality` DU cases: `AlpsRole of kind: AlpsRoleKind * value: string`
3. Update ALPS parser (`Classification.fs`) to map `[<Literal>]` string constants → sub-DU kinds
4. Update ALPS generator to map sub-DU kinds → string IDs for serialization
5. Update all pattern matches in consuming code (find via `| AlpsRole` and `| AlpsDuality` grep)
6. Existing ALPS round-trip tests must still pass — no new behavior, only stronger typing

### Key files
- `src/Frank.Statecharts.Core/Ast/Types.fs` — DU definitions
- `src/Frank.Statecharts/Alps/Classification.fs` — constants + mapping
- ALPS parser and generator modules

problem_statement:
HTTP-dereferenceable shape URIs for ALPS def
## Summary

ALPS `def` on transition descriptors currently uses `urn:frank:shape:` URIs (matching ShapeGenerator convention). Per Amundsen's guidance, `def` values should be dereferenceable HTTP URLs so agents can follow their nose from the ALPS profile to the SHACL shape.

## What to change

1. **Per-resource shape endpoints** — Serve SHACL shapes at `/shapes/{slug}` (e.g., `/shapes/games`), not just the current `/shapes/_project` monolith
2. **Fragment identifiers** — Each type within a resource's shapes gets a fragment: `{baseUri}/shapes/{slug}#MakeMove`
3. **Update `def` URI generation** — `resolveShapeUri` produces HTTP URLs using the baseUri available in the generator
4. **Content negotiation** — Serve shapes as `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json`, or `application/rdf+xml` based on Accept header

## Context

Introduced in #131 (role-aware SHACL shape references). The URN scheme is internally consistent but not dereferenceable. Amundsen (ALPS author) recommended HTTP URLs from the start, but per-resource shape endpoints are a prerequisite that was out of scope for #131.

## Dependencies

- #131 (introduces `def` on ALPS transition descriptors)
[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

## Contract addendum — HTTP-dereferenceable shape URIs

Each resource exposes its SHACL shape document at `GET /shapes/{slug}`. The
endpoint supports `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json`, and
`application/rdf+xml` according to `Accept`; an absent or unusable `Accept`
header defaults to `text/turtle`. Responses include `Vary: Accept`, and an
unknown slug returns 404.

For a resource with a non-empty base URI, every emitted ALPS `def` URI has the
form `{baseUri}/shapes/{slug}#{typeName}`. A trailing slash on the base URI is
normalized so that exactly one slash precedes `shapes`. The fragment identifies
the corresponding SHACL node shape in the document served by that resource's
shape endpoint. When no base URI is available, shape URI resolution retains the
`urn:frank:shape:` fallback.

The ALPS generator API provides `AlpsGeneratorOptions` in
`Frank.Statecharts.Alps.GeneratorCommon`. Its `DefBaseUri: string option` and
`ResourceSlug: string option` fields configure def emission. The option-bearing
functions `generateAlpsJsonWithOptions` and `generateAlpsXmlWithOptions` accept
those options followed by the statechart document. When both values are
provided, they emit `def` values for state and data descriptors; when either is
absent, they do not emit `def`. The existing `generateAlpsJson` and
`generateAlpsXml` functions remain the no-options variants and do not emit
`def` values.

+module Frank.Affordances.Tests.ShapeDereferencingTests
+
+open System
+open System.IO
+open System.Net
+open System.Net.Http
+open System.Text.Json
+open System.Xml.Linq
+open Expecto
+open Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder
+open Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http
+open Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost
+open Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
+open Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting
+open VDS.RDF
+open VDS.RDF.Parsing

+open Frank.Resources.Model
+open Frank.Statecharts.Ast
+open Frank.Statecharts.Alps.GeneratorCommon
+open Frank.Statecharts.Alps.JsonGenerator
+open Frank.Statecharts.Alps.XmlGenerator
+
+let private shapeEndpoint = "http://example.com/api/shapes/games"
+let private nodeShapeClass = "http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#NodeShape"
+let private rdfType = "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type"
+
+// The resource's served shape document contains a named node shape for every
+// descriptor in the ALPS fixture.  The subjects deliberately use the public
+// endpoint URI and fragment form, rather than an unrelated internal URI.
+let private shaclTurtleFixture =
+    """@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
+@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
+
+<http://example.com/api/shapes/games#gameState> a sh:NodeShape ;
+    sh:targetClass <urn:frank:type:gameState> .
+
+<http://example.com/api/shapes/games#position> a sh:NodeShape ;
+    sh:targetClass <urn:frank:type:position> .
+"""
+
+let private testProfiles: ProjectedProfiles =
+    { AlpsProfiles = Map.empty
+      RoleAlpsProfiles = Map.empty
+      OwlOntologies = Map.empty
+      ShaclShapes = Map.ofList [ ("games", shaclTurtleFixture) ]
+      JsonSchemas = Map.empty }
+
+let private generatorOptions: AlpsGeneratorOptions =
+    { DefBaseUri = Some "http://example.com/api"
+      ResourceSlug = Some "games" }
+
+let private buildDoc () =
+    { Title = None
+      InitialStateId = None
+      Elements =
+        [ StateDecl
+              { Identifier = Some "gameState"
+                Label = None
+                Kind = StateKind.Regular
+                Children = []
+                Activities = None
+                Position = None
+                Annotations = [] } ]
+      DataEntries = []
+      Annotations =
+        [ AlpsAnnotation(AlpsVersion "1.0")
+          AlpsAnnotation(AlpsDataDescriptor("position", Some(None, "Board position"))) ] }
+
+let private fetchShape (mediaType: string) =
+    let builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder([||])
+    builder.WebHost.UseTestServer() |> ignore
+    builder.Services.AddRouting() |> ignore
+    let app = builder.Build()
+    app.UseRouting() |> ignore
+    app.UseEndpoints(fun endpoints -> endpoints.MapProfiles(testProfiles)) |> ignore
+    app.Start()
+
+    use server = app.GetTestServer()
+    use client = server.CreateClient()
+    use request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/shapes/games")
+    request.Headers.Add("Accept", mediaType)
+    let response = client.SendAsync(request).Result
+
+    Expect.equal response.StatusCode HttpStatusCode.OK "Dereferencing the shape endpoint should return 200"
+    Expect.equal response.Content.Headers.ContentType.MediaType mediaType "The requested representation should be returned"
+    let body = response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().Result
+    (app :> IDisposable).Dispose()
+    body
+
+let private graphContainsNodeShape (subjectUri: string) (graph: IGraph) =
+    graph.Triples
+    |> Seq.exists (fun (triple: Triple) ->
+        match triple.Subject, triple.Predicate, triple.Object with
+        | (:? IUriNode as subject), (:? IUriNode as predicate), (:? IUriNode as obj) ->
+            subject.Uri.ToString() = subjectUri
+            && predicate.Uri.ToString() = rdfType
+            && obj.Uri.ToString() = nodeShapeClass
+        | _ -> false)
+
+let private parseTurtle (body: string) =
+    let graph = new Graph() :> IGraph
+    use reader = new StringReader(body)
+    TurtleParser().Load(graph, reader)
+    graph
+
+let private parseRdfXml (body: string) =
+    let graph = new Graph() :> IGraph
+    use reader = new StringReader(body)
+    RdfXmlParser().Load(graph, reader)
+    graph
+
+let private jsonContainsNodeShape (subjectUri: string) (body: string) =
+    use document = JsonDocument.Parse(body)
+
+    let rec visit (element: JsonElement) =
+        match element.ValueKind with
+        | JsonValueKind.Object ->
+            let hasSubject =
+                match element.TryGetProperty("@id") with
+                | true, value -> value.GetString() = subjectUri
+                | _ -> false
+
+            let hasNodeShapeType =
+                match element.TryGetProperty("type") with
+                | true, value when value.ValueKind = JsonValueKind.Object ->
+                    match value.TryGetProperty("@id") with
+                    | true, id -> id.GetString() = nodeShapeClass
+                    | _ -> false
+                | _ -> false
+
+            (hasSubject && hasNodeShapeType)
+            || (element.EnumerateObject() |> Seq.exists (fun property -> visit property.Value))
+        | JsonValueKind.Array -> element.EnumerateArray() |> Seq.exists visit
+        | _ -> false
+
+    visit document.RootElement
+
+let private assertDefDereferencesToNodeShape (defUrl: string) =
+    let fragmentIndex = defUrl.LastIndexOf('#')
+    Expect.isGreaterThan fragmentIndex 0 "A def URI should contain a type fragment"
+    let endpoint = defUrl.Substring(0, fragmentIndex)
+    let fragment = defUrl.Substring(fragmentIndex + 1)
+    Expect.equal endpoint shapeEndpoint "A def URI should target its resource shape endpoint"
+    Expect.isFalse (String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace fragment) "A def URI should name a concrete shape"
+
+    let subjectUri = endpoint + "#" + fragment
+    let turtle = fetchShape "text/turtle"
+    Expect.isTrue (graphContainsNodeShape subjectUri (parseTurtle turtle)) "Turtle must contain the def fragment as a SHACL node shape"
+
+    let jsonLd = fetchShape "application/ld+json"
+    Expect.isTrue (jsonContainsNodeShape subjectUri jsonLd) "JSON-LD must contain the def fragment as a SHACL node shape"
+
+    let rdfXml = fetchShape "application/rdf+xml"
+    Expect.isTrue (graphContainsNodeShape subjectUri (parseRdfXml rdfXml)) "RDF/XML must contain the def fragment as a SHACL node shape"
+
+let private jsonDefs (json: string) =
+    use document = JsonDocument.Parse(json)
+    document.RootElement.GetProperty("alps").GetProperty("descriptor")
+    |> fun descriptors ->
+        [ for index in 0 .. descriptors.GetArrayLength() - 1 do
+              let descriptor = descriptors.[index]
+              match descriptor.TryGetProperty("def") with
+              | true, def -> yield def.GetString()
+              | _ -> () ]
+
+let private xmlDefs (xml: string) =
+    let document = XDocument.Parse(xml)
+    document.Root.Elements(XName.Get "descriptor")
+    |> Seq.choose (fun descriptor ->
+        match descriptor.Attribute(XName.Get "def") with
+        | null -> None
+        | attribute -> Some attribute.Value)
+    |> Seq.toList
+
+[<Tests>]
+let shapeDereferencingTests =
+    testList
+        "ShapeDereferencing"
+        [ testCase "every ALPS JSON def fragment denotes a served SHACL node shape in every representation"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let defs = generateAlpsJsonWithOptions generatorOptions (buildDoc ()) |> jsonDefs
+              Expect.isNonEmpty defs "Configured JSON generation should emit def values"
+              defs |> List.iter assertDefDereferencesToNodeShape
+
+          testCase "every ALPS XML def fragment denotes a served SHACL node shape in every representation"
+          <| fun _ ->
+              let defs = generateAlpsXmlWithOptions generatorOptions (buildDoc ()) |> xmlDefs
+              Expect.isNonEmpty defs "Configured XML generation should emit def values"
+              defs |> List.iter assertDefDereferencesToNodeShape ]
