@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.Fixtures
+
+import java.io.{ByteArrayOutputStream, PrintStream}
+import java.net.URLClassLoader
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+import java.nio.file.{Files, Path, StandardCopyOption}
+
+import com.typesafe.config.ConfigFactory
+
+/** Test fixture: enables diagnostics for THIS forked JVM, calls `Diagnostics.printIfEnabled()`, and reports ONLY what that
+  * call itself emits to an observable sink:
+  *
+  *   - every event the call delivers to the diagnostics logger is captured through a test-owned appender attached around
+  *     the call (so an implementation that emits a logging event is always observed, whatever console appender state the
+  *     fork started with), and
+  *   - everything the call writes straight to the process console is captured at the same time.
+  *
+  * The captured sink output is then echoed to the fork's real stdout for the driving spec to inspect. When the call emits
+  * NOTHING to any observable sink, the fixture prints nothing and still exits 0 -- the spec distinguishes that silent run
+  * from emitted output that failed the redaction assertions, so an implementation that never emits a diagnostics event
+  * cannot satisfy the scenarios. It never changes production behavior nor any production internal state: it only attaches /
+  * detaches a test-owned appender and lets THIS freshly launched process resolve the driver-supplied operator configuration
+  * file through Typesafe Config's standard classpath-resource loading, exactly as an operator-launched process would.
+  */
+object DiagnosticsRenderMain {
+  private val FixtureRedactionConfigPath = "test.fixture.redactionConfig"
+
+  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
+    sys.props("picatinny.diagnostics.enabled") = "true"
+    deliverOperatorConfigViaStandardLoading()
+
+    val consoles = new ByteArrayOutputStream()
+    val realOut  = System.out
+    val tee      = new PrintStream(consoles, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name())
+
+    var logged: List[String] = Nil
+    try {
+      System.setOut(tee)
+      logged = ForkedLogCapture.infoMessages("org.galaxio.gatling.diagnostics.Diagnostics") {
+        org.galaxio.gatling.diagnostics.Diagnostics.printIfEnabled()
+      }
+    } finally {
+      tee.flush()
+      System.setOut(realOut)
+    }
+
+    logged.foreach(realOut.println)
+    val consoleText = consoles.toString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name())
+    consoleText.linesIterator.filter(_.trim.nonEmpty).foreach(realOut.println)
+  }
+
+  /** When the driver supplies a HOCON file, make it the application configuration resource `simulation.conf` of THIS freshly
+    * launched process: the operator settings are staged at the front of the standard classpath-resource resolution, layered
+    * OVER the library's own `simulation.conf` (its configuration underneath, exactly the standard priority the library's
+    * defaults carry for an operator-launched process). Every configuration read production then performs -- the first and only
+    * one in this freshly launched process, before any configuration object has been lineage-cached -- resolves
+    * `system properties > operator settings > library simulation defaults`, the documented operator channel, with the exact
+    * types the operator file declares: a genuinely list-valued setting stays list-valued (a comma-separated `-D` string would
+    * test a different interface from the documented HOCON setting) while real JVM `-D` arguments keep their higher priority.
+    * Test-owned: it only stages files in the fork's own temporary directory and adjusts THIS process's own resource loading;
+    * it never touches production objects or state.
+    */
+  private def deliverOperatorConfigViaStandardLoading(): Unit =
+    sys.props.get(FixtureRedactionConfigPath).foreach { operatorFilePath =>
+      val directory = stageOperatorSimulationConf(java.nio.file.Paths.get(operatorFilePath))
+      // The standard resource resolution consults the current thread's context classloader.
+      Thread.currentThread().setContextClassLoader(childFirstLoader(directory))
+      ConfigFactory.invalidateCaches()
+    }
+
+  /** Stages the operator HOCON file as a front-of-classpath `simulation.conf` that falls back to the library's own
+    * `simulation.conf`, and returns the staging directory. An included resource is always LOWER precedence than the file that
+    * includes it, so the operator settings override the library defaults exactly like an operator's own configuration layered
+    * over the shipped defaults. Test-owned: only stages copies in the fork process's own temporary directory.
+    */
+  private def stageOperatorSimulationConf(operatorFile: Path): java.io.File = {
+    val directory = Files.createTempDirectory("picatinny-operator-config").toFile
+    directory.deleteOnExit()
+
+    val libraryDefaults = new java.io.File(directory, "picatinny-library-simulation.conf")
+    val libraryStream   = getClass.getClassLoader.getResourceAsStream("simulation.conf")
+    if (libraryStream == null) Files.write(libraryDefaults.toPath, Array.emptyByteArray)
+    else
+      try Files.copy(libraryStream, libraryDefaults.toPath, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING)
+      finally libraryStream.close()
+    libraryDefaults.deleteOnExit()
+
+    val staged    = new java.io.File(directory, "simulation.conf")
+    val stagedSrc =
+      "# Application configuration for THIS forked process: operator settings layered over the library's simulation defaults.\n" +
+        "include \"picatinny-library-simulation.conf\"\n" +
+        new String(Files.readAllBytes(operatorFile), StandardCharsets.UTF_8) + "\n"
+    Files.write(staged.toPath, stagedSrc.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
+    staged.deleteOnExit()
+    directory
+  }
+
+  /** A class loader that resolves classpath resources from the staging directory FIRST (child-first), delegating everything
+    * else to the fork's normal loader, so the staged `simulation.conf` is the one the standard configuration resolution finds
+    * while every class and every other resource still resolves exactly as the forked JVM would resolve it. */
+  private def childFirstLoader(directory: java.io.File): ClassLoader = {
+    val delegate: ClassLoader = getClass.getClassLoader
+    new URLClassLoader(Array(directory.toURI.toURL), null) {
+      override def getResource(name: String): java.net.URL = {
+        val own = findResource(name)
+        if (own != null) own else delegate.getResource(name)
+      }
+
+      override def getResources(name: String): java.util.Enumeration[java.net.URL] = {
+        val all = new java.util.Vector[java.net.URL]()
+        val own = findResources(name)
+        while (own.hasMoreElements) all.add(own.nextElement())
+        val parentResources = delegate.getResources(name)
+        val ownStrings      = (0 until all.size()).map(all.get(_).toString).toSet
+        while (parentResources.hasMoreElements) {
+          val url = parentResources.nextElement()
+          if (!ownStrings(url.toString)) all.add(url)
+        }
+        all.elements()
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+}

+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.Fixtures
+
+import ch.qos.logback.classic.Level
+import ch.qos.logback.classic.spi.ILoggingEvent
+import ch.qos.logback.core.AppenderBase
+import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
+
+import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue
+import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters._
+
+/** Minimal INFO+ log capture usable from fork-side fixture mains. Same capture contract as the in-process
+  * `org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.LogCapture`, but sandboxed to THIS (already isolated, driver-owned) JVM: no cross-process
+  * sharing exists here, so events are returned unfiltered. It depends only on logback/SLF4J types that already exist and never
+  * references the production implementation under test.
+  */
+private[Fixtures] object ForkedLogCapture {
+
+  def infoMessages(loggerName: String)(body: => Unit): List[String] = {
+    val logger        = logbackLogger(loggerName)
+    val captured      = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue[ILoggingEvent]()
+    val appender      = new AppenderBase[ILoggingEvent] {
+      override def append(event: ILoggingEvent): Unit = captured.add(event)
+    }
+    appender.start()
+    val previousLevel = logger.getLevel
+    logger.setLevel(Level.INFO)
+    logger.addAppender(appender)
+    try body
+    finally {
+      logger.detachAppender(appender)
+      logger.setLevel(previousLevel)
+    }
+    captured.asScala.iterator.map(_.getFormattedMessage).toList
+  }
+
+  @annotation.tailrec
+  private def logbackLogger(loggerName: String, attemptsLeft: Int = 2000): ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger =
+    LoggerFactory.getLogger(loggerName) match {
+      case logback: ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger => logback
+      case _ if attemptsLeft > 0                  => Thread.sleep(1); logbackLogger(loggerName, attemptsLeft - 1)
+      case other                                  => other.asInstanceOf[ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger]
+    }
+}

+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.Fixtures

+/** Generic driver main that every JVM-isolated scenario runs through: it applies exactly the driver-controlled properties to
+  * THIS freshly launched JVM (which no concurrently running spec can touch), refreshes the global configuration resolution
+  * cache so the new driver properties take effect, then delegates to the scenario's fixture main. Test-owned: it only adjusts
+  * ITS OWN process before observing it; it never changes production behavior.

+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.Fixtures
+
+import org.galaxio.gatling.diagnostics.StartupBanner
+
+/** Test fixture main: renders the startup banner exactly once against the driver-controlled configuration and reports its Base
+  * URL, then runs the banner's REAL emission (`StartupBanner.printIfEnabled()`, the very call production gatekeepers invoke)
+  * while every output shape an emitter can take is intercepted, and reports the emitted banner reconstructed from that
+  * observation -- never from a re-render:
+  *
+  * {{{
+  *   RENDERED| <Base URL value from the banner's one rendering>
+  *   VERDICT| <the driver verdict line received on stdin>
+  *   EMITTED| <Base URL value observed in the banner the real emission delivered, or <emission-silent>>
+  *   EMISSION| <line>   (each emitted banner line, quoted verbatim)
+  * }}}
+  *
+  * Both sinks a banner emitter can use are captured at once, so ANY emitter shape is observed: Scala `Console` output for
+  * `println`-style emitters (`Console.withOut` intercepts `println` even when it writes through `Console.out` rather than the
+  * raw `System.out` stream), and the formatted SLF4J/logging events of logging emitters through the test-owned in-memory
+  * appender attached around the call. The fixture only observes and reports; it never changes production behavior.
+  */
+object StartupBannerEmissionMain {
+
+  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
+    val rendered = baseUrlOf(renderBanner())
+    println(s"RENDERED| $rendered")
+    println("READY| await-driver-verdict")
+    System.out.flush()
+    val verdict  = Option(scala.io.StdIn.readLine()).getOrElse("<driver-missing>")
+    println(s"VERDICT| $verdict")
+
+    val emitted = emitBannerOnce()
+    println(s"EMITTED| ${emitted.map(_._1).getOrElse("<emission-silent>")}")
+    emitted.foreach { case (_, bannerLines) =>
+      bannerLines.foreach(line => println(s"EMISSION| $line"))
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Enables the banner for this fork, then calls `StartupBanner.printIfEnabled()` exactly once with Scala `Console` output
+    * captured (println-style sinks) and a test-owned appender collecting the formatted logger events emitted while the call
+    * runs (logging sinks). When the call emitted anything, the emitted banner's Base URL line plus every captured banner line
+    * are returned -- the banner as EMITTED, never the fixture's own rendering.
+    */
+  private def emitBannerOnce(): Option[(String, Seq[String])] = {
+    sys.props("picatinny.startup.banner.enabled") = "true"
+    com.typesafe.config.ConfigFactory.invalidateCaches()
+
+    val capture       = new java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream()
+    val capturedOut   = new java.io.PrintStream(capture, true, java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name())
+    var logged: List[String] = Nil
+    scala.Console.withOut(capturedOut) {
+      logged = ForkedLogCapture.infoMessages("org.galaxio.gatling.diagnostics") {
+        StartupBanner.printIfEnabled()
+      }
+    }
+    capturedOut.flush()
+
+    val consoleText = capture.toString(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name())
+    val consoleLines = consoleText.linesIterator.filter(_.trim.nonEmpty).toSeq
+
+    pickBannerBlock(logged)
+      .orElse(pickBannerBlock(consoleLines))
+      .map { bannerLines =>
+        baseUrlOf(bannerLines.mkString("\n")) -> bannerLines
+      }
+  }
+
+  /** Extracts the banner block from captured lines: it starts above the first line that mentions "Picatinny Gatling Run" (the
+    * banner headline) or, failing that, the first line mentioning "Base URL", and runs to the captured lines' end. Returns
+    * `None` when the captured lines carry no banner at all. Only emitted lines enter; nothing is re-rendered here.
+    */
+  private def pickBannerBlock(capturedLines: Seq[String]): Option[Seq[String]] = {
+    val headlineIdx  = capturedLines.indexWhere(_.contains("Picatinny Gatling Run"))
+    val baseUrlIdx   = capturedLines.indexWhere(_.contains("Base URL"))
+    val anchorIdx    = Seq(headlineIdx, baseUrlIdx).filter(_ >= 0) match {
+      case Seq() => return None
+      case idxs  => idxs.min
+    }
+    val from         = capturedLines.drop((anchorIdx - 2).max(0)).filter(_.trim.nonEmpty)
+    if (from.isEmpty) None else Some(from)
+  }
+
+  private def renderBanner(): String = {
+    val module = Class.forName("org.galaxio.gatling.diagnostics.StartupBanner$").getField("MODULE$").get(null)
+    val render = module.getClass.getDeclaredMethods
+      .find(m => m.getName == "render" && m.getParameterCount == 0)
+      .getOrElse(throw new NoSuchMethodException("render"))
+    render.setAccessible(true)
+    render.invoke(module).toString
+  }
+
+  private def baseUrlOf(bannerText: String): String =
+    bannerText.linesIterator
+      .find(_.contains("Base URL"))
+      .map(_.split("Base URL", 2).lift(1).map(_.dropWhile(c => c == ' ' || c == ':').trim).getOrElse(""))
+      .filter(_.nonEmpty)
+      .getOrElse("<no Base URL line>")
+}

+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil
+
+import java.io.File
+import scala.io.Source
+import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters._
+
+/** Runs a main class from the test classpath in a fresh, separate JVM process. The management-factory input arguments
+  * (`-Dkey=value`) of the already-running test JVM cannot be changed, so scenarios that depend on a specific argument set
+  * launch a forked JVM that has exactly those arguments. Test-owned: it only starts child processes and collects their output;
+  * it never changes production behavior.
+  */
+object ForkedJvm {
+
+  final case class Result(exitCode: Int, stdout: String, stderr: String)
+
+  /** Start `mainClass` with `vmArgs` as JVM input arguments and `args` as program arguments, wait for completion and collect
+    * stdout/stderr. Deterministic: output is fully drained on dedicated threads and the wait is bounded.
+    */
+  def run(mainClass: String, vmArgs: Seq[String] = Nil, args: Seq[String] = Nil, timeoutSeconds: Long = 180): Result = {
+    val cp                     = effectiveClasspath
+    val command                = Seq(javaBinary) ++ vmArgs ++ Seq("-cp", cp, mainClass) ++ args
+    val process                = new ProcessBuilder(command.asJava).start()
+    val (stdoutReader, stdout) = drain(process.getInputStream)
+    val (stderrReader, stderr) = drain(process.getErrorStream)
+
+    val completed = process.waitFor(timeoutSeconds, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+    if (!completed) {
+      process.destroyForcibly()
+      stdoutReader.join(5000)
+      stderrReader.join(5000)
+      throw new IllegalStateException(
+        s"forked JVM '$mainClass' did not finish within $timeoutSeconds seconds; stdout so far: ${stdout.mkString}",
+      )
+    }
+    stdoutReader.join(10000)
+    stderrReader.join(10000)
+    Result(process.exitValue(), stdout.mkString, stderr.mkString)
+  }
+
+  /** The classpath for the forked JVM, recovered from the locations classes are actually loaded from. Whether the tests run in
+    * a forked sbt JVM or in the sbt process, the anchor libraries below each resolve to one concrete jar; adding those anchors
+    * FIRST (so their exact versions win on the fork's classpath) and then every other jar of the local artifact cache
+    * reproduces the full test classpath — extra cached jars never override the anchors.
+    */
+  private def effectiveClasspath: String = {
+    val fromProperty = sys.props.getOrElse("java.class.path", "").split(File.pathSeparator).toSeq.filter(_.nonEmpty)
+
+    val anchors = Seq(
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[ForkedJvm.type]),                                    // test classes
+      codeSourceRoot(Class.forName("org.galaxio.gatling.config.ConfigManager$")), // production classes
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[scala.Function0[_]]),                                // scala-library (exact version)
+      codeSourceRoot(Class.forName("scala.reflect.internal.Types")),              // scala-reflect (matching version)
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[org.slf4j.LoggerFactory]),
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger]),                     // logback-classic
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[ch.qos.logback.core.AppenderBase[_]]),               // logback-core
+      codeSourceRoot(classOf[com.typesafe.config.ConfigFactory]),
+      codeSourceRoot(Class.forName("com.typesafe.scalalogging.Logger")),
+    ).flatten
+
+    val cachedJars = anchors.flatMap(cacheRootOf).distinct.flatMap(jarsUnder)
+
+    // anchors first (exact versions), then remaining cached jars, then the current JVM classpath
+    (anchors ++ cachedJars ++ fromProperty).filter(_.nonEmpty).distinct.mkString(File.pathSeparator)
+  }
+
+  /** The local artifact-cache root an anchor file lives under (the first ancestor directory named `maven2`). */
+  private def cacheRootOf(path: String): Option[String] =
+    Iterator
+      .iterate(Option(new File(path)))(_.flatMap(f => Option(f.getParentFile)))
+      .takeWhile(_.isDefined)
+      .flatten
+      .find(_.getName == "maven2")
+      .map(_.getAbsolutePath)
+
+  private def jarsUnder(root: String): Seq[String] = {
+    val out                   = Vector.newBuilder[String]
+    def walk(dir: File): Unit =
+      Option(dir.listFiles()).toSeq.flatten.sortBy(_.getName).foreach { f =>
+        if (f.isDirectory) walk(f)
+        else if (f.getName.endsWith(".jar") && !f.getName.endsWith("-sources.jar") && !f.getName.endsWith("-javadoc.jar"))
+          out += f.getAbsolutePath
+      }
+    walk(new File(root))
+    out.result()
+  }
+
+  private def codeSourceRoot(cls: Class[_]): Option[String] =
+    Option(cls.getProtectionDomain.getCodeSource)
+      .map(_.getLocation)
+      .map(url => new File(url.toURI).getAbsolutePath)
+
+  private def javaBinary: String = {
+    val fromHome = new File(sys.props.getOrElse("java.home", ""), "bin/java")
+    if (fromHome.isFile) fromHome.getAbsolutePath else "java"
+  }
+
+  /** Starts `mainClass`, then hands `dialogue` control over the child's stdin while the child's stdout is drained line-by-line
+    * into a thread-safe buffer. Blocks until the child exits (bounded); returns its exit code with the full stdout text.
+    */
+  def interactive(mainClass: String, args: Seq[String])(dialogue: JvIsolation.Dialogue): (Int, String) = {
+    val cp      = effectiveClasspath
+    val command = Seq(javaBinary) ++ Seq("-cp", cp, mainClass) ++ args
+    val process = new ProcessBuilder(command.asJava).start()
+
+    val lines  = new java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue[String]()
+    val reader = new Thread(() => {
+      val source = new java.io.BufferedReader(new java.io.InputStreamReader(process.getInputStream, "UTF-8"))
+      try Iterator.continually(source.readLine()).takeWhile(_ != null).foreach(lines.add)
+      finally source.close()
+    })
+    reader.setDaemon(true)
+    reader.start()
+
+    val drainedErr = new StringBuilder
+    val errReader  = new Thread(() => {
+      val source = scala.io.Source.fromInputStream(process.getErrorStream, "UTF-8")
+      try source.foreach(drainedErr.append(_))
+      finally source.close()
+    })
+    errReader.setDaemon(true)
+    errReader.start()
+
+    val writer                = new java.io.BufferedWriter(new java.io.OutputStreamWriter(process.getOutputStream, "UTF-8"))
+    val write: String => Unit = line => { writer.write(line); writer.newLine(); writer.flush() }
+    val close: () => Unit     = () => writer.close()
+    dialogue.run(write, close, scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.CollectionHasAsScala(lines).asScala.toList)
+
+    val completed = process.waitFor(180, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.SECONDS)
+    if (!completed) {
+      process.destroyForcibly()
+      throw new IllegalStateException(
+        s"interactive forked JVM '$mainClass' did not finish in time; stdout so far: ${scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.CollectionHasAsScala(lines).asScala.mkString("\n")}; stderr so far: $drainedErr",
+      )
+    }
+    reader.join(10000)
+    errReader.join(10000)
+    val out       = scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.CollectionHasAsScala(lines).asScala.mkString("\n")
+    (process.exitValue(), out + (if (drainedErr.isEmpty) "" else s"\n[stderr]\n$drainedErr"))
+  }
+
+  private def drain(stream: java.io.InputStream): (Thread, StringBuilder) = {
+    val builder = new StringBuilder
+    val thread  = new Thread(() => {
+      val source = Source.fromInputStream(stream, "UTF-8")
+      try source.foreach(builder.append(_))
+      finally source.close()
+    })
+    thread.setDaemon(true)
+    thread.start()
+    (thread, builder)
+  }
+}
+
+/** A [[ForkedJvm]]-managed forked JVM that reads nothing but freshly built driver properties.
+  *
+  * ScalaTest runs suites in PARALLEL threads sharing one JVM (and its single global `ConfigFactory` default resolution), so a
+  * scenario that depends on driver-controlled system properties must not set them in-process: a parallel suite could observe,
+  * mutate, or clear them mid-read. `IsolatedDriverFork` keeps each scenario in its own process where the driver (and only the
+  * driver) controls the property values, then hands back the captured console output. Test-owned: it only starts child
+  * processes and collects their output.
+  */
+/** JVM-isolated driver-property scenarios for redaction specs: ScalaTest runs suites in PARALLEL threads sharing one JVM (and
+  * its single global default configuration resolution), so a scenario that depends on driver-controlled `-D` system properties
+  * must not set them in-process -- a parallel suite could observe, mutate, or clear them mid-run. [[JvIsolation]] keeps each
+  * scenario in a freshly launched JVM where the driver (and only the driver) controls the property values, then hands back the
+  * fork's full console output for the assertions. Test-owned: it only starts child processes and collects their output; it
+  * never changes production behavior.
+  */
+object JvIsolation {
+
+  private val DriverMain = "org.galaxio.gatling.testutil.Fixtures.IsolatedScenarioDriverMain"
+
+  /** Runs `fixtureMainClass` in ONE forked JVM with `sysProps` applied and reports the fork's whole console output. */
+  def forkedOutput(fixtureMainClass: String, sysProps: Map[String, String]): String =
+    ForkedJvm.run(DriverMain, args = Seq(IsolatedScenario(fixtureMainClass, sysProps).encode)).stdout
+
+  /** Returns the fork's exit code (0 == the fixture completed and reported) together with its output. */
+  def forkedResult(fixtureMainClass: String, sysProps: Map[String, String]): (Int, String) = {
+    val result = ForkedJvm.run(DriverMain, args = Seq(IsolatedScenario(fixtureMainClass, sysProps).encode))
+    (result.exitCode, result.stdout)
+  }
+
+  /** Drives one interactive forked scenario: starts `fixtureMainClass` with `sysProps` applied, forwards stdin lines written by
+    * `dialogue` to the fork, and collects everything the fork prints. `dialogue` receives a one-shot writer and the lines the
+    * fork has emitted SO FAR; it ends by writing a final verdict line and closing.
+    */
+  def forkedDialogue(fixtureMainClass: String, sysProps: Map[String, String])(dialogue: Dialogue): (Int, String) =
+    ForkedJvm.interactive(DriverMain, Seq(IsolatedScenario(fixtureMainClass, sysProps).encode))(dialogue)
+
+  /** What the driver does with the fork's stdin while the fork is mid-run. */
+  trait Dialogue {
+    def run(write: String => Unit, close: () => Unit, forkLines: => List[String]): Unit
+  }
+}
+
+/** Encoding of one JVM-isolated scenario: which fixture main to run and which `-D` properties the driver controls. Encoded onto
+  * the fork's command line (program args, never JVM input arguments), so the fork's own input-argument listing stays exactly
+  * what the launcher passed and property values with whitespace survive unmangled.
+  */
+final case class IsolatedScenario(fixtureMainClass: String, sysProps: Map[String, String]) {
+  def encode: String =
+    (fixtureMainClass +: sysProps.toSeq.map { case (k, v) => s"$k\u0001$v" }).mkString("\u0002")
+}
+
+object IsolatedScenario {
+  def decode(line: String): IsolatedScenario = {
+    val parts = line.split("\u0002", -1).toSeq
+    val props = parts
+      .drop(1)
+      .map { entry =>
+        val idx = entry.indexOf('\u0001')
+        entry.take(idx) -> entry.drop(idx + 1)
+      }
+      .toMap
+    IsolatedScenario(parts.head, props)
+  }
+}

+package org.galaxio.gatling.testutil
+
+import ch.qos.logback.classic.spi.ILoggingEvent
+import ch.qos.logback.classic.{Level, Logger => LogbackLogger}
+import ch.qos.logback.core.AppenderBase
+import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
+
+import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue
+import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters._
+
+/** Shared log capture for tests â safe under ScalaTest's PARALLEL suite execution.
+  *
+  * Capturing mutates the GLOBAL logback `LoggerContext` (a logger's level + attached appenders), which is shared across suites.
+  * Two safeguards keep it deterministic without serializing the whole test run:
+  *
+  *   1. `synchronized` â serializes the level save/set/restore + appender attach/detach so two captures never corrupt each
+  *      other's level restore (the part that genuinely needs mutual exclusion).
+  *   2. thread-name filter + a thread-safe queue â while a capture window is open, OTHER (non-capturing) suites running in
+  *      parallel may still log to the same logger on their own threads. The appender is backed by a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` (so
+  *      concurrent foreign appends can't corrupt it), and the result keeps only events emitted on the capturing thread (the
+  *      body logs synchronously on the caller thread), discarding foreign noise.
+  *
+  * This helper depends ONLY on logback/SLF4J types that already exist at the current revision â it has no dependency on any
+  * production masking class.
+  */
+object LogCapture {
+
+  /** Capture the events `body` emits under `loggerName` at `level` (inclusive), on the calling thread only. */
+  def events(loggerName: String, level: Level)(body: => Unit): List[ILoggingEvent] = synchronized {
+    val logger        = logbackLogger(loggerName)
+    val captured      = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue[ILoggingEvent]()
+    val appender      = new AppenderBase[ILoggingEvent] {
+      override def append(event: ILoggingEvent): Unit = captured.add(event)
+    }
+    appender.start()
+    val captureThread = Thread.currentThread().getName
+    val previousLevel = logger.getLevel
+    logger.setLevel(level)
+    logger.addAppender(appender)
+    try body
+    finally {
+      logger.detachAppender(appender)
+      logger.setLevel(previousLevel)
+    }
+    captured.asScala.iterator.filter(_.getThreadName == captureThread).toList
+  }
+
+  /** Capture INFO+ events and return their rendered messages. */
+  def infoMessages(loggerName: String)(body: => Unit): List[String] =
+    events(loggerName, Level.INFO)(body).map(_.getFormattedMessage)
+
+  /** Resolve the logback `Logger`, retrying past SLF4J's initialization window.
+    *
+    * Under parallel suite STARTUP, `LoggerFactory.getLogger` may briefly return a temporary
+    * `org.slf4j.helpers.SubstituteLogger` until logback finishes binding â casting that to `ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger`
+    * throws `ClassCastException`. The first real call triggers binding; we retry briefly until the backend is installed
+    * (bounded so a genuine misbind still surfaces a clear cast error rather than hanging).
+    */
+  @annotation.tailrec
+  private def logbackLogger(loggerName: String, attemptsLeft: Int = 2000): LogbackLogger =
+    LoggerFactory.getLogger(loggerName) match {
+      case logback: LogbackLogger => logback
+      case _ if attemptsLeft > 0  => Thread.sleep(1); logbackLogger(loggerName, attemptsLeft - 1)
+      case other                  => other.asInstanceOf[LogbackLogger] // exhausted â surface a clear cast error
+    }
+}

+package org.galaxio.gatling.utils.jwt
+
+import org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers
+import org.scalatest.wordspec.AnyWordSpec
+
+import java.security.{KeyPairGenerator, PrivateKey}
+
+/** Unit tests (test-model layer 1) for [[SigningKey]] secret redaction. `toString` must never expose the HMAC secret or the
+  * asymmetric key material, while the `value` accessor still returns the raw material (public API intact).
+  */
+class SigningKeySpec extends AnyWordSpec with Matchers {
+
+  "SigningKey.StringSecret" should {
+    "redact the secret in toString while keeping the value accessor intact" in {
+      val key = SigningKey.StringSecret("topsecret")
+
+      key.toString should not include "topsecret"
+      s"key=$key" should not include "topsecret" // interpolated/derived rendering also redacted
+      key.value shouldBe "topsecret"             // raw material still accessible via the public accessor
+    }
+  }
+
+  "SigningKey.AsymmetricKey" should {
+    "redact the key material in toString while keeping the value accessor intact" in {
+      val privateKey: PrivateKey = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").generateKeyPair().getPrivate
+      val key                    = SigningKey.AsymmetricKey(privateKey)
+
+      key.toString should not include privateKey.toString
+      key.value shouldBe privateKey
+    }
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
Fetch all repo issue closers
## Current Behavior
`FetchRepoIssueClosers()` misses some issue closers. Specifically, `dfIssueClosers <- FetchRepoIssueClosers(strRepo = "gsm.reporting")` throws out issue 30, because it sees the issue closer as `"ProjectV2"`, and it doesn't know what to do with that sort of closer.

## Expected Behavior
`dfIssueClosers <- FetchRepoIssueClosers(strRepo = "gsm.reporting")` SHOULD find [issue 30 in gsm.reporting](https://github.com/Gilead-BioStats/gsm.reporting/issues/30), and connect it to a particular commit or to [PR 34](https://github.com/Gilead-BioStats/gsm.reporting/pull/34).

## QC Approach
<!-- How will the quality of the implementation be verified? -->
In addition to standard QC (e.g., code reviews, automated checks) the following QC measures will be implemented:

[ ] Update existing Qualification/Unit Tests 
[ ] New Unit Tests

## Context (Environment)
<!--- Providing context helps us reproduce the issue and come up with a solution -->

### Additional contract requirements

When a closed issue's recorded closer is a `ProjectV2` object,
`FetchRepoIssueClosers()` must recover and report a qualifying alternate
closer in the documented issue-closer output fields. A qualifying pull request
is merged and belongs to the repository being fetched; a qualifying commit may
also be reported. Thus the recovery for gsm.reporting issue 30 must connect the
issue to its qualifying commit or to merged pull request 34. Cross-repository
and unmerged pull requests are not qualifying alternate closers.

+#'   requests linked to an issue. Only pull request candidates appear there,
+#'   because a commit is never a member of that field.
+TestIssueProjectV2WithRecoveryCandidates <- function(
+  intIssue,
+  lCandidates = list()
+) {
+  list(
+    number = intIssue,
+    timelineItems = list(
+      nodes = c(
+        lapply(lCandidates, function(lCandidate) {
+          list(closer = lCandidate)
+        }),
+        list(list(closer = list(`__typename` = "ProjectV2")))
+      )
+    ),
+    closedByPullRequestsReferences = list(
+      nodes = unname(purrr::keep(
+        lCandidates,
+        function(lCandidate) {
+          identical(lCandidate$`__typename`, "PullRequest")
+        }
+      ))
+    )
+  )

+  ))))

+  lPR <- list(
+    `__typename` = "PullRequest",
+    number = intPR,
+    merged = lglMerged,
+    repository = list(nameWithOwner = strRepo)
+  )
+  if (!is.null(strSHA)) {
+    lPR$mergeCommit <- list(oid = strSHA)
+  }
+  lPR

+#' appear.
+ExpectQualifyingRecovery <- function(dfResult, dfQualifying) {
+  chrQualifying <- paste(
+    dfQualifying$Issue,
+    dfQualifying$CloserType,
+    dfQualifying$CloserSHA,
+    dfQualifying$CloserPRNumber
+  )
+  chrRecovered <- paste(
+    dfResult$Issue,
+    dfResult$CloserType,
+    dfResult$CloserSHA,
+    dfResult$CloserPRNumber
+  )
+  expect_true(
+    nrow(dfResult) >= length(unique(dfQualifying$Issue)) &&
+      nrow(dfResult) <= nrow(dfQualifying) &&
+      all(chrRecovered %in% chrQualifying) &&
+      all(unique(dfQualifying$Issue) %in% dfResult$Issue),
+    info = paste(
+      "Each issue must be connected to a qualifying commit or merged pull",
+      "request, and nothing else may be reported. Got:",
+      paste(utils::capture.output(print(dfResult)), collapse = "\n"),
+      "Expected a non-empty subset of:",
+      paste(utils::capture.output(print(dfQualifying)), collapse = "\n")
+    )
+  )

problem_statement:
Update UAT issue body on change
## Summary
> As a package tester, in order to tweak instructions without changing the issue and to make sure my tests always stay in sync with their corresponding issues, I would like the body of `qcthat-uat` issues to update to match the body generated in the `ExpectUserAccepts()` call.

## Proposed Solution (Optional)
We currently find the specific issue for a given `ExpectUserAccepts()` by finding all children of the target item, and then filtering by *title* (which is built from the `strDescription` and `intIssue` args). We don't really pay attention to the body (except when creating the issue). Instead, build the body before the creation step, and, if the item exists but its body doesn't match, update it. This can probably happen at the same time that we're assigning the issue, although it probably wouldn't be the end of the world if we sent a second Update.

### Additional contract requirements

When `ExpectUserAccepts()` runs and finds an existing `qcthat-uat` issue that
matches its issue title, the body of that issue ends up identical to the body
that the current `ExpectUserAccepts()` call would create on a fresh issue,
given the same inputs:

- The body begins with the line "Close this issue to indicate your acceptance."
- Any review instructions supplied with the call appear next, and
- The body ends with a Markdown checkbox (`- [ ] `) for each supplied check
  item.

If the existing issue's body already matches that content, the issue is left
unchanged. If it does not match, the issue's body is updated to match. In
either case, the issue itself is still the matching one (same number, title,
and labels). This holds whether the difference comes from the instructions or
from the checklist items.

problem_statement:
Proposal: Always convert DateTime to UTC during serialization
Since dates should pretty much always be stored in UTC would it be reasonable to automatically convert DateTime objects to UTC during serialization? Could this at least be an option in the generator? I know I could write my own DateTime converter but then I have to remember to use it every time I create a new DateTime field.

I see https://github.com/google/json_serializable.dart/pull/811, but that was abandoned. I think making this a generator setting, maybe off by default to prevent issues with existing codebases, would be ideal.

### Additional contract requirements

The generator gains an opt-in option for serializing `DateTime` values in UTC.

- The `JsonSerializable` annotation exposes a new nullable boolean member
  `dateTimeUtc`. The corresponding build-configuration key is
  `date_time_utc`. The key must be accepted as supported, and a non-boolean
  value for it in the build configuration must be rejected with the same
  configuration-validation error used for the other supported keys.
- The option is `false` by default. With the option disabled, `DateTime` values
  are serialized exactly as in previous releases, using the string returned by
  `DateTime.toIso8601String()`.
- When `dateTimeUtc` is `true`, every `DateTime` value is serialized as the
  string produced by `toUtc().toIso8601String()`. This holds for non-nullable
  and nullable `DateTime` fields and for `DateTime` values nested in
  collections, including list elements and map values. `DateTime` map keys
  are not affected by the option and keep their existing form.
- A non-null value of `dateTimeUtc` on the `JsonSerializable` annotation of a
  class takes precedence over the build-configuration value for that class;
  when the annotation member is null, the build-configuration value applies.

problem_statement:
`NullValue` is serialized as `"NULL_VALUE"`
It should be serialized as `null`

### Additional contract requirements

## JSON codec semantics for the well-known `NullValue` and `Value` types

The following behaviors of the public API are part of the contract for this
task. They describe the behavior of `NullValue` and `Value` from the
`google_cloud_protobuf` package when converted to and from their protobuf
(JSON) representations.

### `NullValue`

- `NullValue.nullValue.toJson()` returns the Dart `null` value.
- `NullValue.fromJson(null)` returns `NullValue.nullValue`.
- `NullValue.fromJson('NULL_VALUE')` also returns `NullValue.nullValue`, so
  that the canonical proto3 JSON name of the enum value is accepted when
  decoding.

### `Value`

- `Value(nullValue: NullValue.nullValue).toJson()` returns the Dart `null`
  value, and `Value.fromJson(null)` decodes to a value whose `nullValue`
  getter is `NullValue.nullValue`.
- `Value(numberValue: n).toJson()` returns the number `n`; decoding a JSON
  number (an integer or a double) sets `numberValue` to the corresponding
  `double`.
- `Value(stringValue: s).toJson()` returns the string `s`, and decoding a
  JSON string sets `stringValue` to that string.
- `Value(boolValue: b).toJson()` returns the boolean `b`, and decoding a JSON
  boolean sets `boolValue` to that boolean.
- A `Value` holding a `ListValue` serializes to a JSON list and decodes from
  a JSON list; a `null` element of the list corresponds to
  `Value(nullValue: NullValue.nullValue)`.
- A `Value` holding a `Struct` serializes to a JSON object and decodes from a
  JSON object; a `null` property value corresponds to
  `Value(nullValue: NullValue.nullValue)`.

problem_statement:
FieldMask not correctly serialized using camelCase
From https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/field_mask.proto

```
// In JSON, a field mask is encoded as a single string where paths are
// separated by a comma. Fields name in each path are converted
// to/from lower-camel naming conventions.

```

### Additional contract requirements

This task concerns the protocol-buffers JSON representation of a
`google.protobuf.FieldMask`. In JSON a field mask is encoded as a single
string: its paths are separated by commas, and the field names in each
path are converted to or from lower-camel naming conventions.

- On encode, each path's `snake_case` components are converted to
  lower-camel (`foo_bar` becomes `fooBar`), and the converted paths are
  joined with commas into a single string.
- On decode, each comma-separated path's lower-camel components are
  converted back to `snake_case` (`fooBar` becomes `foo_bar`). This
  conversion also applies to components containing runs of capital
  letters: each capitalized letter becomes an underscore followed by the
  lowercased letter (for example, `userHTTPRequest` decodes to
  `user_h_t_t_p_request`).
- Dot-separated structure within a path is preserved: only the field
  names are converted, not the `.` separators between them.

+  static FieldMask decode(Object? format) {

+    ];
+    return FieldMask(paths: paths);
+  }

+  static String _lowerUnderscoreToLowerCamel(String str) {
+    final sb = StringBuffer();
+    var capitalizeNext = false;
+    for (var i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
+      final c = str[i];
+      if (c == '_') {
+        capitalizeNext = true;
+      } else if (capitalizeNext) {
+        sb.write(c.toUpperCase());
+        capitalizeNext = false;
+      } else {
+        sb.write(c.toLowerCase());

+    }
+    return sb.toString();
+  }

+    final sb = StringBuffer();

problem_statement: xaxs/yaxs not restored when set When `xaxs` and `yaxs` are set (e.g., automatically in `type_barplot` and `type_spineplot`), then they don't get restored afterwards affecting subsequent output. Example: ``` tinyplot(~ species, data = penguins, type = type_barplot()) tinyplot(1:10, pch = 19, cex = 2) ``` ``` tinyplot(species ~ island, data = penguins) tinyplot(1:10, pch = 19, cex = 2) ``` Note the clipping of the first and last point in the scatterplot due to the modified `xaxs`/`yaxs` settings. [HIDDEN] ### Additional contract requirements Any `xaxs` and `yaxs` graphics parameter values in effect on the current graphics device before a `tinyplot()` call must still hold after that call returns, including when the plot type takes over these interval styles internally (e.g., bar plots, spine plots, or an explicit `xaxs`/`yaxs` argument). Restoration must recover the previously active values, whether or not they match the defaults, and must cover each of the two parameters independently. Subsequent plots on the same device must therefore not be affected by clipped or otherwise shifted axis behavior caused by an earlier internally adjusted plot.

+new_plot_dev = function() {

problem_statement:
[Intermediate]: Implement HIP-1313 High-Volume Entity Creation
### 🧩 Intermediate Friendly

This issue is a good fit for contributors who are already familiar with the
Hiero Swift SDK and feel comfortable navigating the codebase.

Intermediate Issues often involve:
- Exploring existing implementations  
- Understanding how different components work together  
- Making thoughtful changes that follow established patterns  

The goal is to support deeper problem-solving while keeping the task clear,
focused, and enjoyable to work on.

### 🐞 Problem Description

The Hiero Swift SDK does not currently support [HIP-1313](https://hips.hedera.com/hip/hip-1313) which introduces high-volume throttles for entity creation transactions.

HIP-1313 introduces a parallel throttle system for high-volume entity creation. Users can opt into this system by setting a boolean flag on their transactions. When enabled:
- Transactions use a separate set of high-volume throttles with dedicated capacity
- Dynamic pricing applies based on throttle utilization (higher usage = higher fees)
- Users should set `maxTransactionFee` to control costs
- Standard throttles remain unchanged for users who don't opt in

Without this feature, developers cannot access additional entity creation capacity during peak times, which may slow down applications that need to create many items quickly (such as onboarding large groups of users).

**Relevant files:**
- `Sources/Hiero/Transaction.swift` (base class)
- Protobuf bindings for `TransactionBody`

### 💡 Expected Outcome

Add support for the `highVolume` flag to the base `Transaction` class, allowing all transaction types to opt into high-volume throttles for entity creation.

#### API Changes

Add the following to the `Transaction` class:

```swift
public class Transaction {
    /// Whether to use high-volume throttles for this transaction.
    /// When true, enables high-volume throttles and pricing for entity creation.
    /// Only affects supported transaction types; otherwise, it is ignored.
    public var highVolume: Bool
    
    /// Sets whether to use high-volume throttles for this transaction.
    /// - Parameter highVolume: If true, uses high-volume throttles and pricing
    /// - Returns: Self for method chaining
    @discardableResult
    public func highVolume(_ highVolume: Bool) -> Self
}
```

The implementation should:
- Default `highVolume` to `false`
- Prevent modification after the transaction is frozen[HIDDEN]
- Serialize the flag to the protobuf `high_volume` field[HIDDEN]
- Deserialize the flag when reading from protobuf
- Follow existing patterns for property accessors in the Transaction class

#### Supported Transaction Types

The `highVolume` flag affects these transaction types (ignored for others):

| Transaction Class | Description |
|-------------------|-------------|
| `TopicCreateTransaction` | Create a new topic |
| `ContractCreateTransaction` | Create a new smart contract |
| `AccountAllowanceApproveTransaction` | Approve allowances |
| `AccountCreateTransaction` | Create a new account |
| `TransferTransaction` | Transfer (for hollow account creation) |
| `FileCreateTransaction` | Create a new file |
| `FileAppendTransaction` | Append to a file |
| `ScheduleCreateTransaction` | Create a scheduled transaction |
| `TokenAirdropTransaction` | Airdrop tokens |
| `TokenAssociateTransaction` | Associate tokens to an account |
| `TokenCreateTransaction` | Create a new token |
| `TokenClaimAirdropTransaction` | Claim airdropped tokens |
| `TokenMintTransaction` | Mint tokens |

### 🧠 Implementation Notes

#### 1. Verify Protobuf Bindings
- Check that `TransactionBody` protobuf includes the `high_volume` field[HIDDEN]
- If not present, regenerate Swift protobuf bindings

#### 2. Update Transaction Base Class
- Add `highVolume` property with default value of `false`
- Add `highVolume(_ highVolume: Bool) -> Self` fluent setter method
- [HIDDEN] to prevent modification after freezing
- Update `toTransactionBodyProtobuf` to include `highVolume` in the protobuf output
- Update `init(protobuf:)` to read `highVolume` from the protobuf

#### 3. Add Unit Tests
- Test that `highVolume` defaults to `false`
- Test setting `highVolume` to `true`
- Test that `highVolume` cannot be set after transaction is frozen
- Test serialization/deserialization preserves `highVolume` flag
- Test that `highVolume` is correctly included in protobuf output

#### 4. Add Integration Tests
- Test creating an account with `highVolume` enabled
- Test that transaction succeeds with appropriate `maxTransactionFee`
- Test that transaction fails with `INSUFFICIENT_TX_FEE` when `maxTransactionFee` is too low

#### 5. Add Example
- Create an example demonstrating high-volume account creation

#### Example Usage

```swift
import Hiero

// Create an account using high-volume throttles
let accountCreateTx = try AccountCreateTransaction()
    .key(.single(newAccountKey.publicKey))
    .initialBalance(Hbar(10))
    .highVolume(true)
    .maxTransactionFee(Hbar(5))  // Important: set a fee limit
    .freezeWith(client)
    .sign(newAccountKey)

let response = try await accountCreateTx.execute(client)
let receipt = try await response.getReceipt(client)
let accountId = receipt.accountId!

print("Created account \(accountId) using high-volume throttles")
```

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria

To help get this change merged smoothly:

- [ ] `highVolume` property is available on all `Transaction` subclasses
- [ ] Setting `highVolume(true)` correctly serializes to the protobuf `high_volume` field
- [ ] Deserializing a transaction with `high_volume = true` correctly sets the `highVolume` property
- [ ] The flag cannot be modified after a transaction is frozen
- [ ] Unit tests pass for the new functionality
- [ ] Integration tests pass on testnet (when HIP-1313 is enabled)
- [ ] Example code compiles and runs successfully
- [ ] Follow existing project conventions
- [ ] Pass all CI checks

### 📋 Contribution Guide

To help your contribution go as smoothly as possible, we recommend following these steps:

- [ ] Comment `/assign` to request the issue
- [ ] Wait for assignment
- [ ] Fork the repository and create a branch
- [ ] Set up the project using the instructions in `README.md`
- [ ] Make the requested changes
- [ ] Sign each commit using `-s -S`
- [ ] Push your branch and open a pull request

Read [Workflow Guide](docs/training/workflow.md) for step-by-step workflow guidance.  
Read [README.md](README.md) for setup instructions.

❗ Pull requests **cannot be merged** without `S` and `s` signed commits.  
See the [Signing Guide](docs/training/signing.md).

### 📚 Additional Context or Resources

#### References
- **HIP**: https://hips.hedera.com/hip/hip-1313
- **SDK Design Document**: https://github.com/hiero-ledger/sdk-collaboration-hub/blob/main/proposals/hips/hip-1313.md

#### Test Plan

1. **Given** an `AccountCreateTransaction` is configured with `highVolume(true)`, **when** the transaction is executed, **then** the account is created successfully using high-volume throttles.

2. **Given** an `AccountCreateTransaction` is configured with `highVolume(true)` and a valid `maxTransactionFee(fee)`, **when** the transaction is executed, **then** the account is created successfully and the fee charged respects the maximum transaction fee setting.

3. **Given** an `AccountCreateTransaction` is configured with `highVolume(true)` and a `maxTransactionFee(fee)` that is lower than the actual fee required, **when** the transaction is executed, **then** the transaction fails with an `INSUFFICIENT_TX_FEE` error.

[Intermediate]: Implement HIP-1313 High-Volume Entity Creation
### 🧩 Intermediate Friendly

This issue is a good fit for contributors who are already familiar with the
Hiero Swift SDK and feel comfortable navigating the codebase.

Intermediate Issues often involve:
- Exploring existing implementations  
- Understanding how different components work together  
- Making thoughtful changes that follow established patterns  

The goal is to support deeper problem-solving while keeping the task clear,
focused, and enjoyable to work on.

### 🐞 Problem Description

The Hiero Swift SDK does not currently support [HIP-1313](https://hips.hedera.com/hip/hip-1313) which introduces high-volume throttles for entity creation transactions.

HIP-1313 introduces a parallel throttle system for high-volume entity creation. Users can opt into this system by setting a boolean flag on their transactions. When enabled:
- Transactions use a separate set of high-volume throttles with dedicated capacity
- Dynamic pricing applies based on throttle utilization (higher usage = higher fees)
- Users should set `maxTransactionFee` to control costs
- Standard throttles remain unchanged for users who don't opt in

Without this feature, developers cannot access additional entity creation capacity during peak times, which may slow down applications that need to create many items quickly (such as onboarding large groups of users).

**Relevant files:**
- `Sources/Hiero/Transaction.swift` (base class)
- Protobuf bindings for `TransactionBody`

### 💡 Expected Outcome

Add support for the `highVolume` flag to the base `Transaction` class, allowing all transaction types to opt into high-volume throttles for entity creation.

#### API Changes

Add the following to the `Transaction` class:

```swift
public class Transaction {
    /// Whether to use high-volume throttles for this transaction.
    /// When true, enables high-volume throttles and pricing for entity creation.
    /// Only affects supported transaction types; otherwise, it is ignored.
    public var highVolume: Bool
    
    /// Sets whether to use high-volume throttles for this transaction.
    /// - Parameter highVolume: If true, uses high-volume throttles and pricing
    /// - Returns: Self for method chaining
    @discardableResult
    public func highVolume(_ highVolume: Bool) -> Self
}
```

The implementation should:
- Default `highVolume` to `false`
- Prevent modification after the transaction is frozen[HIDDEN]
- Serialize the flag to the protobuf `high_volume` field[HIDDEN]
- Deserialize the flag when reading from protobuf
- Follow existing patterns for property accessors in the Transaction class

#### Supported Transaction Types

The `highVolume` flag affects these transaction types (ignored for others):

| Transaction Class | Description |
|-------------------|-------------|
| `TopicCreateTransaction` | Create a new topic |
| `ContractCreateTransaction` | Create a new smart contract |
| `AccountAllowanceApproveTransaction` | Approve allowances |
| `AccountCreateTransaction` | Create a new account |
| `TransferTransaction` | Transfer (for hollow account creation) |
| `FileCreateTransaction` | Create a new file |
| `FileAppendTransaction` | Append to a file |
| `ScheduleCreateTransaction` | Create a scheduled transaction |
| `TokenAirdropTransaction` | Airdrop tokens |
| `TokenAssociateTransaction` | Associate tokens to an account |
| `TokenCreateTransaction` | Create a new token |
| `TokenClaimAirdropTransaction` | Claim airdropped tokens |
| `TokenMintTransaction` | Mint tokens |

### 🧠 Implementation Notes

#### 1. Verify Protobuf Bindings
- Check that `TransactionBody` protobuf includes the `high_volume` field[HIDDEN]
- If not present, regenerate Swift protobuf bindings

#### 2. Update Transaction Base Class
- Add `highVolume` property with default value of `false`
- Add `highVolume(_ highVolume: Bool) -> Self` fluent setter method
- [HIDDEN] to prevent modification after freezing
- Update `toTransactionBodyProtobuf` to include `highVolume` in the protobuf output
- Update `init(protobuf:)` to read `highVolume` from the protobuf

#### 3. Add Unit Tests
- Test that `highVolume` defaults to `false`
- Test setting `highVolume` to `true`
- Test that `highVolume` cannot be set after transaction is frozen
- Test serialization/deserialization preserves `highVolume` flag
- Test that `highVolume` is correctly included in protobuf output

#### 4. Add Integration Tests
- Test creating an account with `highVolume` enabled
- Test that transaction succeeds with appropriate `maxTransactionFee`
- Test that transaction fails with `INSUFFICIENT_TX_FEE` when `maxTransactionFee` is too low

#### 5. Add Example
- Create an example demonstrating high-volume account creation

#### Example Usage

```swift
import Hiero

// Create an account using high-volume throttles
let accountCreateTx = try AccountCreateTransaction()
    .key(.single(newAccountKey.publicKey))
    .initialBalance(Hbar(10))
    .highVolume(true)
    .maxTransactionFee(Hbar(5))  // Important: set a fee limit
    .freezeWith(client)
    .sign(newAccountKey)

let response = try await accountCreateTx.execute(client)
let receipt = try await response.getReceipt(client)
let accountId = receipt.accountId!

print("Created account \(accountId) using high-volume throttles")
```

problem_statement:
Support multiple secondary structures per fragment
Split from #259:

In our current system representation, fragments can be part of at most one secondary structure. However, PDB structures such as `1GJC` and `8QJB` declare certain fragments to be part of multiple beta sheets, either as a different strand of the same sheet or as a strand of a separate sheet:

**1GJC**
```
SHEET    1   A 7 PHE B  30  ARG B  36  0                              <---          
SHEET    2   A 7 VAL B  38  SER B  48 -1  O  THR B  39   N  ARG B  35           
SHEET    3   A 7 TRP B  51  SER B  54 -1  O  TRP B  51   N  MET B  47           
SHEET    4   A 7 ALA B 104  ARG B 109 -1  O  ALA B 104   N  SER B  54           
SHEET    5   A 7 MET B  81  ILE B  89 -1  N  GLU B  84   O  ARG B 109           
SHEET    6   A 7 TYR B  64  LEU B  68 -1  O  TYR B  64   N  VAL B  85           
SHEET    7   A 7 PHE B  30  ARG B  36 -1  N  ALA B  32   O  TYR B  67 <--- same sheet, different strand
```

**8QJB**
```
SHEET    1 AA3 8 ASP A 428  ARG A 432  0                               <---
SHEET    2 AA3 8 ASP A 418  THR A 422 -1  N  PHE A 421   O  LEU A 429  
SHEET    3 AA3 8 MET A 411  HIS A 415 -1  N  HIS A 415   O  ASP A 418  
SHEET    4 AA3 8 ILE A 480  HIS A 487 -1  O  TYR A 481   N  LEU A 412  
SHEET    5 AA3 8 HIS A 469  LEU A 475 -1  N  ILE A 472   O  ALA A 485  
SHEET    6 AA3 8 LEU A 460  ASP A 464 -1  N  ILE A 462   O  GLN A 471  
SHEET    7 AA3 8 GLN A 447  ASP A 455 -1  N  ARG A 451   O  PHE A 463  
SHEET    8 AA3 8 ILE A 438  ASN A 444 -1  N  PHE A 439   O  GLY A 454  
SHEET    1 AA479 ASP A 428  ARG A 432  0                               <-- different sheet
```

### Additional contract requirements

Fragments may participate in any number of secondary structure elements, including several strands of the same beta sheet and strands of different sheets.

## Constructing secondary structures

A secondary structure is constructed from inclusive endpoint fragments:

```julia
SecondaryStructure(first_fragment::Fragment, last_fragment::Fragment,
                   number::Int, type::SecondaryStructureType;
                   name = "", kwargs...)
```

The endpoints must belong to the same chain. The new secondary structure is registered in that chain and covers every fragment from the first endpoint through the last endpoint in chain fragment order.

## Membership queries

- `fragments(ss::SecondaryStructure)` returns the fragments covered by `ss`.
- `nfragments(ss::SecondaryStructure)` returns their count.
- `secondary_structures(frag::Fragment)` returns all secondary structures covering `frag`, or an empty collection when none cover it.
- `nsecondary_structures(frag::Fragment)` returns the number of structures covering `frag`.
- `residues`/`nucleotides` and `nresidues`/`nnucleotides` accept a `SecondaryStructure` or `SecondaryStructureTable` and restrict covered fragments by variant.

A fragment must report every covering secondary structure, rather than only one parent structure. The previous one-to-one parent query is replaced by these plural membership queries.

## Deletion and file loading

`delete!(ss; keep_fragments = true)` removes only `ss`; its fragments and memberships in other secondary structures remain intact. With `keep_fragments = false`, deleting a secondary structure also removes its covered fragments.

When loading a file with multiple secondary-structure declarations that cover the same fragments, each declaration is registered independently. Generated names for loaded declarations are not part of this contract.

problem_statement:
Retry: re-run failing scenarios a configurable number of times
Found via the [Cucumber Compatibility Kit](https://github.com/cucumber/compatibility-kit): the `retry` family of samples (`retry`, `retry-ambiguous`, `retry-pending`, `retry-undefined`) covers re-running failed scenarios. This is an optional Cucumber feature (only a subset of implementations support it), but it is useful for flaky end-to-end suites.

## How it should work

- A configuration option (and/or per-scenario tag) sets the maximum number of attempts for a scenario, e.g. `retry: 2` meaning up to two re-runs after an initial failure.
- A scenario that passes on any attempt counts as passing for the run; reporting should still record the earlier failed attempts and ideally mark the scenario as flaky.
- Only genuine failures are retried — scenarios that are undefined, ambiguous, or pending will fail identically every time, so retrying them is pointless and real Cucumber implementations skip retrying those result types (the CCK has dedicated samples asserting this).
- Each attempt runs with fresh scenario state, including before/after hooks.

### Additional contract requirements

## Retry — additional observable requirements

### Configuring the retry limit

- A retry limit of `n` means one initial attempt plus up to `n` re-runs of
  the same scenario in the same test run (for example, a limit of `2` allows
  up to three attempts).
- With neither configuration nor a tag, or with the configuration value set
  to `nil`, a failing scenario runs exactly once.
- A non-integer retry configuration value must cause the affected scenario to
  fail with an error message that mentions the retry configuration and shows
  the offending value itself.

### Retry tags

- A tag of the form `@retry-<n>`, where `<n>` is a non-negative integer, sets
  the retry limit. Such a tag may be placed at the Feature, Rule, Scenario,
  Scenario Outline, or Examples level.
- The tag from the most specific enclosing level wins for each scenario: an
  Examples-level tag beats its outline's tag; a scenario-level tag beats the
  rule's and feature's tags; a rule-level tag beats the feature's tag. Any
  `@retry-<n>` tag overrides the global configuration for the scenarios it
  governs, including `@retry-0`, which exempts those scenarios from retrying
  even when a wider-scope tag or the configuration would retry them.

### Per-attempt semantics

- Each attempt runs the complete scenario lifecycle — before-scenario hooks,
  background steps, scenario steps, and after-scenario hooks — as if it were
  a fresh execution of the scenario.
- The context visible during each attempt includes the current attempt number
  as `retry_attempt`, counting from `1` for the first attempt.
- A passing attempt ends the retry loop: passed scenarios are never re-run.
  Retrying also prints an observable repeat-run notice naming the retried
  scenario, so quiet flakiness stays visible in the run's output, while a
  scenario that never produces a failed attempt prints no such notice.
- A scenario that exhausts all of its attempts fails with the final attempt's
  own failure error.

### Which failures are retried

- Retrying applies to every failure class: raised exceptions, process exits
  (such as call timeouts), and throws. All failure classes receive identical
  per-attempt treatment, including after-step hooks observing a failed status
  and failure output that includes the failing exit or throw reason.
- Undefined, ambiguous, and pending scenarios are never retried: they run
  exactly once and report the same failure as they would without any retry
  configuration, and no retry notice is printed for them.
- A before-all (run-level setup) failure is never retried; its original error
  is reported identically for every scenario in the run and before-all hooks
  run only once per run.

### Context isolation between attempts

- Every attempt must start from the same initial context — the context
  updates returned by before hooks and steps of a failed attempt must never
  be visible in any later attempt, including in later attempts' background
  steps, scenario steps, and hooks. This isolation covers the run context
  only; anything an attempt stores outside it (for example, in shared
  processes or the process dictionary) still survives between attempts.

### Attachments under retry

- Attachments recorded during a scenario are attributed to the attempt that
  recorded them, and recordings from every attempt remain inspectable for the
  run. When a scenario fails after exhausting its attempts, the failure
  output lists only the attachments recorded by the failing (final) attempt —
  each exactly once — and does not repeat attachments from earlier attempts.

+### Scenario-Level Retry
+
+Failing scenarios can be retried automatically, matching the retry
+mechanism of other Cucumber implementations. Configure a global retry
+limit:
+
+```elixir
+# config/test.exs
+config :cucumber, retry: 2  # up to 3 attempts per failing scenario
+```
+
+Or opt individual scenarios (or whole features) in with a `@retry-n` tag,
+which overrides the global config — including `@retry-0` to exempt a
+scenario. The most specific tag wins: a scenario's tag beats its rule's
+or its feature's, and an `Examples`-level tag beats the outline's — so
+`@retry-0` on a scenario also exempts it from a feature- or rule-wide
+retry tag:
+
+```gherkin
+@retry-2
+Scenario: occasionally slow external service
+  Given the payment provider responds
+```
+
+Each attempt re-runs the full scenario lifecycle — before hooks,
+background, steps, and after hooks — with a fresh context (the 1-based
+attempt number is available as `context.retry_attempt`). The scenario
+passes if any attempt passes; each retry prints a one-line flake warning
+so quiet flakiness stays visible. Failures of every class are retried —
+raised exceptions, exits (e.g. a `GenServer.call` timeout), and throws.
+Undefined, ambiguous, and pending scenarios are never retried — they
+cannot succeed by repetition — and neither is a `before_all` hook
+failure, whose result is cached for the whole run.
+
+"Fresh context" means the context *map*: attempts re-run in the same
+test process, so everything else survives between them. `on_exit`
+callbacks don't run until the test process exits, processes started
+with `start_supervised!` are still running (a retry starting the same
+named process will see `:already_started`), and the process dictionary
+persists. Steps in retried scenarios should tolerate re-entry — or
+reset shared state in a `before_scenario` hook, which runs at the top
+of every attempt.

+defmodule Cucumber.RetryTest do
+  @moduledoc """
+  Behavior tests for retry (#26), driven by the vendored CCK `retry`,
+  `retry-undefined`, `retry-ambiguous`, and `retry-pending` samples plus
+  inline features for the Elixir-specific surface (`@retry-n` tags, fresh
+  context per attempt, hook re-runs).
+
+  The CCK runs its retry samples with `--retry 2`; the equivalent here is
+  `config :cucumber, retry: 2`, set per test via `with_retry_config/2`.
+  Attempt counting uses the Collector: a step counts its own prior events
+  to decide whether to fail, mirroring the reference step definitions'
+  module-level counters.
+  """
+
+  use Cucumber.BehaviorCase
+
+  alias Cucumber.BehaviorCase.Collector
+
+  defp with_retry_config(retries, fun) do
+    Application.put_env(:cucumber, :retry, retries)
+
+    try do
+      fun.()
+    after
+      Application.delete_env(:cucumber, :retry)
+    end
+  end
+
+  defmodule Steps do
+    use Cucumber.StepDefinition
+
+    step "a step that always passes", _context do
+      Collector.record(:always_passes)
+      :ok
+    end
+
+    step "a step that passes the second time", _context do
+      Collector.record(:second_time)
+
+      if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &(&1 == :second_time)) < 2 do
+        raise "Exception in step"
+      end
+
+      :ok
+    end
+
+    step "a step that passes the third time", _context do
+      Collector.record(:third_time)
+
+      if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &(&1 == :third_time)) < 3 do
+        raise "Exception in step"
+      end
+
+      :ok
+    end
+
+    step "a step that always fails", _context do
+      Collector.record(:always_fails)
+      raise "Exception in step"
+    end
+
+    step "a pending step", _context do
+      Collector.record(:pending_step)
+      :pending
+    end
+
+    step "a step that exits the first time", _context do
+      Collector.record(:exit_step)
+
+      if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &(&1 == :exit_step)) < 2 do
+        exit(:simulated_timeout)
+      end
+
+      :ok
+    end
+
+    step "a step that throws the first time", _context do
+      Collector.record(:throw_step)
+
+      if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &(&1 == :throw_step)) < 2 do
+        throw(:simulated_ball)
+      end
+
+      :ok
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "the CCK retry sample (retry limit 2)" do
+    test "failing scenarios are retried up to the limit; passes aren't retried" do
+      run =

+          run_feature(fixture("retry"), steps: [Steps])
+        end)
+
+      # Only "a step that always fails" exhausts its attempts and fails
+      assert %{total: 4, failures: 1, passed: 3} = run
+
+      # Passing test cases aren't retried
+      assert count(run.events, :always_passes) == 1
+      # Fail-once passes on the second attempt
+      assert count(run.events, :second_time) == 2
+      # Fail-twice continues retrying up to the limit
+      assert count(run.events, :third_time) == 3
+      # Fail-always runs retries + 1 attempts, then fails with the step error
+      assert count(run.events, :always_fails) == 3
+
+      # Each retry prints a flake warning naming the retried scenario
+      assert run.output =~ ~r/retry/i
+      assert run.output =~ "Test cases that fail are retried if within the --retry limit"
+
+      # The exhausted scenario fails with the step's own error
+      assert run.output =~ "Exception in step"
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "statuses that never retry" do
+    test "undefined scenarios run exactly once (CCK retry-undefined)" do
+      run =

+        end)
+
+      assert %{total: 1, failures: 1} = run
+      assert run.output =~ "No matching step definition"
+      refute run.output =~ "Cucumber: retrying scenario"
+    end
+
+    test "ambiguous scenarios run exactly once (CCK retry-ambiguous)" do
+      defmodule AmbiguousSteps do
+        use Cucumber.StepDefinition

+        step "an ambiguous step", _context do
+          :ok
+        end
+

+          :ok
+        end
+      end

+      refute run.output =~ "Cucumber: retrying scenario"
+    end
+

+
+    test "a @retry-0 tag overrides the global config to a single attempt" do

+    test "a scenario-level @retry-n beats a feature-level @retry-0" do

+        # into background and scenario steps, which assert on it below.
+        before_scenario context, name: "pollute first attempt" do
+          if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &(&1 == :before_hook)) == 1 do
+            {:ok, Map.put(context, :polluted, true)}
+          else
+            :ok
+          end
+        end
+
+        after_scenario _context do
+          Collector.record(:after_hook)
+          :ok
+        end
+      end
+
+      defmodule IsolationSteps do
+        use Cucumber.StepDefinition
+        import ExUnit.Assertions
+
+        step "a background step", _context do
+          Collector.record(:background_step)
+          :ok
+        end
+
+        step "a step that pollutes the context then fails once", context do
+          assert context.from_hook
+
+          if context.retry_attempt == 1 do
+            # The first attempt's own setup pollution must be visible here
+            # — proving the runtime propagates context updates — and then
+            # the attempt fails, triggering the retry.
+            assert Map.has_key?(context, :polluted)
+          else
+            # Every later attempt must start from a fresh context: nothing
+            # a previous attempt added may still be present.
+            refute Map.has_key?(context, :polluted)
+          end
+
+          Collector.record({:attempt, context.retry_attempt})
+
+          if Enum.count(Collector.events(), &match?({:attempt, _}, &1)) < 2 do
+            raise "flaky"
+          end
+
+          :ok
+        end
+      end
+
+      run =
+        run_feature(
+          """
+          Feature: isolation
+            Background:
+              Given a background step
+
+            @retry-1
+            Scenario: retried with fresh state
+              Given a step that pollutes the context then fails once
+          """,
+          steps: [IsolationSteps],
+          hooks: [RetryHooks]
+        )
+
+      assert %{total: 1, failures: 0, passed: 1} = run
+
+      # Hooks and background ran once per attempt, and the context carried
+      # the 1-based attempt number
+      assert count(run.events, :before_hook) == 2
+      assert count(run.events, :background_step) == 2
+      assert count(run.events, :after_hook) == 2
+      assert [{:attempt, 1}, {:attempt, 2}] = Enum.filter(run.events, &(match?({:attempt, _}, &1)))
+    end
+  end
+end

+defmodule RetrySteps do
+  use Cucumber.StepDefinition
+
+  step "a flaky step that passes on the second attempt", context do
+    # Retry attempts run sequentially in the same test process, so the
+    # process dictionary counts attempts and resets naturally per test run
+    attempts = Process.get(:flaky_step_attempts, 0) + 1

problem_statement:
Remove hardcoded indentation settings from ftplugin
The ftplugin currently sets tabstop, shiftwidth, and softtabstop to 4 over [here](https://github.com/hxueh/beancount.nvim/blob/main/ftplugin/beancount.lua#L14-L17).

This means that `.editorconfig` settings get overridden (since they are evaluated before ftplugin).

Is this a personal preference? I see that the beancount repo examples are all double space indented.

Right now I've overridden the behaviour by making my own `after/ftplugin/beancount.lua` file setting `vim.bo.
*` to be two spaces.

Would you consider removing these lines?

Alternatives could be extending the config options for the plugin to either skip setting tab/shift options
or override the settings. Or recommend people do something like:

```
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  pattern = "beancount",
  callback = function()
    vim.bo.tabstop = ?
    ...
  end,
})
```
(not 100% of the ordering of adding autocmds and plugins)

I'm not a fan of modeline configs personally, anyway lots of options ð

### Additional contract requirements

When the beancount ftplugin loads for a buffer, it must not override that buffer's preconfigured `expandtab`, `shiftwidth`, `tabstop`, or `softtabstop` values, so that user- or project-level indentation settings (for example from `.editorconfig` or `after/ftplugin` files) remain in effect.

When indenting a posting line, the plugin must honor the buffer's effective indentation configuration:

- If `expandtab` is set for the buffer, the inserted indentation consists of spaces whose count equals the buffer's effective shift width (as reported by `shiftwidth()`).
- If `expandtab` is not set for the buffer, the inserted indentation is a single tab character, regardless of the buffer's `tabstop` or `shiftwidth` values.
- After the indentation is inserted, the cursor is positioned at the end of the inserted indent.

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+-- Tests for beancount formatter module
+-- Verifies that posting-line indentation honors the buffer's effective
+-- indentation configuration: space indentation at the effective shift
+-- width when expandtab is set, tab indentation when expandtab is not set.
+
+---@diagnostic disable-next-line: redundant-parameter
+vim.opt.runtimepath:prepend(vim.fn.getcwd())
+
+print("Running formatter tests...")
+
+local function test_assert(condition, message)
+  if not condition then
+    error("Test failed: " .. (message or "assertion failed"))
+  end
+end
+
+local tests_run = 0
+local tests_passed = 0
+
+local function run_test(name, test_fn)
+  tests_run = tests_run + 1
+  local success, err = pcall(test_fn)
+  -- Emit the machine-readable result line first. In nvim headless mode the
+  -- message layer can merge the first print after buffer manipulation into
+  -- the previous line, so keep parser lines away from that position.
+  if success then
+    tests_passed = tests_passed + 1
+    print("Success || formatter_test.lua: " .. name)
+    print("  PASS " .. name)
+  else
+    print("Fail || formatter_test.lua: " .. name)
+    print("  FAIL " .. name .. ": " .. tostring(err))
+  end
+end
+
+local formatter = require("beancount.formatter")
+
+-- Create a fresh buffer with an empty line, preconfigure the given
+-- buffer-local options, run indent_posting_line on the first line, and
+-- return the resulting line content along with the buffer number.
+local function indent_empty_line_with(opts)
+  local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
+  vim.api.nvim_set_current_buf(bufnr)
+  for name, value in pairs(opts) do
+    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_option(bufnr, name, value)
+  end
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false, { "" })
+  formatter.indent_posting_line(1)
+  local line = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, 1, false)[1]
+  return bufnr, line, vim.fn.col(".")
+end
+
+-- Verify posting-line indentation uses a single tab when expandtab is not set
+run_test("indent_posting_line uses a tab when expandtab=false", function()
+  local bufnr, line, col = indent_empty_line_with({ expandtab = false, tabstop = 8, shiftwidth = 3 })
+  test_assert(line == "\t", "expected a single tab, got: " .. vim.inspect(line))
+  test_assert(col == #line, "expected cursor at the end of the inserted indent, got column: " .. col)
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(bufnr, { force = true })
+end)
+
+-- Verify posting-line indentation uses the effective shift width of spaces
+-- when expandtab is set, even with deliberately different tabstop/shiftwidth
+run_test("indent_posting_line uses shiftwidth spaces when expandtab=true", function()
+  local bufnr, line, col = indent_empty_line_with({ expandtab = true, tabstop = 8, shiftwidth = 3 })

problem_statement:
Add float support
- float parsing
- float machine types
- ExpressibleByFloatingPointLiteral

### Additional contract requirements

- The language provides two floating-point machine types, `Float32` and `Float64`, both available through the standard library.
- The parser accepts decimal floating-point literals, including literals with a fractional part and/or a decimal exponent (optionally marked with a sign, using either `e` or `E`), and literals whose digits are separated by underscores.
- A floating-point literal can be explicitly ascribed to `Float32` or `Float64` with `as`, and each of these types can be initialized from a floating-point literal through an expected-type annotation (e.g. `let a: Float32 = 0.5`); such programs type-check, lower through IR, and code-generate successfully.
- The standard library declares a trait `ExpressibleByFloatingPointLiteral` for types that can be expressed by a floating-point literal; both `Float32` and `Float64` conform to it.
