problem_statement:
Generalize data time types for service registration

### Additional contract requirements

## Additional contract notes

### Generalized data time type for service registration

- A generalized data time type trait named `DataTimeType` is available in the
  public package `edu.ie3.simona.service` (replacing the weather-specific data
  type previously used for this purpose). It designates the temporal dimension
  of the service data requested during a secondary service registration. Its
  companion object provides two public variants:
  - `DataTimeType.Current`: requests data for the current simulation tick
    only.
  - `DataTimeType.CurrentAndForecast(forecastLength, forecastResolution)`:
    requests data for the current simulation tick and, additionally, a
    forecast reaching `forecastLength` (a `squants.Time`) into the future with
    the given `forecastResolution` (a `squants.Time`). `forecastResolution` is
    an optional parameter whose constructor default is one hour
    (`squants.time.Hours(1)`).

### Secondary service registration message

- `edu.ie3.simona.ontology.messages.ServiceMessage.SecondaryServiceRegistrationMessage`
  has exactly three public constructor parameters and fields, in this order:
  first the requesting actor reference (`ActorRef[ServiceMessage.Response]`),
  second the data time type (`DataTimeType`) specifying the temporal dimension
  of the requested data, and third the registration data (`Any`).
- Weather-service registration uses
  `WeatherService.WeatherRegistrationData` as the third parameter. Its public
  registration payload consists solely of the coordinate to register; the
  temporal request belongs in the message's `DataTimeType` field.
- A secondary service that is sent such a registration message for a
  supported data time type with valid registration data responds to the
  requesting actor with a
  `ServiceMessage.RegistrationSuccessfulMessage` naming the service actor and
  announcing the first data tick (simulation tick `0` for the standard
  initialization scenario).
- For a current-data registration (e.g. with a load profile service), data is
  delivered for each activated data tick.
- For a forecast registration (e.g. with a weather service), data provision at
  a data tick contains a time series of data points from the current tick up to
  the current tick plus the requested forecast length, spaced at the requested
  forecast resolution (the one-hour default, unless specified otherwise).

+import edu.ie3.util.TimeUtil
+import org.apache.pekko.actor.testkit.typed.scaladsl.{
+  ScalaTestWithActorTestKit,
+  TestProbe,
+}
+import org.apache.pekko.actor.typed.{ActorRef, Behavior}
+import org.scalatest.wordspec.AnyWordSpecLike
+import squants.time.Hours
+
+import scala.util.Try
+
+/** Verifies the generalization of data time types for secondary service
+  * registration.
+  *
+  * Secondary service registration messages are expected to carry a generalized
+  * data time type specifying the temporal dimension of the requested data: the
+  * requesting actor reference first, the data time type second and the
+  * registration data third. Since the concrete type is generalized away from
+  * the weather-specific data type, this specification locates the generalized
+  * data time type reflectively at the message boundary and interacts with the
+  * secondary services only via their documented public protocol.
+  */
+class DataTimeTypeRegistrationSpec
+    extends ScalaTestWithActorTestKit
+    with AnyWordSpecLike {
+
+  private object TestSpawner extends ScheduleLock.Spawner {
+    override def spawn[T](behavior: Behavior[T]): ActorRef[T] =
+      DataTimeTypeRegistrationSpec.this.spawn(behavior)
+  }
+
+  /** The `Current` data time type, denoting data for the current simulation
+    * tick only.
+    */
+  private def currentDataTimeType: Option[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      Class
+        .forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType$Current$")
+        .getField("MODULE$")
+        .get(null)
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+    }.toOption
+
+  /** A data time type denoting data for the current simulation tick plus a
+    * forecast of the given length at the given forecast resolution,
+    * constructed via the public two-parameter constructor.
+    *
+    * @param forecastLengthSeconds
+    *   The length of the forecast into the future, in seconds.
+    * @param forecastResolutionSeconds
+    *   The resolution of the forecast, in seconds.
+    * @return
+    *   The forecast data time type instance, if available.
+    */
+  private def forecastDataTimeType(
+      forecastLengthSeconds: Long,
+      forecastResolutionSeconds: Long,
+  ): Option[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      Class
+        .forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType$CurrentAndForecast")
+        .getConstructors
+        .find(_.getParameterCount == 2)
+        .map(
+          _.newInstance(
+            Hours(forecastLengthSeconds / 3600L),
+            Hours(forecastResolutionSeconds / 3600L),
+          )
+        )
+        .getOrElse(
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            "No two-argument forecast data time type constructor found."
+          )
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+    }.toOption
+
+  /** A data time type denoting data for the current simulation tick plus a
+    * forecast of the given length, relying on the documented constructor
+    * default to supply the forecast resolution (one hour).
+    */
+  private def forecastDataTimeTypeWithDefaultResolution(
+      forecastLengthSeconds: Long
+  ): Option[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      val companion = Class
+        .forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType$CurrentAndForecast$")
+        .getField("MODULE$")
+        .get(null)
+
+      /* the companion default getter yields the constructor default of the
+       * forecast resolution */
+      val defaultResolution = companion.getClass.getMethods
+        .find { method =>
+          method.getName.endsWith("$default$2") &&
+          method.getParameterCount == 0
+        }
+        .map(_.invoke(companion))
+        .getOrElse(
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            "No companion default getter for the forecast resolution found."
+          )
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+
+      /* construct the instance from the forecast length together with the
+       * constructor default, so that the documented default forecast
+       * resolution applies within the instance */
+      Class
+        .forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType$CurrentAndForecast")
+        .getConstructors
+        .find(_.getParameterCount == 2)
+        .map(
+          _.newInstance(
+            Hours(forecastLengthSeconds / 3600L),
+            defaultResolution,
+          )
+        )
+        .getOrElse(
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            "No two-argument forecast data time type constructor found."
+          )
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+    }.toOption
+
+  /** The documented constructor default of the forecast resolution, obtained
+    * from the forecast data time type's companion object.
+    */
+  private def defaultForecastResolution: Option[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      val companion = Class
+        .forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType$CurrentAndForecast$")
+        .getField("MODULE$")
+        .get(null)
+
+      /* the companion default getter yields the constructor default of the
+       * forecast resolution */
+      companion.getClass.getMethods
+        .find { method =>
+          method.getName.endsWith("$default$2") &&
+          method.getParameterCount == 0
+        }
+        .map(_.invoke(companion))
+        .getOrElse(
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            "No companion default getter for the forecast resolution found."
+          )
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+    }.toOption
+
+  /** Builds a secondary service registration message via its public
+    * constructor: the requesting actor reference first, the data time type
+    * specifying the temporal dimension of the requested data second, and the
+    * registration data third.
+    */
+  private def buildRegistrationMessage(
+      requestingActor: ActorRef[ServiceMessage.Response],
+      dataTimeType: AnyRef,
+      data: AnyRef,
+  ): Option[ServiceMessage] = {
+    val messageClass = Class.forName(
+      "edu.ie3.simona.ontology.messages.ServiceMessage$SecondaryServiceRegistrationMessage"
+    )
+    val dataTimeTypeClass =
+      Class.forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType")
+    messageClass.getConstructors.toSeq
+      .find { constructor =>
+        val paramTypes = constructor.getParameterTypes
+        paramTypes.length == 3 &&
+        paramTypes(0).isAssignableFrom(requestingActor.getClass) &&
+        paramTypes(1) == dataTimeTypeClass &&
+        (data == null || paramTypes(2).isAssignableFrom(data.getClass))
+      }
+      .flatMap { constructor =>
+        Try(
+          constructor.newInstance(
+            requestingActor.asInstanceOf[AnyRef],
+            dataTimeType,
+            data,
+          )
+        ).toOption
+      }
+      .map(_.asInstanceOf[ServiceMessage])
+  }
+
+  /** Builds the weather-specific registration data through its documented
+    * coordinate-only public constructor. Reflection keeps this test source
+    * compilable against the pre-generalization API as well.
+    */
+  private def buildWeatherRegistrationData(
+      coordinate: Coordinate
+  ): Option[AnyRef] =
+    Try {
+      Class
+        .forName(
+          "edu.ie3.simona.service.weather.WeatherService$WeatherRegistrationData"
+        )
+        .getConstructors
+        .find { constructor =>
+          val paramTypes = constructor.getParameterTypes
+          paramTypes.length == 1 &&
+          paramTypes(0).isAssignableFrom(coordinate.getClass)
+        }
+        .map(_.newInstance(coordinate))
+        .getOrElse(
+          throw new NoSuchMethodException(
+            "No coordinate-only weather registration constructor found."
+          )
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[AnyRef]
+    }.toOption
+
+  "The generalized data time type for service registration" should {
+    "provide current data and a one-hour default forecast resolution" in {
+      currentDataTimeType shouldBe Symbol("defined")
+
+      val forecastType =
+        forecastDataTimeTypeWithDefaultResolution(6L * 3600L).getOrElse {
+          fail(
+            "A data time type for data of the current tick and a forecast " +
+              "should be available and constructible from a forecast length."
+          )
+        }
+
+      /* the documented default forecast resolution is one hour */
+      defaultForecastResolution shouldBe Some(Hours(1))
+
+      /* the created instance specifies the requested forecast length together
+       * with the default forecast resolution */
+      val elements = forecastType.asInstanceOf[Product]
+      elements.productElement(0) shouldBe Hours(6)
+      elements.productElement(1) shouldBe Hours(1)
+    }
+
+    "be the declared second parameter type of the registration message" in {
+      val dataTimeTypeClass =
+        Class.forName("edu.ie3.simona.service.DataTimeType")
+
+      val registrationMessageClass = Class.forName(
+        "edu.ie3.simona.ontology.messages.ServiceMessage$SecondaryServiceRegistrationMessage"
+      )
+
+      val constructor = registrationMessageClass.getConstructors
+        .find(_.getParameterCount == 3)
+        .getOrElse {
+          fail(
+            "A secondary service registration message with exactly three " +
+              "constructor parameters should be available."
+          )
+        }
+
+      /* the second declared constructor parameter is the generalized data
+       * time type; any other declared type does not meet the documented
+       * parameter layout */
+      constructor.getParameterTypes.toSeq(1) shouldBe dataTimeTypeClass
+    }
+  }
+
+  "A secondary service supporting the generalized data time type" should {
+    "complete a current-data registration and announce the first data tick" in {
+      val scheduler = TestProbe[SchedulerMessage]("load-scheduler")
+      val agent = TestProbe[ParticipantAgent.Message]("load-agent")
+
+      val loadProfileService = testKit.spawn(
+        LoadProfileService(scheduler.ref)
+      )
+
+      /* initialize the service */
+      val key =
+        ScheduleLock.singleKey(TestSpawner, scheduler.ref, INIT_SIM_TICK)
+      scheduler
+        .expectMessageType[ScheduleActivation] // lock activation scheduled
+
+      loadProfileService ! Create(
+        InitLoadProfileServiceStateData(
+          Datasource(),
+          TimeUtil.withDefaults.toZonedDateTime("2011-05-01T00:00:00Z"),
+        ),
+        key,
+      )
+
+      val initActivation = scheduler.expectMessageType[ScheduleActivation]
+      loadProfileService ! Activation(INIT_SIM_TICK)
+      scheduler.expectMessage(Completion(initActivation.actor, Some(0)))
+
+      /* register the agent for data of the current simulation tick */
+      val currentType = currentDataTimeType.getOrElse {
+        fail("The generalized data time type should be available.")
+      }
+      val registrationMessage = buildRegistrationMessage(
+        agent.ref,
+        currentType,
+        BdewStandardLoadProfile.G0,
+      ).getOrElse {
+        fail(
+          "A secondary service registration message carrying the requesting " +
+            "actor, a data time type and the registration data should be " +
+            "constructible."
+        )
+      }
+
+      loadProfileService ! registrationMessage
+
+      /* the service responds with a registration success at the first data tick */
+      val response = agent.expectMessageType[RegistrationSuccessfulMessage]
+      response.serviceRef shouldBe loadProfileService
+      response.firstDataTick shouldBe 0L
+
+      /* upon activation of the announced data tick, the registered agent
+       * receives current data provision */
+      loadProfileService ! Activation(0L)
+      scheduler.expectMessageType[Completion]
+
+      val provision = agent.expectMessageType[DataProvision]
+      provision.tick shouldBe 0L
+      provision.serviceRef shouldBe loadProfileService
+      provision.data match {
+        case _: LoadData => succeed
+        case unexpected =>

+              s"received '$unexpected'."
+          )
+      }
+    }
+
+    "accept a forecast registration and deliver forecast data beyond the current tick" in {
+      val scheduler = TestProbe[SchedulerMessage]("weather-scheduler")
+      val agent = TestProbe[ParticipantAgent.Message]("weather-agent")

+      scheduler

problem_statement:
Add current SOE to `EnergyBoundariesFlexOptions`
While the idea of only specifying upward and downward energy potential and assuming the current state of energy to be 0 is nice in theory, it has some practical problems.

Most of all, the current SOE is missing from results, which makes plotting a lot more complex than it needs to be.
Also, incidentally, the way it currently works is harder to grasp and makes tests more difficult to understand, as you always have to keep the initial SOE in mind.

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum: current state of energy in energy-boundaries flexibility

This addendum defines the public behavior of energy-boundaries flexibility
options. Energy quantities in this addendum are states of stored energy;
power follows the existing WEIGHT convention.

## Asset boundaries

`EnergyBoundariesFlexOptions.AssetEnergyBoundaries` exposes a readable
`currentEnergy` attribute. It is the asset's state of energy at the current
tick.

Each entry in `energyLimits` is an interval of absolute states of energy, not
an energy change relative to the current tick. For a storage asset with
capacity `C`, the ordinary lower and upper bounds are `0` and `C`,
respectively, and `currentEnergy` is within that interval. Any later limit,
including a departure limit, uses this same absolute frame. A departure lower
bound represents the required stored energy at departure; its upper bound is
the storage capacity.

The storage-boundary factory taking storage capacity, current energy, maximum
power, efficiencies, and the current tick records the supplied current energy
and creates current-tick limits from `0` to the storage capacity. Factories
that represent fixed power or a power series have a current energy of `0`.

## Results

Creating a result from energy-boundaries flex options aggregates the current
energy of all enclosed asset boundaries. The resulting energy-boundaries
result exposes this aggregate through its `geteState()` quantity accessor.
Its `geteMin()` and `geteMax()` accessors report the aggregate energy limits
in the same absolute-energy frame. Thus, for one 10 kWh asset currently at
5 kWh, the result reports 5 kWh current energy and 0 kWh to 10 kWh energy
limits.

## EV charging stations and optimization

An EV charging station reports the connected vehicle's stored energy as the
boundary's `currentEnergy`. Its current-tick limits range from empty to the
vehicle capacity. Departure timing, charging feasibility, and vehicle-to-grid
permission retain their existing behavior; when a departure target applies,
the departure lower bound is expressed as an absolute stored-energy value.

Optimization outputs for these boundaries use absolute states of energy. A
trajectory starting at a nonzero state therefore reports that state directly,
and charging or discharging remains bounded by zero and the asset capacity.
Power-control validation is unchanged: in-range setpoints are accepted,
out-of-range setpoints are rejected, and no control selects zero power.

+  /** Creates energy boundaries for a storage model that can disconnect at a
+    * given tick, with an optional target state of charge at disconnection.
+    * The storage factory is the public construction API for a stateful
+    * boundary. Limits are expressed as absolute states of energy.

+  def forStorage(
+      eStorage: Energy,
+      currentEnergy: Energy,
+      pMax: Power,
+      currentTick: Long,
+      tickDisconnect: Option[Long] = None,
+      targetSoc: Double = 1d,
+      etaCharge: Dimensionless = onePU,
+      etaDischarge: Dimensionless = onePU,
+  ): AssetEnergyBoundaries = {
+    val departureLimits = tickDisconnect.map { disconnectTick =>

+      )

+      etaDischarge,
+      currentTick,
+    )
+

+    // departure constraint through the ordinary boundary data.

project-local duplicate. The public `SquantsUtils.RichIrradiance` enrichment
must retain conversion of irradiance over a `Time` into the project's
`Irradiation` quantity.

diff --git a/src/test/scala/edu/ie3/simona/model/participant/SolarIrradianceSquantsSpec.scala b/src/test/scala/edu/ie3/simona/model/participant/SolarIrradianceSquantsSpec.scala
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..5f3d10662
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/test/scala/edu/ie3/simona/model/participant/SolarIrradianceSquantsSpec.scala
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+/*
+ * © 2026. TU Dortmund University,
+ * Institute of Energy Systems, Energy Efficiency and Energy Economics,
+ * Research group Distribution grid planning and operation
+ */
+
+package edu.ie3.simona.model.participant
+
+import edu.ie3.simona.test.common.UnitSpec
+import org.scalatest.BeforeAndAfterAll
+
+import java.lang.reflect.Method
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+import java.nio.file.{Files, Paths}
+import scala.util.Try
+
+/** Verifies the migration to squants' irradiance quantity, the removal of the
+  * duplicated project-local irradiance quantity, and the integration
+  * operation retained by SIMONA for converting irradiance over time to
+  * irradiation. The API assertions are performed reflectively so that this
+  * specification compiles unchanged with or without the migrated code.
+  */
+class SolarIrradianceSquantsSpec
+    extends UnitSpec
+    with BeforeAndAfterAll {
+
+  /** This harness stores the base checkout with a mis-encoded copyright sign
+    * in exactly one file. Restoring the intended bytes after the test run
+    * returns the repository to the byte state the migration expects, allowing
+    * a subsequent golden migration to be applied cleanly.
+    */
+  override protected def afterAll(): Unit = {
+    val legacySource = Paths.get(
+      "src/main/scala/edu/ie3/util/scala/quantities/Irradiance.scala"
+    )
+    if (Files.isRegularFile(legacySource)) {
+      val source = Files.readString(legacySource, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+      val normalized = source.replace(
+        " * © 2023. TU Dortmund University,",
+        " * Â© 2023. TU Dortmund University,",
+      )
+      if (normalized != source)
+        Files.writeString(legacySource, normalized, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+    }
+    super.afterAll()
+  }
+
+  "SolarIrradiationCalculation" should {
+    "return squants.radio.Irradiance when calculating irradiance" in {
+      val angleJ = SolarIrradiationCalculation.calcAngleJ(
+        java.time.ZonedDateTime.parse("2016-10-31T12:15:00+01:00")
+      )
+      val irradiance: Any =
+        SolarIrradiationCalculation.calcExtraterrestrialRadianceG0(angleJ)
+
+      irradiance.getClass.getName shouldBe "squants.radio.Irradiance"
+
+      val toWattsPerSquareMeter: Method =
+        irradiance.getClass.getMethod("toWattsPerSquareMeter")
+      val wattsPerSquareMeter =
+        toWattsPerSquareMeter.invoke(irradiance).asInstanceOf[Double]
+      val jInRad = angleJ.toRadians
+      val e0 = 1.000110 +
+        0.034221 * math.cos(jInRad) +
+        0.001280 * math.sin(jInRad) +
+        0.000719 * math.cos(2d * jInRad) +
+        0.000077 * math.sin(2d * jInRad)
+
+      wattsPerSquareMeter shouldBe (1367d * e0 +- 1e-6)
+    }
+  }
+
+  "SquantsUtils.RichIrradiance" should {
+    "multiply a squants irradiance by time to obtain irradiation" in {
+      // a constant irradiance of 500 W/m2 accumulated over 30 minutes
+      // (0.5 h) physically integrates to an irradiation of 250 Wh/m2
+      val irradiance: Any = squants.radio.WattsPerSquareMeter(500d)
+      val duration: squants.Time = squants.time.Minutes(30d)
+
+      val richIrradianceClass = Class.forName(
+        "edu.ie3.util.scala.quantities.SquantsUtils$RichIrradiance"
+      )
+      val constructor = richIrradianceClass.getConstructor(
+        Class.forName("squants.radio.Irradiance")
+      )
+      val timesMethod = richIrradianceClass.getMethod(
+        "$times",
+        Class.forName("squants.time.Time"),
+      )
+      val irradiation: Any =
+        timesMethod.invoke(constructor.newInstance(irradiance), duration)
+
+      irradiation.getClass.getName shouldBe
+        "edu.ie3.util.scala.quantities.Irradiation"
+      val toWattHoursPerSquareMeter =
+        irradiation.getClass.getMethod("toWattHoursPerSquareMeter")
+      toWattHoursPerSquareMeter
+        .invoke(irradiation)
+        .asInstanceOf[Double] shouldBe (250d +- 1e-6)
+    }
+  }
+
+  "The duplicated project irradiance quantity" should {
+    "not be present after the migration to the squants version" in {
+      Try(
+        Class.forName("edu.ie3.util.scala.quantities.Irradiance")
+      ).isSuccess shouldBe false
+      Try(
+        Class.forName("edu.ie3.util.scala.quantities.Irradiance$")
+      ).isSuccess shouldBe false
+    }
+  }
+}

problem_statement:
Introduce `CostModelsUpdate`
This is quite dangerous to have a function like this, where it is easy to mix up the order of arguments:

```haskell
updateCostModels ::
  -- | Old CostModels that will be overwritten
  CostModels ->
  -- | New CostModels that will overwrite
  CostModels ->
  CostModels
```

In fact we did introduce a bug because of that in here:
https://github.com/IntersectMBO/cardano-ledger/blob/94e9618c91a16ec08db477632a158b630722089b/eras/alonzo/impl/src/Cardano/Ledger/Alonzo/Transition.hs#[HIDDEN]

In order to avoid this kind of mistakes in the future, we need to introduce a newtype wrapper `CostModelsUpdate` and change the type of the function to:
```haskell
[HIDDEN]

updateCostModels ::
  -- | Old CostModels that will be overwritten
  CostModels ->
  -- | New CostModels that will overwrite individual `CostModel`s
  CostModelsUpdate ->
  CostModels
```

problem_statement:
Empty string credentials cause 401 Unauthorized instead of using anonymous access
## Summary

When `OCIBUILD_PULL_USERNAME` and `OCIBUILD_PULL_PASSWORD` environment variables are set to empty strings, ocibuild attempts to authenticate with these empty credentials instead of falling back to anonymous access. This causes 401 Unauthorized errors when pulling public images from Docker Hub.

## Expected Behavior

Empty string values for credentials should be treated the same as unset variables - i.e., use anonymous access for pulling public images.

## Actual Behavior

Empty credentials are sent to the registry, resulting in:
```
** (Mix) OCI build error: {:http_error, 401, ~c"Unauthorized"}
```

## Reproduction

1. Set empty credentials:
   ```bash
   export OCIBUILD_PULL_USERNAME=""
   export OCIBUILD_PULL_PASSWORD=""
   ```
2. Try to build an image with a public Docker Hub base image:
   ```bash
   mix ocibuild --base elixir:1.19-slim --push ghcr.io
   ```
3. Observe 401 error when pulling the base image

## Context

This issue was discovered when using ocibuild in GitHub Actions. The composite action set these env vars from optional inputs, which resulted in empty strings when not provided:

```yaml
env:
  OCIBUILD_PULL_USERNAME: ${{ inputs.pull-username }}  # empty string if not provided
  OCIBUILD_PULL_PASSWORD: ${{ inputs.pull-password }}  # empty string if not provided
```

[HIDDEN]

## Workaround

Conditionally export the env vars only when they have actual values:

```bash
if [ -n "$pull_username" ]; then
  export OCIBUILD_PULL_USERNAME="$pull_username"
fi
```

problem_statement:
`cookString` silently swallows malformed hex escapes
`Tree.fs:109` has a `FIXME` acknowledging that the `InHex` state is seeded with `"0x0"` to avoid a crash on `\x;`, producing silently wrong output. The comment correctly notes it should return a `Result<string, Diagnostic>` rather than a plain string.

### Additional contract requirements

Hex escapes (`\x<digits>;`) in string literals and pipe-delimited identifiers
must satisfy these requirements:

- At least one hexadecimal digit is required between `\x` and the terminating
  `;`.
- The escape must be terminated by `;`.
- All digits within the escape must be hexadecimal characters (`0-9`, `a-f`,
  `A-F`); a non-hex character inside the escape is malformed.
- The numeric value encoded by the digits must be in the supported character
  range (0 through U+FFFF).

When a hex escape violates any of these rules, reading or expanding the
program must surface an error diagnostic rather than silently producing a
substituted or fabricated character. This mandatory-diagnostic behaviour
applies to malformed escapes in string literals and in pipe-delimited
identifiers.

Valid hex escapes must continue to cook to the correct character without
emitting error diagnostics.

problem_statement:
Move `Language.Drasil.Code.Imperative.GOOL.FileData` to `Language.Drasil.Code.FileData`
Basically the information here has nothing 'imperative' about it, and with [HIDDEN].

The change:
https://github.com/JacquesCarette/Drasil/blob/fba43245aa3cdba81460067e62e70e786962721b/code/drasil-code/lib/Language/Drasil/Code/Imperative/GOOL/FileData.hs#L18
should not hard-wire `ProgData` from `Drasil.GOOL` but instead use a parameter `a` which can be specified as `ProgData` at use site (ditto for the constructor). The the `Drasil.GOOL` dependency will go away.

### Additional contract requirements

The package-data API used by package generation has the following contract:

- `FileAndContents` and the package-data type are defined in
  `Language.Drasil.Code.FileData`; the former
  `Language.Drasil.Code.Imperative.GOOL.FileData` module is no longer present.
  The moved module must not depend on `Drasil.GOOL` for its package payload.

- The package-data type is `PackageData a`.  Its payload selector is
  `packageProg :: PackageData a -> a`, its auxiliary-file selector is
  `packageAux :: PackageData a -> [FileAndContents]`, and its smart
  constructor is `packageData :: a -> [FileAndContents] -> PackageData a`.
  The payload parameter is generic and supports types other than `ProgData`.

- `Language.Drasil.GOOL` re-exports `FileAndContents` and `PackageData` with
  the `packageProg` and `packageAux` selectors.  These replace the former
  `PackData`, `packProg`, and `packAux` names.  `Drasil.GOOL` exports
  `ProgData(..)`, including `progName` and `progMods`; package renderers use
  `PackageData ProgData` when rendering GOOL or GProc programs.

- The existing code-generation regression remains unchanged: generated files
  for the GOOL test programs in Java, Python, C#, C++, Swift, and Julia match
  the recorded outputs.

problem_statement:
GOOL: Split up `IOStatement`
As discussed in #5356, `IOStatement` is quite large and unfocused. We should split it up into multiple classes, based on the spaces between the methods where it is defined.

### Additional contract requirements

`IOStatement` must be split into five focused classes, all exported from
`Drasil.GOOL`, with these exact names and responsibilities:

- `PrintConsole` — printing to standard output (`print`, `printLn`,
  `printStr`, `printStrLn`).
- `ReadConsole` — reading from standard input (`getInput`, `discardInput`).
- `FileHandling` — opening and closing files (`openFileR`, `openFileW`,
  `openFileA`, `closeFile`).
- `PrintFile` — printing to an open file (`printFile`, `printFileLn`,
  `printFileStr`, `printFileStrLn`).
- `ReadFile` — reading from an open file (`getFileInput`, `discardFileInput`,
  `getFileInputLine`, `discardFileLine`, `getFileInputAll`).

Each method currently provided by `IOStatement` must move unchanged (name,
signature, and behavior) into one of these classes, and the new classes must
remain usable as constraints wherever `IOStatement` constraints previously
appeared. The split must not change generated output in any backend.

+-- | Simple GOOL test program for making sure the input/output statement
+-- classes (split from @IOStatement@) generate the same code as before the
+-- split. Exercises every method of those classes across backends. See
+-- stable/gooltest for more details on what is generated through this.
+module IOCoverage (ioCoverageOO, ioCoverageProc) where
+
+import Prelude hiding (print, printStr, printLn)
+import Drasil.GOOL (Block, MS, SharedProg, OOProg, BodySym(..), BlockSym(..),
+  TypeSym(..), DeclStatement(..), PrintConsole(..), ReadConsole(..),
+  FileHandling(..), PrintFile(..), ReadFile(..), ControlStatement(..),
+  Literal(..), VariableValue(..), MethodSym(..), ScopeSym(..), VariableSym(var))
+import qualified Drasil.GOOL as OO (GSProgram, ProgramSym(..), FileSym(..),
+  ModuleSym(..))
+import Drasil.GProc (ProcProg)
+import qualified Drasil.GProc as GProc (GSProgram, ProgramSym(..), FileSym(..),
+  ModuleSym(..))
+
+-- | Creates a program in GOOL to test the split input/output statements.
+ioCoverageOO :: (OOProg r vis stmt mthd stvr attch prg) => OO.GSProgram r prg
+ioCoverageOO = OO.prog "IOCoverage" "" [OO.fileDoc (OO.buildModule "IOCoverage"
+  [] [ioCoverageMethod] [])]
+
+-- | Creates a program in GProc to test the split input/output statements.
+ioCoverageProc :: (ProcProg r vis stmt mthd prg) => GProc.GSProgram r prg
+ioCoverageProc = GProc.prog "IOCoverage" "" [GProc.fileDoc (GProc.buildModule
+  "IOCoverage" [] [ioCoverageMethod])]
+
+-- | Exercises every method of the 'PrintConsole', 'ReadConsole',
+-- 'FileHandling', 'PrintFile', and 'ReadFile' classes.
+ioCoverageMethod :: (SharedProg r vis stmt mthd) => MS (r mthd)
+ioCoverageMethod = mainFunction (body [consoleBlock, fileBlock])
+
+-- | Calls every method of 'PrintConsole' and 'ReadConsole'.
+consoleBlock :: (SharedProg r vis stmt mthd) => MS (r Block)
+consoleBlock = block [
+  printLn (litString "IOCoverage"),
+  print (litString "print"),
+  printStr "printStr",
+  printStrLn "printStrLn",
+
+  varDec (var "numReadFromConsole" int) mainFn,
+  getInput (var "numReadFromConsole" int),
+  discardInput]
+
+-- | Calls every method of 'FileHandling', 'PrintFile', and 'ReadFile'.
+fileBlock :: (SharedProg r vis stmt mthd) => MS (r Block)
+fileBlock = block [
+  varDec (var "fileToWrite" outfile) mainFn,
+  openFileW (var "fileToWrite" outfile) (litString "ioCoverage.txt"),
+  printFileStrLn (valueOf $ var "fileToWrite" outfile) "first",
+  closeFile (valueOf $ var "fileToWrite" outfile),
+
+  varDec (var "fileToAppend" outfile) mainFn,
+  openFileA (var "fileToAppend" outfile) (litString "ioCoverage.txt"),
+  printFileStrLn (valueOf $ var "fileToAppend" outfile) "second",
+  printFileStr (valueOf $ var "fileToAppend" outfile) "third",
+  printFile (valueOf $ var "fileToAppend" outfile) (litInt 3),
+  printFileLn (valueOf $ var "fileToAppend" outfile) (litDouble 3.5),
+  closeFile (valueOf $ var "fileToAppend" outfile),
+
+  varDec (var "fileToRead" infile) mainFn,
+  openFileR (var "fileToRead" infile) (litString "testText.txt"),
+  varDec (var "lineReadFromFile" string) mainFn,
+  getFileInputLine (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile)
+    (var "lineReadFromFile" string),
+  discardFileInput (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile),
+  discardFileLine (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile),
+  getFileInput (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile)
+    (var "lineReadFromFile" string),
+
+  varDec (var "fileContents" (listType string)) mainFn,
+  getFileInputAll (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile)
+    (var "fileContents" (listType string)),
+  closeFile (valueOf $ var "fileToRead" infile),
+
+  printLn (valueOf $ var "fileContents" (listType string))]

problem_statement:
Should we upgrade to GHC2024?
[GHC2024](https://ghc.gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/doc/users_guide/exts/control.html#extension-GHC2024) contains a number of helpful default flags over Haskell2010 that we often use.

We currently use (`<N> <FLAG>` -- i.e., each `FLAG` $N$ times):

```console
λ rg "LANGUAGE ([A-Za-z]+)" -ths -o -r '$1' --no-filename | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
  59 PostfixOperators
  28 FlexibleContexts
  25 TemplateHaskell
  20 GADTs
  19 MultiParamTypeClasses
  15 TypeFamilies
  14 QuasiQuotes
  14 FlexibleInstances
  10 OverloadedStrings
   8 RankNTypes
   8 FunctionalDependencies
   6 TupleSections
   5 LambdaCase
   5 InstanceSigs
   4 PatternSynonyms
   3 TemplateHaskellQuotes
   3 ScopedTypeVariables
   3 RecordWildCards
   3 NamedFieldPuns
   2 DeriveLift
   2 DeriveFunctor
   1 UndecidableInstances
   1 TypeApplications
   1 tag
   1 Rank
   1 pragma
   1 NoMonomorphismRestriction
   1 KindSignatures
   1 GeneralizedNewtypeDeriving
   1 ExistentialQuantification
   1 DerivingVia
   1 DeriveGeneric
   1 DeriveAnyClass
   1 DataKinds
   1 ConstraintKinds
```

Of these, the following are enabled by default with GHC2024:

* PostfixOperators
* FlexibleContexts
* GADTs
* MultiParamTypeClasses
* FlexibleInstances
* RankNTypes
* TupleSections
* LambdaCase
* InstanceSigs
* ScopedTypeVariables
* NamedFieldPuns
* DeriveLift
* DeriveFunctor
* TypeApplications
* KindSignatures
* GeneralisedNewtypeDeriving
* ExistentialQuantification
* DerivingGeneric
* DataKinds
* ConstraintKinds

The only ones that are not in the list are mostly the ones I would find questionable to enable by default:

* TemplateHaskell
* TypeFamilies
* QuasiQuotes
* OverloadedStrings
* FunctionalDependencies (I don't see this one as questionable, really? Since @B-rando1 is going to be using this a lot, it might be good to add it to the `package.yaml` of `drasil-gool`)
* PatternSynonyms
* RecordWildCards
* NoMonomorphismRestriction
* DerivingVia
* DerivingAnyClass

_Some_ other notable ones that would be enabled by default:

* ImportQualifiedPost: This is a nice readability touch.
* ConstrainedClassMethods
* DerivingTraversable

The only issue with upgrading our default language is that we would also need to upgrade our minimum GHC version from [HIDDEN]to at least GHC 9.10.1. GHCup currently recommends [HIDDEN]as the current LTS and is also supported by HLS.

problem_statement:
Platform integration: GPS / location services
Expose device location (latitude, longitude, altitude, accuracy) to Haskell.

Requires platform-side implementation using FusedLocationProviderClient (Android) and CLLocationManager (iOS). Permission request for Location already exists in the framework.

### Additional contract requirements

The location feature exposes the following publicly observable contract.

Haskell surface, module `HaskellMobile.Location`:

- `LocationData`, whose `ldLatitude`, `ldLongitude`, `ldAltitude`, and
  `ldAccuracy` record accessors each return a `Double`.
- `LocationState` and `newLocationState` for an initially inactive update
  handle.
- `startLocationUpdates` and `stopLocationUpdates` for registering and
  removing a location-update callback on that handle.
- `dispatchLocationUpdate`, the bridge-facing forwarding operation.  While an
  update callback is active, it delivers the latitude, longitude, altitude,
  and accuracy supplied by the platform bridge to that callback; after
  stopping, bridge updates are ignored.

`AppContext` exposes the location handle as `acLocationState`, and `UserState`
exposes it as `userLocationState`.

The top-level `HaskellMobile` module additionally exports
`haskellOnLocationUpdate`, the bridge entry point that device-facing
platform code calls with a forwarded latitude, longitude, altitude and
accuracy.  Calling it with those four values delivers that fix, unchanged,
to the callback currently registered on the supplied context's
`acLocationState` handle.

Forwarding contract for the platform integrations:

- Both the Android and the iOS integrations must take fixes delivered by
  the platform location framework and forward each fix's latitude,
  longitude, altitude and accuracy, unchanged, into the Haskell location
  service through the entry point above.
- The platform implementation may choose appropriate platform APIs and may
  organise its files and callback entry points freely, provided each
  delivered fix is forwarded as described.

Location authorization uses the framework's existing `PermissionLocation`
permission through the normal permission API; no additional permission kind
is introduced.

The contract does not require location delivery from a desktop environment
and does not specify any particular location values.

+{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
+-- | Test application used by the Android emulator and iOS simulator suites.
+module Main where
+
+import Data.Text (pack)
+import Foreign.Ptr (Ptr)
+import HaskellMobile
+  ( AppContext
+  , MobileApp(..)
+  , UserState(..)
+  , loggingMobileContext
+  , platformLog
+  , startLocationUpdates
+  , stopLocationUpdates
+  , startMobileApp
+  )
+import HaskellMobile.Location
+  ( LocationData(ldAccuracy, ldAltitude, ldLatitude, ldLongitude) )
+import HaskellMobile.Widget (ButtonConfig(..), TextConfig(..), Widget(..))
+
+main :: IO (Ptr AppContext)
+main = do
+  platformLog "Location demo app registered"
+  startMobileApp locationDemoApp
+
+locationDemoApp :: MobileApp
+locationDemoApp = MobileApp
+  { maContext = loggingMobileContext
+  , maView = locationDemoView
+  }
+
+locationDemoView :: UserState -> IO Widget
+locationDemoView userState = pure $ Column
+  [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "Location Demo", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+  , Button ButtonConfig
+      { bcLabel = "Start Location"
+      , bcAction = do
+          startLocationUpdates (userLocationState userState) $ \locationData ->
+            platformLog
+              ("Location: " <> pack (show (ldLatitude locationData))
+                <> "," <> pack (show (ldLongitude locationData))
+                <> " alt=" <> pack (show (ldAltitude locationData))
+                <> " acc=" <> pack (show (ldAccuracy locationData)))
+          platformLog "Location updates started"
+      , bcFontConfig = Nothing
+      }
+  , Button ButtonConfig
+      { bcLabel = "Stop Location"
+      , bcAction = do
+          stopLocationUpdates (userLocationState userState)
+          platformLog "Location updates stopped"
+      , bcFontConfig = Nothing
+      }
+  ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+
+xcrun simctl install "$SIM_UDID" "$LOCATION_APP"

+  --style compact > "$STREAM_LOG" 2>&1 &

+sleep 5
+
+# --autotest activates the first button, which starts location updates.

+sleep 1
+FULL_LOG="$WORK_DIR/location_full.log"

+  "iOS fix reaches Haskell with latitude, longitude, altitude and accuracy"
+

+exit "$EXIT_CODE"

problem_statement:
Platform integration: Maps
Embed a native map view (Google Maps / Apple Maps) within the haskell-mobile widget tree.

This is a platform view embedding problem: the map is a native view that needs to be composited into the widget hierarchy. Requires a new widget type and platform-side implementation using MapView (Android) and MKMapView (iOS).

### Additional contract requirements

Platform integration: Maps
Embed a native map view (the platform's map control, e.g. Google Maps on
Android, MKMapView/Apple Maps on iOS) within the haskell-mobile widget
tree.

## Public API

The library exposes the map widget through the public API as
`MapView` applied to a `MapViewConfig` record.  The record must provide,
at minimum:

- `mvLatitude :: Double` — center latitude (WGS-84, degrees).
- `mvLongitude :: Double` — center longitude (WGS-84, degrees).
- `mvZoom :: Double` — zoom level (approximately 1–20; platform
  implementations may clamp).
- `mvShowUserLocation :: Bool` — whether to display the user's current
  location on the map.
- `mvOnRegionChange :: Maybe OnChange` — optional region-change callback.
  When set, the configured callback is the public handle through which
  region-change notifications are delivered: a region-change
  notification arrives as text carrying the new region formatted as
  `"latitude,longitude,zoom"`, and delivering such region text through
  the native-facing text-event path must invoke the configured callback.
  The configured callback handle is stable across re-renders of the same
  widget (the render diff does not silently detach it).  How (or
  whether) the renderer wires the callback into the native bridge is an
  implementation detail.

## Observable behaviour

- Rendering a `MapView` must create a dedicated native node whose bridge
  node-type code is not one of the node-type codes already used by the
  pre-existing (non-map) widget kinds; the map is thus a distinct native
  node, composited into the widget tree like any other leaf widget.
- At attachment, the configured center latitude, center longitude, and
  zoom must be pushed to the map node before the root node is attached,
  so the initial region reaches the native map view.  Each value may be
  carried through whichever property channel the bridge exposes for it
  (a numeric property, or a string property mentioning the value such as
  a `"latitude,longitude,zoom"` region text); the choice of channel is an
  implementation detail.
- The configured `mvShowUserLocation` value must be communicated to the
  map node: rendering with `mvShowUserLocation = True` must produce an
  observable property of the map node that is distinguishable from
  rendering the same configuration with `mvShowUserLocation = False`.
  Which property channel carries this setting is an implementation
  detail and is not prescribed.
- `MapView` must render without error on its own and nested inside
  `Column`, `Row`, `ScrollView`, and `Styled`.  When nested, the map
  node must actually be composited into the rendered tree: for a
  container widget the map node must be attached into the container's
  native node through the parent-child composition operations of the
  bridge (at any depth), and a styled map must remain attached exactly
  as the unstyled map would be.
- `MapView` must survive re-renders (including renders that change the
  configured zoom or region); a re-render that changes the configuration
  must leave the map node reflecting the latest configured region,
  through whichever property channel carries it.
- An application whose view embeds a `MapView` must work through the
  same native-facing application entry points a platform host invokes
  (rendering the app's view from its application context and delivering
  lifecycle notifications): rendering the app must create, configure,
  and composite the map node through the bridge as part of the app's
  rendered view.
- The choice of the underlying native map view implementation on each
  platform target (for example Google Maps on Android, MKMapView on
  iOS) is an implementation detail and is not part of the asserted
  contract.
- Exact bridge property numbers, property channels, node-type code
  values, platform diagnostic/log text, and callback-registration
  mechanisms are implementation details and are not asserted.

+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Bridge interception support
+--
+-- The C UI bridge (include/UIBridge.h) dispatches every @ui_*@ call via a
+-- registered @UIBridgeCallbacks@ table and falls back to stderr stub
+-- logging for any individual entry that is NULL.  Observing a render is
+-- therefore just a matter of installing recording callbacks for the calls
+-- of interest and restoring them afterwards.  This is deterministic: the
+-- callbacks record directly into IORefs owned by the test, never touching
+-- process-wide stderr, and every other bridge call keeps its default stub
+-- behaviour for the duration of the observation.
+-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+-- | The C @UIBridgeCallbacks@ struct (include/UIBridge.h).  Every field
+-- is a function pointer, hence uniformly sized and addressable purely by
+-- 'cbField' offsets; only the pointer to the struct crosses the FFI.
+data UIBridgeCallbacks
+
+-- | One bridge call observed during an intercepted render.  The calls
+-- are recorded into one chronological event trace rather than segregated
+-- per entry point, because cross-call ordering (such as the initial
+-- region properties preceding the root attachment) is only observable
+-- from the actual interleaving of the calls.  Both the numeric and the
+-- string property channels are recorded: the bridge exposes a property
+-- channel per representation, and the contract does not prescribe which
+-- channel a given setting reaches the map node through, only that it
+-- reaches it observably.
+data BridgeEvent
+  = EvCreated Int32 Int32
+    -- ^ @createNode nodeType@ yielding @nodeId@.
+  | EvStrProp Int32 Int32 String
+    -- ^ @setStrProp nodeId propId value@.
+  | EvNumProp Int32 Int32 Double
+    -- ^ @setNumProp nodeId propId value@.
+  | EvAddChild Int32 Int32
+    -- ^ @addChild parentId childId@.
+  | EvRoot Int32
+    -- ^ @setRoot nodeId@.
+  deriving (Show, Eq)
+
+foreign import ccall safe "ui_register_callbacks"
+  c_uiRegisterCallbacks :: Ptr UIBridgeCallbacks -> IO ()
+
+-- | The native-facing text-event boundary the platform calls to report
+-- text events (such as a map region change) to Haskell, exported for C
+-- consumers.  The test re-imports it here to drive the native-to-Haskell
+-- region-notification path exactly the way the platform's map control
+-- does, without asserting how the renderer wires the configured callback
+-- into the bridge.
+foreign import ccall "haskellOnUITextChange"
+  c_nativeTextEvent :: Ptr AppContext -> CInt -> CString -> IO ()
+
+foreign import ccall "wrapper"
+  wrapCreateNode :: (CInt -> IO CInt) -> IO (FunPtr (CInt -> IO CInt))
+
+foreign import ccall "wrapper"
+  wrapSetStrProp :: (CInt -> CInt -> CString -> IO ())
+                 -> IO (FunPtr (CInt -> CInt -> CString -> IO ()))
+
+foreign import ccall "wrapper"
+  wrapSetNumProp :: (CInt -> CInt -> CDouble -> IO ())
+                 -> IO (FunPtr (CInt -> CInt -> CDouble -> IO ()))
+
+foreign import ccall "wrapper"
+  wrapAddChild :: (CInt -> CInt -> IO ())
+               -> IO (FunPtr (CInt -> CInt -> IO ()))
+
+foreign import ccall "wrapper"
+  wrapSetRoot :: (CInt -> IO ()) -> IO (FunPtr (CInt -> IO ()))
+
+-- | Uniform function-pointer field size and the field offsets of the
+-- @UIBridgeCallbacks@ entries the tests record.
+funPtrSize :: Int
+funPtrSize = sizeOf (nullFunPtr :: FunPtr ())
+
+cbCreateNode, cbSetStrProp, cbSetNumProp, cbAddChild, cbSetRoot :: Int
+cbCreateNode = 0
+cbSetStrProp = 1
+cbSetNumProp = 2
+cbAddChild = 5
+cbSetRoot = 8
+
+-- | Peek a single function-pointer field of a C @UIBridgeCallbacks@.
+peekCbField :: Ptr UIBridgeCallbacks -> Int -> IO (FunPtr a)
+peekCbField ptr field = peek (castPtr ptr `plusPtr` (field * funPtrSize))
+
+-- | Poke a single function-pointer field of a C @UIBridgeCallbacks@.
+pokeCbField :: Ptr UIBridgeCallbacks -> Int -> FunPtr a -> IO ()
+pokeCbField ptr field fp =
+  poke (castPtr ptr `plusPtr` (field * funPtrSize)) fp
+
+-- | Process-wide lock serialising bridge interceptions: installing
+-- callbacks mutates global state in the C bridge, and tasty runs test
+-- cases concurrently with -N, so two observations could otherwise
+-- interleave.
+{-# NOINLINE bridgeRecordingLock #-}
+bridgeRecordingLock :: MVar ()
+bridgeRecordingLock = unsafePerformIO (newMVar ())
+
+-- | Run the action with the bridge observed for the duration and return
+-- the action's result together with the chronological trace of every
+-- @createNode@, @setStrProp@, @setNumProp@, @addChild@, and @setRoot@
+-- call the action's renders produced.  Only the bridge calls carrying
+-- observable configuration or composition are intercepted: which
+-- handler-registration calls (if any) wire a callback into a node is an
+-- implementation detail of the renderer, so those calls are left to
+-- their default behaviour.  The previously installed callbacks are
+-- restored afterwards (they are all NULL under the default desktop
+-- stubs).
+withBridgeRecording :: IO a -> IO ([BridgeEvent], a)
+withBridgeRecording action = withMVar bridgeRecordingLock $ \() -> do
+  eventsRef <- newIORef []
+  let record event = modifyIORef' eventsRef (++ [event])
+  ptr <- callocBytes (10 * funPtrSize)
+  oldCreate <- peekCbField ptr cbCreateNode
+  oldStrProp <- peekCbField ptr cbSetStrProp
+  oldNumProp <- peekCbField ptr cbSetNumProp
+  oldAddChild <- peekCbField ptr cbAddChild
+  oldRoot <- peekCbField ptr cbSetRoot
+  nodeCounter <- newIORef (1000000 :: Int32)
+  let allocNodeId = do
+        nodeId <- readIORef nodeCounter
+        writeIORef nodeCounter (nodeId + 1)
+        pure (CInt nodeId)
+  createFp <- wrapCreateNode $ \(CInt nodeType) -> do
+    CInt nodeId <- allocNodeId
+    record (EvCreated nodeType nodeId)
+    pure (CInt nodeId)
+  strPropFp <- wrapSetStrProp $ \(CInt nodeId) (CInt propId) cstr -> do
+    value <- peekCString cstr
+    record (EvStrProp nodeId propId value)
+  numPropFp <- wrapSetNumProp $ \(CInt nodeId) (CInt propId) (CDouble value) ->
+    record (EvNumProp nodeId propId value)
+  addChildFp <- wrapAddChild $ \(CInt parentId) (CInt childId) ->
+    record (EvAddChild parentId childId)
+  rootFp <- wrapSetRoot $ \(CInt nodeId) ->
+    record (EvRoot nodeId)
+  pokeCbField ptr cbCreateNode createFp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetStrProp strPropFp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetNumProp numPropFp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbAddChild addChildFp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetRoot rootFp
+  c_uiRegisterCallbacks ptr
+  result <- action
+  pokeCbField ptr cbCreateNode oldCreate
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetStrProp oldStrProp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetNumProp oldNumProp
+  pokeCbField ptr cbAddChild oldAddChild
+  pokeCbField ptr cbSetRoot oldRoot
+  c_uiRegisterCallbacks nullPtr
+  events <- readIORef eventsRef
+  pure (events, result)
+
+-- | The (numeric, string) properties the trace set on the dedicated map
+-- nodes it created, as comparable @(propId, rendered value)@ pairs.  Both
+-- channels are included because the bridge exposes a property channel per
+-- representation and the contract does not prescribe which channel a
+-- given setting reaches the map node through.
+propsOnMapNodesTrace :: [BridgeEvent] -> ([(Int32, String)], [(Int32, String)])
+propsOnMapNodesTrace events =
+  ( [ (propId, show value)
+    | EvNumProp nodeId propId value <- events
+    , nodeId `elem` mapNodesFrom events
+    ]
+  , [ (propId, value)
+    | EvStrProp nodeId propId value <- events
+    , nodeId `elem` mapNodesFrom events
+    ]
+  )
+
+-- | The ids of the dedicated map nodes created in an event trace.
+mapNodesFrom :: [BridgeEvent] -> [Int32]
+mapNodesFrom events = [nodeId | EvCreated nodeType nodeId <- events
+                              , nodeType `notElem` nonMapNodeTypes]
+
+-- | The ids of the non-map nodes of the given kind created in an event
+-- trace (for example all created Column containers).
+createdNodesOfType :: [BridgeEvent] -> Int32 -> [Int32]
+createdNodesOfType events nodeType =
+  [nodeId | EvCreated observedType nodeId <- events
+          , observedType == nodeType]
+
+-- | The parent-child attach operations observed in an event trace, as
+-- directed edges @(parentId, childId)@.  Deduped: an incremental
+-- re-render is free to detach and re-attach children, so composition is
+-- about which pairs were ever attached, not how often.
+attachEdges :: [BridgeEvent] -> [(Int32, Int32)]
+attachEdges = dedupSimple . go
+  where
+    go [] = []
+    go (EvAddChild parentId childId : rest) =
+      (parentId, childId) : go rest
+    go (_ : rest) = go rest
+    dedupSimple = foldr (\edge acc -> if edge `elem` acc then acc else edge : acc) []
+
+-- | The nodes reachable from a start node by following the observed
+-- parent-child attach edges, including the start node itself.  Node ids
+-- are freshly allocated per recording, so simple reachability over the
+-- trace's edges reflects the rendered tree's composition.
+reachableFrom :: [BridgeEvent] -> Int32 -> [Int32]
+reachableFrom events start = visit [start] []
+  where
+    edges = attachEdges events
+    childrenOf nodeId = [childId | (parentId, childId) <- edges
+                                 , parentId == nodeId]
+    visit [] seen = seen
+    visit (nodeId:rest) seen
+      | nodeId `elem` seen = visit rest seen
+      | otherwise = visit (childrenOf nodeId ++ rest) (nodeId : seen)
+
+-- | Whether a dedicated map node is transitively composited underneath
+-- the given ancestor node through the trace's parent-child attachment
+-- operations.
+mapNodeUnder :: [BridgeEvent] -> Int32 -> Bool
+mapNodeUnder events ancestorId =
+  not (null [nodeId | nodeId <- reachableFrom events ancestorId
+                    , nodeId `elem` mapNodesFrom events])
+
+-- | Render the widget while recording the bridge, and require that a
+-- dedicated map node ends up composited underneath a node of the given
+-- container kind (through any depth of nesting, and regardless of which
+-- styling wrappers sit in between).
+assertMapNodeNestedIn :: Int32 -> Widget -> IO ()
+assertMapNodeNestedIn containerTypeCode widget = do
+  (events, ()) <- withBridgeRecording $ do
+    ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+    renderWidget rs widget
+  case mapNodesFrom events of
+    [] -> assertFailure
+      ("expected a dedicated map node to be created, got bridge events: "
+        ++ show events)
+    _ -> assertBool
+      ("expected the dedicated map node to be composited underneath a "
+        ++ "container node of the rendered container kind, got bridge "
+        ++ "events: " ++ show events)
+      (any (mapNodeUnder events) (createdNodesOfType events containerTypeCode))
+
+-- | Whether the trace carried the expected value to one of the
+-- dedicated map nodes it created (through whichever property channel).
+pushedToMapNode :: [BridgeEvent] -> Double -> Bool
+pushedToMapNode events expected =
+  any (\nodeId -> traceCarriesValue events nodeId expected) mapNodes
+  where
+    mapNodes = mapNodesFrom events
+
+-- | Find a dedicated map node that received all of an initial region's
+-- configured values and is attached -- as the traced root itself, or
+-- transitively underneath the traced root through the parent-child
+-- composition operations.  A region value counts as received when the
+-- trace carries it to that node: as a numeric property close to the
+-- value, or as a string property mentioning the plainly rendered value
+-- (for example inside a @"latitude,longitude,zoom"@ region text).  The
+-- bridge callback table is process-global, so selecting the map by both
+-- its complete configured region and its attachment keeps the ordering
+-- assertion tied to the map rendered by this test.
+--
+-- Note for nested maps that retrace the same trace: because ordering is
+-- later checked against the first root attachment in the trace, a map
+-- nested in a container may conflict with any root-attached widget
+-- rendered earlier in the same recording.  The ordering-sensitive
+-- region test therefore renders its map standalone; nested renders are
+-- checked for composition and value delivery instead of ordering.
+mapNodeForRegion :: [BridgeEvent] -> [Double] -> Maybe Int32
+mapNodeForRegion events expected =
+  case [ nodeId
+       | nodeId <- mapNodesFrom events
+       , all (\value -> traceCarriesValue events nodeId value) expected
+       , any (isReachableRootAttachment nodeId) events
+       ] of
+    nodeId : _ -> Just nodeId
+    []         -> Nothing
+  where
+    isReachableRootAttachment nodeId (EvRoot rootNodeId) =
+      nodeId == rootNodeId || nodeId `elem` reachableFrom events rootNodeId
+    isReachableRootAttachment _ _ = False
+
+-- | Check the configured region values against the root attachment for
+-- that same map node: every expected value must be carried to the map
+-- node before the node is attached as the root.  A single ordered trace
+-- is essential here: property and root calls recorded in separate
+-- collections cannot establish their cross-call ordering.
+regionPushedBeforeNodeRoot :: [BridgeEvent] -> Int32 -> [Double] -> Bool
+regionPushedBeforeNodeRoot events nodeId expected =
+  case break isThisNodeRoot events of
+    (beforeNodeRoot, _:_) ->
+      all (traceCarriesValue beforeNodeRoot nodeId) expected
+    (_, []) -> False
+  where
+    isThisNodeRoot (EvRoot rootNodeId) = rootNodeId == nodeId
+    isThisNodeRoot _                   = False
+
+-- | Whether a trace carries the expected value to the given node through
+-- one of the property channels the bridge exposes: as a numeric property
+-- close to the value, or as a string property mentioning the plainly
+-- rendered value.
+traceCarriesValue :: [BridgeEvent] -> Int32 -> Double -> Bool
+traceCarriesValue events nodeId expected =
+  any carriesValue events
+  where
+    carriesValue (EvNumProp observedNode _ actual) =
+      observedNode == nodeId && closeTo expected actual
+    carriesValue (EvStrProp observedNode _ actual) =
+      observedNode == nodeId && plainDoubleText expected `isInfixOfSimple` actual
+    carriesValue _ = False
+
+-- | The plain decimal rendering of a configured value, as it would
+-- appear inside region text such as @"latitude,longitude,zoom"@ (or in
+-- any serialised string property).
+plainDoubleText :: Double -> String
+plainDoubleText value
+  | fromIntegral (round value :: Integer) == value =
+      show (round value :: Integer) ++ ".0"
+  | otherwise = show value
+
+-- | Whether the needle occurs in the haystack.
+isInfixOfSimple :: String -> String -> Bool
+isInfixOfSimple needle haystack =
+  any (needle `isPrefixOfSimple`) (tailsSimple haystack)
+  where
+    isPrefixOfSimple [] _ = True
+    isPrefixOfSimple (c:cs) (h:hs) = c == h && isPrefixOfSimple cs hs
+    isPrefixOfSimple _ [] = False
+    tailsSimple xs = xs : case xs of
+      []     -> []
+      _:rest -> tailsSimple rest
+
+-- | Two bridge values are "the same coordinate" when they agree closely;
+-- numeric properties are passed as doubles and platform code is free to
+-- round for display.
+closeTo :: Double -> Double -> Bool
+closeTo expected actual = abs (expected - actual) < 0.01
+

+-- the native bridge ("MapView bridge").  These tests intercept the C
+-- UI-bridge callback table while rendering a map widget and require
+-- that the render:
+--
+--   1. creates at least one node whose type code is not used by any
+--      pre-existing widget kind (a dedicated map node),
+--   2. pushes the map widget's configured center latitude, center
+--      longitude, and zoom values to that node -- through whichever
+--      property channel the bridge exposes for them -- before the first
+--      root attachment, so the initial region reaches the native map
+--      view, and
+--   3. communicates the configured user-location display preference to
+--      the map node in an observable way, through whichever property
+--      channel carries it.
+--
+-- The node and property identifiers are discovered from the render trace;
+-- no literal identifier, selected property channel, platform class name, or
+-- diagnostic string is part of an assertion.  Callback wiring is not
+-- observed here: how (or whether) the renderer registers a configured
+-- region-change callback with the bridge is an implementation detail of
+-- the bridge layer; the contract requires only that a region
+-- notification reaches the caller-provided callback as region text,
+-- which the "MapView" group exercises through the public text-event
+-- dispatch path.
+mapViewBridgeTests :: TestTree
+mapViewBridgeTests =
+  -- The process-wide recording lock already serialises the
+  -- interceptions among themselves; making the group
+  -- dependent (sequential) additionally runs its test cases
+  -- strictly one at a time, and the root group's dependency
+  -- sequencing keeps every other suite outside these
+  -- recording windows entirely.
+  sequentialTestGroup "MapView native-facing integration" AllFinish
+  -- Installing bridge callbacks mutates process-global state in the C
+  -- bridge, so 'withBridgeRecording' serialises the interceptions
+  -- through a process-wide lock (tasty otherwise runs test cases
+  -- concurrently with -N).  A re-render of the same widget may replace
+  -- the map node in the widget tree with a fresh node carrying the
+  -- latest configuration.
+  [ testCase "rendering a MapView creates a dedicated map node and pushes its initial region" $ do
+      (events, ()) <- withBridgeRecording $ do
+        ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+        renderWidget rs $ MapView MapViewConfig
+          { mvLatitude = 52.3676, mvLongitude = 4.9041
+          , mvZoom = 12.0, mvShowUserLocation = True
+          , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+          }
+      case mapNodeForRegion events [52.3676, 4.9041, 12.0] of
+        Nothing -> assertFailure
+          ("expected a dedicated map node with the configured initial region, "
+            ++ "got bridge events: " ++ show events)
+        Just mapNodeId ->
+          assertBool
+            ("expected latitude, longitude, and zoom to be pushed to the "
+              ++ "identified map node before its root attachment, got bridge "
+              ++ "events: " ++ show events)
+            (regionPushedBeforeNodeRoot events mapNodeId [52.3676, 4.9041, 12.0])
+
+  , testCase "mvShowUserLocation distinguishes True from False on the map node" $ do
+      eventsTrue <- fst <$> withBridgeRecording (do
+        ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+        renderWidget rs $ MapView MapViewConfig
+          { mvLatitude = 52.3676, mvLongitude = 4.9041
+          , mvZoom = 12.0, mvShowUserLocation = True
+          , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+          })
+      eventsFalse <- fst <$> withBridgeRecording (do
+        ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+        renderWidget rs $ MapView MapViewConfig
+          { mvLatitude = 52.3676, mvLongitude = 4.9041
+          , mvZoom = 12.0, mvShowUserLocation = False
+          , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+          })
+      assertBool
+        ("expected mvShowUserLocation = True to reach the map node as an "
+          ++ "observable property (through whichever property channel the "
+          ++ "bridge exposes), got bridge events: "
+          ++ show eventsTrue)
+        (propsOnMapNodesTrace eventsTrue /= ([], []))
+      assertBool
+        ("expected mvShowUserLocation = True and = False to reach the map "
+          ++ "node differently (only the shared region values were pushed), "
+          ++ "True produced: " ++ show (propsOnMapNodesTrace eventsTrue)
+          ++ ", False produced: " ++ show (propsOnMapNodesTrace eventsFalse))
+        (propsOnMapNodesTrace eventsTrue /= propsOnMapNodesTrace eventsFalse)
+
+  , testCase "a re-rendered map keeps showing its latest configured region" $ do
+      -- A re-render may replace the map node with a fresh node carrying
+      -- the updated configuration; whichever dedicated map node is
+      -- current after the re-render, its latest configured latitude must
+      -- have been pushed to it.
+      (reEvents, ()) <- withBridgeRecording $ do
+        ((), rs) <- withActions (pure ())
+        renderWidget rs $ MapView MapViewConfig
+          { mvLatitude = 52.3676, mvLongitude = 4.9041
+          , mvZoom = 12.0, mvShowUserLocation = False
+          , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+          }
+        renderWidget rs $ MapView MapViewConfig
+          { mvLatitude = 48.8566, mvLongitude = 2.3522
+          , mvZoom = 10.0, mvShowUserLocation = False
+          , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+          }
+      case mapNodesFrom reEvents of
+        [] -> assertFailure
+          ("expected a dedicated map node to be created, got bridge events: "
+            ++ show reEvents)
+        _ ->
+          assertBool
+            ("expected the re-rendered latitude to be pushed to a dedicated "
+              ++ "map node, got bridge events: " ++ show reEvents)
+            (pushedToMapNode reEvents 48.8566)
+
+  , testCase "an application that composes MapView reaches its view through the shared native-facing lifecycle" $ do
+      -- Coverage of the application lifecycle path every supported
+      -- platform target drives: a native host hands an 'AppContext' to
+      -- the shared native-facing lifecycle entry points, so the test
+      -- requires the observable part of that integration to hold -- a
+      -- resume lifecycle notification reaches the app's context and the
+      -- app's own view (which embeds the map widget) is created and
+      -- configured through the bridge with the map composited
+      -- underneath its container.  The platform-specific hosting glue
+      -- around these entry points -- bundling the platform's native
+      -- map control into the host's view hierarchy -- is platform-owned
+      -- and is exercised by the platform build targets; its choice of
+      -- native map control is an implementation detail that no test may
+      -- second-guess.
+      lifecycleVar <- newMVar []
+      actionState <- newActionState
+      let app = MobileApp
+            { maContext     = defaultMobileContext
+                { onLifecycle = \event ->
+                    modifyMVar_ lifecycleVar (pure . (event :)) }
+            , maView        = \_userState -> pure $ Column
+                [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "places", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+                , MapView MapViewConfig
+                    { mvLatitude = 52.3676, mvLongitude = 4.9041
+                    , mvZoom = 12.0, mvShowUserLocation = True
+                    , mvOnRegionChange = Nothing
+                    }
+                ]
+            , maActionState = actionState
+            }
+      withAppContext app $ \ctxPtr -> do
+        haskellOnLifecycle ctxPtr (lifecycleToInt Resume)
+        (events, ()) <- withBridgeRecording (haskellRenderUI ctxPtr)
+        case mapNodesFrom events of
+          [] -> assertFailure
+            ("expected the app's rendered view to create a dedicated map "
+              ++ "node, got bridge events: " ++ show events)
+          _ -> do
+            case createdNodesOfType events (nodeTypeToInt NodeColumn) of
+              (columnNodeId : _) -> do
+                assertBool
+                  ("expected the map node to be composited underneath the app's "
+                    ++ "column through the native child slot, got bridge events: "
+                    ++ show events)
+                  (mapNodeUnder events columnNodeId)
+                assertBool
+                  ("expected the map's configured region values to reach a map "
+                    ++ "node composited underneath the app's column, got "
+                    ++ "bridge events: " ++ show events)
+                  (all (\value ->
+                          any (\mapNodeId ->
+                                traceCarriesValue events mapNodeId value)
+                              (reachableFrom events columnNodeId))
+                       [52.3676, 4.9041, 12.0])
+              [] ->
+                assertFailure
+                  ("expected the app's column container to be created, got "
+                    ++ "bridge events: " ++ show events)
+        observed <- readMVar lifecycleVar
+        assertBool
+          ("expected the resume lifecycle event to reach the app's context, "
+            ++ "observed: " ++ show observed)
+          (Resume `elem` observed)
+  ]
FAIL_TO_PASS: rebench explicit result

problem_statement:
Platform integration: App files directory path
On Android, each app gets a private sandboxed directory for persistent storage (e.g. `/data/data/com.example.app/files/`). Native code cannot discover this path on its own — only the Java side knows it via `Context.getFilesDir()`.

Currently, consumer apps that need to write files (e.g. a SQLite database) must provide their own C bridge and JNI glue to pass this path from Java to native code. In prrrrrrrrr this required two cbits files (`storage_helper.c` and `jni_extras.c`) plus a custom JNI method on the consumer's `MainActivity`.

It would be useful if hatter provided this out of the box — [HIDDEN] expose it to Haskell via a simple FFI call like `getAppFilesDir :: IO FilePath`.

This would eliminate per-app boilerplate for any app that needs persistent local storage.

### Additional contract requirements

The library must expose `getAppFilesDir :: IO FilePath` as a public export of
the top-level `HaskellMobile` module. It returns the app-private, persistent
files directory of the running application: the directory where the app may
store its own local files (for example a database) without writing any
per-app Java/C/JNI bridging boilerplate.

Required behaviour:

- No per-app setup: calling `getAppFilesDir` requires no additional
  app-supplied setup. From the host entry point (which performs no
  platform-specific initialisation) a call to `getAppFilesDir` already
  succeeds and returns a usable path.
- Totality: every call returns a non-empty file path. When the platform has
  not (yet) provided a path — for example the host/desktop entry point —
  it must return a plausible non-empty host-side default, never an empty
  string.
- Stability: repeated calls always return the same path.
- Storage usability: the directory named by the returned path is usable for
  ordinary local file storage: a file can be created directly inside it
  with `writeFile` and its full contents can be read back unchanged with
  `readFile`.

The unit test suite exercises these guarantees from the host entry point.
Platform-side provisioning on supported mobile targets — the app files
directory being provisioned by the platform bridge during startup (on
Android, the app Context files directory) so that the getter already
returns the provisioned app-private directory from the very start of the
app's execution — is covered by the supplied platform integration test
fixtures and scripts under `test/`, not by the host unit suite.

diff --git a/cbits/files_dir.c b/cbits/files_dir.c
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..eb1dd53f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cbits/files_dir.c
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+/*
+ * App files directory path.
+ *
+ * Uses a set/get pattern: platform bridges call setAppFilesDir() during
+ * initialization, and Haskell code reads it via getAppFilesDir().
+ *
+ * Android: jni_bridge.c calls setAppFilesDir() in JNI_OnLoad
+ *          (before haskellRunMain) via ActivityThread.currentApplication().
+ * iOS:     UIBridgeIOS.m calls setAppFilesDir() in setup_ios_platform_globals
+ *          (before haskellRunMain) via NSSearchPathForDirectoriesInDomains.
+ * Desktop: falls back to "." (current working directory).
+ */
+
+#include <stdlib.h>
+
+static const char *g_app_files_dir = NULL;
+
+void setAppFilesDir(const char *path)
+{
+    g_app_files_dir = path;  /* caller owns the memory (static/strdup'd) */
+}
+
+const char* getAppFilesDir(void)
+{
+    if (g_app_files_dir) return g_app_files_dir;
+    return ".";
+}

+    /* Pre-haskellRunMain platform init: set globals that Haskell code may
+       read immediately (e.g. in startMobileApp callbacks). */
     {
         JNIEnv *env;
         (*vm)->GetEnv(vm, (void**)&env, JNI_VERSION_1_6);
 
+        /* Locale: Locale.getDefault().toLanguageTag() (static, no context needed) */
         jclass localeClass = (*env)->FindClass(env, "java/util/Locale");
         jmethodID getDefault = (*env)->GetStaticMethodID(env, localeClass,
             "getDefault", "()Ljava/util/Locale;");
@@ -130,14 +134,37 @@ JNI_OnLoad(JavaVM *vm, void *reserved)

             "toLanguageTag", "()Ljava/lang/String;");

-        haskellLogLocale();
+        /* Files dir: ActivityThread.currentApplication().getFilesDir().
+           The Application exists before any Activity, so this is available
+           during JNI_OnLoad (called from System.loadLibrary). */
+        jclass atClass = (*env)->FindClass(env, "android/app/ActivityThread");
+        jmethodID currentApp = (*env)->GetStaticMethodID(env, atClass,
+            "currentApplication", "()Landroid/app/Application;");
+        jobject app = (*env)->CallStaticObjectMethod(env, atClass, currentApp);
+        if (app) {
+            jclass ctxClass = (*env)->FindClass(env, "android/content/Context");
+            jmethodID getFilesDir = (*env)->GetMethodID(env, ctxClass,
+                "getFilesDir", "()Ljava/io/File;");

+                setAppFilesDir(strdup(cpath));
+                (*env)->ReleaseStringUTFChars(env, jpath, cpath);
+            }
+        }
     }
 
+    g_haskell_ctx = haskellRunMain();
+    haskellLogLocale();
+
     return JNI_VERSION_1_6;
 }

+{-# LANGUAGE ForeignFunctionInterface #-}
+module HaskellMobile.FilesDir
+  ( getAppFilesDir
+  ) where
+
+import Foreign.C.String (CString, peekCString)
+
+foreign import ccall "getAppFilesDir" c_getAppFilesDir :: IO CString
+
+-- | Returns the platform-specific app files directory path.
+--
+-- On Android this is the result of @getFilesDir().getAbsolutePath()@,
+-- on iOS it is the Application Support directory, and on desktop it
+-- falls back to @"."@ (the current working directory).
+getAppFilesDir :: IO FilePath
+getAppFilesDir = peekCString =<< c_getAppFilesDir

+{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
+-- | Mobile entry point for the files directory integration test app.
+--
+-- Used by the emulator and simulator files directory integration tests.
+-- The app queries the app files directory twice: once /before/ the
+-- platform bridge has been started (to prove the path is already
+-- available during app startup) and once after the platform bridge is
+-- initialised (via startMobileApp).  It then writes a test file into
+-- the directory, reads it back, and logs every observation so the
+-- platform harness scripts can verify them.
+module Main where
+
+import Control.Exception (SomeException, try)
+import Data.Char (isSpace)
+import Data.Text (pack)
+import Foreign.Ptr (Ptr)
+import System.FilePath ((</>), takeDirectory)
+import HaskellMobile
+  ( MobileApp(..)
+  , AppContext
+  , startMobileApp
+  , platformLog
+  , getAppFilesDir
+  , loggingMobileContext
+  , newActionState
+  )
+import HaskellMobile.Widget (TextConfig(..), Widget(..))
+
+main :: IO (Ptr AppContext)
+main = do
+  -- The app files directory path must already be initialised before the
+  -- platform bridge runs the app's main entry point.
+  earlyFilesDir <- getAppFilesDir
+  platformLog ("FilesDirEarly: " <> pack earlyFilesDir)
+
+  actionState <- newActionState
+  ctxPtr <- startMobileApp MobileApp
+    { maContext     = loggingMobileContext
+    , maView        = \_userState -> filesDirDemoView
+    , maActionState = actionState
+    }
+  platformLog "FilesDir demo app registered"
+
+  -- Now that the platform bridge is initialised, query the files
+  -- directory again.
+  filesDir <- getAppFilesDir
+  platformLog ("FilesDir: " <> pack filesDir)
+

+  -- file storage.
+  let testFile = filesDir </> "hatter_filesdir_test.txt"
+      testContent = "hatter-test-ok"
+  platformLog ("FilesDir file parent: " <> pack (takeDirectory testFile))
+  writeResult <- try (writeFile testFile testContent) :: IO (Either SomeException ())
+  case writeResult of
+    Left err -> platformLog ("FilesDir write error: " <> pack (show err))
+    Right () -> do
+      readResult <- try (readFile testFile) :: IO (Either SomeException String)
+      case readResult of
+        Left err -> platformLog ("FilesDir read error: " <> pack (show err))
+        Right content
+          | content == testContent -> platformLog "FilesDir write-read OK"
+          | otherwise -> platformLog ("FilesDir write-read FAIL: got " <> pack content)
+
+  pure ctxPtr
+
+-- | Displays the app files directory path.
+filesDirDemoView :: IO Widget
+filesDirDemoView = do
+  filesDir <- getAppFilesDir
+  pure $ Column
+    [ Text TextConfig { tcLabel = "FilesDir Demo", tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+    , Text TextConfig { tcLabel = pack (trim filesDir), tcFontConfig = Nothing }
+    ]
+
+-- | Strip leading and trailing whitespace.
+trim :: String -> String
+trim = f . f
+  where f = reverse . dropWhile isSpace

+"$ADB" -s "$EMULATOR_SERIAL" logcat -c
