problem_statement:
No runtime permission management API
The Android manifest declares no permissions. The iOS side has no usage description strings (\`NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription\`, \`NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription\`, etc.) in Info.plist.

Beyond missing declarations, there is no Haskell API to:
- Request permissions at runtime
- Check current grant status
- Respond to user decisions (grant/deny)

On modern Android (API 26+) and iOS, dangerous permissions (location, Bluetooth, camera) must be requested at runtime with explicit user prompts. The OS will kill or silently block operations attempted without prior grant.

Without a permission bridge, an application cannot know whether it has access, cannot prompt the user, and cannot degrade gracefully when denied.

### Additional contract requirements

Runtime permission management contract.

The library provides a public runtime permission module named
`HaskellMobile.Permission`.

`Permission` has exactly the constructors `PermissionLocation`,
`PermissionBluetooth`, `PermissionCamera`, `PermissionMicrophone`,
`PermissionContacts`, and `PermissionStorage`, in that declaration order, and
supports equality. `PermissionStatus` has exactly the constructors
`PermissionGranted` and `PermissionDenied` and supports equality.

The value-level API is:

* `newPermissionState :: IO PermissionState` creates an isolated state for
  pending permission requests. `PermissionState` is opaque. A request made
  through one state can only be resolved through that same state.
* `requestPermission :: PermissionState -> Permission -> (PermissionStatus ->
  IO ()) -> IO ()` records a request and allocates a `CInt` request ID.
  Request IDs start at 0 and increase sequentially for each newly-created
  state. Resolving a request invokes its callback exactly once.
* `dispatchPermissionResult :: PermissionState -> CInt -> CInt -> IO ()`
  resolves the pending request identified by the request ID using the supplied
  status code. A result for an unknown or already-resolved ID has no effect.
  A status code that does not decode leaves the request pending so that a
  later valid result can resolve it.
* `checkPermission :: Permission -> IO PermissionStatus` reports the current
  grant status synchronously.

The public conversion functions are `permissionToInt :: Permission -> CInt`
and `permissionStatusFromInt :: CInt -> Maybe PermissionStatus`.
`PermissionLocation` through `PermissionStorage` encode as 0 through 5 in
that order. Status code 0 decodes to `Just PermissionGranted` and status code
1 to `Just PermissionDenied`; every other status code decodes to `Nothing`.

`HaskellMobile` publicly exports `AppState(..)` and `globalAppState ::
AppState`. The field `appPermissionState :: AppState -> PermissionState`
provides an application's shared permission state. In the desktop test
backend, requests through that shared state resolve as `PermissionGranted`,
and `checkPermission` reports `PermissionGranted` for every permission.

Android and iOS adapters present their respective runtime authorization UI and
route the resulting grant or denial back through the public request/result
semantics above. Their conformance is defined by those observable semantics;
this portable test contract does not prescribe native source-file names,
method spellings, symbols, or project-layout details. Platform UI presentation
requires an Android or iOS integration environment rather than a desktop
source-text test.

Beyond missing declarations, there is no Haskell API to:
- Request permissions at runtime
- Check current grant status
- Respond to user decisions (grant/deny)

On modern Android (API 26+) and iOS, dangerous permissions (location, Bluetooth, camera) must be requested at runtime with explicit user prompts. The OS will kill or silently block operations attempted without prior grant.

Without a permission bridge, an application cannot know whether it has access, cannot prompt the user, and cannot degrade gracefully when denied.
contract_addendum:
Runtime permission management contract.

The library provides a public runtime permission module named
`HaskellMobile.Permission`.

`Permission` has exactly the constructors `PermissionLocation`,
`PermissionBluetooth`, `PermissionCamera`, `PermissionMicrophone`,
`PermissionContacts`, and `PermissionStorage`, in that declaration order, and
supports equality. `PermissionStatus` has exactly the constructors
`PermissionGranted` and `PermissionDenied` and supports equality.

The value-level API is:

* `newPermissionState :: IO PermissionState` creates an isolated state for
  pending permission requests. `PermissionState` is opaque. A request made
  through one state can only be resolved through that same state.
* `requestPermission :: PermissionState -> Permission -> (PermissionStatus ->
  IO ()) -> IO ()` records a request and allocates a `CInt` request ID.
  Request IDs start at 0 and increase sequentially for each newly-created
  state. Resolving a request invokes its callback exactly once.
* `dispatchPermissionResult :: PermissionState -> CInt -> CInt -> IO ()`
  resolves the pending request identified by the request ID using the supplied
  status code. A result for an unknown or already-resolved ID has no effect.
  A status code that does not decode leaves the request pending so that a
  later valid result can resolve it.
* `checkPermission :: Permission -> IO PermissionStatus` reports the current
  grant status synchronously.

The public conversion functions are `permissionToInt :: Permission -> CInt`
and `permissionStatusFromInt :: CInt -> Maybe PermissionStatus`.
`PermissionLocation` through `PermissionStorage` encode as 0 through 5 in
that order. Status code 0 decodes to `Just PermissionGranted` and status code
1 to `Just PermissionDenied`; every other status code decodes to `Nothing`.

`HaskellMobile` publicly exports `AppState(..)` and `globalAppState ::
AppState`. The field `appPermissionState :: AppState -> PermissionState`
provides an application's shared permission state. In the desktop test
backend, requests through that shared state resolve as `PermissionGranted`,
and `checkPermission` reports `PermissionGranted` for every permission.

Android and iOS adapters present their respective runtime authorization UI and
route the resulting grant or denial back through the public request/result
semantics above. Their conformance is defined by those observable semantics;
this portable test contract does not prescribe native source-file names,
method spellings, symbols, or project-layout details. Platform UI presentation
requires an Android or iOS integration environment rather than a desktop
source-text test.

+      callbackCount <- newIORef (0 :: Int)

+      stateB <- newPermissionState
+      actualA <- newIORef (Nothing :: Maybe PermissionStatus)
+      actualB <- newIORef (Nothing :: Maybe PermissionStatus)
+      requestPermission stateA PermissionLocation
+        (\status -> modifyIORef' actualA (const (Just status)))
+      requestPermission stateB PermissionCamera
+        (\status -> modifyIORef' actualB (const (Just status)))

+      dispatchPermissionResult stateB 0 1

+      callbackCount <- newIORef (0 :: Int)
+      actual <- newIORef (Nothing :: Maybe PermissionStatus)

+      dispatchPermissionResult permissionState 0 0

+      finalStatus @?= Just PermissionGranted

+      dispatchPermissionResult permissionState 999 0

+      actual <- newIORef (Nothing :: Maybe PermissionStatus)
+      requestPermission permissionState PermissionStorage
+        (\status -> modifyIORef' actual (const (Just status)))
+      dispatchPermissionResult permissionState 0 0

+      second <- newIORef (Nothing :: Maybe PermissionStatus)

+        (\status -> modifyIORef' second (const (Just status)))

+        , PermissionStorage

+      permissionToInt PermissionBluetooth  @?= 1
+      permissionToInt PermissionCamera     @?= 2
+      permissionToInt PermissionMicrophone @?= 3
+      permissionToInt PermissionContacts   @?= 4
+      permissionToInt PermissionStorage    @?= 5

+      permissionStatusFromInt 1 @?= Just PermissionDenied

+  , testCase "unknown status bridge codes do not decode" $ do

Track board SubBoard model/API slice
## Symptom

`/Users/dancer/Downloads/masc_sns.agent.final/masc_sns.agent.final.md` marks SubBoard as Phase 2/3 work, not implemented in the current board model/API/UI.

## Reproduction

- Inspect the artifact's final PR split: `board-subboard-model`.
- Search current open issues for `subboard board`: no open tracker found before creating this issue.

## Suspected Cause

The existing board implementation is still centered on flat posts/comments/reactions. There is no separate SubBoard domain model, routing contract, permission boundary, or dashboard navigation surface yet.

## Tried

- Kept SubBoard out of PR #13321 because that PR only closes the Phase 1A embedded reaction preview gap.
- Verified no duplicate open issue via `gh issue list --search "subboard board"`.

### Additional contract requirements

# SubBoard model/API slice

This task covers only the SubBoard domain model and its in-process
`Board`/`Board_dispatch` API (the model/API slice). HTTP route handlers,
authorization/permission enforcement beyond expressing the access policy on
the record, and dashboard navigation surfaces are out of scope: nothing in
this contract requires them.

## Model

- The board library exposes a SubBoard record type with at least these
  fields: `id`, `slug`, `name`, `description`, `owner`, `access`,
  `created_at`, `post_count`.
- `id` has type `Board.Sub_board_id.t`; the module `Board.Sub_board_id`
  provides `to_string : t -> string` and `of_string`.
- `owner` has type `Board.Agent_id.t`, convertible with
  `Board.Agent_id.to_string`.
- `access` has type `Board.sub_board_access` with constructors
  `Board.Open`, `Board.Members_only`, and `Board.Owner_only`.

## Operations

All operations are functions of the `Board_dispatch` module and must work
with the JSONL backend selected by `Board_dispatch.init_jsonl` (the default
test configuration: `MASC_BASE_PATH` set to a fresh directory,
`Board.reset_global_for_test ()`, `Board_dispatch.reset_for_test ()`,
`Board_dispatch.init_jsonl ()`).

- `Board_dispatch.create_sub_board ~slug ~name ~description ~owner ?access ()`
  returns `(Board.sub_board, Board.board_error) result`.
  - The `~owner` argument is supplied as a plain `string` containing the
    owner agent's identifier (for example `"agent-1"`); the returned
    record stores it in the `owner` field of type `Board.Agent_id.t`.
  - The returned record preserves the supplied name, description, and owner;
    it starts with `post_count` zero and a creation timestamp in `created_at`.
  - The generated identifier can be converted to a string and parsed back
    with `Board.Sub_board_id`.
  - The slug is trimmed and lowercased, then validated: 1-64 characters
    consisting of lowercase alphanumerics, hyphens, and underscores,
    starting with an alphanumeric. An invalid slug fails with
    `Validation_error`.
  - Creating a sub-board whose slug is already in use fails with
    `Already_exists`.
  - When `access` is omitted, the created sub-board's access is
    `Board.Open`.
- `Board_dispatch.get_sub_board ~sub_board_id` accepts either a sub-board
  id string or a slug and returns the matching sub-board; an unknown id or
  slug fails with `Invalid_id`.
- `Board_dispatch.list_sub_boards ()` returns all sub-boards sorted by
  `created_at` ascending.
- `Board_dispatch.delete_sub_board ~sub_board_id` accepts either a
  sub-board id string or a slug; deleting an unknown id or slug fails with
  `Invalid_id`. After deletion, looking the sub-board up by id or by slug
  fails with `Invalid_id`.
- Sub-boards created through the JSONL backend are retained when the board
  and dispatch state are reset and the same JSONL backend is initialized
  again for the same base path.

## Errors

Relevant `Board.board_error` constructors for this slice:
`Validation_error` (invalid slug), `Already_exists` (duplicate slug), and
`Invalid_id` (unknown id/slug on lookup or delete).

+
+// --- SubBoard API ---
+
+function normalizeSubBoardAccess(raw: unknown): SubBoardAccess {
+  if (raw === 'members_only' || raw === 'owner_only') return raw
+  return 'open'
+}
+
+export function normalizeSubBoard(raw: unknown): SubBoard | null {
+  if (!isRecord(raw)) return null
+  const id = asString(raw.id, '').trim()
+  const slug = asString(raw.slug, '').trim()
+  const name = asString(raw.name, '').trim()
+  if (!id || !slug) return null
+  return {
+    id,
+    slug,
+    name,
+    description: asString(raw.description, ''),
+    owner: asString(raw.owner, ''),
+    access: normalizeSubBoardAccess(raw.access),
+    created_at: asNullableIsoTimestamp(raw.created_at) ?? new Date(0).toISOString(),
+    post_count: asInt(raw.post_count) ?? 0,
+  }
+}
+
+export async function fetchSubBoards(): Promise<SubBoard[]> {
+  const data = await withRetries('fetchSubBoards', () => get('/api/v1/board/sub-boards'))
+  if (!isRecord(data)) return []
+  const raw = Array.isArray(data.sub_boards) ? data.sub_boards : []
+  return raw.flatMap((r: unknown) => {
+    const sb = normalizeSubBoard(r)
+    return sb ? [sb] : []
+  })
+}
+
+export async function fetchSubBoard(subBoardId: string): Promise<SubBoard | null> {
+  const data = await withRetries('fetchSubBoard', () => get(`/api/v1/board/sub-boards/${encodeURIComponent(subBoardId)}`))
+  return normalizeSubBoard(data)
+}
+
+export function createSubBoard(
+  slug: string,
+  name: string,
+  description: string,
+  access?: SubBoardAccess,
+): Promise<unknown> {
+  const body: Record<string, string> = { slug, name, description }
+  if (access) body.access = access
+  return post('/api/v1/board/sub-boards', body)
+}

-## 11. 불변식 (Invariants)
+## 11. SubBoard (하위 게시판)
+
+SubBoard는 보드 내에 독립적인 이름 공간(named namespace)을 제공하는 Phase 2 기능이다. 각 SubBoard는 고유한 슬러그(slug)와 접근 정책(access policy)을 가진다.
+
+### 11.1 타입
+
+```ocaml
+module Sub_board_id : sig
+  type t
+  val prefix : string            (* "sb-" *)
+  val make : unit -> t
+  val to_string : t -> string
+  val of_string : string -> (t, board_error) Result.t
+end
+
+type sub_board_access =
+  | Open          (* 누구나 게시 가능 *)
+  | Members_only  (* 멤버만 게시, 전체 읽기 가능 *)
+  | Owner_only    (* 소유자만 게시, 전체 읽기 가능 *)
+
+type sub_board = {
+  id          : Sub_board_id.t;
+  slug        : string;     (* lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens/underscores, 1-64 chars *)
+  name        : string;
+  description : string;
+  owner       : string;
+  access      : sub_board_access;
+  created_at  : float;
+  post_count  : int;
+}
+```
+
+### 11.2 HTTP 라우팅 계약
+
+| Method | Path | 설명 |
+|--------|------|------|
+| GET | `/api/v1/board/sub-boards` | 전체 SubBoard 목록 (`{sub_boards: [...]}`) |
+| POST | `/api/v1/board/sub-boards` | SubBoard 생성 (`slug`, `name`, `description`, `access?` 필요) |
+| GET | `/api/v1/board/sub-boards/<id_or_slug>` | 단일 SubBoard 조회 (ID 또는 slug로 검색) |
+
+POST 요청은 `with_tool_auth` (`tool_name: "board_sub_board_create"`)로 인증.
+
+### 11.3 접근 정책 (Permission Model)

+(** {1 SubBoard Operations} *)
+
+let sub_board_access_to_string = function
+  | Open -> "open"
+  | Members_only -> "members_only"
+  | Owner_only -> "owner_only"
+
+let sub_board_access_of_string_opt = function
+  | "open" -> Some Open
+  | "members_only" -> Some Members_only
+  | "owner_only" -> Some Owner_only
+  | _ -> None
+
+let sub_board_to_yojson (sb : sub_board) : Yojson.Safe.t =
+  `Assoc [
+    ("id", `String (Sub_board_id.to_string sb.id));
+    ("slug", `String sb.slug);
+    ("name", `String sb.name);
+    ("description", `String sb.description);
+    ("owner", `String (Agent_id.to_string sb.owner));
+    ("access", `String (sub_board_access_to_string sb.access));
+    ("created_at", `Float sb.created_at);
+    ("post_count", `Int sb.post_count);
+  ]
+
+let sub_board_of_yojson (json : Yojson.Safe.t) : sub_board option =
+  let open Safe_ops in
+  match json with
+  | `Assoc _ ->
+      let id_s = json_string_opt "id" json |> Option.value ~default:"" in
+      let slug = json_string_opt "slug" json |> Option.value ~default:"" in
+      let name = json_string_opt "name" json |> Option.value ~default:"" in
+      let description = json_string_opt "description" json |> Option.value ~default:"" in
+      let owner_s = json_string_opt "owner" json |> Option.value ~default:"" in
+      let access_s = json_string_opt "access" json |> Option.value ~default:"open" in
+      let created_at = json_float_opt "created_at" json |> Option.value ~default:0.0 in
+      let post_count = json_int_opt "post_count" json |> Option.value ~default:0 in
+      (match Sub_board_id.of_string id_s, Agent_id.of_string owner_s,
+             sub_board_access_of_string_opt access_s with
+       | Ok id, Ok owner, Some access when slug <> "" ->
+           Some { id; slug; name; description; owner; access; created_at; post_count }
+       | _ -> None)
+  | _ -> None
+
+let rewrite_sub_boards store =
+  try
+    ensure_masc_dir ();
+    let path = sub_boards_path () in
+    let buf = Buffer.create 1024 in
+    Hashtbl.iter (fun _ (sb : sub_board) ->
+      Buffer.add_string buf (Yojson.Safe.to_string (sub_board_to_yojson sb));
+      Buffer.add_char buf '\n'
+    ) store.sub_boards;
+    (match Fs_compat.save_file_atomic path (Buffer.contents buf) with
+     | Ok () -> ()
+     | Error msg -> record_persist_error ~where:"rewrite_sub_boards" msg)
+  with Sys_error msg -> record_persist_error ~where:"rewrite_sub_boards" msg
+
+let append_sub_board (sb : sub_board) =
+  try
+    ensure_masc_dir ();
+    let path = sub_boards_path () in
+    Fs_compat.append_file path (Yojson.Safe.to_string (sub_board_to_yojson sb) ^ "\n")
+  with Sys_error msg -> record_persist_error ~where:"append_sub_board" msg
+
+let valid_slug_pattern = Re.Pcre.re {|^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$|} |> Re.compile
+
+let create_sub_board store ~slug ~name ~description ~owner
+    ?(access = Open) () : (sub_board, board_error) Result.t =
+  let slug = String.lowercase_ascii (String.trim slug) in
+  if String.length slug < 1 || String.length slug > 64
+     || not (Re.execp valid_slug_pattern slug) then
+    Error (Validation_error
+      (Printf.sprintf "Invalid sub-board slug %S: must be 1-64 lowercase alphanumeric/-/_" slug))
+  else
+    match Agent_id.of_string owner with
+    | Error e -> Error e
+    | Ok owner_id ->
+        with_lock store (fun () ->
+          if Hashtbl.mem store.sub_boards_by_slug slug then
+            Error (Already_exists
+              (Printf.sprintf "Sub-board slug %S already exists" slug))
+          else begin
+            let current = Hashtbl.length store.sub_boards in
+            if current >= Limits.max_sub_boards then
+              Error (Capacity_exceeded { current; max = Limits.max_sub_boards })
+            else begin
+              let id = Sub_board_id.generate () in
+              let sb = {
+                id;
+                slug;
+                name = String.trim name;
+                description = String.trim description;
+                owner = owner_id;
+                access;
+                created_at = Time_compat.now ();
+                post_count = 0;
+              } in
+              Hashtbl.replace store.sub_boards (Sub_board_id.to_string id) sb;
+              Hashtbl.replace store.sub_boards_by_slug slug (Sub_board_id.to_string id);
+              append_sub_board sb;
+              Ok sb
+            end
+          end)
+
+let get_sub_board store ~sub_board_id : (sub_board, board_error) Result.t =
+  with_lock store (fun () ->
+    match Hashtbl.find_opt store.sub_boards sub_board_id with
+    | Some sb -> Ok sb
+    | None ->
+        (* fallback: try slug *)
+        match Hashtbl.find_opt store.sub_boards_by_slug sub_board_id with
+        | Some id ->
+            (match Hashtbl.find_opt store.sub_boards id with
+             | Some sb -> Ok sb
+             | None -> Error (Invalid_id (Printf.sprintf "Sub-board not found: %s" sub_board_id)))
+        | None -> Error (Invalid_id (Printf.sprintf "Sub-board not found: %s" sub_board_id)))
+
+let list_sub_boards store : sub_board list =
+  with_lock store (fun () ->
+    Hashtbl.fold (fun _ sb acc -> sb :: acc) store.sub_boards []
+    |> List.sort (fun (a : sub_board) (b : sub_board) ->
+        compare a.created_at b.created_at))
+
+let delete_sub_board store ~sub_board_id : (unit, board_error) Result.t =
+  with_lock store (fun () ->
+    match Hashtbl.find_opt store.sub_boards sub_board_id with
+    | None ->
+        (match Hashtbl.find_opt store.sub_boards_by_slug sub_board_id with
+         | None -> Error (Invalid_id (Printf.sprintf "Sub-board not found: %s" sub_board_id))
+         | Some id ->
+             Hashtbl.remove store.sub_boards id;
+             Hashtbl.remove store.sub_boards_by_slug sub_board_id;
+             rewrite_sub_boards store;
+             Ok ())
+    | Some sb ->
+        Hashtbl.remove store.sub_boards sub_board_id;
+        Hashtbl.remove store.sub_boards_by_slug sb.slug;
+        rewrite_sub_boards store;
+        Ok ())
+

problem_statement:
incident: remove FSM guard counter-mode escape hatch
## Symptom
The live incident analysis calls out FSM guard soft mode as a keeper silent-failure vector: assertion failures can be counted and swallowed instead of aborting the turn.

## Current main evidence
- `lib/keeper/keeper_fsm_guard_runtime.ml` defaults to hard mode, but `MASC_FSM_GUARD_ASSERT=0` still disables re-raise.
- `lib/keeper/keeper_fsm_guard_runtime.mli`, `docs/observability/keeper-turn-fsm-metrics.md`, and related comments still document the soft/counter mode.

## Required fix
Make FSM guard violations fail closed unconditionally: bump the Prometheus violation counter and re-raise `Assert_failure` every time. Remove the operator/runtime soft-mode contract from docs/tests.

problem_statement:
fix(test): test_operator_control CI failure — FileSystem backend pub/sub not supported
## Problem

`Build and Test` CI job fails on main due to `test_operator_control` tests.

```
[ERROR] [Misc] broadcast publish failed for default: (Backend_core.BackendNotSupported
   "FileSystem backend does not support pub/sub")
```

CI forces `MASC_STORAGE_TYPE=filesystem` (test/dune env), but operator_control tests rely on `broadcast publish` which requires PostgreSQL backend.

## Impact
- main CI `Build and Test` is red
- Blocks accurate CI signal for all PRs

## Possible fixes
1. Skip pub/sub-dependent operator tests when backend is FileSystem
2. Add a mock/stub pub/sub for FileSystem backend in test context
3. Separate operator tests into a dedicated test group with PG backend requirement

## Context
Discovered during #1427 (Eio test context fix). main branch also fails with same error.

### Additional contract requirements

## Filesystem CI broadcasts

The filesystem-backed CI configuration must permit the operator-control
broadcast action to complete without reporting a failed publish notification.
The durable room message remains required. Real-time notification is optional
for a storage backend that does not support it, so it may be delivered locally,
omitted, or handled without an error report. No in-memory or filesystem
subscriber delivery, count, or fan-out guarantee is required by this contract.

   tmp_dir
 
+
+(** Run [f] while collecting its stderr.  This observes the diagnostic emitted
+    by the filesystem CI broadcast path without requiring a backend-specific
+    delivery or subscriber-count contract. *)
+let capture_stderr f =
+  let read_fd, write_fd = Unix.pipe () in
+  let saved_stderr = Unix.dup Unix.stderr in
+  Unix.dup2 write_fd Unix.stderr;
+  Unix.close write_fd;
+  let outcome =
+    match f () with
+    | value -> Ok value
+    | exception exn -> Error (exn, Printexc.get_raw_backtrace ())
+  in
+  flush stderr;
+  Unix.dup2 saved_stderr Unix.stderr;
+  Unix.close saved_stderr;
+  let buffer = Buffer.create 256 in
+  let bytes = Bytes.create 256 in
+  let rec read_all () =
+    match Unix.read read_fd bytes 0 (Bytes.length bytes) with
+    | 0 -> ()
+    | count ->
+        Buffer.add_subbytes buffer bytes 0 count;
+        read_all ()
+  in
+  read_all ();
+  Unix.close read_fd;
+  match outcome with
+  | Ok value -> (value, Buffer.contents buffer)
+  | Error (exn, backtrace) -> Printexc.raise_with_backtrace exn backtrace
+
+let contains text fragment =
+  let text_length = String.length text in
+  let fragment_length = String.length fragment in
+  let rec loop offset =
+    fragment_length = 0
+    || (offset + fragment_length <= text_length
+       && (String.sub text offset fragment_length = fragment
+          || loop (offset + 1)))
+  in
+  loop 0

problem_statement:
health build.commit can report repo HEAD for stale binary
## Symptom

After the 0.19.20 version truth bump merged, the live 8935 process reported a fresh repo commit in `/health.build.commit`, while the executable still reported the old package version.

Observed on 2026-05-17:

- repo truth: `dune-project`, `masc_mcp.opam`, ROADMAP, and Product Operating Plan all report `0.19.20`
- `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe --version` prints `0.19.19`
- `/health` reports `version=0.19.19` but `build.commit=86a54fddf0`
- `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe` mtime was `2026-05-17 16:35`, before the later main merges

This makes `build.commit` look like a compile-time binary identity even when it appears to be runtime repo HEAD truth.

## Reproduction

1. Merge a docs/version bump or other main commit without rebuilding `bin/main_eio.exe`.
2. Start the existing `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe` from the repo root.
3. Compare:
   - `./_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe --version`
   - `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8935/health | jq '.version, .build.commit, .build.executable_path'`
   - `ls -l _build/default/bin/main_eio.exe`

## Suspected cause

[HIDDEN]

## Tried

- Rebuilt/restarted live 8935 from the existing root binary to restore service.
- Tried focused rebuild via `scripts/dune-local.sh build bin/main_eio.exe`; initially blocked by `/tmp/me-dune-local.lock`.
- Tried direct `dune build --root . bin/main_eio.exe`; blocked by root `_build/.lock`.

## Desired fix

Separate these fields explicitly, for example:

- `binary_commit` or `compiled_commit`: compile-time build identity if available, otherwise null/unknown
- `repo_head_commit`: current checkout HEAD at runtime
- `binary_version`: compiled package version
- `repo_version`: current `dune-project` package version, if read at runtime

Until that split exists, dashboard/runtime trust should avoid treating `/health.build.commit` as proof that the running binary was rebuilt from that commit.

### Additional contract requirements

## Build identity in health and runtime diagnostics

The health response distinguishes the identity of the running executable from
information read from its current checkout.  Its `build` object includes:

- `binary_version`, the version compiled into the running executable, alongside
  the backwards-compatible `release_version`;
- `repo_version`, when the current checkout's package version can be read;
- `binary_commit`, the compiled build commit when build metadata is available;
- `repo_head_commit`, the current checkout HEAD when it can be resolved; and
- `commit`, a backwards-compatible value that is the compiled commit when
  available and otherwise the runtime repository HEAD.

Commit fields are nullable when their corresponding metadata cannot be
obtained.  When `commit` is non-null, `commit_source` is a non-empty string so
consumers can distinguish compiled metadata from a runtime checkout value
without relying on the commit text; when `commit` is null the representation
of `commit_source` is unspecified.  Repository-derived fields are checkout
observations and do not establish that the executable was rebuilt from that
checkout.

The dashboard runtime-resolution payload exposes the same distinction through
`runtime_binary_git_commit` and `runtime_repo_head_git_commit`.  The former may
be null when compiled metadata is unavailable; the latter reports the runtime
checkout HEAD when available.  Consumers must not use the latter as evidence
of binary freshness.

After the 0.19.20 version truth bump merged, the live 8935 process reported a fresh repo commit in `/health.build.commit`, while the executable still reported the old package version.

Observed on 2026-05-17:

- repo truth: `dune-project`, `masc_mcp.opam`, ROADMAP, and Product Operating Plan all report `0.19.20`
- `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe --version` prints `0.19.19`
- `/health` reports `version=0.19.19` but `build.commit=86a54fddf0`
- `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe` mtime was `2026-05-17 16:35`, before the later main merges

This makes `build.commit` look like a compile-time binary identity even when it appears to be runtime repo HEAD truth.

## Reproduction

1. Merge a docs/version bump or other main commit without rebuilding `bin/main_eio.exe`.
2. Start the existing `_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe` from the repo root.
3. Compare:
   - `./_build/default/bin/main_eio.exe --version`
   - `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8935/health | jq '.version, .build.commit, .build.executable_path'`
   - `ls -l _build/default/bin/main_eio.exe`

## Suspected cause

[HIDDEN]

## Tried

- Rebuilt/restarted live 8935 from the existing root binary to restore service.
- Tried focused rebuild via `scripts/dune-local.sh build bin/main_eio.exe`; initially blocked by `/tmp/me-dune-local.lock`.
- Tried direct `dune build --root . bin/main_eio.exe`; blocked by root `_build/.lock`.

## Desired fix

Separate these fields explicitly, for example:

- `binary_commit` or `compiled_commit`: compile-time build identity if available, otherwise null/unknown
- `repo_head_commit`: current checkout HEAD at runtime
- `binary_version`: compiled package version
- `repo_version`: current `dune-project` package version, if read at runtime

Until that split exists, dashboard/runtime trust should avoid treating `/health.build.commit` as proof that the running binary was rebuilt from that commit.
contract_addendum:
## Build identity in health and runtime diagnostics

The health response distinguishes the identity of the running executable from
information read from its current checkout.  Its `build` object includes:

- `binary_version`, the version compiled into the running executable, alongside
  the backwards-compatible `release_version`;
- `repo_version`, when the current checkout's package version can be read;
- `binary_commit`, the compiled build commit when build metadata is available;
- `repo_head_commit`, the current checkout HEAD when it can be resolved; and
- `commit`, a backwards-compatible value that is the compiled commit when
  available and otherwise the runtime repository HEAD.

Commit fields are nullable when their corresponding metadata cannot be
obtained.  When `commit` is non-null, `commit_source` is a non-empty string so
consumers can distinguish compiled metadata from a runtime checkout value
without relying on the commit text; when `commit` is null the representation
of `commit_source` is unspecified.  Repository-derived fields are checkout
observations and do not establish that the executable was rebuilt from that
checkout.

The dashboard runtime-resolution payload exposes the same distinction through
`runtime_binary_git_commit` and `runtime_repo_head_git_commit`.  The former may
be null when compiled metadata is unavailable; the latter reports the runtime
checkout HEAD when available.  Consumers must not use the latter as evidence
of binary freshness.

+  let target = Filename.concat dir "build_identity_probe.exe" in

+     let input = open_in_bin source in
+     Fun.protect
+       ~finally:(fun () -> close_in_noerr input)
+       (fun () ->
+         let output = open_out_bin target in
+         Fun.protect
+           ~finally:(fun () -> close_out_noerr output)
+           (fun () ->
+             let size = in_channel_length input in
+             output_string output (really_input_string input size)));

+  let previous = Sys.getenv_opt "MASC_BUILD_GIT_COMMIT" in

+   | None -> Unix.putenv "MASC_BUILD_GIT_COMMIT" "");

+  let binary_commit = nullable_string json "binary_commit" in
+  let repo_head_commit = nullable_string json "repo_head_commit" in
+  let commit = nullable_string json "commit" in
+  let commit_source = nullable_string json "commit_source" in
+  let repo_version = nullable_string json "repo_version" in
+  (match expect_binary_commit with
+   | Some compiled ->

+       (Some compiled) binary_commit
+   | None ->
+     Alcotest.(check (option string))
+       (label ^ ": no compiled build metadata") None binary_commit);
+  (match expect_repo_head with
+   | Some head ->
+     Alcotest.(check (option string))
+       (label ^ ": controlled checkout HEAD reported as repository head")

+       (label ^ ": repository HEAD unavailable") None repo_head_commit);

+     documented precedence a consumer sees. *)

+    (label ^ ": compatibility commit mirrors reported inputs")
+    (match binary_commit, repo_head_commit with
+     | Some compiled, _ -> Some compiled
+     | None, Some head -> Some head
+     | None, None -> None)
+    commit;
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    (label ^ ": provenance accompanies a known compatibility commit") true
+    (match commit, commit_source with
+     | Some _, Some source -> String.trim source <> ""
+     | Some _, None -> false
+     | None, _ -> true);
+  (match expect_repo_version with
+   | Some _ ->
+     Alcotest.(check (option string))

+       expect_repo_version repo_version
+   | None ->

+let run_command_in_dir ~cwd argv =
+  let previous_dir = Sys.getcwd () in
+  Fun.protect
+    ~finally:(fun () -> Sys.chdir previous_dir)
+    (fun () ->
+      Sys.chdir cwd;
+      let command = String.concat " " (List.map Filename.quote argv) in
+      let channel = Unix.open_process_in command in
+      let output = Buffer.create 4096 in
+      Fun.protect
+        ~finally:(fun () ->
+          match Unix.close_process_in channel with
+          | Unix.WEXITED 0 -> ()
+          | _ -> Alcotest.failf "probe command failed: %s" command)
+        (fun () ->
+          (try
+             while true do
+               Buffer.add_string output (input_line channel);
+               Buffer.add_char output '\n'
+             done
+           with End_of_file -> ());

problem_statement:
P1: move keeper tool-call JSONL appends off the tool hot path
## Problem

The 24-Keeper risk report identifies inline post-tool logging as a remaining stop-risk:

- `keeper_hooks_oas.ml` / `mcp_server_eio_call_tool.ml` call `Keeper_tool_call_log.log_call` on the tool completion path.
- `Keeper_tool_call_log.log_call` currently performs the full JSON construction and `Dated_jsonl.append` synchronously.
- Under a synchronized 24-Keeper tool burst, slow filesystem writes or a contended `Dated_jsonl` mutex can hold tool completion and delay turn-slot release.

This is not a correctness-only issue. It is a liveness issue: a noncritical observability sink can become part of the critical path that keeps the world reacting.

## Scope

Implement the smallest code-level P1-B slice:

- Add a bounded best-effort async queue for `Keeper_tool_call_log` durable appends.
- Keep JSON/redaction/semantic construction deterministic and covered by existing tests.
- In production server startup, start a background drain fiber and a shutdown drain hook.
- Preserve current synchronous behavior for tests/CLI paths that initialize the store without starting the drain fiber.
- Add regression coverage proving that when async mode is active, `log_call` returns before the queued record is flushed, and `flush_now`/the drain path persists it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool-call JSONL append is no longer mandatory inline I/O on the server tool completion hot path.
- Queue is bounded; overflow drops are visible through a counter/log instead of blocking.
- Existing dashboard readers continue to use `read_recent`, `read_window`, and `read_latest` unchanged.
- Focused OCaml tests cover async enqueue/flush semantics.
- Local verification includes `ocamlformat --check`, `git diff --check`, focused Dune build, and focused test executable.

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

`Keeper_tool_call_log` supports a bounded, best-effort asynchronous persistence mode for production server use. This mode preserves the existing record format, redaction, and reader behavior (`read_recent`, `read_window`, and `read_latest`).

### Public async operations

- `start_flush_fiber ~sw ~clock` enables asynchronous persistence for the initialized logger and starts a switch-bound background drain fiber. The fiber stops draining when `sw` finishes; pending accepted records still held at that point remain flushable. It also arranges for pending accepted records to be drained during application shutdown.
- `flush_now ()` synchronously drains pending asynchronous records. It is safe when the queue is empty or asynchronous mode is inactive.
- `dropped_count_for_testing ()` reports records rejected because the bounded acceptance queue was full. It is intended for unit-test observability.

### Required behavior

- Calling `init` without starting the flush fiber retains synchronous append behavior for CLI and test callers: a completed `log_call` is immediately visible to readers.
- Once asynchronous persistence has been enabled, a completed `log_call` does not require durable append I/O: the record may remain not yet visible to readers until a flush or a drain makes it durable. Record JSON construction, redaction, and semantics are unchanged.
- The asynchronous queue is bounded: it accepts at most 4096 records per drain batch (matching the established `Tool_metrics_persist` convention). When full, additional records must be rejected and the rejection reported (counter or warning log) rather than blocking callers.
- The production server background-maintenance startup path (`Server_bootstrap_loops.start_background_maintenance`) enables asynchronous persistence after logger initialization. Application shutdown drains pending accepted records before exit.

No drain interval, scheduler ordering, or shutdown-hook name/priority is part of this contract.

problem_statement:
room: Default scope masc_dir reads current_room file on every call
[HIDDEN]. 동일 요청 중 room 전환 가능. Fix: config 생성 시 resolve.

### Additional contract requirements

**Room scope resolution:**

- Room scope is resolved when a room configuration value is created, not on every directory access. After creation, all room paths derived from a configuration are stable: later changes to the current room do not move an existing configuration to a different room.
- A configuration whose scope is the default scope always uses the default (root) room directory (`.masc/`), regardless of which room is recorded as the current room, and regardless of any room switches performed during the same request or process lifetime. In particular, a default-scope configuration created before entering another room continues to observe the default room's state after the room switch.
- Callers that need a configuration bound to the room recorded as current must resolve the scope explicitly. The public `Room.config_with_resolved_scope` helper is the supported way to do this: it snapshots the current room at the moment it is called and returns a configuration bound to that room. In a fresh workspace with no recorded current room, the snapshot resolves to the default (root) room.
- A configuration returned by `Room.config_with_resolved_scope` keeps observing the room it resolved to. If the current room changes afterwards (for example by entering a different room), the resolved configuration still reads and writes the room captured at resolution time.

problem_statement:
Centralize Memory OS recall and retention constants in policy SSOT
Symptom
- Memory OS audit/review found recall and retention constants split across implementation modules (`keeper_memory_os_io.ml`, `keeper_memory_os_recall.ml`) while docs describe them as product policy.
- Examples include max rendered facts/episodes/shared facts, episode tail scan, and fact/event/episode store caps.

Repro
- Inspect `lib/keeper/keeper_memory_os_io.ml` for `fact_recall_window`, `fact_store_max`, `event_recall_window`, `event_store_max`, `episode_file_window`, `episode_file_store_max`.
- Inspect `lib/keeper/keeper_memory_os_recall.ml` for `default_max_facts`, `default_max_episodes`, `default_max_shared_facts`, `episode_tail_scan`.
- See PR #22288 review discussion.

Likely cause
- Constants were introduced near their consumers, then became cross-cutting retention/recall policy.

Tried
- Left out of PR #22288 follow-up patch to avoid broad API churn while addressing correctness review items.

Acceptance
- Move or expose these policy values through a single Memory OS policy/config SSOT.
- Update audit/docs/tests to reference the SSOT names rather than restating raw magic numbers where possible.

### Additional contract requirements

The supported Memory OS policy API is `Masc.Keeper_memory_os_policy`. It owns
these recall and retention values: `fact_recall_window`, `fact_store_max`,
`event_recall_window`, `event_store_max`, `episode_file_window`,
`episode_file_store_max`, `recall_default_max_facts`,
`recall_default_max_episodes`, `recall_default_max_shared_facts`, and
`recall_episode_tail_scan`.

The existing public compatibility values in `Masc.Keeper_memory_os_io`
(`fact_recall_window`, `fact_store_max`, `event_recall_window`,
`event_store_max`, `episode_file_window`, and `episode_file_store_max`) and
in `Masc.Keeper_memory_os_recall` (the default fact, shared-fact, and episode
limits) remain available. They obtain their effective settings directly from
the policy API rather than declaring numbers or deriving local policy values.
Recall's episode-tail behavior likewise obtains its setting from that policy
API. The public I/O and recall interface documentation identifies the policy
API as the owner; its prose, heading structure, and declaration order are
otherwise unconstrained.

The existing retention, recall, dashboard behavior, hysteresis behavior, and
public dashboard selection-policy JSON schema remain unchanged.

[Audit] String action dispatch를 variant type으로 전환 (Impact 5/5)
## 코드 품질 감사 결과 — 의미 점수 5 (버그 직결)

### 문제
`room_task.ml:389`와 `tool_task.ml:378`에서 task action을 string으로 받아 `String.lowercase_ascii` 후 match한다.

```ocaml
let action = String.lowercase_ascii action in
match action, task.task_status with
| "claim", Types.Todo -> ...
| "start", Types.Claimed { assignee; _ } -> ...
| "done", Types.Claimed | "done", Types.InProgress -> ...
| _ -> Error (...)  (* catch-all이 누락 case를 삼킴 *)
```

### 위험

problem_statement:
keeper: define structured deliberation schema and remove free-form JSON recovery
## Desired outcome
Keeper deliberation requests a schema-forced structured result instead of recovering JSON from free-form model text.

## Problem statement
Parent issue #4738 defines the broader boundary change, but the first independent step is to remove brace/fence recovery from the model boundary itself.

Right now keeper deliberation still:
- builds a prompt
- accepts arbitrary text back
- tries to recover a JSON object from that text

That leaves the most fragile part of the control path outside the typed contract.

## Proposed approach
- Define a keeper deliberation schema using OAS `Structured`.
- Request only schema-conforming output from the model.
- Replace free-form JSON extraction in keeper deliberation with structured parsing.
- Keep the existing typed action ADT as the parsed target.
- Add focused tests for malformed/non-conforming model output.

## Non-goals
- Reworking keeper action execution in this issue
- Adding new keeper action types
- Changing triage heuristics

## Links
- Parent: #4738
- Parent/design context: #4308

### Additional contract requirements

Keeper deliberation must obtain the model's decision as a schema-forced structured result defined with the OAS `Structured` interface (the `Agent_sdk.Structured.schema` record), instead of recovering JSON from free-form model text.

Observable requirements:

- The `Keeper_deliberation` module exposes a value named `structured_result_schema` of type `structured_result Agent_sdk.Structured.schema`, where `structured_result` is a record type with fields `action` (the existing `deliberation_action` ADT), `reasoning` (a string), and `confidence` (a float).
- The schema's `name` field is exactly `keeper_deliberation_decision`, and its `params` include a required parameter named `action`.
- The schema's `parse` function accepts a JSON decision bundle such as `{"action":"noop","params":{"reason":"quiet"},"reasoning":"nothing","confidence":0.9}` and returns the typed structured result, keeping the existing action ADT as the parsed target. It clamps a provided `confidence` to the range 0.0 through 1.0 (so a value above 1.0 becomes 1.0 and a value below 0.0 becomes 0.0) and defaults an omitted `confidence` to 0.5.
- The text produced by `build_deliberation_prompt` requests the model return only the schema-conforming tool input object and contains the exact sentence fragment ``tool input object for schema `keeper_deliberation_decision` ``. It no longer contains the obsolete instruction `Respond with ONLY a JSON object` that asked for a free-form JSON object.
- `parse_deliberation_response` accepts only a complete, strict JSON decision object. It must reject, without any fence/brace recovery: fenced JSON (e.g. wrapped in triple-backtick `json` fences), JSON embedded in surrounding free-form prose, malformed JSON, and empty input, as well as decision bundles with a missing or unknown `action`.

problem_statement:
Track keeper playground-scoped read boundary isolation
## Summary
Keeper read access should default to each keeper's playground roots rather than the whole `MASC_BASE_PATH`, while still allowing explicit custom paths when intentionally configured.

## Problem
`MASC_BASE_PATH` can be broad for coordination (`~/me`), but keeper read tools and shell cwd defaults should not inherit that breadth. Without additional isolation, keepers can directly read sibling repos inside the shared base path.

## Desired behavior
- default keeper read root is `.masc/playground/<keeper>/`
- default shell cwd for keeper read/write commands is the keeper playground
- explicit custom paths remain possible when configured intentionally
- sibling repos are not readable by default just because they are under `MASC_BASE_PATH`

## Evidence
- reproduced by reading `workspace/yousleepwhen/oas/lib/approval.ml` from a keeper attached to a broad base path
- fixed by constraining read resolution and default cwd to keeper effective allow roots
- validated with `test_keeper_tool_exposure` and `test_keeper_pr_workflow`

### Additional contract requirements

Keeper tools are observably scoped to the keeper playground by default:

- A `keeper_shell_readonly` `pwd` operation with no explicit arguments runs in the keeper's playground directory and reports that directory as the working directory.
- A `keeper_bash` command with no explicit `cwd` runs in the keeper's playground directory.
- A `keeper_fs_read` for a path outside the keeper's configured allowed roots (for example a file in a sibling repository inside a shared base path) fails rather than returning the file contents.
- This denial cannot be bypassed with relative path traversal outside the playground, by relying on bare repository-relative paths being located under sibling directories, or through a symlink placed inside the keeper playground that points outside the allowed roots; the same denial applies to file reads through `keeper_shell_readonly`.
- A keeper whose configuration explicitly allows a custom path can still read that path successfully.
- `keeper_bash` (and `keeper_shell_readonly` `bash`) commands referencing absolute paths outside the allowed roots fail, including when the paths are quoted.

+let strip_wrapping_quotes token =
+  let len = String.length token in
+  if len >= 2 then
+    let first = token.[0] and last = token.[len - 1] in
+    if (first = '"' && last = '"') || (first = '\'' && last = '\'')
+    then String.sub token 1 (len - 2)
+    else token
+  else token
+
+let looks_like_url token =
+  let token = strip_wrapping_quotes token in
+  match String.index_opt token ':' with
+  | Some idx when idx + 2 < String.length token ->
+    token.[idx + 1] = '/' && token.[idx + 2] = '/'
+  | _ -> false
+
+let is_path_flag token =
+  match strip_wrapping_quotes token with
+  | "-C" | "--git-dir" | "--work-tree" | "--exec-path" -> true
+  | _ -> false
+
+let path_value_of_flagged_token token =
+  let token = strip_wrapping_quotes token in
+  let prefixes =
+    [ "--git-dir="; "--work-tree="; "--exec-path=" ]
+  in
+  List.find_map
+    (fun prefix ->
+       if String.starts_with ~prefix token then
+         Some
+           (String.sub token (String.length prefix)
+              (String.length token - String.length prefix))
+       else None)
+    prefixes
+
+let looks_like_path_token token =
+  let token = strip_wrapping_quotes token in
+  token <> ""
+  && not (looks_like_url token)
+  &&
+  (token = "." || token = ".."
+   || String.starts_with ~prefix:"/" token
+   || String.starts_with ~prefix:"./" token
+   || String.starts_with ~prefix:"../" token
+   || String.starts_with ~prefix:"~/" token
+   || String.contains token '/')
+
+let has_path_rewrite_syntax cmd =
+  String.exists
+    (function
+      | '\'' | '"' | '\\' | '*' | '?' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' -> true
+      | _ -> false)
+    cmd
+
+let validate_command_paths ?workdir cmd =
+  match workdir with
+  | None -> Ok ()
+  | Some _ ->
+    if String.contains cmd '/' && has_path_rewrite_syntax cmd then
+      Error
+        "Path syntax blocked: shell quoting, globbing, brace expansion, and backslash escapes are not allowed for path-bearing keeper commands. Use plain unquoted paths and explicit cwd."
+    else
+    let rec loop expect_path_value = function
+      | [] -> Ok ()
+      | token :: rest ->
+        let token = strip_wrapping_quotes token in
+        if token = "" then loop expect_path_value rest
+        else if expect_path_value then
+          if validate_path ?workdir token then loop false rest
+          else
+            Error
+              (Printf.sprintf
+                 "Path blocked: %s (outside allowed directories for this keeper command)"
+                 token)
+        else
+          match path_value_of_flagged_token token with

+            if validate_path ?workdir value then loop false rest
+            else
+              Error
+                (Printf.sprintf
+                   "Path blocked: %s (outside allowed directories for this keeper command)"
+                   value)
+          | None when is_path_flag token -> loop true rest
+          | None when looks_like_path_token token ->
+            if validate_path ?workdir token then loop false rest
+            else
+              Error
+                (Printf.sprintf
+                   "Path blocked: %s (outside allowed directories for this keeper command)"
+                   token)
+          | None -> loop false rest

problem_statement:
feat(keeper): consecutive noop backoff to prevent board_list token waste
## Problem
- Keeper calls `keeper_board_list` on proactive turns, reads posts, takes no action
- noop_turn_count is cumulative only — no consecutive tracking
- effective_scheduled_autonomous_cooldown ignores noop history
- Prompt encourages "board_list to observe" pattern causing token waste

[HIDDEN]

[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

# Consecutive no-op backoff for scheduled autonomous turns

Keeper metadata tracks an integer `consecutive_noop_count` for scheduled
autonomous turns. New metadata starts at zero, and metadata saved before this
field existed must load it as zero. The current value is included in keeper
metadata serialization under the key `consecutive_noop_count` and survives a
save/load round trip.

A scheduled autonomous turn is a no-op when it produces no visible text and
uses no tools, or uses only these observation-only tools:

- `keeper_stay_silent`
- `keeper_board_list`
- `keeper_context_status`
- `keeper_tool_search`

Each such turn increments the count. A scheduled autonomous turn that produces
visible text or uses any other tool resets the count to zero. A reactive turn,
including one triggered by a mention, board event, or scope message, neither
increments nor resets this scheduled-turn count.

The effective scheduled autonomous cooldown is the configured base cooldown
multiplied by `2^min(n, 3)`, where `n` is the current consecutive no-op count.
Thus the multipliers for counts zero, one, two, and three-or-more are 1, 2, 4,
and 8. A non-positive count has the same cooldown effect as zero.

Existing idle decay applies after that multiplication. At or before the
backed-off cooldown boundary there is no decay. For each additional complete
backed-off-cooldown interval that has elapsed, the cooldown is halved, subject
to the existing decay cap and configured minimum-cooldown floor. Scheduled
turn decisions use this result consistently for eligibility, their reported
effective cooldown, and any reported remaining cooldown time. Consequently,
sequential no-op outcomes can keep a later scheduled turn pending beyond the
unmultiplied base cooldown, while a productive outcome resets the count and
returns later decisions to the base-cooldown behavior.

For callers that evaluate the rule directly,
`effective_scheduled_autonomous_cooldown` takes labeled `base_cooldown` and
`since_last` integer arguments, an optional labeled integer
`consecutive_noop_count` argument defaulting to zero, and a final `unit`
argument. The calculation is pure and does not mutate keeper state.

problem_statement:
chore(server): health probe paths duplicated in 5 files with no SSOT module
## Context

Found during \`/loop\` SSOT sweep tick 4 (2026-04-18). Follow-up in the same series as #8355, #8387.

\`/health/live\` and \`/health/ready\` are registered as routes, whitelisted for auth, used as liveness probe defaults, and referenced by startup takeover. The strings appear 10 times across 5 files with no central constant.

## Evidence

\`\`\`
lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml:93  Router.get \"/health/live\" liveness_handler     # HTTP/1 register
lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml:94  Router.get \"/health/ready\" readiness_handler   # HTTP/1 register
lib/server/server_h2_gateway.ml:180                 | \`GET, \"/health/live\" ->                    # HTTP/2 match arm
lib/server/server_h2_gateway.ml:190                 | \`GET, \"/health/ready\" ->                   # HTTP/2 match arm
lib/server/server_auth.ml:388                       || String.equal path \"/health/live\"           # public read whitelist
lib/server/server_auth.ml:389                       || String.equal path \"/health/ready\"
bin/main_eio.ml:131                                 || String.equal path \"/health/live\"           # startup path filter
bin/main_eio.ml:132                                 || String.equal path \"/health/ready\"
lib/server/server_startup_takeover.ml:107           ?(path = \"/health/live\") port               # liveness probe default
lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml:93,94  # already counted above (same file)
\`\`\`

Also `/health` alone (bare) appears at `bin/main_eio.ml:130`, `lib/provider_adapter.ml:504-509`, `lib/http_server_eio.ml:547`, `lib/dashboard/dashboard_surface_readiness.ml:*`.

## Failure modes

1. **HTTP/1 vs HTTP/2 divergence** — adding a third health path (e.g. `/health/startup`) to the HTTP/1 router leaves it 404 on HTTP/2 unless someone remembers to edit `server_h2_gateway.ml` too. No compile-time link between the two routers.
2. **Auth whitelist rot** — renaming `/health/ready` → `/healthz/ready` without touching `server_auth.ml:389` silently makes the probe require an admin token → LB marks pod unhealthy on deploy.
3. **Takeover probe uses `/health/live` literal** — if the liveness route ever moves, `server_startup_takeover.ml:107` still probes the old path and falsely declares \"no prior process\" on takeover.

The coupling is purely by string equality. There is no compile-time guarantee that router-register / auth-whitelist / probe-default stay aligned.

## Proposal

Add `lib/server/server_route_paths.ml(i)`:

[HIDDEN]

[HIDDEN]

No behaviour change; just names the coupling.

## Anti-goals

- Do **not** collapse HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 dispatch into one router — the two protocols have different pattern-match and dispatch mechanisms for good reason. Only the string constants are shared.
- Do **not** move `/api/v1/gate/*` routes into the same module — those belong to their own subsystem (gate). Health is a separate concern.

## Scope

~40 LOC new module + ~10 LOC of edits. Small enough for a single PR.

## Related

- masc-mcp#8355 — `.masc/` path SSOT
- masc-mcp#8387 — `\"127.0.0.1\"` literal SSOT
- masc-mcp#8352 — env var literal SSOT

### Additional contract requirements

## Health probe path single source of truth

To satisfy this issue, all of the following must hold:

- A single dedicated shared source module — inside the server library or
  shared between the server library and the binary — is the single source of
  truth for both health probe wire paths. The wire formats must stay exactly
  `/health/live` (liveness) and `/health/ready` (readiness), so external
  monitors and load balancers keep working.
- The literals `/health/live` and `/health/ready` appear in that one module
  only: they are defined there as named constants and must not be hard-coded
  anywhere else.
- Each of the following coupled consumers must derive the probe paths from
  that shared module instead of hard-coding them:
  - the HTTP/1 route registration for the liveness and readiness handlers;
  - the HTTP/2 gateway dispatch for the liveness and readiness match arms;
  - the unauthenticated public-read whitelist, which must accept both probe
    paths (as it does today);
  - the binary's request filter, which must keep both probe paths exempt
    from global rate limiting (as they are today);
  - the startup-takeover liveness probe, whose default request path must
    remain `/health/live`.
- The choice of module name, value names, and any helper APIs (constant
  values, membership predicates, or path lists exporting the constants by
  reference) is left to the implementation.
- There is no behaviour change: both probes keep returning their current
  responses and keep being reachable without authentication.
- Anti-goals from the issue still apply: do not collapse the HTTP/1 and
  HTTP/2 dispatch into one router, and do not move the `/api/v1/gate/*`
  routes into the shared module.

+          else

+            | '"' -> i + 1

+           irrelevant for the comment analysis that follows. *)

+                    && text.[i + 1 + idl] = '}'

+          in

+            | '{' ->

+                   && ((text.[j] >= 'a' && text.[j] <= 'z')

+                       || text.[j] = '_')

+                else j
+              in

+                 && id_end + 1 < n && not (char_is_ident text.[id_end + 1])

+        let open_col = ref 0 in

+          let i = ref 0 in

+                     not (col_in_ranges (ranges_of_line comments i) col))
+                   (string_occurrences line ("\"" ^ lit ^ "\"")))

+      in
+      let rec collect_ml_files dir prefix acc =

+           paths, so a shared module in any nested library location
+           is discovered just as a top-level one. *)

+      in

+        (* A source expression is often wrapped across lines (a guarded
+           match arm whose [when ... ->] guard continues on the next
+           source line, or a pipeline argument continued under its
+           operator); joining those continuations keeps the wrapped
+           layout equivalent to the one-line form. Each entry of the
+           returned list is one line of [lines] whose continuation
+           lines (the following lines, up to the first one ending the

+              | Some name ->
