+        expand []
+      in
+      let shared_value_mentions line module_name value_names =
+        (* Distinct values of the shared module actually projected in
+           [line]: as a qualified reference ([M.name] or
+           [Masc_mcp.M.name]). *)
+        let via_projection =
+          List.filter (fun vn ->
+            List.exists
+              (fun occ ->
+                let dot = occ - 1 in
+                if dot <= 0 then false
+                else
+                  (* walk back over the module path and see whether
+                     the shared module name appears in it *)
+                  let rec mod_start i =
+                    if i >= 0
+                       && (char_is_ident line.[i] || line.[i] = '.')
+                    then mod_start (i - 1)
+                    else i
+                  in
+                  let ms = mod_start (dot - 1) in
+                  let prefix =
+                    String.sub line (ms + 1) (dot - ms - 1)
+                  in
+                  List.exists (fun seg ->
+                    seg = module_name)
+                    (String.split_on_char '.' prefix))
+              (string_occurrences line vn))
+            value_names
+        in
+        List.sort_uniq String.compare via_projection
+      in
+      let expression_derives line module_name value_names aliases =
+        (* The line draws the probe path from the shared module by
+           projecting one of its values (constant, path list, or
+           membership helper), by mentioning the shared module at all
+           (e.g. [Mod.public] where [public] is any exported list of
+           the constants), or by using a same-file alias resolved to
+           such a reference. A bare shared value name also counts when
+           the consumer opened the shared module — and an [open Mod]
+           line anywhere in the consumer's scope makes that
+           arrangement recognized. *)
+        shared_value_mentions line module_name value_names <> []
+        || references_module line module_name
+        || (aliases <> [] && List.exists (contains_unqualified line) aliases)
+      in
+      let consumer_lines_of file =
+        (* Non-empty source lines of the consumer file, with comment
+           ranges removed and string-literal bodies blanked. *)
+        List.filter
+          (fun l -> String.trim l <> "")
+          (file_lines_clean ~strip_comments:true file)
+      in
+      let definition_blocks defining_lines =
+        (* Groups of lines, one per top-level definition. *)
+        let rec collect acc current = function
+          | [] ->
+            (match current with [] -> List.rev acc | _ -> List.rev (List.rev current :: acc))
+          | l :: rest ->
+            if is_let_definition l then
+              (match current with
+               | [] -> collect acc [ l ] rest
+               | _ -> collect (List.rev current :: acc) [ l ] rest)
+            else
+              (match current with
+               | [] -> collect acc [] rest
+               | _ -> collect acc (l :: current) rest)
+        in
+        collect [] [] defining_lines
+      in
+      let coverage_closure value_names module_name defining_lines initial =
+        (* Transitive closure over shared-module value definitions:
+           if the consumer relies on a helper whose definition names
+           other shared values, those count too (e.g. a predicate
+           defined over a list of both constants). *)
+        let blocks = definition_blocks defining_lines in
+        (* Inside the defining module itself, a value may refer to its
+           peers either unqualified or by self-qualified projection,
+           so accept both forms here. *)
+        let local_mentions text =
+          List.sort_uniq String.compare
+            (List.filter (fun vn -> contains_unqualified text vn)
+               value_names)
+        in
+        let step used =
+          List.sort_uniq String.compare
+            (used
+             @ List.concat_map
+                 (fun v ->
+                   List.concat_map (fun blk ->
+                     if contains_sub blk ("let " ^ v ^ " =")
+                        || contains_sub blk ("let " ^ v ^ " :")
+                        || contains_sub blk ("let rec " ^ v ^ " ")
+                     then
+                       List.sort_uniq String.compare
+                         (shared_value_mentions blk module_name value_names
+                          @ local_mentions blk)
+                     else [])
+                     (List.map (String.concat " ") blocks))
+                 used)
+        in
+        let rec fix s =
+          let s' = step s in
+          if List.length s' = List.length s then s else fix s'
+        in
+        fix initial
+      in
+      let check_coverage ~file ~lines ~module_name ~value_names ~aliases
+          ~defining_lines ~what =
+        (* At least one relevant line must draw from the shared
+           module; the shared values used across those lines (closed
+           under helper definitions) must mention at least two
+           distinct shared values, so both probe paths are covered —
+           per-path constants, a path list of both, a predicate over
+           both, or any equivalent helper arrangement the addendum
+           permits. *)
+        let relevant =
+          List.filter
+            (fun l -> expression_derives l module_name value_names aliases)
+            lines
+        in
+        if relevant = [] then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "%s: the %s must draw the probe paths from the shared module %s"
+            file what module_name;
+        let used =
+          List.sort_uniq String.compare
+            (List.concat_map
+               (fun l ->
+                 shared_value_mentions l module_name value_names
+                 @ (value_names
+                    |> List.filter (fun vn ->
+                         List.mem vn aliases
+                         && contains_unqualified l vn)))
+               relevant)
+        in
+        let covered =
+          coverage_closure value_names module_name defining_lines used
+        in
+        (* A single used value also covers both paths when the module
+           defines both probe literals as constants and that value is
+           not one of the two literal-bearing constants — then it can
+           only be a list or predicate built over them. *)
+        let literal_consts =
+          List.filter
+            (fun v ->
+              List.exists
+                (fun dl ->
+                  contains_sub dl ("let " ^ v ^ " =")
+                  && contains_sub dl "\"")
+                defining_lines)
+            value_names
+        in
+        let helper_covers =
+          used <> []
+          && List.exists (fun v -> not (List.mem v literal_consts)) used
+        in
+        if List.length covered < 2 && not helper_covers then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "%s: the %s must cover both probe paths via the shared module %s \
+             (per-path constants or a shared list/predicate/helper defined \
+             over both)"
+            file what module_name
+      in
+      let defining_values () =
+        let defining = defining_file () in
+        (defining, module_name_of defining, names_defined_in defining,
+         file_lines_clean ~strip_comments:true defining)
+      in
+      let consumer_scope_with_aliases file =
+        (* The complete cleaned lines of [file] plus the aliases
+           resolvable from that same scope and the shared module's own
+           defined names (so bare references after [open Mod] count). *)
+        let (defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines) =
+          defining_values ()
+        in
+        let lines = consumer_lines_of file in
+        let aliases0 = resolve_aliases lines module_name in
+        (* Lines of the consumer that open the shared module make its
+           value names usable unqualified. *)
+        let opened =
+          List.exists
+            (fun l ->
+              let t = String.trim l in
+              t = "open " ^ module_name
+              || t = "open Masc_mcp." ^ module_name
+              || (String.length t >= 9 && String.sub t 0 9 = "let open "
+                  && contains_sub t (module_name ^ " in")))
+            lines
+        in
+        let aliases =
+          if opened
+          then List.sort_uniq String.compare (aliases0 @ value_names)
+          else aliases0
+        in
+        (defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines, lines,
+         aliases)
+      in
+      let is_public = Masc_mcp.Server_auth.is_public_read_path in
+      let public_probe_paths =
+        (* The probe paths as exposed by the unauthenticated
+           public-read whitelist predicate over well-known candidate
+           wire paths (interning the plausible routes in both the
+           issue's evidence list and the surrounding health
+           namespace); per the addendum this set must be exactly the
+           two probes, which pins the shared constants' wire format
+           and verifies the whitelist's derivation without naming
+           the constants. *)
+        let candidates =
+          [ "/health"; "/health/live"; "/health/ready"; "/healthz";
+            "/livez"; "/readyz"; "/live"; "/ready"; "/ping";
+            "/health/alive"; "/health/liveness"; "/health/readiness";
+            "/probe"; "/probes"; "/status"; "/health/start";
+            "/health/startup" ]
+        in
+        List.filter (fun p -> p <> "/health" && is_public p) candidates
+      in
+      let list_summarizes paths =
+        (* Compact description of a probe-path set for failure
+           messages and comparison. *)
+        "[" ^ String.concat "; " (List.map (Printf.sprintf "%S") paths)
+        ^ "]"
+      in
+      let auth_whitelist_block () =
+        (* The whitelist predicate's own body: from its definition
+           header until the next top-level definition. *)
+        let cls = consumer_lines_of "lib/server/server_auth.ml" in
+        let rec collect acc in_body = function
+          | [] -> List.rev acc
+          | l :: rest ->
+            if contains_sub l "is_public_read_path" then
+              collect (l :: acc) true rest
+            else if in_body && is_let_definition l then List.rev acc
+            else if in_body then collect (l :: acc) in_body rest
+            else collect acc in_body rest
+        in
+        collect [] false cls
+      in
+      let health_mentioning_lines lines module_name =
+        (* Lines of the rate-limit filter region that can mention a
+           probe path: by the remaining quoted literal ([/health]),
+           by a health/probe-suggestive identifier, or by referencing
+           the shared module (directly or through a same-file alias).
+           In this file any such line belongs to the probe
+           rate-limit-exemption plumbing, so the collection is the
+           exemption expression's own text rather than a picked
+           subset. *)
+        List.filter
+          (fun l ->
+            contains_sub l "/health"
+            || contains_sub l "health" || contains_sub l "probe"
+            || contains_sub l "liveness" || contains_sub l "readiness"
+            || references_module l module_name
+            || contains_sub l "skip_rate_limit")
+          lines
+      in
+      [
+      Alcotest.test_case "both probes reachable without auth via the shared paths"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        (* Semantic: the unauthenticated reachability decision the
+           server itself applies. Whatever names the shared module
+           uses, the whitelist it feeds must accept exactly the two
+           probe wire paths among plausible candidates — so the shared
+           constants are pinned to the wire format and the whitelist
+           keeps both probes reachable without authentication. *)
+        if public_probe_paths <> [ "/health/live"; "/health/ready" ]
+        then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "the unauthenticated public probe path set must be exactly              the two probe wire paths [/health/live; /health/ready]              (the shared constants pinned to their wire format); got:              %s"
+            (list_summarizes public_probe_paths);
+        ());
+      Alcotest.test_case "constants pinned to wire format in one shared module"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        let defining = defining_file () in
+        let (raw, _s, comments) = stripped_source defining in
+        let content =
+          String.concat " "
+            (List.mapi (fun i line ->
+               let ranges = ranges_of_line comments i in
+               let buf = Buffer.create (String.length line) in
+               String.iteri (fun col c ->
+                 if not (col_in_ranges ranges col) then Buffer.add_char buf c)
+                 line;
+               Buffer.contents buf)
+               raw)
+        in
+        if not (contains_sub content "\"/health/live\"") then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "%s must pin the exact literal wire path \"/health/live\""
+            defining;
+        if not (contains_sub content "\"/health/ready\"") then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "%s must pin the exact literal wire path \"/health/ready\""
+            defining);
+      Alcotest.test_case "shared module is a dedicated non-consumer file"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        let defining = defining_file () in
+        if List.mem defining consumer_files then
+          Alcotest.failf
+            "probe path literals live in consumer %s; they must move to \
+             a dedicated shared module"
+            defining);
+      Alcotest.test_case "auth whitelist derives both probes from the shared module"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        (* Structural: the whitelist predicate's own body must draw
+           the probe paths from the shared module (so it cannot drift
+           from the shared constants) — direct projection, a shared
+           list/predicate helper, or a same-file alias. The behavioral
+           guarantee itself is asserted semantically in the first
+           test. *)
+        let (_defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines, _cls,
+             aliases) =
+          consumer_scope_with_aliases "lib/server/server_auth.ml"
+        in
+        let lines = auth_whitelist_block () in
+        check_coverage ~file:"lib/server/server_auth.ml" ~lines
+          ~module_name ~value_names ~aliases ~defining_lines
+          ~what:"public-read whitelist that keeps the probes reachable \
+                 without authentication");
+      Alcotest.test_case "binary rate-limit exemptions match the whitelist"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        (* Semantic-by-comparison: every probe path the server serves
+           without authentication (the whitelist's probe set) must
+           also be exempt from the binary's global rate limit. The
+           exemption is anchored by requiring the rate-limit filter's
+           probe-bearing lines to draw from the same shared module the
+           whitelist derives from — so an exemption hard-coded to
+           stale probe paths (the drift failure mode) cannot pass. *)
+        let (_defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines, lines,
+             aliases) =
+          consumer_scope_with_aliases "bin/main_eio.ml"
+        in
+        let filter_lines = health_mentioning_lines lines module_name in
+        check_coverage ~file:"bin/main_eio.ml" ~lines:filter_lines
+          ~module_name ~value_names ~aliases ~defining_lines
+          ~what:"rate-limit exemption for the probes");
+      Alcotest.test_case "HTTP/1 routes register the shared paths"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        (* Rebuild each [Router.get] route pipeline as one unit: the
+           registration line plus any arguments continued on the
+           following source lines, so a wrapped pipeline counts
+           exactly as the equivalent one-line form would. *)
+        let (_defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines, lines,
+             aliases) =
+          consumer_scope_with_aliases
+            "lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml"
+        in
+        let route_units =
+          expression_units
+            (fun l -> contains_sub l "Router.get")
+            lines
+        in
+        let route_lines =
+          List.filter (fun l -> contains_sub l "Router.get") route_units
+        in
+        check_coverage
+          ~file:"lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml"
+          ~lines:route_lines ~module_name ~value_names ~aliases
+          ~defining_lines ~what:"route registrations for both probes");
+      Alcotest.test_case "HTTP/2 dispatch matches the shared paths"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        let (_defining, module_name, value_names, defining_lines, lines,
+             aliases) =
+          consumer_scope_with_aliases "lib/server/server_h2_gateway.ml"
+        in
+        (* Rebuild each guarded match arm as one unit: the [`GET
+           pattern line plus its [when ... ->] guard/handler
+           continuation lines. A long arm wrapped across source lines
+           (the guard carrying the shared-module reference on its own
+           continuation line) must count exactly as the equivalent
+           one-line guarded arm would. *)
+        let starts_match_arm l =
+          let t = String.trim l in
+          t <> "" && t.[0] = '|'
+        in
+        let dispatch_arms =
+          expression_units ~next_starts_unit:starts_match_arm
+            (fun l -> contains_sub l "`GET")
+            lines
+        in
+        let dispatch_units =
+          List.filter (fun l -> contains_sub l "`GET") dispatch_arms
+        in
+        check_coverage ~file:"lib/server/server_h2_gateway.ml"
+          ~lines:dispatch_units ~module_name ~value_names ~aliases
+          ~defining_lines ~what:"dispatch arms for both probes");
+      Alcotest.test_case "startup takeover keeps the shared liveness path as default"
+        `Quick (fun () ->
+        let (_defining, module_name, value_names, _defining_lines, lines,
+             aliases) =
+          consumer_scope_with_aliases "lib/server/server_startup_takeover.ml"
+        in
+        (* The probe function's relevant lines: its definition and
+           any optional-path parameter/default within it, up to the
+           next top-level definition. *)
+        let block =
+          let rec collect acc in_probe = function
+            | [] -> List.rev acc
+            | l :: rest ->
+              if is_let_definition l && contains_sub l "probe_liveness"
+              then collect (l :: acc) true rest
+              else if in_probe && is_let_definition l then (
+                (* next top-level definition: stop, unless this very
+                   line still carries a probe path default *)
+                if contains_sub l "path = " || contains_sub l "path="
+                then collect (l :: acc) false rest
+                else List.rev acc)
+              else if in_probe then collect (l :: acc) true rest
+              else collect acc in_probe rest
+          in
+          collect [] false lines
+        in
+        let whole = if block = [] then lines else block @ lines in
+        (match
+           List.find_opt
+             (fun l ->
+               (contains_sub l "?path =" || contains_sub l "?(path ="
+                || contains_sub l "~path" || contains_sub l "path = "))
+             whole
+         with
+         | None ->
+           Alcotest.failf
+             "probe_liveness in lib/server/server_startup_takeover.ml \
+              must keep a default request path expression"
+         | Some line ->
+           if not (expression_derives line module_name value_names aliases)
+           then
+             Alcotest.failf
+               "the startup-takeover default request path must be the \
+                liveness probe path drawn from the shared module %s, \
+                got: %s"
+               module_name (String.trim line)));
+      ]);
     "verdict_ssot", [
       (* Issue #8436: payload-bearing variants need a witness function
          (not List.map verdict_to_string list, which would emit "WARN: "

problem_statement:
chore(autoresearch): rename legacy `swarm_link` -> `execution_link` after swarm removal
## Observation

After removing `agent_sdk.swarm` (#8562) and `lib/swarm/*` (#8565), the only remaining \`swarm\` reference in active masc-mcp code is a data type in autoresearch:

\`\`\`
lib/autoresearch/autoresearch_types.ml:55:type swarm_link = {
  loop_id : string;
  session_id : string;
  operation_id : string option;
  task_id : string option;
  target_file : string;
  program_note : string option;
  created_by : string option;
  linked_at : float;
}
\`\`\`

The type links an autoresearch loop to an execution session — the fields are generic coordination concepts (session_id, task_id, etc.). The \`swarm_\` prefix is a naming legacy from when actual swarm coordination existed.

## Evidence

\`\`\`
$ git grep -nE 'swarm_link|save_swarm_link|load_swarm_link|swarm.json'
lib/autoresearch/autoresearch_types.ml:55
lib/autoresearch/autoresearch_serde.ml:3,322,335,336
lib/autoresearch/autoresearch_storage.ml:4,21,57,92,94,95
lib/autoresearch.ml:69,70,85,86,87,88,89,346,348
lib/tool_autoresearch.ml
lib/dashboard/dashboard_http_autoresearch.ml
...
\`\`\`

~15 files reference \`swarm_link\`. Also \`results/<loop_id>/swarm.json\` on disk — a rename would need either a migration or a two-key read window.

## Plan

[HIDDEN]

## Risk

Medium. Touches ~15 files plus on-disk persistence naming. Suggest a dedicated PR with a migration note.

## Out of scope

This issue is only about naming. Functionality stays identical.

problem_statement:
Keeper should stay always-on and auto-recover
## Problem
Resident keepers can remain registered in metadata while the live agent/runtime is actually offline. Dashboard surfaces then show an offline keeper, and operators need manual recovery.

## Why this matters
- persistent keepers like `sangsu` look like they should be alive, but can silently disappear at runtime
- dashboard/read-model truthfulness is improved by PR #858, but runtime continuity still needs a real fix
- repeated manual recovery makes the system feel unreliable

## Expected outcome
- resident keeper runtime should auto-resume or auto-recover after restart/crash
- desired resident keepers should converge toward a live runtime, not just stored metadata
- dashboard should distinguish `desired but offline`, `recovering`, and `healthy` states clearly

## Suggested scope
- keeper bootstrap / auto-resume / recover path
- desired-vs-live reconciliation for resident keepers
- operator-visible runtime state transitions and proof

## Related
- PR #858 fixes dashboard/read-model fallback for tool audit fields
- this issue tracks the separate runtime continuity work

### Additional contract requirements

Resident keeper runtime continuity.

Desired always-on (resident) keepers must converge toward a live runtime, not merely remain registered in stored metadata.

Bootstrap and reconciliation behavior:

- Whenever keeper bootstrap or any subsequent reconciliation pass runs, a desired resident keeper whose live runtime is not running must be (re)started automatically. A keeper whose most recent recorded activity is old or missing (quiet or stale activity) is still subject to this recovery: quietness or staleness alone never prevents recovery.
- After a restart or crash, a subsequent reconciliation pass must converge a desired resident keeper back to a running live runtime, so keeper status reads report its runtime as running again.

Operator-visible continuity state:

- Keeper status, snapshot, and dashboard reads expose a `diagnostic` object that contains a `continuity_state` string. Its supported values are:
  - `"desired_offline"`: the keeper is a desired always-on keeper and its live runtime is not currently running.
  - `"recovering"`: the keeper's live runtime has been (re)started by a bootstrap or reconciliation pass and is converging back toward a settled live state.
  - `"healthy"`: the keeper's live runtime is running and aligned with its desired always-on presence.
  - `"offline"`: the keeper is not desired as always-on and is not running.
- While a desired resident keeper is stopped, every read surface must show `"desired_offline"` for it. Once a bootstrap or reconciliation pass has restarted it, every read surface must show `"recovering"` while it is converging, and `"healthy"` once its live runtime is settled and aligned with the desired presence.

Settling bound:

- The settling criterion is fixed and observable: a desired resident keeper's live runtime is settled once the same live runtime has been running uninterrupted for at least 60 seconds. Immediately after a (re)start, every read surface may (and must) report `"recovering"` for that keeper; once the runtime has run uninterrupted for at least 60 seconds, every read surface must report `"healthy"`.
- Recovery is transitional, not permanent: an implementation must not keep reporting `"recovering"` indefinitely for a keeper whose live runtime has long been running and aligned with its desired presence. Reporting `"recovering"` only within the stated 60-second settling window after the latest (re)start satisfies this requirement.

problem_statement:
rename `times` to `mul`
both gemini and chatgpt agree that `times` doesn't make sense with add, sub, div. They both independently suggested `mul` as the best option. This also leaves all three with 3 letter names, which is nice.

### Additional contract requirements

Integer multiplication in `Bosatsu/Predef` is exposed under the exported
name `mul` (a function of type `Int -> Int -> Int`).

- `mul` computes integer multiplication: `mul(a, b)` evaluates to the
  integer product of `a` and `b`. Existing expressions rewritten to call
  `mul` keep their previous meaning, including constant folding and
  normalization of products with small integer literals.
- The former predef name `times` for integer multiplication is no longer
  part of `Bosatsu/Predef`: programs that reference `times` as a predef
  binding (for example `times(6, 7)`, `6.times(7)`, or
  `operator * = times`) are rejected. Other existing predef names such as
  `timesf` (Float64 multiplication) are unchanged.
- All supported backends must honor the same predef surface: evaluating,
  testing, and generating code (including the C backend, which links
  generated code against the repository C runtime sources) must resolve
  `Bosatsu/Predef::mul` and compute multiplication with it; no supported
  backend may require the former name.

problem_statement:
design a Bytes type
Design a bosatsu external `Bytes` type which is semantically basically `Array[Byte]` but not parametric so it can be stored as a [HIDDEN].

Make an API consistent with Bosatsu/Predef::List and Bosatsu/Collection/Array. We should have the ability to convert to `Array[Int]` and `from_List_Int(ints: List[Int]): Bytes` which takes the low 8 bits of each int in 2's complement and converts those to a number from 0 to 255.

We should consult the python3 bytes and memoryview API and use that for inspiration. We need to stay immutable and consistent with existing Bosatsu, but also ideally as close to python3 bytes/memoryview as possible. This is our number 3 goal after: must be immutable and be consistent with bosatsu style especially List and Array.

Where should it live? Maybe in Bosatsu/IO which is where it would be useful.

Propose Bosatsu/IO/Core functions to work with binary files using Handles and Bytes to read and write data. Add a section for how these functions can be as efficient as possible with the constraints that we have. Speak to what external functions we should have so that the external function is "big enough" to do significant work where it can leverage mutability and keep the API boundary of the function pure and immutable.

### Additional contract requirements

# Bytes contract addendum

The Bytes interface covered by this contract is the `Bosatsu/IO/Bytes` package.
It provides an opaque, non-parametric external `Bytes` value. `Bytes` values are
immutable sequences of byte values.

The package provides `empty_Bytes`, `size_Bytes`, `from_List_Int`,
`from_Array_Int`, `to_List_Int`, and `to_Array_Int`.

- `empty_Bytes` has no elements and `size_Bytes(empty_Bytes)` is zero.
- `size_Bytes` is the number of byte values in the sequence.
- `from_List_Int` and `from_Array_Int` retain input order and normalize every
  input integer to its low eight bits. Thus `[-1, 0, 1, 255, 256, 257]`
  represents `[255, 0, 1, 255, 0, 1]`.
- `to_List_Int` and `to_Array_Int` return the represented values in order, with
  every returned integer in the inclusive range 0 through 255.

This addendum does not require semantics for other Bytes collection operations,
JSON serialization, or binary Handle I/O operations.

problem_statement:
Allow Custom operator to be called as functor with points
## Problem

Currently, built-in operators can be constructed directly from points:

```julia
lap = laplacian(points)
grad = gradient(points)
∂x = partial(points, 1, 1)
```

But `Custom` operators created with `@operator` require the `custom()` function as an intermediary:

```julia
ℒ = @operator(∇²)
op = custom(points, ℒ)  # have to go through `custom()`
```

This is inconsistent with the rest of the API.

## Proposed Change

Make `Custom{N}` a functor so it can be called directly with points:

```julia
ℒ = @operator(∇²)
op = ℒ(points)           # consistent with laplacian(points), gradient(points), etc.
op = ℒ(points; k=30, basis=PHS(5))  # with keyword arguments
```

problem_statement:
Modernize Julia CI and evaluate version floor
## Context

The JuliaQUBO package stack is currently mixed across Julia compat floors and CI versions. Julia 1.12 is the current stable series, while Julia 1.10 is the current LTS series. We should modernize CI coverage and then make an explicit decision about whether each package can raise its `[compat] julia` floor.

## Recommendation

Use two kinds of CI lanes:

- an explicit minimum-supported Julia version, matching this package's `[compat] julia` floor;
- `version: '1'` for the current stable Julia release.

Prefer `version: '1'` over hard-coding `version: '1.12'` for the latest-stable lane, so CI automatically catches issues when Julia 1.13 becomes stable. Only use `1.12` as a temporary audit lane or if the package intentionally pins CI to that release series.

## Tasks

- Audit this repository's current `[compat] julia`, CI matrix, documentation workflow, and any package-specific runtime constraints.
- Add or update CI so it tests the current advertised floor and latest stable Julia (`version: '1'`).
- Run the package test suite, docs build, and any downstream/foreign package tests under the proposed floor and latest stable.
- If the current floor is no longer worth supporting, propose a PR that raises `[compat] julia` to the agreed floor and updates CI/docs accordingly.
- Document the floor change in release notes or changelog if support for older Julia versions is dropped.

## Acceptance criteria

- CI covers both the supported floor and current stable Julia.
- Any floor increase is intentional, documented, and checked against dependent JuliaQUBO packages.
- The package keeps using stable public Julia APIs compatible with the declared floor.

@@ -0,0 +1,400 @@
+import TOML
+import Test
+
+const PACKAGE_ROOT = normpath(joinpath(@__DIR__, ".."))
+
+# Derive the advertised `[compat] julia` floor from the package itself: CI must
+# exercise whatever floor the package declares rather than a hard-coded series.
+function _julia_floor()::VersionNumber
+    compat = TOML.parsefile(joinpath(PACKAGE_ROOT, "Project.toml"))["compat"]
+    return VersionNumber(compat["julia"])
+end
+
+_indent(line::AbstractString) = length(line) - length(lstrip(line))
+
+# Discover every workflow file that defines the repository's CI instead of
+# hard-coding one filename.
+function _workflow_paths()
+    dir = joinpath(PACKAGE_ROOT, ".github", "workflows")
+    isdir(dir) || return String[]
+    return sort([joinpath(dir, name) for name in readdir(dir)
+                 if endswith(name, ".yml") || endswith(name, ".yaml")])
+end
+
+# Collect the lines nested under `key:` (the first match), returning the block
+# body plus any inline value that followed the key on the same line. This is a
+# deliberately tiny structural YAML reader: indentation only.
+function _mapping_block(lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString}, key::String)
+    pattern = Regex("^([ \\t]*)-?[ \\t]*" * key * raw"[ \t]*:[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$")
+    for (i, line) in pairs(lines)
+        m = match(pattern, line)
+        m === nothing && continue
+        indent = length(m.captures[1])
+        last = i
+        for j in (i + 1):length(lines)
+            stripped = strip(lines[j])
+            if !isempty(stripped) && !startswith(stripped, "#") &&
+               _indent(lines[j]) <= indent
+                break
+            end
+            last = j
+        end
+        return lines[(i + 1):last], m.captures[2]
+    end
+    return SubString[], nothing
+end
+
+# Split a workflow into the blocks of lines that describe each top-level job,
+# without requiring any particular job name.
+function _job_blocks(lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})::Vector{Vector{SubString}}
+    jobs_body, _ = _mapping_block(lines, "jobs")
+    jobs = Vector{SubString}[]
+    job_indent = nothing
+    for line in jobs_body
+        stripped = strip(line)
+        (isempty(stripped) || startswith(stripped, "#")) && continue
+        indent = _indent(line)
+        if job_indent === nothing
+            job_indent = indent
+        end
+        indent < job_indent && break
+        if indent == job_indent &&
+           occursin(r"^[ \t]*[A-Za-z0-9_\"'.-]+[ \t]*:[ \t]*$", line)
+            push!(jobs, SubString[])
+        elseif !isempty(jobs)
+            push!(jobs[end], line)
+        end
+    end
+    return jobs
+end
+
+# Split a scalar or flow-list value ("['1.10', '1']", "'1'", 1.10) into its
+# YAML scalar items, stripping surrounding quotes from each.
+function _yaml_scalar_list(value::AbstractString)::Vector{String}
+    value = strip(replace(value, r"\s+#.*$" => "")) # drop trailing comments
+    isempty(value) && return String[]
+    if startswith(value, "[")
+        close = findfirst(']', value)
+        close === nothing && return String[]
+        value = value[2:(close - 1)]
+        return [strip(item, [' ', '\t', '\'', '"']) for item in split(value, ',')
+                if !isempty(strip(item))]
+    end
+    if length(value) >= 2 &&
+       ((first(value) == '\'' && last(value) == '\'') ||
+        (first(value) == '"' && last(value) == '"'))
+        value = value[2:(end - 1)]
+    end
+    return [string(value)]
+end
+
+# Expand a flow mapping row into its `key: value` items so combination rows
+# such as `{version: '1.10', os: ubuntu-latest}` expose their fields.
+function _flow_items(item::AbstractString)
+    text = strip(item)
+    startswith(text, "{") || return [text]
+    close = findlast('}', text)
+    close === nothing && return [text]
+    return [strip(part) for part in split(text[2:(close - 1)], ',')
+            if !isempty(strip(part))]
+end
+
+_version_like(values) = unique(string(value) for value in values
+                               if !isempty(value) && isdigit(first(strip(value))))
+
+# Map every matrix axis and extra combination row of a job to the values they
+# can contribute. Each row records its kind (`block-map` rows belong to the
+# named axis or combination field; `flow-map` rows come from flow-style combos
+# such as `- {version: '1.10', os: ubuntu-latest}`), the axis or field key,
+# and one offered value. Axis names are arbitrary (`version`, `julia`,
+# `julia-version`, ...), so nothing here assumes a name.
+function _matrix_maps(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})
+    rows = NamedTuple{(:kind, :key, :value),Tuple{String,String,String}}[]
+    # Flow-style strategy, e.g. `strategy: {matrix: {version: ['1.10', '1']}}`:
+    # axis keys that carry flow lists become block-map rows with those lists.
+    strategy, strategy_inline = _mapping_block(job_lines, "strategy")
+    if strategy_inline !== nothing && occursin("matrix", strategy_inline)
+        for m in eachmatch(r"([A-Za-z0-9_\"'-]+)\s*:\s*(\[[^\]]*\])", strategy_inline)
+            append!(rows, [(kind = "block-map",
+                            key = string(strip(m.captures[1], ['\'', '"'])),
+                            value = item)
+                           for item in _yaml_scalar_list(m.captures[2])])
+        end
+        isempty(rows) || return rows
+    end
+    matrix_body, matrix_inline = _mapping_block(strategy, "matrix")
+    if matrix_inline !== nothing && startswith(strip(matrix_inline), "{")
+        # Flow-style matrix mapping on a single line.
+        for m in eachmatch(r"([A-Za-z0-9_\"'-]+)\s*:\s*(\[[^\]]*\]|[^,}]+)", matrix_inline)
+            for value in _yaml_scalar_list(m.captures[2])
+                push!(rows, (kind = "block-map",
+                             key = string(strip(m.captures[1], ['\'', '"'])),
+                             value = value))
+            end
+        end
+        return rows
+    end
+    # Block-style matrix: axis fields sit at one indent, block-list items and
+    # combination rows (`include:`/`exclude:`) sit below them.
+    axis_indent = nothing
+    axis_key = nothing
+    for line in matrix_body
+        stripped = strip(line)
+        (isempty(stripped) || startswith(stripped, "#")) && continue
+        indent = _indent(line)
+        if axis_indent === nothing
+            axis_indent = indent
+        end
+        item = match(r"^[ \t]*-[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", line)
+        header = item === nothing ?
+                 match(r"^[ \t]*([A-Za-z0-9_\"'-]+)[ \t]*:[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", line) :
+                 nothing
+        if header !== nothing
+            key = string(strip(header.captures[1], ['\'', '"']))
+            if indent <= axis_indent
+                axis_key = key
+            end
+            for value in _yaml_scalar_list(header.captures[2])
+                push!(rows, (kind = "block-map", key = key, value = value))
+            end
+        elseif item !== nothing
+            body = item.captures[1]
+            for piece in _flow_items(body)
+                field = match(r"(?:^|[{,])\s*([A-Za-z0-9_\"'-]+)\s*:\s*(.*)$", piece)
+                if field === nothing
+                    # A bare scalar is a block-list value of the current axis.
+                    axis_key === nothing && continue
+                    for value in _yaml_scalar_list(piece)
+                        push!(rows, (kind = "block-map", key = axis_key, value = value))
+                    end
+                else
+                    kind = startswith(strip(body), "{") ? "flow-map" : "block-map"
+                    key = string(strip(field.captures[1], ['\'', '"']))
+                    for value in _yaml_scalar_list(field.captures[2])
+                        push!(rows, (kind = kind, key = key, value = value))
+                    end
+                end
+            end
+        end
+    end
+    return rows
+end
+
+# The values a job exposes through `matrix.<axis>`, restricted to values that
+# belong to exactly that axis: block/flow-style axis entries together with
+# combination rows (`include:`/`exclude:`) that name that axis. Values from
+# unrelated axes are never mixed in.
+function _axis_versions(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString}, axis::AbstractString)
+    values = String[]
+    for row in _matrix_maps(job_lines)
+        row.kind == "block-map" && isempty(row.key) && continue
+        row.key == axis || continue
+        append!(values, _yaml_scalar_list(row.value))
+    end
+    return _version_like(values)
+end
+
+# Identify whether a single workflow line is itself a conventional Julia
+# installation invocation: the official setup action, a juliaup installer, or
+# a direct Julia download.
+function _julia_install_line(line::AbstractString)::Bool
+    startswith(lstrip(line), "#") && return false
+    pattern = r"(?i)julia-actions/setup-julia|juliaup|julialang\.org|julia-[0-9][0-9a-zA-Z+.\-]*-(?:linux|win|mac)"
+    return occursin(pattern, line)
+end
+
+# Which Julia versions are handed to this job's Julia-install steps? Only a
+# `version:` setting that is consumed by a Julia-install invocation counts: a
+# literal `version: 'X'` on such a step contributes `X`, and when the install
+# step passes a matrix variable through (`version: ${{ matrix.<axis> }}`),
+# only that axis's own version-looking values define the lanes it selects.
+# `version:` inputs that belong to unrelated steps or actions are ignored.
+function _step_versions(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})::Vector{String}
+    versions = String[]
+    step_consumes = nothing
+    for line in job_lines
+        (isempty(strip(line)) || startswith(lstrip(line), "#")) && continue
+        # A new step begins at a `- ` list entry whose `uses:` or `run:`
+        # invocation determines whether any `version:` input below it feeds a
+        # Julia installation.
+        boundary = match(r"^[ \t]*-[ \t]", line)
+        if boundary !== nothing
+            invoked = match(r"^[ \t]*-[ \t]*(?:uses|run)[ \t]*:", line)
+            step_consumes = invoked === nothing ? false : _julia_install_line(line)
+            continue
+        end
+        is_consuming = _julia_install_line(line)
+        is_consuming && (step_consumes = true)
+        m = match(r"^[ \t]*-?[ \t]*version[ \t]*:[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", line)
+        m === nothing && continue
+        consumes = (step_consumes === true) || _julia_install_line(m.captures[1])
+        consumes || continue
+        value = m.captures[1]
+        ref = match(r"\$\{\{[^}]*matrix\.([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)[^}]*\}\}", value)
+        if ref === nothing
+            append!(versions, _yaml_scalar_list(value))
+        else
+            union!(versions, _axis_versions(job_lines, ref.captures[1]))
+        end
+        (step_consumes === nothing) && (step_consumes = is_consuming)
+    end
+    return _version_like(versions)
+end
+
+# Conventional ways of installing Julia in CI: the official setup action,
+# setup-julia named steps, juliaup installers, or direct Julia downloads.
+function _installs_julia(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})::Bool
+    pattern = r"(?i)julia-actions/setup-julia|setup[-_ ]?julia[^.]|juliaup|julialang\.org|julia-[0-9][0-9a-zA-Z+.\-]*-(?:linux|win|mac)"
+    return any(line -> occursin(pattern, line) && !startswith(lstrip(line), "#"), job_lines)
+end
+
+# Conventional ways of running the package test suite in CI.
+function _runs_tests(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})::Bool
+    pattern = r"(?i)julia-actions/julia-runtest|julia[-_ ]?runtest|Pkg\.test|pkg['\"]?>?[ \t]*test\b|--eval[^\"']*\btest|runtests\.jl"
+    return any(line -> occursin(pattern, line) && !startswith(lstrip(line), "#"), job_lines)
+end
+
+# Julia versions named directly by install steps that bypass a `version:`
+# setting, such as `juliaup add 1.10`, `julia +1.10`, or a downloaded
+# `julia-1.10-linux-x86_64` archive.
+function _install_versions(job_lines::AbstractVector{<:AbstractString})::Vector{String}
+    versions = String[]
+    for line in job_lines
+        startswith(lstrip(line), "#") && continue
+        for m in eachmatch(r"(?i)juliaup\s+(?:channel\s+)?add\s+['\"]?([0-9][0-9a-zA-Z+.\-]*)", line)
+            push!(versions, m.captures[1])
+        end
+        for m in eachmatch(r"(?i)\bjulia\s*\+\s*['\"]?([0-9][0-9a-zA-Z+.\-]*)", line)
+            push!(versions, m.captures[1])
+        end
+        for m in eachmatch(r"(?i)\bjulia-([0-9][0-9a-zA-Z+.\-]*)-(?:linux|win|mac)", line)
+            push!(versions, m.captures[1])
+        end
+    end
+    return _version_like(versions)
+end
+
+# All Julia versions under which the repository's CI installs Julia and runs
+# the package test suite, regardless of workflow filename, job naming, matrix
+# axis naming, or the concrete setup/test mechanism in use.
+function _ci_test_versions(workflow::AbstractString)::Vector{String}
+    versions = String[]
+    for job_lines in _job_blocks(split(workflow, '\n'))
+        (_installs_julia(job_lines) && _runs_tests(job_lines)) || continue
+        union!(versions, _step_versions(job_lines))
+        union!(versions, _install_versions(job_lines))
+    end
+    return versions
+end
+
+Test.@testset "CI tests the declared Julia compat floor and the latest stable release" begin
+    lanes = Set{String}()
+    for path in _workflow_paths()
+        union!(lanes, _ci_test_versions(read(path, String)))
+    end
+
+    # The advertised `[compat] julia` floor must be exercised as an explicit
+    # CI lane that installs Julia and runs the package tests.
+    floor = _julia_floor()
+    # Compare semantically: an explicit lane such as 1.10.0 counts as covering
+    # the declared 1.10 floor, while older series and later feature releases
+    # must not be mistaken for it.
+    floor_lane = any(lanes) do lane
+        try
+            v = VersionNumber(lane)
+            return v.major == floor.major && v.minor == floor.minor &&
+                   v >= floor
+        catch
+            return false
+        end
+    end
+    Test.@test floor_lane
+
+    # A latest-stable lane must exist and use the floating `1` so that CI
+    # tracks newly released stable Julia versions automatically.
+    Test.@test "1" in lanes
+
+    # Self-audit: the lane analysis itself must honor common, documented CI
+    # layouts and must not credit a lane with values from unrelated matrix
+    # axes. These synthetic cases keep the checks above honest.
+    alternate_axis = """
+    jobs:
+      test:
+        strategy:
+          matrix:
+            julia: ['1.10', '1']
+            os: ['ubuntu-latest']
+        steps:
+          - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v1
+            with:
+              version: \${{ matrix.julia }}
+          - uses: julia-actions/julia-runtest@v1
+    """
+    Test.@test _ci_test_versions(alternate_axis) == ["1.10", "1"]
+
+    # A juliaup-based floor lane must be credited even without setup-julia.
+    juliaup_floor = """
+    jobs:
+      test:
+        steps:
+          - run: juliaup add 1.10
+          - run: Pkg.test()
+    """
+    Test.@test _ci_test_versions(juliaup_floor) == ["1.10"]
+
+    # An unrelated digit-valued matrix axis must not supply a lane version:
+    # only the axis consumed by the setup step defines its lanes.
+    unrelated_axis = """
+    jobs:
+      test:
+        strategy:
+          matrix:
+            python: ['1']
+            julia: ['1.10']
+            os: ['ubuntu-latest']
+        steps:
+          - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v1
+            with:
+              version: \${{ matrix.julia }}
+          - uses: julia-actions/julia-runtest@v1
+    """
+    Test.@test _ci_test_versions(unrelated_axis) == ["1.10"]
+
+    # An unrelated action's `version:` input must never be credited as a Julia
+    # lane: only the Julia-install invocation's own version settings count.
+    unrelated_action_version = """
+    jobs:
+      test:
+        steps:
+          - uses: actions/checkout@v5
+            with:
+              version: '1'
+          - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v1
+            with:
+              version: '1.10'
+          - uses: julia-actions/julia-runtest@v1
+    """
+    Test.@test _ci_test_versions(unrelated_action_version) == ["1.10"]
+
+    # An explicit patch-level representation of the floor must be accepted:
+    # 1.10.0 covers the declared 1.10 floor just as 1.10 does.
+    explicit_patch_floor = """
+    jobs:
+      test:
+        strategy:
+          matrix:
+            julia: ['1.10.0', '1']
+            os: ['ubuntu-latest']
+        steps:
+          - uses: julia-actions/setup-julia@v1
+            with:
+              version: \${{ matrix.julia }}
+          - uses: julia-actions/julia-runtest@v1
+    """
+    explicit_lanes = _ci_test_versions(explicit_patch_floor)
+    Test.@test explicit_lanes == ["1.10.0", "1"]
+    Test.@test any(lane -> begin
+                       v = VersionNumber(lane)
+                       v.major == floor.major && v.minor == floor.minor && v >= floor
+                   end, explicit_lanes)
+end

problem_statement:
Avoid the Gaussian-only road
i think we should solve @GearsAD ‘s concerns regarding softtype on CG first before we close this?  I’m happy with name only if it solves the right problem.  I’m worried about the CG stuff going down a Gaussian-only road and end up forcing the overall DFG side to a crisp but overly restrictive DataLevel1 space.  I mean that users just want Level1 and moan it’s not working well enough, and somehow get out of using Level2.  To help avoid all that i think softtypename::Symbol/String is good.

Just to reiterate, i originally wanted to avoid duplication of the whole softtype so just guessed name as a string as cheap hack.  Without the necessary type information for non-Julia use cases, i’m not sure... Again the question for me is what do we want from Summary (what is the one sentence existence proof for Summary/Level1?).

Is it fair for a user to avoid the Julia internals just to get the inference product in a usable way, or should they at least don some of the Julia-ness to use the inference products?  Perhaps i should add, (again) that we are not building Gaussian-only, so the user should get the full beliefs, not just hide behind PPE.  That means DataLevel2.  I don’t want to dumb down the output and look shoddy against a more mature Gaussian-only system.  I’d rather force the user into Julia or build a better multilang interface (I vote the latter). 

I know Neo4j has a bunch of nice features for Gaussian-only, but that should be “supportive” not “authoritative” in the design.

I would argue Summary/Level1 CANNOT be it is the final inference product.  The final inference product is and always should be DataLevel2.

TL;DR I fairly strongly feel softtypename as Symbol/String or remove completely from Level1.  If there are cool features in Neo4j we can leverage, then leave that door open;  but the DB should not dictate our design too much but rather store what is needed — pattern here is *strongly* non-Gaussian (ie not just PPE).

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum defines the public behavioral contract for the new non-Gaussian belief representation
added by this change. It states only observable behavior.

## `HomotopyDensityDFG` belief representation

A new hybrid (non)parametric belief representation type named `HomotopyDensityDFG` is introduced.
It replaces the previous stored homotopy belief representation; public behavior that previously
referenced the old stored-homotopy-belief name now refers to `HomotopyDensityDFG`. In particular,
the `belief` field of a `State` (and therefore of every state stored in a `VariableDFG` variable)
holds a `HomotopyDensityDFG`, so observable state beliefs are `HomotopyDensityDFG` instances and
are not instances of the replaced representation.

- `HomotopyDensityDFG` is a parametric type `HomotopyDensityDFG{T, P}`, where `T` is a state type
  and `P` is its associated manifold point type.
- A `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance exposes at least the following user-visible fields: `points`,
  `weights`, `principal_elements`, `principal_forms`, `topologykind`, and `trailing_forms`.
- Two instances are equal (`==`) when their corresponding contents are equal, so that an instance
  constructed from scratch compares equal to an identical instance recovered from serialization.
- All behavior described in this addendum applies generically to any state type instance
  `T::AbstractStateType`, including state types defined by users outside the package; it is not
  specific to any particular state type, manifold, or manifold point representation.

## Outer constructor from a state type instance

Calling `HomotopyDensityDFG(T_instance)` with a state type instance `T_instance` returns a
default-constructed `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}` for which
all of the following observable defaults hold:

- the computed result type is exactly
  `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}`;
- `points` is empty;
- `weights` is empty;
- `principal_elements` is empty;
- `principal_forms` is empty;
- `topologykind` holds a default value that is a subtype of the package's abstract homotopy
  topology type.

A keyword-argument form of the parametric constructor allows `principal_elements` and
`principal_forms` to be supplied at construction time.

## States and variables store `HomotopyDensityDFG` beliefs

Constructing a state, e.g. `State(:default, T_instance)`, produces a state whose `belief` is a
`HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}`. States added to a
`VariableDFG` variable (e.g. via `addState!`) likewise have `HomotopyDensityDFG` beliefs, for any
state type as described above.

## JSON serialization round-trip through the abstract belief type

A `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance can be serialized to JSON with the package's DFG JSON style and
deserialized back by parsing the resulting JSON text against the *abstract* `HomotopyDensityDFG`
type name (i.e. without supplying the concrete type parameters), using the same style:

- Serializing uses `JSON.json(bel; style = DFGJSONStyle())` (pretty printing optional).
- Deserializing uses `JSON.parse(jstr, HomotopyDensityDFG; style = DFGJSONStyle())`.
- The parsed result is a concrete `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance whose inferred type parameters
  match the source instance's state type (and hence it is a subtype of
  `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance)}`), and it compares equal (`==`) to the source instance.

problem_statement_base:
Avoid the Gaussian-only road
i think we should solve @GearsAD ‘s concerns regarding softtype on CG first before we close this?  I’m happy with name only if it solves the right problem.  I’m worried about the CG stuff going down a Gaussian-only road and end up forcing the overall DFG side to a crisp but overly restrictive DataLevel1 space.  I mean that users just want Level1 and moan it’s not working well enough, and somehow get out of using Level2.  To help avoid all that i think softtypename::Symbol/String is good.

Just to reiterate, i originally wanted to avoid duplication of the whole softtype so just guessed name as a string as cheap hack.  Without the necessary type information for non-Julia use cases, i’m not sure... Again the question for me is what do we want from Summary (what is the one sentence existence proof for Summary/Level1?).

Is it fair for a user to avoid the Julia internals just to get the inference product in a usable way, or should they at least don some of the Julia-ness to use the inference products?  Perhaps i should add, (again) that we are not building Gaussian-only, so the user should get the full beliefs, not just hide behind PPE.  That means DataLevel2.  I don’t want to dumb down the output and look shoddy against a more mature Gaussian-only system.  I’d rather force the user into Julia or build a better multilang interface (I vote the latter). 

I know Neo4j has a bunch of nice features for Gaussian-only, but that should be “supportive” not “authoritative” in the design.

I would argue Summary/Level1 CANNOT be it is the final inference product.  The final inference product is and always should be DataLevel2.

TL;DR I fairly strongly feel softtypename as Symbol/String or remove completely from Level1.  If there are cool features in Neo4j we can leverage, then leave that door open;  but the DB should not dictate our design too much but rather store what is needed — pattern here is *strongly* non-Gaussian (ie not just PPE).

contract_addendum:
This addendum defines the public behavioral contract for the new non-Gaussian belief representation
added by this change. It states only observable behavior.

## `HomotopyDensityDFG` belief representation

A new hybrid (non)parametric belief representation type named `HomotopyDensityDFG` is introduced.
It replaces the previous stored homotopy belief representation; public behavior that previously
referenced the old stored-homotopy-belief name now refers to `HomotopyDensityDFG`. In particular,
the `belief` field of a `State` (and therefore of every state stored in a `VariableDFG` variable)
holds a `HomotopyDensityDFG`, so observable state beliefs are `HomotopyDensityDFG` instances and
are not instances of the replaced representation.

- `HomotopyDensityDFG` is a parametric type `HomotopyDensityDFG{T, P}`, where `T` is a state type
  and `P` is its associated manifold point type.
- A `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance exposes at least the following user-visible fields: `points`,
  `weights`, `principal_elements`, `principal_forms`, `topologykind`, and `trailing_forms`.
- Two instances are equal (`==`) when their corresponding contents are equal, so that an instance
  constructed from scratch compares equal to an identical instance recovered from serialization.
- All behavior described in this addendum applies generically to any state type instance
  `T::AbstractStateType`, including state types defined by users outside the package; it is not
  specific to any particular state type, manifold, or manifold point representation.

## Outer constructor from a state type instance

Calling `HomotopyDensityDFG(T_instance)` with a state type instance `T_instance` returns a
default-constructed `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}` for which
all of the following observable defaults hold:

- the computed result type is exactly
  `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}`;
- `points` is empty;
- `weights` is empty;
- `principal_elements` is empty;
- `principal_forms` is empty;
- `topologykind` holds a default value that is a subtype of the package's abstract homotopy
  topology type.

A keyword-argument form of the parametric constructor allows `principal_elements` and
`principal_forms` to be supplied at construction time.

## States and variables store `HomotopyDensityDFG` beliefs

Constructing a state, e.g. `State(:default, T_instance)`, produces a state whose `belief` is a
`HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance), getPointType(T_instance)}`. States added to a
`VariableDFG` variable (e.g. via `addState!`) likewise have `HomotopyDensityDFG` beliefs, for any
state type as described above.

## JSON serialization round-trip through the abstract belief type

A `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance can be serialized to JSON with the package's DFG JSON style and
deserialized back by parsing the resulting JSON text against the *abstract* `HomotopyDensityDFG`
type name (i.e. without supplying the concrete type parameters), using the same style:

- Serializing uses `JSON.json(bel; style = DFGJSONStyle())` (pretty printing optional).
- Deserializing uses `JSON.parse(jstr, HomotopyDensityDFG; style = DFGJSONStyle())`.
- The parsed result is a concrete `HomotopyDensityDFG` instance whose inferred type parameters
  match the source instance's state type (and hence it is a subtype of
  `HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T_instance)}`), and it compares equal (`==`) to the source instance.
- This round-trip behavior is required both for containers whose `points` have been populated and
  for containers constructed with populated `principal_elements`, `principal_forms`, or
  `trailing_forms` contents, for any state type as described above.

+    form = resolveType(lazyobj.formkind[])
+    statekind = liftStateKind(lazyobj.statekind[])

+"""
+    HomotopyDensityDFG{T <: StateType, P}
+
+Hybrid belief representation with natural transition between (non)parametric representations.
+
+**THIS IS IMPORTANT**: Fundamentally related to `HomotopyDensity` definition in AMP.jl.
+
+!!! warning "Raw Data Container"
+    `HomotopyDensityDFG` is the raw data schema used for database storage and serialization.
+    Mutating this structure in-place is discouraged. Rather, construct a new `State` object 
+    and call `addState!` or `mergeState!`.
+
+Notes:
+- These are the internal raw beliefs and need to be viewed through a lens such as 
+provided by AMP for features like pdf evaluation. 
+- Allows partials as identified by list of coordinate dimensions via `.reprkind{...L}.partial`
+  - e.g. legacy `partial = [1;3] or (1,3)`
+    - When building a partial belief, use full points with necessary information in the specified partial coords.
+- Replaces ManellicTree, ManifoldKernelDensity, KernelDensityEstimate, GaussianMixtureModel, PCA, Mixtures
+  - a.k.a. model order reduction given a topology selection
+"""
+@kwdef struct HomotopyDensityDFG{T <: StateType, P}
+    reprkind::HomotopyReprDFG{T} =
+        HomotopyReprDFG(DefaultTopologyKind(), DefaultFormKind(), T(), nothing)
+    """A hint for downstream solvers on how to interpret this data (The 'How')"""
+    topologykind::AbstractHomotopyTopology = DefaultTopologyKind()
+
+    points::Vector{P} = P[] # previously `val`
+    weights::Vector{Float64} = Float64[]
+    """
+    In model order reduction, PCA, and modal analysis, the terms for the eigenvectors associated with the largest and smallest eigenvalues are commonly:
+      Major eigenvectors are often called "dominant eigenvectors," or simply "leading modes." In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), these are the "principal components."
+      Minor eigenvectors are sometimes called "trailing eigenvectors," or "residual modes." In PCA, these correspond to the components with the smallest variance.
+    """
+    principal_coeffs::Vector{Float64} = Vector{Float64}() # FIXME getMajorsLength(reprkind))
+    principal_elements::Vector{P} = P[] # previously `val[1]` for Gaussian
+    principal_forms::Vector{Matrix{Float64}} = Matrix{Float64}[] # previously `covar` existed but was stored in `bw` (hacky)
+    """
+    Store minor eigenvalue details such as leaf bandwidth or reconstruction vectors.
+    - When lifted for compute efficiency, this field is likely to hold something like PDMats.
+    - When lowered or for serde, this field is likely to hold Dict{Int, Vector{Float64}}.
+    """
+    trailing_forms::SparseVector{Matrix{Float64}, Int} = spzeros(Matrix{Float64}, 1) #previously `bw`
+    """
+    Geometric points permute field, allows fast binary tree operations and geometric points splits for manellic (ball) trees. 
+    - Geometric split reqs at least 2*(N+1)-1 points -- e.g. when nodes have only right children, points=[1,2,-3].
+    """
+    structure::SparseVector{Vector{Int}, Int} = spzeros(Vector{Int}, 1)
+end
+
+JSON.omit_empty(::Type{<:HomotopyDensityDFG}) = true
+
+function HomotopyDensityDFG(T::AbstractStateType)
+    return HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(T), getPointType(T)}()
+end
+
+function StructUtils.fielddefaults(
+    ::StructUtils.StructStyle,
+    ::Type{HomotopyDensityDFG{T, P}},
+) where {T, P}
+    return (
+        topologykind = DefaultTopologyKind(),
+        principal_coeffs = Float64[],
+        principal_elements = P[],
+        principal_forms = Matrix{Float64}[],
+        weights = Float64[],
+        points = P[],
+        trailing_forms = sparsevec(Int[], Matrix{Float64}[]),
+    )
+end
+
+function StructUtils.fieldtags(::StructUtils.StructStyle, ::Type{<:HomotopyDensityDFG})
+    return (reprkind = (choosetype = resolveHomotopyReprDFGType,),)
+end
+
+function resolveHomotopyDensityDFGType(lazyobj)
+    statekind = liftStateKind(lazyobj.reprkind.statekind[])
+    return HomotopyDensityDFG{typeof(statekind), getPointType(statekind)}
+end
+
+@choosetype HomotopyDensityDFG resolveHomotopyDensityDFGType

problem_statement:
resources/read: support ResourceContents returns from data_provider (incl. binary BlobResourceContents)
Found during a docs-correctness audit (follow-up to #53).

**Current behavior** (`src/protocol/handlers.jl` `handle_read_resource`): the resource's `data_provider` is called with **no arguments** and the return value is unconditionally JSON-encoded into a single text contents entry:

```julia
data = resource.data_provider()
contents = [LittleDict{String,Any}(
    "uri" => string(resource.uri),
    "text" => JSON3.write(data),
    "mimeType" => resource.mime_type
)]
```

**Consequences:**
1. **Binary resources cannot be served** via `resources/read` — there is no path that produces a `blob` contents entry, even though `BlobResourceContents` exists and is exported.
2. Returning `TextResourceContents`/`BlobResourceContents` from a provider (which our own docs used to show) double-encodes the struct into the `text` field instead of using it as the contents object.
3. A `String` return is JSON-quoted (`"..."`) rather than used verbatim, which is surprising for `text/plain` resources.
4. Resources are matched by exact URI only; the old docs implied wildcard URIs (`file://*`) reach the provider with the requested URI — they don't (providers take no arguments).

**Proposal (additive, 0.5.x):**
- If `data_provider()` returns a `ResourceContents` (or `Vector{ResourceContents}`), serialize it directly (text → `text`, blob → base64 `blob`), keeping the JSON-encode fallback for plain data — mirroring how tool returns auto-wrap.
- Optionally pass-through `String` returns verbatim for non-JSON mime types.
- URI templates / parameterized providers are a separate, larger feature (`resource_templates` already exists as a field) — out of scope here.

problem_statement_base:
resources/read: support ResourceContents returns from data_provider (incl. binary BlobResourceContents)
Found during a docs-correctness audit (follow-up to #53).

**Current behavior** (`src/protocol/handlers.jl` `handle_read_resource`): the resource's `data_provider` is called with **no arguments** and the return value is unconditionally JSON-encoded into a single text contents entry:

```julia
data = resource.data_provider()
contents = [LittleDict{String,Any}(
    "uri" => string(resource.uri),
    "text" => JSON3.write(data),
    "mimeType" => resource.mime_type
)]
```

**Consequences:**
1. **Binary resources cannot be served** via `resources/read` — there is no path that produces a `blob` contents entry, even though `BlobResourceContents` exists and is exported.
2. Returning `TextResourceContents`/`BlobResourceContents` from a provider (which our own docs used to show) double-encodes the struct into the `text` field instead of using it as the contents object.
3. A `String` return is JSON-quoted (`"..."`) rather than used verbatim, which is surprising for `text/plain` resources.
4. Resources are matched by exact URI only; the old docs implied wildcard URIs (`file://*`) reach the provider with the requested URI — they don't (providers take no arguments).

**Proposal (additive, 0.5.x):**
- If `data_provider()` returns a `ResourceContents` (or `Vector{ResourceContents}`), serialize it directly (text → `text`, blob → base64 `blob`), keeping the JSON-encode fallback for plain data — mirroring how tool returns auto-wrap.
- Optionally pass-through `String` returns verbatim for non-JSON mime types.
- URI templates / parameterized providers are a separate, larger feature (`resource_templates` already exists as a field) — out of scope here.

Docs were updated (post-#53 audit) to describe the current contract honestly; this issue tracks lifting the limitation.

# Minimal 7z shim for Julia Pkg PlatformEngines. The 7z bundled with this
# Julia requires GLIBC_2.38 (unavailable on Debian 12), which breaks Pkg's

        *) exec gzip -dc "$a" ;;
      esac
    done

        -*) ;;
        *) if [ -z "$out" ]; then out="$a"; else src="$a"; fi ;;
      esac
    done
    if [ -n "$src" ]; then gzip -c "$src" > "$out"; else gzip -c > "$out"; fi

problem_statement:
Resource URI templating: route templated URIs to a provider that receives the requested uri
Follow-up to #59/#62, requested by the aimg (proposal-mcp) downstream: their artifacts form a content-addressed namespace (`aimg://result/<uuid5>`), so registering one `MCPResource` per artifact works but is the wrong long-term shape — *"URI templating (provider receives the requested uri, resolves it against the Workspace) is the clean long-term fit... want soon, not blocking"*.

**Current behavior**: `resources/read` matches resources by exact URI string and calls `data_provider()` with zero arguments. Templated/wildcard URIs are not routed (and never were — the docs that implied otherwise were fixed in #62).

**Sketch**:
- A `ResourceTemplate` registration [HIDDEN] carrying an RFC 6570-style `uriTemplate` and a provider that receives the requested URI (or the extracted template variables)
- `resources/read`: exact-URI match first (today's path), then template match
- `resources/templates/list` support for discovery (spec method)
- Provider return contract identical to #62 (`ResourceContents`/vector, String, JSON fallback)

**Spec refs**: resources/templates/list and `uriTemplate` are in the MCP spec's resources section; templating is additive (0.5.x-compatible).

### Additional contract requirements

Resource URI templates: registration, discovery, and read routing.

**Template registration.** Servers can hold resource templates, supplied at
construction (`mcp_server(...; resource_templates = [...])`) or added afterwards with
`register!(server, template)`, which returns the server. Each template carries at
least a `name` and a `uri_template`; `mime_type`, `description`, a human-friendly
`title`, `icons`, and a `_meta` metadata dictionary are optional. A template may also
carry a `data_provider`; a template without one is advertised in listings but cannot
serve reads.

**URI template matching.** A public `match_uri_template(template, uri)` function
matches a URI string against a template containing `{var}` placeholders. It returns
the extracted variable bindings as a dictionary of strings on a full match, and
`nothing` when the URI does not match. Semantics:

- Matching compares the whole URI: literal template characters (including
  regex-significant ones such as `.`) match themselves exactly.
- Each placeholder captures one or more characters but never a `/`.
- Adjacent placeholders with no literal separator (e.g. `{a}{b}`) are ambiguous and
  never match.
- A repeated variable name must capture the same value in every position, otherwise
  the URI does not match.
- A template without placeholders matches only the identical literal URI.

**Read routing and providers.** `resources/read` first resolves the URI against
exact-URI resources; only when no exact resource matches is the URI routed through the
registered templates, and an exact-URI resource always wins over a matching template.
The first matching template that has a provider serves the read; a matching template
without a provider is skipped in favor of later templates. If nothing serves the URI,
the request fails with a resource-not-found error.

arguments — the requested URI and the extracted-variable dictionary; both forms are

problem_statement_base:
Resource URI templating: route templated URIs to a provider that receives the requested uri
Follow-up to #59/#62, requested by the aimg (proposal-mcp) downstream: their artifacts form a content-addressed namespace (`aimg://result/<uuid5>`), so registering one `MCPResource` per artifact works but is the wrong long-term shape — *"URI templating (provider receives the requested uri, resolves it against the Workspace) is the clean long-term fit... want soon, not blocking"*.

**Current behavior**: `resources/read` matches resources by exact URI string and calls `data_provider()` with zero arguments. Templated/wildcard URIs are not routed (and never were — the docs that implied otherwise were fixed in #62).

**Sketch**:
- A `ResourceTemplate` registration [HIDDEN] carrying an RFC 6570-style `uriTemplate` and a provider that receives the requested URI (or the extracted template variables)
- `resources/read`: exact-URI match first (today's path), then template match
- `resources/templates/list` support for discovery (spec method)
- Provider return contract identical to #62 (`ResourceContents`/vector, String, JSON fallback)

**Spec refs**: resources/templates/list and `uriTemplate` are in the MCP spec's resources section; templating is additive (0.5.x-compatible).
contract_addendum:
Resource URI templates: registration, discovery, and read routing.

**Template registration.** Servers can hold resource templates, supplied at
construction (`mcp_server(...; resource_templates = [...])`) or added afterwards with
`register!(server, template)`, which returns the server. Each template carries at
least a `name` and a `uri_template`; `mime_type`, `description`, a human-friendly
`title`, `icons`, and a `_meta` metadata dictionary are optional. A template may also
carry a `data_provider`; a template without one is advertised in listings but cannot
serve reads.

**URI template matching.** A public `match_uri_template(template, uri)` function
matches a URI string against a template containing `{var}` placeholders. It returns
the extracted variable bindings as a dictionary of strings on a full match, and
`nothing` when the URI does not match. Semantics:

- Matching compares the whole URI: literal template characters (including
  regex-significant ones such as `.`) match themselves exactly.
- Each placeholder captures one or more characters but never a `/`.
- Adjacent placeholders with no literal separator (e.g. `{a}{b}`) are ambiguous and
  never match.
- A repeated variable name must capture the same value in every position, otherwise
  the URI does not match.
- A template without placeholders matches only the identical literal URI.

**Read routing and providers.** `resources/read` first resolves the URI against
exact-URI resources; only when no exact resource matches is the URI routed through the
registered templates, and an exact-URI resource always wins over a matching template.
The first matching template that has a provider serves the read; a matching template
without a provider is skipped in favor of later templates. If nothing serves the URI,
the request fails with a resource-not-found error.

A template provider may accept either one argument — the full requested URI — or two
arguments — the requested URI and the extracted-variable dictionary; both forms are
supported and receive those arguments. Provider return values follow the same contract
as plain resources: resource-contents values (or a vector of them) are served
directly, strings become verbatim text content carrying the template's MIME type, and
any other value is JSON-encoded into a text entry. An exception raised by a provider
surfaces as an internal-error response, not as a thrown exception from the request
handling.

**Discovery.** `resources/templates/list` returns a `resourceTemplates` array whose
entries carry `uriTemplate` and `name`, plus `description`, `mimeType`, `title`,
`icons`, and `_meta` whenever those are set on the template (unset optional fields are
omitted). Pagination cursors on the request are accepted.

+"""

+        -> Vector{LittleDict{String,Any}}
+
+Normalize a resource provider's return value into spec `resources/read` contents
+entries: `TextResourceContents`/`BlobResourceContents` (or a vector of them) serialize
+directly — the only path that can produce binary `blob` contents; a `String` becomes
+the text verbatim; anything else (including custom `ResourceContents` subtypes) is
+JSON-encoded into a text entry carrying `fallback_uri`/`fallback_mime`.
+"""
+function normalize_read_contents(data, fallback_uri::String, fallback_mime::String)
+    wire_contents = Union{TextResourceContents,BlobResourceContents}
+    if data isa wire_contents
+        [serialize_resource_contents(data)]
+    elseif data isa Vector && !isempty(data) && all(x -> x isa wire_contents, data)
+        [serialize_resource_contents(x) for x in data]
+    else
+        [LittleDict{String,Any}(
+            "uri" => fallback_uri,
+            "text" => data isa AbstractString ? String(data) : JSON3.write(data),
+            "mimeType" => fallback_mime
+        )]
+    end
+end
+
+_regex_escape(s::AbstractString) =
+    replace(s, r"([\\^\$\.\|\?\*\+\(\)\[\]\{\}])" => s"\\\1")
+
+"""
+    match_uri_template(template::String, uri::String) -> Union{Nothing,Dict{String,String}}
+
+Match `uri` against an RFC 6570 level-1 URI template. Each `{var}` placeholder matches
+one path segment (one or more characters excluding `/`). Returns the extracted
+variables on a full match, `nothing` otherwise.
+
+Deliberate subset of RFC 6570: variable names are `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` (no dotted or
+pct-encoded names); adjacent placeholders with no literal between them (`{a}{b}`) are
+ambiguous and never match; a repeated variable name must capture the same value in
+every position.
+"""
+function match_uri_template(template::String, uri::String)::Union{Nothing,Dict{String,String}}
+    names = String[]
+    pattern = IOBuffer()
+    print(pattern, "^")
+    pos = 1
+    for m in eachmatch(r"\{([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\}", template)
+        # Adjacent placeholders ({a}{b}) have no separator to split the captures
+        # on — ambiguous extraction and a regex-backtracking hazard on
+        # client-controlled URIs. Treat the template as unmatchable.
+        m.offset == pos && !isempty(names) && return nothing
+        print(pattern, _regex_escape(template[pos:prevind(template, m.offset)]))
+        push!(names, String(m.captures[1]))
+        print(pattern, "([^/]+)")
+        pos = m.offset + ncodeunits(m.match)
+    end
+    print(pattern, _regex_escape(template[pos:end]), "\$")
+    mm = match(Regex(String(take!(pattern))), uri)
+    mm === nothing && return nothing
+    vars = Dict{String,String}()
+    for (n, c) in zip(names, mm.captures)
+        v = String(c)
+        # A repeated variable name must capture one consistent value
+        haskey(vars, n) && vars[n] != v && return nothing
+        vars[n] = v
+    end
+    vars
+end
+
