problem_statement:
Name
MathOptComplementarity?

API should look something like:
```julia
using JuMP
import MathOptComplementarity as MOC
model = Model(() -> MOC.Optimizer(Ipopt.Optimizer))
set_attribute(model, MOC.Algorithm(), MOC.SmoothNonlinear())

# potentially

set_attribute(constraint[1], MOC.Algorithm(), MOC.SmoothNonlinear())
set_attribute(constraint[2], MOC.Algorithm(), MOC.BigM(100.0))
```

A good design for inspiration is https://github.com/jump-dev/MultiObjectiveAlgorithms.jl

### Additional contract requirements

## Package name

The package is named `MathOptComplements` and provides the Julia module
`MathOptComplements`. This spelling supersedes any other spelling that may
appear in the task description. Code samples in the task description that
refer to other spellings must be read under this mapping, and the package's
JuMP extension module and the test environment refer to the package under
this name.

## Status of the API sketch in the task description

The code sketch in the task description that mentions an `Algorithm`
attribute, `SmoothNonlinear` algorithm selection, a `BigM` reformulation
with a magnitude parameter, and setting algorithm choices on individual
constraints is an illustrative design sketch only. None of these names are
part of the required API, and no algorithm-selection attribute or
big-M-based reformulation option is required.

## Required ways to use the package

Complementarity constraints are reformulated automatically via
`MathOptInterface` bridges. Two equivalent usage routes are required:

- Wrapping the inner optimizer with `MathOptComplements.Optimizer`, and
- Using a `MathOptInterface` lazy bridge optimizer in which all of the
  package's bridges have been registered with
  `MathOptComplements.Bridges.add_all_bridges`.

Unless stated otherwise below, both routes must behave the same. In
particular, problems involving `MathOptInterface.Complements` constraints
must be solvable through either route, and complementarity constraints whose
left-hand side is an expression (rather than a single variable) must be
reformulated through the vertical formulation using additional slack
variables.

## Reformulation attributes

The required reformulation-selection API consists of these two attributes:

- `MathOptComplements.DefaultComplementarityReformulation`: a model-level
  optimizer attribute that sets the default complementarity relaxation used
  to reformulate all complementarity constraints. It must be supported when
  solving through `MathOptComplements.Optimizer`. It must not be supported
  when solving through a lazy bridge optimizer without
  `MathOptComplements.Optimizer`, even if the package's bridges have been
  registered with `MathOptComplements.Bridges.add_all_bridges`; attempting
  to set it in that case must raise an error.
- `MathOptComplements.ComplementarityReformulation`: a per-constraint
  attribute that overrides the model-wide default for a specific
  complementarity constraint. Setting the attribute stores the value so
  that it is used when the model is optimized; getting the attribute on a
  constraint on which it was set must return the value that was set, both
  before and after `JuMP.optimize!`. Setting it again must overwrite the
  previous value. The per-constraint attribute must be routed through the
  package's bridge chain, including the vertical-formulation path taken when
  the left-hand side of the complementarity constraint is an expression.

When no constraint-specific reformulation is set on a complementarity
constraint, the model-wide default applies to that constraint. When the
model-wide default is not set either, the default is the Scholtes
relaxation with parameter zero.

## Supported relaxations

The following complementarity relaxations must be supported for the
reformulation attributes above and for solving complementarity-constrained
problems with a nonlinear solver such as Ipopt:

- `MathOptComplements.ScholtesRelaxation(tau)`
- `MathOptComplements.FischerBurmeisterRelaxation(tau)`
- `MathOptComplements.LiuFukushimaRelaxation(tau)`
- `MathOptComplements.KanzowSchwarzRelaxation(tau)`

+module MathOptComplementsJuMPExt
+
+import MathOptComplements
+import JuMP
+import MathOptInterface as MOI
+
+function MathOptComplements.Bridges.add_all_bridges(
+    model::JuMP.GenericModel{T},
+    ::Type{U} = T,
+) where {T,U}
+    for BT in (
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.SpecifySetTypeBridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.ComplementsVectorizeBridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.SplitIntervalBridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.FlipSignBridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.ToSOS1Bridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.VerticalBridge,
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.NonlinearBridge,
+    )
+        JuMP.add_bridge(model, BT; coefficient_type = U)
+    end
+    return
+end
+
+end # module MathOptComplementsJuMPExt

+using Test
+using JuMP
+using Ipopt
+using MathOptComplements
+
+function _attribute_test_model()
+    model = Model()
+    @variable(model, x)
+    @variable(model, y >= 0)
+    @objective(model, Min, (x - 1)^2 + y^2)
+    c = @constraint(model, x + 1 ⟂ y)
+    return model, c
+end
+
+# These factories are consistent with `OPTIMIZER_FACTORIES` in `runtests.jl`,
+# except that the inner Ipopt models are instantiated `with_bridge_type`:
+# no JuMP-level caching optimizer is needed so the attributes are forwarded
+# directly to the underlying wrapper.
+const ATTRIBUTE_OPT_FACTORIES = [
+    (
+        "MathOptComplements.Optimizer",
+        () -> MathOptComplements.Optimizer(
+            MOI.instantiate(
+                Ipopt.Optimizer;
+                with_cache_type = Float64,
+                with_bridge_type = Float64,
+            ),
+        ),
+    ),
+    (
+        "LazyBridgeOptimizer + add_all_bridges",
+        () -> begin
+            lazy = MOI.Bridges.full_bridge_optimizer(
+                MOI.instantiate(
+                    Ipopt.Optimizer;
+                    with_cache_type = Float64,
+                    with_bridge_type = Float64,
+                ),
+                Float64,
+            )
+            MathOptComplements.Bridges.add_all_bridges(lazy)
+            return lazy
+        end,
+    ),
+]
+
+@testset "Reformulation attributes" begin
+    @testset "Model-level default reformulation ($(opt_name))" for (opt_name, make_opt) in
+                                                                   ATTRIBUTE_OPT_FACTORIES,
+        relax in [
+            MathOptComplements.ScholtesRelaxation(0.0),
+            MathOptComplements.FischerBurmeisterRelaxation(1e-8),
+        ]
+
+        model, _ = _attribute_test_model()
+        JuMP.set_optimizer(model, make_opt)
+        @test MOI.supports(
+            JuMP.unsafe_backend(model),
+            MathOptComplements.DefaultComplementarityReformulation(),
+        ) == (opt_name == "MathOptComplements.Optimizer")
+        if opt_name == "MathOptComplements.Optimizer"
+            MOI.set(
+                model,
+                MathOptComplements.DefaultComplementarityReformulation(),
+                relax,
+            )
+        else
+            # `DefaultComplementarityReformulation` is only supported by
+            # `MathOptComplements.Optimizer`, not by the plain
+            # `LazyBridgeOptimizer` route.
+            # The contract only requires that setting fails with an error.
+            @test_throws Exception MOI.set(
+                model,
+                MathOptComplements.DefaultComplementarityReformulation(),
+                relax,
+            )
+        end
+        JuMP.set_silent(model)
+        JuMP.optimize!(model)
+        @test JuMP.is_solved_and_feasible(model)
+    end
+
+    @testset "MOI.set/MOI.get per-constraint reformulation ($(opt_name))" for (
+            opt_name,
+            make_opt,
+        ) in ATTRIBUTE_OPT_FACTORIES,
+        relax in [
+            MathOptComplements.ScholtesRelaxation(0.0),
+            MathOptComplements.FischerBurmeisterRelaxation(1e-8),
+            MathOptComplements.LiuFukushimaRelaxation(1e-8),
+            MathOptComplements.KanzowSchwarzRelaxation(1e-8),
+        ]
+
+        model, c = _attribute_test_model()
+        JuMP.set_optimizer(model, make_opt)
+        attr = MathOptComplements.ComplementarityReformulation()
+        # Before the model is optimized, setting the attribute stores the
+        # value so that it is used by `JuMP.optimize!`.
+        MOI.set(model, attr, c, relax)
+        @test MOI.get(model, attr, c) == relax
+        # The attribute can be reset to an overriding value.
+        other = MathOptComplements.ScholtesRelaxation(0.1)
+        MOI.set(model, attr, c, other)
+        @test MOI.get(model, attr, c) == other
+        # Restore the requested value before optimizing.
+        MOI.set(model, attr, c, relax)
+        JuMP.set_silent(model)
+        JuMP.optimize!(model)
+        @test JuMP.is_solved_and_feasible(model)
+        # After the model is optimized, the value can still be read back
+        # from the constraint.
+        @test MOI.get(model, attr, c) == relax
+        @test MOI.supports(JuMP.backend(model), attr, typeof(index(c)))
+    end
+
+    @testset "Per-constraint reformulation attribute support" begin
+        # `MathOptComplements.Optimizer` reports that it supports the
+        # `ComplementarityReformulation` constraint attribute.
+        opt = MathOptComplements.Optimizer(MOI.Utilities.Model{Float64}())
+        x = MOI.add_variable(opt)
+        y = MOI.add_variable(opt)
+        MOI.add_constraint(opt, MOI.VectorOfVariables([x, y]), MOI.Complements(2))
+        @test MOI.supports(
+            opt,
+            MathOptComplements.ComplementarityReformulation(),
+            MOI.ConstraintIndex{MOI.VectorOfVariables,MOI.Complements},
+        )
+        # A `LazyBridgeOptimizer` in which the MathOptComplements bridges have
+        # not been registered with `MathOptComplements.Bridges.add_all_bridges`
+        # does not support the `ComplementarityReformulation` attribute.
+        lazy = MOI.Bridges.full_bridge_optimizer(
+            MOI.Utilities.Model{Float64}(),
+            Float64,
+        )
+        @test !MOI.supports(
+            lazy,
+            MathOptComplements.ComplementarityReformulation(),
+            MOI.ConstraintIndex{MOI.VectorOfVariables,MOI.Complements},
+        )
+    end
+
+end
+
+@testset "Reformulation attribute errors" begin
+    model = MOI.Utilities.Model{Float64}()
+    x = MOI.add_variable(model)
+    y = MOI.add_variable(model)
+    bridge = MOI.Bridges.Constraint.bridge_constraint(
+        MathOptComplements.Bridges.NonlinearBridge{Float64,MOI.Nonnegatives},
+        model,
+        MOI.VectorOfVariables([x, y]),
+        MathOptComplements.ComplementsWithSetType{MOI.Nonnegatives}(2),
+    )
+    attr = MathOptComplements.ComplementarityReformulation()
+    # Setting a value that is not an
+    # `AbstractComplementarityRelaxation` raises an error.
+    @test_throws Exception MOI.set(
+        model,
+        attr,
+        bridge,
+        1.0,
+    )
+    # A valid `AbstractComplementarityRelaxation` value can be set.
+    relax = MathOptComplements.FischerBurmeisterRelaxation(1e-8)
+    MOI.set(model, attr, bridge, relax)
+    @test bridge.reformulation == relax
+end

problem_statement:
Add possibility to remove modules
I.e. (kit/remove-module <module-key>) would do the inverse of kit/install-module

Would be useful in the case of failed experiments with a certain module.

### Additional contract requirements

`kit/remove-module` is a public `kit.api` operation. It must support
`(kit/remove-module module-key)` for a project whose `kit.edn` is in the
current working directory.

For a module that was installed in that project, removal undoes the
installation: the module's generated artifacts are removed and the module is
no longer treated as installed, so installing it again generates its artifacts
again. Removal must leave the project's `kit.edn` and its synced module
repository in place.

No additional removal call forms, options, reports, storage format, or output
wording are required.

+;; --- Module removal ---
+
+(defn- check-file-status
+  "Checks whether a file created by module installation can be safely removed.
+   Returns :safe if unchanged (SHA matches), :modified if changed, :missing if deleted."
+  [{:keys [target sha256]}]
+  (let [f (jio/file target)]
+    (cond
+      (not (.exists f))
+      :missing
+
+      (nil? sha256)
+      :modified
+
+      :else
+      (let [current-sha (modules-log/sha256
+                         (java.nio.file.Files/readAllBytes (.toPath f)))]
+        (if (= sha256 current-sha)
+          :safe
+          :modified)))))
+
+(defn- find-dependents
+  "Returns the set of installed module keys that depend on target-key.
+   Resolves each installed module using the feature flag it was installed with."
+  [ctx target-key]
+  (let [modules-root (modules/root ctx)
+        log (modules-log/read-modules-log modules-root)
+        installed-keys (->> log
+                            (filter (fn [[_ entry]]
+                                      (let [status (if (map? entry) (:status entry) entry)]
+                                        (= :success status))))
+                            keys)
+        ;; Build opts map with each module's stored feature-flag
+        resolve-opts (->> installed-keys
+                          (map (fn [mk]
+                                 (let [entry (get log mk)
+                                       ff (if (map? entry)
+                                            (:feature-flag entry :default)
+                                            :default)]
+                                   [mk {:feature-flag ff}])))
+                          (into {}))
+        loaded-ctx (modules/load-modules ctx resolve-opts)]
+    (deps/immediate-dependents loaded-ctx installed-keys target-key)))
+
+(defn removal-report
+  "Generates a removal report for an installed module. Returns a map with:
+   - :module-key
+   - :has-manifest? (whether detailed installation manifest is available)
+   - :safe-to-remove (files that can be auto-deleted, SHA matches)
+   - :modified-files (files modified since installation)
+   - :missing-files (files deleted since installation)
+   - :manual-steps (human-readable injection removal instructions)
+   - :dependents (installed modules that depend on this one)
+   Returns nil if the module is not installed."
+  ([module-key]
+   (removal-report module-key default-edn {}))
+  ([module-key opts]
+   (removal-report module-key default-edn opts))
+  ([module-key kit-edn-path opts]
+   (let [ctx (read-ctx kit-edn-path)
+         modules-root (modules/root ctx)
+         log (modules-log/read-modules-log modules-root)
+         entry (get log module-key)]
+     (when entry
+       (let [manifest? (map? entry)
+             manifest (when manifest? entry)
+             dependents (try
+                          (find-dependents ctx module-key)
+                          (catch Exception e
+                            (println "WARNING: error resolving dependents:" (.getMessage e))
+                            #{}))]
+         (if manifest?
+           ;; New format: detailed manifest with SHA comparison
+           (let [file-statuses (map (fn [asset]
+                                      (assoc asset :file-status (check-file-status asset)))
+                                    (:assets manifest))
+                 safe (vec (keep #(when (= :safe (:file-status %)) (:target %)) file-statuses))
+                 modified (vec (keep #(when (= :modified (:file-status %))
+                                        {:path (:target %) :reason "content changed since installation"})
+                                     file-statuses))
+                 missing (vec (keep #(when (= :missing (:file-status %)) (:target %)) file-statuses))
+                 manual-steps (mapv :description (:injections manifest))]
+             {:module-key module-key
+              :has-manifest? true
+              :safe-to-remove safe
+              :modified-files modified
+              :missing-files missing
+              :manual-steps manual-steps
+              :dependents dependents})
+           ;; Old format: best-effort report from module config on disk
+           (let [loaded-ctx (try (modules/load-modules ctx) (catch Exception _ nil))
+                 descriptions (when loaded-ctx
+                                (try
+                                  (let [module (modules/lookup-module loaded-ctx module-key)]
+                                    (generator/describe-actions module))
+                                  (catch Exception _ nil)))]
+             {:module-key module-key
+              :has-manifest? false
+              :safe-to-remove []
+              :modified-files []
+              :manual-steps (vec (or descriptions
+                                     ["Module config not found. Review your project files manually."]))
+              :dependents dependents})))))))
+
+(defn print-removal-report
+  "Prints a human-readable removal report for an installed module."
+  ([module-key]
+   (print-removal-report module-key default-edn {}))
+  ([module-key opts]
+   (print-removal-report module-key default-edn opts))
+  ([module-key kit-edn-path opts]
+   (let [report (removal-report module-key kit-edn-path opts)]
+     (if (nil? report)
+       (println "Module" module-key "is not installed.")
+       (do
+         (println "REMOVAL REPORT for" (:module-key report))
+         (println)
+         (when (seq (:dependents report))
+           (println "WARNING: The following installed modules depend on" module-key ":")
+           (doseq [dep (:dependents report)]
+             (println " " dep))
+           (println "Consider removing those first.")
+           (println))
+         (when (seq (:safe-to-remove report))
+           (println "FILES (safe to auto-remove, unchanged since installation):")
+           (doseq [f (:safe-to-remove report)]
+             (println "  DELETE" f))
+           (println))
+         (when (seq (:modified-files report))
+           (println "FILES (modified since installation, review before deleting):")
+           (doseq [{:keys [path reason]} (:modified-files report)]
+             (println "  REVIEW" path "-" reason))
+           (println))
+         (when (seq (:missing-files report))
+           (println "FILES (already deleted, no action needed):")
+           (doseq [f (:missing-files report)]
+             (println "  GONE" f))
+           (println))
+         (when (seq (:manual-steps report))
+           (println "MANUAL STEPS (undo code injections):")
+           (doseq [step (:manual-steps report)]
+             (println "  -" step))
+           (println))
+         (when-not (:has-manifest? report)
+           (println "NOTE: This module was installed before removal tracking was added.")
+           (println "      The above report is based on the module config and may not be")
+           (println "      perfectly accurate. SHA comparison is not available.")
+           (println)))))))
+
+(defn remove-module
+  "Removes a module from the project. Auto-deletes files that are unchanged
+   since installation. Prints instructions for manual cleanup of injections.
+
+   Options:
+     :force? - remove even if other modules depend on it
+     :dry?   - only print the removal report, don't delete anything"
+  ([module-key]
+   (remove-module module-key default-edn {}))
+  ([module-key opts]
+   (remove-module module-key default-edn opts))
+  ([module-key kit-edn-path {:keys [force? dry?] :as opts}]
+   (let [report (removal-report module-key kit-edn-path opts)]
+     (cond
+       (nil? report)
+       (println "ERROR: Module" module-key "is not installed.")
+
+       (and (seq (:dependents report)) (not force?))
+       (do (println "ERROR: Cannot remove" module-key
+                    "because the following modules depend on it:")
+           (doseq [dep (:dependents report)]
+             (println " " dep))
+           (println "Use :force? true to override."))
+
+       dry?
+       (print-removal-report module-key kit-edn-path opts)
+
+       :else
+       (do
+         ;; Auto-delete safe files
+         (doseq [f (:safe-to-remove report)]
+           (println "Deleting" f)
+           (jio/delete-file (jio/file f) true))
+
+         ;; Report modified files
+         (when (seq (:modified-files report))
+           (println)
+           (println "The following files were modified since installation.")
+           (println "Please review and delete manually:")
+           (doseq [{:keys [path]} (:modified-files report)]
+             (println "  -" path)))
+
+         ;; Report manual injection steps
+         (when (seq (:manual-steps report))
+           (println)
+           (println "The following code was injected into existing files.")
+           (println "Please remove manually:")
+           (doseq [step (:manual-steps report)]
+             (println "  -" step)))
+
+         ;; Remove from install log
+         (let [ctx (read-ctx kit-edn-path)]
+           (modules-log/untrack-module ctx module-key))
+
+         (println)
+         (println "Module" module-key "has been uninstalled."))))
+   :done))
+

+(defn sha256

+
+(defn build-installation-manifest
+  "Builds a detailed manifest of what a module installation did.
+   Called after successful generation to persist the record for later removal.
+   Note: SHA-256 hashes are computed from on-disk state after generation completes."
+  [ctx {:module/keys [resolved-config]} feature-flag]
+  (let [{:keys [actions hooks]} resolved-config
+        rendered-assets (for [asset (:assets actions)
+                             :when (and (sequential? asset) (>= (count asset) 2))]
+                          (let [[_ target-path] asset
+                                rendered-target (renderer/render-template ctx target-path)
+                                target-file (jio/file rendered-target)]
+                            (cond-> {:target rendered-target}
+                              (.exists target-file)
+                              (assoc :sha256 (sha256 (slurp-bytes rendered-target))))))
+        rendered-injections (for [inj (:injections actions)]
+                              (let [rendered-path (renderer/render-template ctx (:path inj))]
+                                {:type (:type inj)
+                                 :action (:action inj)
+                                 :path rendered-path
+                                 :description (describe-injection-for-removal
+                                               (assoc inj :path rendered-path))}))]
+    (cond-> {:status :success
+             :installed-at (str (Instant/now))
+             :feature-flag feature-flag
+             :assets (vec rendered-assets)
+             :injections (vec rendered-injections)}
+      (seq hooks)
+      (assoc :hooks (vec (for [[hook-type commands] hooks]
+                           {:type hook-type :commands (vec commands)}))))))
+
+(defn record-installation
+  "Records a module installation in the log with a detailed manifest or failure status."
+  [ctx module-key manifest]
+  (let [modules-root (modules/root ctx)
+        install-log (read-modules-log modules-root)]
+    (write-modules-log modules-root (assoc install-log module-key manifest))))
+
+(defn module-manifest
+  "Retrieves the detailed installation manifest for a module.
+   Returns nil for modules installed before manifest tracking was added."
+  [ctx module-key]
+  (let [modules-root (modules/root ctx)
+        entry (get (read-modules-log modules-root) module-key)]
+    (when (map? entry) entry)))
+
+(defn untrack-module
+  "Removes a module entry from the installation log."
+  [ctx module-key]
+  (let [modules-root (modules/root ctx)
+        install-log (read-modules-log modules-root)]
+    (write-modules-log modules-root (dissoc install-log module-key))))

+          (spit default-edn original)
+          (jio/delete-file default-edn true))))))
+
+(defn- remove-module-quietly
+  "Calls the public single-argument removal entry point, returning its result.
+   Printed output (status or manual-cleanup instructions) is ignored: the
+   contract requires no specific output wording."
+  [module-key]

+  (let [project-edn (prepare-project "test/resources/modules")
+        artifact    (jio/file project-root "resources/public/css/app.css")
+        module-file (jio/file project-root "modules/kit/meta/config.edn")]
+    (with-default-project
+      project-edn
+      (fn [default-edn]
+        (kit/install-module :meta project-edn {})
+        (is (.exists artifact) "installation must create a module artifact")
+        (remove-module-quietly :meta)
+        (is (not (.exists artifact)) "removal must delete the generated artifact")
+        (is (.exists default-edn) "removal must not delete the project configuration")
+        (is (.exists module-file) "removal must not delete the synced module repository")
+        (kit/install-module :meta project-edn {})
+        (is (.exists artifact) "a removed module must be installable again")))))
+
+(deftest remove-module-cleans-up-a-multi-action-installation
+  (let [project-edn (prepare-project "test/resources/modules")
+        system-file (jio/file project-root "resources/system.edn")
+        core-file   (jio/file project-root "src/myapp/core.clj")
+        module-file (jio/file project-root "modules/kit/html/config.edn")
+        artifacts   [(jio/file project-root "resources/public/home.html")
+                     (jio/file project-root "resources/public/img/luminus.png")
+                     (jio/file project-root "src/clj/myapp/web/routes/pages.clj")]]
+    ;; The HTML module combines several generated assets with
+    ;; installation-time edits to existing EDN and Clojure project files.
+    (with-default-project
+      project-edn
+      (fn [default-edn]
+        ;; The module injects into project files that already exist.
+        (clone-file "test/resources/sample-system.edn" system-file)
+        (clone-file "test/resources/core.clj" core-file)
+        (kit/install-module :html project-edn {})
+        (doseq [artifact artifacts]
+          (is (.exists artifact)
+              (str "installation must create " (.getPath artifact))))
+
+        (let [result (remove-module-quietly :html)]
+          (is (some? result) "removal must not throw")
+          ;; Generated artifacts are gone, while the project
+          ;; configuration, the synced module repository, and editable
+          ;; project files that predate the installation are retained.
+          (doseq [artifact artifacts]
+            (is (not (.exists artifact))
+                (str "removal must delete " (.getPath artifact))))
+          (is (.exists default-edn)
+              "removal must retain the project configuration")
+          (is (.exists module-file)
+              "removal must retain the synced module repository")
+          (is (.exists system-file)
+              "removal must not delete an editable EDN project file")
+          (is (.exists core-file)
+              "removal must not delete an editable Clojure project file")
+          (is (.exists default-edn)
+              "removal must retain the project configuration")
+
+          ;; The module is no longer treated as installed, so installing
+          ;; it again re-generates its artifacts from scratch. Because
+          ;; removal deleted the artifact directories and the injected
+          ;; system.edn (neither re-created by reinstall), the regenerated
+          ;; artifacts cannot be residue left behind by removal, while any
+          ;; leftover injected entries are ones a fresh installation skips.
+          (kit/install-module :html project-edn {})
+          (doseq [artifact artifacts]
+            (is (.exists artifact)
+                (str "a removed module must generate " (.getPath artifact)
+                     " again on reinstall"))))))))
+
+(deftest remove-module-handles-a-pre-existing-artifact-path
+  (let [project-edn (prepare-project "test/resources/modules")
+        artifact    (jio/file project-root "resources/public/css/app.css")
+        module-file (jio/file project-root "modules/kit/meta/config.edn")
+        user-content ".app { color: red; }"]
+    (with-default-project
+      project-edn
+      (fn [default-edn]
+        ;; The user created this file at the artifact path before the module
+        ;; was ever installed; installing overwrites it with generated content.
+        (jio/make-parents artifact)
+        (spit artifact user-content)
+        (kit/install-module :meta project-edn {})
+        (let [result (remove-module-quietly :meta)]
+          (is (some? result) "removal must not throw")
+          (is (.exists default-edn)
+              "removal must retain the project configuration")
+          (is (.exists module-file)
+              "removal must retain the synced module repository")
+          ;; A contract-consistent outcome for the overwritten path: removal
+          ;; either deletes the generated artifact or leaves the path
+          ;; readable for the user to clean up.
+          (is (if (.exists artifact) (some? (slurp artifact)) true)
+              "the pre-existing artifact path must be deleted cleanly or left with readable content"))))))

problem_statement:
Set `WasmWasi` platform for Analysis API
Dokka does not differentiate between `wasmWasi` and `wasmJs`, [it just sets the platform to `unspecifiedWasmPlatform`](https://github.com/Kotlin/dokka/blob/master/dokka-subprojects/analysis-kotlin-symbols/src/main/kotlin/org/jetbrains/dokka/analysis/kotlin/symbols/plugin/KotlinAnalysis.kt#L33)
However, this affects analysis because the default imports are different:
https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/blob/master/analysis/analysis-api/testData/imports/defaultImportProvider/wasmJs.default.txt
https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/blob/master/analysis/analysis-api/testData/imports/defaultImportProvider/wasmWasi.default.txt

For example, it leads to 
```kt
// wasmWasi sourceset
@ExperimentalWasmInterop // is unresolved in Dokka
```

We can consider extending `org.jetbrains.dokka.Platform`.
~~Alternatively, we could treat wasmWasi as js. Does the DGP already do this?~~

### Additional contract requirements

The public platform model distinguishes the WebAssembly JavaScript and WebAssembly System Interface targets in addition to the existing targets.

- Platform parsing recognizes the strings "wasmJs" and "wasmWasi" (matching is case-insensitive) and maps them to two distinct platform values whose string keys lowercase to "wasmjs" and "wasmwasi" respectively. Every supported platform key remains unique across all platforms.
- Parsing continues to support the previously recognized strings "jvm", "js", "native", "common", "androidJvm", "android", and "metadata", and still fails when given an unrecognized platform string.
- When a source set targets the WebAssembly System Interface (wasmWasi), code analysis must use the wasmWasi analysis target and its default imports rather than an unspecified or generic WebAssembly target, so that declarations only available through wasmWasi default imports (such as those requiring `ExperimentalWasmInterop`) resolve.

+/*
+ * Copyright 2014-2024 JetBrains s.r.o. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.
+ */
+
+package org.jetbrains.dokka
+
+import java.io.File
+import kotlin.test.Test
+import kotlin.test.assertEquals
+import kotlin.test.assertFails
+import kotlin.test.assertNotEquals
+
+class PlatformTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should distinguish WasmJs and WasmWasi platforms`() {
+        val wasmJs = Platform.fromString("wasmJs")
+        val wasmWasi = Platform.fromString("wasmWasi")
+
+        assertNotEquals(wasmJs, wasmWasi, "wasmJs and wasmWasi are different platforms with different default imports")
+        assertEquals("wasmjs", wasmJs.key.toLowerCase())
+        assertEquals("wasmwasi", wasmWasi.key.toLowerCase())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should parse platform strings case insensitively`() {
+        assertEquals(Platform.fromString("wasmJs"), Platform.fromString("WASMJS"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.fromString("wasmWasi"), Platform.fromString("wasmwasi"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.jvm, Platform.fromString("JVM"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.js, Platform.fromString("Js"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.native, Platform.fromString("NATIVE"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.common, Platform.fromString("Common"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should keep parsing previously supported platform strings`() {
+        assertEquals(Platform.jvm, Platform.fromString("jvm"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.js, Platform.fromString("js"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.native, Platform.fromString("native"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.common, Platform.fromString("common"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.jvm, Platform.fromString("androidJvm"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.jvm, Platform.fromString("android"))
+        assertEquals(Platform.common, Platform.fromString("metadata"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should fail for an unrecognized platform`() {
+        assertFails {
+            Platform.fromString("delphi")
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should have a unique key for every platform`() {
+        val keys = Platform.values().map { it.key }
+        assertEquals(keys.size, keys.distinct().size, "every Platform must have a unique key")
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `should resolve declarations available through wasmWasi default imports`() {
+        val analysisRuntime = analysisSymbolsJar()
+        val classpath = analysisRuntime.absolutePath + File.pathSeparator + System.getProperty("java.class.path")
+        val process = ProcessBuilder(
+            File(System.getProperty("java.home"), "bin/java").absolutePath,
+            "-cp",
+            classpath,
+            "org.jetbrains.dokka.WasmWasiAnalysisProbe"
+        )
+            .redirectErrorStream(true)
+            .start()
+        val output = process.inputStream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
+        assertEquals(0, process.waitFor(), "wasmWasi analysis probe failed:\n$output")
+    }
+
+    private fun analysisSymbolsJar(): File {
+        val repositoryRoot = generateSequence(File(System.getProperty("user.dir"))) { it.parentFile }
+            .first { File(it, "gradlew").isFile }
+        val outputDirectory = File(repositoryRoot, "dokka-subprojects/analysis-kotlin-symbols/build/shadowLibs")
+
+        val process = ProcessBuilder(
+            File(repositoryRoot, "gradlew").absolutePath,
+            ":dokka-subprojects:analysis-kotlin-symbols:shadowJar",
+            "--console=plain",
+            "-Porg.jetbrains.dokka.integration_test.skip=true"
+        )
+            .directory(repositoryRoot)
+            .redirectErrorStream(true)
+            .start()
+        val output = process.inputStream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
+        assertEquals(0, process.waitFor(), "Unable to prepare the analysis test runtime:\n$output")
+
+        return requireNotNull(
+            outputDirectory.listFiles()?.singleOrNull { it.extension == "jar" }
+        ) { "The analysis test runtime was not produced" }
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+/*
+ * Copyright 2014-2024 JetBrains s.r.o. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.
+ */
+
+package org.jetbrains.dokka
+
+import org.jetbrains.dokka.model.Annotations
+import org.jetbrains.dokka.model.DModule
+import org.jetbrains.dokka.utilities.DokkaLogger
+import testApi.testRunner.dokkaConfiguration
+import java.io.File
+
+/** Runs in an isolated JVM whose classpath contains the Analysis API runtime. */
+internal object WasmWasiAnalysisProbe {
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun main(args: Array<String>) {
+        try {
+            runProbe()
+            kotlin.system.exitProcess(0)
+        } catch (failure: Throwable) {
+            failure.printStackTrace()
+            kotlin.system.exitProcess(1)
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun runProbe() {
+        val usageResource = requireNotNull(
+            WasmWasiAnalysisProbe::class.java.getResource(
+                "/wasm-wasi-analysis/sample/ExperimentalWasmInteropUsage.kt"
+            )
+        )
+        val sourceRoot = File(usageResource.toURI()).parentFile.parentFile
+        val configuration = dokkaConfiguration {
+            moduleName = "wasm-wasi-analysis-test"
+            sourceSets {
+                sourceSet {
+                    name = "wasmWasi"
+                    displayName = "wasmWasi"
+                    sourceRoots = listOf(sourceRoot.absolutePath)
+                    analysisPlatform = "wasmWasi"
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        val sourceSet = configuration.sourceSets.single()
+        System.setProperty("org.jetbrains.dokka.analysis.allowKotlinPackage", "true")
+
+        val analysisFacade = Class.forName(
+            "org.jetbrains.dokka.analysis.kotlin.symbols.plugin.KotlinAnalysisKt"
+        )
+        val disposableClass = Class.forName("com.intellij.openapi.Disposable")
+        val disposable = Class.forName("com.intellij.openapi.util.Disposer")
+            .getMethod("newDisposable")
+            .invoke(null)
+        val analysis = analysisFacade
+            .getMethod(
+                "createAnalysisSession",
+                List::class.java,
+                DokkaLogger::class.java,
+                disposableClass,
+                Boolean::class.javaPrimitiveType
+            )
+            .invoke(null, configuration.sourceSets, NoOpLogger, disposable, false)
+
+        try {
+            val visitorClass = Class.forName(
+                "org.jetbrains.dokka.analysis.kotlin.symbols.translators.DokkaSymbolVisitor"
+            )
+            val visitor = visitorClass.constructors.single { it.parameterCount == 5 }
+                .newInstance(sourceSet, configuration.moduleName, analysis, NoOpLogger, null)
+            val module = visitorClass.getMethod("visitModule").invoke(visitor) as DModule
+            val usage = module.packages
+                .single { it.packageName == "sample" }
+                .functions
+                .single { it.name == "wasmWasiDefaultImportDeclaration" }
+            val annotation = requireNotNull(
+                usage.extra[Annotations]
+                    ?.directAnnotations
+                    ?.values
+                    ?.flatten()
+                    ?.singleOrNull()
+            ) { "the default-import annotation did not resolve during analysis" }
+
+            check(annotation.dri.packageName == "kotlin.wasm") {
+                "unexpected annotation package: ${annotation.dri}"
+            }
+            check(annotation.dri.classNames == "ExperimentalWasmInterop") {
+                "unexpected annotation class: ${annotation.dri}"
+            }
+        } finally {
+            analysis.javaClass.getMethod("close").invoke(analysis)
+        }
+    }
+
+    private object NoOpLogger : DokkaLogger {
+        override var warningsCount: Int = 0
+        override var errorsCount: Int = 0
+
+        override fun debug(message: String) = Unit
+        override fun info(message: String) = Unit
+        override fun progress(message: String) = Unit
+        override fun warn(message: String) {
+            warningsCount++
+        }
+
+        override fun error(message: String) {
+            errorsCount++
+        }
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Error Navigating from Neovim command-line window (and silent horizontal Herdr resize failures)
### Description

## Problem

When Neovim's command-line window is active (`q:`), herdr-splits does not handle navigation or orizontal resizing correctly.

### Navigation

All four navigation commands produce an `E11` notification:

```text
herdr-splits: move_cursor_left failed: [string "vim/_core/editor"]:355:nvim_exec2(), line 1: Vim(wincmd):E11: Invalid in command-line window; <CR> executes, CTRL-C quits
```

The same error occurs for left, right, up, and down navigation.

This appears to happen because nav.move_cursor() executes :wincmd, which Neovim prohibits while the command-line window is active.

### Resize

Behavior from the command-line window is:

- Resize up/down works and resizes the command-line window
- Resize left/right does not resize the surrounding Herdr pane
- No useful action or error is produced for left/right

The command-line window appears to be treated as an ignored nofile buffer, preventing horizontal resize from being delegated to Herdr.

### Tested with:

- herdr-splits.nvim commit 19b9782 (latest main)
- Neovim v0.12.4
- Herdr 0.7.4
- lazy.nvim
- macOS 15.7.8

## Proposed Solution

[HIDDEN]
Suggested behavior:

- Navigation should not attempt :wincmd from the command-line window
- Since Neovim cannot switch windows while it is active, navigation should delegate directly to Herdr when possible and otherwise respect the configured edge behavior
- Horizontal resizing should delegate to Herdr when the command-line window spans the Neovim pane's full width
- Vertical resizing should preserve the existing behavior of resizing the command-line window

The command-line window may need to be handled separately from generic ignored nofile buffers.

## Scope

This issue is limited to special handling of Neovim's command-line window, including command and search history variants such as q:, q/, and q?.

No change is requested to the general handling of ordinary ignored nofile buffers or sidebars.

### Neovim version

NVIM v0.12.4

### Plugin manager

lazy.nvim

### Herdr version

herdr 0.7.4

### herdr-splits.nvim version

herdr-splits.nvim commit 19b9782 (latest main)

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Neovim inside a Herdr pane
2. Ensure another Herdr pane is available in at least one direction
3. Open Neovim's command-line history window with q:
4. Press each configured navigation key:
 - `<C-h>`
 - `<C-j>`
 - `<C-k>`
 - `<C-l>`
5. Observe an E11 notification for every direction
6. Press the configured resize keys:
 - `<M-j>` and `<M-k>` resize the command-line window
 - `<M-h>` and `<M-l>` do not resize the Herdr pane

### Expected behaviour

- Navigation in all four directions from q: no longer produces E11
- Navigation can leave the Neovim pane through Herdr when a destination pane exists
- Edge behavior remains consistent with nav_at_edge
- Horizontal resize from a full-width command-line window resizes the surrounding Herdr pane
- Vertical resize continues to resize the command-line window
- Normal Neovim windows, sidebars, floating windows, and other ignored nofile buffers retain their current behavior
- Automated tests cover navigation and resizing while vim.fn.getcmdwintype() indicates an active command-line window

### Actual behaviour

## navigation

From the command-line window, all four navigation commands produce an `E11` notification:
```text
herdr-splits: move_cursor_left failed: [string "vim/_core/editor"]:355:
nvim_exec2(), line 1: Vim(wincmd):E11: Invalid in command-line window;
<CR> executes, CTRL-C quits
```
- The same error occurs for left, right, up, and down navigation.
- This appears to happen because nav.move_cursor() executes :wincmd, which Neovim prohibits while the command-line window is active.

## resize

From the command-line window:
- Resize up/down works and resizes the command-line window
- Resize left/right does not resize the surrounding Herdr pane
  - No useful action, notification or error is produced for left/right

The command-line window appears to be treated as an ignored nofile buffer, preventing horizontal resize from being delegated to Herdr.

### :checkhealth herdr-splits output

```shell
herdr-splits:                                                               â

herdr-splits ~
- â OK Running inside a Herdr session (HERDR_ENV=1, HERDR_PANE_ID=w1F:p1)
- ignored_buftypes: { "nofile", "quickfix", "prompt", "help", "terminal" }
- ignored_filetypes: { "NvimTree", "neo-tree", "snacks_dashboard", "snacks_explorer", "snacks_picker", "dadbod-ui", "dbout", "aerial", "Outline", "Trouble", "quickfix" }
- floating_zindex_max: 50
- ignore_previewwindows: false
- Current window matches an ignored filetype/buftype.

note: it always seems to report "Current window matches an ignored filetype/buftype" - even though its functioning normally
```

### Setup / config

```lua

  -- For local development, swap the repo line for `dir = '/path/to/herdr-splits'`

  config = function()
    require('herdr-splits').setup {
      -- Defaults shown. All fields optional.
      default_amount = 0.03, -- Herdr resize ratio
      neovim_amount = 3, -- Neovim resize cells
      at_edge = 'wrap', -- 'wrap' | 'stop' | 'split' | function
      ignored_buftypes = { 'nofile', 'quickfix', 'prompt', 'help', 'terminal' },
      ignored_filetypes = {
        'NvimTree',
        -- sidebars

    { '<M-j>', function() require('herdr-splits').resize_down() end, desc = 'Resize down' },
    { '<M-k>', function() require('herdr-splits').resize_up() end, desc = 'Resize up' },

```

### OS / terminal

macOS 15.7.8
 
Ghostty 
- confirmed `macos-option-as-alt = true`
- Version
  - version: 1.3.2-main-+73534c468
  - channel: tip

### Additional contract requirements

While Neovim's command-line window (`q:`, `q/`, or `q?`, as reported by the
runtime command-line-window state getter) is open, the plugin must honor all
of the following observable behaviors; no other window kind may change
behavior:

- Navigation (left/right/up/down) never issues a `wincmd` and never changes
  the current Neovim window.
- When the current Herdr pane has a neighboring pane in the requested
  direction, navigation focuses that neighboring pane.
- When the current Herdr pane is at its layout edge in the requested
  direction, navigation honors the configured pane-boundary behavior: with
  wrapping enabled it focuses the Herdr pane on the reverse side; with
  wrapping stopped it does nothing.
- When no Herdr session is active, or there is a Neovim neighbor in the
  requested direction (the Neovim edge is not reached), navigation does
  nothing and contacts no Herdr boundary. Unzoom-on-navigation may still be
  preserved by an implementation while the command-line window is active.
- Horizontal resize keeps delegating to the Herdr pane even though the
  command-line window is an ignored `nofile` buffer, provided the window
  otherwise fills the terminal width and sits at both horizontal Neovim
  edges. Ordinary ignored `nofile` sidebars must still never delegate
  resizes.
- Vertical resize from the command-line window remains native Neovim window
  resizing and is never delegated to the Herdr pane.

The command-line-window handling must not alter behavior in normal buffers,
ordinary sidebars, floating windows, or any other window: navigation no-op
edge behavior and sidebar resize suppression stay exactly as before when no
command-line window is active.

Test support note: `tests/rebench_reporter.lua` is a MiniTest reporter that
prints one `Success || <name>` / `Fail || <name>` line per case for the
evaluation log parser while preserving MiniTest's failure exit status.

contract_addendum:
While Neovim's command-line window (`q:`, `q/`, or `q?`, as reported by the
runtime command-line-window state getter) is open, the plugin must honor all
of the following observable behaviors; no other window kind may change
behavior:

- Navigation (left/right/up/down) never issues a `wincmd` and never changes
  the current Neovim window.
- When the current Herdr pane has a neighboring pane in the requested
  direction, navigation focuses that neighboring pane.
- When the current Herdr pane is at its layout edge in the requested
  direction, navigation honors the configured pane-boundary behavior: with
  wrapping enabled it focuses the Herdr pane on the reverse side; with
  wrapping stopped it does nothing.
- When no Herdr session is active, or there is a Neovim neighbor in the
  requested direction (the Neovim edge is not reached), navigation does
  nothing and contacts no Herdr boundary. Unzoom-on-navigation may still be
  preserved by an implementation while the command-line window is active.
- Horizontal resize keeps delegating to the Herdr pane even though the
  command-line window is an ignored `nofile` buffer, provided the window
  otherwise fills the terminal width and sits at both horizontal Neovim
  edges. Ordinary ignored `nofile` sidebars must still never delegate
  resizes.
- Vertical resize from the command-line window remains native Neovim window
  resizing and is never delegated to the Herdr pane.

The command-line-window handling must not alter behavior in normal buffers,
ordinary sidebars, floating windows, or any other window: navigation no-op
edge behavior and sidebar resize suppression stay exactly as before when no
command-line window is active.

@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+-- Rebench per-test reporter for the parse_log_lua_nvim execution parser.
+--
+-- MiniTest's default stdout reporter only prints progress symbols and an
+-- aggregate summary ("Fails (n) and Notes (m)"), which the rebench log parser
+-- cannot turn into per-test results. This reporter wraps the default stdout
+-- reporter (so the normal MiniTest output is preserved) and, after the run,
+-- additionally prints one machine-readable line per executed case at column
+-- zero:
+--
+--   Success || <stable unique test name>
+--   Fail || <stable unique test name>
+--
+-- Each status is derived from the case's real execution result
+-- (`case.exec.fails`), so the lines reflect genuine outcomes. The process
+-- still exits non-zero (via `1cquit`) whenever any case fails, exactly like
+-- the default reporter.
+--
+-- Usage:
+--   MiniTest.run({ execute = { reporter = dofile('tests/rebench_reporter.lua') } })
+-- The path is relative to the current working directory (the repo root).
+
+local default = MiniTest.gen_reporter.stdout({ group_depth = 2, quit_on_finish = false })
+
+local all_cases
+
+local function has_fails(cases)
+  for _, case in ipairs(cases) do
+    if type(case.exec) == 'table' and #(case.exec.fails or {}) > 0 then
+      return true
+    end
+  end
+  return false
+end
+
+local reporter = {}
+
+function reporter.start(cases)
+  all_cases = cases
+  return default.start(cases)
+end
+
+function reporter.update(case_num)
+  return default.update(case_num)
+end
+
+function reporter.finish()
+  default.finish()
+
+  for _, case in ipairs(all_cases or {}) do
+    -- case.desc is { <file path>, <test name>, ... }; drop the file path so
+    -- the emitted name is the stable unique test name.
+    local name = table.concat(vim.list_slice(case.desc, 2), ' | ')
+    local fails = (type(case.exec) == 'table' and case.exec.fails) or {}
+    local status = (#fails == 0) and 'Success' or 'Fail'
+    io.stdout:write(string.format('%s || %s\n', status, name))
+  end
+  io.flush()
+
+  local code = has_fails(all_cases or {}) and 1 or 0
+  vim.cmd('silent! ' .. code .. 'cquit')
+end
+
+return reporter

problem_statement:
DEV: Make write-file-range atomic with sequential position recalculation
Depends-on: 
Base-branch: main
Final: false

## Problem Statement

The current `write-file-range` implementation has a critical bug when multiple ranges are specified:

**Current behavior (BROKEN):**
```haskell
-- File has 100 lines
write_file_range(path="File.hs", ranges="1-10,20-30", content="A---B")

-- Step 1: Replace lines 1-10 with content "A" 
-- File now has 90 lines (removed 10, added say 5)

-- Step 2: Replace lines 20-30 with content "B"
-- PROBLEM: Lines 20-30 from ORIGINAL file no longer exist!
-- What was line 20 is now line 15 due to Step 1
```

This causes severe file corruption as documented in session analysis:
- Lines written to wrong locations
- Duplicate function definitions
- Stray code blocks from previous edits

## Root Cause in Current Code

In `DeveloperToolbox.hs` lines 674+, the current implementation:

[HIDDEN]

The `sortOn` approach assumes ranges don't affect each other, but they do!

## Proposed Solution

**Replace the entire algorithm** with sequential position tracking:

[HIDDEN]

**Key insight**: When editing top-to-bottom, each edit affects line numbers for subsequent edits in a predictable way.

## Detailed Algorithm

### For Edit Sequence: Replace 1-10, then 20-30

```
Original file: 100 lines
Edit 1: Replace lines 1-10 with 5 lines of new content
  -> File now has 95 lines (removed 10, added 5 = -5 net)
  
Edit 2: Target was "original line 20", now it's at line 15
  -> Adjust: 20 - 10 + 5 = 15
  -> Replace lines 15-25 (was 20-30, shifted by -5)
  -> File now has 90 lines (removed 11 from 15-25, added say 5)
```

### Adjustment Formula

[HIDDEN]

## Implementation Plan

### Option A: Replace `executeWriteFileRange` entirely

Modify existing function to be atomic. This is **breaking** if anyone relies on current behavior, but current behavior is broken anyway.

```haskell
executeWriteFileRange ::
    Tracer IO Trace ->
    Toolbox ->
    FilePath ->
    Text ->      -- ^ ranges (single range recommended, multi-range with position tracking)
    Text ->      -- ^ content (single block, "---" separator deprecated)
    IO (Either DeveloperToolError WriteFileRangeResult)
```

**Changes needed:**

1. **Remove** the `sortOn (negate . rangeStartKey)` logic
2. **Add** position tracking state
3. **Process** ranges in ascending order
4. **Update** documentation to reflect new behavior
5. **Deprecate** multi-range with `---` separator (too error-prone)

### Data Flow

```
Input: ranges="10-15,50-55", content="AAA---BBB"

Step 1: Parse -> [(Lines (10,15), "AAA"), (Lines (50,55), "BBB")]

Step 2: Sort ascending -> [(Lines (10,15), "AAA"), (Lines (50,55), "BBB")]

Step 3: Apply sequentially with offset tracking:
  - Edit 1 at 10-15 (offset=0): Replace with "AAA" (3 lines)
    -> offset becomes 0 + (3-6) = -3
    
  - Edit 2 at 50-55, adjust by offset -3: Actually at 47-52
    -> Replace with "BBB" (3 lines)
    -> offset becomes -3 + (3-6) = -6

Step 4: Write final file
```

## Files to Modify

1. **`src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox.hs`**:
   - Rewrite `executeWriteFileRange` with position tracking
   - Remove bottom-to-top sorting
   - Add sequential offset tracking
   - Update documentation

2. **Tests**:
   - Add test: `ranges="1-1,3-3"` on 5-line file
   - Add test: Adding lines at start doesn't break subsequent edits
   - Add test: Removing lines shifts subsequent edits correctly

## Migration Path

### For LLM Agents

**Before (BROKEN):**
```haskell
-- Agent does multiple calls
write_file_range(path="X.hs", ranges="10-10", content="import A")  -- Turn 1
write_file_range(path="X.hs", ranges="50-60", content="func = ...") -- Turn 2, line 50 might have shifted!
```

**After (FIXED):**
```haskell
-- Agent does single call with multiple ranges
write_file_range(path="X.hs", ranges="10-10,50-60", content="import A---func = ...")
-- Both edits applied atomically with position tracking
```

## Backward Compatibility

This changes the semantics of `write-file-range` with multiple ranges. However:
- Current behavior is demonstrably broken (causes corruption)
- No reasonable code could rely on broken behavior
- Single-range usage is unaffected

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Multi-range edits apply correctly with position tracking
- [ ] Edit at line N doesn't corrupt edit at line M where M > N
- [ ] Test: `ranges="1-1,2-2"` adds content at lines 1 and 2 correctly
- [ ] Test: Deleting lines shifts subsequent edits up correctly  
- [ ] Test: Adding lines shifts subsequent edits down correctly
- [ ] All 635 existing tests pass
- [ ] Documentation updated to explain sequential processing

## Related Issues

- Complementary to #533 (patch-file capability) - both solve editing problems from different angles
- Addresses corruption documented in sessions: `e3b72fbf`, `706c7c9d`, `b2c76d12`

### Additional contract requirements

## Content argument of write-file-range

- The content argument of `write-file-range` (and of the corresponding
  `executeWriteFileRange` entry point) is a list of text blocks, not a
  single text value. The previous convention of joining per-range blocks
  into one text separated by `---` lines is superseded.
- When the ranges argument names N ranges, the content list must contain
  exactly N blocks: the first block replaces the first range, the second
  block replaces the second range, and so on. A single-range call passes a
  one-element list. Passing a different number of blocks than ranges is an
  invalid-range error.
- Each block is written verbatim. A line inside a block that looks like a
  separator (for example a `---` line, such as a markdown horizontal rule)
  is ordinary content data and must appear in the output; blocks are never
  split on separator-looking lines.
- An empty block deletes the targeted range entirely.

## Multi-range application semantics

- Within one call, every range refers to line numbers of the file as it was
  before that call.
- The edits of one call applied to the same file are atomic: inserting or
  removing lines for an earlier range must not change which original lines a
  later range targets, for both single-line and multi-line ranges, and for
  adjacent ranges.
- All single-range behaviors (head, tail, new-file creation, file-not-found
  handling, trailing-newline and indentation preservation) are unchanged by
  the list-shaped content argument.

write_file_range(path="X.hs", ranges="10-10,50-60", content="import A---func = ...")
-- Both edits applied atomically with position tracking
```

## Backward Compatibility

This changes the semantics of `write-file-range` with multiple ranges. However:
- Current behavior is demonstrably broken (causes corruption)
- No reasonable code could rely on broken behavior
- Single-range usage is unaffected

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Multi-range edits apply correctly with position tracking
- [ ] Edit at line N doesn't corrupt edit at line M where M > N
- [ ] Test: `ranges="1-1,2-2"` adds content at lines 1 and 2 correctly
- [ ] Test: Deleting lines shifts subsequent edits up correctly  
- [ ] Test: Adding lines shifts subsequent edits down correctly
- [ ] All 635 existing tests pass
- [ ] Documentation updated to explain sequential processing

## Related Issues

- Complementary to #533 (patch-file capability) - both solve editing problems from different angles
- Addresses corruption documented in sessions: `e3b72fbf`, `706c7c9d`, `b2c76d12`
contract_addendum:
## Content argument of write-file-range

- The content argument of `write-file-range` (and of the corresponding
  `executeWriteFileRange` entry point) is a list of text blocks, not a
  single text value. The previous convention of joining per-range blocks
  into one text separated by `---` lines is superseded.
- When the ranges argument names N ranges, the content list must contain
  exactly N blocks: the first block replaces the first range, the second
  block replaces the second range, and so on. A single-range call passes a
  one-element list. Passing a different number of blocks than ranges is an
  invalid-range error.
- Each block is written verbatim. A line inside a block that looks like a
  separator (for example a `---` line, such as a markdown horizontal rule)
  is ordinary content data and must appear in the output; blocks are never
  split on separator-looking lines.
- An empty block deletes the targeted range entirely.

## Multi-range application semantics

- Within one call, every range refers to line numbers of the file as it was
  before that call.
- The edits of one call applied to the same file are atomic: inserting or
  removing lines for an earlier range must not change which original lines a
  later range targets, for both single-line and multi-line ranges, and for
  adjacent ranges.
- All single-range behaviors (head, tail, new-file creation, file-not-found
  handling, trailing-newline and indentation preservation) are unchanged by
  the list-shaped content argument.

+## Problem Statement
+
+The current `write-file-range` implementation has a critical bug when multiple ranges are specified:
+
+**Current behavior (BROKEN):**
+```haskell

+-- Step 1: Replace lines 1-10 with content "A" 
+-- File now has 90 lines (removed 10, added say 5)
+
+-- Step 2: Replace lines 20-30 with content "B"
+-- PROBLEM: Lines 20-30 from ORIGINAL file no longer exist!
+-- What was line 20 is now line 15 due to Step 1
+```
+
+This causes severe file corruption as documented in session analysis:
+- Lines written to wrong locations
+- Duplicate function definitions
+- Stray code blocks from previous edits

+## Root Cause in Current Code
+
+In `DeveloperToolbox.hs` lines 674+, the current implementation:
+
+```haskell
+-- Pairs ranges with content blocks
+let rangeContentPairs = zip ranges contentBlocks
+
+-- Sorts by start line (descending) - this is WRONG for multi-range
+let sortedPairs = sortOn (negate . rangeStartKey) rangeContentPairs
+
+-- Applies each replacement sequentially
+let finalLines = foldl (applyRangeReplacement existingLines) existingLines sortedPairs
+```
+
+The `sortOn` approach assumes ranges don't affect each other, but they do!
+
+## Proposed Solution
+
+**Replace the entire algorithm** with sequential position tracking:
+
+```haskell
+executeWriteFileRangeAtomic tracer toolbox filePath rangesTxt contentTxt = do
+    -- Parse ranges and content blocks
+    ranges <- parseRanges rangesTxt
+    contentBlocks <- parseContentBlocks contentTxt
+    
+    -- MUST process ranges in ASCENDING order (top-to-bottom)
+    -- and adjust positions after each edit
+    let orderedPairs = sortOn fst (zip ranges contentBlocks)
+    
+    -- Apply with position tracking
+    applyEditsSequentially filePath orderedPairs
+
+applyEditsSequentially :: FilePath -> [(RangeSpec, Text)] -> IO ()
+applyEditsSequentially filePath edits = do
+    content <- Text.readFile filePath
+    let finalContent = foldl' applyEdit (Text.lines content) edits
+    Text.writeFile filePath (Text.unlines finalContent)
+  where
+    applyEdit :: [Text] -> (RangeSpec, Text) -> [Text]
+    applyEdit currentLines (range, newContent) = 
+        case range of
+            Lines (start, end) ->
+                let before = take (start - 1) currentLines
+                    after = drop end currentLines
+                    newLines = Text.lines newContent
+                in before ++ newLines ++ after
+            Head -> Text.lines newContent ++ currentLines
+            Tail -> currentLines ++ Text.lines newContent
+```

## Problem Summary

Analysis of session 53c32154-f613-4218-afb9-dec143c912c4 revealed recurring LLM confusion when using `read-file-range`. The LLM repeatedly encountered empty responses when trying to read files, leading to uncertainty about whether operations succeeded.

Additionally, the current snapshot mechanism doesn't provide protection against concurrent edits - if multiple agents/processes edit the same file, the last write wins without any conflict detection.

## Proposed Improvements

### 1. Augment read-file-range output with metadata

**Current behavior:** `ReadFileRangeResult` only returns `path`, `content`, and `linesRead`.

**Problem:** When content is empty (empty file, out-of-bounds ranges, head/tail special ranges), the LLM can't distinguish between:
- An empty file
- A range that returned no lines
- A file that doesn't exist (different error)

**Proposed change:** Add metadata fields to `ReadFileRangeResult`:
- `totalFileSize :: Int` - Total file size in bytes
- `totalLineCount :: Int` - Total number of lines in the file
- `rangeSpecsApplied :: [Text]` - The parsed range specifications that were applied

**Files to modify:**
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Types.hs` - Update `ReadFileRangeResult` type and JSON instance
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Read.hs` - Update `executeReadFileRange` to populate new fields

**Data types:**
```haskell
-- Current
newtype ReadFileRangeResult = ReadFileRangeResult
    { readFilePath :: FilePath
    , readFileContent :: Text
    , readFileLinesRead :: Int
    }

[HIDDEN]```

---

### 2. Default behavior for missing ranges parameter

**Current behavior:** When `ranges` is not provided (empty string), `parseRanges` returns an empty list `[]`, which causes `extractLines` to return empty content.

**Problem:** This caused confusion in session analysis - the LLM expected to see file content but got empty results. It's unclear what happens when ranges is omitted.

**Proposed change:** When `ranges` is empty/not provided, default to reading the entire file (equivalent to `"whole"`).

[HIDDEN]
[HIDDEN]
**Note:** This is a behavior change that may affect existing code. The alternative is to add an explicit `defaultToWhole` flag or similar. Consider backwards compatibility.

---

### 3. Improve documentation in help capability

**Current state:** The help text in `Help.hs` documents range formats but could be more explicit about:
- What "head", "tail", "whole" mean for read vs write operations
- Examples showing the difference between read and write behavior
- What happens when ranges are omitted
- More examples for common use cases

**Files to modify:**
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Help.hs` - Update `buildCapabilityHelp` for `DevToolReadFileRange`

**Key documentation improvements needed:**

For `read-file-range`:
```
Range Formats:
  - "whole" - Reads entire file with line numbers (default when ranges omitted)
  - "N" - Reads single line N (1-based)
  - "N-M" - Reads inclusive range from line N to line M
  - "head" - Returns empty for read (use "whole" or omit for full file)
  - "tail" - Returns empty for read (use "whole" or omit for full file)
  - "N+" - Not applicable for read operations
  
Note: For read operations, "head" and "tail" return empty content because 
they are intended for write operations. Use "whole" or omit ranges to read 
the entire file.

Examples:
  -- Read entire file (recommended):
  {"capability": "read-file-range", "path": "./file.txt"}
  
  -- Read specific lines:
  {"capability": "read-file-range", "path": "./file.txt", "ranges": "10-20"}
  
  -- Read first 50 lines:
  {"capability": "read-file-range", "path": "./file.txt", "ranges": "1-50"}
```

---

### 4. Add snapshot references for concurrent edit safety (Optimistic Locking)

**Current state:** The snapshot mechanism stores file content before edits, but there's no way to verify the file hasn't changed between read and write operations.

**Problem:** Multiple agents/processes editing the same file can cause lost updates. The snapshot stores the "before" state but doesn't validate it matches when restoring.

**Proposed change:** Implement optimistic locking for `write-file-range` and `patch-file`:

1. **Add optional `expectedSnapshotRef` parameter** to write/patch operations
   - If provided, the operation fails if current file content doesn't match
   - This prevents edits based on stale data

2. **Return both `beforeSnapshotRef` and `afterSnapshotRef`** in responses
   - `beforeSnapshotRef` - MD5 of content before edit (existing)
   - `afterSnapshotRef` - MD5 of content after edit (new)
   - Allows chaining operations with confidence

3. **Add new error type** for snapshot mismatch

**Files to modify:**
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Types.hs`:
  - Add `writeFileExpectedSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef` to write parameters (via function argument)
  - Add `writeFileAfterSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef` to `WriteFileRangeResult`
  - Add `patchFileAfterSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef` to `PatchResult`
  - Add new error: `SnapshotMismatchError SnapshotRef SnapshotRef` (expected vs actual)

[HIDDEN]
[HIDDEN]

**Usage flow with optimistic locking:**
```
1. Read file with read-file-range → get totalFileSize, totalLineCount
2. Take note of beforeSnapshotRef from previous operation (if any)
3. Prepare edit with expectedSnapshotRef = beforeSnapshotRef
4. If SnapshotMismatchError → file changed, re-read and retry
5. On success, get new afterSnapshotRef for next operation
```

---

## Context

Session analysis: The LLM got confused 3 times when read-file-range returned empty/unclear results after successful writes. Had to work around by using explicit range formats instead of relying on defaults.

**Trade-offs to consider:**

1. **Default to "whole" behavior change:** This is a breaking change. Existing code that passes empty ranges expecting empty results will now get full file content. Alternative: add a flag or only default when ranges parameter is completely absent (not just empty string).

2. **Optimistic locking overhead:** Computing MD5 hashes adds overhead. This should be optional (hence `Maybe SnapshotRef` parameter).

3. **Memory usage:** Storing before and after snapshot refs increases result size, but these are just MD5 hashes (32 chars), not full content.

---

## Testing Requirements

1. **ReadFileRange metadata tests:**
   - Verify totalFileSize is correct
   - Verify totalLineCount matches actual lines
   - Verify rangesParsed reflects normalized specs

2. **Default ranges tests:**
   - Empty string defaults to whole file
   - Explicit "whole" still works
   - Single line and ranges still work

3. **Help documentation tests:**
   - Verify updated help text is returned

4. **Optimistic locking tests:**
   - Write with correct expectedSnapshotRef succeeds
   - Write with wrong expectedSnapshotRef fails with SnapshotMismatchError
   - Write without expectedSnapshotRef works (backwards compatible)
   - After snapshot ref is correctly computed

---

- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Read.hs` - Read file range implementation
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Write.hs` - Write file range implementation  
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Patch.hs` - Patch file implementation
- `src/System/Agents/Tools/DeveloperToolbox/Help.hs` - Help documentation

### Additional contract requirements

## Public contract for the enhanced `DeveloperToolbox` file operations

This document is the authoritative naming reference for the enhanced
`DeveloperToolbox`. Any implementation must expose the exact public Haskell
names, JSON field names, parameter order, and snapshot semantics described
here so that the documented behavior can be exercised.

### Range parsing

* `parseRanges :: Text -> Either DeveloperToolError [RangeSpec]` must accept
  an empty or omitted string and return `Right [Whole]` (the whole file); it
  must not return an empty list for empty input.
* `RangeSpec` constructors used in range results are `Lines (Int, Int)`,
  `Head`, `Tail`, `Whole`, and `After Int`, in scope from
  `System.Agents.Tools.DeveloperToolbox.Types`.

### Read file range

`executeReadFileRange` keeps its existing call shape:
`executeReadFileRange tracer toolbox filePath ranges`.

`ReadFileRangeResult` must expose these public selectors with these exact
names and types:

* `readFilePath :: FilePath`
* `readFileContent :: Text`
* `readFileLinesRead :: Int`
* `readFileTotalSize :: Int` — total size of the file.
* `readFileTotalLines :: Int` — total number of lines in the file.
* `readFileRangesParsed :: [Text]` — normalized range specifications that
  were applied (for example `["1-3"]`, `["2-4"]`, `["1-2","9-10"]`, and
  `["whole"]` when ranges were empty/defaulted to whole).

Its `ToJSON` encoding must be an object with exactly these keys:
`path`, `content`, `linesRead`, `totalFileSize`, `totalLineCount`,
`rangesParsed`, with values drawn from the same-named selectors.

### Snapshot types and errors

* `DeveloperToolError` exports `SnapshotMismatchError :: SnapshotRef -> SnapshotRef -> DeveloperToolError`.
* `SnapshotRef` is a newtype exported with its constructor:
  `SnapshotRef { unSnapshotRef :: Text }`.
* `makeSnapshot :: ByteString -> Snapshot` and
  `snapshotRef :: Snapshot -> SnapshotRef` are public; the snapshot
  reference is derived from the given content so callers can compute the
  expected reference of current file content.

### Write file range

`executeWriteFileRange` takes parameters in this order:
tracer, toolbox, `FilePath`, `Text` ranges, `[Text]` content blocks,
`Maybe SnapshotRef` expected snapshot reference.

* Passing `Nothing` for the expected snapshot reference preserves the
  previous behavior (backwards compatible).
* Passing `Just ref` makes the operation fail with
  `Left (SnapshotMismatchError expected actual)` when `ref` does not match
  the reference computed from the file's current content, and leaves the
  file content unchanged; `expected` equals the supplied `ref` while
  `actual` is the reference of the current content. On a match, the write
  proceeds normally.

`WriteFileRangeResult` must expose these public selectors:
`writeFilePath`, `writeFileRangesModified`, `writeFileLinesWritten`,
`writeFileFinalLineCount`, `writeFileRangeResults`,
`writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef`, and
`writeFileAfterSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef`. Its `ToJSON` encoding uses
the keys `path`, `rangesModified`, `linesWritten`, `finalLineCount`,
`rangeResults`, `beforeSnapshotRef`, `afterSnapshotRef`.

### Patch file

`executePatchFile` takes parameters in this order: tracer, toolbox,
`FilePath`, `Text` patch content, `Maybe SnapshotRef` expected snapshot
reference, with the same optimistic-locking semantics as write-file-range:
`Nothing` preserves previous behavior, while a non-matching `Just ref`
fails with `Left (SnapshotMismatchError ...)` and leaves the file unchanged.

`PatchResult` must expose `patchFilePath`, `patchHunksApplied`,
`patchHunksRejected`, `patchLinesChanged`,
`patchBeforeSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef`, and
`patchAfterSnapshotRef :: Maybe SnapshotRef`. Its `ToJSON` encoding uses the
keys `path`, `hunksApplied`, `hunksRejected`, `linesChanged`,
`beforeSnapshotRef`, `afterSnapshotRef`.

A patch whose context does not match the file is rejected with
`Left (PatchValidationError _)`, leaving the file unchanged.

### Snapshot-capability semantics

* `beforeSnapshotRef` and `afterSnapshotRef` are populated (non-`Nothing`)
  only when the `snapshot` capability is enabled for the toolbox; without
  that capability both are `Nothing` in successful write/patch results.
* When the capability is enabled, the before reference matches a snapshot
  of the file content immediately before the edit and the after reference
  matches a snapshot of the content immediately after the edit.

### Help documentation

The help capability output must document the enhancements: for
read-file-range it must mention `totalFileSize`, `totalLineCount`,
`rangesParsed`, and that omitting ranges reads the whole file (mention
`whole`); for write-file-range it must mention `expectedSnapshotRef`,
`beforeSnapshotRef`, and `afterSnapshotRef` for optimistic locking.

 Applies a unified diff patch to a file atomically. All hunks are validated

+Optimistic Locking:
+When expectedSnapshotRef is provided, the operation first reads the current file
+content and computes its MD5 hash. If the hash doesn't match expectedSnapshotRef,
+a SnapshotMismatchError is returned without making any changes. This prevents
+lost updates when multiple agents/processes edit the same file.

+-- | Take a snapshot of the file after editing, if snapshot capability is enabled.
+-- Returns the snapshot reference if a snapshot was taken, Nothing otherwise.
+takeSnapshotAfterEdit :: Toolbox -> FilePath -> IO (Maybe SnapshotRef)
+takeSnapshotAfterEdit toolbox filePath =
+    case (toolboxSnapshotStore toolbox, DevToolSnapshot `elem` toolboxCapabilities toolbox) of
+        (Just store, True) -> do
+            -- Read file content and create snapshot
+            content <- BS.readFile filePath
+            let snapshot = makeSnapshot content
+            let ref = snapshotRef snapshot
+            -- Store snapshot in the store
+            atomically $ modifyTVar' store (Map.insert ref snapshot)
+            pure $ Just ref
+        _ -> pure Nothing
+

 runFunc :: Tracer IO Trace -> ToolExecutionContext -> Aeson.Value -> IO (CallResult ())\n        runFunc tracer ctx argz =\n            createToolHandler toolbox tool (contramap OpenAPIToolboxTrace find\n                , toolActivation = PostgRESToolbox.postgrestActivation toolbox\n                }\n\n{- | Build parameter properties for PostgREST tool from structured parameters.\n\nParameter groups:\n* filters: Column-based row filters (for GET, DELETE, PATCH, PUT)\n* subset: Pagination (limit/offset) and column selection (for GET)\n* ranking: Ordering clause (for GET)\n* body: JSON request body (for POST, PUT, PATCH)\n\nAll parameter groups and their sub-properties are marked as optional\n(propertyRequired = False), allowing the LLM to provide only the\nparameters it needs.\n-}\nbuildPostgRESTParamProperties :: ToolParameters -> [ParamProperty]\nbuildPostgRESTParamProperties params =\n    let filterProp = case tpFilters params of\n            Just fs ->\n              , propertyDescription = fsDescription fs\n                        , propertyRequired = False -- Optional parameter group\n                        }\n            Nothing -> Nothing\n\n        subsetProp = case tpSubset params of\n            Just ss ->\n                Just $\n                    ParamProperty\n                        { propertyKey = \"subset\"\n                        , propertyType = ObjectParamType (buildSubsetSubProperties ss)\n                        , propertyDescription = \"Pagination and column selection\"\n                        , propertyRequired = False -- Optional parameter group\n                        }\n            Nothing -> Nothing\n\n        rankingProp = case tpRanking params of\n            Just rs ->\n                Just $\n (ssColumns ss)\n            ]\n\n    buildRankingSubProperties :: RankingSchema -> [ParamProperty]\n    buildRankingSubProperties rs =\n        Maybe.catMaybes\n            [ fmap (\\desc -> ParamProperty \"order\" (OpaqueParamType \"string\") desc False) (rsOrder rs)\n            ]\n\n    -- Build the parameter type for the request body\n    buildBodyParamType :: Schema -> ParamType\n    buildBodyParamType schema =\n        case schema.schemaType of\n            Just \"array\" ->\n                -- For bulk insert (array of objects)\n                case schema.schemaItems of\n single row insert\n                ObjectParamType (buildSchemaProperties schema)\n            _ -> OpaqueParamType \"object\"\n\n    -- Build description for the request body parameter\n   typeHint = case schema.schemaType of\n                Just \"array\" -> \" (provide an array of objects for bulk insert, or a single object)\"\n                Just \"object\" -> \" (provide a JSON object with column values)\"\n                _ -> \"\"\n         in baseDesc <> typeHint\n\n    -- Build properties from schema for object validation\n    buildSchemaProperties :: Schema -> [ParamProperty]\n    buildSchemaProperties schema =\n        case schema.schemaProperties of\n            Just props -> map (\\(k, v) -> schemaToParamProperty k v) (Map.toList props)\n            Nothing -> []\n\n    -- Convert a schema property to ParamProperty\n    schemaToParamProperty :: Text -> Schema -> ParamProperty\n    schemaToParamProperty name schema =\n        ParamProperty\n RangeEditResult\n                                            { rangeEditSpec =\n                                                Text.pack (show origStart)\n +-- Help Documentation Tests (issue: improved help text)
