+
+helpDocumentationTests :: TestTree
+helpDocumentationTests =
+    testGroup
+        "Help Documentation"
+        [ testCase "read-file-range help documents metadata and default whole" testHelpReadFileRangeDocumentsMetadata
+        , testCase "write-file-range help documents optimistic locking" testHelpWriteFileRangeDocumentsOptimisticLocking

+
+-- | The help text for read-file-range must document the metadata fields and
+-- the default "whole" behavior when ranges are omitted (issue requirement #3).
+testHelpReadFileRangeDocumentsMetadata :: Assertion
+testHelpReadFileRangeDocumentsMetadata = do
+    toolbox <- testToolboxWithCapabilities [DevToolReadFileRange, DevToolHelp]
+    result <- Help.executeHelp toolbox
+    case result of
+        Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+        Right helpText -> do
+            assertBool "help should document totalFileSize" $
+                "totalFileSize" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+            assertBool "help should document totalLineCount" $
+                "totalLineCount" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+            assertBool "help should document rangesParsed" $
+                "rangesParsed" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+            assertBool "help should document default whole behavior" $
+                "whole" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+
+-- | The help text for write-file-range must document optimistic locking via
+-- the expectedSnapshotRef parameter (issue requirement #4 documentation).
+testHelpWriteFileRangeDocumentsOptimisticLocking :: Assertion
+testHelpWriteFileRangeDocumentsOptimisticLocking = do
+    toolbox <- testToolboxWithCapabilities [DevToolWriteFileRange, DevToolHelp]
+    result <- Help.executeHelp toolbox
+    case result of
+        Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+        Right helpText -> do
+            assertBool "help should document expectedSnapshotRef" $
+                "expectedSnapshotRef" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+            assertBool "help should document beforeSnapshotRef" $
+                "beforeSnapshotRef" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+            assertBool "help should document afterSnapshotRef" $
+                "afterSnapshotRef" `Text.isInfixOf` helpText
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Read File Range JSON Serialization Tests
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+readFileRangeJsonTests :: TestTree
+readFileRangeJsonTests =
+    testGroup
+        "Read File Range JSON Serialization"
+        [ testCase "Read result JSON contains metadata keys with correct values" testReadResultJsonMetadataKeys
+        ]
+
+-- | The serialized read-file-range result must expose the metadata under
+-- the documented JSON names with values matching the result fields.
+testReadResultJsonMetadataKeys :: Assertion
+testReadResultJsonMetadataKeys = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeReadFileRange silent toolbox filePath "1-3"
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right readResult ->
+                -- The result must serialize to exactly this JSON object:
+                -- every documented key present with the correct value.
+                toJSON readResult
+                    @?= object
+                        [ "path" .= readFilePath readResult
+                        , "content" .= readFileContent readResult
+                        , "linesRead" .= readFileLinesRead readResult
+                        , "totalFileSize" .= readFileTotalSize readResult
+                        , "totalLineCount" .= readFileTotalLines readResult
+                        , "rangesParsed" .= readFileRangesParsed readResult
+                        ]
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Write Optimistic Locking Tests (snapshot capability enabled)
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+writeLockingEnabledTests :: TestTree
+writeLockingEnabledTests =
+    testGroup
+        "Write Optimistic Locking (snapshot enabled)"
+        [ testCase "Write with snapshot capability returns before and after snapshot refs" testWriteEnabledReturnsVerifiedRefs
+        , testCase "Write with wrong snapshot ref fails without changing the file" testWriteEnabledMismatchUnchanged
+        , testCase "Write result JSON contains all documented keys" testWriteResultJsonKeys
+        ]
+
+-- | With the snapshot capability enabled, a successful write must return a
+-- before snapshot ref matching the pre-edit content and an after snapshot
+-- ref matching the post-edit content.
+testWriteEnabledReturnsVerifiedRefs :: Assertion
+testWriteEnabledReturnsVerifiedRefs = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+        expectedRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+        result <-
+            DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                silent
+                toolbox
+                filePath
+                "5"
+                ["REPLACED\n"]
+                (Just expectedRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right writeResult -> do
+                writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Just expectedRef
+                actualAfterRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+                writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Just actualAfterRef
+                (writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult /= writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult)
+                    @? "after snapshot ref should differ from before snapshot ref after an edit"
+
+-- | With the snapshot capability enabled, a write with a wrong expected
+-- snapshot ref must fail with a snapshot mismatch error and must leave the
+-- file content unchanged.
+testWriteEnabledMismatchUnchanged :: Assertion
+testWriteEnabledMismatchUnchanged = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+        contentBefore <- Text.readFile filePath
+        let wrongRef = SnapshotRef "definitely-wrong-hash"
+        result <-
+            DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                silent
+                toolbox
+                filePath
+                "5"
+                ["REPLACED\n"]
+                (Just wrongRef)
+        case result of
+            Left (SnapshotMismatchError expected actual) ->
+                expected @?= wrongRef
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Expected SnapshotMismatchError, got: " ++ show err
+            Right _ -> assertFailure "Expected error for mismatched snapshot ref"
+        contentAfter <- Text.readFile filePath
+        contentAfter @?= contentBefore
+
+
+-- | The serialized write-file-range result must expose exactly the
+-- documented JSON keys, with values matching the result selectors
+-- (including the snapshot references derived from the file content).
+testWriteResultJsonKeys :: Assertion
+testWriteResultJsonKeys = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+        result <-
+            DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                silent
+                toolbox
+                filePath
+                "5"
+                ["REPLACED\n"]
+                Nothing
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right writeResult ->
+                toJSON writeResult
+                    @?= object
+                        [ "path" .= writeFilePath writeResult
+                        , "rangesModified" .= writeFileRangesModified writeResult
+                        , "linesWritten" .= writeFileLinesWritten writeResult
+                        , "finalLineCount" .= writeFileFinalLineCount writeResult
+                        , "rangeResults" .= writeFileRangeResults writeResult
+                        , "beforeSnapshotRef" .= writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult
+                        , "afterSnapshotRef" .= writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult
+                        ]
+-- | Compute the snapshot reference of a file's current content.
+computeFileSnapshotRef :: FilePath -> IO SnapshotRef
+computeFileSnapshotRef filePath = do
+    content <- Text.readFile filePath
+    pure $ snapshotRef (makeSnapshot (Text.encodeUtf8 content))
+
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Patch File Optimistic Locking Tests
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+patchFileLockingTests :: TestTree
+patchFileLockingTests =
+    testGroup
+        "Patch File Optimistic Locking"
+        [ testCase "Patch applies hunks to a matching file" testPatchAppliesHunks
+        , testCase "Patch with non-matching context is rejected without changing the file" testPatchContextMismatch
+        , testCase "Patch with correct expected snapshot ref succeeds and returns refs" testPatchCorrectRefSucceeds
+        , testCase "Patch with wrong expected snapshot ref fails without changing the file" testPatchWrongRefFails
+        , testCase "Patch with correct expected snapshot ref without snapshot capability succeeds with no refs" testPatchCorrectRefNoCapability
+        , testCase "Patch result JSON contains all documented keys" testPatchResultJsonKeys
+        ]
+
+-- | A unified-diff patch that replaces the fifth line of the test file.
+testPatchText :: Text
+testPatchText =
+    Text.unlines
+        [ "--- a/testfile.txt"
+        , "+++ b/testfile.txt"
+        , "@@ -5,1 +5,1 @@"
+        , "-Line 5: Fifth line"
+        , "+Line 5: Patched fifth line"
+        ]
+
+-- | A patch whose context does not match the test file.
+testMismatchPatchText :: Text
+testMismatchPatchText =
+    Text.unlines
+        [ "--- a/testfile.txt"
+        , "+++ b/testfile.txt"
+        , "@@ -5,1 +5,1 @@"
+        , "-No such line exists here"
+        , "+Line 5: Patched fifth line"
+        ]
+
+-- | Execute patch-file without an expected snapshot ref.
+executePatchNoRef :: FilePath -> Text -> IO (Either DeveloperToolError PatchResult)
+executePatchNoRef filePath patch = do
+    toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+    DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath patch Nothing
+
+-- | Baseline: patch-file applies hunks and reports the before/after
+-- snapshot references of the file content.
+testPatchAppliesHunks :: Assertion
+testPatchAppliesHunks = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        result <- executePatchNoRef filePath testPatchText
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right patchResult -> do
+                patchHunksApplied patchResult @?= 1
+                patchLinesChanged patchResult @?= 2
+                content <- Text.readFile filePath
+                assertBool "Should contain patched line" $
+                    "Line 5: Patched fifth line" `Text.isInfixOf` content
+                assertBool "Original line should be gone" $
+                    not ("Line 5: Fifth line" `Text.isInfixOf` content)
+
+-- | Patch-file with the correct expected snapshot ref (the snapshot of the
+-- current file content) must succeed and must return before/after snapshot
+-- references matching the file content around the edit.
+testPatchCorrectRefSucceeds :: Assertion
+testPatchCorrectRefSucceeds = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+        expectedRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath testPatchText (Just expectedRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right patchResult -> do
+                patchHunksApplied patchResult @?= 1
+                patchBeforeSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Just expectedRef
+                actualAfterRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+                patchAfterSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Just actualAfterRef
+                (patchAfterSnapshotRef patchResult /= patchBeforeSnapshotRef patchResult)
+                    @? "after snapshot ref should differ from before snapshot ref after a patch"
+
+-- | Patch-file with a wrong expected snapshot ref must fail with a snapshot
+-- mismatch error and must leave the file content unchanged.
+testPatchWrongRefFails :: Assertion
+testPatchWrongRefFails = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- snapshotTestToolbox
+        contentBefore <- Text.readFile filePath
+        let wrongRef = SnapshotRef "definitely-wrong-hash"
+        -- Use a patch that would apply cleanly, so only the snapshot
+        -- mismatch can trigger an error.
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath testPatchText (Just wrongRef)
+        case result of
+            Left (SnapshotMismatchError expected actual) -> do
+                expected @?= wrongRef
+                -- The reported actual reference must be computed from the
+                -- current file content (which the failed patch left
+                -- unchanged).
+                actualRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+                actual @?= actualRef
+                (actual /= wrongRef) @? "actual ref should differ from the wrong expected ref"
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Expected SnapshotMismatchError, got: " ++ show err
+            Right _ -> assertFailure "Expected error for mismatched snapshot ref"
+        contentAfter <- Text.readFile filePath
+        contentAfter @?= contentBefore
+
+-- | A patch whose context does not match the file is rejected with a
+-- patch-validation error, leaving the file content unchanged.
+testPatchContextMismatch :: Assertion
+testPatchContextMismatch = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        contentBefore <- Text.readFile filePath
+        result <- executePatchNoRef filePath testMismatchPatchText
+        case result of
+            Left (PatchValidationError _) -> pure ()
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Expected PatchValidationError, got: " ++ show err
+            Right _ -> assertFailure "Expected error for non-matching patch context"
+        contentAfter <- Text.readFile filePath
+        contentAfter @?= contentBefore
+
+-- | With a correct expected snapshot ref but without the snapshot
+-- capability, a patch must still succeed, and both returned snapshot
+-- reference fields must be Nothing.
+testPatchCorrectRefNoCapability :: Assertion
+testPatchCorrectRefNoCapability = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <-
+            testToolboxWithCapabilities
+                [ DevToolReadFileRange
+                , DevToolWriteFileRange
+                , DevToolPatchFile
+                ]
+        expectedRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath testPatchText (Just expectedRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Patch with correct snapshot ref should succeed: " ++ show err
+            Right patchResult -> do
+                patchHunksApplied patchResult @?= 1
+                patchBeforeSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Nothing
+                patchAfterSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Nothing
+        applied <- Text.readFile filePath
+        assertBool "Should have patched content" $
+            "Line 5: Patched fifth line" `Text.isInfixOf` applied
+
+-- | The serialized patch-file result must expose exactly the documented
+-- JSON keys, with values matching the result selectors (including the
+-- snapshot references derived from the file content).
+testPatchResultJsonKeys :: Assertion
+testPatchResultJsonKeys = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        result <- executePatchNoRef filePath testPatchText
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right patchResult ->
+                toJSON patchResult
+                    @?= object
+                        [ "path" .= patchFilePath patchResult
+                        , "hunksApplied" .= patchHunksApplied patchResult
+                        , "hunksRejected" .= patchHunksRejected patchResult
+                        , "linesChanged" .= patchLinesChanged patchResult
+                        , "beforeSnapshotRef" .= patchBeforeSnapshotRef patchResult
+                        , "afterSnapshotRef" .= patchAfterSnapshotRef patchResult
+                        ]

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- Optimistic Locking Tests
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+optimisticLockingTests :: TestTree
+optimisticLockingTests =
+    testGroup
+        "Optimistic Locking with expected_snapshot_ref"
+        [ testCase "Write without expected_snapshot_ref works" testWriteWithoutSnapshotRef
+        , testCase "Write with correct expected_snapshot_ref succeeds" testWriteWithCorrectSnapshotRef
+        , testCase "Write with correct expected_snapshot_ref succeeds with no snapshot refs without snapshot capability" testWriteCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs
+        , testCase "Patch with correct expected_snapshot_ref succeeds with no snapshot refs without snapshot capability" testPatchCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs
+        , testCase "Patch with wrong expected_snapshot_ref fails without snapshot capability without changing the file" testPatchWrongRefNoCapability
+        , testCase "Write with wrong expected_snapshot_ref fails" testWriteWithWrongSnapshotRef
+        , testCase "afterSnapshotRef is returned on success" testAfterSnapshotRefReturned
+        ]
+
+-- | Test that write without expected_snapshot_ref works (backwards compatible)
+testWriteWithoutSnapshotRef :: Assertion
+testWriteWithoutSnapshotRef = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                    silent
+                    toolbox
+                    filePath
+                    "5"
+                    ["REPLACED\n"]
+                    Nothing
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right writeResult -> do
+                writeFileRangesModified writeResult @?= 1
+                content <- Text.readFile filePath
+                assertBool "Should have replaced content" $ "REPLACED" `Text.isInfixOf` content
+
+-- | Test that write with the correct expected_snapshot_ref succeeds.
+-- The correct reference is the MD5 snapshot of the current file content,
+-- computed via the publicly exported makeSnapshot (issue: optimistic locking).
+testWriteWithCorrectSnapshotRef :: Assertion
+testWriteWithCorrectSnapshotRef = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        content <- Text.readFile filePath
+        let correctRef = snapshotRef (makeSnapshot (Text.encodeUtf8 content))
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                    silent
+                    toolbox
+                    filePath
+                    "5"
+                    ["REPLACED\n"]
+                    (Just correctRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Write with correct snapshot ref should succeed: " ++ show err
+            Right writeResult -> do
+                writeFileRangesModified writeResult @?= 1
+                written <- Text.readFile filePath
+                assertBool "Should have replaced content" $ "REPLACED" `Text.isInfixOf` written
+                -- Without the snapshot capability both returned snapshot
+                -- reference fields must be Nothing.
+                writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+                writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+
+-- | Test that write with wrong expected_snapshot_ref fails with SnapshotMismatchError
+testWriteWithWrongSnapshotRef :: Assertion
+testWriteWithWrongSnapshotRef = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        let wrongRef = SnapshotRef "definitely-wrong-hash"
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                    silent
+                    toolbox
+                    filePath
+                    "5"
+                    ["REPLACED\n"]
+                    (Just wrongRef)
+        case result of
+            Left (SnapshotMismatchError expected actual) -> do
+                -- expected ref is the one we supplied, actual differs from it
+                expected @?= wrongRef
+                -- The reported actual reference must be the snapshot of the
+                -- current file content (which the failed write left
+                -- unchanged).
+                actualRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+                actual @?= actualRef
+                (actual /= wrongRef) @? "actual ref should differ from the wrong expected ref"
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Expected SnapshotMismatchError, got: " ++ show err
+            Right _ -> assertFailure "Expected error for mismatched snapshot ref"
+
+-- | Test that afterSnapshotRef is returned on success
+testAfterSnapshotRefReturned :: Assertion
+testAfterSnapshotRefReturned = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withStandardTestFile tmpDir $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                    silent
+                    toolbox
+                    filePath
+                    "5"
+                    ["REPLACED\n"]
+                    Nothing
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ show err
+            Right writeResult -> do
+                -- beforeSnapshotRef and afterSnapshotRef should both be Nothing
+                -- since snapshot capability is not enabled in test toolbox
+                writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+                writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+
+
+-- | Compute the snapshot reference of a file's current content via the
+-- publicly exported makeSnapshot/snapshotRef functions.
+computeFileSnapshotRef :: FilePath -> IO SnapshotRef
+computeFileSnapshotRef filePath = do
+    content <- Text.readFile filePath
+    pure $ snapshotRef (makeSnapshot (Text.encodeUtf8 content))
+
+-- | With a correct expected_snapshot_ref but without the snapshot
+-- capability, a write must still succeed, and both returned snapshot
+-- reference fields must be Nothing.
+testWriteCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs :: Assertion
+testWriteCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withTestFile tmpDir "Alpha\nBeta\n" $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <- testToolbox
+        correctRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executeWriteFileRange
+                    silent
+                    toolbox
+                    filePath
+                    "2"
+                    ["Gamma\n"]
+                    (Just correctRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Write with correct snapshot ref should succeed: " ++ show err
+            Right writeResult -> do
+                writeFileRangesModified writeResult @?= 1
+                writeFileBeforeSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+                writeFileAfterSnapshotRef writeResult @?= Nothing
+                content <- Text.readFile filePath
+                content @?= "Alpha\nGamma\n"
+
+-- | With a correct expected_snapshot_ref but without the snapshot
+-- capability, a patch-file call must still succeed, and both returned
+-- snapshot reference fields must be Nothing.
+testPatchCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs :: Assertion
+testPatchCorrectRefNoSnapshotRefs = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withTestFile tmpDir "Alpha\nBeta\n" $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <-
+            testToolboxWithCapabilities
+                [ DevToolReadFileRange
+                , DevToolWriteFileRange
+                , DevToolPatchFile
+                ]
+        correctRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+        let patchText =
+                Text.unlines
+                    [ "--- a/testfile.txt"
+                    , "+++ b/testfile.txt"
+                    , "@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@"
+                    , "-Beta"
+                    , "+Gamma"
+                    ]
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath patchText (Just correctRef)
+        case result of
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Patch with correct snapshot ref should succeed: " ++ show err
+            Right patchResult -> do
+                patchHunksApplied patchResult @?= 1
+                patchBeforeSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Nothing
+                patchAfterSnapshotRef patchResult @?= Nothing
+                content <- Text.readFile filePath
+                content @?= "Alpha\nGamma\n"
+
+-- | With a wrong expected_snapshot_ref and without the snapshot capability,
+-- a patch-file call must still perform optimistic-lock validation: it must
+-- fail with a SnapshotMismatchError carrying the supplied expected reference
+-- and the actual reference computed from the unchanged current file content,
+-- and it must leave the file content unchanged. The snapshot capability only
+-- affects whether successful result reference fields are populated, not lock
+-- validation.
+testPatchWrongRefNoCapability :: Assertion
+testPatchWrongRefNoCapability = withTempDir $ \tmpDir ->
+    withTestFile tmpDir "Alpha\nBeta\n" $ \filePath -> do
+        toolbox <-
+            testToolboxWithCapabilities
+                [ DevToolReadFileRange
+                , DevToolWriteFileRange
+                , DevToolPatchFile
+                ]
+        let wrongRef = SnapshotRef "definitely-wrong-hash"
+        let patchText =
+                Text.unlines
+                    [ "--- a/testfile.txt"
+                    , "+++ b/testfile.txt"
+                    , "@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@"
+                    , "-Beta"
+                    , "+Gamma"
+                    ]
+        -- Use a patch that would apply cleanly, so only the snapshot
+        -- mismatch can trigger an error.
+        result <- DeveloperToolbox.executePatchFile silent toolbox filePath patchText (Just wrongRef)
+        case result of
+            Left (SnapshotMismatchError expected actual) -> do
+                expected @?= wrongRef
+                -- The reported actual reference must be the snapshot of the
+                -- current file content (which the failed patch left
+                -- unchanged).
+                actualRef <- computeFileSnapshotRef filePath
+                actual @?= actualRef
+                (actual /= wrongRef) @? "actual ref should differ from the wrong expected ref"
+            Left err -> assertFailure $ "Expected SnapshotMismatchError, got: " ++ show err
+            Right _ -> assertFailure "Expected error for mismatched snapshot ref"
+        content <- Text.readFile filePath
+        content @?= "Alpha\nBeta\n"
FAIL_TO_PASS: rebench explicit result

problem_statement:
Canceling a queued lock waiter can permanently transfer ownership to a coroutine that will never resume
**Severity:** high (7.5)
**Type:** Insecure Design
**Source:** [HIDDEN]

The lock queue holds only a coroutine and has no cancellation/removal hook. A waiter is enqueued and suspended here:

[HIDDEN]

If that coroutine is canceled through Copas while waiting (for example, `copas.removethread`, which is also used by `future:cancel()`), the lock entry remains. On release, the lock unconditionally makes the stale coroutine its owner *before* attempting to wake it:

[HIDDEN]

Copas cancellation removes the coroutine from the sleeping set, so `wakeup(next_up)` cannot resume it; even if it is later presented to the scheduler, the canceled coroutine is discarded rather than executing [HIDDEN] and eventually releasing. The lock remains owned forever by the canceled waiter. Cancellation of the current owner is similarly unrecoverable because there is no owner-death cleanup.

Concrete remote exploit scenario: a server runs per-request work as cancelable futures and uses a shared lock around a cache/database operation. An attacker makes a request wait behind the lock and disconnects, causing the server to call `future:cancel()`/`copas.removethread()` for that request. When the active request releases, ownership transfers to the canceled request, and every subsequent request using the lock times out. No large request volume is required.

Full report: https://console.zeroquarry.com/reports/071a2dbf-cfcf-4f85-9730-5b201c9f96e1/findings/06c0303b-6ae5-4ff0-b747-e282f50ce429

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum: cancellation of copas lock waiters

This addendum clarifies the publicly observable behavior required of
`copas.lock` when threads waiting on a lock are canceled externally, for
example via `copas.removethread` (which is also what `future:cancel()`
uses under the hood).

## Queued-waiter cancellation (required)

A thread that is queued and suspended while waiting to acquire a lock may
be canceled while it is still waiting in line. In that case:

- When the current owner releases the lock, the release must not hand
  ownership to the canceled waiter, because that coroutine will never
  resume again and therefore could never release the lock. Ownership must
  instead go to a waiting coroutine that can actually resume.
- No legitimate waiter queued behind the canceled one may starve: it must
  still acquire the lock and must be able to release it normally.
- After a canceled queued waiter has been skipped, the lock must remain
  freely acquirable and releasable through the public `get`/`release`
  operations; it must not appear owned forever by the canceled thread.

## Owner cancellation (not prescribed)

The hidden tests constrain only the queued-waiter cancellation scenario
above. They do not prescribe any specific recovery mechanism or outcome
for the case where the coroutine currently owning a lock is canceled;
implementations are free to handle that case (or not handle it) as they
see fit, and no particular result (such as a waiter's timeout or an
ownership handoff) is required by the test contract for it.

--- a/tests/lock.lua
+++ b/tests/lock.lua
@@ -104,4 +104,53 @@ copas.loop(function()
 end)
 assert(test_complete, "test did not complete!")
 
+
+-- Test 2: canceling a queued waiter must not permanently transfer ownership
+-- to it, locking out every legitimate waiter behind it forever.
+-- See https://github.com/lunarmodules/copas/issues/199
+local test2_complete = false
+copas.loop(function()
+
+  local lock2 = assert(Lock.new(10))
+  assert(lock2:get()) -- owned by this (the main) coroutine
+
+  -- queue a waiter that will be canceled (eg. via future:cancel()) while
+  -- it is still waiting in line for the lock
+  local canceled_queued = copas.addthread(function()
+    lock2:get()
+  end)
+
+  -- queue a legitimate waiter behind it
+  local waiter_result
+  copas.addthread(function()
+    local ok, err = lock2:get()
+    waiter_result = ok and "got it" or err
+    if ok then
+      assert(lock2:release())
+    end
+  end)
+
+  copas.pause(0.5) -- let both threads actually enqueue and block on the lock
+
+  copas.removethread(canceled_queued) -- simulate external cancellation while queued
+
+  copas.pause(0.5) -- let the cancellation take effect before releasing
+
+  assert(lock2:release()) -- must hand the lock to the legitimate waiter
+
+  copas.pause(0.5) -- give the legitimate waiter time to run and release
+
+  assert(waiter_result == "got it",
+    "expected the legitimate waiter to get the lock, got: "..tostring(waiter_result))
+
+  -- recovery through public lock operations only: the lock must be freely
+  -- re-acquirable after a canceled queued waiter was skipped
+  assert(lock2:get(5), "expected the lock to be acquirable again, it stayed owned")
+  assert(lock2:release())
+
+  test2_complete = true
+end)
+assert(test2_complete, "test 2 did not complete!")
+
+
 print("test success!")

+#!/bin/sh
+# Test support runner: execute each target copas test in a subprocess and
+# report a per-test result line derived from its real exit status.
+# Emits lines of the form:  Success || <name>   /   Fail || <name>
+# Exits non-zero if any selected test fails.
+cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
+overall=0
+run() {
+  file="$1"; name="$2"
+  out=$(timeout 120 lua5.1 "$file" 2>&1)
+  ec=$?
+  printf '%s\n' "$out"
+  if [ "$ec" -eq 0 ]; then
+    printf 'Success || %s\n' "$name"
+  else
+    printf 'Fail || %s\n' "$name"
+    overall=1
+  fi
+}
+run lock.lua "lock.lua"
+exit "$overall"
FAIL_TO_PASS: lock.lua

[Feature]: Add option to disable the auto-formatting
### Problem

I don't like the format enforced by gdformat, so I don't use it.
However the plugin will always try to execute it, resulting in an error message each time I save.
I tried to set `formatter = nil` and `formatter = ""` but without success.

### Proposed solution

Add an option to opt-out of the auto-call to gdformat.
e.g.: `formatter = false` 

Aside from that it is a great plugin, thanks for the work!

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

+### `godotdev` says "Neovim server already running" after you already quit
+
+This is usually caused by an older wrapper that probes with `nvr --remote-expr` but does not pass `--nostart`.
+
+- Update the wrapper so the probe line is exactly:
+  ```bash
+  if command -v "$NVR" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$NVR" --nostart --servername "$SOCKET" --remote-expr '1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  ```
+- Without `--nostart`, `nvr` can report success without proving that the target socket is your live Neovim server, so the wrapper may print `Neovim server already running at /tmp/godot.pipe` even after exit.
+- If you are already stuck with a stale socket, remove it once with:
+  ```bash
+  rm -f /tmp/godot.pipe
+  ```
+

problem_statement:
Fix parse ward names with special characters

### Additional contract requirements

# Ward-name matching

Ward names in study-phase configuration are literal identifiers. A configured
`ward_name` containing characters that have special meaning in pattern syntax
(such as parentheses, brackets, dots, asterisks, or plus signs) must be
accepted and must resolve when the same ward name is looked up. The configured
phase for the lookup timestamp must be returned.

Ward-name matching must not give those characters pattern semantics. A lookup
name that is not exactly identical to a configured `ward_name` must not resolve
to that ward, even when treating the lookup name as a pattern would produce a
match.

Malformed ward-phase definitions, including definitions with unsupported keys
or an unquoted `+` separator, must be rejected with an error. The wording of
validation errors is not part of this contract.
problem_statement_base: Fix parse ward names with special characters

problem_statement:
[Unifex] User-defined state can't use user-defined types
When defining the state struct, which name is defined by `Unifex.Specs.DSL.state_type/1`, it has to be defined in a header file with the name corresponding to the the `spec.exs` file. This file is included at the top of the generated header, in which all types from `spec.exs` file are defined. The consequence of this is the fact that user-defined types cannot be used as fields of the user-defined state, because the state definition always appears before user-defined type definitions.

Forward declaration of State is also not feasible, because the generated source file calls `sizeof(UnifexState)`, for which the state needs to be defined.

### Additional contract requirements

Unifex native interfaces that declare a user-defined state type (`state_type`
in the interface specification) support state fields whose types are themselves
user-defined types — both structs and enums — declared in the same interface
specification. The generated native code for such an interface compiles cleanly
and a native library can initialize and use a state containing these fields.

This applies to every supported interface configuration: NIF, CNode, an
interface that provides both NIF and CNode from a single specification, and an
interface selected via `bundlex.exs`. The supported behavior is behavior-level:
the generated code must compile and the native functions that use the state must
work. The exact generated file names, include ordering, and byte-level generated
text are not part of this contract.

 If you want to pass enum to Unifex function on Elixir side, you have to use atom (this same, that was used in enum definition in `*.spec.exs` file). By analogy, the result of Unifex function returning enum will be visible as an atom on the Elixir side. What is important, declaration of a specific struct in `*.spec.exs` will not automatically make it available in your Elixir code - you are responsible for providing struct module on your own.
+
+### Using custom types in your state
+
+Your native `state_type` struct can hold fields of any enum or struct declared in `*.spec.exs`. Forward-declare the state above the generated header include, and put the full definition below it.
+
+For example, with this `example.spec.exs`:
+
+```elixir
+state_type "MyState"
+
+type my_struct :: %My.Struct{
+  id: int,
+  name: string
+}
+
+type my_enum :: :option_one | :option_two | :option_three
+```
+
+your `example.h` becomes:
+
+```c
+#pragma once
+
+typedef struct MyState MyState;
+
+#include "_generated/example.h"
+
+struct MyState {
+  int int_field;
+  my_struct struct_field;
+  MyEnum enum_field;
+};
+```

problem_statement:
[Governance] Update source file copyright notices to CNCF community ownership
Ahead of formal repository transfer to the `open-telemetry` GitHub organization, intellectual property declarations across source files must be updated.

**Current Header Across Files:**
```dart
// Copyright 2025, Michael Bushe, All rights reserved.
```

**Expected Transition:**  
Update headers across all `.dart` source files to comply with CNCF project IP guidelines (e.g., `Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors`).

### Additional contract requirements

# Copyright governance scope and requirements

This addendum defines the exact corpus and rules that the copyright-header
update must satisfy. It clarifies which Dart sources are swept, how they are
checked, and which files are exempt.

## Checked corpus

The governance header sweep covers exactly the hand-maintained `.dart` source
files under these repository trees:

- `lib/`
- `example/`
- `tool/`

Recursion into hidden directories (names beginning with `.`) is skipped.

Out of scope:

- The existing `test/` Dart suite is not part of this sweep and does not need
  to be re-headed.
- Loose root-level scratch scripts (for example `test_lambda_comparison.dart`
  and `test_otel_log.dart`) are not project source files and are out of scope.

## Exempt files

The following are exempt and must be left exactly as they are (they must not
gain the CNCF ownership text):

- Generated protobuf sources under `lib/proto/` (produced by the proto setup
  tooling) are generated output and excluded.
- `lib/testing.dart`
- `lib/src/trace/export/test_file_exporter.dart`
- `example/grafana/grafana_smoke_test.dart`

## Header requirements for in-scope files

Each in-scope file must satisfy all of the following:

- Carry a copyright line declaring CNCF community ownership, namely
  `Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors`, inside its leading comment block
  (the run of `//` comment lines at the top of the file, after any optional
  `#!` shebang line and following blank lines). Merely placing the text
  anywhere in the file body is not sufficient.
- Its leading copyright block must not retain any other copyright declaration
  alongside the CNCF ownership line; the prior personal notice (the
  `Michael Bushe` copyright shown in the base statement) must be replaced, not
  merely appended to.
- Executable tool scripts (the `tool/read_*.dart` utilities) must keep `#!`
  on the first line; the copyright header follows the shebang.

gain the CNCF ownership text):

## Header requirements for in-scope files

Each in-scope file must satisfy all of the following:

- Carry a copyright line declaring CNCF community ownership, namely
  `Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors`, inside its leading comment block
  (the run of `//` comment lines at the top of the file, after any optional
  `#!` shebang line and following blank lines). Merely placing the text
  anywhere in the file body is not sufficient.
- Its leading copyright block must not retain any other copyright declaration
  alongside the CNCF ownership line; the prior personal notice (the
  `Michael Bushe` copyright shown in the base statement) must be replaced, not
  merely appended to.
- Executable tool scripts (the `tool/read_*.dart` utilities) must keep `#!`
  on the first line; the copyright header follows the shebang.

problem_statement:
Security: dashboard control endpoint applies auto-approved interventions without auth
## Dashboard control endpoint: unauthenticated auto-approved interventions

**Source:** Copilot review on miniforge#1454 (D-4), plus operator direction to track a standing security/auth item.

### The exposure
The web dashboard's `POST /api/workflow/<id>/command` endpoint (`components/web-dashboard/src/ai/miniforge/web_dashboard/server/handlers.clj`, `request-workflow-intervention!`) stamps requests with `:intervention/request-source :dashboard`. After D-4 that source is in `operator/consumer.clj auto-approve-request-sources`, so the intervention skips the `:pending-human` gate and is applied immediately (pause/resume/cancel).

The auth gate in `server.clj` only enforces when `auth/enabled?` — i.e. when users are configured. On a no-auth deployment every route, including the command endpoint, is open. So an unauthenticated HTTP caller can trigger auto-approved control actions.

**Not a D-4 regression:** the pre-D-4 `.edn` command poller had the identical unauthenticated exposure — D-4 only routes it through the governed lifecycle. Shipped as-is per operator decision; this issue tracks the fix.

### Options (from the #1454 discussion)
- **(b) Require auth on the control endpoint** even when browse-auth is disabled — read-only viewing stays open, control mutations need a session. Keeps `:cli` (local, no HTTP) and `:dashboard` (now session-gated) auto-approved. Recommended.
- (a) Remove `:dashboard`/`:cli` from `auto-approve-request-sources` — parks their control at `:pending-human`; needs the approver UI (below) or the buttons go dead.

### Broader auth/security posture to review while here
- **Approver UI** for `:pending-human` interventions — without it, any narrowing of the auto-approve set produces silently-dead controls. This is the load-bearing missing piece.
- `auto-approve-request-sources` policy overall (`components/operator/src/ai/miniforge/operator/consumer.clj`): which sources are "the operator IS the human" vs. delegated (`:meta-agent`, `:api` already park).
- Whether control mutations (vs. read-only views) should always require identity regardless of the global browse-auth toggle.
- CLI `mf workflow cancel` path (`:cli` source): local trust assumption — confirm it can't be driven remotely.

### Acceptance
A no-auth dashboard cannot apply an intervention without an authenticated operator session; or the auto-approve set excludes HTTP-exposed sources and an approver UI exists so narrowing doesn't dead-button the controls.

### Additional contract requirements

This addendum states what the hidden acceptance tests for the dashboard
workflow-control fix require, without prescribing any implementation.

- **Invariant.** An unauthenticated HTTP request to a workflow control
  endpoint (`POST /api/workflow/<id>/command` and any sibling route that
  submits a `pause`/`resume`/`cancel` workflow intervention) must not
  apply an intervention without an authenticated operator session or a
  pending human decision. "Apply" means the intervention reaches the
  governed operator channel in a state that lets it be carried out
  without any further human decision, and the wire acknowledges it as
  accepted/forwarded.
- **No prescribed refusal shape.** The fix may refuse the request up
  front (any non-2xx HTTP status, any body) or accept it and park it as
  visibly pending a human decision (the response, the observed
  intervention request, or both name a pending-human state). The tests
  do not require a 401, a particular error payload, or a particular
  channel API name.
- **Observability.** The tests observe submissions through the event
  seam the dashboard itself uses to submit intervention requests; the
  observation lane is isolated per run in its own scratch directory so
  nothing ambient is mistaken for evidence. A submission that travels a
  different path to the same isolated observation lane is credited as
  observed.
- **Requester honesty.** The recorded intervention requester is always
  derived server-side (the dashboard surface, or an authenticated
  session identity); a principal the caller names in the request body
  never becomes the recorded requester on either submission format.
- **Operator channel stays usable.** When operator login IS configured,
  a valid authenticated operator session must be able to reach the
  governed control channel with each control verb; every operator action
  produces at most one intervention request.
- **Read-only browsing stays open.** On a dashboard with no operator
  login configured, GET/HEAD read-only views answer successfully; no
  login redirect or auth challenge is introduced for browsing.
- **Public machine endpoints stay alive.** The declared public
  event-ingest POST lane accepts well-formed payloads outright (2xx) on
  a no-auth dashboard; it never answers with an authentication challenge
  or a login redirect. The acceptance scope is workflow control
  endpoints only — no requirements are placed on unrelated mutation
  routes.
