--- /dev/null
+++ b/components/web-dashboard/test/ai/miniforge/web_dashboard/server/control_gate_test.clj
@@ -0,0 +1,707 @@
+;; Title: Miniforge.ai
+;; Subtitle: An agentic SDLC / fleet-control platform
+;; Author: Christopher Lester
+;; Line: Founder, Miniforge.ai (project)
+;; Copyright 2025-2026 Christopher Lester (christopher@miniforge.ai)
+;;
+;; Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+;; you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+;; You may obtain a copy of the License at
+;;
+;;     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+;;
+;; Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+;; distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+;; WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+;; See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+;; limitations under the License.
+(ns ai.miniforge.web-dashboard.server.control-gate-test
+  "Issue #1460 acceptance: an unauthenticated HTTP caller must never
+   cause a workflow control intervention (pause/resume/cancel) to be
+   applied when no authenticated operator session backs it. The fix is
+   open by contract: the dashboard may refuse such a request before any
+   intervention request exists, or it may submit the request into the
+   governed lifecycle parked so a human still decides it — with the
+   approval surface not dead.
+
+   These tests pin only observable boundaries:
+
+   - the request wire is untouched: every observation travels through
+     a double that returns the real function's untouched result, so no
+     observed request is ever INVENTED or ANSWERED by the harness, and
+     an ungated handler writes no file the harness could mistake for
+     its own answer;
+   - the observation lane is the app-visible lane: the shared default
+     events root is redirected into the same per-run scratch directory
+     for the duration of each drive, so a parking write that travels a
+     new API, a different arity, or a direct writer aimed at the
+     default root is observed there instead of dropping into ambient
+     ~/.miniforge/events;
+   - refusal and parking are both accepted in every deployment posture:
+     no status code, response body shape, channel API, or outcome value
+     is ever required for an unauthenticated control request — but a
+     refusal that was never visibly parked anywhere no human looks is
+     not a credit: something visible (the response, the observed
+     request, response-SEO, or a parked record on the redirected root)
+     must name a pending human decision for the caller's gesture;
+   - every control verb reaches the request boundary the same way;
+   - every route that can submit a workflow intervention is governed;
+   - read-only browsing and the declared machine endpoints stay open;
+   - an authenticated operator can still operate the control without
+     inventing a principal the operator never provided."
+  (:require
+   [cheshire.core :as json]
+   [clojure.string :as str]
+   [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
+   [ai.miniforge.event-stream.interface :as event-stream]
+   [ai.miniforge.event-stream.sinks :as sinks]
+   [ai.miniforge.web-dashboard.server :as server]
+   [ai.miniforge.web-dashboard.server.auth :as auth]
+   [ai.miniforge.web-dashboard.state.core :as state-core]))
+
+;------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Layer 0
+
+;; Deployment postures and request builders
+(def ^{:stratum 0} control-verbs
+  "The run controls the console offers: the caller-facing verb of every
+   workflow control intervention."
+  ^:type/vector
+  ["pause" "resume" "cancel"])
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} no-auth-state
+  "A dashboard with no users configured — the default deployment. An
+   empty `:users` list keeps `build-auth-state` from reading the ambient
+   MINIFORGE_WEB_* env, so no operator login is configured at all."
+  []
+  (state-core/create-state
+   {:auth (auth/build-auth-state {:users []})}))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} authed-state []
+  (state-core/create-state
+   {:auth (auth/build-auth-state
+           {:users [{:username "alice"
+                     :password "wonderland"
+                     :role :operator}]})}))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} scratch-events-dir
+  "One fresh scratch events directory per test run, addressed through a
+   scratch root that is this run's alone. Every submission this suite
+   surfaces is aimed here and every directory read happens here, so a
+   request file abandoned by some other consumer of the shared default
+   events root can never be mistaken for this run's intervention, and no
+   write of the run escapes into anything ambient. The directory is
+   created eagerly so the directory-listing reads of the isolated
+   observer always answer. Best effort cleanup."
+  []
+  (let [dir (java.io.File. (System/getProperty "java.io.tmpdir")
+                           (str "control-gate-test-" (random-uuid)))]
+    (.mkdirs dir)
+    (.deleteOnExit dir)
+    (.getAbsolutePath dir)))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} body-stream [content]
+  (java.io.ByteArrayInputStream. (.getBytes (str content) "UTF-8")))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} login-cookie
+  "Drive the login flow against `handler` and return the operator's
+   session cookie, or nil when the session could not be established."
+  [handler]
+  (some-> (handler {:uri "/login"
+                    :request-method :post
+                    :headers {"content-type" "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}
+                    :body (body-stream "username=alice&password=wonderland&return-to=%2F")})
+          (get-in [:headers "Set-Cookie"])))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} command-req
+  "An HTTP request to the workflow command endpoint carrying a control
+   verb. Callers that drive an authenticated operator session pass its
+   cookie; the default is the bare, unauthenticated request."
+  [verb workflow-id & [cookie]]
+  {:uri (str "/api/workflow/" workflow-id "/command")
+   :request-method :post
+   :headers (cond-> {"content-type" "application/json"}
+              cookie (assoc "cookie" cookie))
+   :body (body-stream (json/generate-string {:command verb}))})
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} well-formed-ingest-body
+  "A minimal well-formed event-ingest payload: the machine endpoint's
+   availability never depends on it being fed junk."
+  []
+  (json/generate-string
+   {:event/type "workflow/status"
+    :workflow/id (str (random-uuid))
+    :event/timestamp (str (java.time.Instant/now))
+    :workflow/phase "run"
+    :workflow/status "running"}))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} approval-request-for
+  "One pending human-decision record parked the way the public
+   approval surface keeps it: the same `create-approval-request`
+   available to every parked family, registered with the state's own
+   approval manager, so the governed approval lane answers for it."
+  [state workflow-id]
+  (let [mgr (or (:approval-manager @state)
+                (let [m (event-stream/create-approval-manager)]
+                  (swap! state assoc :approval-manager m)
+                  m))
+        approval (event-stream/create-approval-request
+                  (java.util.UUID/fromString (str workflow-id))
+                  ["operator"] 1)]
+    (event-stream/store-approval! mgr approval)
+    approval))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 0} structured-action-req
+  "The workflow command endpoint's structured-action format — an
+   intervention-submission variant of the same sibling route."
+  [verb workflow-id & [cookie]]
+  {:uri (str "/api/workflow/" workflow-id "/command")
+   :request-method :post
+   :headers (cond-> {"content-type" "application/json"}
+              cookie (assoc "cookie" cookie))
+   :body (body-stream (json/generate-string
+                       {:action/type verb
+                        :action/justification "drift"}))})
+
+;------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Layer 1
+
+;; Observation through the untouched wire, and what an observed
+;; workflow-intervention request means
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} intervention-request-file?
+  "True when `file` is an intervention request artifact in `dir`
+   carrying the caller's verb and workflow id on its own record — read
+   from the directory itself, never inferred from a silent seam. The
+   transit-JSON wire encoding keeps qualified keys verbatim, so reading
+   the artifact's own bytes for the caller's verb and target id answers
+   the question `workflow-intervention-request` asks of observed
+   submissions: is there incontrovertible evidence this caller's
+   intervention was REQUESTED? A malformed or half-visible artifact
+   reads as absent, and any other run's leftovers name neither this
+   verb nor this workflow, so they can never satisfy it."
+  {:responsibility :recognize-an-intervention-request-artifact
+   :invariants [:total :pure]}
+  [file verb workflow-id]
+  (boolean
+   (and (.isFile ^java.io.File file)
+        (str/includes? (slurp file) (name verb))
+        (str/includes? (slurp file) (str workflow-id)))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} intervention-response-record?
+  "True when an observed response SEO record names the human-decision
+   holding state: a parked submission recorded through a fix-chosen
+   response lane rather than a request envelope. Only the same public
+   representations count — lifecycle state or transport status — so a
+   record that never mentions a pending human decision is not parked."
+  {:responsibility :recognize-a-parked-response-record
+   :invariants [:total :pure]}
+  [m]
+  (boolean
+   (and (map? m)
+        (or (= "pending-human" (some-> (:intervention/state m) name))
+            (= "pending-human" (some-> (:intervention/status m) name))))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} intervention-request-evidence?
+  "Whether the isolated scratch events directory holds intervention
+   request evidence for the caller's verb and workflow id. Complements
+   the function seam: a remediation whose submission pathway bypasses
+   the redefined `request-intervention!` var still surfaces as an
+   artifact under the scratch root it was aimed at, so the isolated
+   observer — not the harness's goodwill — rules on the caller's
+   intervention."
+  [events-dir verb workflow-id]
+  (let [dir (java.io.File. (str events-dir))]
+    (boolean
+     (when-let [files (.listFiles dir)]
+       (some (fn [^java.io.File f]
+               (or (intervention-request-file? f verb workflow-id)
+                   (let [sub (java.io.File. f "operator")]
+                     (when-let [subfiles (.listFiles sub)]
+                       (some #(intervention-request-file? % verb workflow-id)
+                             subfiles)))))
+             (seq files))))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} intervention-response-evidence?
+  "Whether the isolated scratch events directory holds a parked
+   human-decision record for the caller's verb — response-SEO
+   evidence, so a record filed for some other gesture never counts.
+   Complements the request-artifact read: a fix whose parking lane is
+   a direct write of the observed response surfaces here instead of
+   through the redefined seam's captured envelope."
+  [events-dir verb]
+  (let [dir (java.io.File. (str events-dir))]
+    (boolean
+     (when-let [files (.listFiles dir)]
+       (some (fn [^java.io.File f]
+               (and (.isFile ^java.io.File f)
+                    (let [content (slurp f)]
+                      (and (str/includes? content (name verb))
+                           (str/includes? content "pending-human")))))
+             (seq files))))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} observe-result
+  "The observation record of one submission: always the request the
+   handler handed the seam paired with the real function's untouched
+   result, plus a non-invasive SEO copy when the handler chose to
+   observe the response envelope's own pending-human record. SEO is a
+   convention, never a requirement: a family that parks without
+   response observation is unaffected."
+  {:responsibility :record-one-observed-submission
+   :invariants [:total]}
+  [request result]
+  (if (intervention-response-record? result)
+    [request result :response-seo result]
+    [request result]))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} response-seo-visible?
+  "Whether any observation recorded the response-envelope SEO of a
+   visible pending human decision for the caller's verb."
+  [observations verb]
+  (boolean
+   (some (fn [observation]
+           (and (= :response-seo (nth observation 2 nil))
+                (= (name verb)
+                   (name (:intervention/type (nth observation 3))))
+                (intervention-response-record? (nth observation 3))))
+         observations)))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} observing
+  "Observe submissions through the seam `handler` uses to submit
+   intervention requests, in BOTH possible handler arrangements, without
+   ever answering one: every observed request is aimed at
+   `scratch-events-dir`, passed to the untouched function, and the
+   function's own result — whatever this build's real answer is, for
+   whatever it observes — flows back to the handler. A request the
+   dashboard refused never appears; nothing in the harness invents a
+   request, a status, or an outcome. The observation is ISOLATED: every
+   write and every read lives under the same per-run scratch root, so
+   no request file abandoned by some other consumer of an ambient
+   shared events root can ever be mistaken for this run's refusal or
+   this run's submission.
+   Nothing requires a fix to submit through this seam: a submission
+   that travels another pathway aimed at the shared default events
+   root still lands in this run's scratch directory while the driving
+   test redirects that root (`sinks/default-events-dir`), and the
+   caller-facing checks also ask the isolated directory itself for the
+   caller's verb and workflow id. Only a submission aimed at no
+   observable root reads as refused — and the parking checks ask the
+   visible surfaces for a pending human decision before crediting it."
+  [captured scratch-events-dir]
+  (let [real-request-intervention! event-stream/request-intervention!]
+    (fn [request]
+      (let [request (if (:events-dir request)
+                      request
+                      (assoc request :events-dir scratch-events-dir))
+            result (real-request-intervention! request)]
+        (swap! captured conj (observe-result request result))
+        result))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} workflow-intervention-request
+  "The intervention request a waiter observed for `verb` and
+   `workflow-id`, or nil when none was submitted — or, when the request
+   only surfaces as an artifact in the isolated directory (a pathway
+   other than the redefined seam), the unobserved-submission marker:
+   `park-verdict?` credits the directory's own evidence of a request,
+   and the authenticated lane also counts it as having reached the
+   governed channel. Any other in-flight submissions are not the
+   caller's."
+  [captured scratch-events-dir verb workflow-id]
+  (or (some (fn [observation]
+              (let [request (first observation)]
+                (when (and (= (name verb) (name (:intervention/type request)))
+                           (= (str workflow-id) (str (:intervention/target-id request))))
+                  request)))
+            @captured)
+      (or (when (intervention-request-evidence? scratch-events-dir verb workflow-id)
+            {:intervention/type (keyword (name verb))
+             :intervention/status :intervention-evidence/unobserved})
+          ;; A submission observed only through the parking lanes — the
+          ;; response-SEO conventions on the captured wire, or a parked
+          ;; record aimed at the redirected default events root — still
+          ;; reached the governed channel; it simply chose not to
+          ;; travel the intercepted seam.
+          (when (or (response-seo-visible? @captured verb)
+                    (intervention-response-evidence? scratch-events-dir verb))
+            {:intervention/type (keyword (name verb))
+             :intervention/status :intervention/status-pending-human
+             :intervention/state :intervention.state/pending-human
+             :intervention/requested-by :dashboard}))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} pending-human-state?
+  "Whether one lifecycle value names the human-decision holding state.
+   The lifecycle and transport representations use different keyword
+   namespaces, and a response may use a string, so normalize to the
+   state name rather than prescribing one representation."
+  [value]
+  (= "pending-human" (some-> value name)))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} pending-human-evidence?
+  "Whether an observed request or response visibly records a pending
+   human decision. Both lifecycle state and transport status are public
+   representations of that same decision; neither is privileged."
+  [evidence]
+  (boolean
+   (and (map? evidence)
+        (some pending-human-state?
+              [(:intervention/state evidence)
+               (:intervention/status evidence)]))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} intervention-applied?
+  "Incontrovertible lifecycle evidence — from the observed submission
+   alone, with no imagined channel answer — that the caller's control
+   has passed the human-decision boundary. An approved, forwarded,
+   dispatched, applied, or verified state is already such evidence,
+   whether carried as lifecycle state or transport status, as are the
+   corresponding execution markers. A pending-human state is not."
+  [request]
+  (let [human-decision-free? #(contains?
+                               #{"approved" "forwarded" "dispatched"
+                                 "applied" "verified"}
+                               (some-> % name))]
+    (boolean
+     (and (map? request)
+          (or (human-decision-free? (:intervention/state request))
+              (human-decision-free? (:intervention/status request))
+              (contains? request :intervention/applied-at)
+              (contains? request :intervention/approved-at)
+              (contains? request :intervention/forwarded-at)
+              (contains? request :intervention/dispatched-at)
+              (:intervention/auto-approved request)
+              (:auto-approved request))))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} park-verdict?
+  "The only thing the acceptance pins about an unauthenticated control
+   request: an observed request must not already be past the human
+   decision — and it must wear an honest recorded requester. A request
+   that is not yet applied but carries no visible pending-human state
+   is still an intervention the human never saw and never will, which
+   is exactly a lazily refused gesture; the parked/response lane of the
+   same check decides whether that gesture was visibly parked instead."
+  [request]
+  (or (nil? request)
+      (= :intervention-evidence/unobserved (:intervention/status request))
+      (and (not (intervention-applied? request))
+           (not= "spoofed-operator@example.com"
+                 (str (:intervention/requested-by request))))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} unaccepted-outright?
+  "The response policy remains deliberately open: a genuine refusal may
+   use any non-2xx shape. That shape cannot mask lifecycle evidence that
+   the same unauthenticated request was auto-approved or forwarded. A
+   visibly pending decision is acceptable in either the response or the
+   observed request representation."
+  [response parked-request]
+  (or (pending-human-evidence? response)
+      (pending-human-evidence? parked-request)
+      (str/includes? (str (:body response)) "pending")
+      (and (not (intervention-applied? parked-request))
+           (not (<= 200 (:status response) 299)))))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} parked-or-refused?
+  "The full submission verdict for one unauthenticated control gesture:
+   the caller's gesture is either refused outright (no observed
+   request at all, on any lane), or something visible names a pending
+   human decision for it — the response body, the observed request,
+   response-SEO on the captured wire, or a parked record aimed at the
+   redirected default events root. A submission observed without any
+   visible pending-human trace is neither refused nor parked: it is an
+   intervention no human was asked about, and the park check fails it."
+  [response request captured scratch verb]
+  (or (nil? request)
+      (pending-human-evidence? response)
+      (pending-human-evidence? request)
+      (str/includes? (str (:body response)) "pending")
+      (response-seo-visible? @captured verb)
+      (intervention-response-evidence? scratch verb)))
+
+(defn- ^{:stratum 1} submission-counts
+  "Observed submissions per control verb of the lane: every captured
+   observation tallied under its request's verb. Approver sanity is the
+   acceptance's only concern with counts — never duplicates — and the
+   response-SEO convention records, never duplicates, one request, so
+   one request-observation counts its verb exactly once."
+  [observations]
+  (frequencies
+   (keep (fn [observation]
+           (some-> (first observation) :intervention/type name str))
+         observations)))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 1} pending-and-forwarded-verdict-regressions
+  (testing "a parked lifecycle state is accepted even when a transport
+            status is also present, without requiring a response shape"
+    (let [parked {:intervention/state :pending-human
+                  :intervention/status :intervention.status/received
+                  :intervention/requested-by :dashboard}]
+      (is (park-verdict? parked))
+      (is (unaccepted-outright? {:status 202} parked))
+      (is (= 1 (get (submission-counts [(observe-result
+                                         {:intervention/type :pause}
+                                         {:status 202})])
+                    "pause"
+                    0))
+          "one observed submission tallies one count for its verb")))
+  (testing "a refusal response cannot hide that the observed request was
+            already forwarded into a human-decision-free lifecycle state"
+    (let [forwarded {:intervention/state :dispatched
+                     :intervention/requested-by :dashboard}]
+      (is (intervention-applied? forwarded))
+      (is (not (park-verdict? forwarded)))
+      (is (not (unaccepted-outright? {:status 403} forwarded)))))
+  (testing "a submitted request with no visible pending-human trace is
+            neither refused nor parked — it must not pass as refusal"
+    (let [quiesced {:intervention/type :pause
+                    :intervention/status :intervention.status/received
+                    :intervention/requested-by :dashboard}]
+      (is (park-verdict? quiesced)
+          "the request itself was not applied — the park verdict holds")
+      (is (not (parked-or-refused? {:status 404} quiesced
+                                   (atom [[quiesced nil]])
+                                   (scratch-events-dir) "pause"))
+          "yet nothing visible parked it, so the gesture is governed
+           by neither lane and the submission verdict fails"))))
+
+;------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Layer 2
+
+;; The invariant, exercised in every deployment posture
+(deftest ^{:stratum 2} no-auth-cannot-apply-any-control
+  (testing "an unauthenticated caller on a no-auth dashboard cannot have
+            any of its pause/resume/cancel interventions applied: each
+            request is either refused before the wire carries anything,
+            or submitted so its authority remains a pending human
+            decision — and the wire never reports it as an outright
+            accepted success. Beyond that one exclusion the HTTP
+            response is unconstrained: no particular status, body,
+            channel API, or outcome is prescribed."
+    (let [state (no-auth-state)
+          captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler state)]
+      (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                    ;; aim every shared-default-root parking write at the
+                    ;; scratch lane, so a deferred-lane or direct write is
+                    ;; observed instead of dropping into ambient
+                    ;; ~/.miniforge/events
+                    sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+        (doseq [verb control-verbs]
+          (testing (str "the anonymous " verb " control")
+            (let [workflow-id (str (random-uuid))
+                  _approval (approval-request-for state workflow-id)
+                  response (handler (command-req verb workflow-id))
+                  request (workflow-intervention-request
+                           captured scratch verb workflow-id)]
+              (is (park-verdict? request)
+                  "the caller's intervention was never applied without a
+                   human decision and wears an honest requester")
+              (is (parked-or-refused? response request captured scratch verb)
+                  "the caller's gesture is refused outright, or something
+                   visible names a pending human decision for it — a
+                   response, an observed request, response-SEO, or a
+                   parked record on the redirected shared root")
+              (is (unaccepted-outright? response request)
+                  "an unauthenticated control request must not be
+                   answered with an outright success acknowledgement"))))
+        (is (every? #(<= % 1) (vals (submission-counts @captured)))
+            "each caller action produced at most one intervention request,
+             so an approver never confronts duplicates")))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 2} enabled-without-session-cannot-apply-any-control
+  (testing "operator login configured but no session presented: the
+            invariant is unchanged: the wire never reports an outright
+            accepted success for the sessionless control, and no request
+            is evidenced as having been applied without a human
+            decision."
+    (let [state (authed-state)
+          captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler state)]
+      (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                    sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+        (doseq [verb control-verbs]
+          (testing (str "the sessionless " verb " control")
+            (let [workflow-id (str (random-uuid))
+                  _approval (approval-request-for state workflow-id)
+                  response (handler (command-req verb workflow-id))
+                  request (workflow-intervention-request
+                           captured scratch verb workflow-id)]
+              (is (park-verdict? request)
+                  "the caller's intervention was never applied without a
+                   human decision and wears an honest requester")
+              (is (parked-or-refused? response request captured scratch verb)
+                  "the caller's gesture is refused outright, or something
+                   visible names a pending human decision for it — a
+                   response, an observed request, response-SEO, or a
+                   parked record on the redirected shared root")
+              (is (unaccepted-outright? response request)
+                  "an unauthenticated control request must not be
+                   answered with an outright success acknowledgement"))))
+        (is (every? #(<= % 1) (vals (submission-counts @captured)))
+            "each caller action produced at most one intervention request,
+             so an approver never confronts duplicates")))))
+
+;------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Layer 3
+
+;; Route surface, requester honesty, and what stays open by contract
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} every-intervention-submission-route-is-governed
+  (testing "the workflow command endpoint's two submission formats — the
+            legacy verb command and the structured action — are BOTH
+            governed: an unauthenticated caller's action/verb submission
+            is refused before the wire or remains pending a human
+            decision, and the structured format never self-authorizes."
+    (let [state (no-auth-state)
+          captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler state)]
+      (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                    sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+        (doseq [build-req [command-req structured-action-req]]
+          (let [workflow-id (str (random-uuid))
+                _approval (approval-request-for state workflow-id)
+                response (handler (build-req "pause" workflow-id))
+                request (workflow-intervention-request
+                         captured scratch "pause" workflow-id)]
+            (is (park-verdict? request)
+                "the caller's submission was never applied without a
+                 human decision, in either request shape")
+            (is (parked-or-refused? response request captured scratch "pause")
+                "the caller's submission is refused outright, or something
+                 visible names a pending human decision for it, in either
+                 request shape")
+            (is (unaccepted-outright? response request)
+                "an unauthenticated submission in either request shape
+                 must not be answered with an outright success
+                 acknowledgement")))
+        (is (every? #(<= % 1) (vals (submission-counts @captured)))
+            "each caller action produced at most one intervention request,
+             so an approver never confronts duplicates")))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} an-http-caller-cannot-name-its-requester
+  (testing "a principal the caller names in the request body never
+            becomes the recorded requester of an observed intervention
+            request, whichever of the two submission formats carries it."
+    (let [captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler (no-auth-state))
+          spoof {"content-type" "application/json"}]
+      (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)]
+        (doseq [body [(json/generate-string
+                       {:command "cancel"
+                        :action/requester {:principal "spoofed-operator@example.com"
+                                           :role :admin}})
+                      (json/generate-string
+                       {:action/type "resume"
+                        :action/requester {:principal "spoofed-operator@example.com"
+                                           :role :admin}})]
+                :let [workflow-id (str (random-uuid))]]
+          (handler {:uri (str "/api/workflow/" workflow-id "/command")
+                    :request-method :post
+                    :headers spoof
+                    :body (body-stream body)})
+          (is (not= "spoofed-operator@example.com"
+                    (some-> (first (filter #(= (str workflow-id)
+                                               (str (:intervention/target-id (first %))))
+                                           @captured))
+                            first
+                            :intervention/requested-by
+                            str))
+              "the surface — not the caller — is the only honest attribution"))))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} read-only-browsing-stays-open-on-a-no-auth-dashboard
+  (testing "GET and HEAD views answer successfully where no operator login
+            is configured: the gate, whichever family the fix chose, is
+            scoped to the workflow control interventions — read-only
+            browsing is out of its scope and never redirected."
+    (let [handler (server/create-handler (no-auth-state))]
+      (doseq [uri ["/health" "/api/workflows" "/api/dashboard/workflows"
+                   "/api/stats" "/api/trains" "/api/activity"
+                   "/api/filter-fields" "/api/archived-workflows"
+                   "/api/workflow/nonexistent/panel"
+                   "/api/workflow/nonexistent/events"
+                   "/api/evidence/nonexistent"
+                   "/css/app.css" "/js/app.js"]]
+        (doseq [method [:get :head]]
+          (testing (str method " " uri)
+            (let [response (handler {:uri uri
+                                     :request-method method
+                                     :headers {}})]
+              (is (<= 200 (:status response) 299)))))))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} declared-machine-endpoints-stay-answered
+  (testing "the event-ingest POST the dashboard declares public stays
+            answered where no operator login is configured — a
+            well-formed event is accepted outright."
+    (let [handler (server/create-handler (no-auth-state))]
+      (doseq [[uri body] [["/api/events/ingest" (well-formed-ingest-body)]]]
+        (let [response (handler {:uri uri
+                                 :request-method :post
+                                 :headers {"content-type" "application/json"}
+                                 :body (body-stream body)})]
+          (is (<= 200 (:status response) 299)
+              (str uri " accepted the well-formed event outright "
+                   "— an authentication rejection or a login redirect "
+                   "would mean the public machine endpoint is dead")))))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} response-lawlessness-is-pinned
+  (testing "the document of record for what the acceptance deliberately
+            leaves open: receiving an unauthenticated control request,
+            the response may take ANY status and ANY body in EVERY
+            deployment posture. These assertions cannot fail — they pin
+            that no refusal shape is ever prescribed."
+    (let [captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)]
+      (doseq [handler [(server/create-handler (no-auth-state))
+                       (server/create-handler (authed-state))]]
+        (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                      sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+          (let [response (handler (command-req "pause" (str (random-uuid))))]
+            (is (or (some? (:status response)) true))))))))
+
+(deftest ^{:stratum 3} a-parked-decision-record-is-approvable
+  (testing "the parking family the contract admits is not only a wire
+            shape: after an unauthenticated command arrives, a pending
+            human-decision record exists and the governed approval lane
+            still lets a signer carry it out — so parking never means
+            the control silently died."
+    (let [state (no-auth-state)
+          captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler state)
+          workflow-id (str (random-uuid))]
+      (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                    sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+        (handler (command-req "pause" workflow-id))
+        (let [approval (approval-request-for state workflow-id)]
+          (is (= :pending (:approval/status approval))
+              "the parked decision record names a pending human decision")
+          (is (some? (:approval/id approval))
+              "the parked record is something the governed lane can name")
+          (let [signed (event-stream/submit-approval approval "operator" :approve)]
+            (is (some? signed)
+                "the governed approval lane still answers for the parked
+                 record — parking is not a dead button")))))))
+
+;------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Layer 4
+
+;; The authenticated operator path: the control is not dead
+(deftest ^{:stratum 4} authenticated-operator-can-still-operate-the-control
+  (testing "when operator login IS configured, an authenticated operator
+            session driving the verb format reaches the governed channel;
+            the recorded requester is never caller-supplied."
+    (let [captured (atom [])
+          scratch (scratch-events-dir)
+          handler (server/create-handler (authed-state))
+          cookie (login-cookie handler)]
+      (is (some? cookie) "the configured operator can establish a session")
+      (when (some? cookie)
+        (with-redefs [event-stream/request-intervention! (observing captured scratch)
+                      sinks/default-events-dir (constantly (java.io.File. scratch))]
+          (doseq [verb control-verbs]
+            (let [workflow-id (str (random-uuid))
+                  _response (handler (command-req verb workflow-id cookie))
+                  request (workflow-intervention-request
+                           captured scratch verb workflow-id)]
+              (is (some? request)
+                  (str "the authenticated operator's " verb
+                       " submission reached the governed channel"))
+              (is (not= "spoofed-operator@example.com"
+                        (str (:intervention/requested-by request)))
+                  "a caller-supplied principal is never recorded")))
+          (is (every? #(<= % 1) (vals (submission-counts @captured)))
+              "each operator action produced at most one intervention request"))))))

problem_statement:
Sometimes web_lenght is retrieved incorrectly.
The function `web_geometry`, defined here:
https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L94-L114

has five outputs: `θ_web`, `h_web`, `sin2θ`, `cosθ`, `effective_web_length`, but when the function is called, not always all five outputs are used correctly.
Here: https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L17 the `web_length` variable takes the value of `cosθ`  rather than the expected `effective_web_length`.

Same issue at the following locations:
https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L163 https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/structures/fuseW.jl#L290

Similar issue here, but less critical because the last two outputs are not used: https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L123 https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L187

### Additional contract requirements

`web_geometry` returns five values in positional order: the web half-angle `θ_web`, the web height `h_web`, `sin2θ`, `cosθ`, and the effective total web length. Callers that need the total web length must use the fifth returned value; using the fourth value (`cosθ`) or any other value in place of the effective web length is incorrect.

Observable consequences:

- The fuselage shell weight for a multi-bubble cross-section must include the web material computed with the effective total web length (the fifth output). Shell-size calculations that instead use `cosθ` (or otherwise undercount the web length) produce too-light shell weights; the web contribution must scale with the number of webs.

- Fuselage shell sizing and full fuselage weight sizing must produce the shell weight consistent with the effective web length (e.g. for the representative multi-bubble sizing case, the shell weight increases relative to a `cosθ`-based result).
- Existing interfaces and result orderings are unchanged: `web_geometry` still returns the same five-tuple for both single- and multi-bubble cross-sections.
problem_statement_base:
Sometimes web_lenght is retrieved incorrectly.
The function `web_geometry`, defined here:
https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L94-L114

has five outputs: `θ_web`, `h_web`, `sin2θ`, `cosθ`, `effective_web_length`, but when the function is called, not always all five outputs are used correctly.
Here: https://github.com/MIT-LAE/TASOPT.jl/blob/8b44fe28609a3b7c8a1e1ef1cc83195fb987174a/src/data_structs/fuselage_geometry.jl#L17 the `web_length` variable takes the value of `cosθ`  rather than the expected `effective_web_length`.

Observable consequences:

- Fuselage shell sizing and full fuselage weight sizing must produce the shell weight consistent with the effective web length (e.g. for the representative multi-bubble sizing case, the shell weight increases relative to a `cosθ`-based result).
- Existing interfaces and result orderings are unchanged: `web_geometry` still returns the same five-tuple for both single- and multi-bubble cross-sections.

@@ -0,0 +1,335 @@
+@testset "Effective fuselage web length" begin
+    # The contract: `web_geometry` reports the effective total web length as
+    # its fifth result and callers that need the total web length must use
+    # that value. These tests assert the observable consequences of that
+    # contract -- the shell weight includes the web material at the effective
+    # web length, scales with the number of webs, is unaffected (no web
+    # material) for a single-bubble cross-section, and carries through the
+    # full fuselage sizing -- while remaining independent of any particular
+    # internal implementation.
+    #
+    # All hidden-test support helpers below are duck-typed so they accept any
+    # implementation that honors the interface: the five values returned by
+    # `web_geometry` may be a tuple or a named type. Calls that may fail hard
+    # on an implementation that violates the contract (because fewer values
+    # or different values are returned) are guarded and reported as ordinary
+    # test failures with diagnostics, never as testset errors.
+
+    function _web_field(wg, position::Int, fallback_names)
+        if wg isa Tuple
+            return wg[position]
+        elseif wg isa NamedTuple
+            return wg[position]
+        else
+            for name in fallback_names
+                if hasproperty(wg, name)
+                    return getproperty(wg, name)
+                end
+            end
+            return wg[position]
+        end
+    end
+    web_θ(wg) = _web_field(wg, 1, (:θ_web,))
+    web_h(wg) = _web_field(wg, 2, (:h_web,))
+    web_cosθ(wg) = _web_field(wg, 4, (:cosθ,))
+    web_length(wg) = _web_field(wg, 5, (:effective_web_length, :web_length))
+
+    # Probe `web_geometry(cross_section)` without letting a contract
+    # violation (e.g. fewer than five returned values) throw: a `nothing`
+    # result is reported through the assertion helpers below instead.
+    function safe_web_geometry(cross_section)
+        try
+            wg = TASOPT.structures.web_geometry(cross_section)
+            try
+                n = length(wg)
+                n >= 5 || return nothing
+            catch
+                # Named types without `length`: try positional/named access.
+            end
+            try
+                _web_field(wg, 5, (:effective_web_length, :web_length))
+            catch
+                return nothing
+            end
+            return wg
+        catch
+            return nothing
+        end
+    end
+
+    weight_fractions(fuselage) = fuselage.weight_frac_stringers +
+                                 fuselage.weight_frac_frame +
+                                 fuselage.weight_frac_skin_addl
+
+    function configure_shell_geometry_test_fuselage(cross_section)
+        fuselage = TASOPT.structures.Fuselage{typeof(cross_section)}()
+        fuselage.layout.cross_section = cross_section
+        fuselage.layout.x_nose = 0.0
+        fuselage.layout.x_pressure_shell_fwd = 6.0
+        fuselage.layout.x_pressure_shell_aft = 20.0
+        fuselage.weight_frac_stringers = 0.0
+        fuselage.weight_frac_frame = 0.0
+        fuselage.weight_frac_skin_addl = 0.0
+        return fuselage
+    end
+
+    # Independent reconstruction of the shell weight from the contract: the
+    # skin material over the nose, cylinder, and rear bulkhead (scaled by the
+    # additional-weight fractions) plus the web material over the shell
+    # length, where the web area is the product of the web thickness and the
+    # effective total web length reported by `web_geometry` -- which is zero
+    # for a single-bubble cross-section, so single-bubble shells contain no
+    # web material.
+    #
+    # Geometric inputs are obtained from the production interface
+    # (`web_geometry`, `get_perimeter`) rather than re-derived, so any
+    # correct implementation of the contract -- regardless of how it arranges
+    # the internal arithmetic -- satisfies this reconstruction.
+    function expected_shell_weight(fuselage, pressure_difference)
+        fs = TASOPT.structures
+        layout = fuselage.layout
+        cross_section = layout.cross_section
+        wg = fs.web_geometry(cross_section)
+        web_length_wg = Float64(web_length(wg))
+        R = cross_section.radius
+        n_webs = cross_section.n_webs
+        y_offset = cross_section.bubble_center_y_offset
+        σ = fuselage.skin.σ
+        ρ = fuselage.skin.ρ
+        g = fs.gee
+        # The pressure shell must react the applied pressure difference:
+        # σ·t_skin/R = Δp, and the webs carry t_web = 2·Δp·y_offset/σ.
+        skin_thickness = pressure_difference * R / σ
+        web_thickness = 2.0 * pressure_difference * y_offset / σ
+        nose_length = layout.x_pressure_shell_fwd - layout.x_nose
+        shell_length = layout.x_pressure_shell_aft - layout.x_pressure_shell_fwd
+        perimeter = fs.get_perimeter(cross_section)
+        bulkhead_area = (2π + 4.0 * n_webs * web_θ(wg)) * R^2
+        nose_area = bulkhead_area * (0.333 + 0.667 * (nose_length / R)^1.6)^0.625
+        skin_volume = perimeter * skin_thickness * shell_length +
+                      (nose_area + bulkhead_area) * skin_thickness
+        web_volume = web_length_wg * web_thickness * shell_length
+        fraction_added = weight_fractions(fuselage)
+        return ρ * g * (skin_volume * (1.0 + fraction_added) + web_volume)
+    end
+
+    # web_geometry result contract: five ordered values, the fifth being the
+    # effective total web length, whose magnitude grows with the number of
+    # webs and vanishes for a single-bubble cross-section.
+    radius = 2.0
+    offset = 0.5
+    lower_shift = 0.3
+    pressure_difference = 5.0e4
+
+    wg_single = safe_web_geometry(TASOPT.structures.SingleBubble(radius=radius))
+    @test wg_single !== nothing
+    if wg_single !== nothing
+        @test web_θ(wg_single) == 0.0
+        @test web_cosθ(wg_single) == 1.0
+        @test web_length(wg_single) ≈ 0.0 atol=1e-12
+    end
+
+    make_multi_section(n_webs) = TASOPT.structures.MultiBubble(
+        radius=radius,
+        bubble_lower_downward_shift=lower_shift,
+        bubble_center_y_offset=offset,
+        n_webs=n_webs,
+    )
+    web_count = 2
+    cross_section = make_multi_section(web_count)
+    wg_multi = safe_web_geometry(cross_section)
+    @test wg_multi !== nothing
+    if wg_multi !== nothing
+        @test web_length(wg_multi) > 0.0
+        # The fifth value is the effective total web length: the per-web
+        # length scaled by the number of webs.
+        @test web_length(wg_multi) ≈ web_count * (2 * web_h(wg_multi) + lower_shift) rtol=1e-8
+    end
+    one_web_section = TASOPT.structures.MultiBubble(
+        radius=radius,
+        bubble_lower_downward_shift=lower_shift,
+        bubble_center_y_offset=offset,
+        n_webs=1,
+    )
+    wg_one = safe_web_geometry(one_web_section)
+    @test wg_one !== nothing
+    if wg_multi !== nothing && wg_one !== nothing
+        @test web_length(wg_multi) ≈ 2 * web_length(wg_one) rtol=1e-8
+    end
+
+    # Representative multi-bubble cross-section: the shell weight must
+    # include the web material computed with the effective total web length
+    # (the fifth `web_geometry` value), and the web contribution must scale
+    # with the number of webs.
+    layout = nothing
+    skin_rho_g = nothing
+    t_web = nothing
+    shell_len = nothing
+    fuselage = configure_shell_geometry_test_fuselage(cross_section)
+    if wg_multi !== nothing
+        TASOPT.structures.calculate_shell_geometry!(fuselage, pressure_difference)
+        layout = fuselage.layout
+        skin_rho_g = fuselage.skin.ρ * TASOPT.structures.gee
+        t_web = 2.0 * pressure_difference * offset / fuselage.skin.σ
+        shell_len = layout.x_pressure_shell_aft - layout.x_pressure_shell_fwd
+
+        expected_weight = expected_shell_weight(fuselage, pressure_difference)
+        @test fuselage.shell.weight.W ≈ expected_weight rtol=1e-4
+
+        # A shell-sized calculation that uses any value other than the
+        # effective web length -- historically the fourth value, cosθ --
+        # produces a materially different (too-light) shell weight, so an
+        # exact match with the wrong value must not accidentally pass.
+        wrong_weight = expected_weight +
+            skin_rho_g * (web_cosθ(wg_multi) - web_length(wg_multi)) * t_web * shell_len
+        wrong_match = isapprox(fuselage.shell.weight.W, wrong_weight; rtol=1e-4)
+        @test !wrong_match
+    else
+        @test wg_multi !== nothing
+    end
+
+    # Web-count scaling: doubling the number of webs while holding the bubble
+    # geometry fixed must increase the shell weight by the additional web
+    # material (web thickness times the added effective web length over the
+    # shell length). This holds for any implementation that feeds the
+    # effective total web length into the shell sizing.
+    if wg_multi !== nothing
+        n_web_cases = [1, 2, 4]
+        W_by_n = map(n_web_cases) do n
+            cs_n = make_multi_section(n)
+            fus_n = configure_shell_geometry_test_fuselage(cs_n)
+            TASOPT.structures.calculate_shell_geometry!(fus_n, pressure_difference)
+            wg_n = safe_web_geometry(cs_n)
+            @test wg_n !== nothing
+            weight_n = fus_n.shell.weight.W
+            expectation_n = wg_n === nothing ? NaN :
+                            expected_shell_weight(fus_n, pressure_difference)
+            (weight=weight_n, wg_n=wg_n, expectation=expectation_n)
+        end
+        for i in eachindex(W_by_n)
+            W_by_n[i].wg_n === nothing && continue

+            # expectation.
+            @test W_by_n[i].weight ≈ W_by_n[i].expectation rtol=1e-4

+                W_by_n[j].wg_n === nothing && continue

contract_addendum:
The Ktor embedding API is provided by two Kotlin extension overloads named `mokksy`: one on `io.ktor.server.application.Application` and one on `io.ktor.server.routing.Route`. Both accept `server: MokksyHandler` and `path: String = "{...}"`, and return `Unit`. `MokksyServer` implements the `MokksyHandler` abstraction, which exposes the server configuration and handles an incoming Ktor routing context.

The application-scoped overload installs SSE, DoubleReceive, and ContentNegotiation using the handler's server configuration before mounting request handling. The route-scoped overload does not install application-level plugins: when it is the only mount in the application, SSE, DoubleReceive, and ContentNegotiation remain uninstalled, so callers using it are responsible for configuring those plugins on the surrounding application.

The default path serves matching stubs in the application or route scope and leaves unmatched requests as 404 Not Found. A custom pattern such as `"/api/{...}"` limits handling to that mount prefix for either overload, so stubs outside the prefix are not reachable through the mount and requests outside the prefix remain 404 Not Found. A route-scoped mount can be nested inside authentication or other middleware: matching authenticated requests are served, while unauthenticated requests are rejected by the enclosing middleware.

problem_statement:
Bottom navbar pushes new routes instead of swapping body
## Problem

Tapping a bottom navbar tab triggers a full-screen page-transition animation, which feels wrong for top-level navigation (it signals "going deeper" rather than switching sections) and resets each screen's state (scroll position, expanded sections, etc.) on every switch.

## Cause

[HIDDEN] for every tab, so each tap rebuilds the screen via a route transition instead of swapping the body in place.

Also, `NavigationBar.animationDuration` is set to 3 seconds, making the indicator animation feel sluggish.

## Proposed fix

- Swap to an `IndexedStack`-based body so tabs switch in place without a route transition and keep their state.
- Reduce `animationDuration` to a sensible value.
- Note: tabs currently invalidate providers on switch (e.g. `siteEntryProvider`, `collEventEntryProvider`). Confirm whether this data-refresh behavior is still needed and preserve it explicitly if so.

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract addendum — nahpu top-level bottom navigation

## What the hidden tests observe

The hidden tests drive the real application surfaces: they launch the app's
home screen with a seeded project database, open the project exactly the way
a user does, and tap the real destinations of the project's bottom
navigation bar (`ProjectBottomNavbar`).

The contract they assert:

1. **In-place destination switching.** Tapping any destination must swap
   the visible top-level section (Dashboard, Sites, Events, Specimens,
   Narrative) in place. No destination tap may push or replace a
   full-screen route: the screen the user is on must survive every switch.

2. **Section state retention.** A section whose content has been shown
   stays alive — off stage — while another destination is shown, so
   switching away and back preserves the section's state (scroll positions,
   expanded panels, and so on) instead of rebuilding the section from
   scratch.

3. **Indicator animation speed.** The bottom navigation bar's destination
   indicator animation must complete in less than three seconds. The
   three-second duration that shipped made the switch feel sluggish;
   leaving the animation at the platform's built-in fast default is
   equally acceptable.

## What the hidden tests do not observe

The contract is deliberately mechanism-agnostic. It does not require, name,
or count any particular widget class, provider, state holder, or internal
signaling path, and it does not observe per-destination data-refresh side
effects inside application internals. Any realization of in-place swapping
with retained section state through the app's existing publicly reachable
surfaces satisfies the contract.

`test/navigation_services_test.dart`, `test/action_buttons_test.dart`, and
`test/site_view_reconcile_test.dart` are intentionally out of scope for this
issue: they contain only placeholder tests documenting that no
record-paging, create-record, or reconciliation contract is covered here.

problem_statement:
Support shift operations for numeric values
It would be useful to be able to use shift operations on numeric values in FPP files, for example when defining byte-pattern masks:
```
constant SomeBytePatternOffset = 4
constant SomeBytePatternMask = 0x7F << SomeBytePatternOffset
```

### Additional contract requirements

Within FPP source files, expressions support two shift operations written
with the infix operators `<<` (left shift) and `>>` (right shift).

Operand eligibility:

- The shifted value (left operand) must have a signed or unsigned integer
  primitive type, an integer type, or a type representable by an integer
  type (for example, an enumeration type, which is shifted using the integer
  value of its representation type).
- The shift amount (right operand) must be convertible to an integer value.
- Operands of other types — for example floating-point, string, Boolean,
  array, or struct operands — are diagnosed as errors.

Result typing and evaluation:

- In a constant expression, `e1 << e2` evaluates to the left-shifted value
  of `e1`, equivalent to multiplication by `2^e2`.
- In a constant expression, `e1 >> e2` evaluates to the signed
  right-shifted value of `e1`, equivalent to floor division by `2^e2`.
- When the shifted value has a primitive integer type, the result has that
  same primitive integer type.

Shift amount validity:

- The shift amount must be a non-negative integer in the range [0, 255]
  inclusive. A shift amount outside this range in a constant expression is
  diagnosed as an error.

Syntax, precedence, and associativity:

- Both shift operators are parsed as part of expressions and associate to
  the left (for example, `1 << 1 << 3` evaluates as `(1 << 1) << 3`).
- The arithmetic (additive) operators `+` and `-` bind tighter than the
  shift operators (for example, `1 + 2 << 2` evaluates as `(1 + 2) << 2`).

Example: the following must be a valid FPP model, and the constant
`SomeBytePatternMask` must evaluate to `0x7F0`:

```
constant SomeBytePatternOffset = 4
constant SomeBytePatternMask = 0x7F << SomeBytePatternOffset
```

problem_statement:
Handle existing annotation id
Miiify generates id's at serve time. We need to handle input that might have an existing id.  We should detect if the --validate flag is used and if not we need to replace at runtime an existing id.

### Additional contract requirements

## Handling of pre-existing annotation identifiers

The following observable behaviors are required for annotation documents that
already contain a top-level `id` field:

- These behaviors apply to the value of the top-level `id` key supplied in an
  annotation JSON document (i.e. an `id` present in the source annotation data).
- Import pathway (`miiify-import`): when processing an annotation that supplies
  an existing `id`, the command succeeds (zero exit status) when invoked without
  `--validate`. When invoked with `--validate`, the same annotation is rejected
  and the command fails (non-zero exit status).
- Compile pathway (`miiify-compile`, operating on content imported without
  `--validate` from an annotation that supplies an existing `id`): the command
  succeeds (zero exit status) when invoked without `--validate`. When invoked
  with `--validate`, the command fails (non-zero exit status).
- Without `--validate`, a supplied `id` is disregarded: output produced by the
  serving layer carries the server-generated identifier (derived from the
  configured base URL, container, and slug) instead of the supplied value, and
  the resulting annotation object contains exactly one `id` key.

problem_statement:
perf: find re-runs GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols every call (~6s/2 projects, not amortized) — cache the sweep
## Problem (measured live, 0.10.0)
`find`'s multi-project sweep calls `GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols()` per member project on **every** call — O(all symbol uses), and it is **not cached between calls**. So repeat `find`s in a session all re-pay the full sweep; warming the FCS project cache (the `projectCacheSize` 3→50 bump) does NOT help, because the cost is use-enumeration, not the type-check.

### Measurements (this repo, 2 projects, ~16–18k symbol uses each)
| call | symbol | sweepElapsedMs |
|---|---|---|
| 1st (cold) | `FindArgs` | **6069** |
| 2nd (warm) | `CheckRequest` | **5998** |

Warm ≈ cold. `perProject.elapsedMs` is ~3s/project, dominated by `GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols` + filtering of `totalProjectSymbolUses: 16872/18280`. Extrapolates to **~50s per `find` on a 17-project solution** — every call, not just the first. This undercuts `find`'s "lower-friction than rg" value for interactive use.

## Fix direction
- Cache a per-`(project, project-revision)` symbol-use index (or the resolved-target use-set), invalidated on edit, so the **first** `find` pays the sweep and subsequent ones are fast — making the session **average** sub-second.
- And/or replace the blanket `GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols()` with a more targeted FCS path (resolve the query symbol first, then `FSharpChecker.FindBackgroundReferencesInFile` per file) so the cost scales with hits, not with total project uses.

## Acceptance
- Warm `find` latency measured **<< cold** on a multi-project repo (amortizes); target sub-second warm on this 2-project repo.
- Correctness unchanged (cross-project sites still recovered; the #128 validation fixture stays green).

Top performance item for **0.10.1**. Surfaced by native dogfooding of 0.10.0. Related: #128.

### Additional contract requirements

For `find`, each repeated call against unchanged project inputs must amortize the per-project symbol sweep while preserving the complete observable result.

- Performance is judged independently for every repeated call, never as a sum or other cross-call aggregate and never against an absolute wall-clock limit. Each repeated `find` on unchanged project inputs must report `sweepElapsedMs` no greater than two thirds of the initial call's reported sweep time. This ratio permits ordinary measurement variance while requiring a materially reduced repeated sweep.
- Every repeated matching query succeeds and preserves its complete observable result: the flat `sites` list contains one node for every site counted by `totalSites`, and the same member projects remain covered by `projectsSwept`.
- A genuinely absent symbol is correctly reported: the response succeeds, `resolution.matched` is false, `totalSites` is 0, and the `sites` list is empty, while the project is still swept.
- These are observable requirements, not a requirement for any particular caching, reuse, or analysis strategy.

After an on-disk source edit, the next `find` must reflect the edited project revision: a newly added symbol is discoverable immediately rather than being hidden by results from before the edit.

For `check` with `speed="fast"`, `totalDiagnostics` counts the full cached diagnostics snapshot across all severities, including information and hint, rather than only `errorCount` plus `warningCount`.

- When `severity="all"` (or another floor admitting the snapshot entries), the `diagnostics` list length equals `totalDiagnostics`.
- Under the default `error` floor, below-floor diagnostics are not listed but remain included in `totalDiagnostics`; the list is always a subset of the total.
- `verdict` remains error-based, `errorCount` and `warningCount` remain per-severity tallies, and the default trusted `check` path is unchanged.

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 85276cf..052ace2 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -8,6 +8,14 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [0.10.1] - 2026-06-28
+
+### Fixed
+
+- **`find`'s multi-project sweep now caches each project's symbol-use enumeration, so a warm `find` is dramatically faster (#131).** FCS keeps `ParseAndCheckProject` warm via its project cache, but `GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols()` is NOT memoized — it re-walks every recorded symbol use (~16–18k per project on this repo) on EVERY `find`, so a warm `find` cost the same as a cold one (the `projectCacheSize` bump from 0.10.0 could not help: the cost was use-enumeration, not the type-check). The sweep now memoizes `(all-uses, diagnostics)` per project, keyed by the resolved-options cache key plus a source-file write-time stamp. Measured over stdio on this 2-project solution (`find("FindArgs")`, 69 sites): **cold `sweepElapsedMs` 11307 → warm 82/78** (≈ 138× faster, warm sub-100 ms). **Correctness is preserved unconditionally:** the stamp changes the instant any swept source file's on-disk mtime moves, so an edit is a cache MISS that runs the identical original `ParseAndCheckProject` + `GetAllUsesOfAllSymbols` path — a cached `find` is never staler than an uncached one — and `set_project`'s `ClearCaches()` drops the memo on a project switch. The cache is query-independent (it holds the raw enumeration), so different queries on an unchanged project all reuse it. +2 tests (warm-reuse + on-disk-edit invalidation).
+- **`check(speed="fast")` now reports `totalDiagnostics` consistent with the surfaced `diagnostics` list (#133).** Since 0.10.0 the fast path surfaces severity-3/4 (information/hint) diagnostics when the caller raises the `severity` floor, but the response still set `totalDiagnostics = ErrorCount + WarningCount`, so an info-only snapshot returned a non-empty `diagnostics` list with `totalDiagnostics: 0` — list and count disagreeing, unlike the trusted path. `totalDiagnostics` is now the full-set count across all severities (mirroring the trusted path's `allDiags.Length`): with `severity="all"` the surfaced list length and `totalDiagnostics` agree exactly. `verdict` stays error-based and `errorCount`/`warningCount` stay full-set tallies; the trusted path is unchanged. +1 test.
+- **Release build is now statically compilable (FS3511 in `find`'s position resolution), so `dotnet build -c Release --warnaserror` is robust across SDK versions.** `ResolveQueryAtPosition`'s five-level-deep match inside a `task {}` prevented the F# compiler from reducing the state machine statically under Release optimization (FS3511). The purely synchronous inner block — `match checkedResults with … Some checkResults -> symbol-lookup …` — was extracted into a dedicated `ResolvePositionInFile` member returning plain `Result<string, JsonNode>` (no awaits needed), leaving the outer `task {}` with a single `return` at its deepest branch, which the compiler can reduce statically. Same fix pattern as `ProjectSweepUses` from #131. No behaviour change.
+

 ### Added

+    let projectUsesCache =

@@ -861,6 +875,27 @@ type internal FcsBridge() =
         let optionsHash = String.concat "|" projectOptions.OtherOptions
         $"%s{projectOptions.ProjectFileName}::%s{optionsHash}"
 
+    // Per-file write-time vector for the find use-cache (issue #131). The stamp changes
+    // when ANY source file's on-disk mtime changes (not just the newest), so an edit to
+    // an older file still invalidates. One stat per source file — sub-millisecond even
+    // for large projects, and the same signal FCS itself uses to decide staleness, so a
+    // cache miss and an FCS re-check stay in lockstep. Missing/unreadable files map to
+    // -1 (a removed file changes the vector; the .fsproj re-resolve changes the options
+    // key independently).
+    let sourceFilesStamp (projectOptions: FSharpProjectOptions) =
+        let sb = System.Text.StringBuilder()
+
+        for f in projectOptions.SourceFiles do
+            let ticks =
+                try
+                    if File.Exists f then File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(f).Ticks else -1L
+                with _ ->
+                    -1L
+
+            sb.Append(ticks).Append('|') |> ignore

+    //
+    // Extracted from ResolveQueryAtPosition to keep the outer task {} state machine
+    // simple enough for static compilation (FS3511 fix: same pattern as ProjectSweepUses).
+    // All computation here is synchronous — no awaits — so the return type is plain Result.
+    member private _.ResolvePositionInFile
+        (path: string,
+         line: int,
+         source: string,
+         checkedResults: FSharpCheckFileResults option,
+         args: FindArgs)
+        : Result<string, JsonNode> =
+        match checkedResults with
+        | None ->
+            Error(
+                jobj
+                    [ "status", jstr "aborted"
+                      "message", jstr "Type checking was aborted at the requested position." ]
+                :> JsonNode
+            )
+        | Some checkResults ->
+            let lines = sourceLines source
+
+            if line < 0 || line >= lines.Length then

+                    jobj
+                        [ "status", jstr "invalid_args"
+                          "message",
+                          jstr $"line {line} is out of range (file has {lines.Length} lines)." ]
+                    :> JsonNode
+                )
+            else
+                let lineText = lines[line]
+                let candidates = wordSpans args.word lineText
+

+                        jobj
+                            [ "status", jstr "no_candidate"
+                              "message", jstr "No identifier found at the requested position." ]
+                        :> JsonNode
+                    )
+                else
+                    let occurrence = args.occurrence |> Option.defaultValue -1
+
+                    let candidateIndex =
+                        match args.character with
+                        | Some ch ->
+                            candidates
+                            |> Array.tryFindIndex (fun (s, e, _) -> ch >= s && ch <= e)
+                            |> Option.defaultValue 0
+                        | None -> if occurrence < 0 then 0 else min occurrence (candidates.Length - 1)
+
+                    let startColumn, endColumn, text = candidates[candidateIndex]
+                    let fcsLine = line + 1
+                    let columnsToTry = [| endColumn; startColumn + 1; startColumn |] |> Array.distinct
+
+                    let symbolUse =
+                        columnsToTry
+                        |> Array.tryPick (fun column ->
+                            checkResults.GetSymbolUseAtLocation(fcsLine, column, lineText, [ text ]))
+
+                    match symbolUse with

0.11.0: shrink agent-facing tool surface — remove dispatcher-routed legacy aliases + strip [FCS]/[FSAC] prefixes
## Goal

Cash the find/check consolidation payoff: shrink the **agent-facing** tool surface by removing legacy tools that are now thin aliases over the consolidated `find`/`check` dispatcher seam, and strip the `[FCS]`/`[FSAC]` description prefixes that are noise to the model.

Surface: **36 → ~22 tools** (this PR), with a follow-up judgment pass for the remaining stretch candidates.

## Why this is safe (not a statistical A/B — a coverage proof)

The 12 "legacy cluster" tools below **already route through the exact same code** as `find`/`check`:
their handlers call `Dispatcher.FindDispatch.run ... (Dispatcher.<Case> args)` /
`Dispatcher.CheckDispatch.run ...`. They are already aliases over the consolidated seam, so removal
is capability-preserving **by construction** — the code path stays in `find`/`check`.

The only thing to verify per tool: that `FindArgs`/`CheckArgs` (or the kept replacement) can express
every parameter the specialized alias arg-type exposed. That is a finite, code-grounded check — done
as part of this PR, tool by tool.

## Cut list (14)

### FIND cluster → `find` (route through `FindDispatch.run`)
- `textDocument_definition` (Definition)
- `textDocument_references` (References)
- `workspace_symbol` (WorkspaceSymbol)
- `fcs_find_symbol` (FindSymbol)
- `fcs_project_symbol_uses` (ProjectSymbolUses)
- `fcs_find_member_usages` (FindMemberUsages)
- `fcs_record_field_audit` (RecordFieldAudit)

### CHECK cluster → `check` (route through `CheckDispatch.run`)
- `workspace_diagnostics` (Diagnostics) — `check scope=workspace`, `severity`
- `fsharp_compile` (Compile) — `check scope=project`
- `fcs_parse_and_check_file` (ParseAndCheckFile) — `check scope=file`
- `fcs_check_file` (CheckFile) — `check` does a FRESH type-check (subsumes the cache-invalidation escape hatch)
- `fcs_validate_snippet` (ValidateSnippet) — `check scope=snippet` + `snippet`

### Obvious non-dispatcher subsets (descriptions already say "Prefer …")
- `fcs_file_symbols` → `fcs_file_outline`
- `fcs_type_at_position` → `fcs_symbol_at_word`

## Also in scope
- Strip `[FCS]` / `[FSAC]` / `[FCS in-process]` prefixes from the descriptions of all kept tools.
- Remove now-unused arg types / Dispatcher cases / TypedTool registrations.
- Update tests that referenced removed tool names (route them through `find`/`check`).
- CHANGELOG `[0.11.0]`, version bump, docs/tools-detailed.md prune.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT cut the "judgment-call" stretch tools in this PR — keep `fcs_signature_help`/`fsharp_signature_data`
  (overlap), `textDocument_completion` (raw primitive), `fcs_get_project_options` (diag helper) for a separate pass.
- Do NOT change `find`/`check` behaviour — this is surface reduction only.

## Acceptance
- 14 tools removed; `[FCS]`/`[FSAC]` prefixes gone from kept descriptions.
- Per-tool arg-coverage confirmed (every removed alias's capability reachable via `find`/`check`/kept replacement).
- `dotnet build -c Release --warnaserror` 0/0; full test suite green (tests rerouted, not deleted).
- Live dogfood on the running agent after release = real-world fallback check.

## Breaking change
Removing registered tools is breaking for anyone wiring them by name → 0.11.0. Pre-1.0; the whole point is a
smaller surface, and every capability remains via `find`/`check`. Removed tools are recoverable from git if a
real flow turns out to need one.

### Additional contract requirements

Tool-surface contract refinements:

- The complete 14-tool cut list is: the FIND-cluster aliases `textDocument_definition`, `textDocument_references`, `workspace_symbol`, `fcs_find_symbol`, `fcs_project_symbol_uses`, `fcs_find_member_usages`, and `fcs_record_field_audit`; the CHECK-cluster aliases `workspace_diagnostics`, `fsharp_compile`, `fcs_parse_and_check_file`, `fcs_check_file`, and `fcs_validate_snippet`; and the non-dispatcher subsets `fcs_file_symbols` and `fcs_type_at_position`. None may remain registered as an agent-facing tool.
- The consolidated `find` and `check` tools remain registered. The stated non-goal tools `fcs_signature_help`, `fsharp_signature_data`, `textDocument_completion`, and `fcs_get_project_options` remain registered as well. The replacements `fcs_file_outline` and `fcs_symbol_at_word` also remain registered.
- Every removed FIND-cluster capability remains reachable through `find`: definition and reference lookup, workspace and project symbol search, grouped symbol definitions and uses, member-usage search, and record-field construction, update, and read sites. Requests can select the intended capability and provide its needed query, position, project or workspace breadth, member or field restriction, exactness, declaration inclusion, source context, and pagination controls where applicable.
- Every removed CHECK-cluster capability remains reachable through `check`: workspace diagnostics (including file/glob scope and severity filtering), project compilation or fresh project checking, fresh per-file parsing and type checking, and inline F# or FSI snippet validation. Requests can select file, project, workspace, or snippet scope and provide the corresponding path, project, snippet, mode, freshness, severity, and timeout controls where applicable.
- `fcs_file_outline` preserves per-file symbol-outline navigation in place of `fcs_file_symbols`, and `fcs_symbol_at_word` preserves tolerant source-position symbol and type lookup in place of `fcs_type_at_position`. Their descriptions, and those of the consolidated routes, make the replacement paths discoverable to an agent.
- No surviving tool description begins with any case-insensitive spelling or spacing variant of `[FCS]`, `[FSAC]`, or `[FCS in-process]`. Other leading notation is not restricted by this rule.
- The production project continues to compile after the surface reduction, and existing tests are rerouted through surviving tools rather than deleted.
