diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index d58931d..7cfd8f9 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -8,6 +8,26 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [0.11.0] - 2026-06-28
+
+### Removed
+
+- **BREAKING — the agent-facing MCP tool surface shrank from 36 → 22 tools: 14 thin single-tool aliases over the consolidated `find` / `check` were removed (#136).** Since 0.10.0 these were already steered toward `find` / `check` via `Prefer …` description hints; #136 completes the consolidation by dropping the registrations. The backend `FcsBridge` / `FsAutoCompleteBridge` methods (`FindSymbol`, `References`, `WorkspaceSymbol`, `CompileProject`, `ParseAndCheckFile`, `ValidateSnippet`, etc.) are unchanged — only the agent-facing tool registrations were removed. Removed tools, grouped:
+  - **find cluster (7):** `textDocument_definition`, `textDocument_references`, `workspace_symbol`, `fcs_find_symbol`, `fcs_project_symbol_uses`, `fcs_find_member_usages`, `fcs_record_field_audit`
+  - **check cluster (5):** `workspace_diagnostics`, `fsharp_compile`, `fcs_parse_and_check_file`, `fcs_check_file`, `fcs_validate_snippet`
+  - **low-level position/symbol (2):** `fcs_file_symbols`, `fcs_type_at_position`
+
+  Every capability remains reachable: cross-project **and** single-project symbol / reference / record-field-set / member-usage search via `find` (with `kind` + `scope` narrowing); type-check verdicts for file / project / workspace / inline snippet via `check`; raw per-file symbol extraction via `fcs_file_outline`; and position- or unsaved-buffer symbol / type lookups via `fcs_symbol_at_word`.
+
+### Changed
+
+- **`[FCS in-process]` / `[FSAC]` / `[meta]` description prefixes were stripped from all 22 remaining tool descriptions — each now leads with its action verb.** The implementation-layer tag leaked an internal backend distinction into the most valuable routing position (the first token the agent reads) without helping the call/skip decision. The `ToolDescriptionSchemaTests` (`dotnet test` gate) and `scripts/audit-tool-descriptions.py` schema rule were inverted accordingly: from "every description must start with a recognized tag" to "no description may start with a `[`-bracket tag", and the overlap-pair set was pruned to the three pairs whose members both still exist (`fcs_referenced_symbols`↔`fcs_nuget_types`, `fcs_nuget_types`↔`fcs_nuget_members`, `fcs_signature_help`↔`fsharp_signature_data`). `docs/tool-description-schema.md` documents the new rule.
+- **`find`'s description was rewritten to advertise member call-site search and to drop now-stale references.** A tool-selection A/B (120 agents — the pre-consolidation 34-tool surface vs this 22-tool surface) caught a single regression from the removals: with the dedicated `fcs_find_member_usages` gone, agents fell back to `rg` for "find call sites of a `.Member()` on a type" in 5/5 trials instead of reaching for `find` — its old text under-sold the member-usage intent and still named the deleted `fcs_find_symbol` / `fcs_record_field_audit`. The rewrite leads with the four intents (definitions, references, record-field set sites, member call-sites on a type `x.Foo`) and contrasts against textual `rg`. A re-test dropped member-usage fallback from 100% → 0% (36/36 trials chose `find`), no regression on the other find tasks.
+
+### Notes
+
+- **Accepted limitations of the consolidated path (carried over from the 0.10.0 `find` / `check` design):** `find` / `check` do not accept `text` (unsaved buffer content) or raw `projectOptions` / `workspacePath` overrides — Write the file to disk first, then call `find` / `check`. Position-based and unsaved-buffer symbol / type lookups remain available through `fcs_symbol_at_word`.
+
 ## [0.10.1] - 2026-06-28
 
 ### Fixed

problem_statement:
Bad indentation in Python if/else blocks?
Hi, I've been trying this plugin out and it seems to be working pretty nicely. One issue I ran into is in Python code:

```
if foo:
	bar()
elif baz:
	blah()
```

EDIT: I misdescribed the situation, it's possible this behavior is intended. If I delete line 2 (dd) then paste above ([p), it will paste `bar()` instead of `    bar()`, indenting to the `else baz:` line instead of inside the `if foo:` block. I initially assumed this was a bug but I can see how the "smart" behavior here is ambiguous and either option is valid.

### Additional contract requirements

The issue report concerns linewise pastes around Python `if`/`elif` blocks:
the deleted `if`-branch body line must be restored cleanly (content intact,
surrounding lines unchanged) and placed one indentation level inside the
branch it belongs to, not as a sibling of the branch header.

In particular:

- Pasting (`p` / `]p`) on an `if foo:` header whose branch body is empty
  because the very next line is an `elif` or `else` header at the same
  indent must place the pasted content inside that branch, indented one
  level deeper than the header line.
- Pasting back above an `elif` header with `[p` / `P` (restore-at-boundary)
  must restore the deleted body line inside the branch at body indent,
  without mangling its content or corrupting any surrounding line.

These requirements describe the expected acceptance behavior for the
reported scenario; they do not prescribe any particular implementation.

+    end
+  end

problem_statement:
perf(auth): Validate OAuth2 provider endpoints once at construction, not per-request
## Summary

Validate OAuth2 provider endpoints once at construction time instead of on every token request, eliminating redundant DNS resolution overhead at scale.

## User Story

As Jess, I want my OAuth2 token requests to be fast so that my application can handle high throughput without unnecessary latency.

## Context

Currently `validateSecureUrlWithDns` is called on every token request in `Auth.OAuth2.Client.requestTokens`. At 50k req/s this creates significant overhead:
- DNS resolution on every request
- Repeated validation of static provider endpoints

**Problem:**
- Token endpoints are provider configuration, not user input
- They don't change between requests
- DNS resolution can be slow and adds latency

## Proposed Solution

1. Create a `ValidatedProvider` type that can only be constructed via validation
2. Validate provider endpoints once at construction/initialization
3. `exchangeCode`, `refreshToken` etc. accept `ValidatedProvider` instead of `Provider`
4. Skip per-request DNS validation for already-validated endpoints

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ValidatedProvider` type created with smart constructor
- [ ] Validation happens once at provider construction
- [ ] Token requests use pre-validated endpoints
- [ ] Performance improvement measurable (benchmark before/after)
- [ ] Documentation updated with new pattern

[HIDDEN]

## Effort Estimate

**effort: 3** - Requires type changes that propagate through the API, but the pattern is straightforward.

---

Related: #271, #267

💬 **Questions?** [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/neohaskell) - we'd love to help!

### Additional contract requirements

The OAuth2 provider-validation change has the following public contract.

* `Auth.OAuth2` exports the abstract `ValidatedProvider` type, the
  `getValidatedProvider :: ValidatedProvider -> Provider` accessor, and
  `validateProvider :: Provider -> Task OAuth2Error ValidatedProvider`.
  `validateProvider` validates the authorization and token endpoints before it
  returns a wrapper. Both endpoints must be HTTPS and must satisfy the
  existing SSRF protections, including rejection of private and loopback
  addresses and DNS-based address validation. An invalid endpoint is reported
  as `EndpointValidationFailed`.
* When endpoint DNS resolution is performed by `validateProvider` and a
  hostname cannot be resolved, for example because the environment provides
  no working DNS resolver, `validateProvider` fails instead of returning a
  wrapper, and the reported failure message states that DNS resolution
  failed.
* `Auth.OAuth2.Types` provides
  `unsafeValidatedProvider :: Provider -> ValidatedProvider` solely for
  isolated test fixtures whose deliberately local endpoints cannot satisfy
  production endpoint validation. Application code must construct providers
  with `validateProvider`.
* The high-throughput token operations are exported by `Auth.OAuth2` with the
  following signatures:

  ```haskell
  exchangeCodeValidated :: ValidatedProvider -> ClientId -> ClientSecret -> RedirectUri -> AuthorizationCode -> Task OAuth2Error TokenSet
  exchangeCodeWithPkceValidated :: ValidatedProvider -> ClientId -> ClientSecret -> RedirectUri -> AuthorizationCode -> CodeVerifier -> Task OAuth2Error TokenSet
  refreshTokenValidated :: ValidatedProvider -> ClientId -> ClientSecret -> RefreshToken -> Task OAuth2Error TokenSet
  ```

  These operations accept only a `ValidatedProvider` and reuse the endpoint
  validation completed during construction; they do not perform endpoint
  validation again for an individual token request.
* `Auth.OAuth2.Provider` exports `ValidatedOAuth2ProviderConfig` as a concrete
  record type whose constructor `ValidatedOAuth2ProviderConfig` and record
  selectors are exported. It carries the original unvalidated `Provider`
  configuration, the pre-validated `ValidatedProvider` used for token
  operations, and the same provider-integration fields as
  `OAuth2ProviderConfig`: `provider`, `validatedProvider`, `clientId`,
  `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, `scopes`, `onSuccess`, `onFailure`,
  `onDisconnect`, `successRedirectUrl`, and `failureRedirectUrl`.
  `OAuth2RouteDeps.providers` is a map of these validated configurations, so
  applications validate provider configuration during initialization before
  creating OAuth2 routes.

The existing non-pre-validated OAuth2 operations remain available for callers
that have not yet moved provider initialization to the validated flow.

+-- | Make a token request to a pre-validated provider endpoint.
+-- SECURITY: Endpoint URL validation is SKIPPED because ValidatedProvider
+-- guarantees the URL was validated at construction time.
+-- This is the high-performance path for 50k+ req/s scenarios.
+--
+-- AUDIT: Logs security events for EU/GDPR compliance:
+-- * Token request attempts (with sanitized endpoint)
+-- * Token request failures (with error category, no secrets)
+-- * Token request successes (no token values logged)
+requestTokensValidated ::
+  Text ->
+  [(Text, Text)] ->
+  Task OAuth2Error TokenSet
+requestTokensValidated tokenEndpoint formParams = do
+  -- AUDIT: Log token request attempt (sanitized - no secrets)
+  let sanitizedEndpoint = sanitizeUrlForAudit tokenEndpoint
+  Console.print [fmt|[OAuth2 Audit] Token request to #{sanitizedEndpoint} (pre-validated)|]
+    |> Task.ignoreError
+  let request =
+        Http.request
+          |> Http.withUrl tokenEndpoint
+          |> Http.withTimeout 10 -- 10s timeout for OAuth2 token requests
+  let formArray = formParams |> Array.fromLinkedList
+  result <-
+    Http.postForm @TokenResponse request formArray
+      |> Task.mapError parseHttpError
+      |> Task.asResult
+  case result of
+    Err err -> do
+      -- AUDIT: Log failure (error category only, no secrets)
+      Console.print [fmt|[OAuth2 Audit] Token request failed: #{sanitizedEndpoint} - #{errorCategory err}|]
+        |> Task.ignoreError
+      Task.throw err
+    Ok response -> do
+      -- AUDIT: Log success (no token values)
+      Console.print [fmt|[OAuth2 Audit] Token request succeeded: #{sanitizedEndpoint}|]
+        |> Task.ignoreError
+      Task.yield
+        TokenSet
+          { accessToken = mkAccessToken response.access_token
+          , refreshToken = response.refresh_token |> fmap mkRefreshToken
+          , expiresInSeconds = response.expires_in
+          }
+
+
+-- | Sanitize URL for audit logs - extract only scheme://host:port
+-- SECURITY: Never log full URLs which may contain query parameters with secrets
+sanitizeUrlForAudit :: Text -> Text
+sanitizeUrlForAudit urlText = do
+  let urlString = Text.toLinkedList urlText
+  case URI.parseURI urlString of
+    Nothing -> "<invalid-url>"
+    Just uri -> do
+      let scheme = Text.fromLinkedList (URI.uriScheme uri)
+      case URI.uriAuthority uri of
+        Nothing -> scheme
+        Just auth -> do
+          let host = Text.fromLinkedList (URI.uriRegName auth)
+          let port = Text.fromLinkedList (URI.uriPort auth)
+          Text.concat [scheme, "//", host, port]
+
+
+-- | Extract error category for audit logging (no secrets)
+errorCategory :: OAuth2Error -> Text
+errorCategory err = case err of
+  TokenRequestFailed _ -> "token_request_failed"
+  InvalidGrant _ -> "invalid_grant"
+  InvalidClient _ -> "invalid_client"
+  ScopeDenied _ -> "scope_denied"
+  MalformedResponse _ -> "malformed_response"
+  NetworkError _ -> "network_error"
+  EndpointValidationFailed _ -> "endpoint_validation_failed"
+  InvalidState _ -> "invalid_state"
+  InvalidPkceVerifier _ -> "invalid_pkce_verifier"
+  InvalidRedirectUri _ -> "invalid_redirect_uri"
+
+

 -- If the error message contains OAuth2 error JSON, parse it to specific error type.
 -- Otherwise, return a generic NetworkError.

problem_statement:
feat(RequestContext): type `timestamp` as `DateTime` to remove `time` leak from consumers
## Summary

`RequestContext.timestamp` is currently typed as `UTCTime` (from the `time` package) at [`core/service/Service/Auth.hs:74`](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/blob/main/core/service/Service/Auth.hs#L74). Every consumer that records this value on an event has to convert it to `DateTime` (the `nhcore` type), and the only way to do that today is to import `Data.Time.Clock`, `Data.Time.Clock.POSIX`, and `GHC.Real` — all outside `nhcore`.

The stated invariant for NeoHaskell projects is that *only* `nhcore` should appear on the import surface. Since the context is constructed inside `nhcore` and consumed by `nhcore`-only code, the `UTCTime` in the field signature is a leak with no upside: nothing in the public API actually needs the `time` type.

## Proposed change

Retype the field directly:

```haskell
-- core/service/Service/Auth.hs
data RequestContext = RequestContext
  { user      :: Maybe UserClaims
  , files     :: Map FileRef ResolvedFile
  , requestId :: Uuid
  , timestamp :: DateTime   -- was: UTCTime
  }
```

Construction sites already call `Clock.getCurrentTime` and would switch to `DateTime.now` (which already exists at [`core/core/DateTime.hs`](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/blob/main/core/core/DateTime.hs)):

- `emptyContext` — use a `DateTime` built from `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0` instead of the hand-rolled `UTCTime (fromGregorian 1970 1 1) 0`.
- `anonymousContext` / `authenticatedContext` — replace `GhcClock.getCurrentTime |> Task.fromIO` with `DateTime.now`.

After this change, `Service.Auth` no longer needs to import `Data.Time`, `Data.Time.Calendar`, or `Data.Time.Clock`, and consumers stamp events with `ctx.timestamp` directly — no converter, no foreign imports.

## Why this over a `UTCTime → DateTime` converter

The original framing of this issue (adding `DateTime.fromUtcTime`) treated the `UTCTime` in `RequestContext` as load-bearing. It isn't:

- `DateTime` is a `newtype` around `UTCTime`, so there's no representational cost to switching.
- The conversion has no information for the consumer to act on — it's pure boilerplate. Better to never produce the wrong type in the first place than to ship a converter every consumer is obliged to call.
- A converter would still leave the leak in the *type signature* of `RequestContext`, even if a re-export hid the import. Retyping the field removes the leak at the source.

## Scope

- Touches `Service.Auth` (field type + three constructors).
- Anywhere inside `nhcore` that reads `ctx.timestamp` and expects `UTCTime` needs to either work with `DateTime` directly or call an internal accessor. A quick grep for `\.timestamp` and `RequestContext` should bound this.
- Test helpers in `core/testlib/Test/Service/Command/` that build a `RequestContext` will need the same retype.

## Compatibility

problem_statement_base:
feat(RequestContext): type `timestamp` as `DateTime` to remove `time` leak from consumers
## Summary

`RequestContext.timestamp` is currently typed as `UTCTime` (from the `time` package) at [`core/service/Service/Auth.hs:74`](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/blob/main/core/service/Service/Auth.hs#L74). Every consumer that records this value on an event has to convert it to `DateTime` (the `nhcore` type), and the only way to do that today is to import `Data.Time.Clock`, `Data.Time.Clock.POSIX`, and `GHC.Real` — all outside `nhcore`.

The stated invariant for NeoHaskell projects is that *only* `nhcore` should appear on the import surface. Since the context is constructed inside `nhcore` and consumed by `nhcore`-only code, the `UTCTime` in the field signature is a leak with no upside: nothing in the public API actually needs the `time` type.

## Proposed change

Retype the field directly:

```haskell
-- core/service/Service/Auth.hs
data RequestContext = RequestContext
  { user      :: Maybe UserClaims
  , files     :: Map FileRef ResolvedFile
  , requestId :: Uuid
  , timestamp :: DateTime   -- was: UTCTime
  }
```

Construction sites already call `Clock.getCurrentTime` and would switch to `DateTime.now` (which already exists at [`core/core/DateTime.hs`](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/blob/main/core/core/DateTime.hs)):

- `emptyContext` — use a `DateTime` built from `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0` instead of the hand-rolled `UTCTime (fromGregorian 1970 1 1) 0`.
- `anonymousContext` / `authenticatedContext` — replace `GhcClock.getCurrentTime |> Task.fromIO` with `DateTime.now`.

After this change, `Service.Auth` no longer needs to import `Data.Time`, `Data.Time.Calendar`, or `Data.Time.Clock`, and consumers stamp events with `ctx.timestamp` directly — no converter, no foreign imports.

## Why this over a `UTCTime → DateTime` converter

The original framing of this issue (adding `DateTime.fromUtcTime`) treated the `UTCTime` in `RequestContext` as load-bearing. It isn't:

- `DateTime` is a `newtype` around `UTCTime`, so there's no representational cost to switching.
- The conversion has no information for the consumer to act on — it's pure boilerplate. Better to never produce the wrong type in the first place than to ship a converter every consumer is obliged to call.
- A converter would still leave the leak in the *type signature* of `RequestContext`, even if a re-export hid the import. Retyping the field removes the leak at the source.

## Scope

- Touches `Service.Auth` (field type + three constructors).
- Anywhere inside `nhcore` that reads `ctx.timestamp` and expects `UTCTime` needs to either work with `DateTime` directly or call an internal accessor. A quick grep for `\.timestamp` and `RequestContext` should bound this.
- Test helpers in `core/testlib/Test/Service/Command/` that build a `RequestContext` will need the same retype.

## Compatibility

Breaking for any out-of-tree consumer that reads `ctx.timestamp` as `UTCTime`. The expected migration in consumer code is *deletion*: drop the local `utcTimeAsDateTime` helper and the `time` / `GHC.Real` imports, and use `ctx.timestamp` directly. That's a net-negative diff for every affected file — the breakage is the feature.

## Notes

Spotted by an automated scan flagging non-`nhcore` imports in consumer projects. Six command files in `evoca-payment-gateway` currently each carry a duplicated `utcTimeAsDateTime` helper plus the three foreign imports; all six become a single-line cleanup once the field is retyped.

@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+# ADR-0056: Retype `RequestContext.timestamp` as `DateTime`
+
+## Status
+
+Proposed
+
+## Context
+
+### Current State
+
+`RequestContext` lives in [`core/service/Service/Auth.hs`](../../core/service/Service/Auth.hs)
+and is the value every command's `decide` function receives. One of its fields
+is `timestamp :: UTCTime`, where `UTCTime` is the type from the upstream `time`
+package.
+
+```haskell
+data RequestContext = RequestContext
+  { user      :: Maybe UserClaims
+  , files     :: Map FileRef ResolvedFile
+  , requestId :: Uuid
+  , timestamp :: UTCTime   -- leaks `Data.Time` into every consumer
+  }
+```
+
+Inside `nhcore`, there is no reader of `ctx.timestamp` at all: `grep` for
+`.timestamp` across `core/` and `testbed/` returns nothing. The field exists
+purely so out-of-tree consumers can stamp events with a request time.
+
+Out of the framework, every consumer that reads `ctx.timestamp` and wants to
+record it on an event has to convert it to `DateTime` (the `nhcore`
+[newtype around `UTCTime`](../../core/core/DateTime.hs)). The only way to do
+that today is for the consumer to import `Data.Time.Clock`,
+`Data.Time.Clock.POSIX`, and `GHC.Real`, and hand-roll a converter. The stated
+invariant for NeoHaskell projects is that _only_ `nhcore` types may appear on
+the import surface, so the field signature is a leak with no upside.
+
+### Use Cases
+
+- A consumer command stamps an event with the request time:
+  `OrderPlaced { placedAt = ctx.timestamp, ... }`. Today, `placedAt` must
+  either be typed as `UTCTime` (forcing the `time` import on the event type)
+  or be paired with a hand-rolled `utcTimeAsDateTime` helper.
+- A test helper builds a `RequestContext` for a decider unit test. Today, the
+  helper imports `Data.Time.Clock` and `Data.Time.Calendar` to construct a
+  literal `UTCTime`. With `DateTime`, it calls `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0`.
+- An anonymous or authenticated request is built from inside a transport. The
+  transport calls `Clock.getCurrentTime |> Task.fromIO`. With `DateTime`, it
+  calls `DateTime.now`.
+
+### Design Goals
+
+1. **No `Data.Time` on the public import surface.** `Service.Auth` is
+   re-exported through the framework's command-handler scaffolding. Anything
+   on the type signature of `RequestContext` is on Jess's import surface.
+   `UTCTime` is not.
+2. **Zero behavioural change.** `DateTime` is a `newtype` over `UTCTime`. The
+   wire representation, the JSON encoding, and the value of "now" are all
+   bit-identical to today.
+3. **Net-negative diff for consumers.** Every consumer file that currently
+   defines a `utcTimeAsDateTime` helper plus three `Data.Time*` /
+   `GHC.Real` imports gets to delete them. The breakage is the feature.
+
+### GitHub Issue
+
+- [#629: feat(RequestContext): type `timestamp` as `DateTime` to remove `time` leak from consumers](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/issues/629)
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Retype the field
+
+`RequestContext.timestamp` is changed from `UTCTime` to `DateTime`. The
+re-export and module surface are otherwise unchanged.
+
+```haskell
+data RequestContext = RequestContext
+  { user      :: Maybe UserClaims
+  , files     :: Map FileRef ResolvedFile
+  , requestId :: Uuid
+  , timestamp :: DateTime   -- was: UTCTime
+  }
+```
+
+| Candidate                                                                          | Verdict    | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
+| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Add `DateTime.fromUtcTime :: UTCTime -> DateTime` and leave the field as `UTCTime` | Rejected   | Ships a converter every consumer must call. The `UTCTime` stays in the public type signature, so the import-surface leak is unfixed. The original framing of #629 took this path; it was abandoned during the review.                                     |
+| Re-export `UTCTime` from `nhcore`                                                  | Rejected   | Removes the import-line leak only. The _type_ on the field is still from an external package, so any change in the upstream `time` API still ripples into consumer code. Treats the symptom, not the leak.                                                |
+| **Retype the field directly to `DateTime`**                                        | **Chosen** | `DateTime` is already the `nhcore` representation of an instant; there is no information loss. The field's only function is to carry an instant, so there is no reason for the carrier type to be the upstream one. Net-negative diff for every consumer. |
+
+### 2. Constructor sites switch to `DateTime` primitives
+
+Three constructors inside `Service.Auth` and one test helper in
+`core/testlib/Test/Service/Command/Decide/Spec.hs` build a `RequestContext`
+today. Each switches to a `DateTime`-flavoured equivalent.
+
+| Constructor                                                           | Today                                                     | After                         |
+| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
+| `emptyContext`                                                        | `GhcClock.UTCTime (GhcCalendar.fromGregorian 1970 1 1) 0` | `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0` |
+| `anonymousContext`                                                    | `GhcClock.getCurrentTime \|> Task.fromIO`                 | `DateTime.now`                |
+| `authenticatedContext`                                                | `GhcClock.getCurrentTime \|> Task.fromIO`                 | `DateTime.now`                |
+| `Test.Service.Command.Decide.Spec.authenticatedContext` (test helper) | `GhcClock.UTCTime (GhcCalendar.fromGregorian 1970 1 1) 0` | `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0` |
+
+After the change, neither `Service.Auth` nor the affected test helper imports
+`Data.Time`, `Data.Time.Calendar`, or `Data.Time.Clock`.
+
+### 3. Public API
+
+```haskell
+-- Service.Auth (unchanged signatures, only the field type moves)
+emptyContext         :: RequestContext
+anonymousContext     :: Task err RequestContext
+authenticatedContext :: UserClaims -> Task err RequestContext
+withFiles            :: Map FileRef ResolvedFile -> RequestContext -> RequestContext
+```
+
+No new function is introduced. No existing function changes its arity, name,
+or `Task`/`Result` signature.
+
+## Consequences
+
+### Positive
+
+- Consumer projects collapse to a single-line cleanup per file: read `ctx.timestamp`
+  directly.
+- The `time`, `GHC.Real`, and `Data.Time.Calendar` imports leave
+  `Service.Auth` and the affected test helper.
+- `RequestContext` becomes typeable by reading nothing but `nhcore` modules,
+  matching the framework's own invariant.
+
+### Negative
+
+- Breaking change for any out-of-tree consumer that today reads
+  `ctx.timestamp` as `UTCTime`. The migration is _deletion_ — drop the local
+  converter and the foreign imports — but it is still a recompile.
+
+### Risks
+
+- A consumer might pattern-match on the `UTCTime` constructor today (i.e.
+  `case ctx.timestamp of UTCTime day diff -> ...`). After the change, that
+  match no longer typechecks. `DateTime` does not export its data
+  constructor, so the consumer cannot reach the underlying `UTCTime`.
+
+### Mitigations
+
+- The migration shape is documented in the PR body and in the ADR's
+  "Constructor sites" table.
+- If a consumer genuinely needs to inspect the underlying time value, the
+  framework already exposes `DateTime.toEpochSeconds` and
+  `DateTime.fromEpochSeconds`, which round-trip through `Int64`. Adding a
+  `DateTime.toUtcTime` accessor is _not_ part of this ADR — it would
+  re-introduce the leak this ADR removes. If a real use case appears, it is
+  its own ADR.
+
+## References
+
+- [#629: feat(RequestContext): type `timestamp` as `DateTime` to remove `time` leak from consumers](https://github.com/neohaskell/NeoHaskell/issues/629)
+- [`core/service/Service/Auth.hs`](../../core/service/Service/Auth.hs)
+- [`core/core/DateTime.hs`](../../core/core/DateTime.hs)
+- [`core/testlib/Test/Service/Command/Decide/Spec.hs`](../../core/testlib/Test/Service/Command/Decide/Spec.hs)

+module Service.AuthSpec where
+
+import Auth.Claims (UserClaims (..))
+import Array qualified
+import Core
+import DateTime qualified
+import Map qualified
+import Service.Auth (RequestContext (..))
+import Service.Auth qualified as Auth
+import Test
+import Test.Service.Command.Decide.Spec qualified as DecideSpec
+import Uuid qualified
+
+
+spec :: Spec Unit
+spec = do
+  describe "Service.Auth" do
+    describe "emptyContext" do
+      it "returns RequestContext with all fields set" \_ -> do
+        -- Happy path: emptyContext successfully constructs a context.
+        -- What this case proves: emptyContext produces a well-formed RequestContext.
+        let ctx = Auth.emptyContext
+        ctx.user |> shouldBe Nothing
+        ctx.files |> shouldBe Map.empty
+        ctx.requestId |> shouldBe Uuid.nil
+
+      it "timestamp field is exactly DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0" \_ -> do
+        -- Edge case: the timestamp value is Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z).
+        -- What this case proves: emptyContext.timestamp is the epoch constant, not an arbitrary time.
+        let ctx = Auth.emptyContext
+        ctx.timestamp |> DateTime.toEpochSeconds |> shouldBe 0
+
+      it "timestamp is a DateTime value with zero epoch seconds" \_ -> do
+        -- Edge case: verify round-trip consistency (epoch is boundary).
+        -- What this case proves: DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0 and toEpochSeconds round-trip identity.
+        let expected = DateTime.fromEpochSeconds 0
+        let ctx = Auth.emptyContext
+        ctx.timestamp |> shouldBe expected
+
+    describe "anonymousContext" do
+      it "returns RequestContext with Nothing user and empty files" \_ -> do
+        -- Happy path: anonymousContext executes and yields a context.
+        -- What this case proves: anonymousContext constructs a request context with correct default fields.
+        ctx <- Auth.anonymousContext
+        ctx.user |> shouldBe Nothing
+        ctx.files |> shouldBe Map.empty
+
+      it "requestId is generated (not nil)" \_ -> do
+        -- Edge case: verify requestId is freshly generated, not a sentinel value.
+        -- What this case proves: anonymousContext calls Uuid.generate, not hardcoded Uuid.nil.
+        ctx <- Auth.anonymousContext
+        ctx.requestId |> shouldNotBe Uuid.nil
+
+      it "timestamp is current time (within 5 seconds of sampling)" \_ -> do
+        -- Edge case: timestamp is "now", not a constant or arbitrary value.
+        -- What this case proves: anonymousContext calls DateTime.now to capture wall-clock time.
+        beforeNow <- DateTime.now
+        ctx <- Auth.anonymousContext

problem_statement:
File-upload dedup returns a FileRef without checking the blob still exists
## Summary

`Service/FileUpload/Web.hs` (`handleUploadImpl`) deduplicates uploads on owner + content hash via the state store, and on a match **returns the existing `FileRef` without verifying that the blob still exists in the `BlobStore`**. If that blob is ever lost — switching `BlobStore` backends, an ephemeral storage dir that comes back empty, manual deletion, retention/GC — then every subsequent upload of the same content keeps short-circuiting to a `FileRef` whose blob is gone. Any downstream read then fails with `"File blob is missing from storage"`, permanently, because dedup never falls through to actually re-store the blob.

## Where

```haskell
-- 2. Check for existing upload with same content (dedup)
existingRef <- stateStore.findByContentHash ownerHashValue contentHash

case existingRef of
  Just fileRef -> do
    Log.info "Duplicate upload detected, returning existing FileRef" |> Task.ignoreError
    existingState <- stateStore.getState fileRef ...
    case existingState of
      Just (Pending pendingFile)     -> Task.yield UploadResponse { ... }   -- returns ref, no blob check
      Just (Confirmed confirmedFile) -> Task.yield UploadResponse { ... }   -- returns ref, no blob check
      _ -> normalUploadFlow ...   -- Deleted/Initial already falls through
```

The `Pending`/`Confirmed` branches trust the state store entry and never consult `blobStore`.

## Repro

1. Upload a file — blob is stored, state records owner+content hash.
2. Lose the blob from the `BlobStore` backend (e.g. the blob was written under a `BlobStore.Local` root that was ephemeral and is now a fresh/empty mount, or switch backends).
3. Re-upload the **same content**: log shows `Duplicate upload detected, returning existing FileRef`, and the returned ref points at a missing blob. Retrieving it fails with `File blob is missing from storage`.

## Suggested fix

Before returning a dedup match, verify the blob exists and self-heal if not:

[HIDDEN]

[HIDDEN] instead of poisoning a content hash forever.

### Additional contract requirements

- When an upload matches existing content by owner and content hash (dedup), the returned `FileRef`/`blobKey` must refer to content that actually exists in the blob store. A dedup match must never yield a successful response whose blob is gone.
- If the blob backing a dedup match is missing (for either a `Pending` or a `Confirmed` uploaded file), re-uploading the same content must restore retrievable content: after the re-upload, retrieving via the returned `blobKey` yields the exact uploaded bytes. Re-uploading the same content must not permanently poison the content hash; the returned reference must be usable.
- If the blob is missing and the content cannot be re-stored, the upload must surface an error instead of returning a successful response that points at missing content.

+-- | Guard a deduplication match against blob loss (issue #713).
+--
+-- Before returning an existing 'FileRef', verify its blob is still present in
+-- the 'BlobStore'; if it is missing — or its presence cannot be confirmed (the
+-- existence check itself errored) — re-store the caller's content under the
+-- SAME blob key so the returned reference is never dangling. Healing in place
+-- (same key, no state-store write) preserves dedup identity and is robust on
+-- every backend: unlike falling through to a fresh upload, it cannot collide
+-- with the (owner, content_hash) unique constraint and re-return the stale ref.
+--
+-- The re-stored bytes are the caller's own content, matched to the existing
+-- entry by the same owner-scoped content hash, so healing never crosses owners
+-- or writes different content. 'BlobStore.store' overwrites idempotently, so a
+-- redundant re-store (e.g. after a transient existence-check error) is harmless.
+ensureBlobPresent :: BlobStore -> BlobKey -> Bytes -> Task Text Unit
+ensureBlobPresent blobStore blobKey content = do
+  existsResult <- blobStore.exists blobKey |> Task.asResult
+  blobPresent <- case existsResult of
+    Ok present -> Task.yield present
+    Err existsErr -> do
+      -- Presence unknown: keep the real error in the server log, then treat as
+      -- missing and heal (re-store is idempotent).
+      Log.warn [fmt|Dedup blob existence check errored (#{show existsErr}); treating as missing|]
+        |> Task.ignoreError
+      Task.yield False
+  if blobPresent
+    then pass
+    else do
+      Log.warn "Deduplicated blob unavailable; self-healing by re-storing content"
+        |> Task.ignoreError
+      storeResult <- blobStore.store blobKey content |> Task.asResult
+      case storeResult of
+        Ok _ -> pass
+        Err storeErr -> do
+          -- The BlobStoreError (e.g. StorageError "disk full") stays in the
+          -- server log; the client only ever sees a generic message (S8).
+          Log.critical [fmt|Failed to re-store blob during dedup self-heal: #{show storeErr}|]
+            |> Task.ignoreError
+          Task.throw "Failed to restore missing file content. Please retry."
+
+

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+# Change 001: Verify the blob still exists before returning a dedup match on file upload
+
+File-upload deduplication currently returns an existing `FileRef` on an
+owner+content-hash match **without checking that the blob is still present** in
+the `BlobStore`. If the blob is ever lost (backend switch, ephemeral storage
+dir, retention/GC, manual deletion), every subsequent upload of the same
+content keeps short-circuiting to a `FileRef` whose blob is gone, and every
+downstream read fails permanently with `File blob is missing from storage`.
+This change makes dedup self-healing: before returning a match, verify the blob
+exists and, if it does not, re-store the content under the same blob key so the
+returned reference is never dangling.
+
+```yaml spec
+issue: issue#713                # issue#NNN or adhoc:<slug>
+kind: bug                       # feature | bug | refactor
+touches: [file-upload]          # capability IDs from codemap/capabilities.yaml (closed list)
+breaking: false                 # MUST be true if the contract delta has any `-` line
+new-dependency: false           # any new build-depends / flake input
+new-capability: false           # this change adds a row to codemap/capabilities.yaml
+new-extension-point: false      # this change adds a row to codemap/extension-points.yaml
+```
+
+## Contract delta
+
+Internal-only fix. The public API surface of `Service.FileUpload.Web` is
+unchanged — `handleUploadImpl` keeps its signature; the self-heal lives in a
+new non-exported helper. No `codemap/signatures/` line is added or removed, so
+the promised diff is empty.
+
+```diff signatures
+```
+
+## Criteria
+
+`kind: bug` → C1 is the failing reproduction test, committed red in the draft
+PR. The behavior crosses the filesystem boundary (a real `BlobStore.Local`
+losing a blob), so the reproductions are `integration`.
+
+| ID | Behavior | Proving test | Level |
+|----|----------|--------------|-------|
+| C1 | Re-uploading content whose deduplicated **Pending** blob was lost returns a `FileRef` whose blob is present again (self-heal), not a dangling ref | `Service.FileUpload.ContentDedupSpec` "dedup self-heals a missing Pending blob on re-upload" | integration |
+| C2 | Same self-heal when the dedup match is a **Confirmed** file | `Service.FileUpload.ContentDedupSpec` "dedup self-heals a missing Confirmed blob on re-upload" | integration |
+| C3 | Self-heal preserves dedup identity — same `FileRef` and same `blobKey` as the original — and the re-stored blob retrieves the exact uploaded content | `Service.FileUpload.ContentDedupSpec` "dedup self-heal preserves FileRef/blobKey and restores exact content" | integration |
+| C4 | When the existence check itself errors, dedup still heals (re-stores) rather than returning a possibly-dangling ref | `Service.FileUpload.ContentDedupSpec` "dedup self-heals when the existence check errors" | integration |
+| C5 | Healthy path preserved — when the blob is present, a duplicate upload still returns the existing `FileRef`/`blobKey` unchanged | `Service.FileUpload.ContentDedupSpec` "duplicate upload returns same blobKey as original" | integration |
+
+## User impact
+
+Not breaking. No signature or wire-format change; `UploadResponse` still omits
+`blobKey` from JSON. Behavior only changes on the failure path: an upload that
+previously returned a reference to a missing blob (poisoning the content hash
+forever) now re-stores the content and returns a valid reference. The re-stored
+bytes are the caller's own uploaded content, matched by the same owner-scoped
+content hash, so there is no cross-owner exposure. Testbed: no acceptance-test
+change — blob loss cannot be induced over HTTP; covered at the integration
+level.
+
+Side effect of making the reproduction executable: `ContentDedupSpec` is listed
+in the cabal `other-modules` but was never registered in
+`core/test-service/Main.hs`, so its dedup coverage compiled but never ran. This
+change registers it, so the regression tests **and** the existing dedup suite
+now execute.
+
+## ADR
+
+Not required — no trigger (breaking / new-dependency / new-capability /
+new-extension-point all false). The design choice (re-store under the existing
+blob key rather than falling through to a fresh upload, which would collide with
+the owner+content-hash unique constraint and re-return the stale ref) is
+recorded here and in the implementation comment, not as an ADR.
+
+**Completeness (from the security + design-alternative review lenses):** the
+missing-blob guard (`ensureBlobPresent`) is applied at **all four** sites that
+return a pre-existing `FileRef` — the two dedup branches (Pending/Confirmed) and
+the two 23505 concurrent-race retry branches in `normalUploadFlow` — since the
+race-retry path returns a stored `blobKey` with the same absent check and is the
+same defect class. The race branches only fire under the Postgres unique
+constraint, so they are covered structurally by the shared helper (proven by
+C1–C4 on the in-memory store) rather than by a separate, non-deterministic
+concurrency criterion. `handleDownloadImpl`'s `File blob is missing from storage`
+remains a detect-only backstop, unchanged.

+by any run, via optional repeatable `./dev telemetry finish … --improvement
+<type>:<dest>`. `./dev retrospect` surfaces them ("Improvements shipped") — a
+destination recurring there is a proven friction point for the miner. The
+failure-path `--asset-delta` enforcement is unchanged.
+

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+# ADR-0069: Security design-review records are local-only, never pushed
+
+> Follows [ADR-0067](0067-contract-delta-spec-gate.md) (spec gate) and
+> [ADR-0068](0068-failure-asset-delta-and-learning-loop.md) (Phase 6). Amends the
+> Phase-5 design-review record policy.
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted
+
+## Context
+
+The risk-tiered design reviews (Phase 5) produce a committed record next to the
+spec: `NNN-slug.security-review.md` and `NNN-slug.perf-review.md`. The original
+policy committed **both** to the PR branch as the compliance audit trail, gated
+at PR-ready by `./dev spec-check --reviews-pr` (a CI step in `checks.yml`).
+
+`neohaskell/NeoHaskell` is a **public** repository. A security design review is,
+by construction, a map of a change's attack surface: the trust boundaries it
+touches, the STRIDE questions asked, which vectors were considered and *why they
+were judged non-exploitable*. Committing that to public git history hands an
+attacker a curated, per-change threat model — including, for any review that
+does find a real issue, a description of the weakness before (or after) it is
+fixed. The audit-trail benefit does not justify publishing the attack surface.
+
+Perf reviews carry no such exposure — they discuss allocation, complexity, and
+benchmark budgets, not how to break the system.
+
+## Decision
+
+**Security review records are local-only; perf review records stay committed.**
+
+- `docs/changes/*.security-review.md` is **gitignored** — written on the
+  developer's working tree, never committed or pushed. The audit trail lives on
+  the maintainer's machine / secure store, outside public git history.
+- The review is still **mandatory and enforced**, just not in CI:
+  - `./dev spec-check --reviews-local` (dev machine) requires the gitignored
+    security record to exist on disk (and backlink its spec) before the pipeline
+    flips a PR to ready.
+  - `./dev spec-check --reviews-pr` (CI) now gates only **committed** review
+    kinds (perf). It can no longer see — and therefore no longer requires — a
+    security record, which is intentionally absent from CI's checkout.
+- `speclib.LOCAL_ONLY_REVIEW_KINDS = ("security",)` is the single source of the
+  split; the two gates share one core (`missing_review_records(..., kinds=…)`).
+
+## Consequences
+
+- **Attack surface stays private.** The primary goal.
+- **Weaker public audit trail for security.** CI can prove a *perf* review
+  happened; it cannot prove a *security* review happened, because the artifact
+  never reaches CI. The guarantee moves to the local gate + the pipeline state
+  (`.pipeline/state.json` records the design-review stage) + the maintainer's
+  local records. This is the accepted trade: privacy over public provability.
+- **A pushed security review is a policy violation**, not just untidy. If one is
+  ever committed, purge it from history (`git filter-branch`/`filter-repo` +
+  force-push the unmerged branch) — the gitignore prevents recurrence.
+- Migration: the first real security review (change 001, issue #713) was pushed
+  before this ADR. It was untracked and gitignored, so it is absent from the
+  PR's tip — a **squash-merge** collapses the branch to one commit whose diff has
+  no security record, keeping `main` clean. (An intermediate branch commit still
+  holds it until the branch is deleted; for a higher-sensitivity review, purge
+  with `git filter-repo`/`filter-branch` + force-push before merge instead.)

+                  }
+            env.stateStore.updateState response1.fileRef confirmEvent
+            env.blobStore.delete response1.blobKey
+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|delete failed: #{show e}|])

+            blobPresent <- env.blobStore.exists response2.blobKey
+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|exists failed: #{show e}|])

+            -- retrieves the exact uploaded content, whatever its identity.

+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|retrieve failed: #{show e}|])
+            restored |> shouldBe content

+            response1 <- uploadFile env "owner1" "file.txt" "text/plain" content
+            env.blobStore.delete response1.blobKey
+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|delete failed: #{show e}|])
+            response2 <- uploadFile env "owner1" "file.txt" "text/plain" content
+            -- The returned reference must be usable: the blob behind it
+            -- retrieves the exact uploaded content, whatever its identity.
+            restored <- env.blobStore.retrieve response2.blobKey
+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|retrieve failed: #{show e}|])
+            restored |> shouldBe content
+
+        it "dedup surfaces an error (no dangling ref) when the blob cannot be restored" \_ -> do
+          withTestDedupEnv \env -> do
+            let content = "self-heal store-failure content" |> Text.toBytes
+            response1 <- uploadFile env "owner1" "file.txt" "text/plain" content
+            env.blobStore.delete response1.blobKey
+              |> Task.mapError (\e -> [fmt|delete failed: #{show e}|])
+            -- Blob is gone AND re-storing fails: the upload must surface an
+            -- error, never a dangling ref (any error detail is logged
+            -- server-side; only the absence of a successful response matters).
+            let faultingBlobStore =
+                  (env.blobStore)
+                    { store = \_ _ -> Task.throw (StorageError "injected store failure") }
+            result <-
+              handleUploadImpl env.config faultingBlobStore env.stateStore "owner1" "file.txt" "text/plain" content
+                |> Task.asResult
+            case result of
+              Ok _ -> fail "expected re-store failure to surface as an error, not a dangling ref"

problem_statement:
Option to disable extensions
In particular, footnotes aren't part of commonmark. They're being parsed in my markdown documents which contain text like `^[a-z]`.

### Additional contract requirements

In addition to the base problem statement, the requested capability must behave as follows:

- Parsing must accept a boolean option named exactly `:disable-footnotes`.
- The option must be supported by both parsing entry points of the public API: `nextjournal.markdown/parse` accepts it in its `opts` map argument, and `nextjournal.markdown/parse*` accepts it under the `:opts` key of its `ctx` argument. It must behave identically through both entry points.
- When the option is not given, or is given with a falsey value, footnote parsing stays enabled exactly as before: both inline footnote syntax (for example `^[a-z]`) and reference footnote syntax (for example `[^{label}]` together with a corresponding `[^{label}]: ...` definition) are parsed into footnotes, through both entry points.
- When `:disable-footnotes true` is given, through either entry point:
  - Inline footnote syntax (for example `^[a-z]`) and reference footnote syntax (for example `[^{label}]` and its `[^{label}]: ...` definition) must be left as ordinary literal text in the paragraph content; nothing must be removed from the document body.
  - The resulting document must have an empty top-level `:footnotes` collection.
  - The option must only affect footnote parsing: other parsing options given alongside it (for example heading id/emoji handling or an explicit document title) must behave exactly as they do without footnote disabling.
- This addendum is exercised by the evaluator-configured JVM test suite; behavior on the ClojureScript/JavaScript runtime is out of scope for the evaluated contract.

problem_statement:
Add directives
See yellow team sprint 2 retrospective document for more details. Add directives to expose things like printing, displaying axioms, and so on. No hurry to do this, but it will definitely be useful, so despite the low priority for now feel free to take this on early.

### Additional contract requirements

# Directives

Directives are top-level statements in a proof file, at the same level as
`Axiom` and `Theorem` declarations, that inspect the environment or a term
without adding a declaration. A directive line starts with one of the
following spellings and may appear anywhere among and interleaved with
declarations:

- `#print axioms <name>`
- `#infer <term>`
- `#check <term> : <type>`
- `#reduce <term>`

Each directive reports its result by printing to standard output.

## `#print axioms <name>`

Prints the axioms that the theorem `<name>` (transitively) depends on. The
output identifies `<name>` and prints the name of every axiom the theorem
depends on, without printing the names of axioms it does not depend on. If
`<name>` is not a theorem declared in the current environment, processing
must not raise an error; instead the output reports the failure to locate
`<name>` and includes the given name.

## `#infer <term>`

Infers the type of `<term>` in the current environment and prints the
complete inferred type on a single output line. For example, after
`Axiom Point : Type`, `#infer (fun (x : Point) => x)` must print a function
type whose domain and codomain are `Point` (either the explicit dependent
form `(x : Point) -> Point` or the plain non-dependent form
`Point -> Point`).

## `#check <term> : <type>`

Checks whether `<term>` has type `<type>` in the current environment.

- On success, processing completes without raising an error and prints a
  report that both announces the successful check and includes a
  pretty-printing of the confirmed type.
- If `<term>` does not have type `<type>`, processing must raise an
  elaboration error such as `Error.ElabError`. This semantic failure is
  distinct from a syntax (parsing) failure: the directive syntax itself must
  parse successfully, so an implementation that merely does not recognize
  `#check` does not satisfy this requirement.

## `#reduce <term>`

Reduces `<term>` (including beta-reduction) in the current environment and
prints the complete reduct. The output must identify the report as coming
from the `#reduce` directive and print the entire reduced term; for example,
after `Axiom Point : Type` and `Axiom p : Point`,
`#reduce (fun (x : Point) => x) p` must print the reduct `p` in full (not
the unreduced application).

## Compatibility with the base language

Top-level parsing of a proof file must accept a sequence of statements in
which directives and declarations are freely interleaved. File processing
continues according to the usual rules: declarations are type-checked and
added to the environment as before, while directives produce output and
leave the environment otherwise unchanged. Adding directives must not
change the behavior of any previously existing functionality (in
particular, declaration processing and the existing error types) and must
not change any previously existing public module names, types, or
signatures.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7137743
--- /dev/null
+++ b/elab/directives.ml
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+open Types
+open Statement
+
+let process_directive (e : ctx) (dir : directive) : unit =
+  match dir with
+  | PrintAxioms (prop_name, loc) -> (
+      let prefix = "[" ^ Pretty.pp_loc loc ^ "] " in
+      match Hashtbl.find_opt e.env prop_name with
+      | Some record -> (
+          match record.data with
+          | Theorem used_axioms ->
+              print_endline (prefix ^ "Axioms used in " ^ prop_name ^ ":");
+              List.iter print_endline used_axioms
+          | Axiom -> print_endline (prefix ^ prop_name ^ " is an axiom itself."))
+      | None ->
+          print_endline (prefix ^ "Error: Proposition '" ^ prop_name ^ "' not found."))
+  | Infer (t, loc) ->
+      let prefix = "[" ^ Pretty.pp_loc loc ^ "] " in
+      (* create hole for elaborator to solve *)
+      let t_meta = Typecheck.hole_to_meta e [] t in
+      (* infer type *)
+      let ty_term = Typecheck.infertype e t_meta in
+      (* replace holes *)
+      let ty_filled = Typecheck.replace_metas e ty_term in
+      Hashtbl.clear e.metas;
+      print_endline (prefix ^ "#infer: " ^ Pretty.term_to_string e ty_filled)
+  | Check (t, ty, loc) ->
+      let prefix = "[" ^ Pretty.pp_loc loc ^ "] " in
+      (* process provided type to make sure valid type *)
+      let ty_meta = Typecheck.hole_to_meta e [] ty in
+      Typecheck.check_is_type e ty_meta;
+      let ty_filled = Typecheck.replace_metas e ty_meta in
+      Hashtbl.clear e.metas;
+      (* process term provided *)
+      let t_meta = Typecheck.hole_to_meta e [] t in
+      (* call elaborator to check if term matches type *)
+      Typecheck.checktype e t_meta ty_filled;
+      let _ = Typecheck.replace_metas e t_meta in
+      Hashtbl.clear e.metas;
+
+      print_endline
+        (prefix ^ "#check successful: Term is well-typed as "
+        ^ Pretty.term_to_string e ty_filled)
+  | Reduce (t, loc) ->
+      let prefix = "[" ^ Pretty.pp_loc loc ^ "] " in
+      let t_meta = Typecheck.hole_to_meta e [] t in
+      let reduced_term = Pretty.reduce e t_meta in
+      print_endline (prefix ^ "#reduce: " ^ Pretty.term_to_string e reduced_term)

+type decl_type =

+  | Axiom  (** [Axiom] is the type of axioms. *)

+  | PrintAxioms of string * range
+      (** [PrintAxioms(name, loc)] corresponds to #print axioms name. *)
+  | Infer of term * range  (** [Infer(t, loc)] corresponds to #infer t. *)
+  | Check of term * term * range  (** [Check(t, ty, loc)] corresponds to #check t : ty. *)
+  | Reduce of term * range  (** [Reduce(t, loc)] corresponds to #reduce t. *)

+type statement =
+  | Declaration of declaration

+          environment. *)
+  | Directive of directive
+      (** [Directive(dir)] is a parsed directive, printing information to stdout. *)

+(* Behavioral tests for the top-level proof-file directives:
+   #print axioms, #infer, #check, and #reduce.
+
+   A directive is a top-level statement written in a proof file that inspects the
+   environment or a term (rather than adding a declaration).  Processing a directive
+   reports its result on standard output.  These tests only assert the observable
+   reporting requirements of the directives, not any particular wording or layout:
+   any output that satisfies the stated requirement is accepted.
+
+   This module also checks that adding directives does not change the behavior of
+   previously existing functionality: declaration processing, the axiom-dependency
+   query, and the public declaration type and pretty-printer are exercised exactly
+   as the pre-existing tests use them. *)
+
+open Elab
+
+(* Capture everything written to stdout while running [f]. *)
+let with_captured_stdout (f : unit -> unit) : string =
+  let old_stdout = Unix.dup Unix.stdout in
+  let read_end, write_end = Unix.pipe () in
+  Unix.dup2 write_end Unix.stdout;
+  f ();
+  flush_all ();
+  Unix.dup2 old_stdout Unix.stdout;
+  Unix.close write_end;
+  Unix.close old_stdout;
+  let buf = Buffer.create 256 in
+  let chunk = Bytes.create 1024 in
+  let rec loop () =
+    match Unix.read read_end chunk 0 1024 with
+    | 0 -> ()
+    | n ->
+        Buffer.add_subbytes buf chunk 0 n;
+        loop ()
+  in
+  loop ();
+  Unix.close read_end;
+  Buffer.contents buf
+
+let contains (haystack : string) (needle : string) : bool =
+  let n = String.length needle and h = String.length haystack in
+  let rec go i =
+    if i + n > h then false
+    else if String.sub haystack i n = needle then true
+    else go (i + 1)
+  in
+  n = 0 || go 0
+
+(* Does [s] print the name [name] as a clearly delimited, standalone
+   occurrence?  An occurrence preceded or followed by a letter (as in "Point"
+   when looking for "p", or in "fail" when looking for "p") never counts, and
+   neither does one glued to digits or underscores without an intervening
+   delimiter.  Whitespace-delimited, quoted, and punctuated printings (" p ",
+   "'p", "(p)", "p,", "p.", "'p'") are all accepted, so the report's own
+   punctuation and quoting are unconstrained. *)
+let prints_name (s : string) (name : string) : bool =
+  let n = String.length name and h = String.length s in
+  let is_letter c = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') in
+  let is_name_char c =
+    is_letter c || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c = '_'
+  in
+  (* Any other character, including punctuation and non-ASCII (e.g. Unicode
+     quote) bytes, is a delimiter. *)
+  let delimiter c = (not (is_name_char c)) || Char.code c >= 0x80 in
+  let rec go i =
+    if i + n > h then false
+    else if String.sub s i n = name then
+      let left_letter = i > 0 && is_letter s.[i - 1] in
+      let right_letter = i + n < h && is_letter s.[i + n] in
+      let left_ok = (not left_letter) && (i = 0 || delimiter s.[i - 1]) in
+      let right_ok =
+        (not right_letter) && (i + n = h || delimiter s.[i + n])
+      in
+      (left_ok && right_ok) || go (i + 1)
+    else go (i + 1)
+  in
+  n = 0 || go 0
+
+(* Does any line of [s] contain [needle]? *)
+let any_line (s : string) (needle : string) : bool =
+  List.exists (fun line -> contains line needle) (String.split_on_char '\n' s)
+
+(* Write [contents] to a temporary file and return its path. *)

+(* #print axioms lists the axiom dependencies of the named theorem.  The
+   dependency report is transitive: axioms used by other theorems that the
+   result depends on must be included, while an axiom the theorem does not
+   depend on must be omitted.  The report may explain the dependency; it is

+              Axiom Q : Prop\n\
+              Axiom q : Q\n\
+              Axiom R : Prop\n\
+              Axiom r : R\n\

+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#print axioms report mentions the queried non-theorem by name"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(prints_name out "p");
+  let lowered = String.lowercase_ascii out in
+  let signals =
+    [ "not"; "no "; "non-"; "error"; "unknown"; "miss"; "absent"; "fail";
+      "invalid"; "axiom"; "itself"; "empty"; "none"; "zero"; "succe"; "ok";
+      "pass"; "done"; "check"; "found" ]
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#print axioms report announces the outcome for the non-theorem name"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(List.exists (fun signal -> contains lowered signal) signals)
+
+(* #infer prints the complete inferred type of a term on a single output line.
+   The line must contain a complete function type whose domain and codomain are
+   both "Point": either the explicit dependent form or the plain non-dependent
+   form. *)
+let test_infer_prints_type () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  let out =
+    with_captured_stdout (fun () ->
+        Interface.process_file e
+          (write_temp_file "Axiom Point : Type\n#infer (fun (x : Point) => x)\n"))
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#infer prints a nonempty report"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(report_is_nonempty out);
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#infer prints the complete inferred type on a single line"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:
+      (any_line out "(x : Point) -> Point" || any_line out "Point -> Point")
+
+(* #check confirms a well-typed term: it prints a success report that announces
+   the successful check (and so differs from the failure to check) and includes
+   a pretty-printing of the confirmed type. *)
+let test_check_accepts_well_typed_term () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  let out =
+    with_captured_stdout (fun () ->
+        Interface.process_file e
+          (write_temp_file
+             "Axiom Point : Type\n\
+              #check (fun (x : Point) => x) : (Point -> Point)\n"))
+  in
+  (* Any spelling of the confirmed type is accepted; the source spelling is
+     only a fallback for a report that reuses it verbatim. *)
+  let spellings =
+    [ "(x : Point) -> Point"; "Point -> Point"; "(Point -> Point)" ]
+  in
+  let confirms =
+    report_is_nonempty out
+    && List.exists (fun spelling -> any_line out spelling) spellings
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#check prints a success report including the confirmed type"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:confirms;
+  (* The report must announce the success of the check, not merely echo the
+     type.  Case and punctuation are unconstrained; any conventional success
+     wording is accepted. *)
+  let lowered = String.lowercase_ascii out in
+  let signals =
+    [ "succe"; "ok"; "well-typed"; "well typed"; "valid"; "accept"; "check";
+      "holds"; "pass" ]
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#check report announces the successful check"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(List.exists (fun signal -> contains lowered signal) signals)
+
+(* Classify how processing a source file fails, if it fails at all.
+   Parsing succeeds when no [Error.ParseError] is raised. *)
+type failure = NoFailure | ParseFailed | OtherError
+
+let classify_failure (source : string) : failure =
+  try
+    let e = Interface.create () in
+    Interface.process_file e (write_temp_file source);
+    NoFailure
+  with
+  | Error.ElabError { error_type = Error.ParseError _; _ } -> ParseFailed
+  | Error.ElabError { error_type = Error.TypeMismatch _; _ } -> OtherError
+  | _ -> OtherError
+
+(* Does processing the source file raise an elaboration error (rather than a
+   parse failure or an unrelated exception)? *)
+let raises_elab_error (source : string) : bool =
+  try
+    let e = Interface.create () in
+    Interface.process_file e (write_temp_file source);
+    false
+  with
+  | Error.ElabError { error_type = Error.ParseError _; _ } -> false
+  | Error.ElabError _ -> true
+  | _ -> false
+
+(* #check fails (rather than silently accepting) on an ill-typed term.
+   The failure must come from type-checking the term against the asserted type,
+   not from a refusal to parse, so this input must parse cleanly in the base
+   language where unsupported syntax is a parse error. *)
+let test_check_rejects_ill_typed_term () =
+  let failed =
+    try
+      let e = Interface.create () in
+      Interface.process_file e
+        (write_temp_file "Axiom Point : Type\n#check p : Point\n");
+      false
+    with _ -> true
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#check reports failure for an ill-typed term"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:failed;
+  (* The required error class is an elaboration error ([Error.ElabError]),
+     raised from type-checking, not a parse failure or an unrelated
+     exception. *)
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#check failure is an elaboration error"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(raises_elab_error "Axiom Point : Type\n#check p : Point\n");
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#check parses the directive syntax (failure must not be a parse error)"
+    ~expected:false
+    ~actual:
+      (classify_failure
+         "Axiom Point : Type\n#check (fun (x : Point) => x) : Point\n"
+      = ParseFailed)
+
+(* #reduce reduces a term (including beta-reduction) and prints the complete
+   reduct, identifying the report as coming from the #reduce directive. *)
+let test_reduce_beta_reduces () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  let out =
+    with_captured_stdout (fun () ->
+        Interface.process_file e
+          (write_temp_file
+             "Axiom Point : Type\n\
+              Axiom p : Point\n\
+              #reduce (fun (x : Point) => x) p\n"))
+  in
+  (* The reduct [p] must be printed as a clearly delimited, standalone name:
+     an unreduced application prints additional material instead, and a
+     reduced-but-renamed output ("x", "f0", ...) can never produce [p].
+     Whitespace, punctuation, and quoting around the reduct are accepted
+     however the report is laid out. *)
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#reduce prints the complete reduct"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(prints_name out "p");
+  (* The report must identify the #reduce reduction rather than echoing the
+     checked application.  The same term processed with #check prints a success
+     report about the type; a reduction report must be distinguishable from that
+     announcement, so the two reports cannot be identical. *)
+  let check_out =
+    let e2 = Interface.create () in
+    with_captured_stdout (fun () ->
+        Interface.process_file e2
+          (write_temp_file
+             "Axiom Point : Type\n\
+              Axiom p : Point\n\
+              #check (fun (x : Point) => x) p : Point\n"))
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#reduce reduces the same application that #check accepts"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(report_is_nonempty check_out);
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:
+      "#reduce report identifies the reduction (distinct from the #check \
+       announcement of the same term)"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(out <> check_out);
+  (* The report must explicitly identify itself as coming from the reduction
+     directive, not merely differ from the #check report.  Case and punctuation
+     are unconstrained; any label mentioning reduction is accepted. *)
+  let lowered = String.lowercase_ascii out in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"#reduce report explicitly identifies the reduction directive"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(contains lowered "#reduce" || contains lowered "reduc")
+
+(* Directives and declarations can be freely interleaved: a directive between
+   declarations processes normally, and the declaration following it is still
+   processed and added to the environment. *)
+let test_directive_between_declarations () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  let processed =
+    try
+      ignore
+        (with_captured_stdout (fun () ->
+             Interface.process_file e
+               (write_temp_file
+                  "Axiom Point : Type\n\
+                   Axiom p : Point\n\
+                   #infer p\n\
+                   Theorem after_directive : Point := p\n")));
+      true
+    with _ -> false
+  in
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:
+      "a directive interleaved between declarations does not interrupt file \
+       processing"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:processed;
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"the theorem declared after the directive is added to the environment"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(Interface.list_axioms e "after_directive" <> [])
+
+(* Adding directives must not change the behavior of declaration-only files: a
+   file containing only Axiom and Theorem declarations still processes and the
+   theorem's axiom dependency is recorded exactly as before. *)
+let test_declaration_only_file_processes () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  Interface.process_file e
+    (write_temp_file
+       "Axiom Point : Type\nAxiom p : Point\nTheorem via_p : Point := p\n");
+  Alcotest.check'
+    (Alcotest.list Alcotest.string)
+    ~msg:"declaration-only processing records the theorem's axiom dependency"
+    ~expected:[ "p" ]
+    ~actual:(Interface.list_axioms e "via_p")
+
+(* Adding directives must not change previously existing public names, types,
+   or signatures.  The public modules the pre-existing tests rely on must still
+   be present with the same observable behavior: the term pretty-printer and
+   the kernel pretty-printer still render as the pre-existing tests confirm,
+   and the environment query still reports axiom dependencies. *)
+let test_public_modules_unchanged () =
+  let e = Interface.create () in
+  let l = Term.dummy_range in
+  (* Term pretty-printing is unchanged. *)
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.string
+    ~msg:"term pretty-printing is unchanged"
+    ~expected:"fun (x : A) (y : B) => x"
+    ~actual:
+      (Pretty.term_to_string e
+         Util.(nfun "x" (name "A") (nfun "y" (name "B") (bvar 1))));
+  (* Hole pretty-printing is unchanged. *)
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.string
+    ~msg:"hole pretty-printing is unchanged"
+    ~expected:"?m0"
+    ~actual:(Pretty.term_to_string e { inner = Term.Hole 0; loc = l });
+  (* The axiom-dependency query still processes a declaration-only file and
+     reports the dependent axiom. *)
+  Interface.process_file e
+    (write_temp_file "Axiom Point : Type\nAxiom p : Point\nTheorem thm : Point := p\n");
+  Alcotest.check'
+    Alcotest.bool
+    ~msg:"the axiom-dependency query is unchanged"
+    ~expected:true
+    ~actual:(List.mem "p" (Interface.list_axioms e "thm"))
+
+let suite =
+  let open Alcotest in
+  ( "Directives",
+    [
+      test_case "#print axioms lists dependencies" `Quick
+        test_print_axioms_lists_dependencies;
+      test_case "#print axioms unknown proposition" `Quick
+        test_print_axioms_unknown_proposition;
+      test_case "#print axioms on an existing axiom" `Quick
+        test_print_axioms_on_existing_axiom;
+      test_case "#infer prints inferred type" `Quick test_infer_prints_type;
+      test_case "#check accepts well-typed term" `Quick
+        test_check_accepts_well_typed_term;
+      test_case "#check rejects ill-typed term" `Quick
+        test_check_rejects_ill_typed_term;
+      test_case "#reduce beta-reduces" `Quick test_reduce_beta_reduces;
+      test_case "directive between declarations" `Quick
+        test_directive_between_declarations;
+      test_case "declaration-only file still processes" `Quick
+        test_declaration_only_file_processes;
+      test_case "public modules types and signatures unchanged" `Quick
+        test_public_modules_unchanged;
+    ] )

problem_statement:
Move automation into its own directory
Tactic implementations and the infrastructure for it should be in an automation directory, not part of the elaborator. There should also be an "Area: Automation" category in labels corresponding to that on GitHub issues.

### Additional contract requirements

## Observable relocation contract

No new tactic interfaces are introduced by this change: every tactic entry
point keeps its existing name, type, and observable behavior. The change is a
relocation that is observable as described below.

- The implementations of the built-in proof tactics (including
  `reflexivity`, `sorry`, `exact`, `apply`, `rewrite`, `exists`, the
  context tactics `intro` and `have`, and the tacticals such as sequencing,
  `try`, and `repeat`) must physically move out of the elaborator source
  tree into the project's own top-level `automation` directory. Leaving the
  tactic implementation in the elaborator tree and adding a copy or shim in
  the automation tree does not satisfy the task.
- The relocated tactics are built as an `automation` library that makes the
  tactic entry points reachable as `Automation.Tactics`. This is the same
  module interface the elaborator previously exposed, moved to the new
  location; its behavior is unchanged.
- The supporting infrastructure used by the tactics — the proof-state data
  structures and helpers, the tactic result and registry types, the
  typechecker, the environment-processing interface, and the term and
  reduction machinery — stays in the elaborator library, which continues to
  expose those modules with unchanged behavior. The automation code refers
  to them through the elaborator library.
- The registered built-in tactics must be wired up when the production
  executables start: running the project's `nicegeo` executable on a proof
  file that uses the built-in tactics must succeed from startup, without
  any additional client-side initialization.
- Every tactic's behavior is unchanged by the relocation: success and
  failure cases, failure messages, goal manipulation, and kernel checking
  all behave exactly as before.

## Issue-label scope

- The task statement's request for an `Area: Automation` category among the
  issue labels on GitHub concerns the repository's GitHub issue tracker,
  which is administered on the hosting platform. The checked-out codebase
  contains no local issue-label store or label declaration, and nothing in
  the checkout defines existing `Area:` labels, so this requirement has no
  repository-owned, evaluator-observable representation and cannot be
  expressed as a correctness condition on the project's code or its test
  suite. It is therefore outside the scope of the checkout-verifiable
  contract defined here; the relocation contract above is the complete
  evaluator-checked obligation.

diff --git a/test/automation/test_executable_runner.ml b/test/automation/test_executable_runner.ml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..870b07c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/automation/test_executable_runner.ml
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+(* Executable-level and relocation checks on the tactic automation:
+
+   1. The supported startup path of the production [nicegeo] executable: invoked through
+      its installed public name ([dune exec nicegeo -- <file>]) rather than a test-side
+      hard-coded build-directory artifact path, it must process a tactic-bearing proof
+      file successfully from startup, without any client-side initialization,
+      demonstrating that the built-in tactics are available for proofs whenever the
+      executable starts. The child runs from a scratch working directory that receives
+      an explicit absolute copy of the project's default environment file, so the check
+      never depends on the executable resolving that file relative to whatever working
+      directory it happens to be launched from, nor on any relative proof path.
+
+   2. The tactic implementation must have physically moved out of the elaborator source
+      tree into the project's own top-level [automation] directory: the automation
+      source tree must provide the tactics implementation module, and the elaborator
+      directory must not retain tactic implementation sources of its own — not even as
+      a leftover copy or shim forwarding to the relocated module. *)
+
+(* The test harness runs from [_build/default/test/automation] inside the dune build
+   directory; the project source root sits above the build directory. *)
+let dune_build = Filename.concat (Sys.getcwd ()) "../.."
+let source_root = Filename.concat dune_build "../.."
+
+(* The publicly installed name the production executable is invoked under. *)
+let nicegeo_public_name = "nicegeo"
+
+(* Directories that may hold the relocated tactic implementation in the checkout. *)
+let automation_source_dirs = [ "automation"; "automation/tactics" ]
+let elab_source_dir = "elab"
+let tactics_implementation_file = "tactics.ml"
+
+let scratch_root = Filename.concat dune_build "test/automation/executable_wiring"
+
+let rec mkdir_p (dir : string) : unit =
+  if not (Sys.file_exists dir) then (
+    mkdir_p (Filename.dirname dir);
+    Unix.mkdir dir 0o755)
+
+let copy_file (src : string) (dst : string) : unit =
+  let ic = open_in_bin src in
+  let oc = open_out_bin dst in
+  let bufsize = 4096 in
+  let buf = Bytes.create bufsize in
+  let rec pump () : unit =
+    let read = input ic buf 0 bufsize in
+    if read > 0 then (
+      output oc buf 0 read;
+      pump ())
+  in
+  pump ();
+  close_in ic;
+  close_out oc
+
+let write_file (filename : string) (contents : string) : unit =
+  let oc = open_out filename in
+  output_string oc contents;
+  close_out oc
+
+let tactic_bearing_proof : string =
+  "Axiom T_exec : Type\n\
+   Axiom p_exec : T_exec\n\
+   Theorem proof_exec : Eq T_exec p_exec p_exec\n\
+   Proof.\n\
+   \  reflexivity.\n\
+   Qed.\n"
+
+let test_executable_wiring () =
+  let previous_cwd = Sys.getcwd () in
+  let run_dir = Filename.concat scratch_root "run" in
+  let proof_file = Filename.concat run_dir "proof_exec_wiring.ncg" in
+  let copied_default_env = Filename.concat run_dir "synthetic/env.ncg" in
+  let cleanup () : unit =
+    try Unix.chdir previous_cwd with Sys_error _ -> ()
+  in
+  let status =
+    Fun.protect ~finally:cleanup (fun () ->
+        mkdir_p (Filename.dirname copied_default_env);
+        write_file proof_file tactic_bearing_proof;
+        (* Hand the child an explicit, absolute env file: the child never has to fall
+           back to resolving its prelude relative to this scratch directory. *)
+        copy_file
+          (Filename.concat source_root "synthetic/env.ncg")
+          copied_default_env;
+        Unix.chdir run_dir;
+        let cmd =
+          String.concat
+            " "
+            [
+              "dune exec";
+              "--root";
+              Filename.quote source_root;
+              nicegeo_public_name;
+              "--";
+              Filename.quote proof_file;
+            ]
+        in
+        Sys.command cmd)
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "nicegeo closes a tactic-bearing proof from startup" true (status = 0)
+
+let source_file_exists (rel : string) : bool =
+  Sys.file_exists (Filename.concat source_root rel)
+
+let test_tactics_moved_into_automation () =
+  let automation_provides_tactics =
+    List.exists
+      (fun dir -> source_file_exists (Filename.concat dir tactics_implementation_file))
+      automation_source_dirs
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "automation tree provides the tactics implementation module" true
+    automation_provides_tactics
+
+let test_no_leftover_tactic_sources_in_elab () =
+  let leftovers =
+    [ tactics_implementation_file; "tactics.mli" ]
+    |> List.map (Filename.concat elab_source_dir)
+    |> List.filter source_file_exists
+  in
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "no tactic implementation sources remain in the elaborator directory" true
+    (leftovers = [])
+
+let suite =
+  let open Alcotest in
+  ( "Automation.Executable",
+    [
+      test_case "executable wiring closes a tactic-bearing proof" `Quick
+        test_executable_wiring;
+      test_case "tactics implementation lives in the automation tree" `Quick
+        test_tactics_moved_into_automation;
+      test_case "no tactic sources remain in the elaborator tree" `Quick
+        test_no_leftover_tactic_sources_in_elab;
+    ] )
