+open Elab.Term
+open Elab.Types
+open Elab.Proofstate
+open Automation.Tactics
+
+let e = Elab.Interface.create ()
+let t k = { inner = k; loc = dummy_range }
+
+(* Build a goal state with one hypothesis [name : hyp_ty] and goal type [goal_ty]. *)
+let start_with_hyp hyp_name hyp_ty goal_ty =
+  let bid = gen_binder_id () in
+  let hyp = { hyp_name; hyp_bid = bid; hyp_def = None; hyp_type = hyp_ty } in
+  let id = gen_hole_id () in
+  Hashtbl.replace e.metas id { ty = Some goal_ty; context = [ bid ]; sol = None };
+  let g = { ctx = [ hyp ]; goal_type = goal_ty; goal_id = id } in
+  { statement = t (Hole id); open_goals = [ g ]; elab_ctx = e }
+
+(* [h : Sort 1 -> Sort 0], goal [Sort 0]: apply opens one subgoal [Sort 1]. *)
+let test_apply_opens_subgoal () =
+  let premise = t (Sort 1) in
+  let conclusion = t (Sort 0) in
+  let arrow_bid = gen_binder_id () in
+  let h_ty = t (Arrow (None, arrow_bid, premise, conclusion)) in
+  let st = start_with_hyp "h" h_ty conclusion in
+  match apply "h" st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success: %s" msg
+  | Success st' ->
+      Alcotest.(check int) "one subgoal remaining" 1 (List.length st'.open_goals);
+      Alcotest.(check bool)
+        "subgoal type is Sort 1"
+        true
+        (st'.open_goals |> List.hd |> fun g -> g.goal_type.inner = Sort 1)
+
+(* [h : Sort 0], goal [Sort 0]: no arrow — apply behaves like exact. *)
+let test_apply_no_arrow () =
+  let st = start_with_hyp "h" (t (Sort 0)) (t (Sort 0)) in
+  match apply "h" st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> Alcotest.(check bool) "proof complete" true (is_complete st')
+
+(* Conclusion does not match goal — apply should fail. *)
+let test_apply_conclusion_mismatch () =
+  let arrow_bid = gen_binder_id () in
+  let h_ty = t (Arrow (None, arrow_bid, t (Sort 1), t (Sort 1))) in
+  let st = start_with_hyp "h" h_ty (t (Sort 0)) in
+  let meta_count_before = Hashtbl.length st.elab_ctx.metas in
+  match apply "h" st with
+  | Success _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected Failure"
+  | Failure msg ->
+      Alcotest.(check int)
+        "failed apply does not leak a fresh meta"
+        meta_count_before
+        (Hashtbl.length st.elab_ctx.metas);
+      Alcotest.(check bool)
+        "message mentions apply"
+        true
+        (String.length msg >= 6 && String.sub msg 0 6 = "apply:")
+
+(* Unknown name should fail with a clear message. *)
+let test_apply_unknown_name () =
+  let st = init_state ~elab_ctx:e (t (Sort 0)) in
+  match apply "no_such_lemma" st with
+  | Success _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected Failure"
+  | Failure msg ->
+      Alcotest.(check string)
+        "unknown name message"
+        "apply: unknown name 'no_such_lemma'."
+        msg
+
+(* No goals remaining: use the no-arrow path to fully close the state, then apply again. *)
+let test_apply_no_goals () =
+  let st = start_with_hyp "h" (t (Sort 0)) (t (Sort 0)) in
+  let st' =
+    match apply "h" st with
+    | Success s -> s
+    | Failure _ -> Alcotest.fail "first apply should succeed"
+  in
+  match apply "h" st' with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.(check string) "no goals message" "No goals remaining." msg
+  | Success _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected Failure on completed state"
+
+let suite =
+  let open Alcotest in
+  ( "Tactic.apply",
+    [
+      test_case "opens subgoal for premise" `Quick test_apply_opens_subgoal;
+      test_case "no arrow behaves like exact" `Quick test_apply_no_arrow;
+      test_case "fails on conclusion mismatch" `Quick test_apply_conclusion_mismatch;
+      test_case "fails on unknown name" `Quick test_apply_unknown_name;
+      test_case "fails when no goals remain" `Quick test_apply_no_goals;
+    ] )

+open Elab.Term

+
+let t k = { inner = k; loc = dummy_range }
+let name s = t (Name s)
+
+let setup_env () =
+  let ctx = Elab.Interface.create () in
+  Hashtbl.add ctx.env "A" { name = "A"; ty = t (Sort 0); data = Axiom };
+  Hashtbl.add ctx.env "B" { name = "B"; ty = t (Sort 0); data = Axiom };
+  ctx
+
+let start ctx ty = init_state ~elab_ctx:ctx ty
+
+(** [intro] should peel off the arrow, push the hypothesis into the context, and leave the
+    return type as the new goal. *)
+let test_intro_success () =
+  let ctx = setup_env () in
+  let goal_ty = t (Arrow (Some "x", 0, name "A", name "B")) in
+  let st = start ctx goal_ty in
+
+  match intro "h_A" st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success but got Failure: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> (
+      match st'.open_goals with
+      | [ g ] ->
+          (* verify the goal type is now just B *)
+          Alcotest.(check bool)
+            "goal is B"
+            true
+            (match g.goal_type.inner with Name "B" -> true | _ -> false);
+          (* verify the local context has exactly 1 hypothesis *)
+          Alcotest.(check int) "context has 1 hypothesis" 1 (List.length g.ctx);
+          (* verify the hypothesis is named "h_A" *)
+          let hyp = List.hd g.ctx in
+          Alcotest.(check string) "hypothesis name" "h_A" hyp.hyp_name
+      | _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected exactly 1 open goal")
+
+(** [intro] should fail safely if goal is not an implication/forall. *)
+let test_intro_failure () =
+  let ctx = setup_env () in
+  let goal_ty = name "A" in
+  let st = start ctx goal_ty in
+
+  match intro "h" st with
+  | Success _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected Failure but intro succeeded on a non-arrow goal"
+  | Failure _ -> Alcotest.(check pass) "failed safely" () ()
+
+(** [have] should split the current goal G into two goals:
+    - The type T
+    - The continuation T -> G *)
+let test_have_success () =
+  let ctx = setup_env () in
+  let goal_ty = name "B" in
+  let st = start ctx goal_ty in
+
+  match have "h_A" (name "A") st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success but got Failure: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> (
+      match st'.open_goals with
+      | [ proof_goal; cont_goal ] ->

+          Alcotest.failf
+            "expected exactly 2 open goals, got %d"
+            (List.length st'.open_goals))

+    [

+      test_case "intro fails on non-arrow" `Quick test_intro_failure;
+      test_case "have splits goal into proof and continuation" `Quick test_have_success;

+  Elab.Interface.process_file env path_to_env;

+    let lexbuf = Lexing.from_string s in
+    let stmts = Elab.Parser.main Elab.Lexer.token lexbuf in
+    List.iter (Elab.Interface.process_statement env) stmts

+  process "Axiom A : Type";
+  process "Axiom a : A";
+  (env, process)

+

+  match tac st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "tactic failed: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> st'

+let to_kterm env tm =

+let kernel_check env proof goal_ty =
+  let proof_k = to_kterm env (replace_metas env proof) in
+  let ty_k = to_kterm env (replace_metas env goal_ty) in
+  let inferred = Kernel.Infer.Internals.inferType env.kenv (Hashtbl.create 0) proof_k in

+  let got = pp_term env (Elab.Reduce.reduce env (List.hd st.open_goals).goal_type) in

+*)
+let test_exists_kernel_check () =
+  let env, _ = make_env () in
+  let goal_ty = elab env "Exists A (fun (a : A) => True)" in

+open Elab.Term
+open Elab.Proofstate
+open Automation.Tactics
+
+let e = Elab.Interface.create ()
+let t k = { inner = k; loc = dummy_range }
+let name s = t (Name s)
+let app f x = t (App (f, x))
+let eq_term a lhs rhs = app (app (app (name "Eq") a) lhs) rhs
+let start ty = init_state ~elab_ctx:e ty
+
+(* [Eq A a a] : both sides are syntactically identical Names. No beta-reduction needed. *)
+let test_refl_identical () =
+  let a = name "A" in
+  let tm = name "a" in
+  let st = start (eq_term a tm tm) in
+  match reflexivity st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success but got Failure: %s" msg
+  | Success st' ->
+      Alcotest.(check bool) "proof is complete after reflexivity" true (is_complete st')
+
+(** [Eq A (f x) (f x)] — both sides are the same App node. *)
+let test_refl_app () =
+  let a = name "A" in
+  let side = app (name "f") (name "x") in
+  let st = start (eq_term a side side) in
+  match reflexivity st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "expected Success: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> Alcotest.(check bool) "proof complete" true (is_complete st')
+
+let suite =
+  let open Alcotest in
+  ( "Tactic.reflexivity",
+    [
+      test_case "identical names" `Quick test_refl_identical;
+      test_case "identical App nodes" `Quick test_refl_app;
+    ] )

+open Elab.Proofstate
+open Elab.Tactic
+open Automation.Tactics
+
+let path_to_env = "../../../../synthetic/env.ncg"
+
+(*
+  Create the starting environment that we use in the tests.
+  It adds axioms for the types we care about in the tests.
+*)
+let make_env () =
+  let env = Elab.Interface.create () in
+  Elab.Interface.process_file env path_to_env;
+  let process s =
+    let lexbuf = Lexing.from_string s in
+    let stmts = Elab.Parser.main Elab.Lexer.token lexbuf in
+    List.iter (Elab.Interface.process_statement env) stmts
+  in
+  process
+    "Theorem Eq.symm : (A: Type) -> (a: A) -> (b: A) -> (Eq A a b) -> (Eq A b a) := fun \
+     (A: Type) (a b : A) (eq_ab : Eq A a b) => Eq.elim A a (fun (x : A) => Eq A x a) \
+     (Eq.intro A a) b eq_ab";
+  process "Axiom A : Type";
+  process "Axiom a : A";
+  process "Axiom b : A";
+  process "Axiom f : A -> A";
+  process "Axiom a_eq_b : Eq A a b";
+  (env, process)
+
+let elab env s = Elab.Typecheck.elaborate env (Elab.Interface.parse_term s) None
+
+let run_tactic tac st =
+  match tac st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "tactic failed: %s" msg
+  | Success st' -> st'
+
+(** Convert an elab term to a kernel term *)
+let to_kterm env tm =
+  Elab.Reduce.delta_reduce env tm true
+  |> Elab.Reduce.reduce env |> Elab.Convert.conv_to_kterm
+
+(** Check that the kernel accepts [proof] as having type [goal_ty]. *)
+let kernel_check env proof goal_ty =
+  let proof_k = to_kterm env (apply_meta env proof) in
+  let ty_k = to_kterm env goal_ty in
+  let inferred = Kernel.Infer.Internals.inferType env.kenv (Hashtbl.create 0) proof_k in
+  Kernel.Infer.Internals.isDefEq env.kenv (Hashtbl.create 0) inferred ty_k
+
+(* Check that single usage of `rewrite` wcreates the correct new goal type. *)
+let test_rewrite_simple () =
+  let env, _ = make_env () in
+  let goal_ty = elab env "Eq A (f a) (f b)" in
+  let st = init_state ~elab_ctx:env goal_ty in
+  let st = run_tactic (rewrite (elab env "a_eq_b")) st in
+  Alcotest.(check int) "one remaining goal" 1 (List.length st.open_goals);
+  let got = pp_term env (Elab.Reduce.reduce env (List.hd st.open_goals).goal_type) in
+  let exp = pp_term env (elab env "Eq A (f b) (f b)") in
+  Alcotest.(check string) "new goal is Eq A (f b) (f b)" exp got
+
+(* Check that `rewrite` fails when the `lhs` does not appear. *)
+let test_rewrite_no_match () =
+  let env, process = make_env () in
+  process "Axiom x : A";
+  process "Axiom y : A";
+  process "Axiom c : A";
+  process "Axiom d : A";
+  process "Axiom c_eq_d : Eq A c d";
+  let st = init_state ~elab_ctx:env (elab env "Eq A x y") in
+  match rewrite (elab env "c_eq_d") st with
+  | Success _ -> Alcotest.fail "expected missing lhs to fail"
+  | Failure _ -> ()
+
+(*
+  Checks that using `rewrite` and then `reflexivity` tactics produce
+  a proof term that the kernel accepts.
+*)
+let test_rewrite_kernel_check () =
+  let env, _ = make_env () in
+  let goal_ty = elab env "Eq A (f a) (f b)" in
+  let st = init_state ~elab_ctx:env goal_ty in
+  let st = st |> run_tactic (rewrite (elab env "a_eq_b")) |> run_tactic reflexivity in
+  Alcotest.(check bool) "no remaining goals" true (is_complete st);
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    "kernel accepts proof"
+    true
+    (kernel_check env st.statement goal_ty)
+
+let suite =
+  let open Alcotest in
+  ( "Tactic.rewrite",
+    [
+      test_case "rewrite simple" `Quick test_rewrite_simple;
+      test_case "rewrite no match" `Quick test_rewrite_no_match;
+      test_case "rewrite kernel check" `Quick test_rewrite_kernel_check;
+    ] )

+  let st = start ctx goal_ty in
+
+  let tac = succeed_tac >> reflexivity in
+
+  match tac st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "Sequence failed: %s" msg
+  | Success final_st ->
+      Alcotest.(check bool) "proof is complete" true (is_complete final_st)

+  let goal_ty = eq_term (name "A") (name "x") (name "x") in

+  | Success final_st ->
+      Alcotest.(check bool) "proof is complete after try" true (is_complete final_st)
+
+(** Test [repeat]. [repeat fail_tac] applies 0 times safely without crashing and then
+    [reflexivity] closes the goal *)
+let test_repeat () =
+  let ctx = setup_env () in
+  let goal_ty = eq_term (name "A") (name "x") (name "x") in
+  let st = start ctx goal_ty in
+
+  let tac = repeat fail_tac >> reflexivity in
+
+  match tac st with
+  | Failure msg -> Alcotest.failf "Repeat failed: %s" msg
+  | Success final_st ->
+      Alcotest.(check bool) "proof is complete after repeat" true (is_complete final_st)
+
+let suite =

+      test_case "sequence (>>)" `Quick test_seq;

problem_statement:
Support for general Unicode symbols
It would be nice for our proofs to use things like `α` for circles.

### Additional contract requirements

The proof language must accept UTF-8 encoded Unicode symbols in source text, in addition to the existing ASCII syntax.

- Unicode characters such as the Greek letter α must be accepted as identifiers wherever ASCII identifiers are allowed (for example, in binder names, axioms, and terms).
- A Unicode identifier must be preserved as written, so that it can be referenced by the exact same name later (for example, as the name of an introduced hypothesis).
- The Unicode symbols ∀ and ∃ must be usable as universal- and existential-quantifier notations that produce the same meaning as the corresponding existing ASCII spellings.
- The Unicode symbol → must be usable as a function/forall arrow and must produce the same meaning as the existing ASCII `->` spelling.

These requirements concern only observable source-language behavior: parsing of Unicode inputs and the meaning and name-preservation of the results. They impose no constraint on how parsing is implemented, on which libraries or dependencies are used, or on any internal lexer, token, or buffer interfaces.

@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+open Parser
+
+(* Valid identifier characters, stolen and adapted from Lean *)
+
+(* Letter-like Unicode ranges (Greek, Coptic, etc.) *)
+let letter_like_unicode = [%sedlex.regexp?
+    0x3B1 .. 0x3C9     |  (* Lower greek *)
+    0x391 .. 0x3A9     |  (* Upper greek *)
+    0x3CA .. 0x3FB     |  (* Coptic letters *)
+    0x1F00 .. 0x1FFE   |  (* Polytonic Greek Extended *)
+    0x2100 .. 0x214F   |  (* Letter-like symbols block *)
+    0x1D49C .. 0x1D59F    (* Latin Script, Double-struck, Fractur *)
+]
+
+(* Subscript and superscript Unicode *)
+let subscript_superscript_unicode = [%sedlex.regexp?
+    0x207F .. 0x2089  |  (* n superscript and numeric subscripts *)
+    0x2090 .. 0x209C  |  (* letter-like subscripts *)
+    0x1D62 .. 0x1D6A     (* letter-like subscripts *)
+]
+
+(* Characters allowed at the start of an identifier *)
+let ident_start = [%sedlex.regexp?
+    'a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' | 
+    letter_like_unicode
+]
+
+(* Characters allowed in the middle of an identifier *)
+let ident_continue = [%sedlex.regexp?
+    'a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' |
+    '\'' | '?' | '!' | '.' |
+    letter_like_unicode | subscript_superscript_unicode
+]
+
+(* Characters allowed at the end of an identifier, ident_continue without '.' *)
+let ident_end = [%sedlex.regexp?
+    'a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' |
+    '\'' | '?' | '!' |
+    letter_like_unicode | subscript_superscript_unicode
+]
+
+let ident = [%sedlex.regexp? ident_start | ident_start, Star ident_continue, ident_end]
+let string_char = [%sedlex.regexp? 'a' .. 'z' | 'A' .. 'Z' | '0' .. '9' | '_' | '.' | '/']
+
+let token lexbuf =
+  let rec token lexbuf =
+    match%sedlex lexbuf with
+    | Plus (' ' | '\t' | '\r' | '\n') -> token lexbuf
+    | "(*" ->
+        comment lexbuf;
+        token lexbuf
+    | "fun" -> FUN
+    | "Axiom" -> AXIOM
+    | "Theorem" -> THEOREM
+    | "Definition" -> DEFINITION
+    | "Import" -> IMPORT
+    | ":=" -> DEFEQ
+    | "->" | Utf8 "→" -> ARROW
+    | "<->" | Utf8 "↔" -> IFF
+    | "=>" -> MAPSTO
+    | ":" -> COLON
+    | "(" -> LPAREN
+    | ")" -> RPAREN
+    | "Type" -> TYPE
+    | "Prop" -> PROP
+    | "_" -> UNDERSCORE
+    | "=" -> EQUALS
+    | Utf8 "≠" -> NOT_EQUALS
+    | "<" -> LESS_THAN
+    | "+" -> PLUS
+    | "\\/" | Utf8 "∨" -> OR
+    | "/\\" | Utf8 "∧" -> AND
+    | "~" | Utf8 "¬" -> NOT
+    | Utf8 "∃" -> EXISTS
+    | Utf8 "∀" -> FORALL
+    | "," -> COMMA
+    | "#print" -> PRINT_DIRECTIVE
+    | "#infer" -> INFER_DIRECTIVE
+    | "#check" -> CHECK_DIRECTIVE
+    | "#reduce" -> REDUCE_DIRECTIVE
+    | "#opaque" -> OPAQUE_DIRECTIVE
+    | '"', Star string_char, '"' ->
+        let s = Sedlexing.Utf8.lexeme lexbuf in
+        let len = String.length s in
+        STRING_LITERAL (String.sub s 1 (len - 2))
+    | ident -> IDENT (Sedlexing.Utf8.lexeme lexbuf)
+    | "Proof." -> PROOF
+    | "Qed." -> QED
+    | "." -> PERIOD
+    | eof -> EOF
+    | any ->
+        let bad = Sedlexing.Utf8.lexeme lexbuf in
+        failwith (Printf.sprintf "unexpected character: %S" bad)
+    | _ -> failwith "unreachable"
+  and comment lexbuf =
+    match%sedlex lexbuf with
+    | "*)" -> ()
+    | "(*" ->
+        comment lexbuf;
+        comment lexbuf
+    | eof -> failwith "Unterminated comment"
+    | any -> comment lexbuf
+    | _ -> failwith "unreachable"
+  in
+  token lexbuf

+(*
+  Checks that terms written with the Unicode universal- and
+  existential-quantifier symbols (U+2200 forall and U+2203 exists) are
+  accepted in place of the corresponding existing ASCII spellings and
+  elaborate to the same terms as those spellings. This is the behavior
+  requested by the "Support for general Unicode symbols" issue.
+
+  The contract fixes the *meaning* of the quantifier symbols, not one
+  exact surface spelling. An implementation may, for example, treat
+  U+2200 as another spelling of the ASCII "->" function/forall arrow,
+  add a dedicated prefix notation such as "U+2200 (b : A), ...", or
+  treat U+2203 as another spelling of the defined name Exists in an
+  application such as "U+2203 A (fun c => ...)". Therefore this test
+
+  - requires that at least one contract-consistent spelling using
+    U+2200 of a simple universal proposition is accepted, and that at
+    least one contract-consistent spelling using U+2203 of a simple
+    existential proposition is accepted, without mandating any
+    particular one of the spellings, and
+  - requires that *every* accepted contract-consistent spelling of a
+    proposition that nests a universal quantifier around an existential
+    one elaborates to exactly the same term as the ASCII spelling of
+    the same proposition (and analogously for the plain existential
+    proposition).
+
+  All candidate terms are parsed through the public
+  [Elab.Interface.parse_term] entrypoint only, so the test does not
+  depend on any internal lexer, token, or grammar interface.
+*)
+let test_parse_unicode_quantifiers () =
+  let env, _ = make_env () in
+  (* U+2203 (exists) and U+2200 (forall) as UTF-8 encoded strings. *)
+  let exists_sym = "\226\136\131" in
+  let forall_sym = "\226\136\128" in
+  let try_elab s =
+    match Elab.Typecheck.elaborate env (Elab.Interface.parse_term s) None with
+    | tm -> Some tm
+    | exception _ -> None
+  in
+  (* Check that every candidate spelling the implementation accepts
+     elaborates to the same term as the ASCII spelling of the same
+     proposition; candidates the implementation does not accept impose
+     no requirement. *)
+  let check_accepted_forms ascii_s ascii_pp candidates =
+    List.iter
+      (fun (s, desc) ->
+        match try_elab s with
+        | Some tm ->
+            Alcotest.(check string)
+              (Printf.sprintf "accepted form (%s) matches ASCII %S" desc ascii_s)
+              ascii_pp (pp_term env tm)
+        | None -> ())
+      candidates
+  in
+  (* Acceptance, universal: the simple universal proposition
+     "(b : A) -> Eq A b a" must be expressible with U+2200. Every
+     candidate below is a contract-consistent spelling of that
+     proposition, so the implementation must accept at least one of
+     them, but no particular one is mandated. *)
+  let simple_forall_ascii = pp_term env (elab env "(b : A) -> Eq A b a") in
+  let simple_forall_candidates =
+    [
+      (Printf.sprintf "(b : A) %s Eq A b a" forall_sym,
+       "pair notation with U+2200 in place of ->");
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s (b : A), Eq A b a" forall_sym,
+       "prefix spelling using U+2200");
+    ]
+  in
+  check_accepted_forms "(b : A) -> Eq A b a" simple_forall_ascii
+    simple_forall_candidates;
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    (Printf.sprintf "some quantifier-symbol spelling of %S is accepted"
+       "(b : A) -> Eq A b a")
+    true
+    (List.exists (fun (s, _) -> try_elab s <> None) simple_forall_candidates);
+  (* Acceptance, existential: the ASCII spelling
+     "Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)". *)
+  let exists_ascii = pp_term env (elab env "Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)") in
+  let exists_candidates =
+    [
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s A (fun c => Eq A a c)" exists_sym,
+       "application with U+2203 in place of the defined name Exists");
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s (c : A), Eq A a c" exists_sym,
+       "prefix spelling using U+2203");
+    ]
+  in
+  (* Every accepted spelling using U+2203 must elaborate to the same
+     term as the ASCII spelling ... *)
+  check_accepted_forms "Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)" exists_ascii
+    exists_candidates;
+  (* ... and at least one such spelling must be accepted. *)
+  Alcotest.(check bool)
+    (Printf.sprintf "some quantifier-symbol spelling of %S is accepted"
+       "Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)")
+    true
+    (List.exists (fun (s, _) -> try_elab s <> None) exists_candidates);
+  (* Meaning: the universal proposition with a nested existential, the
+     ASCII spelling "(b : A) -> Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)". No
+     particular spelling using the quantifier symbols is required to be
+     accepted, but every contract-consistent spelling that the
+     implementation does accept must elaborate to the same term as the
+     ASCII spelling. *)

+    pp_term env (elab env "(b : A) -> Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)")

+  let forall_candidates =

+       "pair notation with U+2200 in place of ->");
+      (Printf.sprintf "(b : A) %s %s A (fun c => Eq A a c)" forall_sym
+         exists_sym,
+       "pair notation with U+2200 and U+2203 in place of Exists");
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s (b : A), Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)" forall_sym,
+       "prefix U+2200 with ASCII Exists");
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s (b : A), %s A (fun c => Eq A a c)" forall_sym
+         exists_sym,
+       "prefix U+2200 with U+2203 in place of Exists");
+      (Printf.sprintf "%s (b : A), %s (c : A), Eq A a c" forall_sym exists_sym,
+       "prefix spelling using U+2200 and U+2203");
+    ]
+  in
+  check_accepted_forms "(b : A) -> Exists A (fun c => Eq A a c)" forall_ascii
+    forall_candidates

problem_statement:
Allow tracking bookmark with non-yet-tracked remotes
When publishing a branch on Git remote, we need to track the bookmark (`bt`) first and then push (`Pp`). However, when selecting what to track, not only do `foo@origin` and `foo@upstream` count (assuming we have `origin` and `upstream` as configured remotes), but also `foo` (meaning `foo@<default-remote>`), and the latter is not shown in the dropdown list (fortunately I can type it manually, but alas).

It should also be noted that `jj bookmark track foo@origin` is deprecated in favor of `jj bookmark track foo --remote origin`, so it's possibly worth adjusting the mapped command at the same time.

Many thanks in advance ð

### Additional contract requirements

Bookmark track (popup) clarification:

- The bookmark track picker lists the cross-product of local bookmark names and
  every configured Git remote, i.e. one candidate "name@remote" for each
  combination of a local bookmark and a configured remote. Unqualified local
  bookmark names (which would implicitly target a default remote) are not
  offered as picker candidates; every choice is explicit. When no Git remotes
  are configured, the picker opens with an empty candidate list.
- Confirming a bookmark track action must target the selected bookmark at the
  selected remote. The underlying track command may be issued either in the
  qualified form ("bookmark name@remote") or in the equivalent split form that
  passes the bookmark name and the remote separately (e.g. "--remote remote");
  both command forms are acceptable, and migrating to the split form is not
  mandatory. The visible outcome is unchanged: on success an informational
  notification is shown, while a failed track command produces a warning
  notification that includes the track failure.
- Cancelling the picker performs no track command at all.

diff --git a/tests/specs/neojj/popups/bookmark/actions_spec.lua b/tests/specs/neojj/popups/bookmark/actions_spec.lua
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..00000000
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/specs/neojj/popups/bookmark/actions_spec.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,285 @@
+local MODULE = "neojj.popups.bookmark.actions"
+
+-- Freshly re-requires the actions module and its dependencies so each
+-- scenario can provide *behavioral* test doubles for the modules the track
+-- action talks to. The doubles only need to satisfy the observable contract:
+-- any picker-cache-shaped module that yields local bookmark names, any
+-- remote-listing command that reports the configured Git remotes, and any
+-- track-command builder whose invocation can be observed.
+local function run_track(scenario)
+  local state = {
+    track_calls = {},
+    picker_items = nil,
+    opened = false,
+    infos = {},
+    warns = {},
+  }
+
+  local local_bookmarks = scenario.local_bookmarks or { "main", "dev" }
+  local remotes = scenario.remotes or { "origin" }
+  local remote_lines = {}
+  for _, remote in ipairs(remotes) do
+    table.insert(remote_lines, remote .. " git@example.com:org/repo.git")
+  end
+  local track_result = scenario.track_result or { code = 0, stderr = {} }
+
+  -- Observable record of a track invocation: the bookmark name and the remote
+  -- it targets. The remote may be supplied separately or embedded in the
+  -- bookmark argument as "name@remote"; both shapes are recorded identically.
+  local function record(name, remote)
+    if not remote and type(name) == "string" then
+      name, remote = name:match("^(.+)@([^@]+)$")
+    end
+    table.insert(state.track_calls, { name = name, remote = remote })
+  end
+
+  -- Track-command test double tolerant of both invocation shapes:
+  -- args(name).call() and args(name).remote(remote).call().
+  local track_builder_double = {
+    args = function(name)
+      local builder = { _shape = {} }
+      builder.remote = function(remote)
+        builder._shape.remote = remote
+        return builder
+      end
+      builder.call = function()
+        record(name, builder._shape.remote)
+        return track_result
+      end
+      return builder
+    end,
+  }
+
+  -- jj library double, including the "neojj.lib.jj.bookmark" submodule that
+  -- some command-construction styles route the track invocation through.
+  local jj_double = {
+    cli = {
+      bookmark_track = track_builder_double,
+      git_remote_list = {
+        call = function()
+          return { code = 0, stdout = remote_lines }
+        end,
+      },
+    },
+    bookmark = {
+      -- Track double recording the observable (name, remote) pair for every
+      -- permitted invocation form: a single qualified "name@remote" target
+      -- or the equivalent split form track(name, remote). The record helper
+      -- above normalizes a qualified single argument, and an explicit remote
+      -- argument is preserved here instead of being dropped.
+      track = function(target, remote)
+        record(target, remote)
+        return track_result
+      end,
+    },
+  }
+  setmetatable(jj_double, {
+    __index = function(_, key)
+      return require("neojj.lib.jj." .. key)
+    end,
+  })
+
+  -- Picker-cache double whose keys are observable constructors. The original
+  -- module's functions are captured up front, then replaced with recording
+  -- versions so observable behavior is checked no matter which picker-cache
+  -- function builds the track candidates from the repository state below.
+  local picker_cache_original = require("neojj.lib.picker_cache")
+  local picker_cache_double = {}
+  for key, value in pairs(picker_cache_original) do
+    if type(value) == "function" then
+      picker_cache_double[key] = function(...)
+        return value(...)
+      end
+    else
+      picker_cache_double[key] = value
+    end
+  end
+
+  local function wrap_constructor(key)
+    local underlying = picker_cache_double[key]
+    if type(underlying) == "function" then
+      picker_cache_double[key] = function(...)
+        local result = underlying(...)
+        if type(result) == "table" then
+          local open_async = result.open_async
+          result.open_async = function(self, opts)
+            state.opened = true
+            state.picker_items = result.list
+            if open_async then
+              return open_async(self, opts)
+            end
+          end
+        end
+        return result
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  -- The track candidates depend on configuring the repository state that the
+  -- picker data flows from. The local bookmark names are stored in the
+  -- repository state, and the configured remote names come from the remote
+  -- listing double above, so candidates follow the observable contract.
+  local repo_original = require("neojj.lib.jj.repository")
+  local repo_double = setmetatable({}, { __index = repo_original })
+  repo_double.state = { bookmarks = { items = {} } }
+  repo_double.instance = function()
+    return repo_double
+  end
+  for _, name in ipairs(local_bookmarks) do
+    table.insert(repo_double.state.bookmarks.items, { name = name })
+  end
+  local jj_repo_meta = {
+    __index = function(_, key)
+      if key == "repo" then
+        return repo_double
+      end
+      return require("neojj.lib.jj." .. key)
+    end,
+  }
+
+  -- Assemble the doubles.
+  local saved = {}
+  local function override(name, value)
+    saved[name] = package.loaded[name]
+    package.loaded[name] = value
+  end
+  override("neojj.lib.jj", setmetatable({
+    cli = jj_double.cli,
+    bookmark = jj_double.bookmark,
+  }, jj_repo_meta))
+  override("neojj.lib.jj.bookmark", jj_double.bookmark)
+  override("neojj.lib.jj.cli", jj_double.cli)
+  override("neojj.lib.jj.repository", repo_double)
+  override("neojj.lib.picker_cache", picker_cache_double)
+  override("neojj.lib.notification", {
+    info = function(msg)
+      table.insert(state.infos, msg)
+    end,
+    warn = function(msg)
+      table.insert(state.warns, msg)
+    end,
+  })
+  override("neojj.lib.input", {
+    get_user_input = function()
+      return nil
+    end,
+    get_permission = function()
+      return false
+    end,
+  })
+  override("neojj.lib.finder", package.loaded["neojj.lib.finder"])
+  override("neojj.buffers.fuzzy_finder", {
+    new = function(items)
+      return {
+        list = items,
+        open_async = function(_, opts)
+          state.opened = true
+          state.picker_items = items
+          if type(scenario.select) == "function" then
+            return scenario.select(items, opts)
+          end
+          return scenario.select
+        end,
+      }
+    end,
+  })
+
+  for _, key in ipairs { "get_local_bookmark_names", "get_bookmark_names", "get_trackable_bookmark_names", "get_bookmarks" } do
+    wrap_constructor(key)
+  end
+
+  local saved_subject = package.loaded[MODULE]
+  package.loaded[MODULE] = nil
+
+  local ok, err = pcall(function()
+    require(MODULE).track()
+  end)
+
+  package.loaded[MODULE] = saved_subject
+  for name, prev in pairs(saved) do
+    package.loaded[name] = prev
+  end
+
+  assert.is_true(ok, err)
+  return state
+end
+
+--- Sorts a copy of the picker items lexicographically.
+local function sorted(items)
+  local copy = vim.deepcopy(items or {})
+  table.sort(copy)
+  return copy
+end
+
+describe("bookmark track action", function()
+  it("shows cross-product of local bookmarks and remotes in picker", function()
+    local state = run_track {
+      remotes = { "origin" },
+      select = "main@origin",
+    }
+
+    assert.is_true(state.opened)
+    assert.are.same({ "dev@origin", "main@origin" }, sorted(state.picker_items))
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.track_calls)
+    assert.are.equal("main", state.track_calls[1].name)
+    assert.are.equal("origin", state.track_calls[1].remote)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.warns)
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.infos)
+  end)
+
+  it("builds cross-product for multiple remotes", function()
+    local state = run_track {
+      remotes = { "origin", "upstream" },
+      select = "dev@upstream",
+    }
+
+    assert.is_true(state.opened)
+    assert.are.same(
+      { "dev@origin", "dev@upstream", "main@origin", "main@upstream" },
+      sorted(state.picker_items)
+    )
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.track_calls)
+    assert.are.equal("dev", state.track_calls[1].name)
+    assert.are.equal("upstream", state.track_calls[1].remote)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.warns)
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.infos)
+  end)
+
+  it("shows empty picker when no remotes are configured", function()
+    local state = run_track {
+      remotes = {},
+      select = nil,
+    }
+
+    assert.is_true(state.opened)
+    assert.are.same({}, sorted(state.picker_items))
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.track_calls)
+  end)
+
+  it("shows warning on track failure including the failure message", function()
+    local state = run_track {
+      remotes = { "origin" },
+      select = "main@origin",
+      track_result = { code = 1, stderr = { "error: bookmark main is conflicted" } },
+    }
+
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.track_calls)
+    assert.are.equal("main", state.track_calls[1].name)
+    assert.are.equal("origin", state.track_calls[1].remote)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.infos)
+    assert.are.equal(1, #state.warns)
+    assert.is_truthy(state.warns[1]:find("bookmark main is conflicted", 1, true))
+  end)
+
+  it("aborts when picker is canceled", function()
+    local state = run_track {
+      remotes = { "origin" },
+      select = nil,
+    }
+
+    assert.is_true(state.opened)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.track_calls)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.infos)
+    assert.are.equal(0, #state.warns)
+  end)
+end)

problem_statement:
[Bug]: Future dates parsed to past
### Contact Details

_No response_

### What happened?

**Expected behaviour**

When providing a date in the future, there should be an indication, that the date is in the future (e.g. "in 20 seconds")

**Actual behaviour**

When providing a date in the future, the absolute value of the time difference is used, resulting in an incorrect representation, that always talks about the time being in the past

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run this code:
```dart
 DateTime futureTime = DateTime.now().add(const Duration(seconds: 20));
 String futureTimeString = GetTimeAgo.parse(futureTime);
 print('Future time string: $futureTimeString');
```
2. See the output: `I/flutter (17717): Future time string: 19 seconds ago`  

**Technical Details**

[HIDDEN]

### Version

^2.3.2

### What devices are you seeing the problem on?

Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac, Linux

### OS

Android 12

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

### Additional contract requirements

## Observable behavior for future dates

- When the parsed `DateTime` is in the future relative to the current time, the returned string must convey that the time lies in the future instead of reading as an elapsed, past-style result. In the default English locale, every relative-time branch (the sub-15-second "just now" range, seconds, about a minute, minutes, about an hour, hours, about a day, and days) must render a future input with the future marker: the returned string must begin with `in` followed by a space (for example, a date 20 seconds ahead is presented in a style such as "in 19 seconds" rather than "19 seconds ago", and the sub-15-second "just now" message must not be returned for such an input).
- Non-English locales, whether bundled or custom, are not required to use the English marker `in`, and no particular localized future wording is mandated. For any locale, a future relative-time result must not reuse that locale's past-style output: it must not contain that locale's past marker (for example the French past prefix "il y a", or the past suffix of a custom locale) and must differ from the result produced for the equally distant past date in that same locale.
- For dates beyond the largest relative-time branch (more than 7 days away, where the formatted date is returned), past and future inputs must be distinguishable in the output.
- Existing behavior for past dates is unchanged: all current past-output formats, locale handling, custom locales, and custom date patterns remain as before.

problem_statement:
[FEAT] Optionally ignore casing for `find_file()`
## Feature Request

### Description
Add option to allow `find_file()` to ignore casing.

**Example**
 ```r                                                                                                                                                                               
 library(connector)                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                    
 tmp <- tempdir()                                                                                                                                                                   
 write.csv(data.frame(USUBJID = "SUBJ01"), file.path(tmp, "dm.csv"), row.names = FALSE)                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                    
 cnt <- connector_fs(path = tmp)                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                    
 # Works
 cnt$read_cnt("dm")                                                                                                                                                                 
 #> Ã¢ÂÂ¹ Found one file: /tmp/.../dm.csv                                                                                                                                               
 #>   USUBJID                                                                                                                                                                       
 #> 1  SUBJ01                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                    
 # Fails
 cnt$read_cnt("DM")                                                                                                                                                                 
 #> Error in `find_file()`:                                                                                                                                                         
 #> ! No file found with name: DM                                                                                                                                                   
 ```                  

### Proposed Solution
[HIDDEN]

### Use Case
_General use-case_: Allows scripts to be generated with specifications that are not so tightly coupled with how the data is named on the storage system. 

_Specific example_: When building ADaM programs using mighty, this would allow the ADaM specifications to be made in uppercase as per CDISC guidelines, regardless of how the casing for the datasets is set

### Additional Context

### Impact

### Related Issues
None

### Additional contract requirements

- A boolean global setting controls case-sensitivity of file-name matching. It is exposed as the R option `connector.fs_ignore_case`; when set to `TRUE` it makes file lookups case-insensitive (e.g., a lookup for `"DM"` matches a file named `dm.csv`).
- The default value of this setting is `FALSE`: unless it is explicitly set to `TRUE`, file-name matching remains case-sensitive, and looking up `"DM"` when only `dm.csv` exists reports that no file was found.
- This case-insensitive matching applies both to the internal file-finding utility and to the file-system connector read path, so that reading a table by name from a `ConnectorFS` object (e.g., via `read_cnt`) also honors the setting.
- When the setting is `TRUE` and the file's on-disk name differs in case from the requested name, the lookup succeeds without error and the located file is returned under its actual on-disk name.

problem_statement:
Clean up for `TerrainFollowingDiscretization`
The new terrain-following coordinate implementation in https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/pull/506 can use a bit of clean up:

- find verbose names for the grid-relative vertical velocity and momentum [HIDDEN]
- clean up syntax (eg functions with `_` prefixes which are not kernel functions)
- resolve [HIDDEN] false dichotomy (two names being used for the same object)
- probably should do more validation include a 3D validation of flow over an isolated hill

Any other technical-debt-reducing activities?

cc @kaiyuan-cheng @dkytezab

### Additional contract requirements

# Terrain-following cleanup contract

For terrain-following `CompressibleDynamics`, the coordinate-normal diagnostic
fields are named `contravariant_vertical_velocity` and
`contravariant_vertical_momentum`. The former symbolic field names are removed.

`Breeze.AtmosphereModels.advecting_momentum(model)` is the single momentum
transport dispatch. On terrain-following models its vertical component is the
contravariant vertical momentum. `transport_velocities(model)` likewise returns
the contravariant vertical velocity as its vertical component. The superseded
`transport_momentum` dispatch is removed rather than retained as an alias.

Non-kernel terrain-following helpers use ordinary Julia names without a leading
underscore. Superseded underscored helper forms are removed rather than retained
as aliases; this naming rule does not apply to kernel functions.

The depicted group name is required, not merely illustrative. - The applicable warning period is the deadline's own warning period when one is specified on the deadline (for example with a `-Nd` warning notation); otherwise it is the configured default deadline warning period (`org_deadline_warning_days`, 14 days by default). - Within the warning period, only deadlines at most 7 days in the future are highlighted as upcoming. This default must not override a `@org.agenda.deadline.upcoming` highlight that the user has already defined; a user-defined group takes precedence.

contract_addendum:
All requirements in the base problem statement apply, plus the following clarifications:

- In the agenda view, an unfinished item whose deadline is in the future and falls within its applicable warning period must be highlighted with a public highlight group named `@org.agenda.deadline.upcoming`, instead of the highlight group used for items past their scheduled date. The depicted group name is required, not merely illustrative.
- The applicable warning period is the deadline's own warning period when one is specified on the deadline (for example with a `-Nd` warning notation); otherwise it is the configured default deadline warning period (`org_deadline_warning_days`, 14 days by default).
- Within the warning period, only deadlines at most 7 days in the future are highlighted as upcoming. Future deadlines more than 7 days away still appear in the agenda when they are within their warning period, but receive no special deadline highlight.
- Deadlines due today or in the past keep their existing highlight behavior, done items keep their existing behavior, and scheduled (non-deadline) items are unaffected.
- The `@org.agenda.deadline.upcoming` highlight group must be given a default foreground color derived from the `WarningMsg` highlight, so that it adapts to the active colorscheme and remains distinguishable. This default must not override a `@org.agenda.deadline.upcoming` highlight that the user has already defined; a user-defined group takes precedence.

### Additional contract requirements

## YAML null values

When loading YAML with the default settings, a mapping key followed by a blank
(implicit) value must be preserved as the explicit null sentinel value
(`vim.NIL`) in the resulting table, rather than being omitted (Lua nil). The
remaining values in the input must still be loaded normally. For example,
loading `"tags: \ncomplete: false"` yields a table whose `tags` entry is
`vim.NIL` and whose `complete` entry is `false`.

## Frontmatter serialization of null values

When frontmatter is dumped (including when a note buffer is saved), a
frontmatter entry whose value is the null sentinel (`vim.NIL`) must not be
dropped. It must be emitted as a blank mapping entry, i.e. the key followed by
a colon and nothing after it. For example, serializing
`{ id = "id", aliases = {}, tags = {}, random = vim.NIL }` in field order
produces:

```
---
id: id
aliases: []
tags: []
random:
---
```

Together, these behaviors ensure that saving a buffer preserves blank
frontmatter entries instead of deleting them.

+-- Test support: MiniTest stdout reporter emitting one `parse_log_lua_nvim`
+-- compatible line per executed test case, plus a detailed failure report.
+-- Lines are written at column zero in one of these forms:
+--   "Success || <stable unique test name>"
+--   "Fail || <stable unique test name>"
+--   "Skip || <stable unique test name>"
+-- Each line is derived from the case's real `exec.fails`/`exec.notes` result.
+-- On finish the reporter quits Neovim with `0cquit` when every reported case
+-- passed and `1cquit` when any reported case failed, so the process exit
+-- status reflects the real overall test outcome.
+
+local M = {}
+
+M.new = function()
+  local res = {}
+
+  res.start = function(cases)
+    res.all_cases = cases
+  end
+
+  res.update = function(_) end
+
+  res.finish = function()
+    local all_pass = true
+    local lines = {}
+    for _, case in ipairs(res.all_cases or {}) do
+      local name = table.concat(case.desc or {}, " | ")
+      local exec = case.exec or {}
+      local fails = exec.fails or {}
+      local notes = exec.notes or {}
+      if #fails > 0 then
+        all_pass = false
+        table.insert(lines, "Fail || " .. name)
+        for _, fail in ipairs(fails) do
+          table.insert(lines, "    FAIL detail: " .. tostring(fail))
+        end
+      elseif #notes > 0 and tostring(notes[1]):match("^Skipped") then
+        table.insert(lines, "Skip || " .. name)
+      else
+        table.insert(lines, "Success || " .. name)
+      end
+    end
+    io.stdout:write(table.concat(lines, "\n") .. "\n")
+    io.flush()
+    vim.cmd(("silent! %scquit"):format(all_pass and 0 or 1))
+  end
+
+  return res
+end
+
+return M

+### Suffixes
+
+You can add a suffix to any substitution with `{{var:suffix}}`. The suffix is passed as the second argument to your substitution function. The built-in `date` and `time` substitutions treat the suffix as a format override.

+created: {{date:YYYY-MM-DD}}
+time: {{time:HH:mm}}
+quarter: {{date:Q}}
+```

+  return string.format("%s:%s", tostring(ctx.template_name), tostring(suffix))
+end
+```

diff --git a/scripts/minitest_stdout_reporter.lua b/scripts/minitest_stdout_reporter.lua
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f5d1fd1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/minitest_stdout_reporter.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+--- A `mini.test` reporter that prints one machine-readable, per-test line to
+--- stdout for every executed test case, and exits non-zero when any case fails.
+---
+--- Lines use the stable grammar:
+---   Success || <case description>
+---   Fail || <case description>
+---   Skip || <case description>
+---
+--- This complements `mini.test`'s default dot/summary reporter, which only
+--- prints aggregate output (dots and a fail/notes count) for passing runs and
+--- so does not expose a per-test record.
+---
+--- Usage (headless):
+---   nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./scripts/minimal_init.lua \
+---     -c "lua MiniTest.run_file('tests/test_templates.lua', {
+---           execute = { reporter = dofile('scripts/minitest_stdout_reporter.lua') },
+---         })"
+
+local M = {}
+
+local all_cases
+
+M.start = function(cases)
+  all_cases = cases
+end
+
+M.update = function(case_num)
+  local case = all_cases[case_num]
+  if type(case.exec) ~= "table" then
+    return
+  end
+  local state = case.exec.state
+  -- Only report finished cases.
+  if state == nil or vim.startswith(state, "Executing") then
+    return
+  end
+
+  local status
+  if vim.startswith(state, "Pass") then
+    status = "Success"
+  elseif vim.startswith(state, "Fail") then
+    status = "Fail"
+  else
+    status = "Skip"
+  end
+
+  local name = table.concat(case.desc, " | "):gsub("\n", " ")
+  io.stdout:write(string.format("%s || %s\n", status, name))
+  io.stdout:flush()
+end
+
+M.finish = function()
+  local n_fail = 0
+  for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+    if type(case.exec) == "table" and case.exec.state ~= nil and vim.startswith(case.exec.state, "Fail") then
+      n_fail = n_fail + 1
+    end
+  end
+  vim.cmd(string.format("silent! %scquit", n_fail > 0 and 1 or 0))
+end
+
+return M

+-- Unknown `{{...}}` template variables fall back to an interactive prompt via
+-- `api.input` (see `substitute_template_variables`). Stub it out so the
+-- headless test run never blocks waiting for user input; returning "" skips

 ---@param ctx? obsidian.TemplateContext|{}
@@ -20,6 +28,26 @@ local tmp_template_context = function(ctx)
   })
 end
 
+---Freeze `os.time` to the given epoch while running `fn`.
+---
+---This makes date/time assertions deterministic and independent of when the
+---test suite executes, while testing the substitution pipeline end-to-end
+---(including the substitutions' own `os.time()` calls).
+---
+---@param epoch integer
+---@param fn fun()
+local with_frozen_time = function(epoch, fn)
+  local original_time = os.time
+  os.time = function()
+    return epoch
+  end
+  local ok, err = pcall(fn)
+  os.time = original_time
+  if not ok then
+    error(err, 0)
+  end
+end
+
 T["substitute_template_variables()"] = new_set()
 
 T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should substitute built-in variables"] = function()
@@ -43,6 +71,64 @@ T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should support moment date_format"] = func
   Obsidian.opts.templates.date_format = previous
 end
 
+T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should support template suffix"] = function()
+  local text = "year is {{date:YYYY}} and hour is {{time:HH}}"
+  eq(
+    string.format("year is %s and hour is %s", moment.format(os.time(), "YYYY"), moment.format(os.time(), "HH")),
+    M.substitute_template_variables(text, tmp_template_context())
+  )
+end
+
+T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should support week and quarter date suffixes"] = function()
+  local text = "week is {{date:WW}} and quarter is {{date:Q}}"
+  eq(
+    string.format("week is %s and quarter is %s", moment.format(os.time(), "WW"), moment.format(os.time(), "Q")),
+    M.substitute_template_variables(text, tmp_template_context())
+  )
+end
+
+-- 2022-01-01 12:00:00 UTC. On this date the ISO week (`moment`'s `WW`) is "52"
+-- while strftime `%W` is "00", so a fixed timestamps makes it possible to tell
+-- the correct ISO-week formatter apart from a naive `%W`-style one regardless
+-- of when the test suite happens to run.
+local iso_week_epoch = 1641038400
+T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should treat WW suffix as ISO week, not strftime %W"] = function()
+  with_frozen_time(iso_week_epoch, function()
+    local ww = M.substitute_template_variables("{{date:WW}}", tmp_template_context())
+    -- Sanity check: this epoch really does discriminate ISO week from `%W`
+    -- (in UTC) so the assertions below are meaningful in any timezone.
+    assert(os.date("!%W", iso_week_epoch) == "00", "test epoch must have strftime %W == 00")
+    eq(moment.format(iso_week_epoch, "WW"), ww)
+    eq("52", ww)
+    assert(ww ~= os.date("!%W", iso_week_epoch), "WW suffix must be the ISO week, not strftime %W")
+  end)
+end
+T["substitute_template_variables()"]["should determine suffix substitutions from a fixed frontmatter template"] = function()
+  with_frozen_time(iso_week_epoch, function()
+    local text = table.concat({
+      "---",
+      "created: {{date}} {{time}}",
+      "week: {{date:WW}}",
+      "year: {{date:YYYY}}",
+      "quarter: {{date:Q}}",
+      "---",
+    }, "\n")
+    local expected = table.concat({
+      "---",

problem_statement:
string (non-function) template substitutions broke in v3.15.9
### ð Describe the bug

In v3.15.8, template substitutions used to support values which are strings (as well as values which are functions). Now, all template substitutions _have_ to be functions. This breaks existing behavior for users.

For example, one used to be able to include a substitution like this:
```lua
  USERNAME = os.getenv("USERNAME"),
```
But now one has to wrap it in a function like this:
```lua
  USERNAME = function()
   return os.getenv("USERNAME")
  end,
```
(I've added more complete lazy.nvim configs in the "Config" section below.)

Without wrapping everything in a function, one now gets this error:

```
Error executing Lua callback: ...share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/templates.lua:59: attempt to call upvalue 'subst' (a string value)
stack traceback:
	...share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/templates.lua:59: in function <...share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/templates.lua:58>
	[C]: in function 'gsub'
	...share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/templates.lua:58: in function 'substitute_template_variables'
	...share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/templates.lua:138: in function 'insert_template'
	...im/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/commands/template.lua:16: in function 'insert_template'
	...im/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/commands/template.lua:26: in function 'func'
	...e/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/lua/obsidian/commands/init.lua:130: in function 'handle_command'
	....local/share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/plugin/obsidian.lua:11: in function <....local/share/nvim/lazy/obsidian.nvim/plugin/obsidian.lua:1>
```

The change that broke supporting string values is here: https://github.com/obsidian-nvim/obsidian.nvim/pull/685/changes#diff-d54140184edb31b7cad547ea17fae957e6544793b70a857d79ac6b321ccf377cL85
(removal of lines 85+ of templates.lua broke string support)

I think the old behavior should have been maintained, where values of template substitutions could be either strings or functions (not just functions). Thank you!

### Config

Used to work in v3.15.8, but now broken:
```lua
{
  "obsidian-nvim/obsidian.nvim",
  opts = {
    templates = {
      substitutions = {
        USERNAME = os.getenv("USERNAME"),
      },
    },
  },
},
```

Now one has to wrap it in a function to get it to work in v3.15.9:
```lua
{
  "obsidian-nvim/obsidian.nvim",
  opts = {
    templates = {
      substitutions = {
        USERNAME = function()
          return os.getenv("USERNAME")
        end,
      },
    },
  },
},
```

NOTE: The error only occurs if substitutions are being made in a template that _includes_ that substitution key (in the above example, `{{USERNAME}}`).

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+-- Test-only MiniTest stdout reporter emitting machine-parseable per-test lines.
+--
+-- After all cases finish, each collected case emits exactly one line at column
+-- zero derived from its real final execution result (`exec.fails`):
+--   Success || <stable unique test name>
+--   Fail    || <stable unique test name>
+--   Skip    || <stable unique test name>
+--
+-- The reporter then quits Neovim with a nonzero exit code whenever any
+-- collected case failed, so the process exit status reflects real outcomes.
+local M = {}
+
+local reporter = function(opts)
+  opts = opts or {}
+  local write = function(text)
+    io.stdout:write(text .. "\n")
+    io.flush()
+  end
+
+  local case_name = function(case)
+    local desc = table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+    if case.args == nil or #case.args == 0 then
+      return desc
+    end
+    return ("%s + args %s"):format(desc, vim.inspect(case.args, { newline = "", indent = "" }))
+  end
+
+  local all_cases
+  local res = {}
+
+  res.start = function(cases)
+    all_cases = cases
+  end
+
+  -- Intentionally a no-op: MiniTest calls `update` once per execution step
+  -- (hooks, retries, etc.), so per-case lines are emitted once in `finish`.
+  res.update = function(_) end
+
+  res.finish = function()
+    local has_fails = false
+    for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+      local exec = case.exec
+      local status
+      if exec == nil then
+        status = "Skip"
+      elseif #exec.fails > 0 then
+        status = "Fail"
+        has_fails = true
+      else
+        status = "Success"
+      end
+      write(("%s || %s"):format(status, case_name(case)))
+    end
+    vim.cmd(("silent! %scquit"):format(has_fails and 1 or 0))
+  end
+
+  return res
+end
+
+---Run a single test file with the per-test stdout reporter.
+---@param file string Path to test file relative to the current directory.
+M.run_file = function(file)
+  MiniTest.run_file(file, { execute = { reporter = reporter() } })
+end
+
+return M

problem_statement:
tracking: date parsing and picking
### ð The feature, motivation and pitch

Sometimes I want to create notes for previous days and its tedious to calculate how many days its been since today. I'd like a command like `:Obsidian today 2-13` or `2-13-2025` for instance, to make notes on specific days.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

`:Obsidian today` accepts an optional argument describing which daily note to
open. In addition to the existing behavior, the argument may be a specific
calendar date:

- `:Obsidian today` with no argument opens (creating it if necessary) the
  daily note for today.
- An argument that is a plain integer is a day offset relative to today,
  exactly as before: `1` opens tomorrow's daily note, `-1` opens
  yesterday's daily note, and other positive or negative integers shift by
  exactly that many days.
- A date argument of the form `M-D` (month and day of month, separated by a
  dash, for example `:Obsidian today 2-13`) opens the daily note for that
  calendar date in the current year.
- An argument that is neither a valid day offset nor one of the supported
  date forms is rejected: no daily note is opened or created for it.
- Day offsets are exact: whenever a numeric value is treated as an offset,
  each unit shifts the selected day by exactly one calendar day. For
  non-integer spellings (such as fractional or exponent-notation values) an
  implementation may reject the argument, truncate, or round to the nearest
  whole day, but it must never open a daily note further from today than
  rounding the numeric value up to a whole day would justify.
- The set of supported date orders when an explicit year is given is an
  implementation choice and is intentionally not prescribed here. However,
  any argument containing an explicit four-digit year (such as the
  `2-13-2025` example from the feature request) must be handled
  unambiguously: it must either open the daily note for exactly the stated
  calendar date, or be rejected without opening any daily note. Its year
  component must never be silently dropped so that the daily note for a
  different calendar date is opened instead.
- Likewise, a two-component `M-D` style argument whose components fall
  outside the ordinary calendar ranges (such as an impossible day for the
  given month) must be handled unambiguously: an implementation may reject
  it, or it may normalize it onto the calendar by rolling the overflow
  forward onto the following days, but it must never open a daily note for
  any other date.

+-- moment_lpeg.lua
+local lpeg = vim.lpeg
+
+local P, C, Ct = lpeg.P, lpeg.C, lpeg.Ct
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Locale data (can be swapped later)
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local MONTHS = {
+  "January",
+  "February",
+  "March",
+  "April",
+  "May",
+  "June",
+  "July",
+  "August",
+  "September",
+  "October",
+  "November",
+  "December",
+}
+
+local MONTHS_SHORT = {
+  "Jan",
+  "Feb",
+  "Mar",
+  "Apr",
+  "May",
+  "Jun",
+  "Jul",
+  "Aug",
+  "Sep",
+  "Oct",
+  "Nov",
+  "Dec",
+}
+
+local WEEKDAYS = {
+  "Sunday",
+  "Monday",
+  "Tuesday",
+  "Wednesday",
+  "Thursday",
+  "Friday",
+  "Saturday",
+}
+
+local WEEKDAYS_SHORT = {
+  "Sun",
+  "Mon",
+  "Tue",
+  "Wed",
+  "Thu",
+  "Fri",
+  "Sat",
+}
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Token handlers
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local handlers = {}
+
+local function ordinal_suffix(n)
+  local mod100 = n % 100
+  if mod100 >= 11 and mod100 <= 13 then
+    return "th"
+  end
+  local mod10 = n % 10
+  if mod10 == 1 then
+    return "st"
+  elseif mod10 == 2 then
+    return "nd"
+  elseif mod10 == 3 then
+    return "rd"
+  end
+  return "th"
+end
+
+local function iso_weekday(wday)
+  return ((wday + 5) % 7) + 1
+end
+
+local function week_of_year(date)
+  local jan1 = os.date("*t", os.time { year = date.year, month = 1, day = 1 })
+  return math.floor((date.yday + (jan1.wday - 1) - 1) / 7) + 1
+end
+
+local function iso_week(date, time)
+  local wday = iso_weekday(date.wday)
+  local thursday = time + (4 - wday) * 86400
+  local thursday_date = os.date("*t", thursday)
+  return math.floor((thursday_date.yday - 1) / 7) + 1
+end
+
+local function iso_week_year(date, time)
+  local wday = iso_weekday(date.wday)
+  local thursday = time + (4 - wday) * 86400
+  return os.date("*t", thursday).year
+end
+
+handlers["YYYY"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%04d", d.year)
+end
+handlers["YY"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.year % 100)
+end
+
+handlers["MMMM"] = function(d)
+  return MONTHS[d.month]
+end
+handlers["MMM"] = function(d)
+  return MONTHS_SHORT[d.month]
+end
+handlers["MM"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.month)
+end
+handlers["M"] = function(d)
+  return d.month
+end
+
+handlers["DD"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.day)
+end
+handlers["D"] = function(d)
+  return d.day
+end
+handlers["Do"] = function(d)
+  return tostring(d.day) .. ordinal_suffix(d.day)
+end
+handlers["DDD"] = function(d)
+  return d.yday
+end
+handlers["DDDD"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%03d", d.yday)
+end
+
+handlers["HH"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.hour)
+end
+handlers["H"] = function(d)
+  return d.hour
+end
+
+handlers["hh"] = function(d)
+  local h = d.hour % 12
+  if h == 0 then
+    h = 12
+  end
+  return string.format("%02d", h)
+end
+
+handlers["h"] = function(d)
+  local h = d.hour % 12
+  if h == 0 then
+    h = 12
+  end
+  return h
+end
+
+handlers["mm"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.min)
+end
+handlers["m"] = function(d)
+  return d.min
+end
+
+handlers["ss"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", d.sec)
+end
+handlers["s"] = function(d)
+  return d.sec
+end
+
+handlers["A"] = function(d)
+  return d.hour < 12 and "AM" or "PM"
+end
+handlers["a"] = function(d)
+  return d.hour < 12 and "am" or "pm"
+end
+
+handlers["dddd"] = function(d)
+  return WEEKDAYS[d.wday]
+end
+handlers["ddd"] = function(d)
+  return WEEKDAYS_SHORT[d.wday]
+end
+handlers["dd"] = function(d)
+  return string.sub(WEEKDAYS_SHORT[d.wday], 1, 2)
+end
+handlers["d"] = function(d)
+  return d.wday - 1
+end
+handlers["E"] = function(d)
+  return iso_weekday(d.wday)
+end
+handlers["w"] = function(d)
+  return week_of_year(d)
+end
+handlers["ww"] = function(d)
+  return string.format("%02d", week_of_year(d))
+end
+handlers["W"] = function(d, time)
+  return iso_week(d, time)
+end
+handlers["WW"] = function(d, time)
+  return string.format("%02d", iso_week(d, time))
+end
+handlers["Q"] = function(d)
+  return math.floor((d.month - 1) / 3) + 1
+end
+handlers["Qo"] = function(d)
+  local q = math.floor((d.month - 1) / 3) + 1
+  return tostring(q) .. ordinal_suffix(q)
+end
+handlers["Wo"] = function(d, time)
+  local w = iso_week(d, time)
+  return tostring(w) .. ordinal_suffix(w)
+end
+handlers["GGGG"] = function(d, time)
+  return string.format("%04d", iso_week_year(d, time))
+end
+handlers["GG"] = function(d, time)
+  return string.format("%02d", iso_week_year(d, time) % 100)
+end
+handlers["Z"] = function(_, time)
+  local offset = os.date("%z", time)
+  return string.sub(offset, 1, 3) .. ":" .. string.sub(offset, 4, 5)
+end
+handlers["ZZ"] = function(_, time)
+  return os.date("%z", time)
+end
+handlers["X"] = function(_, time)
+  return math.floor(time)
+end
+handlers["x"] = function(_, time)
+  return math.floor(time * 1000)
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- LPeg grammar
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function token(name)
+  return P(name) / function()
+    return { type = "token", value = name }
+  end
+end
+
+-- Order matters (longest first!)
+local token_pattern = token "YYYY"
+  + token "GGGG"
+  + token "MMMM"
+  + token "dddd"
+  + token "DDDD"
+  + token "MMM"
+  + token "ddd"
+  + token "DDD"
+  + token "GG"
+  + token "YY"
+  + token "MM"
+  + token "DD"
+  + token "Do"
+  + token "HH"
+  + token "hh"
+  + token "ZZ"
+  + token "Qo"
+  + token "Wo"
+  + token "WW"
+  + token "ww"
+  + token "mm"
+  + token "ss"
+  + token "dd"
+  + token "M"
+  + token "D"
+  + token "H"
+  + token "h"
+  + token "m"
+  + token "s"
+  + token "Z"
+  + token "W"
+  + token "w"
+  + token "A"
+  + token "a"
+  + token "d"
+  + token "E"
+  + token "Q"
+  + token "X"
+  + token "x"
+  -- localized
+  + token "LLLL"
+  + token "LLL"
+  + token "LL"
+  + token "LTS"
+  + token "LT"
+  + token "L"
+
+---@diagnostic disable-next-line: param-type-mismatch
+local literal = P "[" * C((1 - P "]") ^ 0) * P "]" / function(s)
+  return { type = "literal", value = s }
+end
+
+-- Any other character
+local text = C(1) / function(s)
+  return { type = "text", value = s }
+end
+
+local grammar = Ct((literal + token_pattern + text) ^ 0)
+
+local LONG_DATE_FORMAT = {
+  L = "MM/DD/YYYY",
+  LL = "MMMM D, YYYY",
+  LLL = "MMMM D, YYYY h:mm A",
+  LLLL = "dddd, MMMM D, YYYY h:mm A",
+  LT = "h:mm A",
+  LTS = "h:mm:ss A",
+}
+
+local function expand_localized(ast)
+  local out = {}
+
+  for _, node in ipairs(ast) do
+    if node.type == "token" and LONG_DATE_FORMAT[node.value] then
+      -- Parse the expanded format recursively
+      local expanded = grammar:match(LONG_DATE_FORMAT[node.value])
+      for _, e in ipairs(expanded) do
+        out[#out + 1] = e
+      end
+    else
+      out[#out + 1] = node
+    end
+  end
+
+  return out
+end
+
+---@param time number
+---@param fmt string
+---@returns string
+return function(time, fmt)
+  local date = os.date("*t", time)
+  local ast = grammar:match(fmt)
+
+  ast = expand_localized(ast)
+
+  local out = {}
+
+  for _, node in ipairs(ast) do
+    if node.type == "token" then
+      out[#out + 1] = tostring(handlers[node.value](date, time))
+    else
+      out[#out + 1] = node.value
+    end
+  end
+
+  return table.concat(out)
+end
