+  [8] = "Aug",
+  [9] = "Sep",
+  [10] = "Oct",
+  [11] = "Nov",
+  [12] = "Dec",
+}
+
+local MONTH_NAME_TO_NUM = {}
+for num, name in pairs(MONTHS) do
+  MONTH_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()] = num
+end
+for num, name in pairs(MONTHS_SHORT) do
+  MONTH_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()] = num
+end
+
+local WEEKDAYS = {
+  [1] = "Sunday",
+  [2] = "Monday",
+  [3] = "Tuesday",
+  [4] = "Wednesday",
+  [5] = "Thursday",
+  [6] = "Friday",
+  [7] = "Saturday",
+}
+
+local WEEKDAYS_SHORT = {
+  [1] = "Sun",
+  [2] = "Mon",
+  [3] = "Tue",
+  [4] = "Wed",
+  [5] = "Thu",
+  [6] = "Fri",
+  [7] = "Sat",
+}
+
+local WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_NUM = {}
+for num, name in pairs(WEEKDAYS) do
+  WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()] = num
+end
+for num, name in pairs(WEEKDAYS_SHORT) do
+  WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()] = num
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Case-insensitive pattern builder
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function case_insensitive(str)
+  local pattern = P ""
+  for i = 1, #str do
+    local c = str:sub(i, i)
+    local lower = c:lower()
+    local upper = c:upper()
+    if lower == upper then
+      pattern = pattern * P(c)
+    else
+      pattern = pattern * (P(lower) + P(upper))
+    end
+  end
+  return pattern
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Ordinal suffix patterns (Do, Qo, Wo)
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function ordinal_pattern()
+  local digit = R "09"
+  local number = C(digit ^ 1)
+  local suffix = case_insensitive "st" + case_insensitive "nd" + case_insensitive "rd" + case_insensitive "th"
+  return number * suffix / function(n)
+    return tonumber(n)
+  end
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Month name patterns
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function build_month_pattern(long_names, short_names)
+  local pattern = P(false)
+
+  -- Add long names first (longest match first)
+  for _, name in ipairs(long_names) do
+    pattern = pattern + case_insensitive(name) * Cc(MONTH_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()])
+  end
+
+  -- Then short names
+  for _, name in ipairs(short_names) do
+    pattern = pattern + case_insensitive(name) * Cc(MONTH_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()])
+  end
+
+  return pattern
+end
+
+local month_name_pattern = build_month_pattern(MONTHS, MONTHS_SHORT)
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Weekday name patterns
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function build_weekday_pattern(long_names, short_names)
+  local pattern = P(false)
+
+  -- Add long names first
+  for _, name in ipairs(long_names) do
+    pattern = pattern + case_insensitive(name) * Cc(WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()])
+  end
+
+  -- Then short names
+  for _, name in ipairs(short_names) do
+    pattern = pattern + case_insensitive(name) * Cc(WEEKDAY_NAME_TO_NUM[name:lower()])
+  end
+
+  return pattern
+end
+
+local weekday_pattern = build_weekday_pattern(WEEKDAYS, WEEKDAYS_SHORT)
+local weekday_short_2char_pattern = case_insensitive "Su"
+  + case_insensitive "Mo"
+  + case_insensitive "Tu"
+  + case_insensitive "We"
+  + case_insensitive "Th"
+  + case_insensitive "Fr"
+  + case_insensitive "Sa"
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Year pivot for YY format (moment.js uses Â±68 years)
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local CURRENT_YEAR = tonumber(os.date "%Y")
+local YEAR_PIVOT = 68
+
+local function parse_two_digit_year(yy_str)
+  local yy = tonumber(yy_str)
+  local current_year_last_two = CURRENT_YEAR % 100
+  local century = math.floor(CURRENT_YEAR / 100)
+
+  -- Standard pivot logic:
+  -- If yy is far in the future (> current + pivot), it's from previous century
+  -- If yy is far in the past (< current - pivot), it's from next century
+  -- Otherwise, it's from current century
+  if yy > current_year_last_two + YEAR_PIVOT then
+    -- e.g., current is 24, yy is 95, pivot is 68
+    -- 95 > 24 + 68 = 92, so 95 is from 1995 (previous century)
+    return (century - 1) * 100 + yy
+  elseif yy < current_year_last_two - YEAR_PIVOT then
+    -- e.g., current is 24, yy is 05, pivot is 68
+    -- 05 < 24 - 68 = -44, so 05 is from 2105 (next century)
+    -- But wait, that doesn't make sense for 1980...
+    -- Actually, this case won't trigger for 1980
+    return (century + 1) * 100 + yy
+  else
+    return century * 100 + yy
+  end
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Token pattern builders
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local token_patterns = {}
+
+-- Year patterns
+token_patterns["YYYY"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 4) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["YY"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / parse_two_digit_year
+end
+
+-- Month patterns
+token_patterns["MMMM"] = function()
+  return month_name_pattern
+end
+
+token_patterns["MMM"] = function()
+  return month_name_pattern
+end
+
+token_patterns["MM"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["M"] = function()
+  -- Match 1-9 or 10-12, preferring 2 digits
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- Day patterns
+token_patterns["DD"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["D"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["Do"] = function()
+  return ordinal_pattern()
+end
+
+token_patterns["DDD"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 3) + C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["DDDD"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 3) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- Hour patterns (24-hour)
+token_patterns["HH"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["H"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- Hour patterns (12-hour)
+token_patterns["hh"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["h"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- Minute patterns
+token_patterns["mm"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["m"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- Second patterns
+token_patterns["ss"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["s"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+-- AM/PM patterns
+token_patterns["A"] = function()
+  return (case_insensitive "AM" + case_insensitive "PM") / function(ampm)
+    return ampm:lower() == "am"
+  end
+end
+
+token_patterns["a"] = function()
+  return (case_insensitive "am" + case_insensitive "pm") / function(ampm)
+    return ampm:lower() == "am"
+  end
+end
+
+-- Weekday patterns
+token_patterns["dddd"] = function()
+  return weekday_pattern
+end
+
+token_patterns["ddd"] = function()
+  return weekday_pattern
+end
+
+token_patterns["dd"] = function()
+  -- 2-character weekday
+  return weekday_short_2char_pattern
+    / function(wd)
+      local map = { su = 1, mo = 2, tu = 3, we = 4, th = 5, fr = 6, sa = 7 }
+      return map[wd:lower()]
+    end
+end
+
+token_patterns["d"] = function()
+  return C(R "06") / function(n)
+    return tonumber(n) + 1
+  end -- 0-6 to 1-7
+end
+
+token_patterns["E"] = function()
+  return C(R "17") / tonumber -- ISO weekday 1-7
+end
+
+-- Week of year
+token_patterns["w"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["ww"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["W"] = function()
+  return (C(R "09" ^ 2) + C(R "09")) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["WW"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["Wo"] = function()
+  return ordinal_pattern()
+end
+
+-- Quarter
+token_patterns["Q"] = function()
+  return C(R "14") / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["Qo"] = function()
+  return ordinal_pattern()
+end
+
+-- ISO week year
+token_patterns["GGGG"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 4) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["GG"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 2) / parse_two_digit_year
+end
+
+-- Timezone patterns
+token_patterns["Z"] = function()
+  -- Format: +05:00, -08:00, or Z (UTC)
+  local sign = S "+-"
+  local hours = R "09" ^ 2
+  local minutes = R "09" ^ 2
+  local offset_pattern = C(sign * hours * P ":" * minutes)
+    / function(tz)
+      local offset_sign = tz:sub(1, 1) == "+" and 1 or -1
+      local offset_hours = tonumber(tz:sub(2, 3))
+      local offset_mins = tonumber(tz:sub(5, 6))
+      return offset_sign * (offset_hours * 60 + offset_mins) * 60
+    end
+  local utc_pattern = case_insensitive "Z" * Cc(0) -- UTC is 0 offset
+  return offset_pattern + utc_pattern
+end
+
+token_patterns["ZZ"] = function()
+  -- Format: +0500, -0800, or Z (UTC)
+  local sign = S "+-"
+  local digits = R "09" ^ 4
+  local offset_pattern = C(sign * digits)
+    / function(tz)
+      local offset_sign = tz:sub(1, 1) == "+" and 1 or -1
+      local offset_hours = tonumber(tz:sub(2, 3))
+      local offset_mins = tonumber(tz:sub(4, 5))
+      return offset_sign * (offset_hours * 60 + offset_mins) * 60
+    end
+  local utc_pattern = case_insensitive "Z" * Cc(0) -- UTC is 0 offset
+  return offset_pattern + utc_pattern
+end
+
+-- Unix timestamps
+token_patterns["X"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 1) / tonumber
+end
+
+token_patterns["x"] = function()
+  return C(R "09" ^ 1) / function(n)
+    return math.floor(tonumber(n) / 1000)
+  end
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Build parser from format string
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+local function token(name)
+  return P(name) / function()
+    return { type = "token", value = name }
+  end
+end
+
+-- Same token pattern as moment.lua
+-- Order matters: longer tokens first, then shorter ones
+local token_pattern = token "YYYY"
+  + token "GGGG"
+  + token "MMMM"
+  + token "dddd"
+  + token "DDDD"
+  + token "LLLL"
+  + token "MMM"
+  + token "ddd"
+  + token "DDD"
+  + token "LTS"
+  + token "LLL"
+  + token "GG"
+  + token "YY"
+  + token "MM"
+  + token "DD"
+  + token "Do"
+  + token "HH"
+  + token "hh"
+  + token "ZZ"
+  + token "Qo"
+  + token "Wo"
+  + token "WW"
+  + token "ww"
+  + token "mm"
+  + token "ss"
+  + token "dd"
+  + token "LL"
+  + token "LT"
+  + token "M"
+  + token "D"
+  + token "H"
+  + token "h"
+  + token "m"
+  + token "s"
+  + token "Z"
+  + token "W"
+  + token "w"
+  + token "A"
+  + token "a"
+  + token "d"
+  + token "E"
+  + token "Q"
+  + token "X"
+  + token "x"
+  + token "L"
+
+local literal = P "[" * C((1 - P "]") ^ 0) * P "]" / function(s)
+  return { type = "literal", value = s }
+end
+
+local text = C(1) / function(s)
+  return { type = "text", value = s }
+end
+
+local format_grammar = Ct((literal + token_pattern + text) ^ 0)
+
+local LONG_DATE_FORMAT = {
+  L = "MM/DD/YYYY",
+  LL = "MMMM D, YYYY",
+  LLL = "MMMM D, YYYY h:mm A",
+  LLLL = "dddd, MMMM D, YYYY h:mm A",
+  LT = "h:mm A",
+  LTS = "h:mm:ss A",
+}
+
+local function expand_localized(ast)
+  local out = {}
+
+  for _, node in ipairs(ast) do
+    if node.type == "token" and LONG_DATE_FORMAT[node.value] then
+      local expanded = format_grammar:match(LONG_DATE_FORMAT[node.value])
+      for _, e in ipairs(expanded) do
+        out[#out + 1] = e
+      end
+    else
+      out[#out + 1] = node
+    end
+  end
+
+  return out
+end
+
+----------------------------------------------------
+-- Build the parsing grammar
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+-- Default values for unspecified fields
+---@type osdateparam
+local DEFAULTS = {
+  year = CURRENT_YEAR,
+  month = 1,
+  day = 1,
+  hour = 0,
+  min = 0,
+  sec = 0,
+  isdst = false,
+}
+
+---@param input string
+---@param fmt string
+---@return osdateparam|nil, string|nil
+return function(input, fmt)
+  if not input or input == "" then
+    return nil, "Empty input"
+  end
+  if not fmt or fmt == "" then
+    return nil, "Empty format"
+  end
+
+  -- Parse format string into AST
+  local ast = format_grammar:match(fmt)
+  if not ast then
+    return nil, "Invalid format string"
+  end
+
+  -- Expand localized formats
+  ast = expand_localized(ast)
+
+  -- Build parsing patterns
+  local patterns = {}
+
+  for _, node in ipairs(ast) do
+    if node.type == "token" then
+      local pattern_builder = token_patterns[node.value]
+      if pattern_builder then
+        -- Wrap pattern to capture with token name
+        local wrapped = pattern_builder() / function(v)
+          return { token = node.value, value = v }
+        end
+        patterns[#patterns + 1] = wrapped
+      else
+        return nil, "Unknown token: " .. node.value
+      end
+    elseif node.type == "literal" then
+      -- Escape special LPeg characters in literals
+      local escaped = node.value:gsub("([%.%+%-%*%?%[%]%^%$%(%)%%])", "%%%1")
+      patterns[#patterns + 1] = P(escaped)
+    elseif node.type == "text" then
+      patterns[#patterns + 1] = P(node.value)
+    end
+  end
+
+  if #patterns == 0 then
+    return nil, "No patterns built"
+  end
+
+  -- Combine all patterns
+  local parser = P ""
+  for _, p in ipairs(patterns) do
+    parser = parser * p
+  end
+  parser = parser * P(-1) -- Ensure full match
+  parser = Ct(parser) -- Capture all results as a table
+
+  -- Parse input
+  local results = parser:match(input)
+
+  if not results or #results == 0 then
+    return nil, "Parse failed"
+  end
+
+  -- Extract values from captures
+  local date_fields = {}
+  local has_am_pm = nil
+  local hour_12 = nil
+  local timezone_offset = nil
+  local unix_timestamp = nil
+
+  for _, result in ipairs(results) do
+    if type(result) == "table" and result.token then
+      local token_name = result.token
+      local value = result.value
+
+      -- Map tokens to date fields
+      if token_name == "YYYY" or token_name == "GGGG" or token_name == "YY" or token_name == "GG" then
+        date_fields.year = value
+      elseif token_name == "MMMM" or token_name == "MMM" or token_name == "MM" or token_name == "M" then
+        date_fields.month = value
+      elseif token_name == "DD" or token_name == "D" or token_name == "Do" then
+        date_fields.day = value
+      elseif token_name == "HH" or token_name == "H" then
+        date_fields.hour = value
+        hour_12 = false
+      elseif token_name == "hh" or token_name == "h" then
+        hour_12 = value
+      elseif token_name == "mm" or token_name == "m" then
+        date_fields.min = value
+      elseif token_name == "ss" or token_name == "s" then
+        date_fields.sec = value
+      elseif token_name == "A" or token_name == "a" then
+        has_am_pm = value -- true for AM, false for PM
+      elseif token_name == "d" or token_name == "E" then
+        date_fields.wday = value
+      elseif token_name == "Q" or token_name == "Qo" then
+        -- Quarter: 1-4 -> convert to month (1, 4, 7, 10)
+        local quarter = value
+        date_fields.month = (quarter - 1) * 3 + 1
+      elseif token_name == "Z" or token_name == "ZZ" then
+        timezone_offset = value
+      elseif token_name == "X" or token_name == "x" then
+        unix_timestamp = value
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+  -- Handle 12-hour format conversion
+  if hour_12 then
+    if has_am_pm == false then -- PM
+      date_fields.hour = (hour_12 % 12) + 12
+    else -- AM or unspecified
+      date_fields.hour = hour_12 % 12
+    end
+  end
+
+  -- Handle Unix timestamp (overrides everything else)
+  if unix_timestamp then
+    local date = os.date("*t", unix_timestamp)
+    if timezone_offset then
+      date.hour = date.hour + math.floor(timezone_offset / 3600)
+    end
+    return date
+  end
+
+  -- Apply defaults
+  for field, default in pairs(DEFAULTS) do
+    if date_fields[field] == nil then
+      date_fields[field] = default
+    end
+  end
+
+  -- Validate date
+  local time = os.time(date_fields)
+  if not time then
+    return nil, "Invalid date"
+  end
+
+  -- Convert to table
+  local result = os.date("*t", time)
+
+  -- Apply timezone offset if provided
+  if timezone_offset then
+    result.hour = result.hour - math.floor(timezone_offset / 3600)
+  end
+
+  return result
+end

diff --git a/scripts/run_tests.lua b/scripts/run_tests.lua
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0c54822
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/run_tests.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+-- Test runner for the obsidian.nvim MiniTest suite.
+--
+-- Runs a fixed list of test files with MiniTest and reports one
+-- machine-readable line per executed test case on stdout in the form:
+--   Success || <test name>
+--   Fail || <test name>
+--   Skip || <test name>
+--
+-- The process exits with status 0 when every test passes and 1 otherwise.
+--
+-- Usage (from the repository root):
+--   nvim --headless --noplugin -l scripts/run_tests.lua [tests/file.lua ...]
+
+-- Pin the timezone so that date assertions are deterministic.
+vim.env.TZ = "UTC"
+
+-- Make the plugin and the MiniTest dependency available.
+vim.opt.rtp:append(vim.uv.cwd())
+vim.opt.rtp:append("deps/mini.test")
+
+local MiniTest = require("mini.test")
+
+-- Restrict collection to real test files under 'tests/' so that helper or
+-- runner scripts (such as this one) are never collected.
+MiniTest.setup {
+  collect = {
+    find_files = function()
+      return vim.fn.globpath("tests", "**/test_*.lua", true, true)
+    end,
+  },
+}
+
+-- Target test files: extra command line arguments, or the default
+-- daily-note command set. `_G.arg` under `-l` holds the script path and any
+-- arguments, so keep only existing files.
+local files = {}
+for _, a in ipairs(_G.arg or {}) do
+  if vim.fn.filereadable(a) == 1 then
+    table.insert(files, a)
+  end
+end
+if #files == 0 then
+  files = {
+    "tests/test_today.lua",
+    "tests/test_daily.lua",
+  }
+end
+
+local cases = MiniTest.collect({
+  find_files = function()
+    return files
+  end,
+  emulate_busted = true,
+})
+
+local reporter = {}
+
+function reporter.start(_) end
+
+function reporter.update(_) end
+
+function reporter.finish()
+  local n_fail = 0
+  -- Print each per-test line with a leading newline so that it always starts
+  -- on a fresh line and is never glued to incidental plugin output.
+  for _, case in ipairs(MiniTest.current.all_cases or {}) do
+    local name = table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+    local n_fails = case.exec and #case.exec.fails or 0
+    local n_notes = case.exec and #case.exec.notes or 0
+    local status
+    if n_fails > 0 then
+      status = "Fail"
+      n_fail = n_fail + 1
+    elseif n_notes > 0 then
+      status = "Skip"
+    else
+      status = "Success"
+    end
+    io.stdout:write("\n" .. status .. " || " .. name)
+  end
+  io.stdout:write("\n")
+  io.stdout:flush()
+  vim.cmd("silent! " .. (n_fail > 0 and 1 or 0) .. "cquit")
+end
+
+MiniTest.execute(cases, { reporter = reporter })

+--- Run the `today` command handler with the given argument string and return
+--- the path of the daily note buffer it opened, or nil if none was opened.
+---@param args string
+---@return string|?
+local function today_opened_path(args)
+  local cmd = require "obsidian.commands.today"
+  local name_before = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
+
+  local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
+  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_name(bufnr, tostring(Obsidian.dir / ".today-cmd-placeholder"))
+  vim.api.nvim_set_current_buf(bufnr)
+
+  local ok, err = pcall(cmd, {
+    args = args,
+    fargs = args ~= "" and { args } or {},
+    bang = false,
+    line1 = 0,
+    line2 = 0,
+    range = 0,
+    count = -1,
+    reg = "",
+    mods = "",
+    smods = {},
+    name = "today",
+  })
+
+  -- Opening a note is scheduled asynchronously by the command, so flush
+  -- pending scheduled callbacks before checking the current buffer.
+  vim.wait(500, function()
+    return false
+  end, 10)
+
+  local opened = nil
+  if ok then
+    local name_after = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
+    if name_after ~= name_before and name_after:match("%.md$") then
+      opened = name_after
+    end
+  end
+
+  pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_delete, bufnr, { force = true })
+  return opened, err
+end
+
+local T = new_set {
+  hooks = {
+    pre_case = function()
+      h.setup_vault()
+    end,
+    post_case = function()
+      h.teardown_vault()
+    end,
+  },
+}
+
+T["no argument opens the daily note for today"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path ""
+  local expected_id = os.date "%Y-%m-%d"
+  eq(nil ~= opened and vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md") or false, true)
+end
+
+T["positive integer offset opens the daily note for tomorrow"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "1"
+  local expected_id = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time() + 24 * 3600)
+  eq(nil ~= opened and vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md") or false, true)
+end
+
+T["negative integer offset opens the daily note for yesterday"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "-1"
+  local expected_id = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time() - 24 * 3600)
+  eq(nil ~= opened and vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md") or false, true)
+end
+
+T["month-day date opens daily note for that date in the current year"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "2-13"
+  local expected_id = os.date "%Y" .. "-02-13"
+  eq(nil ~= opened and vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md") or false, true)
+end
+
+-- An explicit-year date such as the `2-13-2025` example from the feature
+-- request may be resolved to that calendar date or rejected as unsupported,
+-- but its year component must never be silently dropped such that a note for
+-- a different calendar date is opened.
+T["month-day-year date never opens a note for a different date"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "2-13-2025"
+  eq(opened == nil or vim.endswith(opened, "2025-02-13.md"), true)
+end
+
+T["invalid argument does not open a daily note"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "banana"
+  eq(opened, nil)
+end
+
+-- Fractional and exponent-notation spellings are not plain integer offsets.
+-- If they are accepted as numeric offsets at all, they must agree with a
+-- nearest whole-day interpretation, and if a numeric value is accepted, each
+-- unit must shift by exactly one day. In particular, a fractional spelling
+-- must never open a daily note further ahead than rounding up to the next
+-- whole day would justify, and an exponent-notation spelling must either be
+-- rejected or resolve to exactly that many days in the future.
+T["fractional offset never opens a note further ahead than the next whole day up"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "1.5"
+  local tomorrow = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time() + 24 * 3600)
+  local day_after = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time() + 2 * 24 * 3600)
+  eq(opened == nil or vim.endswith(opened, tomorrow .. ".md") or vim.endswith(opened, day_after .. ".md"), true)
+end
+
+T["exponent-notation offset never opens a note for a different date than a thousand days ahead"] = function()
+  local opened = today_opened_path "1e3"
+  local expected_id = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time() + 1000 * 24 * 3600)
+  eq(opened == nil or vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md"), true)
+end
+

+-- the calendar by rolling the overflow forward, but it must never open a
+-- daily note for any other date than its exact forward-rolled calendar
+-- date.

+  -- current year via `os.time` calendar normalization (this is March 2 in
+  -- a common year and March 1 in a leap year).
+  local expected_id = os.date("%Y-%m-%d", os.time { year = tonumber(os.date "%Y"), month = 2, day = 30, hour = 12 })
+  eq(opened == nil or vim.endswith(opened, expected_id .. ".md"), true)
+end

problem_statement:
frontmatter property "links" should wrap wikilinks in quotes
### ð The feature, motivation and pitch

Hi there,
in obsidian you are able to add wikilinks as values inside the "links" property, which looks like this:

```
---
links:
  - "[[someNote]]"
---
```

is there a way to use the autocompletion use of [[ to add links to "links"?
when saving the note,  note_frontmatter_func does not wrap the links in quotes, which is not readable by obsidian.

so writing a "links" value with [[someNote]] should wrap the wikilink automatically to "[[someNote]]"

Thanks for your time!

### Additional contract requirements

When a wikilink (for example `[[someNote]]`) is used as a value of the frontmatter `links` property, saving the note's frontmatter must wrap the wikilink in double quotes so it stays valid, Obsidian-readable YAML, whether the property holds a single link or a list of links. After saving, re-reading the note's frontmatter must yield each `links` wikilink intact as a plain string value, so a link written with the unquoted `[[...]]` wikilink syntax (as produced by autocompletion) is read back as text rather than being misparsed, and the property round-trips losslessly through saving and re-reading.

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+-- Test-support reporter for the audit harness.
+--
+-- The repository's test runner is `mini.test`. Its default stdout reporter
+-- prints only a compact symbol overview plus summary counters, which the
+-- benchmark's `parse_log_lua_nvim` log parser cannot read. That parser accepts
+-- only real, unindented per-test lines on stdout of the form:
+--
+--   Success || <stable unique test name>
+--   Fail || <stable unique test name>
+--   Skip || <stable unique test name>
+--
+-- This module builds a `mini.test` reporter whose per-case verdicts are
+-- derived from each case's real `exec.fails` / `exec.notes` result (exactly
+-- the same data `mini.test` itself uses to decide pass/fail and its exit
+-- status). It emits one accepted line per executed case at column zero, and
+-- still quits Neovim with a non-zero status when any case fails, so the
+-- command reflects real outcomes and exits non-zero on an asserted failure.
+--
+-- Usage:
+--   nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./scripts/minimal_init.lua \
+--     -c "lua MiniTest.run_file('tests/yaml/test_yaml.lua', { execute = { reporter = require('tests.support.reporter')() } })"
+local M = {}
+
+-- Build a reporter table with `start` / `update` / `finish` callbacks as
+-- expected by `MiniTest.execute`.
+---@param opts table|nil Optional fields:
+---  - <quit_on_finish> (boolean) - whether to quit after finishing, with a
+--    non-zero exit status when any case failed. Default: `true`.
+M.new = function(opts)
+  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", { quit_on_finish = true }, opts or {})
+
+  local write = function(text)
+    io.stdout:write(text)
+    io.flush()
+  end
+
+  -- Mirror mini.test's own per-case verdict logic.
+  local verdict = function(case)
+    if case.exec == nil then
+      return "Fail" -- never executed: treat as a failure
+    end
+    if #case.exec.fails > 0 then
+      return "Fail"
+    end
+    if #case.exec.notes > 0 then
+      return "Skip"
+    end
+    return "Success"
+  end
+
+  -- A stable, unique name for the case from its description path.
+  local name = function(case)
+    return table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+  end
+
+  local all_cases
+
+  local reporter = {}
+
+  reporter.start = function(cases)
+    all_cases = cases
+  end
+
+  reporter.update = function(_case_num) end
+
+  reporter.finish = function()
+    local n_fail = 0
+    for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+      local v = verdict(case)
+      if v == "Fail" then
+        n_fail = n_fail + 1
+      end
+      -- Emit one parser-readable line per case at column zero.
+      write(string.format("%s || %s\n", v, name(case)))
+    end
+
+    if not opts.quit_on_finish then
+      return
+    end
+    local command = string.format("silent! %scquit", n_fail > 0 and 1 or 0)
+    vim.cmd(command)
+  end
+
+  return reporter
+end
+
+-- Convenience call form so the reporter can be passed as
+-- `require("tests.support.reporter")()`.
+return setmetatable(M, {
+  __call = function(_, opts)
+    return M.new(opts)
+  end,
+})

problem_statement:
Handle multiline strings in frontmatter
### ð The feature, motivation and pitch

Currently, there seem to be no handling of multi-line strings in the frontmatter: https://yaml-multiline.info/. Even `\n` cant be used, because the string is coerced to a plain one.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

Multiline strings in frontmatter must be supported.

- Values that span multiple lines can be written in frontmatter using the YAML literal block style, where the key line ends with `|` and each content line is indented more deeply than the key. Each indented content line becomes one line of the resulting string, with the common block indentation removed and the lines joined by "\n".
- Multiline string values must survive being serialized and deserialized again without alteration: loading frontmatter, then dumping it, then loading the result must yield the same string value, including every embedded line break.
- Any valid YAML serialization of a multiline value is acceptable as long as it deserializes back to the identical string; no particular serialized form is required.
- This round-trip guarantee applies equally to multiline values of top-level frontmatter keys, multiline values nested inside mapping values, and multiline values on keys that appear alongside other fields of other types.

- This round-trip guarantee applies equally to multiline values of top-level frontmatter keys, multiline values nested inside mapping values, and multiline values on keys that appear alongside other fields of other types.

problem_statement:
Feature request: Merge template frontmatter with existing note frontmatter
## Feature Request

When inserting a template via `:Obsidian template` into a note that already has frontmatter, the template's frontmatter should be **merged** with the existing frontmatter rather than inserted at the cursor position.

## Current Behavior

If a note already has frontmatter and you insert a template that also contains frontmatter, the template's frontmatter block is inserted at the cursor location, resulting in duplicate/invalid YAML blocks.

## Expected Behavior

The frontmatter from the template should be merged into the existing note's frontmatter:
- New keys from the template are added
- Existing keys in the note are preserved (or optionally overwritten)

## Prior Work

This was addressed in [epwalsh/obsidian.nvim#715](https://github.com/epwalsh/obsidian.nvim/pull/715) but was never merged. [HIDDEN]

## Related Issue

- [epwalsh/obsidian.nvim#714](https://github.com/epwalsh/obsidian.nvim/issues/714) - Original issue describing the problem

### Additional contract requirements

When a template is inserted into a note that already has frontmatter, the template's leading YAML frontmatter is merged into the note's existing frontmatter rather than being inserted as a separate frontmatter block at the cursor position.

Observable behavior:

- After inserting a template whose contents start with a frontmatter block into a note that already has frontmatter, the note buffer still contains exactly one frontmatter block (no duplicate or nested YAML blocks).
- Keys that exist only in the note's original frontmatter are preserved.
- Keys that exist only in the template's frontmatter (including aliases, tags, and arbitrary metadata keys) are added to the note's frontmatter.
- When the same key exists in both the note's and the template's frontmatter, the note's original value remains present in the merged frontmatter after insertion.
- The remainder of the template (everything after its leading frontmatter block) is still inserted into the note at the cursor position, and the note's existing content is preserved.
- Inserting a template that has no frontmatter behaves as an ordinary insertion of the template's text at the cursor position and leaves the note's existing frontmatter unchanged.

No new user-facing interfaces are introduced.

+---Open a vault-relative note in the current buffer and place the cursor on the last line.
+---
+---@param contents string
+---
+---@return integer buf
+---@return integer row The one-indexed cursor row.
+local function open_note_in_vault(contents)
+  local path = Obsidian.dir / "current.md"
+  vim.fn.writefile(vim.split(contents, "\n"), tostring(path))
+  vim.cmd("edit " .. tostring(path))
+  local buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
+  local row = vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf)
+  vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { row, 0 })
+  return buf, row
+end
+
+local function buffer_text(buf)
+  return table.concat(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false), "\n")
+end
+
+---The number of frontmatter blocks in the current buffer.
+---
+---@param buf integer
+---
+---@return integer
+local function count_frontmatter_blocks(buf)
+  local in_frontmatter = false
+  local blocks = 0
+  for _, line in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)) do
+    if M._is_frontmatter_boundary(line) then
+      if in_frontmatter then
+        in_frontmatter = false
+        blocks = blocks + 1
+      else
+        in_frontmatter = true
+      end
+    end
+  end
+  return blocks
+end
+
+T["insert_template"]["should merge template frontmatter into existing note frontmatter"] = function()
+  local note_contents = table.concat({
+    "---",
+    "id: current-note",
+    "foo: bar",
+    "---",
+    "",
+    "# Current Note",
+    "",
+    "First existing body line.",
+    "Last existing body line.",
+  }, "\n")
+
+  write_template("with-frontmatter.md", table.concat({
+    "---",
+    "aliases:",
+    "  - From Template",
+    "tags:",
+    "  - new",
+    "template_key: template_value",
+    "foo: baz",
+    "---",
+    "",
+    "Template body line.",
+  }, "\n"))
+
+  local buf, row = open_note_in_vault(note_contents)
+  local note = M.from_buffer(buf)
+  templates.insert_template {
+    type = "insert_template",
+    template_name = "with-frontmatter",
+    templates_dir = api.templates_dir(),
+    location = { buf, 0, row, 0 },
+    partial_note = note,
+  }
+
+  eq(1, count_frontmatter_blocks(buf), "duplicate frontmatter block must not be inserted")
+  local updated = M.from_buffer(buf)
+  -- New keys from the template are added to the existing frontmatter.
+  eq(true, updated:has_alias "From Template")
+  eq(true, updated:has_tag "new")
+  eq("template_value", updated.metadata.template_key)
+  -- Existing keys in the note are preserved.
+  local foo = updated.metadata.foo
+  local foo_values = type(foo) == "table" and foo or { foo }
+  eq(true, vim.tbl_contains(foo_values, "bar"))
+  -- The template body is inserted at the cursor location and the existing body is preserved.
+  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)
+  local pos_of = {}
+  for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
+    if line == "# Current Note" then
+      pos_of.heading = i
+    elseif line == "First existing body line." then
+      pos_of.first_body = i
+    elseif line == "Template body line." then
+      pos_of.template_body = i
+    elseif line == "Last existing body line." then
+      pos_of.last_body = i
+    end
+  end
+  eq(true, pos_of.heading ~= nil and pos_of.first_body ~= nil and pos_of.template_body ~= nil and pos_of.last_body ~= nil)
+  -- The cursor was placed on the final line of the note's body, so the template body must
+  -- appear between the existing body lines rather than before them or after the last one.
+  eq(true, pos_of.template_body > pos_of.first_body)
+  eq(true, pos_of.template_body < pos_of.last_body)
+end
+
+T["insert_template"]["should insert a template without frontmatter at the cursor"] = function()
+  local note_contents = "---\nid: current-note\ntags:\n  - existing\n---\n\n# Current Note\n"
+  write_template("plain.md", "Plain template line.")
+
+  local buf, row = open_note_in_vault(note_contents)
+  local note = M.from_buffer(buf)
+  templates.insert_template {
+    type = "insert_template",
+    template_name = "plain",
+    templates_dir = api.templates_dir(),
+    location = { buf, 0, row, 0 },
+    partial_note = note,
+  }
+
+  eq(1, count_frontmatter_blocks(buf))
+  local text = buffer_text(buf)
+  eq(true, text:find("# Current Note\nPlain template line.", 1, true) ~= nil)
+  eq("existing", (M.from_buffer(buf)).tags[1])
+end
+
+T["insert_template"]["should insert a template with frontmatter into a note without frontmatter"] = function()
+  write_template("with-frontmatter.md", "---\ntags:\n  - new\nfoo: bar\n---\n\nTemplate body line.")
+
+  local buf, row = open_note_in_vault("# Just a heading\n")
+  local note = M.from_buffer(buf)
+  templates.insert_template {
+    type = "insert_template",
+    template_name = "with-frontmatter",
+    templates_dir = api.templates_dir(),
+    location = { buf, 0, row, 0 },
+    partial_note = note,
+  }
+
+  local text = buffer_text(buf)
+  eq(true, text:find("Template body line.", 1, true) ~= nil)
+  eq(true, text:find("# Just a heading", 1, true) ~= nil)
+end
+
 return T

index 0000000..9c4c3fa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/run_target_tests.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+-- Runner used to execute the target tests for this task in a way that is
+-- parseable by the rebench execution validator.
+--
+-- It runs `tests/test_api.lua` through `mini.test` with a custom reporter
+-- which prints exactly one machine-readable line per executed test case at
+-- column zero on stdout:
+--
+--   Success || <test name>
+--   Fail || <test name>
+--   Skip || <test name>
+--
+-- The status of each line is derived from the case's real execution outcome
+-- (`exec.fails` / `exec.notes`), and the process exits with a nonzero status
+-- when any case fails (via `cquit`), so failure/pass cycles stay truthful.
+-- The same lines are mirrored to `$REBENCH_RESULTS_DIR/rebench-test-results.log`
+-- (default `/tmp/rebench-test-results.log`) as a machine-readable report.
+--
+-- Usage (from the repository root):
+--   nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./scripts/minimal_init.lua -l ./scripts/run_target_tests.lua
+local results_dir = os.getenv "REBENCH_RESULTS_DIR" or "/tmp"
+local log_path = results_dir .. "/rebench-test-results.log"
+local log = assert(io.open(log_path, "w"))
+
+local function emit(line)
+  io.stdout:write(line .. "\n")
+  io.stdout:flush()
+  log:write(line .. "\n")
+  log:flush()
+end
+
+local all_cases = {}
+local done = {}
+
+local function case_status(case)
+  if #case.exec.fails > 0 then
+    return "Fail"
+  end
+  -- A case is skipped when `MiniTest.skip()` aborted its test: the skip
+  -- message lands in `exec.notes` while the test body never ran.
+  if #case.exec.notes > 0 then
+    return "Skip"
+  end
+  return "Success"
+end
+
+local reporter = {
+  start = function(cases)
+    all_cases = cases
+  end,
+  update = function(case_num)
+    -- Report each case exactly once, only after it finished executing
+    -- (i.e. when a subsequent case or the finish step starts).
+    for i = 1, case_num - 1 do
+      local prev = all_cases[i]
+      if prev ~= nil and prev.exec ~= nil and not done[i] then
+        done[i] = true
+        emit(("%s || %s"):format(case_status(prev), table.concat(prev.desc, " | ")))
+      end
+    end
+  end,
+  finish = function()
+    for i, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+      if case.exec ~= nil and not done[i] then
+        done[i] = true
+        emit(("%s || %s"):format(case_status(case), table.concat(case.desc, " | ")))
+      end
+    end
+    log:close()
+    local n_fails, n_total = 0, 0
+    for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+      if case.exec ~= nil then
+        n_total = n_total + 1
+        if #case.exec.fails > 0 then
+          n_fails = n_fails + 1
+        end
+      end
+    end
+    io.stdout:write(("Total: %d, Failed: %d\n"):format(n_total, n_fails))
+    io.stdout:flush()
+    vim.cmd(("silent! %dcquit"):format(n_fails > 0 and 1 or 0))
+  end,
+}
+
+MiniTest.run_file("tests/test_api.lua", { execute = { reporter = reporter } })

problem_statement:
Allow disabling sort-by option to ripgrep
### ð The feature, motivation and pitch

I noticed that `--sortr` (argument given to ripgrep) heavily slows down search. The plugin is essentially unusable in my setup with a 1 TB cloud folder mounted as a virtual filesystem.

[HIDDEN]

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

## Search sorting

The `search.sort_by` configuration option may be set to `false` to disable
ripgrep result sorting. When sorting is disabled, neither a `--sort` nor a
`--sortr` option is included in the generated ripgrep arguments, regardless of
the value of `search.sort_reversed`. Any non-false `sort_by` value retains the
existing sorting behavior.

+[Options](#Options)
+
+## Sort By
+
+`opts.search.sort_by` controls how search results are sorted. Valid values are `"modified"` (default), `"created"`, `"accessed"`, and `"path"`. Set to `false` to disable sorting entirely, which can improve performance in large vaults.
+
+## Sort Reversed
+
+`opts.search.sort_reversed` controls the sort direction. Defaults to `true` (newest/last first). Set to `false` to sort ascending.
+
+## Max Lines
+
+`opts.search.max_lines` limits how many lines of each file ripgrep will search. Defaults to `1000`. Set to `nil` to search entire files.
+
+## Options

+--- MiniTest reporter that emits one machine-parsable line per executed test
+--- case. Each line starts at column zero and has the form
+--- `<Status> || <case desc>`, where `<Status>` is `Success`, `Fail`, or
+--- `Skip` and `<case desc>` is the case description joined by " | ". The
+--- status always reflects the real outcome recorded in `case.exec` by
+--- MiniTest. On finish, the reporter exits Neovim with a nonzero status when
+--- any case failed (mirroring `MiniTest.gen_reporter.stdout`).
+
+local M = {}
+
+---@return table reporter MiniTest reporter with `start`/`update`/`finish`.
+M.make_reporter = function()
+  local all_cases = {}
+
+  local write = function(text)
+    io.stdout:write(text .. "\n")
+    io.flush()
+  end
+
+  local reporter = {}
+
+  reporter.start = function(cases) all_cases = cases end
+
+  reporter.update = function(case_num)
+    local case = all_cases[case_num]
+    if type(case) ~= "table" or type(case.exec) ~= "table" then return end
+
+    -- Only report the final per-case state; ignore intermediate states like
+    -- "Executing test" that are emitted while hooks and retries run.
+    local state = case.exec.state
+    if type(state) ~= "string" or state:find("^Executing") then return end
+
+    local name = table.concat(case.desc, " | ")
+    if state:find("^Pass") then
+      write("Success || " .. name)
+    elseif state:find("^Fail") then
+      write("Fail || " .. name)
+    else
+      write("Skip || " .. name)
+    end
+  end
+
+  reporter.finish = function()
+    local has_fails = false
+    for _, case in ipairs(all_cases) do
+      local exec = case.exec or {}
+      local n_fails = type(exec.fails) == "table" and #exec.fails or 0
+      if n_fails > 0 then
+        has_fails = true
+        break
+      end
+    end
+    vim.cmd(("silent! %scquit"):format(has_fails and 1 or 0))
+  end
+
+  return reporter
+end
+
+return M

### Additional contract requirements

# Unicode & Numeric Tag Support — Public Contract Addendum

## Scope

This work provides general support for Unicode (non-Latin, accented, CJK, and
combining-mark) symbols and for numeric-looking tag names in tag recognition
and tag completion, covering note bodies and YAML frontmatter `tags:` list
entries. No new interfaces are introduced.

## Observable requirements

- **Unicode tags in note text.** A hashtag token whose text contains UTF-8
  characters — for example accented letters (`#café`), CJK text (`#中文`),
  characters written with a decomposed combining-mark sequence (for example
  `e` followed by U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT), or text mixing digits with
  letters or CJK characters (`#2025goals`, `#3d打印`) — is recognized as a tag
  in note bodies. Each recognized tag is reported with its exact 1-based,
  inclusive byte positions (start at the `#`), regardless of the script used.
- **Numeric-looking tag names are completable.** A tag name that consists
  solely of digits (for example `2025`) is a valid tag. When it appears as a
  frontmatter `tags:` entry of a note, it is indexed and offered as a
  completion candidate. While completing, the in-progress `#<digits>` token
  the user is typing is treated as a (possibly incomplete) tag, so typing a
  prefix such as `#202` offers matching indexed tags like `#2025` or
  `#2025goals`.
- **Body completion for Unicode and numeric triggers.** When the cursor
  directly follows an in-progress `#…` token containing non-Latin UTF-8
  characters and/or digits in a note body, the completion list includes
  matching tags found anywhere in the vault — whether they were indexed from
  other notes' bodies or from their frontmatter `tags:` entries — and the
  completion item's new text is the full `#`-prefixed tag text.
- **Frontmatter `tags:` completion.** Inside a frontmatter `tags:` list item
  (`  - <prefix>`), in-progress entries (ASCII, Unicode, numeric, or written
  with decomposed combining marks) are completable without typing `#`, and
  the completion item's new text is the bare tag without a `#` prefix.
- **Completion edit ranges.** A completion item's edit range starts at the
  `#` of the in-progress tag (byte index 0 after `#` at the start of a line)
  or immediately after the `- ` marker of a frontmatter list item, and it
  ends at the cursor, so accepting the item replaces exactly the in-progress
  text with the new text.
- **Positions are byte offsets.** Completion requests and tag positions use
  UTF-8 byte offsets into the line, not display columns or character counts.
- **Completions come from the vault index.** Completion candidates derive
  from tags observed across the vault's notes (note bodies and frontmatter
  `tags:` entries); the completion layer does not invent tags.

## Compatibility boundaries

- Existing behavior for ASCII tags, frontmatter tag completion, and wiki-link
  completion is unchanged. In particular, the tag positions reported for
  existing ASCII tag occurrences are the same 1-based, inclusive byte bounds
  as before.
- Previously established exclusions from tag recognition remain excluded:
  escaped `\#`/HTML-escaped occurrences, hashtags inside HTML comments,
  hex-color codes, Markdown anchor links, URL fragments, parenthesized link
  fragments, and hashtags not preceded by whitespace or the start of the
  line.
- A complete, numeric-only hashtag token that appears alone in running note
  text (for example `notes about #2025`, as with issue or ID references) is
  still not indexed as a tag; the completion of numeric tag names is driven
  by the in-progress token being typed and/or by frontmatter `tags:` entries,
  as described above.
- A hashtag whose name mixes digits with letters or other non-digit
  characters (for example `#2025goals`) is an ordinary tag and is recognized
  wherever it appears in note text.

diff --git a/tests/minitest_reporter.lua b/tests/minitest_reporter.lua
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cb71527
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/minitest_reporter.lua
@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+-- Custom MiniTest reporter that emits one machine-readable, parser-friendly
+-- line per collected test case, derived from each case's real execution result
+-- (`case.exec.fails` / `case.exec.notes`). Lines are written unindented to
+-- stdout in the form:
+--   Success || <file> | <case name>
+--   Fail    || <file> | <case name>
+--   Skip    || <file> | <case name>
+-- The reporter exits nonzero (via cquit) when any case fails.
+local M = {}
+
+---@return table MiniTest reporter with start/update/finish
+function M.reporter()
+  local reporter = { cases = {} }
+
+  reporter.start = function(cases)
+    reporter.cases = cases
+  end
+
+  reporter.update = function(_) end
+
+  reporter.finish = function()
+    local cases = reporter.cases or {}
+    local n_fails = 0
+    for _, c in ipairs(cases) do
+      local name = table.concat(c.desc or {}, " | ")
+      local exec = type(c.exec) == "table" and c.exec or { fails = {}, notes = {} }
+      local fails = exec.fails or {}
+      local notes = exec.notes or {}
+      local status
+      if #fails > 0 then
+        status = "Fail"
+        n_fails = n_fails + 1
+      elseif #notes > 0 and tostring(notes[1]):match("^MiniTest%.skip:") then
+        status = "Skip"
+      else
+        status = "Success"
+      end
+      io.stdout:write(("%s || %s\n"):format(status, name))
+      for _, f in ipairs(fails) do
+        local det = table.concat(vim.split(tostring(f), "\n"), " ")
+        det = det:gsub("%s+", " "):gsub("||", "|"):sub(1, 200)
+        io.stdout:write(("  [failure detail] %s | %s\n"):format(name, det))
+      end
+    end
+    io.stdout:write(("SUMMARY || total=%d fails=%d\n"):format(#cases, n_fails))
+    io.flush()
+    vim.cmd(("silent! %scquit"):format(n_fails > 0 and 1 or 0))
+  end
+
+  return reporter
+end
+
+--- Run the given test files with the reporter above.
+---@param files string[]
+function M.run(files)
+  MiniTest.run({
+    collect = {
+      find_files = function()
+        return files
+      end,
+      filter_cases = function(_)
+        return true
+      end,
+    },
+    execute = { reporter = M.reporter(), stop_on_error = false },
+  })
+end
+
+return M

new file mode 100755
index 00000000..09dfbfd6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/passing/tests/run_first_class_module_tests.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+#!/bin/sh
+# Test-only wrapper for the ocamlformat "passing" golden tests covering the
+# issue "Distinguish (module M : S) from (module M) : (module S) in patterns".
+#
+# The repository's native runner for these tests is dune's aggregate diff
+# rules, which do not emit an individually parseable per-case pass/fail
+# record.  This wrapper reproduces the exact per-case commands that dune
+# generates (see test/passing/gen/gen.ml) for the two affected test files,
+# across every profile, and prints one stable line per case:
+#     [PASS] <id> <name>        or        [FAIL] <id> <name>
+# while preserving the underlying aggregate exit status.
+
+set -u
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
+ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)
+OCAMLF="$ROOT/_build/install/default/bin/ocamlformat"
+
+if [ ! -x "$OCAMLF" ]; then
+  echo "error: ocamlformat binary not found at $OCAMLF" >&2
+  echo "error: build it first with: opam exec -- dune build -p ocamlformat-lib,ocamlformat" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+
+fail_count=0
+
+run_case() {
+  id="$1"; name="$2"; profile="$3"; test_name="$4"
+  dir="$ROOT/test/passing/refs.$profile"
+  out=$(mktemp); err=$(mktemp)
+  ( cd "$dir" && "$OCAMLF" --name "$test_name" --margin-check "$ROOT/test/passing/tests/$test_name" >"$out" 2>"$err" )
+  rc=$?
+  ok=1
+  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || ok=0
+  cmp -s "$out" "$dir/$test_name.ref" || ok=0
+  # A missing .err file means the command is expected to produce no stderr
+  # (dune's (diff x.err x.stderr) treats an absent expected file as empty).
+  if [ -f "$dir/$test_name.err" ]; then
+    cmp -s "$err" "$dir/$test_name.err" || ok=0
+  else
+    [ ! -s "$err" ] || ok=0
+  fi
+  if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then
+    echo "[PASS] $id $name"
+  else
+    echo "[FAIL] $id $name"
+    fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
+  fi
+  rm -f "$out" "$err"
+}
+
+id=0
+for profile in default ahrefs janestreet ocamlformat; do
+  for test_name in first_class_module.ml source.ml; do
+    id=$((id + 1))
+    run_case "$id" "$profile/$test_name" "$profile" "$test_name"
+  done
+done
+
+if [ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "ok - all 8 first-class-module golden tests passed"
+  exit 0
+else
+  echo "not ok - $fail_count of 8 first-class-module golden tests failed"
+  exit 1
+fi

2 default/source.ml
3 ahrefs/first_class_module.ml
4 ahrefs/source.ml
5 janestreet/first_class_module.ml
6 janestreet/source.ml
7 ocamlformat/first_class_module.ml
8 ocamlformat/source.ml

problem_statement:
Bug: `match expr with` gets spread into 3 lines in 0.28.1
**Describe the bug**
When a `match expr with` is one of the two branches of `if true then ... else ...` it gets formatted into 3 lines, this behaviour started in 0.28.1 and is not present under 0.27.0. I couldn't find any explanation, or PR related to this change, and it happens for very short lines, so I'm assuming it's a bug

**How to Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Run ocamlformat 0.28.1 with the profile from https://github.com/xapi-project/xen-api/blob/57f657fd85771d901b18658c561f8a0d592f1f0b/.ocamlformat  to format this file:
```
let name =
  if true then
    match expr with true -> () | false -> ()
  else
    match expr with true -> () | false -> ()
```
It produces:

```
let name =
  if true then
    match
      expr
    with
    | true ->
        ()
    | false ->
        ()
  else
    match
      expr
    with
    | true ->
        ()
    | false ->
        ()
```

### Additional contract requirements

## Contract scope

This contract covers the reproduction in the problem statement: a short
`match expr with` expression used as each branch of an `if-then-else`.
To make the relevant formatting configuration self-contained, the test invokes
ocamlformat with `if-then-else=fit-or-vertical` for that input. No matrix of
built-in profiles or unrelated option variants is part of this contract.

For each branch, the formatted output must keep the `match expr with` header
on one line. Match arms may still be laid out vertically. Apart from this
header requirement, the test intentionally does not constrain surrounding
layout or unrelated formatting settings.

problem_statement:
Bug: Unstable comment exceeding the margin with `if-then-else=fit-or-vertical`
Here's the minimal reproducer for an ocamlformat (5ebeb8ea12a0ff1d0d3ecd4c29d226d5b0f53764) instability bug:

**MWE (7 lines):**
```ocaml
let f =
  match x with
  | A ->
    if gf then begin
      (* aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa *)
      if a then b
    end
```

**Minimal .ocamlformat:**
```
if-then-else=fit-or-vertical
```

**Key findings:**

1. The bug requires **`if-then-else=fit-or-vertical`** — this is the only config option needed.
2. The code structure is: a `match` case containing an `if ... then begin (* long comment *) if ... then ... end`.
3. The comment must be long enough to exceed the margin (80 chars). Specifically, the comment content must be ≥69 characters (making the full comment line 81+ chars with `(* ... *)` and indentation).
4. The oscillation seems related to ocamlformat wrapping/unwrapping the comment at the margin boundary in interaction with the `if-then-else=fit-or-vertical` layout decision for the nested `if`.

The MWE files are at mwe.ml. You can reproduce with:
```bash
cd /tmp/ocamlformat-mwe && printf 'if-then-else=fit-or-vertical\n' > .ocamlformat && ocamlformat mwe.ml
```

### Additional contract requirements

## Observable contract

Formatting the following reproducer with `if-then-else=fit-or-vertical` at the
documented 80-column margin must be stable (idempotent):

```ocaml
let f =
  match x with
  | A ->
    if gf then begin
      (* aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa *)
      if a then b
    end
```

That is, formatting this input must terminate successfully, and formatting the
result again with the same configuration must produce exactly the same output.
The comment is deliberately long enough to exceed the margin.

This contract specifies stability only. It does not require a particular output
layout and does not impose requirements on other `if-then-else` modes or
formatting profiles.

@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+(* Formatting-stability test for the documented if-then-else
+   [fit-or-vertical] over-margin-comment reproducer.
+
+   Positional arguments:
+     argv.(1) = path to the ocamlformat binary under test
+     argv.(2) = path to the OCaml test input file
+
+   The input includes a [match] branch containing
+   [if ... then begin (* comment *) if ... then ... end], where the comment
+   is long enough to exceed the 80-column margin.  The input is copied outside
+   the project and formatted twice in separate invocations: first as supplied,
+   then after replacing the temporary input with the first formatted output.
+   The explicit command-line options model an .ocamlformat containing only
+   [if-then-else=fit-or-vertical] at the documented 80-column margin.
+   Formatting must succeed and be stable (idempotent).  No particular layout,
+   other if-then-else mode, or formatting profile is prescribed.
+
+   Report target: [<input-path>/fit-or-vertical]. *)
+
+let run_quiet exe argv =
+  let open Unix in
+  match
+    let devnull = openfile "/dev/null" [O_RDWR] 0o666 in
+    let stdout, stdout_w = pipe () in
+    let stderr, stderr_w = pipe () in
+    let pid = create_process exe argv devnull stdout_w stderr_w in
+    close stdout_w ;
+    close stderr_w ;
+    let read_all fd =
+      let ic = in_channel_of_descr fd in
+      let b = Buffer.create 4096 in
+      ( try
+          while true do
+            Buffer.add_channel b ic 4096
+          done
+        with End_of_file -> () ) ;
+      close_in ic ;
+      Buffer.contents b
+    in
+    let out = read_all stdout and err = read_all stderr in
+    close devnull ;
+    snd (waitpid [] pid), out, err
+  with
+  | WEXITED 0, out, _ -> Ok out
+  | (WEXITED n | WSIGNALED n), _, err ->
+      Error (Printf.sprintf "exit status %d, stderr:\n%s" n err)
+  | WSTOPPED _, _, _ -> Error "formatter subprocess stopped unexpectedly"
+  | exception Unix_error (e, fn, arg) ->
+      Error
+        (Printf.sprintf "cannot run %s: %s (%s %s)" exe (error_message e)
+           fn arg )
+
+let read_file path =
+  let ic = open_in_bin path in
+  Fun.protect ~finally:(fun () -> close_in_noerr ic) (fun () ->
+      let b = Buffer.create 4096 in
+      ( try
+          while true do
+            Buffer.add_channel b ic 4096
+          done
+        with End_of_file -> () ) ;
+      Buffer.contents b )
+
+let with_temporary contents f =
+  let path = Filename.temp_file "ite-stability-" ".ml" in
+  let cleanup () = try Sys.remove path with Sys_error _ -> () in
+  Fun.protect ~finally:cleanup (fun () ->
+      let oc = open_out_bin path in
+      output_string oc contents ;
+      close_out oc ;
+      f path )
+
+let () =
+  let exe, input =
+    match Array.to_list Sys.argv with
+    | [_; exe; input] -> (exe, input)
+    | _ ->
+        prerr_endline
+          "usage: ite_stability <ocamlformat-binary> <ocaml-input-file>" ;
+        Stdlib.exit 2
+  in
+  let invoke file =
+    run_quiet exe
+      [| exe
+       ; "--no-version-check"
+       ; "--enable-outside-detected-project"
+       ; "--margin=80"
+       ; "--if-then-else=fit-or-vertical"
+       ; file |]
+  in
+  let target = Printf.sprintf "%s/fit-or-vertical" input in
+  match with_temporary (read_file input) invoke with
+  | Ok first ->
+      (match with_temporary first invoke with
+      | Ok second when String.equal first second ->
+          Printf.printf "[PASS] %s\n%!" target ;
+          Stdlib.exit 0
+      | Ok _ ->
+          Printf.printf
+            "[FAIL] %s: formatting is not stable: formatting its output changed it\n%!"
+            target ;
+          Stdlib.exit 1
+      | Error e ->
+          Printf.printf "[FAIL] %s: %s\n%!" target e ;
+          Stdlib.exit 1)
+  | Error e ->
+      Printf.printf "[FAIL] %s: %s\n%!" target e ;
+      Stdlib.exit 1

problem_statement:
Use seed in mock data
Creating reprex I realised we do not have seeds for mock data, which cause that when doing the reprex suddently the cohort I created had records out of observation
Since we use it in examples I think it would be better to have a seed and provide always the same output

### Additional contract requirements

- `mockCohortConstructor()` supports an optional integer seed argument that
  makes the generated mock data reproducible.
- Repeated calls without an explicit seed use the default seed and produce
  identical output: every generated clinical table and both cohort tables of
  the returned cdm reference contain the same rows, so cohort contents and
  cohort counts match exactly between runs.
- Repeated calls that pass the same explicit numeric seed must likewise
  return identical output.
- The task does not require any particular numeric default seed value, and it
  does not specify behavior for non-numeric or missing (NULL) seed values.

+test_that("mockCohortConstructor seed produces reproducible output", {
+  skip_on_cran()
+
+  # all tables with randomly generated content
+  generatedTables <- c(
+    "person", "observation_period", "drug_exposure", "condition_occurrence",
+    "observation", "measurement", "death"
+  )
+
+  # helpers to collect and sort tables so that two cdm references can be
+  # compared row by row
+  collectTable <- function(cdm, tableName) {
+    cdm[[tableName]] |>
+      dplyr::collect() |>
+      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything()))
+  }
+  collectCohort <- function(cohortTable) {
+    cohortTable |>
+      dplyr::collect() |>
+      dplyr::arrange(
+        .data$cohort_definition_id, .data$subject_id,
+        .data$cohort_start_date, .data$cohort_end_date
+      )
+  }
+
+  # repeated calls with default arguments give the same output for every
+  # randomly generated table
+  cdm1 <- mockCohortConstructor()
+  cdm2 <- mockCohortConstructor()

+  expect_identical(sort(names(cdm1)), sort(names(cdm2)))
+  for (tableName in generatedTables) {
+    expect_identical(
+      collectTable(cdm1, tableName),
+      collectTable(cdm2, tableName)
+    )
+  }
+
+  # cohort row contents, not only cohort counts, are reproduced
+  expect_identical(collectCohort(cdm1$cohort1), collectCohort(cdm2$cohort1))
+  expect_identical(collectCohort(cdm1$cohort2), collectCohort(cdm2$cohort2))

+  cdm$copy_cohort_b <- copyCohorts(cdm$original_cohort,

+
+  # keep both cohorts

+                                   n = 1,
+                                   cohortId = c(1, 2),
+                                   name = "copy_cohort_c")
+  cdm$copy_cohort_d <- copyCohorts(cdm$original_cohort,
+                                   n = 1,
+                                   cohortId = c("cohort_1", "cohort_2"),
+                                   name = "copy_cohort_d")

+  # cohort not present

problem_statement:
Overwriting cohort settings when using requireSex twice
When calling `requireSex` twice in a row on different cohort ids, only the last value is tracked in the general cohort settings under the "sex" column. The same happens with `requireAge`.

``` r
library(omopgenerics)
library(omock)
library(PatientProfiles)
library(dplyr)
library(CohortConstructor)
library(CohortCharacteristics)
library(CodelistGenerator)

cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed")

hip_fx_codes <- getCandidateCodes(cdm, "hip fracture")
wrist_fx_codes <- getCandidateCodes(cdm, "wrist fracture")
forearm_fx_codes <- getCandidateCodes(cdm, "forearm fracture")
fx_codes <- newCodelist(list("hip_fracture" = hip_fx_codes$concept_id,
                             "wrist_fracture" = wrist_fx_codes$concept_id,
                             "forearm_fracture" = forearm_fx_codes$concept_id))

cdm$fractures <- conceptCohort(cdm,
                               conceptSet = fx_codes,
                               exit = "event_end_date",
                               name = "fractures")

# Case 1: requiring first Female and then Male
cdm$fractures |>
  CohortConstructor::requireSex(
    sex = "Female",
    cohortId = "wrist_fracture",
    name = "fractures"
  ) |>
  CohortConstructor::requireSex(
    sex = "Male",
    cohortId = "hip_fracture",
    name = "fractures"
  ) |>
  CohortConstructor::settings()

# Case 2: requiring first Male and then Female
cdm$fractures |>

    name = "fractures"

problem_statement:
Code Quality: Multiple OpenFoodFactsLanguage enum occurrences in g files
While having a look at https://github.com/openfoodfacts/smooth-app/pull/6215 that multiple g files include the OpenFoodFactsLanguage enum.

It's far from a high priority, but it's wasted storage and bandwidth to have it so many times.

But we have to check if there is even a way to configure it not be included in all files.

https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenfoodfacts%2Fopenfoodfacts-dart%20OpenFoodFactsLanguage.FINNISH&type=code

### Additional contract requirements

## Serialization and Generated-Code Contract

### Serialization preservation
The localized taxonomy classes `TaxonomyCountry`, `TaxonomyOrigin`,
`TaxonomyNova`, `TaxonomyPackagingMaterial`, `TaxonomyPackagingRecycling`,
and `TaxonomyPackagingShape` must preserve their data across typed JSON
serialization. For any instance `item` of these classes, reconstructing
via `fromJson(item.toJson())` must produce an equivalent object (matching
`toString()` output is sufficient evidence of this preservation), and
every populated field value must survive the round trip unchanged. This
must hold for fully populated objects as well as for null and edge cases
(including empty input), and it must not depend on live server data or
network responses.

For `Product`, the preserved values across JSON round trips are limited to
per-language image freshness entries (each image-field freshness timestamp
remains present after the round trip, and null freshness stays null),
localized product-name values, localized ingredients-text values, and the
quantity value.

### Established JSON wire formats
Serialization must keep using the wire formats already established by the
public API. Localized values are serialized as maps keyed by language code,
including single-value fields such as country codes, which stay serialized
as one-entry maps keyed by a language code (for example
`{"en": "BE"}`), not as plain strings. Product image freshness stays
serialized per language with a non-undefined language for every entry, and
its structure follows the established per-language nested format. Each
image-field freshness timestamp remains present after a serialization
round trip.

### Generated-code deduplication
The full `OpenFoodFactsLanguage` enum map (recognizable by its
`OpenFoodFactsLanguage.FINNISH` entry) must not be repeated across the
committed sources of the package: anywhere in `lib/`, that map may appear
in no more than one source file in total. Each of the generated `*.g.dart`
files for `Product`, `TaxonomyCountry`, `TaxonomyOrigin`, `TaxonomyNova`,
`TaxonomyPackagingMaterial`, `TaxonomyPackagingRecycling`, and
`TaxonomyPackagingShape` used to embed its own copy; after the change,
none of them may.

### Determinism
All of the above behavior must be verifiable from committed test data
alone, without calling production or test server endpoints.

+  static Map<String, Map<String, int>>? _toJsonFreshness(
+    Map<OpenFoodFactsLanguage, Map<ImageField, int>>? map,
+  ) {
+    if (map == null) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    final Map<String, Map<String, int>> result = <String, Map<String, int>>{};
+    for (final MapEntry<OpenFoodFactsLanguage, Map<ImageField, int>>
+        entryLanguage
+        in map.entries) {
+      final String languageKey = entryLanguage.key.offTag;
+      final Map<String, int> values = <String, int>{};
+      for (final MapEntry<ImageField, int> entryField
+          in entryLanguage.value.entries) {
+        final String fieldKey = entryField.key.offTag;
+        final int value = entryField.value;
+        values['${fieldKey}_$languageKey'] = value;
+      }
+      result['${ProductField.IMAGES_FRESHNESS_IN_LANGUAGES.offTag}$languageKey'] =
+          values;
+    }
+    return result;
+  }

+      return null;
+    }
+    if (map is! Map<String, dynamic>) {
+      throw Exception(
+        'Expected type: Map<String, List<String>>, got ${map.runtimeType}',
+      );
+    }
+    Map<OpenFoodFactsLanguage, Map<ImageField, int>>? result;
+    const String prefix = 'images_to_update_';
+    for (final MapEntry<String, dynamic> entry in map.entries) {
+      if (entry.key.length <= prefix.length) {
+        continue;
+      }
+      final String languageOffTag = entry.key.substring(prefix.length);

+        entry.value,
+        language,
+      );
+      result ??= <OpenFoodFactsLanguage, Map<ImageField, int>>{};
+      result[language] = values;

problem_statement:
Support API 3.1
### Why - Problem description
We currently support API 3.
There are currently 6 higher versions (up to 3.6) that we don't support.

[2024-12-12 - Product version 1000 - API version 3.1](https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/ref-api-and-product-schema-change-log/#2024-12-12-product-version-1000-api-version-31-renamed-ecoscore_-fields-to-environmental_score_)
>  Renamed ecoscore_ fields to environmental_score_
Breaking changes:
For legal reasons, we had to rename the Eco-Score to Green-Score. To make sure we won't have to update the schema again, we renamed the corresponding fields from ecoscore_ to the generic name environmental_score_

### Additional contract requirements

- Product queries may request `ProductQueryVersion` 3.1. The path returned for a
  barcode must contain the requested version string exactly (for example
  `/api/v3.1/product/<barcode>/`).
- When `ProductField.ECOSCORE_GRADE`, `ProductField.ECOSCORE_SCORE`, and
  `ProductField.ECOSCORE_DATA` are requested, the effective requested field list
  must include both the legacy `ecoscore_*` keys and the renamed
  `environmental_score_*` keys.
- A `Product` parsed from a Product API version 3.1 response that contains
  `environmental_score_grade`, `environmental_score_score`, and
  `environmental_score_data` must serialize those keys back out in its JSON
  representation; the legacy `ecoscore_*` keys must not appear for such a
  product.

problem_statement:
Unit tests for psiedge < psilim logic
Currently, we don't have anything testing the edge truncation logic; we should add some unit tests for this since we could accidentally break this easily and not know. This could include 

- A full run test with solovev and psiedge set to less than 1, confirming the code runs through
- Unit tests for the `findmax_dW_edge!` functionality (`free_compute_wv_spline` and `free_compute_total`, which might be difficult since they currently accept the entire structs including the equilibria.

### Additional contract requirements

Public contract additions for edge-truncation (`psiedge < psilim`) testing:

- When a Solovev example is run with `psiedge` set strictly below the
  integration flux limit `psilim`, the full run must complete and must
  record a non-empty edge dW-scan dataset in its `gpec.h5` output under
  `edge_scan/`. The scanned flux values must begin at or beyond `psiedge`
  (i.e. the scan covers the edge band `[psiedge, psilim]`).
- For the stable single-n Solovev kinetic case, the reported total
  free-boundary energy `vacuum/et` must remain finite and positive.
- Tests must not require exact numeric values for the reported final
  energies; only completion, finiteness, sign, and the observable
  edge-truncation behavior described above are contractual.

problem_statement:
FreeBoundaryStability eigenmode energies written as ~0 in gpec.h5
The FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_energies datasets in gpec.h5 (power-normalized
total / plasma / vacuum energies et[1], ep[1], ev[1]) read ~1e-15, i.e. effectively
zero, while the ideal-stability physics is correct: the in-memory eigenvalue et[1]
is order unity (about 0.8 for the DIII-D-like example), matching DCON (total dW about
+0.76, stable) and the parallel-integration test (et_par about 0.80).

So this is an output / serialization issue in the eigenmode-energy HDF5 write (or its
normalization), not a physics error. It is pre-existing: the regression has tracked
these quantities as ~1e-15 since at least the develop-era baseline.

Fix: write the correct power-normalized eigenmode energies to gpec.h5, and re-pin the
corresponding regression quantities once corrected.

### Additional contract requirements

The acceptance oracle is the serialized output produced by
`examples/DIIID-like_ideal_example`. In `gpec.h5`, the datasets
`FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_energies`,
`FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_plasma_energies`, and
`FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_vacuum_energies` contain the total, plasma, and
vacuum power-normalized mode energies, respectively.

For the first (least-stable) mode, the signed real components are approximately
0.7990 (total), -1.3524 (plasma), and 2.1515 (vacuum), with 15% relative tolerance
to allow normal numerical variation. Thus the plasma contribution is negative,
the vacuum contribution is positive, and plasma plus vacuum equals total.

The three arrays have equal length and contain at least two modes. Their real
parts are finite; for every mode, plasma plus vacuum equals total within a
relative tolerance of 1e-6 (and absolute tolerance of 1e-10). Every real total,
plasma, and vacuum value has magnitude greater than 1e-6, rather than collapsing
to the pre-fix serialization noise floor near 1e-15.

+"""
+    power_norm_matrix!(Nmat, jmat, mpert, npert, dV_dpsi) -> Nmat
+
+Assemble the power-normalization (surface-norm) matrix N from the conjugate-symmetric Jacobian
+Fourier band `jmat` (length 2·mpert−1, evaluated from the `ffit.jmats` spline), such that
+
+    ξ†·N·ξ = ∮ J |ξ(θ)|² dθ / (dV/dψ) = ⟨|ξ|²⟩
+
+is the flux-surface average of the squared boundary displacement — the DCON power normalization
+as a quadratic form. N is Hermitian Toeplitz within each n-block (block-diagonal over n since the
+Jacobian is axisymmetric) and positive definite (J > 0). It is the metric of the generalized
+eigenproblem W·v = λ·N·v solved in `free_run!` and `free_compute_total`: because W and N
+transform by the same congruence under a change of working (Jacobian) coordinate, the pencil
+eigenvalues are power-normalized mode energies that are invariant to that coordinate choice.
+"""
+function power_norm_matrix!(Nmat::AbstractMatrix{ComplexF64}, jmat::AbstractVector{ComplexF64}, mpert::Int, npert::Int, dV_dpsi::Float64)
+    fill!(Nmat, 0.0 + 0.0im)
+    for ipert_n in 1:npert
+        off = (ipert_n - 1) * mpert
+        # Toeplitz band index: harmonic difference (m'−m) ∈ [−(mpert−1), mpert−1] maps to 1…2·mpert−1, midpoint mpert = the m=0 Jacobian coefficient
+        for ipert_m in 1:mpert, jpert_m in 1:mpert
+            Nmat[off+jpert_m, off+ipert_m] = jmat[jpert_m-ipert_m+mpert] / dV_dpsi
+        end
+    end
+    return Nmat
+end

+using HDF5
+
+# Regression coverage for the serialized power-normalized free-boundary energies.
+# In particular, each component is checked independently so a correct total cannot
+# hide an incorrectly serialized plasma/vacuum split.
+let ex = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "examples", "DIIID-like_ideal_example")
+    output = joinpath(ex, "gpec.h5")
+    @testset "FreeBoundaryStability eigenmode energies in gpec.h5" begin
+        rm(output; force = true)
+        try
+            GeneralizedPerturbedEquilibrium.main([ex])

+                et = read(h5["FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_energies"])
+                ep = read(h5["FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_plasma_energies"])
+                ev = read(h5["FreeBoundaryStability/eigenmode_vacuum_energies"])
+
+                @test length(et) == length(ep) == length(ev)
+                @test length(et) >= 2
+                @test all(isfinite, real.(et))
+                @test all(isfinite, real.(ep))
+                @test all(isfinite, real.(ev))
+
+                # Deterministic DIII-D-like least-stable-mode oracle. These signed
+                # component checks distinguish the plasma and vacuum datasets.
+                @test real(et[1]) ≈ 0.7990 rtol = 0.15
+                @test real(ep[1]) ≈ -1.3524 rtol = 0.15
+                @test real(ev[1]) ≈ 2.1515 rtol = 0.15
+
+                # Every mode must retain its energy decomposition and must be well
+                # clear of the pre-fix serialization noise floor.
+                @test all(isapprox.(real.(ep) .+ real.(ev), real.(et); rtol = 1e-6, atol = 1e-10))
+                @test all(abs.(real.(et)) .> 1e-6)
+                @test all(abs.(real.(ep)) .> 1e-6)
+                @test all(abs.(real.(ev)) .> 1e-6)
+            end
+        finally
+            rm(output; force = true)
+        end
+    end
+end

problem_statement:
Snapshots and Android Studio previews are not identical

### Additional contract requirements

Android Studio previews and Paparazzi snapshots must render on one shared reference device so that snapshots and Android Studio previews are identical:

- A single preview reference device is declared as the public constant `OudsPreviewDevice` in `core/src/main/java/com/orange/ouds/core/utilities/OudsPreview.kt`, with the value `Devices.NEXUS_5`.
- Every composable preview annotated directly with the Compose `Preview` annotation that declares an explicit `device` must pass `device = OudsPreviewDevice`. This applies wherever the preview lives in the repository's production sources, and regardless of whether the annotation is written with its plain, fully qualified, or imported-alias name. A direct preview which omits the `device` argument renders on the default preview device and is out of the scope of this shared-device rule; only the explicit selection of a different device is prohibited.
- Every custom preview meta-annotation (for instance `OudsPreviewLightDark`) must declare `device = OudsPreviewDevice` on each of its own `Preview` annotations, so previews rendered through those meta-annotations also run on the shared reference device.
- Previews may additionally declare an explicit `widthDp` or `heightDp`, but never a different explicit device.
- The Paparazzi snapshot infrastructure must render on the same Nexus 5 based device configuration as the previews: the `Paparazzi` rule's effective `deviceConfig` must derive from `DeviceConfig.NEXUS_5`, customized at most through copies (for instance to adapt dimensions, screen density, or font scale), and must never substitute another device. The configuration may be supplied through any conventional Kotlin indirection, such as a direct reference, a `with(DeviceConfig.NEXUS_5) { copy(...) }` expression, a property, or an ordinary factory function, provided the configuration which is actually returned remains based on `DeviceConfig.NEXUS_5`, so snapshots and previews render components identically.
