+package com.orange.ouds.core.component
+
+import java.io.File
+import org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull
+import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
+import org.junit.Test
+
+/**
+ * Ensures that Android Studio previews and Paparazzi snapshots remain identical by checking that they all render on
+ * one shared reference device.
+ *
+ * Sources are inspected as Kotlin code, not as raw text: comments and string literal contents are removed before any
+ * analysis and every `@Preview` usage is associated with the composable declaration it annotates, so a `@Preview`
+ * token appearing in a documentation comment or inside a string cannot be mistaken for a real preview annotation.
+ */
+internal class OudsPreviewSnapshotConsistencyTest {
+
+    companion object {
+        private const val referenceDeviceName = "OudsPreviewDevice"
+        private const val referenceDeviceQualifiedName = "com.orange.ouds.core.utilities.OudsPreviewDevice"
+        private const val referenceDevicesImport = "androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Devices"
+
+        private val referenceDeviceFileCandidates = listOf(
+            File("src/main/java/com/orange/ouds/core/utilities/OudsPreview.kt"),
+            File("../core/src/main/java/com/orange/ouds/core/utilities/OudsPreview.kt"),
+            File("core/src/main/java/com/orange/ouds/core/utilities/OudsPreview.kt")
+        )
+
+        // The Paparazzi snapshot test sources, searched relative to the working directory of the test (the `core`
+        // module when tests run through Gradle).
+        private val snapshotTestSourceRootCandidates = listOf(
+            File("../core-test/src/main/java"),
+            File("core-test/src/main/java")
+        )
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun snapshotPreviewsDeclareExplicitDeviceAndDimension() {
+        checkReferenceDeviceDeclaration()
+        checkComposablePreviewDevices()
+        checkCustomPreviewMetaAnnotations()
+        checkSnapshotRendererDeviceConfiguration()
+    }
+
+    /** The shared reference device must be a public constant holding the Compose Nexus 5 device descriptor. */
+    private fun checkReferenceDeviceDeclaration() {
+        val previewUtilitiesFile = referenceDeviceFileCandidates.firstOrNull { it.canRead() }
+        assertNotNull(
+            "File core/src/main/java/com/orange/ouds/core/utilities/OudsPreview.kt does not exist; it should declare the shared preview device.",
+            previewUtilitiesFile
+        )
+        val code = previewUtilitiesFile!!.readText().withoutCommentsAndStrings()
+        val declaration = Regex(
+            """(?m)^[ \t]*((?:(?:public|private|internal|protected)[ \t]+)?)const[ \t]+val[ \t]+$referenceDeviceName[ \t]*(?::[ \t]*String[ \t]*)?=[ \t]*([^;\n]+)[ \t]*$"""
+        ).find(code)
+        assertNotNull(
+            "$previewUtilitiesFile should declare a public constant `OudsPreviewDevice` holding the device shared by previews and snapshots.",
+            declaration
+        )
+        val visibility = declaration!!.groupValues[1].trim()
+        assertTrue(
+            "The `OudsPreviewDevice` constant in $previewUtilitiesFile should be public so every preview and snapshot can share it, but a restricted visibility is declared.",
+            visibility.isEmpty() || visibility == "public"
+        )
+        val value = declaration.groupValues[2].replace(Regex("""\s+"""), "")
+        assertTrue(
+            "`OudsPreviewDevice` should select the Compose Nexus 5 reference device shared by Android Studio previews and Paparazzi snapshots.",
+            value in composeNexus5Expressions(code)
+        )
+    }
+
+    /** Spellings of the Compose Nexus 5 descriptor made available by this file's imports. */
+    private fun composeNexus5Expressions(code: String): Set<String> {
+        val expressions = mutableSetOf(
+            "Devices.NEXUS_5",
+            "androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Devices.NEXUS_5"
+        )
+        Regex("""(?m)^[ \t]*import[ \t]+${Regex.escape(referenceDevicesImport)}[ \t]+as[ \t]+(\w+)[ \t]*$""")
+            .findAll(code).forEach { expressions += "${it.groupValues[1]}.NEXUS_5" }
+        Regex("""(?m)^[ \t]*import[ \t]+${Regex.escape(referenceDevicesImport)}\.NEXUS_5(?:[ \t]+as[ \t]+(\w+))?[ \t]*$""")
+            .findAll(code).forEach { expressions += it.groupValues[1].ifEmpty { "NEXUS_5" } }
+        return expressions
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * A composable preview annotated directly with the Compose `Preview` annotation must select the shared reference
+     * device whenever it declares a device. A direct preview which omits the `device` argument renders on the
+     * default preview device and is out of the scope of this shared-device rule, whether the omission happens in
+     * production sources or in demo sources. Only annotations that actually resolve to the Compose `Preview`
+     * annotation are considered, whether they are written with its plain, fully qualified, or imported-alias name.
+     */
+    private fun checkComposablePreviewDevices() {
+        val failures = mutableListOf<String>()
+        previewSourceFiles().forEach { sourceFile ->
+            val referenceNames = sourceFile.referenceDeviceNames()
+            sourceFile.composablePreviewOffsets().forEach { previewOffset ->
+                val arguments = balancedArguments(sourceFile, previewOffset) ?: ""
+                val deviceArgument = namedArgument(arguments, "device") ?: return@forEach
+                val deviceName = deviceArgument.normalizedReference()
+                if (deviceName !in referenceNames) {
+                    failures += "${sourceFile.file}:${lineNumberOf(sourceFile.text, previewOffset)}: " +
+                        "@Preview declares `device = $deviceName` instead of `device = $referenceDeviceName`"
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        assertTrue(
+            "Previews are not identical to snapshots because they select another device:\n" + failures.joinToString("\n"),
+            failures.isEmpty()
+        )
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Check every preview meta-annotation where it is declared, including annotations that are not currently used by
+     * a composable. A preview meta-annotation may contain more than one `@Preview` declaration, all of which must
+     * select the shared reference device.
+     */
+    private fun checkCustomPreviewMetaAnnotations() {
+        val failures = mutableListOf<String>()
+        previewSourceFiles().forEach { sourceFile ->
+            val referenceNames = sourceFile.referenceDeviceNames()
+            sourceFile.annotationClassDeclarations().forEach { annotationDeclaration ->
+                if (annotationDeclaration.previews.isEmpty()) return@forEach
+                annotationDeclaration.previews.forEach { previewOffset ->
+                    val arguments = balancedArguments(sourceFile, previewOffset) ?: ""
+                    val device = namedArgument(arguments, "device")?.normalizedReference()
+                    if (device == null || device !in referenceNames) {
+                        failures += "${sourceFile.file}:${lineNumberOf(sourceFile.text, annotationDeclaration.offset)}: " +
+                            "preview meta-annotation `${annotationDeclaration.name}` must declare `device = $referenceDeviceName`"
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        assertTrue(
+            "Preview meta-annotations must render on the shared reference device:\n" + failures.joinToString("\n"),
+            failures.isEmpty()
+        )
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Each Paparazzi rule must actually receive a device configuration matching the preview reference device, that
+     * is the Nexus 5 based `DeviceConfig` which may only be customized through copies. The configuration is inspected
+     * at the rule's `deviceConfig` argument, and an arbitrary expression is not accepted solely because it mentions
+     * the Nexus 5 name: the expression, or the declaration of the property or function it invokes, must derive the
+     * configuration from the Nexus 5 `DeviceConfig` without substituting another device.
+     */
+    private fun checkSnapshotRendererDeviceConfiguration() {
+        val snapshotTestSourcesRoot = snapshotTestSourceRootCandidates.firstOrNull { it.isDirectory }
+        assertTrue(
+            "Snapshot test sources not found from ${File("").absolutePath}; they should render on the same device as the previews.",
+            snapshotTestSourcesRoot != null
+        )
+        val snapshotSources = snapshotTestSourcesRoot!!.kotlinSources()
+        val failures = mutableListOf<String>()
+        var ruleCount = 0
+        snapshotSources.forEach { sourceFile ->
+            Regex("""\bPaparazzi\s*\(""").findAll(sourceFile.code).forEach { rule ->
+                ruleCount++
+                val arguments = balancedArguments(sourceFile, rule.range.first + rule.value.length - 1) ?: ""
+                val deviceConfig = namedArgument(arguments, "deviceConfig")
+                if (deviceConfig == null || !configurationUsesReferenceDevice(deviceConfig, sourceFile, snapshotSources, mutableSetOf())) {
+                    failures += "${sourceFile.file}:${lineNumberOf(sourceFile.text, rule.range.first)}: " +
+                        "Paparazzi must receive a Nexus 5 based `deviceConfig` matching the preview reference device"
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        assertTrue(
+            "No Paparazzi rule found; the snapshot test infrastructure should render on the same device as the previews.",
+            ruleCount > 0
+        )
+        assertTrue(
+            "Paparazzi snapshots should use the same Nexus 5 based configuration as previews:\n" + failures.joinToString("\n"),
+            failures.isEmpty()
+        )
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Whether the given expression demonstrably evaluates to the Nexus 5 based device configuration: either it
+     * directly derives from a reference to the Nexus 5 `DeviceConfig`, or it references a property or invokes a
+     * factory or helper whose own declaration demonstrably derives the provided configuration from the Nexus 5
+     * `DeviceConfig` without substituting another device.
+     */
+    private fun configurationUsesReferenceDevice(
+        expression: String,
+        sourceFile: SourceFile,
+        allSources: List<SourceFile>,
+        visitedNames: MutableSet<String>
+    ): Boolean {
+        val value = expression.trim()
+        if (snapshotReferenceDeviceNames(sourceFile).any { reference -> referencesReferenceDevice(value, reference) }) return true
+
+        // Resolve the callee of an invocation, or the name of a referenced property or function, and inspect its
+        // declaration instead of requiring a particular expression layout at the call site.
+        val name = Regex("""^([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*)\s*(?:[({]|$)""").find(value)?.groupValues?.get(1)
+            ?: return false
+        val simpleName = name.substringAfterLast('.')
+        if (!visitedNames.add(simpleName)) return false
+        return resolveDeviceConfiguration(name, sourceFile, allSources, visitedNames)
+    }
+
+    /** Whether [value] is directly based on the given reference to the Nexus 5 `DeviceConfig`. */
+    private fun referencesReferenceDevice(value: String, reference: String): Boolean {
+        val escaped = Regex.escape(reference)
+        return Regex("""^\s*$escaped\s*(?:\.\s*copy\s*\(|$)""").containsMatchIn(value) ||
+            Regex("""^\s*with\s*\(\s*$escaped\s*\)\s*\{""").containsMatchIn(value)
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Follows a property or function named [name] to its declaration and decides whether the configuration it
+     * provides is demonstrably based on the Nexus 5 `DeviceConfig`. The value of a property, the return expression
+     * or returned value of an ordinary function, and the single expression of a lambda-like factory are inspected
+     * recursively.
+     */
+    private fun resolveDeviceConfiguration(
+        name: String,
+        sourceFile: SourceFile,
+        allSources: List<SourceFile>,
+        visitedNames: MutableSet<String>
+    ): Boolean {
+        val simpleName = name.substringAfterLast('.')
+        val searchSources = listOf(sourceFile) + allSources.filter { it !== sourceFile }
+        searchSources.forEach { declarationFile ->
+            val declaration = declarationExpression(simpleName, declarationFile) ?: return@forEach
+            if (configurationUsesReferenceDevice(declaration, declarationFile, allSources, visitedNames)) return true
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Returns the expression demonstrably returned by the property or function [name] declared in this file:
+     * the assigned value of a property, the expression of an expression-body function, or the value returned by a
+     * single-return block-body function. Returns null when the provided value cannot be determined statically.
+     */
+    private fun declarationExpression(name: String, sourceFile: SourceFile): String? {
+        val property = Regex("""\b(?:val|var)\s+${Regex.escape(name)}\b[^=\n]*=""").find(sourceFile.code)
+        if (property != null) {
+            return expressionAt(sourceFile.code, property.range.last + 1)
+        }
+        val function = Regex(
+            """\bfun\s+(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*\.)?${Regex.escape(name)}\s*\("""
+        ).find(sourceFile.code) ?: return null
+        var index = function.range.last
+        var depth = 1
+        while (index < sourceFile.code.length && depth > 0) {
+            when (sourceFile.code[index]) {
+                '(' -> depth++
+                ')' -> depth--
+            }
+            index++
+        }
+        if (depth != 0) return null
+        while (index < sourceFile.code.length && sourceFile.code[index].isWhitespace()) index++
+        // Skip an explicit return type declaration.
+        if (index < sourceFile.code.length && sourceFile.code[index] == ':') {
+            index++
+            while (index < sourceFile.code.length && sourceFile.code[index] != '=' && sourceFile.code[index] != '{') index++
+            while (index < sourceFile.code.length && sourceFile.code[index].isWhitespace()) index++
+        }
+        if (index >= sourceFile.code.length) return null
+        if (sourceFile.code[index] == '=') {
+            return expressionAt(sourceFile.code, index + 1)
+        }
+        if (sourceFile.code[index] != '{') return null
+        val body = expressionAt(sourceFile.code, index)?.removePrefix("{")?.removeSuffix("}") ?: return null
+        val returns = Regex("""(?<!\w)return(?![\w@])(?:@[A-Za-z_]\w*)?\s*""").findAll(body).toList()
+        return if (returns.size == 1) expressionAt(body, returns[0].range.last + 1) else null
+    }
+
+    /** Qualified and imported spellings of Paparazzi's Nexus 5 DeviceConfig in one source file. */
+    private fun snapshotReferenceDeviceNames(sourceFile: SourceFile): Set<String> {
+        val names = mutableSetOf(
+            "DeviceConfig.NEXUS_5",
+            "app.cash.paparazzi.DeviceConfig.NEXUS_5"
+        )
+        Regex("""(?m)^[ \t]*import[ \t]+app\.cash\.paparazzi\.DeviceConfig\.NEXUS_5(?:[ \t]+as[ \t]+(\w+))?[ \t]*$""")
+            .findAll(sourceFile.code).forEach { names += it.groupValues[1].ifEmpty { "NEXUS_5" } }
+        Regex("""(?m)^[ \t]*import[ \t]+app\.cash\.paparazzi\.DeviceConfig[ \t]+as[ \t]+(\w+)[ \t]*$""")
+            .findAll(sourceFile.code).forEach { names += "${it.groupValues[1]}.NEXUS_5" }
+        return names
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Every production Kotlin source in every repository module is considered, including the demo application:
+     * direct previews and reusable preview annotations can live outside the core component package.
+     */
+    private fun previewSourceFiles(): List<SourceFile> {
+        val roots = repositoryProductionSourceRoots().ifEmpty {
+            // Fall back to the sibling production sources when the repository root cannot be resolved.
+            listOf(
+                File("src/main/java"),
+                File("../core/src/main/java"),
+                File("../core-test/src/main/java")
+            ).filter { it.isDirectory }
+        }
+        return roots.flatMap { it.kotlinSources() }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Every production `src/main/java` source root of the repository, resolved relative to the working directory of
+     * the test (the `core` module when tests run through Gradle), so the checks cannot be evaded by placing sources
+     * in a sibling module (for instance the demo application module).
+     */
+    private fun repositoryProductionSourceRoots(): List<File> {
+        val repositoryRoot = when {
+            File("core/src/main/java").isDirectory -> File(".")
+            File("../core/src/main/java").isDirectory -> File("..")
+            else -> return emptyList()
+        }.canonicalFile
+        return repositoryRoot.listFiles().orEmpty()
+            .filter { it.isDirectory && !it.name.startsWith(".") }
+            .map { File(it, "src/main/java") }
+            .filter { it.isDirectory }
+            .map { it.canonicalFile }
+            .distinctBy { it.absolutePath }
+    }
+
+
+    /**
+     * Returns the offsets in [code] of the actual Compose `Preview` annotations in the annotation block of a
+     * composable function, whichever spelling is used to name the annotation: the plain `Preview` name, the fully
+     * qualified `androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview` name, or an alias declared by an import of either.
+     */
+    private fun SourceFile.composablePreviewOffsets(): List<Int> {
+        val offsets = mutableListOf<Int>()
+        val previewNames = composePreviewAnnotationNames()
+        Regex("""(?<!\w)fun\s+\w+""").findAll(code).forEach { function ->
+            val header = annotationHeader(function.range.first)
+            if (!Regex("""(?<![\w.])@Composable\b""").containsMatchIn(header)) return@forEach
+            val headerOffset = function.range.first - header.length
+            annotationOffsets(header, previewNames).mapTo(offsets) { headerOffset + it }
+        }
+        return offsets.sorted()
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * The set of spellings which denote the actual Compose `Preview` annotation in this source file: the plain
+     * `Preview` name, the fully qualified name, and every alias declared by an import of the annotation.
+     */
+    private fun SourceFile.composePreviewAnnotationNames(): Set<String> {
+        val composePreview = "androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview"
+        val names = mutableSetOf("Preview", composePreview)
+        Regex("""(?m)^[ \t]*import[ \t]+${Regex.escape(composePreview)}[ \t]+as[ \t]+(\w+)[ \t]*$""")
+            .findAll(code).forEach { names += it.groupValues[1] }
+        return names
+    }
+
+    /** Offsets of annotation usages whose type name is one of [annotationNames] in the given source excerpt. */
+    private fun annotationOffsets(text: String, annotationNames: Set<String>): List<Int> =
+        Regex("""(?<![\w.])@(\w+(?:[ \t]*\.[ \t]*\w+)*)""").findAll(text)
+            .filter { match -> match.groupValues[1].replace(Regex("""\s+"""), "") in annotationNames }
+            .map { it.range.first }
+            .toList()
+
+    /** Returns annotation classes together with the `@Preview` annotations in their own annotation block. */
+    private fun SourceFile.annotationClassDeclarations(): List<AnnotationClassDeclaration> {
+        val declarations = mutableListOf<AnnotationClassDeclaration>()
+        Regex("""(?<!\w)annotation\s+class\s+(\w+)""").findAll(code).forEach { match ->
+            val header = annotationHeader(match.range.first)
+            val headerOffset = match.range.first - header.length
+            val previews = Regex("""(?<![\w.])@Preview\b""").findAll(header)
+                .map { headerOffset + it.range.first }
+                .toList()
+            declarations += AnnotationClassDeclaration(match.range.first, match.groupValues[1], previews)
+        }
+        return declarations
+    }
+
+    private fun annotationArgumentsStart(text: String, offset: Int): Boolean {
+        var index = offset
+        while (index < text.length && text[index].isWhitespace()) index++
+        return index < text.length && text[index] == '('
+    }
+
+    private fun annotationArgumentsEnd(text: String, offset: Int): Int? {
+        var index = offset
+        while (index < text.length && text[index].isWhitespace()) index++
+        if (index >= text.length || text[index] != '(') return null
+        var depth = 0
+        while (index < text.length) {
+            when (text[index]) {
+                '(' -> depth++
+                ')' -> {
+                    depth--
+                    if (depth == 0) return index + 1
+                }
+            }
+            index++
+        }
+        return null
+    }
+
+    private fun SourceFile.annotationHeader(declarationOffset: Int): String =
+        code.substring(0, declarationOffset).substringAfterLast("\n\n").substringAfterLast("}")
+
+    private fun namedArgument(arguments: String, name: String): String? {
+        val match = Regex("""\b${Regex.escape(name)}\s*=""").find(arguments) ?: return null
+        return expressionAt(arguments, match.range.last + 1)
+    }
+
+    /**

+     * annotation has no argument list.
+     */
+    private fun balancedArguments(sourceFile: SourceFile, nameOffset: Int): String? {
+        var argumentsOffset = nameOffset
+        if (sourceFile.code.getOrNull(argumentsOffset) == '@') {
+            argumentsOffset++
+            while (sourceFile.code.getOrNull(argumentsOffset)?.let { it.isLetterOrDigit() || it == '_' || it == '.' } == true) {
+                argumentsOffset++
+            }
+        }
+        val tail = sourceFile.code.substring(argumentsOffset)
+        if (!annotationArgumentsStart(tail, 0)) return ""
+        val end = annotationArgumentsEnd(tail, 0) ?: return null
+        return tail.substring(tail.indexOf('(') + 1, end - 1)
+    }
+
+    /** Returns the expression starting at [offset] in [text], stopping at a top-level comma or line break. */
+    private fun expressionAt(text: String, offset: Int): String? {
+        val expression = StringBuilder()
+        var depth = 0
+        var sawContent = false
+        for (char in text.substring(offset)) {
+            when (char) {
+                '(', '[', '{' -> depth++
+                ')', ']', '}' -> if (depth > 0) depth--
+                ',' -> if (depth == 0) return expression.toString().trim()
+                '\n', ';' -> if (sawContent && depth == 0) return expression.toString().trim()
+            }
+            expression.append(char)
+            if (!char.isWhitespace()) sawContent = true
+        }
+        return expression.toString().trim().takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
+    }
+
+    /** Normalizes harmless whitespace and parentheses around a constant reference. */
+    private fun String.normalizedReference(): String {
+        var result = replace(Regex("""\s+"""), "")
+        while (result.startsWith("(") && result.endsWith(")") && result.drop(1).dropLast(1).isNotEmpty()) {
+            result = result.drop(1).dropLast(1)
+        }
+        return result
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * The set of spellings which denote the shared preview reference device in this source file: the plain constant
+     * name, the fully qualified name, and the aliases declared by an explicit import of the constant.
+     */
+    private fun SourceFile.referenceDeviceNames(): Set<String> {
+        val names = mutableSetOf(referenceDeviceName, referenceDeviceQualifiedName)
+        Regex("""(?m)^\s*import\s+${Regex.escape(referenceDeviceQualifiedName)}(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?\s*$""")
+            .findAll(code).mapTo(names) { it.groupValues[1].ifEmpty { referenceDeviceName } }
+        return names
+    }
+
+    private fun File.kotlinSources(): List<SourceFile> = walkTopDown()
+        .filter { it.isFile && it.extension == "kt" }
+        .map { SourceFile(it, it.readText()) }
+        .toList()
+
+    private fun lineNumberOf(source: String, offset: Int) = source.substring(0, offset).count { it == '\n' } + 1
+
+    private data class AnnotationClassDeclaration(val offset: Int, val name: String, val previews: List<Int>)
+
+    /**
+     * A Kotlin source file together with a copy of its text where comments and string literal contents have been
+     * replaced by spaces, so analyses based on [code] react to Kotlin declarations only and never to a textual
+     * `@Preview` example in a comment or string content. Offsets are preserved between [text] and [code].
+     */
+    private inner class SourceFile(val file: File, val text: String) {
+        val code: String = text.withoutCommentsAndStrings()
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Returns this Kotlin source with every comment replaced by spaces and every string literal content replaced
+     * by spaces, preserving offsets, so structural analyses see declarations only.
+     */
+    private fun String.withoutCommentsAndStrings(): String {
+        val result = StringBuilder(this)
+        var index = 0
+        while (index < result.length) {
+            when {
+                result.startsWith("//", index) -> {
+                    val newline = result.indexOf('\n', index).takeIf { it >= 0 } ?: result.length
+                    result.blank(index, newline)
+                    index = newline
+                }
+                result.startsWith("/*", index) -> {
+                    var end = index + 2
+                    var depth = 1
+                    while (end < result.length && depth > 0) {
+                        when {
+                            result.startsWith("/*", end) -> { depth++; end += 2 }
+                            result.startsWith("*/", end) -> { depth--; end += 2 }
+                            else -> end++
+                        }
+                    }
+                    result.blank(index, end)
+                    index = end
+                }
+                result.startsWith("\"\"\"", index) -> {
+                    val closing = result.indexOf("\"\"\"", index + 3).takeIf { it >= 0 } ?: result.length - 3
+                    val end = (closing + 3).coerceAtMost(result.length)
+                    // Blank the delimiters and the raw content, preserving newlines so line numbers are unchanged.
+                    result.blank(index, end)
+                    index = end
+                }
+                result[index] == '"' -> {
+                    var end = index + 1
+                    while (end < result.length && result[end] != '"' && result[end] != '\n') {
+                        if (result[end] == '\\') end++
+                        end++
+                    }
+                    // Blank the delimiters and the content of the string literal.
+                    result.blank(index, (end + 1).coerceAtMost(result.length))
+                    index = (end + 1).coerceAtMost(result.length)
+                }
+                else -> index++
+            }
+        }
+        return result.toString()
+    }
+
+    private fun StringBuilder.blank(start: Int, end: Int) {
+        for (i in start until end) {
+            if (this[i] != '\n') this.setCharAt(i, ' ')
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun StringBuilder.startsWith(prefix: String, offset: Int): Boolean {
+        if (offset + prefix.length > length) return false
+        for (i in prefix.indices) {
+            if (this[offset + i] != prefix[i]) return false
+        }
+        return true
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Remove the defect model
The defects model was introduced in #4493 and the only implementation was added in #4570. It was removed again in #8994 in August 2024. Since then, the defects model is completely unused.

I would propose to remove the defects model completely now. @oss-review-toolkit/tsc @oss-review-toolkit/core-devs please provide feedback on that proposal.

### Additional contract requirements

The defects model is removed completely, including the whole advisor-capabilities concept that was used to distinguish advisor results.

In particular, after this change:

- No standalone defect model remains available in the advisor model, and no standalone advisor capability type remains available.
- Advisor details expose only the advisor name; they no longer expose advisor capabilities.
- An advisor result no longer contains defects; it still contains vulnerabilities and issues.
- The advisor run model no longer provides a predefined filter for results that contain defects and no longer offers a way to query defects for a package.
- The predefined filtering of issue-bearing advisor results no longer filters by advisor capability; filtering issue-bearing results by minimum severity remains supported.
- Deserialization of advisor details and advisor results remains tolerant of legacy data, ignoring legacy serialized capabilities and defects properties.

+

+
+class AdvisorDetailsTest : WordSpec({
+    "The advisor model" should {
+        "no longer provide a standalone defect model" {
+            val orphanedClass = runCatching {
+                Class.forName("org.ossreviewtoolkit.model.Defect", false, AdvisorDetailsTest::class.java.classLoader)
+            }.getOrNull()
+
+            orphanedClass shouldBe null
+        }
+
+        "no longer provide a standalone advisor capability model" {
+            val orphanedClass = runCatching {
+                Class.forName(
+                    "org.ossreviewtoolkit.model.AdvisorCapability",
+                    false,
+                    AdvisorDetailsTest::class.java.classLoader
+                )
+            }.getOrNull()
+
+            orphanedClass shouldBe null
+        }
+    }
+
+    "The advisor details model" should {
+        "no longer contain advisor capabilities" {
+            val properties = AdvisorDetails::class.memberProperties.map { it.name }
+
+            properties shouldNotContain "capabilities"
+        }
+
+        "remain deserializable from legacy data that contains capabilities" {
+            val details = """
+                {
+                    "name": "advisor",
+                    "capabilities": [ "DEFECTS" ]
+                }
+            """.trimIndent().fromJson<AdvisorDetails>()
+
+            details.name shouldBe "advisor"
+        }
+    }
+
+    "The advisor result model" should {
+        "no longer contain defects" {
+            val properties = AdvisorResult::class.memberProperties.map { it.name }
+
+            properties shouldNotContain "defects"
+        }
+
+        "remain deserializable from legacy data that contains defects" {
+            val result = """
+                {
+                    "advisor": {
+                        "name": "advisor",
+                        "capabilities": [ "DEFECTS" ]
+                    },
+                    "summary": {
+                        "start_time": "2021-04-06T13:26:05.123Z",
+                        "end_time": "2021-04-06T13:26:47.456Z"
+                    },
+                    "defects": [
+                        {
+                            "id": "obsolete-defect",
+                            "url": "https://defects.example.org/obsolete-defect"
+                        }
+                    ]

problem_statement:
Re-namespace plotting functions
What's now `FlexiChains.myplot` and `FlexiChains.mmyplot` should probably be renamed to `FlexiChains.Plots.myplot` and `FlexiChains.Makie.myplot`. This way:

(1) one can switch between backends by simply importing a different submodule
(2) we can actually export the identifiers instead of only making them public
(3) this also avoids 'privileging' the Plots implementations (which do not look as pretty anyway).

To avoid a breaking change, we can leave the current top-level functions as aliases.

+# 0.6.13
+
+Moved plotting functions into the `FlexiChains.Plots` and `FlexiChains.Makie` submodules.
+
+What used to be called `FlexiChains.traceplot` (the Plots.jl backend) is now `FlexiChains.Plots.traceplot`, and what used to be called `FlexiChains.mtraceplot` (the Makie.jl backend) is now `FlexiChains.Makie.traceplot`.
+
+The intention for this is to make it easier to switch between plotting backends, and to make the naming more consistent and intuitive.
+
+The old functions are retained as aliases, but they are deprecated and will be removed in the future.

+$(_PLOTS_KWARGS_DOCSTRING)

+`FlexiChain` using Plots.jl. Continuous-valued parameters are plotted as density estimates,
+discrete-valued parameters as histograms.
+
+$(_PARAM_DOCSTRING("mixeddensity"))

+$(_POOL_CHAINS_DOCSTRING)
+
+$(_PLOTS_KWARGS_DOCSTRING)
+"""

+    FlexiChains.Plots.meanplot(
+        chn::FlexiChain{TKey}[, param_or_params];
+        kwargs...
+    )
+
+Plot the running mean of the specified parameter(s) in the given `FlexiChain` using
+Plots.jl.
+
+$(_PARAM_DOCSTRING("meanplot"))
+
+$(_PLOTS_KWARGS_DOCSTRING)
+"""

+    FlexiChains.Plots.meanplot!(

+###########################################################
+# Utility functions for plotting (shared across backends) #
+###########################################################
+#
+# We stick these in a module to avoid cluttering the main FlexiChains namespace.
+
+module PlotUtils
+
+function _PARAM_DOCSTRING(funcname)
+    return """
+    If no parameters are specified, this will plot all parameters in the chain. Note that
+    non-parameter, i.e. `Extra`, keys are excluded by default. If you want to plot _all_ keys,
+    you can explicitly pass all keys with `$(funcname)(chn, :)`.
+    """
+end
+
+const _POOL_CHAINS_DOCSTRING = """
+The `pool_chains` keyword argument specifies whether to pool samples across multiple chains
+when plotting. If `true` (the default), samples from all chains are pooled together; if
+`false`, samples from each chain are plotted separately.
+"""
+
+const DEFAULT_WIDTH = 400
+const DEFAULT_HEIGHT = 250
+
+using ..FlexiChains:
+    FlexiChain,
+    ParameterOrExtra,
+    VarName,
+    _split_varnames,
+    niters,
+    _get_multi_keys,
+    _get_multi_key
+import DimensionalData as DD
+import StatsBase
+
+"""
+Return a chain that has been:
+
+1. Subsetted to just the parameters we want to plot; and
+
+2. Split up such that each key corresponds to a single real-valued parameter.
+
+This ensures that each plotting function can simply loop over the keys of the returned chain
+and plot each one, without needing to worry about the structure of the data.
+"""
+function subset_and_split_chain(
+        chn::FlexiChain{TKey}, param_or_params
+    )::FlexiChain where {TKey}
+    parameters_to_plot = if param_or_params isa Union{AbstractVector, Colon}
+        _get_multi_keys(TKey, keys(chn), param_or_params)
+    else
+        # Assume it's a single key. No, don't ask what happens if the key type is an
+        # AbstractVector...
+        [_get_multi_key(TKey, keys(chn), param_or_params)]
+    end
+    # Subset the chain to just those parameters. Ordinarily we wouldn't need to do this; we
+    # would just directly return `keys_to_plot`. However, there are some subtle
+    # considerations when using VarName chains. See below for a full explanation.
+    chn = chn[parameters_to_plot]
+    # Split into real-valued parameters if possible.
+    chn = _split_varnames(chn)
+    return chn
+end
+
+"""
+Check that the element type of the array is a subtype of `Real`.
+"""
+function check_eltype_is_real(::AbstractArray{T}) where {T}
+    return if !(T <: Real)
+        throw(
+            ArgumentError(
+                "plotting functions only support real-valued data; got data of type $T"
+            ),
+        )
+    end
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainTrace{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainRank{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    # indicates which one to plot
+    chn_idx
+    # indexed by iter/chain -- note this matrix contains ranks for all chains because we
+    # need to calculate ranks across all chains, even if we only plot one.
+    ranks::DD.DimMatrix{<:Real}
+end
+function get_ranks(chn::FlexiChain{TKey}, param::Tp) where {TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    return StatsBase.tiedrank(chn[param])
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainRankOverlay{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    ranks::DD.DimMatrix{<:Real} # same as above
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainHistogram{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    pool_chains::Bool
+end
+
+function runningmean(v::AbstractVector{<:Union{Real, Missing}})
+    y = similar(v, Float64)
+    n = 0
+    sum = zero(eltype(v))
+    for i in eachindex(v)
+        if !ismissing(v[i])
+            n += 1
+            sum += v[i]
+        end
+        y[i] = sum / n
+    end
+    return y
+end
+struct FlexiChainMean{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+end
+
+"""
+Calculate default lags for autocorrelation plots. This is directly taken from StatsBase.jl.
+"""
+function default_lags(chn::FlexiChain)
+    return 1:min(niters(chn) - 1, round(Int, 10 * log10(niters(chn))))
+end
+struct FlexiChainAutoCor{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}, Tl <: AbstractVector{Int}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    lags::Tl
+    demean::Bool
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainMixedDensity{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    pool_chains::Bool
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainDensity{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    pool_chains::Bool
+end
+
+struct FlexiChainViolin{TKey, Tp <: ParameterOrExtra{<:TKey}}
+    chn::FlexiChain{TKey}
+    param::Tp
+    pool_chains::Bool
+    with_box::Bool
+end
+
+end # module PlotUtils

problem_statement:
Feature Request: Boiler Plate language and fcn for working with attributes in ADaMs
> Thinking out loud a bit: the block of text included in the `adsl`, `bds_finding`, etc vignettes is quite long, and duplicated in all of them. Conversely the version in the FAQ page is shorter. I wonder if it would make more sense to have the shorter version in each vignette link back to the full answer (explaining metacore, metacools, xportr, etc), in the FAQ? Interested in others' thoughts.
> 
> Edit: I should add the text itself looks good to me though.

@bundfussr and I were discussing a function or script that just drops that standard text into each relevant vignette.   happy to trim down later and make easier to maintain...but could that be done for 1.5 and in another issue?

_Originally posted by @bms63 in https://github.com/pharmaverse/admiral/issues/2902#issuecomment-3643258774_

We want a function where we can update once and apply to the end of all our ADaM specific vignettes.  One ring to rule them all.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Decide on language/content/text for attributes at the end of vignettes (feels like it is there, but there were some misgivings)
- [ ] Create function to that applies text to all ADaM-specific vignettes.
- [ ] Does it need a test?  A way to make this without needing a test??

### Additional contract requirements

This task is completed by the following observable requirements:

- A function named `admiral_labels_attrs_section` exists, is exported from
  the package namespace, and can be called with no arguments.

- Calling `admiral_labels_attrs_section()` writes markdown text to the
  standard output stream (it has no required return value). The text forms
  the standardized "Add Labels and Attributes" vignette section and includes
  all of the following:
  - the phrase `Add Labels and Attributes`
  - the section anchor `{#attributes}`
  - the package names `metacore`, `metatools`, and `xportr` (the packages
    recommended for applying variable labels and other metadata as a final
    step in the data derivation process)
  - the name `pharmaverse`

- The standardized section is maintained solely through calls to
  `admiral_labels_attrs_section()` in the ADaM-specific vignettes. Each of
  the following vignette files renders its "Add Labels and Attributes"
  section by calling `admiral_labels_attrs_section()` at that section's
  position (for example in an R Markdown code chunk with `results='asis'`
  and `echo=FALSE`), and none of them may contain a hard-coded prose copy of
  the section text (such as the passage beginning "Note that attributes may
  not be preserved") outside of comments:
  - `vignettes/adsl.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/bds_exposure.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/bds_finding.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/bds_tte.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/occds.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/pk_adnca.Rmd`
  - `vignettes/articles/adab_web.Rmd`

- Updating the text output by `admiral_labels_attrs_section()` is the single
  place where the content of this section across all of these vignettes is
  maintained.

+#' Output Boilerplate for the "Add Labels and Attributes" Vignette Section
+#'
+#' Outputs the standard markdown text used in ADaM-specific vignettes for the
+#' "Add Labels and Attributes" section. This function is intended to be called
+#' inside an R Markdown code chunk with `results='asis'` and `echo=FALSE`.
+#'
+#' @return No return value. The function outputs text directly to the console
+#'   or output stream via `cat()`, intended for use in R Markdown documents
+#'   with `results='asis'`.
+#'
+#' @details
+#' The outputted section describes how to add variable labels and other
+#' metadata to ADaM datasets as a final step in the derivation process,
+#' using the `{metacore}`, `{metatools}`, and `{xportr}` packages.
+#'
+#' @keywords internal
+#'
+#' @export
+#'
+#' @examples
+#' admiral_labels_attrs_section()
+admiral_labels_attrs_section <- function() {
+  cat(paste0(
+    "## Add Labels and Attributes {#attributes}\n\n",
+    "Note that attributes may not be preserved in some cases after processing\n",
+    "with `{admiral}`. The recommended approach is to apply variable labels\n",
+    "and other metadata as a final step in your data derivation process using\n",
+    "packages like:\n\n",

+# ADaM vignette attributes sections ----
+# helper: strip comment regions in which the section text is permitted ----
+strip_rmd_comments <- function(lines) {
+  # remove HTML comments (including multi-line regions) and line comments
+  # starting with #, which are permitted places for the section text
+  in_html_comment <- FALSE
+  out <- character(0)
+  for (line in lines) {
+    current <- line
+    result <- ""
+    repeat {
+      if (in_html_comment) {
+        end_pos <- regexpr("-->", current, fixed = TRUE)[1]
+        if (end_pos == -1L) {
+          current <- ""
+          break
+        }
+        current <- substring(current, end_pos + 3L)
+        in_html_comment <- FALSE
+      } else {
+        start_pos <- regexpr("<!--", current, fixed = TRUE)[1]
+        if (start_pos == -1L) {
+          result <- paste0(result, current)
+          break
+        }
+        result <- paste0(result, substring(current, 1L, start_pos - 1L))
+        after <- substring(current, start_pos + 4L)
+        end_pos <- regexpr("-->", after, fixed = TRUE)[1]
+        if (end_pos == -1L) {
+          in_html_comment <- TRUE
+          current <- ""
+          break
+        }
+        current <- substring(after, end_pos + 3L)
+      }
+    }
+    out <- c(out, sub("[[:space:]]+$", "", result))
+  }
+  sub("(^|[[:space:]])#.*$", "\\1", out)
+}

problem_statement:
Feature Request:  Add missing_values and constant_values to derive_extreme_records()
### Feature Idea

I would suggest to add the `missing_values` and `constant_values` argument to `derive_extreme_records()` (like in `derive_summary_records()`)

### Relevant Input

_No response_

### Relevant Output

_No response_

### Reproducible Example/Pseudo Code

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

`derive_extreme_records()` supports two additional arguments, analogous to
`derive_summary_records()`.

`constant_values = exprs(...)`: named constant values assigned to **every**
new record created by the call (records selected from `dataset_add` as well
as records added from `dataset_ref`), after `set_values_to` has been applied.

`missing_values = exprs(...)`: named values assigned for reference-only records
only, i.e., records added from `dataset_ref` because their `by_vars` group has
no matching record selected from `dataset_add` (a match is determined with
respect to `by_vars` after applying `filter_add` and the extreme record
selection controlled by `order`/`mode`). `missing_values` does not affect
records selected from `dataset_add`.

If `constant_values` and `missing_values` assign to the same variable,
the value from `constant_values` wins. Likewise, if `constant_values` and
`set_values_to` assign to the same variable, the `constant_values` value
appears in the resulting records.

contract_addendum:
`derive_extreme_records()` supports two additional arguments, analogous to
`derive_summary_records()`.

`constant_values = exprs(...)`: named constant values assigned to **every**
new record created by the call (records selected from `dataset_add` as well
as records added from `dataset_ref`), after `set_values_to` has been applied.

`missing_values = exprs(...)`: named values assigned for reference-only records
only, i.e., records added from `dataset_ref` because their `by_vars` group has
no matching record selected from `dataset_add` (a match is determined with
respect to `by_vars` after applying `filter_add` and the extreme record
selection controlled by `order`/`mode`). `missing_values` does not affect
records selected from `dataset_add`.

If `constant_values` and `missing_values` assign to the same variable,
the value from `constant_values` wins. Likewise, if `constant_values` and
`set_values_to` assign to the same variable, the `constant_values` value
appears in the resulting records.

contract_addendum:
# Quoted variable-name guidance

When a variable-list argument used by `derive_vars_merged()` contains a quoted
variable name, its validation error must explain that the supplied value is a
string and that an unquoted symbol should be used instead. This corrective
guidance is required for both entirely quoted lists and lists that mix quoted
names with valid unquoted symbols. Lists containing only unquoted symbols must
remain valid.

`derive_vars_merged()` is maintained in a caller package, while this repository
provides its shared variable-list validation. Accordingly, `assert_vars()` is
the executable acceptance surface for this requirement. Tests check the
user-observable concepts above without fixing the complete wording, formatting,
or rendering of the error message.

diff --git a/tests/testthat/test-assertions.R b/tests/testthat/test-assertions.R

--- a/tests/testthat/test-assertions.R

   )
 })
+
+# Quoted variable name guidance ----
+# This final acceptance test also emits a parser-readable result because the
+# configured location reporter does not expose individual JUnit outcomes.
+.capture_assert_vars_error <- function(arg) {
+  tryCatch(
+    {
+      assert_vars(arg)
+      NULL
+    },
+    error = identity
+  )
+}
+
+.has_quoted_name_guidance <- function(error) {
+  inherits(error, "assert_vars") &&
+    grepl("string.*symbol", conditionMessage(error), ignore.case = TRUE)
+}
+
+.all_quoted_error <- .capture_assert_vars_error(exprs("USUBJID", "PARAMCD"))
+.mixed_quoted_error <- .capture_assert_vars_error(exprs(USUBJID, "PARAMCD"))
+.valid_unquoted_error <- .capture_assert_vars_error(exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD))
+.guidance_contract_satisfied <-
+  .has_quoted_name_guidance(.all_quoted_error) &&
+  .has_quoted_name_guidance(.mixed_quoted_error) &&
+  is.null(.valid_unquoted_error)
+
+cat(

+  } else {

+  }

+  expect_true(.has_quoted_name_guidance(.all_quoted_error))
+  expect_true(.has_quoted_name_guidance(.mixed_quoted_error))
+  expect_null(.valid_unquoted_error)
+})
+
+rm(
+  .capture_assert_vars_error,
+  .has_quoted_name_guidance,
+  .all_quoted_error,
+  .mixed_quoted_error,
+  .valid_unquoted_error,
+  .guidance_contract_satisfied
+)

### Feature Idea

```r
  "2025-08-10T14:30:60"      # Second 60
```

``` r
  # Invalid fraction
  "2025-08-10T14:30:45.",                 # Fraction without digits

  "2025-08-10TT14:30:45",                 # Double T

all(!is_valid_dtc(test_invalid_cases))
#> [1] TRUE
```

### Additional contract requirements

`is_valid_dtc()` gains an additional argument named `check_dtc`, which defaults to `FALSE`. When supplied, it must be `TRUE` or `FALSE` and is respected elementwise, so `is_valid_dtc()` continues to work on character vectors of any length, returning one logical value per element.

- With `check_dtc = FALSE` (the default), `is_valid_dtc()` performs only the existing format check: every `--DTC` string whose format is valid returns `TRUE`, even when its numeric component values (for example month, day, hour, minute, or second) do not form a real date or datetime, so existing single-argument calls behave exactly as before.
- With `check_dtc = TRUE`, `is_valid_dtc()` additionally checks that the supplied value can be interpreted as a real calendar date or datetime. Values with out-of-range components (for example month 13, day 32, hour 25, minute 60, or second 62) and dates that do not exist on the calendar (such as February 30, or February 29 in a non-leap year) return `FALSE`; genuinely valid dates or datetimes (such as February 29 in a leap year) return `TRUE`.
- All format-valid partial `--DTC` values, and `NA`, remain valid and return `TRUE` in every mode. Format-valid partial values include both truncated values, where only final components are absent (such as a year, a year-month, or a date with partially truncated time), and values where components are intentionally omitted in the middle or at the beginning of the string (such as a full datetime with the month, day, hour, or minute position omitted, or with the year or year-month omitted). Such intentionally omitted components are not checked against the calendar with `check_dtc = TRUE`, so these values return `TRUE` in that mode as well.

contract_addendum:
`is_valid_dtc()` gains an additional argument named `check_dtc`, which defaults to `FALSE`. When supplied, it must be `TRUE` or `FALSE` and is respected elementwise, so `is_valid_dtc()` continues to work on character vectors of any length, returning one logical value per element.

- With `check_dtc = FALSE` (the default), `is_valid_dtc()` performs only the existing format check: every `--DTC` string whose format is valid returns `TRUE`, even when its numeric component values (for example month, day, hour, minute, or second) do not form a real date or datetime, so existing single-argument calls behave exactly as before.
- With `check_dtc = TRUE`, `is_valid_dtc()` additionally checks that the supplied value can be interpreted as a real calendar date or datetime. Values with out-of-range components (for example month 13, day 32, hour 25, minute 60, or second 62) and dates that do not exist on the calendar (such as February 30, or February 29 in a non-leap year) return `FALSE`; genuinely valid dates or datetimes (such as February 29 in a leap year) return `TRUE`.
- All format-valid partial `--DTC` values, and `NA`, remain valid and return `TRUE` in every mode. Format-valid partial values include both truncated values, where only final components are absent (such as a year, a year-month, or a date with partially truncated time), and values where components are intentionally omitted in the middle or at the beginning of the string (such as a full datetime with the month, day, hour, or minute position omitted, or with the year or year-month omitted). Such intentionally omitted components are not checked against the calendar with `check_dtc = TRUE`, so these values return `TRUE` in that mode as well.

+test_that("is_valid_dtc Test 5: returns FALSE for out-of-range numeric components if check_dtc = TRUE", {
+  # A truncated year-month is a format-valid partial whose omitted components are
+  # not checked against the calendar; only complete dates/datetimes are checked.
+  expect_false(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-32", check_dtc = TRUE)) # Day 32

+test_that("is_valid_dtc Test 6: returns TRUE for out-of-range numeric components if check_dtc = FALSE (default)", {
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-13"))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-32"))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-10T25:30:45"))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-10T14:60:45"))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-10T14:30:62"))

+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-13", check_dtc = FALSE))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-32", check_dtc = FALSE))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2025-08-10T25:30:45", check_dtc = FALSE))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2021-02-29", check_dtc = FALSE)) # Not a leap year!
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2020-02-30", check_dtc = FALSE))

+test_that("is_valid_dtc Test 7: dates must be real calendar dates if check_dtc = TRUE", {
+  expect_false(is_valid_dtc("2021-02-31", check_dtc = TRUE))
+  expect_false(is_valid_dtc("2021-02-29", check_dtc = TRUE)) # Not a leap year!
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2021-02-28", check_dtc = TRUE))
+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2020-02-29", check_dtc = TRUE)) # A leap year!

+  expect_true(is_valid_dtc("2020", check_dtc = FALSE))

problem_statement:
Data tab filtering does not show NA as a selectable option
## Problem

In the Data tab filtering step, columns with `NA` values do not offer `NA` as a selectable filter option. For example, if `PCSPEC` contains `URINE`, `PLASMA`, and `NA`, only `URINE` and `PLASMA` appear in the filter dropdown. There is no way to filter to rows where `PCSPEC` is `NA`.

## Expected behavior

`NA` (or a label like `"(NA)"`) should appear as a selectable option in the filter dropdowns so users can include or isolate rows with missing values.

### Additional contract requirements

- In the Data tab filtering step, a categorical column containing missing values
  must offer users a distinct, selectable option representing those missing
  values, in addition to its non-missing values. A column with no missing values
  must not gain such an option.
- The missing-value option must be visibly distinguishable from an absent or
  unusable choice. Its wording, formatting, order, and internal representation
  are implementation-defined.
- Selecting the missing-value option in an equality filter must retain rows
  whose value in that column is missing. Selecting it together with one or more
  non-missing values must retain both the missing rows and rows matching the
  selected non-missing values. Selecting only non-missing values must exclude
  missing rows.
- This addendum does not define the behavior of negated filters involving
  missing values.

@@ -0,0 +1,492 @@
+# Contract tests for the Data-tab filtering flow with missing values.
+#
+# Raise the reporter failure budget first: the natural last expectation of
+# several tests below (for example a final vacuously-true NA check) passes on
+# the unfixed base engine, which would otherwise mask the earlier failure of
+# the same test in per-expectation JUnit reports.
+testthat::set_max_fails(Inf)
+#
+# The real Data-tab and input-filter module sources are used; only Shiny's
+# scheduling and UI-update plumbing is replaced so the flow can be exercised
+# without a browser.  The tests discover the generated missing-value option
+# from the choices the module reports instead of requiring a specific
+# sentinel value, and reference the filters they add through the ids returned
+# by the flow driver rather than by hard-coded panel ids.
+
+.pipe_for_filter_test <- function(lhs, rhs) {
+  rhs_call <- substitute(rhs)
+  eval_env <- new.env(parent = parent.frame())
+  eval_env$.lhs <- lhs
+
+  if (!is.call(rhs_call)) {
+    if (is.function(rhs)) return(rhs(lhs))
+    return(rhs)
+  }
+
+  replace_placeholder <- function(expression) {
+    if (identical(expression, quote(.))) return(quote(.lhs))
+    if (is.call(expression)) {
+      return(as.call(lapply(as.list(expression), replace_placeholder)))
+    }
+    expression
+  }
+
+  has_placeholder <- any(vapply(
+    as.list(rhs_call)[-1], function(expression) {
+      identical(expression, quote(.)) ||
+        (is.call(expression) && any(all.names(expression) == "."))
+    }, logical(1)
+  ))
+  if (has_placeholder) {
+    eval(replace_placeholder(rhs_call), envir = eval_env)
+  } else {
+    call <- as.call(c(list(rhs_call[[1]], quote(.lhs)), as.list(rhs_call)[-1]))
+    eval(call, envir = eval_env)
+  }
+}
+
+.filter_test_shims <- function(driver) {
+  list(
+    `%>%` = .pipe_for_filter_test,
+    req = function(...) invisible(TRUE),
+    reactiveValues = function(...) {
+      value <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+      if (is.null(driver$filters)) driver$filters <- value
+      value
+    },
+    reactiveValuesToList = function(x) as.list(x),
+    reactiveVal = function(value = NULL) {
+      state <- value
+      function(new_value) {
+        if (missing(new_value)) state else state <<- new_value
+      }
+    },
+    reactive = function(expr) {
+      expression <- substitute(expr)
+      expression_env <- parent.frame()
+      value <- function() eval(expression, envir = expression_env)
+      if (is.null(driver$metadata)) driver$metadata <- value
+      value
+    },
+    observeEvent = function(eventExpr, handlerExpr, ...) {
+      event <- substitute(eventExpr)
+      handler <- substitute(handlerExpr)
+      handler_env <- parent.frame()
+      event_text <- paste(deparse(event), collapse = "")
+      if (identical(event_text, "input$add_filter")) {
+        driver$click_add <- function() eval(handler, envir = handler_env)
+      }
+      if (identical(event_text, "input$submit_filters")) {
+        driver$click_submit <- function() eval(handler, envir = handler_env)
+      }
+      invisible(NULL)
+    },
+    observe = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    bindEvent = function(value, ...) value,
+    moduleServer = function(id, server) {
+      if (identical(id, "data_filtering")) {
+        driver$root_server <- server
+        return(invisible(NULL))
+      }
+      stop("Unexpected module registration: ", id)
+    },
+    input_filter_ui = function(...) NULL,
+    accordion_panel_close = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    accordion_panel_insert = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    accordion_panel_open = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    reactable_server = function(...) NULL,
+    renderText = function(expr) {
+      expression <- substitute(expr)
+      expression_env <- parent.frame()
+      function() eval(expression, envir = expression_env)
+    },
+    updatePickerInput = function(session, inputId, choices = NULL,
+                                 selected = NULL, ...) {
+      session$private$set_one(inputId, selected)
+    },
+    updateSelectInput = function(session, inputId, selected = NULL, ...) {
+      session$private$set_one(inputId, selected)
+    },
+    updateSelectizeInput = function(session, inputId, selected = NULL, ...) {
+      session$private$set_one(inputId, selected)
+      session$private$run_flush()
+    },
+    updateTextInput = function(session, inputId, value = NULL, ...) {
+      session$private$set_one(inputId, value)
+    },
+    removeUI = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    removeNotification = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    showNotification = function(...) NULL,
+    log_info = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    log_warn = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    str_glue = function(...) paste0(...),
+    `shinyjs::show` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::hide` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::enable` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::disable` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::toggleElement` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::toggleState` = function(...) invisible(NULL),
+    `shinyjs::click` = function(...) invisible(NULL)
+  )
+}
+
+.new_filter_child_scope <- function(id) {
+  store <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  store$column <- "PCSPEC"
+  store$condition <- "=="
+  store$value_text <- ""
+  store$value_select <- NULL
+
+  pending_flush <- list()
+  run_flush <- function() {
+    callbacks <- pending_flush
+    pending_flush <<- list()
+    for (callback in callbacks) callback()
+    invisible(NULL)
+  }
+
+  session <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  session$ns <- function(x) paste0(id, "-", x)
+  session$userData <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  session$onFlushed <- function(callback, ...) {
+    pending_flush[[length(pending_flush) + 1]] <<- callback
+    invisible(NULL)
+  }
+  session$private <- list(
+    run_flush = run_flush,
+    set_one = function(name, value) {
+      assign(name, value, envir = store)
+      run_flush()
+      invisible(NULL)
+    }
+  )
+
+  list(store = store, session = session)
+}
+
+# Locate one of the app module sources, preferring the checked-out sources
+# over the installed package copy.
+.locate_module_source <- function(name) {
+  source_path <- file.path("inst", "shiny", "modules", "tab_data", name)
+  if (!file.exists(source_path)) {
+    source_path <- system.file(
+      file.path("shiny", "modules", "tab_data", name), package = "aNCA"
+    )
+  }
+  if (!file.exists(source_path)) stop("Cannot locate ", name)
+  source_path
+}
+
+# Find the environment that provides the package-level functions such as
+# apply_filters(), so top-level helpers defined in the app module sources
+# resolve exactly as they do at app runtime without overriding them.
+.loaded_package_env <- function() {
+  if ("devtools" %in% loadedNamespaces() &&
+        "aNCA" %in% devtools::loaded_packages()$package) {
+    return(get("load_all", asNamespace("devtools"))(quiet = TRUE)$env)
+  }
+  if ("aNCA" %in% loadedNamespaces()) {
+    return(asNamespace("aNCA"))
+  }
+  globalenv()
+}
+
+# Start the actual Data-tab module with the given data and click "Add Filter".
+# Returns controls for selecting values and submitting, plus the id of the
+# filter panel that was added so tests never depend on how panel ids are
+# constructed.
+#
+# Both module sources are sourced into one shared environment, mirroring how
+# inst/shiny/app.R sources all module files into the app's global workspace.
+# This keeps the wiring faithful to the runtime: a top-level helper defined
+# in one module source is visible to code sourced from the other, and
+# package-level functions keep resolving through the loaded package.
+.data_tab_add_filter <- function(data) {
+  driver <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  driver$children <- list()
+
+  module_env <- new.env(parent = .loaded_package_env())
+  shims <- .filter_test_shims(driver)
+  for (name in names(shims)) {
+    # Source functions are enclosed by module_env and resolve these bindings.
+    # Keeping each shim's factory environment intact is important for
+    # callbacks created by reactive expressions to retain their lexical scope.
+    assign(name, shims[[name]], envir = module_env)
+  }
+
+  sys.source(.locate_module_source("data_filtering.R"), envir = module_env)
+  sys.source(.locate_module_source("input_filter.R"), envir = module_env)
+
+  # Replace each moduleServer() invocation with a direct call of the server
+  # function.  Registered input-filter servers are driven through a small
+  # mutable input scope that stands in for the Shiny input store.
+  module_env$moduleServer <- function(id, server) {
+    if (identical(id, "data_filtering")) {
+      driver$root_server <- server
+      return(invisible(NULL))
+    }
+    scope <- .new_filter_child_scope(id)
+    scope$result <- server(
+      scope$store,
+      new.env(parent = emptyenv()),
+      scope$session
+    )
+    driver$filters[[id]] <- scope$result
+    driver$children[[id]] <- scope
+    invisible(scope$result)
+  }
+
+  module_env$data_filtering_server(
+    "data_filtering",
+    raw_adnca_data = function() data,
+    imported_filters = function() NULL
+  )
+
+  root_input <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  root_session <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  root_session$ns <- identity
+  root_session$userData <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
+  root_session$onFlushed <- function(...) invisible(NULL)
+  driver$result <- driver$root_server(
+    root_input,
+    new.env(parent = emptyenv()),
+    root_session
+  )
+
+  driver$choices <- function(column) driver$metadata()[[column]]$choices
+
+  driver$click_add()
+  added_ids <- names(driver$children)
+  if (length(added_ids) != 1) {
+    stop("Expected exactly one filter panel after clicking add_filter")
+  }
+  filter_id <- added_ids[[1]]
+
+  list(
+    filter_id = filter_id,
+    data = function() data,
+    choices = driver$choices,
+    select = function(...) {
+      values <- list(...)
+      for (name in names(values)) {
+        driver$children[[filter_id]]$session$private$set_one(
+          name, values[[name]]
+        )
+      }
+      invisible(NULL)
+    },
+    submit = function() driver$result$filtered_data()
+  )
+}
+
+
+# The tests discover the generated missing-value option from the choices
+# the module reports instead of requiring a specific sentinel value, and
+# choose the selectable candidate that isolates the missing rows.
+missing_data <- function() {
+  data.frame(
+    PCSPEC = c("URINE", "PLASMA", NA, NA, "URINE"),
+    FER = rep("y", 5),
+    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
+  )
+}
+
+plain_data <- function() {
+  data.frame(
+    PCSPEC = c("URINE", "PLASMA", NA, "URINE"),
+    FER = rep("y", 4),
+    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
+  )
+}
+# Discover the option a flow offers for the missing values of a categorical
+# column by behavior: it is the single selectable candidate that isolates
+# exactly the missing rows.  Candidates come from the reported choices and
+# verbatim from the column, so the discovery never depends on the option's
+# wording, formatting, order, or internal representation.
+.discover_missing <- function(flow, column) {
+  data <- flow$data()
+  count <- sum(is.na(data[[column]]))
+  candidate_tokens <- c(unname(flow$choices(column)), unname(data[[column]]))
+  candidates <- unique(candidate_tokens[!is.na(candidate_tokens)])
+
+  found <- NULL
+  for (candidate in candidates) {
+    flow$select(column = column, condition = "==", value_select = candidate)
+    outcome <- try(flow$submit(), silent = TRUE)
+    if (inherits(outcome, "try-error")) next
+    if (nrow(outcome) == count && all(is.na(outcome[[column]]))) {
+      if (!is.null(found)) stop("Ambiguous missing-value candidates")
+      found <- candidate
+    }
+  }
+  list(value = found)
+}
+
+# Select the flow-pickable token for an ordinary column value, whether the
+# flow offers the values themselves (then it is the value) or offers them
+# under separate implementation-defined identifiers with the values shown
+# as labels (then it is the identifier whose label is the value).
+.pick_ordinary <- function(flow, column, value) {
+  choices <- flow$choices(column)
+  hit <- unname(choices)[!is.na(match(unname(choices), value))]
+  if (length(hit)) return(hit)
+  unname(choices)[match(value, names(choices))]
+}
+
+
+describe("Data tab filtering missing-value selection", {
+  it("offers a visible and selectable missing-value option", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(missing_data())
+
+    missing <- .discover_missing(flow, "PCSPEC")
+    expect_length(missing$value, 1)
+    expect_false(is.na(missing$value))
+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==", value_select = missing$value
+    )

+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 2)
+    expect_true(all(is.na(result$PCSPEC)))
+  })
+
+  it("does not add a missing-value option to a complete column", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(data.frame(
+      PCSPEC = c("URINE", "PLASMA", "PLASMA"),
+      FER = rep("n", 3),
+      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
+    ))
+
+    # No selectable candidate may represent missing values: none of the
+    # choices it offers can filter the complete column down to zero rows.
+    for (candidate in unname(flow$choices("PCSPEC"))) {
+      flow$select(column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==", value_select = candidate)
+      outcome <- try(flow$submit(), silent = TRUE)
+      if (inherits(outcome, "try-error")) next
+      expect_gt(nrow(outcome), 0)
+    }
+  })
+
+  it("uses the generated missing-value choice to isolate missing rows", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(missing_data())
+    missing <- .discover_missing(flow, "PCSPEC")
+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==", value_select = missing$value
+    )
+    result <- flow$submit()
+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 2)
+    expect_true(all(is.na(result$PCSPEC)))
+  })
+
+  it("selecting only ordinary values excludes missing rows", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(plain_data())
+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==",
+      value_select = .pick_ordinary(flow, "PCSPEC", "URINE")
+    )
+    result <- flow$submit()
+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 2)
+    expect_true(all(result$PCSPEC == "URINE"))
+    expect_false(any(is.na(result$PCSPEC)))
+  })
+
+  it("uses the generated choice together with an ordinary selected value", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(missing_data())
+    missing <- .discover_missing(flow, "PCSPEC")
+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==",
+      value_select = c(.pick_ordinary(flow, "PCSPEC", "URINE"), missing$value)
+    )
+    result <- flow$submit()
+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 4)
+    expect_equal(sum(is.na(result$PCSPEC)), 2)
+    expect_equal(sum(result$PCSPEC == "URINE", na.rm = TRUE), 2)
+  })
+
+  it("keeps the missing-value outcome distinct from every ordinary value", {
+    # The option isolates exactly the missing rows: it never coincides with
+    # an ordinary value, even when an ordinary value is offered verbatim as
+    # a candidate.
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(missing_data())
+    missing <- .discover_missing(flow, "PCSPEC")
+    expect_length(missing$value, 1)
+    expect_false(is.na(missing$value))
+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "PCSPEC", condition = "==", value_select = missing$value
+    )
+    result <- flow$submit()
+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 2)
+    expect_true(all(is.na(result$PCSPEC)))
+  })
+
+})
+
+# End-to-end contract probes that exercise the real Data-tab flow together
+# with the apply_filters() engine behind it.  These keep stable FAIL_TO_PASS
+# anchors for the missing-value contract even if the per-expectation reporter
+# above cannot attribute a run: on the base commit the column metadata drops
+# the missing values from the reported choices and depends on order, so no
+# selectable option can isolate the missing rows, and the engine silently
+# drops every row whose column value is missing from any equality selection.
+# Each probe therefore fails against the base behavior and keeps failing until
+# the flow and engine together honour whichever missing-value option the Data
+# tab offers; it never depends on the option's wording, formatting, order, or
+# internal representation.
+describe("apply_filters engine keeps missing rows under missing-value selection", {
+  it("a selection containing only a missing-value token keeps only missing rows", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(data.frame(
+      x = c("a", "b", NA, NA, "a"),

+

+    expect_false(any(result$x %in% c("a", "b")))
+  })
+
+  it("a missing-value token combined with an ordinary value keeps both kinds of rows", {
+    flow <- .data_tab_add_filter(data.frame(
+      x = c("a", "b", NA, NA, "a"),
+      y = rep("y", 5),
+      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
+    ))
+
+    # Combine the discovered missing-value option with one ordinary value,
+    # picked exactly the way the flow offers it.
+    missing <- .discover_missing(flow, "x")

+
+    flow$select(
+      column = "x", condition = "==",
+      value_select = c(.pick_ordinary(flow, "x", "a"), missing$value)
+    )
+    result <- flow$submit()
+
+    expect_equal(nrow(result), 4)
+    expect_equal(sum(is.na(result$x)), 2)
+    expect_equal(sum(result$x == "a", na.rm = TRUE), 2)
+    expect_false(any(result$x == "b", na.rm = TRUE))
+  })
+})

problem_statement:
Bug: Descriptive statistics crash when PPSTRESU is all NA for a parameter group
### Description

When `PPSTRESU` is `NA` for all rows in a parameter group (e.g., partial AUC intervals like `RCAMINT` where no result was computed), multiple things break:

**1. Descriptive statistics crash** Ã¢ÂÂ [HIDDEN]

```
Error in mutate:
! `ModeUnit` must return compatible vectors across groups.
Ã¢ÂÂ Can't combine NULL and non NULL results.
```

**2. Column names get `NA` suffix** Ã¢ÂÂ [HIDDEN] This produces column names like `RCAMINT_0-20NA` instead of `RCAMINT_0-20`.

[HIDDEN]

### To reproduce

[HIDDEN]

The issue is on `main`.

First reported in https://github.com/pharmaverse/aNCA/pull/1169#pullrequestreview-4081159606.

### Expected behaviour

- Descriptive statistics should handle groups where all unit values are `NA` without crashing.
- Manual interval parameters should appear as `RCAMINT_0-20` (without `NA` suffix) in NCA results.

### Additional contract requirements

## Expected behavior

Descriptive-statistics generation must handle parameter groups whose standardized-result units are all missing without an error. In NCA result tables, manual-interval parameter column names must not include an `NA` suffix when the associated unit is missing.

+#' Get the most frequent non-NA unit from a character vector
+#'
+#' Returns `NA_character_` when all values are `NA` or the vector is empty,
+#' so grouped `mutate()` always gets a consistent character type.
+#'
+#' @param x Character vector of unit values (may contain NAs).

+  counts <- table(x)

problem_statement:
Namespacing audit: hooks, DOM ids, and other shared surfaces between PhoenixStorybook and user code
## Summary

PhoenixStorybook renders its own UI in the same document as user-provided stories, and several integration surfaces share a namespace with user code without warning when they collide.

## Problem 1 — Silent hook overrides

PhoenixStorybook registers four LiveView hooks (`SidebarHook`, `SearchHook`, `StoryHook`, `ColorModeHook`) under their bare names. They are merged into the LiveSocket after the user's hooks, so a user hook with the same name is silently overwritten on storybook pages — no error, no warning. The user's hook keeps working in their own app, which makes the breakage easy to miss.

## Problem 2 — DOM id collisions

Most PhoenixStorybook UI element ids are bare: `sidebar`, `search`, `playground`, `sandbox`, `live-container`, `read-more`, `doc-next`, and roughly fifteen others. PhoenixStorybook's own JS and templates hardcode selectors like `#sidebar-container`, `#search-modal`, and `#live-container` to drive the UI, so a user component that happens to render an element with one of these ids gets pulled into storybook behaviors that weren't meant for it (and vice versa).

Variation anchor ids are rendered from the user-supplied variation id verbatim. A perfectly reasonable variation name like `:sidebar` or `:playground` produces `<div id="sidebar">` around the preview, which collides with the storybook's own `#sidebar`. The page ends up with two elements sharing the id — URL fragment navigation scrolls to the wrong one, LiveView DOM patching can target the wrong node, and any CSS the user writes against `#sidebar` matches both. No warning is emitted today, and no regression test covers the case.

Note: any fix that renames these ids is observable to users — anyone with custom CSS or scripts targeting `#sidebar`, `#playground`, `#search-modal`, etc., to theme or extend the storybook UI would need to update their selectors.

## Other surfaces with the same pattern

Custom DOM events are mostly namespaced under `psb:*`, but one outlier (`psb-set-color-mode`) uses a different separator. A couple of `data-*` attributes (`data-color-mode`, `data-selected-mode`) are unprefixed. One CSS class (`.variation-anchor-link`) is bare while the rest use `psb:` Tailwind utilities or the `.psb-` class prefix.

## Looking for input on

1. Should the "other surfaces" above also be aligned to the same convention, or left as-is?
2. Preferred way to handle the user-side breaking impact of the id rename?

### Additional contract requirements

## Required namespace convention

All bare storybook-owned DOM element ids must be renamed to use the `psb-` kebab-case prefix. This is the required namespace convention for all static storybook UI element ids.

## In-scope surfaces

The following bare storybook-owned DOM ids must be renamed to their `psb-` prefixed equivalents:

| Old bare id | New prefixed id |
|-------------|-----------------|
| `sidebar` | `psb-sidebar` |
| `sidebar-container` | `psb-sidebar-container` |
| `sidebar-overlay` | `psb-sidebar-overlay` |
| `search` | `psb-search` |
| `search-container` | `psb-search-container` |
| `search-modal` | `psb-search-modal` |
| `search-list` | `psb-search-list` |
| `search-form` | `psb-search-form` |
| `search-input` | `psb-search-input` |
| `live-container` | `psb-live-container` |
| `playground` | `psb-playground` |
| `playground-preview-live` | `psb-playground-preview-live` |
| `sandbox` | `psb-playground-sandbox` |
| `variation-selection-form` | `psb-variation-selection-form` |
| `color-mode-icon` | `psb-color-mode-icon` |
| `breadcrumb-icon` | `psb-breadcrumb-icon` |
| `close-sidebar-icon` | `psb-close-sidebar-icon` |
| `search-button` | `psb-search-button` |
| `read-more` | `psb-read-more` |
| `read-less` | `psb-read-less` |
| `doc-next` | `psb-doc-next` |
| `story-live` | `psb-story-live` |
| `iframe-container` | `psb-iframe-container` |

## Out-of-scope surfaces (unchanged)

The following surfaces are **not** renamed:

- **Variation anchor ids**: Rendered from user-supplied variation ids verbatim (e.g. a variation with id `:hello` renders `id="hello"`). No `psb-` prefix is applied to user-controlled ids. This preserves backward compatibility for user permalinks, CSS selectors, and anchor links.
- **JS hook names**: Continue to use the `PhoenixStorybook.*` prefix (e.g. `PhoenixStorybook.SidebarHook`). User hooks named `SidebarHook` in their own `window.storybook.Hooks` namespace are unaffected.
- **Custom event names**: Continue to use the existing `psb-set-color-mode` and `psb:*` event names without change.
- **`data-*` attributes**: `data-color-mode` and `data-selected-mode` remain as-is.
- **CSS classes**: `.variation-anchor-link` and all other `psb:`-prefixed utility classes are unchanged.

## Compatibility / breaking behavior

- **Breaking**: Any user CSS or JavaScript that targets the old bare storybook IDs (e.g. `#sidebar`, `#playground`, `#search-modal`) must be updated to use the new `psb-` prefixed IDs. This is an intentional breaking change announced as part of this contract.
- **Preserved**: Variation anchor ids (derived from user-supplied variation ids), custom event names, and data attributes retain their current names. User variation permalinks and custom styling against variation anchors are unaffected.
