+package com.uandcode.hilt.autobind.compiler.resolver.collectors
+
+import com.google.devtools.ksp.symbol.KSAnnotation
+import com.google.devtools.ksp.symbol.KSClassDeclaration
+import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.AnnotationSpec
+import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.toAnnotationSpec
+import com.squareup.kotlinpoet.ksp.toClassName
+import com.uandcode.hilt.autobind.compiler.AutoBindException
+import dagger.multibindings.ClassKey
+
+/**
+ * Detects the Dagger map key annotation on an annotated class and/or its alias.
+ *
+ * Detection works by finding any annotation whose own declaration is meta-annotated
+ * with `@dagger.MapKey`. This handles all key types uniformly: built-in
+ * (`@StringKey`, `@IntKey`, `@LongKey`, `@ClassKey`) and user-defined custom keys.
+ *
+ * When no key is found on either the class or the alias, falls back to generating
+ * `@ClassKey(AnnotatedClass::class)`.
+ */
+internal class MapKeyCollector {
+
+    /**
+     * Resolves the map key annotation spec for the given class and annotation source.
+     *
+     * When [annotationSource] == [annotatedClass] (direct annotation, no alias), only
+     * the class is scanned. When they differ (alias mode), both are scanned and checked
+     * for conflicts.
+     */
+    fun collect(
+        annotatedClass: KSClassDeclaration,
+        annotationSource: KSClassDeclaration,
+        originAnnotationName: String,
+    ): AnnotationSpec {
+        val classKeys = findMapKeyAnnotations(annotatedClass, originAnnotationName)
+        val aliasKeys = if (annotationSource != annotatedClass) {
+            findMapKeyAnnotations(annotationSource, originAnnotationName)
+        } else {
+            emptyList()
+        }
+
+        val classKey = classKeys.firstOrNull()
+        val aliasKey = aliasKeys.firstOrNull()
+
+        return when {
+            classKey == null && aliasKey == null -> buildClassKeyFallback(annotatedClass)
+            classKey != null && aliasKey == null -> classKey.toAnnotationSpec()
+            classKey == null && aliasKey != null -> aliasKey.toAnnotationSpec()
+            else -> {
+                val finalClassKey = classKey!!
+                val finalAliasKey = aliasKey!!
+                if (keysAreEqual(finalClassKey, finalAliasKey)) {
+                    finalClassKey.toAnnotationSpec()
+                } else {
+                    if (finalClassKey.shortName.asString() == finalAliasKey.shortName.asString()) {
+                        throw AutoBindException(
+                            "@$originAnnotationName: conflicting map keys: class and alias has " +
+                                    "keys of the same type, but with different values.",
+                            annotatedClass,
+                        )
+                    } else {
+                        throw AutoBindException(
+                            "@$originAnnotationName: conflicting map keys. Class has " +
+                                    "@${finalClassKey.shortName.asString()} but alias " +
+                                    "has @${finalAliasKey.shortName.asString()}.",
+                            annotatedClass,
+                        )
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun findMapKeyAnnotations(
+        classDeclaration: KSClassDeclaration,
+        originAnnotationName: String,
+    ): List<KSAnnotation> {
+        val found = classDeclaration.annotations
+            .filter { annotation ->
+                annotation.annotationType.resolve().declaration
+                    .annotations.any { it.shortName.asString() == MAP_KEY_ANNOTATION_NAME }
+            }
+            .toList()
+
+        if (found.size > 1) {
+            throw AutoBindException(
+                "@$originAnnotationName: only one @MapKey annotation is allowed, " +
+                    "but found: ${found.map { "@${it.shortName.asString()}" }}.",
+                classDeclaration,
+            )
+        }
+
+        return found
+    }
+
+    private fun keysAreEqual(a: KSAnnotation, b: KSAnnotation): Boolean {
+        if (a.annotationType.resolve() != b.annotationType.resolve()) return false
+        if (a.arguments.size != b.arguments.size) return false
+        val aArgs = a.arguments.associateBy { it.name?.asString() }
+        val bArgs = b.arguments.associateBy { it.name?.asString() }
+        return aArgs.keys == bArgs.keys && aArgs.all { (aKey, aValue) ->
+            bArgs[aKey]?.value == aValue.value
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun buildClassKeyFallback(annotatedClass: KSClassDeclaration): AnnotationSpec {
+        return AnnotationSpec.builder(ClassKey::class)
+            .addMember("value = %T::class", annotatedClass.toClassName())
+            .build()
+    }
+
+}
+
+private const val MAP_KEY_ANNOTATION_NAME = "MapKey"

+package com.uandcode.hilt.autobind
+
+import kotlin.reflect.KClass
+
+/**
+ * Generates a Dagger Hilt module that contributes the annotated class into a
+ * multibinding `Map` of each directly implemented interface.
+ *
+ * The annotated class must be a concrete, non-abstract class with a primary
+ * constructor annotated with `@Inject`, and must implement at least one interface.
+ *
+ * A map key annotation (meta-annotated with `@dagger.MapKey`) must be placed on
+ * the annotated class or its alias. If no key is provided, `@ClassKey` using the
+ * annotated class is used as a fallback.
+ *
+ * Example:
+ * ```
+ * @AutoBindsIntoMap
+ * @StringKey("logging")
+ * class LoggingInterceptor @Inject constructor() : Interceptor
+ * ```
+ * Generates:
+ * ```
+ * @Module
+ * @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
+ * internal interface LoggingInterceptor__IntoMapModule {
+ *     @Binds @IntoMap @StringKey("logging")
+ *     fun bindToInterceptor(impl: LoggingInterceptor): Interceptor
+ * }
+ * ```
+ *
+ * Can be combined with [AutoBinds] and [AutoBindsIntoSet] on the same class to produce
+ * a direct binding, a set contribution, and a map contribution simultaneously.
+ *
+ * @property installIn the Hilt component to install the generated module in.
+ *   Defaults to [HiltComponent.Unspecified], which auto-detects the component from
+ *   the scope annotation on the class (falls back to [HiltComponent.Singleton] if unscoped).
+ * @property bindTo explicit list of supertypes to contribute to. When non-empty, only the listed
+ *   types are used instead of all direct supertypes. Each type must be a transitive supertype
+ *   of the annotated class; a compile-time error is emitted otherwise.
+ */
+@Target(AnnotationTarget.CLASS, AnnotationTarget.ANNOTATION_CLASS)
+@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
+public annotation class AutoBindsIntoMap(
+    val installIn: HiltComponent = HiltComponent.Unspecified,
+    val bindTo: Array<KClass<*>> = [],
+)

+    private data class MapKey(val typeFqcn: String, val value: String)
+
+    private data class Binding(
+        val paramType: String,
+        val returnType: String,
+        val isIntoMap: Boolean,
+        val mapKeyType: String?,
+        val mapKeyValue: String?,
+    )
+
+    // region structural bytecode model
+
+    private inner class GeneratedScope(private val classFilesDir: File, val moduleNames: List<String>) {
+        fun mapModule(): ModuleModel {
+            val matching = moduleNames.filter { ModuleModel(classFilesDir, it).mapBindings().isNotEmpty() }
+            assertEquals(1, matching.size, "Expected exactly one generated module with an @IntoMap binding, got $matching among $moduleNames")
+            return ModuleModel(classFilesDir, matching.single())

+            val matching = moduleNames.filter { ModuleModel(classFilesDir, it).mapBindings().isEmpty() }
+            assertEquals(1, matching.size, "Expected exactly one generated module without an @IntoMap binding, got $matching among $moduleNames")
+            return ModuleModel(classFilesDir, matching.single())
+        }
+    }
+
+    private inner class ModuleModel(classFilesDir: File, val name: String) {
+        private val annotations = linkedMapOf<String, MutableMap<String, Any?>>()
+        private val methodBindings = mutableListOf<Binding>()
+
+        init {
+            val classFile = File(classFilesDir, name.replace('.', '/') + ".class")
+            if (classFile.isFile) {
+                parse(classFile)
+            }
+        }
+
+        private fun parse(classFile: File) {
+            ClassReader(classFile.readBytes()).accept(
+                object : ClassVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9) {
+                    override fun visitAnnotation(descriptor: String, visible: Boolean): AnnotationVisitor =
+                        collectAnnotation(descriptor, annotations)
+
+                    override fun visitMethod(
+                        access: Int,
+                        methodName: String,
+                        descriptor: String,
+                        signature: String?,
+                        exceptions: Array<out String>?,
+                    ): MethodVisitor {
+                        val methodAnnotations = linkedMapOf<String, MutableMap<String, Any?>>()
+                        return object : MethodVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9) {
+                            override fun visitAnnotation(desc: String, visible: Boolean): AnnotationVisitor =
+                                collectAnnotation(desc, methodAnnotations)
+
+                            override fun visitEnd() {
+                                val argumentTypes = Type.getArgumentTypes(descriptor).map { it.className }
+                                val returnType = Type.getReturnType(descriptor).className
+                                if (argumentTypes.size == 1 && methodAnnotations.containsKey("dagger.Binds")) {
+                                    val isIntoMap = methodAnnotations.containsKey("dagger.multibindings.IntoMap")
+                                    val keyEntry = if (isIntoMap) {
+                                        methodAnnotations.entries.firstOrNull { (key, _) ->
+                                            key != "dagger.Binds" && key != "dagger.multibindings.IntoMap" && key != "kotlin.Metadata"
+                                        }
+                                    } else {
+                                        null
+                                    }
+                                    methodBindings += Binding(
+                                        paramType = argumentTypes.single(),
+                                        returnType = returnType,
+                                        isIntoMap = isIntoMap,
+                                        mapKeyType = keyEntry?.key,
+                                        mapKeyValue = keyEntry?.value?.get("value")?.let { keyValue(it) },
+                                    )
+                                }
+                            }
+                        }
+                    }
+                },
+                ClassReader.SKIP_CODE or ClassReader.SKIP_DEBUG or ClassReader.SKIP_FRAMES,
+            )
+        }
+
+        private fun keyValue(value: Any?): String? = when (value) {
+            is String -> value
+            is Type -> value.className
+            else -> value?.toString()
+        }
+
+        fun mapBindings(): List<Binding> = methodBindings.filter { it.isIntoMap }
+
+        fun bindings(): List<Binding> = methodBindings
+
+        fun hasIntoMapBindingReturning(returnType: String): Boolean = mapBindings().any { it.returnType == returnType }

+        fun assertInstalledIn(componentFqcn: String) {
+            assertTrue(annotations.containsKey("dagger.Module"), "Expected module '$name' to be a dagger.Module")

+            assertNotNull(installIn, "Expected module '$name' to have dagger.hilt.InstallIn")

+                "Expected module '$name' to be installed in $componentFqcn, but it was installed in $componentNames",
+            )
+        }
+
+        fun assertBinding(paramType: String, returnType: String, mapKey: MapKey) {
+            val matching = mapBindings().filter { it.paramType == paramType && it.returnType == returnType }

+            )

+            assertEquals(mapKey.typeFqcn, binding.mapKeyType, "Map key type mismatch in module '$name'")

+        }
+    }

+    private fun collectAnnotation(descriptor: String, into: MutableMap<String, MutableMap<String, Any?>>): AnnotationVisitor {
+        val fqcn = Type.getType(descriptor).className
+        val members = into.getOrPut(fqcn) { linkedMapOf() }
+        return object : AnnotationVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9) {
+            override fun visit(name: String?, value: Any?) {
+                members[name ?: "value"] = value
+            }
+
+            override fun visitEnum(name: String?, descriptor: String, value: String) {
+                members[name ?: "value"] = value
+            }
+
+            override fun visitAnnotation(name: String?, descriptor: String): AnnotationVisitor {
+                val nested = linkedMapOf<String, MutableMap<String, Any?>>()
+                members[name ?: "value"] = nested
+                return collectAnnotation(descriptor, nested)
+            }
+
+            override fun visitArray(name: String?): AnnotationVisitor {
+                val values = mutableListOf<Any?>()
+                members[name ?: "value"] = values
+                return object : AnnotationVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9) {
+                    override fun visit(ignored: String?, value: Any?) {
+                        values += value
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    // endregion
+
+    private fun JvmCompilationResult.generatedScope(): GeneratedScope {
+        val classFilesDir = resolveClassesDir()
+        assertTrue(classFilesDir.isDirectory, "Compilation output directory $classFilesDir should exist")
+        val generatedSources = sourcesGeneratedBySymbolProcessor.filter { it.extension == "kt" }.toList()
+        assertTrue(generatedSources.isNotEmpty(), "Expected at least one generated Kotlin module source")
+        val moduleClassNames = generatedSources.mapNotNull { file -> parseModuleClassName(file, classFilesDir) }.toList()
+        assertTrue(moduleClassNames.isNotEmpty(), "Could not resolve any generated module class name")
+        return GeneratedScope(classFilesDir, moduleClassNames)
+    }
+
+    private fun JvmCompilationResult.resolveClassesDir(): File {
+        runCatching {
+            val dir = javaClass.getMethod("getOutputDirectory").invoke(this) as File
+            if (dir.isDirectory) return dir
+        }
+        runCatching {
+            val loader = javaClass.getMethod("getClassLoader").invoke(this)
+            if (loader is java.net.URLClassLoader && loader.urLs.isNotEmpty()) {
+                val dir = File(loader.urLs[0].toURI())
+                if (dir.isDirectory) return dir
+            }
+        }
+        error("Could not resolve the compilation output directory for the test compilation")
+    }
+
+    private fun parseModuleClassName(file: File, classFilesDir: File): String? {
+        val text = file.readText()
+        val packageName = Regex("""^\s*package\s+([\w.]+)""", RegexOption.MULTILINE)
+            .find(text)?.groupValues?.get(1) ?: return null
+        val typeNames = Regex(
+            """^\s*(?:@[A-Za-z_][\w.]*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*)*(?:(?:internal|public|private|protected|abstract|sealed|open|enum|annotation|data|value|fun)\s+)*(?:interface|class|object)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)""",
+            RegexOption.MULTILINE,
+        ).findAll(text).map { it.groupValues[1] }.toList()
+        return typeNames.firstOrNull { simple ->
+            File(classFilesDir, "$packageName.$simple".replace('.', '/') + ".class").isFile
+        }?.let { "$packageName.$it" }
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Function to create `packages.json` for existing universe
If you have packages on CRAN and already have a universe, but want to move toward having a custom universe, it'd be helpful to have a function to create a `packages.json` that's equivalent to the current universe to start the repo.

I used this code to create a `packages.json` for https://rstudio.r-universe.dev, which I think is mostly correct, or at least good enough to get me started.

```r
[HIDDEN]
```

### Additional contract requirements

The requested functionality must be delivered as a new publicly exported R function named `use_custom_manifest`.

Required interface:

- It accepts two arguments:
  - `universe`: the name of an existing universe (without the `.r-universe.dev` suffix), e.g. `"jeroen"`.
  - `path`: the file path to which the JSON manifest is written, defaulting to `"packages.json"`.

Required observable behavior:

- It queries the existing universe with that name (which is served at `https://<universe>.r-universe.dev`) and obtains the records for all of its packages.
- It writes a JSON file to `path` containing a top-level array with one object per package in the universe.
- Each entry is an object with exactly two keys, `package` and `url`, whose values are the package name and the URL of its remote repository obtained from the source universe, e.g. `{"package": "mypkg", "url": "https://github.com/owner/mypkg"}`.
- Names and URLs are written as plain JSON strings (scalars are not wrapped in arrays), and the file is written with two-space indentation so that it is human-readable and usable directly as a custom universe manifest.
- The function returns the path to the written file.

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+#' Create `packages.json` for existing universe
+#'
+#' @param universe Name of the universe, e.g. "jeroen"
+#' @param path Absolute path to which the JSON file could be saved.
+#'
+#' @returns The path to the JSON file it created.
+#'
+#' @export
+#' @examplesIf rlang::is_interactive()
+#' json_file <- withr::local_tempfile()
+#' use_custom_manifest("jeroen", json_file)
+#' file.edit(json_file)
+use_custom_manifest <- function(universe, path = "packages.json") {
+  universe::universe_all_packages(universe) |>
+    lapply(`[`, c("Package", "RemoteUrl")) |>
+    lapply(setNames, c("package", "url")) |>
+    jsonlite::write_json(path, pretty = 2, auto_unbox = TRUE)
+
+  path
+}

problem_statement:
Remove default backend (Enzyme) and make DI the main UI 
~~Given recent issues with Enzyme in #25 and newly discovered issues when HVPs are not analytically provided (except in trivially simple cases) Enzyme crashes on cuBLAS operations. Experiments with Mooncake are promising and seem to fix GPU related problems.~~

As a note, Reactant is also looking like a promising ultimate backend.

### Additional contract requirements

Supplementary test-contract requirements for this task:

- `ParallelMALASampler` requires an explicitly selected automatic-differentiation backend. There is no default backend: constructing the sampler without supplying the `backend` keyword argument fails.
- The `backend` keyword accepts Automatic Differentiation backend objects from the ADTypes.jl ecosystem, as used through the DifferentiationInterface.jl interface (for example a ForwardDiff-based backend or an Enzyme-based backend). Backends other than Enzyme are supported.
- When a `DensityModel` does not supply analytic Hessian-vector products, the sampler obtains the Hessian-vector products it needs by differentiating the model's supplied log-density/gradient with the explicitly selected backend through DifferentiationInterface.
- The DynamicPPL/Turing convenience constructor `DensityModel(turing_model::DynamicPPL.Model)` accepts an explicit AD backend selection through its AD-backend keyword argument, which accepts any ADTypes.jl backend usable for computing gradients of the wrapped DynamicPPL model (for example ForwardDiff). Test callers supply this backend explicitly; the constructor then wraps linked-space log-density, gradient, and parameter names so the model works with both samplers.
- No package-wide automated quality or static-analysis gates (such as Aqua or JET test suites) are part of the pass/fail contract for this task.

+# GPU Execution
+
+DEER's prefix-scan and per-step batch evaluations are array-type-agnostic, so the same `ParallelMALASampler` runs on either CPU or GPU.  This page covers when GPU pays off, the current limitations, and a worked example.
+
+---
+
+## When to use GPU
+
+GPU pays off when the per-Newton-step work i.e., evaluating `logdensity_batch` and `grad_logdensity_batch` across the `T`-wide trajectory and the Hutchinson `probes` is large enough to saturate the device.
+
+| Regime | Reach for |
+|---|---|
+| `D` ≲ a few hundred, lightweight `logp` | **CPU.** Per-step cost is dominated by overhead; GPU launch latency wins out. |
+| Large `D`, or `logp` is itself a batched linear-algebra / kernel workload | **GPU.** `T` × `probes` Jacobian work fills the device. |
+| Many independent chains via `MCMCThreads()` | **CPU**, scaled with threads.  GPU chains do not currently share a device pool. |
+
+A useful heuristic: if your CPU `grad_logdensity_batch` already saturates BLAS at the batch sizes DEER passes it (`T` columns, plus `probes` HVP probes), GPU is likely to help.  If not, profile before switching.
+
+---
+
+## Limitations
+
+### 1. DynamicPPL / Turing models are CPU-only
+
+The one-argument `DensityModel(::DynamicPPL.Model)` constructor (and the `LogDensityProblems` path that backs it) executes the model with `Vector{Float64}` parameters on CPU.  There is no path today that runs a `@model` against `CuArray` parameters.
+
+To run on GPU, hand-write `logdensity` / `grad_logdensity` (and the batched variants) directly over `CuArray`s and pass them to `DensityModel`.  This is shown in the example below.
+
+### 2. Enzyme on GPU currently needs `pmcmc_matmul` / `pmcmc_dot` / `pmcmc_dotsum`
+
+`ParallelMCMC` exports three thin wrappers:
+
+```julia
+pmcmc_matmul(A, B)  = A * B
+pmcmc_dot(a, b)     = dot(a, b)
+pmcmc_dotsum(A, B)  = sum(A .* B)
+```
+
+These exist purely so the package can register Enzyme rules against them without committing type piracy on `Base.*`, `Base.dot`, `Base.sum`.  The rules compute primal and cotangents with plain operators *outside* Enzyme's IR rewriter, which keeps them off the reverse-mode path that aborts on GPU.
+
+```
+unsupported tag gc-transition for
+  call i32 @cuMemcpyDtoHAsync_v2(...) [ "jl_roots"(...), "gc-transition"() ]
+UNREACHABLE executed at .../Enzyme/GradientUtils.cpp:309      (signal 6)
+```
+
+When you should use them:
+
+- You are on GPU **and** using `AutoEnzyme()` as the AD backend.
+
+When you do **not** need them:
+
+- CPU code: plain `*`, `dot`, `sum` are faster and clearer.
+- GPU code with `AutoMooncake(; config=nothing)`: Mooncake's own CUDA extension handles these operations natively.
+- GPU code with `AutoZygote()`: Zygote uses ChainRules adjoints, which have cuBLAS-backed rules for `*` / `dot` / `sum` on `CuArray`.
+
+These wrappers are a workaround pending upstream Enzyme support for GPU matmul rules.  Once that lands, plain `A * B` on `CuArray`s will work and the wrappers will be deprecated.
+
+### 3. Gradients must be written as single-op broadcasts, not fused expressions
+
+Enzyme on GPU can lower a single broadcast kernel at a time but aborts when a kernel fuses multiple operations.  This means the fused form
+
+```julia
+# BROKEN: aborts during Enzyme compile on GPU
+gradlogp(β) = -β .- pmcmc_matmul(transpose(X), pmcmc_matmul(X, β)) ./ Float32(N)
+```
+
+must be written as a sequence of single-op stages:
+
+```julia
+# WORKS: each line is one CUDA kernel Enzyme can differentiate
+function gradlogp(β)
+    Xβ = pmcmc_matmul(X, β)
+    Y  = pmcmc_matmul(transpose(X), Xβ)
+    Y  = Y ./ Float32(N)
+    Y  = Y .+ β
+    return -Y
+end
+```
+
+Mooncake does not have this restriction.
+
+---
+
+## Worked example: Bayesian logistic regression on GPU
+
+A standard Bayesian logistic regression with a Gaussian prior; an example model where GPU acceleration actually pays off as `N` and `D` grow.  Posterior:
+
+```math
+\log p(\beta \mid y, X) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\|\beta\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl[ y_i \, x_i^\top \beta - \log(1 + e^{x_i^\top \beta}) \bigr],
+```
+
+with gradient $\nabla_\beta \log p = -\beta + X^\top (y - \sigma(X\beta))$, where $\sigma$ is the logistic sigmoid.
+
+We use a numerically stable softplus on GPU:
+
+```math
+\log(1 + e^{z}) = \max(z, 0) + \log(1 + e^{-|z|}),
+```
+
+so neither the positive nor negative tail overflows in `Float32`.
+
+### Synthetic data
+
+```julia
+using Random, CUDA
+
+D = 50; N = 1000
+rng    = MersenneTwister(0)
+β_true = randn(rng, Float32, D)
+X_cpu  = randn(rng, Float32, N, D)
+probs  = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.(-(X_cpu * β_true)))
+y_cpu  = Float32.(rand(rng, N) .< probs)
+
+X_gpu = CUDA.CuMatrix(X_cpu)
+y_gpu = CUDA.CuVector(y_cpu)
+```
+
+### Mooncake backend (plain operators)
+
+```julia
+using ParallelMCMC, MCMCChains
+using ADTypes, Mooncake
+
+softplus(z) = log1p(exp(-abs(z))) + max(z, zero(z))
+
+logp(β)     = -0.5f0 * sum(abs2, β) + dot(y_gpu, X_gpu * β) -
+              sum(softplus.(X_gpu * β))
+gradlogp(β) = let z = X_gpu * β
+    -β .+ transpose(X_gpu) * (y_gpu .- 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.(-z)))
+end
+
+function logp_batch(B)
+    Z     = X_gpu * B
+    prior = -0.5f0 .* vec(sum(abs2, B; dims=1))
+    ll    = vec(sum(y_gpu .* Z; dims=1)) .- vec(sum(softplus.(Z); dims=1))
+    return prior .+ ll
+end
+function gradlogp_batch(B)
+    Z = X_gpu * B
+    P = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.(-Z))
+    return -B .+ transpose(X_gpu) * (y_gpu .- P)
+end
+
+model   = DensityModel(logp, gradlogp, D;
+                       logdensity_batch=logp_batch,
+                       grad_logdensity_batch=gradlogp_batch)
+sampler = ParallelMALASampler(0.005f0;
+                              T=16, damping=0.5f0,
+                              backend=ADTypes.AutoMooncake(; config=nothing))
+
+chain = sample(model, sampler, 1_600;
+               initial_params=CUDA.zeros(Float32, D),
+               chain_type=MCMCChains.Chains)
+```
+
+Posterior mean recovery error `‖β_post − β_true‖ / ‖β_true‖` should land in the 0.1–0.2 range after a few hundred post-warmup samples.
+
+### Enzyme backend (requires `pmcmc_matmul)
+
+Same model, with the GPU-Enzyme restrictions applied: every `*` becomes `pmcmc_matmul`, every `dot` becomes `pmcmc_dot`, and every gradient broadcast is expanded into single-op stages:
+
+```julia
+using ParallelMCMC, MCMCChains
+using ADTypes, Enzyme
+
+function logp(β)
+    z      = pmcmc_matmul(X_gpu, β)
+    az     = abs.(z)
+    ez     = exp.(.-az)
+    sp1    = log1p.(ez)
+    sp2    = max.(z, 0f0)
+    sp     = sp1 .+ sp2
+    ll     = pmcmc_dot(y_gpu, z) - sum(sp)
+    prior  = -0.5f0 * sum(abs2, β)
+    return prior + ll
+end
+
+function gradlogp(β)
+    z     = pmcmc_matmul(X_gpu, β)
+    ez    = exp.(.-z)
+    den   = 1f0 .+ ez
+    p     = 1f0 ./ den
+    resid = y_gpu .- p
+    g_ll  = pmcmc_matmul(transpose(X_gpu), resid)
+    g     = .-β
+    g     = g .+ g_ll
+    return g
+end
+
+function logp_batch(B)
+    Z      = pmcmc_matmul(X_gpu, B)
+    aZ     = abs.(Z)
+    eZ     = exp.(.-aZ)
+    sp1    = log1p.(eZ)
+    sp2    = max.(Z, 0f0)
+    SP     = sp1 .+ sp2
+    yZ     = y_gpu .* Z
+    ll     = vec(sum(yZ; dims=1)) .- vec(sum(SP; dims=1))
+    prior  = -0.5f0 .* vec(sum(abs2, B; dims=1))
+    return prior .+ ll
+end
+
+function gradlogp_batch(B)
+    Z     = pmcmc_matmul(X_gpu, B)
+    eZ    = exp.(.-Z)
+    denZ  = 1f0 .+ eZ
+    P     = 1f0 ./ denZ
+    Resid = y_gpu .- P
+    G_ll  = pmcmc_matmul(transpose(X_gpu), Resid)
+    G     = .-B
+    G     = G .+ G_ll
+    return G
+end
+
+model   = DensityModel(logp, gradlogp, D;
+                       logdensity_batch=logp_batch,
+                       grad_logdensity_batch=gradlogp_batch)
+sampler = ParallelMALASampler(0.005f0;
+                              T=16, damping=0.5f0,
+                              backend=ADTypes.AutoEnzyme())
+
+chain = sample(model, sampler, 1_600;
+               initial_params=CUDA.zeros(Float32, D),
+               chain_type=MCMCChains.Chains)
+```
+
+The two snippets sample the same posterior; the difference is purely in what the AD backend can chew on.
+
+---
+
+## The AD-HVP fallback (and when to write your own)
+
+DEER needs a Hessian–vector product $H v$ at every Newton step.  `DensityModel` accepts both `gradlogp` and (optionally) `hvp` / `hvp_batch`.  Depending on what you supply, the sampler does one of two things:
+
+- **You supply `hvp` / `hvp_batch`.**  These run as plain kernels.  The AD backend is never invoked for HVPs.
+- **You only supply `gradlogp` / `grad_logdensity_batch`.**  The sampler builds the HVP by differentiating your gradient — either a forward-mode pushforward of `gradlogp` ([`ForwardOnGrad`](https://github.com/rsenne/ParallelMCMC.jl/blob/main/src/DEER/DEER.jl), the default for most backends) or a reverse-mode gradient of `x -> dot(gradlogp(x), v)` ([`ReverseOnGrad`](https://github.com/rsenne/ParallelMCMC.jl/blob/main/src/DEER/DEER.jl), used for `AutoMooncake` and `AutoZygote`).  This is the **AD-HVP fallback**, and it is what the logistic-regression example above uses.
+
+### When the fallback is the right call
+
+- **Complex or composed models.**  Bayesian neural nets, hierarchical models with many transformations, mixtures, or anything where the Hessian has no convenient closed form.  Deriving and maintaining `hvp` by hand for these is error-prone; AD removes a whole class of bugs.
+- **Prototyping.**  You want a correct sampler running before you optimize.  Drop in `gradlogp`, lean on AD, profile later.
+- **Operations that AD libraries handle for free but are tedious to differentiate by hand.**  Special functions, link functions, log-sum-exp, normalizing constants of standard distributions, etc.
+- **You want backend flexibility.**  With only `gradlogp` you can swap `AutoMooncake` ↔ `AutoEnzyme` ↔ `AutoZygote` to compare without rewriting model code.
+
+### When to write your own analytical HVP
+
+- **The HVP has a clean closed form.**  Quadratic priors, Gaussian likelihoods, GLMs (logistic, Poisson, probit) — the second derivative is a known function of intermediate quantities you already compute in `gradlogp`.  A few extra lines and you skip the AD pipeline entirely.
+- **Performance matters and the AD compile is heavy.**  Enzyme and Mooncake both pay a one-shot compilation cost on the user's gradient.  For long-running chains this amortizes, but for many short runs the analytical HVP wins.
+- **You're hitting AD-backend-specific GPU restrictions.**  The [Enzyme limitations](#2-enzyme-on-gpu-currently-needs-pmcmc_matmul-pmcmc_dot-pmcmc_dotsum) above (`pmcmc_*` wrappers, staged broadcasts) only matter when the AD backend is invoked.  Supplying analytical HVP sidesteps them — your `gradlogp` and `hvp` can use plain `*`, `dot`, `sum` even with `backend=AutoEnzyme()`, because the backend is held but never run.
+- **You can reuse intermediates between gradient and HVP.**  When `hvp` shares $X\beta$, $\sigma(X\beta)$, or similar with the gradient computation, an analytical version can be both faster *and* shorter than what AD produces.
+
+### Same example with analytical HVP
+
+For Bayesian logistic regression with a Gaussian prior, the Hessian is
+
+```math
+\nabla^2 \log p = -I - X^\top \, \mathrm{diag}\bigl(\sigma(X\beta) \odot (1 - \sigma(X\beta))\bigr) \, X,
+```
+
+so
+
+```math
+H v = -v - X^\top \bigl[\sigma(X\beta) \odot (1 - \sigma(X\beta)) \odot (X v)\bigr].
+```
+
+Plug it in alongside `gradlogp` and the sampler stops invoking the AD path:
+
+```julia
+function hvp(β, v)
+    z  = X_gpu * β
+    σz = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.(-z))
+    w  = σz .* (1f0 .- σz)
+    -v .- transpose(X_gpu) * (w .* (X_gpu * v))
+end
+function hvp_batch(B, V)
+    Z = X_gpu * B
+    Σ = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.(-Z))
+    W = Σ .* (1f0 .- Σ)
+    -V .- transpose(X_gpu) * (W .* (X_gpu * V))
+end
+
+model = DensityModel(logp, gradlogp, D;
+                     logdensity_batch=logp_batch,
+                     grad_logdensity_batch=gradlogp_batch,
+                     hvp=hvp, hvp_batch=hvp_batch)
+
+# `backend` is still required by the API, but is never invoked.
+sampler = ParallelMALASampler(0.005f0;
+                              T=16, damping=0.5f0,
+                              backend=ADTypes.AutoMooncake(; config=nothing))
+```
+
+This recovers the same posterior as the fallback version — the only difference is that HVPs come from a plain matmul instead of a reverse-mode pass over `gradlogp`.
+

+
+## Picking an AD backend on GPU
+
+| Backend | GPU support | Restrictions | Recommended when |
+|---|---|---|---|

+| `AutoZygote()` | Native (no wrappers) | ChainRules-based; reverse-only, plus no in-place mutation in `gradlogp`| You want plain Julia operators and are already on the ChainRules ecosystem |
+| `AutoForwardDiff()` | Native; works with `*` / `dot` / `sum` / broadcasts on `CuArray{Dual}`| Cost scales as O(D)| Low-D models, prototyping, validating Mooncake/Enzyme results |
+

+module EnzymeExt
+
+using ParallelMCMC: pmcmc_matmul, pmcmc_dot, pmcmc_dotsum
+using ParallelMCMC.DEER: DEER
+using ADTypes: ADTypes
+using LinearAlgebra: dot
+using Enzyme
+using Enzyme.EnzymeCore
+using Enzyme.EnzymeCore.EnzymeRules:
+    EnzymeRules,
+    FwdConfig,
+    RevConfig,
+    Annotation,
+    AugmentedReturn,
+    needs_primal,
+    needs_shadow,
+    overwritten,
+    width
+
+# TODO: Implement matmul overloads upstream in Enzyme. See: https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme.jl/issues/3122
+
+#=
+Tell DEER's forward-on-grad HVP path how to normalize a plain `AutoEnzyme()`:
+pin `mode=Enzyme.Forward` and `function_annotation=Enzyme.Const`. Pinning
+Forward is load-bearing on GPU — without it DI defaults to reverse mode, which
+hits the gc-transition abort documented on the Enzyme rules below.
+
+`mode` and `function_annotation` are normalized independently — a user who
+sets one keeps that choice, but still gets the default for the other.
+
+`set_runtime_activity` is load-bearing for composed `pmcmc_matmul` calls
+(e.g. `pmcmc_matmul(transpose(X), pmcmc_matmul(X, β))`). Static activity
+analysis can't prove the outer call's `transpose(X)` shadow is safe to
+reuse, and Enzyme aborts with `EnzymeRuntimeActivityError`. With runtime
+activity, the shadow is tracked dynamically.
+=#
+function DEER._hvp_forward_backend(backend::ADTypes.AutoEnzyme{M,A}) where {M,A}
+    mode = if backend.mode === nothing
+        Enzyme.set_runtime_activity(Enzyme.Forward)
+    else
+        backend.mode
+    end
+    annotation = A === Nothing ? Enzyme.Const : A
+    return ADTypes.AutoEnzyme(; mode=mode, function_annotation=annotation)
+end
+
+#=
+Tell DEER's reverse-on-grad HVP path how to normalize a plain `AutoEnzyme()`:
+fill in `function_annotation=Enzyme.Const` so Enzyme doesn't throw
+`EnzymeMutabilityException` on the read-only `_HvpReverseClosure` /
+`_BatchHvpReverseClosure` wrappers, and default `mode` to reverse with
+runtime activity. As in `_hvp_forward_backend`, the two fields are
+normalized independently.
+=#
+function DEER._hvp_closure_backend(backend::ADTypes.AutoEnzyme{M,A}) where {M,A}
+    mode = if backend.mode === nothing
+        Enzyme.set_runtime_activity(Enzyme.Reverse)
+    else
+        backend.mode
+    end
+    annotation = A === Nothing ? Enzyme.Const : A
+    return ADTypes.AutoEnzyme(; mode=mode, function_annotation=annotation)
+end
+
+#=
+Native Enzyme rules for the owned wrappers `pmcmc_matmul`, `pmcmc_dot`,
+`pmcmc_dotsum`. They make Enzyme treat each as opaque: primal and cotangents
+are computed by plain `*`, `dot`, `sum`, broadcast outside Enzyme's IR
+rewriter.
+
+Why: reverse-mode Enzyme aborts differentiating a CuArray scalar reduction.
+
+    unsupported tag gc-transition for
+      call i32 @cuMemcpyDtoHAsync_v2(...) [ "jl_roots"(...), "gc-transition"() ]
+    UNREACHABLE executed at .../Enzyme/GradientUtils.cpp:309      (signal 6)
+=#
+
+#=
+pmcmc_matmul(A, B) = A * B   —   matrix output (Duplicated)
+
+JVP:      dY  = dA * B + A * dB
+Pullback: dA += dY * B'
+          dB += A'  * dY
+=#
+
+function EnzymeRules.forward(
+    config::FwdConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_matmul)},
+    RT::Type{<:Annotation},
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.val) : nothing
+    shadow = if A isa Const && B isa Const
+        #=
+        Both args Const → output tangent is structurally zero. We still need
+        to return an output-shaped array (Enzyme's shadow-type check rejects
+        `nothing` when the caller asked for `Duplicated`/`DuplicatedNoNeed`).
+        =#
+        zero(primal === nothing ? pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.val) : primal)
+    elseif A isa Const
+        pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.dval)
+    elseif B isa Const
+        pmcmc_matmul(A.dval, B.val)
+    else
+        pmcmc_matmul(A.dval, B.val) .+ pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.dval)
+    end
+    if RT <: Const
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : nothing
+    elseif RT <: DuplicatedNoNeed
+        return shadow
+    elseif RT <: Duplicated
+        return Duplicated(primal === nothing ? pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.val) : primal, shadow)
+    else
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : shadow
+    end
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.augmented_primal(
+    config::RevConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_matmul)},
+    RT::Type{<:Annotation},
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    Y = pmcmc_matmul(A.val, B.val)
+    cache_A = overwritten(config)[2] ? copy(A.val) : A.val
+    cache_B = overwritten(config)[3] ? copy(B.val) : B.val
+    dY = if RT <: Duplicated || RT <: DuplicatedNoNeed
+        zero(Y)
+    else
+        nothing
+    end
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? Y : nothing
+    return AugmentedReturn(primal, dY, (dY, cache_A, cache_B))
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.reverse(
+    config::RevConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_matmul)},
+    ::Type{<:Annotation},
+    tape,
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    dY, cache_A, cache_B = tape
+    if dY !== nothing
+        if !(A isa Const)
+            A.dval .+= pmcmc_matmul(dY, transpose(cache_B))
+        end
+        if !(B isa Const)
+            B.dval .+= pmcmc_matmul(transpose(cache_A), dY)
+        end
+        fill!(dY, zero(eltype(dY)))
+    end
+    return (nothing, nothing)
+end
+
+#=
+pmcmc_dot(a, b) = dot(a, b)   —   scalar output (Active)
+
+JVP:      dr  = dot(da, b) + dot(a, db)
+Pullback: da += dr * b
+          db += dr * a
+=#
+
+function EnzymeRules.forward(
+    config::FwdConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dot)},
+    RT::Type{<:Annotation},
+    a::Annotation,
+    b::Annotation,
+)
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? pmcmc_dot(a.val, b.val) : nothing
+    if RT <: Const
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : nothing
+    end
+    da_term = a isa Const ? zero(eltype(a.val)) : pmcmc_dot(a.dval, b.val)
+    db_term = b isa Const ? zero(eltype(b.val)) : pmcmc_dot(a.val, b.dval)
+    tangent = da_term + db_term
+    if RT <: DuplicatedNoNeed
+        return tangent
+    elseif RT <: Duplicated
+        return Duplicated(primal === nothing ? pmcmc_dot(a.val, b.val) : primal, tangent)
+    else
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : tangent
+    end
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.augmented_primal(
+    config::RevConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dot)},
+    ::Type{<:Annotation},
+    a::Annotation,
+    b::Annotation,
+)
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? pmcmc_dot(a.val, b.val) : nothing
+    cache_a = (!(b isa Const) && overwritten(config)[2]) ? copy(a.val) : nothing
+    cache_b = (!(a isa Const) && overwritten(config)[3]) ? copy(b.val) : nothing
+    return AugmentedReturn(primal, nothing, (cache_a, cache_b))
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.reverse(
+    config::RevConfig, ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dot)}, dret, tape, a::Annotation, b::Annotation
+)
+    cache_a, cache_b = tape
+    if !(dret isa Const)
+        dr = dret.val
+        if !(a isa Const)
+            bv = cache_b !== nothing ? cache_b : b.val
+            a.dval .+= dr .* bv
+        end
+        if !(b isa Const)
+            av = cache_a !== nothing ? cache_a : a.val
+            b.dval .+= dr .* av
+        end
+    end
+    return (nothing, nothing)
+end
+
+#=
+pmcmc_dotsum(A, B) = sum(A .* B)   —   scalar output (Active)
+
+Same algebra as `pmcmc_dot`, just with matrix args.
+=#
+
+function EnzymeRules.forward(
+    config::FwdConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dotsum)},
+    RT::Type{<:Annotation},
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? pmcmc_dotsum(A.val, B.val) : nothing
+    if RT <: Const
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : nothing
+    end
+    dA_term = A isa Const ? zero(eltype(A.val)) : pmcmc_dotsum(A.dval, B.val)
+    dB_term = B isa Const ? zero(eltype(B.val)) : pmcmc_dotsum(A.val, B.dval)
+    tangent = dA_term + dB_term
+    if RT <: DuplicatedNoNeed
+        return tangent
+    elseif RT <: Duplicated
+        return Duplicated(primal === nothing ? pmcmc_dotsum(A.val, B.val) : primal, tangent)
+    else
+        return needs_primal(config) ? primal : tangent
+    end
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.augmented_primal(
+    config::RevConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dotsum)},
+    ::Type{<:Annotation},
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    primal = needs_primal(config) ? pmcmc_dotsum(A.val, B.val) : nothing
+    cache_A = (!(B isa Const) && overwritten(config)[2]) ? copy(A.val) : nothing
+    cache_B = (!(A isa Const) && overwritten(config)[3]) ? copy(B.val) : nothing
+    return AugmentedReturn(primal, nothing, (cache_A, cache_B))
+end
+
+function EnzymeRules.reverse(
+    config::RevConfig,
+    ::Const{typeof(pmcmc_dotsum)},
+    dret,
+    tape,
+    A::Annotation,
+    B::Annotation,
+)
+    cache_A, cache_B = tape
+    if !(dret isa Const)
+        dr = dret.val
+        if !(A isa Const)
+            Bv = cache_B !== nothing ? cache_B : B.val
+            A.dval .+= dr .* Bv
+        end
+        if !(B isa Const)
+            Av = cache_A !== nothing ? cache_A : A.val
+            B.dval .+= dr .* Av
+        end
+    end
+    return (nothing, nothing)
+end
+
+end # module

+  )
+
+  if (is.null(con))
+    skip("GitHub is not reachable and GITHUB_PAT is not set")
+
+  close(con)
+
+  # note that GitHub will still answer TCP connections and anonymous
+  # HTTP requests with a 403 response even when the per-IP anonymous
+  # rate limit has been exhausted, so connectivity alone is not enough;
+  # verify that the GitHub API can actually service anonymous requests
+  # by checking the remaining core rate limit quota
+  destfile <- renv_scope_tempfile("renv-ratelimit-")
+  status <- tryCatch(
+    download.file(
+      url      = "https://api.github.com/rate_limit",
+      destfile = destfile,
+      quiet    = TRUE,
+      mode     = "wb"
+    ),
+    error   = function(e) 1L,
+    warning = function(w) 1L
+  )
+
+  if (!identical(as.integer(status), 0L) || !file.exists(destfile))
+    skip("GitHub API rate limit quota could not be determined")
+
+  contents <- paste(readLines(destfile, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
+  pattern <- '"remaining"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+'
+  matches <- regmatches(contents, gregexpr(pattern, contents))[[1L]]
+  remaining <- if (length(matches) == 0L)
+    NA_integer_
+  else
+    as.integer(sub('^.*:[[:space:]]*', "", matches[[1L]]))
+
+  if (is.na(remaining) || remaining < quota)

+

### Additional contract requirements

When the namespace of a required package has already been loaded from a
library that is no longer on the active library paths (for example, a
library referenced by a user's `.Rprofile` before `renv` activated the
project), `renv::install()` must not treat that package as already
installed. Invoking `renv::install()` for the project, or for any package
recursively requiring it, must install the package into the requesting
project library; afterwards the package's installation directory
(containing its `DESCRIPTION` file) must exist there.

When the namespace of a required package has already been loaded from a
library that is no longer on the active library paths (for example, a
library referenced by a user's `.Rprofile` before `renv` activated the
project), `renv::install()` must not treat that package as already
installed. Invoking `renv::install()` for the project, or for any package
recursively requiring it, must install the package into the requesting
project library; afterwards the package's installation directory
(containing its `DESCRIPTION` file) must exist there.

problem_statement:
Question: what is the right way to handle libraries like dbplyr that are never called directly
I'm looking for some advice on how to handle libraries that are required by my project but are never called directly. I think the dbplyr library is a good example:

https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/#usage

> Note that you donÃ¢ÂÂt actually need to load dbplyr with [library(dbplyr)](https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/); dplyr automatically loads it for you when it sees you working with a database. Database connections are coordinated by the DBI package. Learn more at https://dbi.r-dbi.org/

**app.R**

```R
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
copy_to(con, mtcars)

mtcars2 <- tbl(con, "mtcars")
mtcars2
```

Set up renv:

```R
renv::init()
renv::snapshot()
renv::restore()
```

How do I ensure that RM will always install `dbplyr`? For my specific use case, I'm trying to deploy an application to Posit Connect. So I need to make sure that Posit Connect picks up `dbplyr` and installs it.

### Additional contract requirements

When a project's code uses `dplyr` together with a database backend (such as
`DBI` and `RSQLite`), `renv::dependencies()` must report `dbplyr` among the
discovered packages, since `dplyr` loads `dbplyr` at runtime when working with
a database.

To be reported, `dbplyr` requires both of the following to hold:

- the project uses `dplyr`, and
- the project uses at least one database backend package (e.g. `DBI`,
  `RSQLite`, or a similar database driver).

Both conditions must be satisfied: code that uses `dplyr` without any database
backend, and code that uses a database backend without `dplyr`, must not
produce a `dbplyr` dependency. This inferred dependency allows
`renv::snapshot()` to record `dbplyr` in the lockfile so that `renv::restore()`
and deployment tools (e.g. publishing to Posit Connect) install it, even though
user code never calls `dbplyr` directly.

+  backend (e.g. RSQLite, RPostgres, duckdb). The rules are configurable via the
+  `renv.dependencies.implied` R option; set it to an empty list to disable this
+  inference entirely. (#2308)
+
 * `renv::restore()` gains a `retry` argument, controlling whether packages
   that fail to install successfully are retried with their latest available

index 3085911e7..99f748c88 100644
--- a/R/dependencies.R
+++ b/R/dependencies.R
@@ -36,6 +36,14 @@
 #' function requires the `stringr` package, but `stringr` is only suggested,
 #' not required, by `tidyr`.
 #'
+#' For a small number of common cases, renv infers these indirect dependencies
+#' from the combination of packages in use. For example, a project that uses
+#' `dplyr` together with a database backend (such as `DBI` and `RSQLite`) is
+#' assumed to also require `dbplyr`, which `dplyr` loads at runtime when working
+#' with databases. These rules are defined by the `renv.dependencies.implied`
+#' \R option; set it to an empty list (`options(renv.dependencies.implied =
+#' list())`) to disable this inference entirely.
+#'
 #' If you find that renv's dependency discovery misses one or more packages
 #' that you actually use in your project, one escape hatch is to include a file
 #' called `_dependencies.R` that includes straightforward library calls:
@@ -256,6 +264,9 @@ renv_dependencies_impl <- function(
   renv_condition_signal("renv.dependencies.elapsed_time", elapsed)
   renv_dependencies_report(errors)
 
+  # augment with packages that are only required indirectly
+  deps <- renv_dependencies_infer_implied(deps)
+
   if (empty(deps) || nrow(deps) == 0L) {
     result <- renv_dependencies_list_empty()
     return(take(result, field))
@@ -1911,6 +1922,66 @@ renv_dependencies_database <- function() {
   }
 }
 
+# rules describing packages that are required only indirectly, and so cannot
+# be discovered by static analysis of user code. each entry maps an implied
+# package to the set of packages whose joint presence implies it: every
+# package in 'all' must be used, plus at least one of the packages in 'any'
+# (when 'any' is non-empty).
+#
+# for example, dplyr loads dbplyr at runtime when used together with a
+# database backend, but neither dplyr nor the user's code ever references
+# dbplyr explicitly.
+renv_dependencies_implied <- function() {
+  getOption("renv.dependencies.implied", default = list(
+    dbplyr = list(
+      all = "dplyr",
+      any = c(
+        "DBI", "RSQLite", "RPostgres", "RPostgreSQL", "RMariaDB",
+        "RMySQL", "odbc", "bigrquery", "duckdb", "RJDBC"
+      )
+    )
+  ))
+}
+
+# given the set of dependencies discovered via static analysis, augment it
+# with any packages that are implied by the combination of packages in use.
+# see renv_dependencies_implied() for the rule format.
+renv_dependencies_infer_implied <- function(deps) {
+
+  if (empty(deps) || nrow(deps) == 0L)
+    return(deps)
+
+  rules <- renv_dependencies_implied()
+  packages <- unique(deps$Package)
+
+  implied <- character()
+  for (package in names(rules)) {
+
+    rule <- rules[[package]]
+
+    # skip packages we've already discovered (or just inferred)
+    if (package %in% c(packages, implied))
+      next
+
+    # require every 'all' package, plus at least one 'any' package
+    if (!all(rule$all %in% packages))
+      next
+
+    if (length(rule$any) && !any(rule$any %in% packages))
+      next
+
+    implied[[length(implied) + 1L]] <- package
+
+  }
+
+  if (empty(implied))
+    return(deps)
+
+  extra <- renv_dependencies_list(source = NA_character_, packages = implied)
+  bind(list(deps, extra))
+
+}
+
 renv_dependencies_list <- function(source,
                                    packages,
                                    require = "",

problem_statement:
Export `renv_lockfile_from_manifest()`?
I found that I needed to create an `renv.lock` from a manifest file, and was surprised that `renv_lockfile_from_manifest()` wasn't yet exported. It looks like it's never been (though it is used in some auto-init code, the tools I'm using don't quite follow that path, so I need to call it manually.

### Additional contract requirements

## Public lockfile-conversion contract

For this issue, the supported public entry point for converting a Posit Connect
manifest is `renv::lockfile()`. This public API supersedes the request to export
the existing manifest-specific helper; no manifest-specific internal helper is
required to be exported.

The following behavior is required:

- `lockfile` is exported from the `renv` namespace.
- `renv::lockfile(from = ...)` accepts either the path to a Posit Connect
  `manifest.json` file or the equivalent already-parsed R list. Both forms
  return the same object of class `renv_lockfile`.
- Supplying `to` writes the converted lockfile at that path and still returns
  the converted lockfile object.
- A source that is not a recognized manifest is rejected as an unrecognized
  lockfile source, rather than being accepted or failing merely because the
  `from` argument is unavailable.

problem_statement:
renv::use() ignores pinned versions when pak is enabled
With pak enabled, `renv::use()` installs the current CRAN version instead of the requested version.

```r
options(
  repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"),
  renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE
)

lib <- tempfile("renv-use-")

renv::use(
  "generics@0.1.3",
  library = lib,
  isolate = TRUE,
  sandbox = FALSE,
  attach = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

actual <- as.character(packageVersion("generics", lib.loc = lib))
actual
#> [1] "0.1.4"

stopifnot(identical(actual, "0.1.3"))
#> Error: identical(actual, "0.1.3") is not TRUE
```

Expected `generics` 0.1.3 to be installed.

For comparison, `renv::install()` preserves the same version specification:

```r
lib <- tempfile("renv-install-")
dir.create(lib)

renv::install(
  "generics@0.1.3",
  library = lib,
  prompt = FALSE
)

as.character(packageVersion("generics", lib.loc = lib))
#> [1] "0.1.3"
```

Reproduced with R 4.6.1, renv 1.2.3, and pak 0.11.1 on macOS arm64.

### Additional contract requirements

When pak is enabled, `renv::use()` must honor an explicitly requested package version. A request for a pinned version must install that version rather than a different available version.

problem_statement:
Fix SNOMED CT CodeSystem Generation
In the Germany Edition v20251115 there is no fully specified name so we can't create a title.

### Additional contract requirements

When a SNOMED CT release contains a module version without a fully
specified name (as in the Germany Edition v20251115), the SNOMED CT
CodeSystem generation from that release must complete successfully.

The generated CodeSystem for a module version without a fully specified
name has no title.

The generated CodeSystems for module versions with a fully specified
name still carry their title as before.

problem_statement:
Add Write-Through Cache Support to Local Page Store
## Problem

In the distributed storage variant, search query clauses are stored in `page-store-cassandra` so all nodes can resolve them via tokens from next-page links. Every paginated request calls `page-store/get` against Cassandra to resolve the token → clauses mapping. Since this mapping is immutable (content-addressed), repeated Cassandra lookups are unnecessary and cause Cassandra to become overwhelmed under load.

## Solution

Extend `::page-store/local` with an optional `:backing-store` dependency implementing a **write-through cache**:

- **`put!`**: write to local Caffeine cache, then await write to backing store before returning the token (correctness requirement: the next-page request may hit a different node with no sticky sessions).
- **`get`**: serve from local Caffeine cache on hit; on miss, fall through to backing store, populate local cache, and return result.

When `:backing-store` is absent, behavior is identical to today (local/single-node case).

## Additional Cleanup

Remove the Integrant `derive` calls that implicitly register both stores under `:blaze/page-store`:

- Remove `(derive ::page-store/local :blaze/page-store)` from `blaze.page-store.local`
- Remove `(derive ::page-store/cassandra :blaze/page-store)` from `blaze.page-store.cassandra`

Update all system configs to reference `::page-store/local` explicitly instead of `:blaze/page-store`. The `PageStore` protocol and `:blaze/page-store` spec are kept for validation purposes.

This makes the distributed topology explicit in the config: the local page store is always the component wired into interactions, optionally backed by Cassandra.

## Config (distributed case)

```edn
::page-store/local    {:expire-duration #ig/ref :blaze/timeout
                       :backing-store   #ig/ref ::page-store/cassandra}
::page-store/cassandra { ... }
```

### Additional contract requirements

The local page store supports an optional backing store and then acts as a write-through cache:

- The optional backing store has to be a page store itself.
- When a backing store is configured, putting clauses stores them locally and in the backing store, and the returned CompletableFuture only completes after the backing store write completed. The future completes with the same content-addressed token as without a backing store.
- When a backing store is configured, getting clauses returns them from the local cache on a hit. On a miss, the clauses are fetched from the backing store, stored in the local cache so that subsequent gets are served locally, and returned. Getting a token missing from both the local cache and the backing store completes exceptionally with a not-found anomaly (the exact anomaly message is not prescribed).
- Without a backing store, behavior is unchanged.

Neither the local page store nor the Cassandra page store is registered under the super key :blaze/page-store anymore. The system configuration refers to the local page store explicitly instead of :blaze/page-store, and the distributed configuration section wires the local page store with the Cassandra page store as its backing store.

problem_statement:
Fix GC Race in Mem-Size Measurement
## Summary

The `:mem-size` property tests in `blaze.fhir.spec-test` fail intermittently with a `real-size` that is far larger than the `calculated-size` (e.g. `{:calculated-size 328, :real-size 1472}` for a `SampledData`). Re-running the measurement on the same value passes, so the failures looked like a JOL problem — and they are, but a usage problem, not a JOL bug.
[HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

The FHIR memory-size helper reports the size of objects reachable from the
measured value that are not reachable from its baseline. A value measured
against itself therefore has size zero. When the baseline and measured values
share reachable objects, those shared objects are excluded from the measured
size.

The reported exclusive size must remain correct when garbage collection occurs
between graph observations.

Fix GC Race in Mem-Size Measurement
## Summary

The `:mem-size` property tests in `blaze.fhir.spec-test` fail intermittently with a `real-size` that is far larger than the `calculated-size` (e.g. `{:calculated-size 328, :real-size 1472}` for a `SampledData`). Re-running the measurement on the same value passes, so the failures looked like a JOL problem — and they are, but a usage problem, not a JOL bug.
[HIDDEN]
contract_addendum:
The FHIR memory-size helper reports the size of objects reachable from the
measured value that are not reachable from its baseline. A value measured
against itself therefore has size zero. When the baseline and measured values
share reachable objects, those shared objects are excluded from the measured
size.

The reported exclusive size must remain correct when garbage collection occurs
between graph observations.

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+(ns blaze.fhir.spec.memory-gc-test
+  "Regression coverage for relocation-safe memory-size measurement."
+  (:require
+   [blaze.fhir.spec.memory :as memory]
+   [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]])
+  (:import
+   [org.openjdk.jol.info GraphLayout]))
+
+(set! *warn-on-reflection* true)
+
+(defn- collect! []
+  (System/gc)
+  (Thread/yield))
+
+(defn- layout ^GraphLayout [& roots]
+  (GraphLayout/parseInstance (object-array roots)))
+
+(defn- size [x]
+  (.totalSize (layout x)))
+
+(defn- equivalent-roots [baseline measured roots]
+  (cond
+    (= 1 (count roots))
+    (if (identical? baseline measured)
+      (let [shared (byte-array 256)]
+        [(object-array [shared (byte-array 4096)])])
+      (let [shared (byte-array 256)]
+        [(object-array [shared])]))
+
+    (identical? (first roots) (second roots))
+    (let [shared (byte-array 256)
+          value (object-array [shared (byte-array 4096)])]
+      [value value])
+
+    :else
+    (let [shared (byte-array 256)]
+      [(object-array [shared])
+       (object-array [shared (byte-array 4096)])])))
+
+(defn- collecting-observation [baseline measured]
+  (let [observations (atom 0)
+        snapshots (atom [])
+        reliable-instrumentation?
+        (= "true" (System/getProperty "jdk.attach.allowAttachSelf"))]
+    (fn [& roots]
+      ;; When JOL has to infer object details, use equivalent live snapshots to
+      ;; deterministically model relocation. The arithmetic implementation is
+      ;; insensitive to their addresses. With instrumentation, use the actual
+      ;; roots while still forcing collection at the same observation boundary.
+      (let [snapshot (if reliable-instrumentation?
+                       roots
+                       (equivalent-roots baseline measured roots))]
+        (swap! snapshots conj snapshot)
+        (let [graph (apply layout snapshot)]
+          (when (= 1 (swap! observations inc))
+            (collect!))
+          graph)))))
+
+(deftest total-size-is-stable-across-collection-test
+  (let [shared (byte-array 256)
+        baseline (object-array [shared])
+        measured (object-array [shared (byte-array 4096)])]
+    (testing "a value measured against itself has no exclusive size"
+      (with-redefs [memory/graph-layout
+                    (collecting-observation measured measured)]
+        (is (zero? (memory/total-size measured measured)))))
+
+    (testing "shared baseline objects remain excluded after collection"
+      (let [expected (- (size measured) (size shared))]
+        (is (pos? expected))
+        (with-redefs [memory/graph-layout
+                      (collecting-observation baseline measured)]
+          (is (= expected (memory/total-size baseline measured))))))))

problem_statement:
solution_jacobian: add ParametricOracle support
`solution_jacobian` currently throws `ArgumentError` for `ParametricOracle` inputs because the constraint sensitivity term[HIDDEN] is not included in the batched Jacobian computation.

The `rrule` pullback handles `ParametricOracle` correctly by adding the constraint sensitivity[HIDDEN]. The workaround is to call the pullback `m` times (once per parameter), but this is slower than a batched approach.[HIDDEN]

problem_statement:
REPL : pureFunctions and captureChecking fail with "language import only allowed at toplevel"
## Compiler version

3.2.2-RC1-bin-SNAPSHOT-git-292e56f

## Minimized code

```scala
scala> import language.experimental.captureChecking
```

## Output

```scala
-- Error: ----------------------------------------------------------------------
1 |import language.experimental.captureChecking
  |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |                      this language import is only allowed at the toplevel
```

## Expectation

Should work. [HIDDEN]

### Additional contract requirements

In the Scala REPL, entering `import language.experimental.captureChecking` or `import language.experimental.pureFunctions` as a standalone top-level input must be accepted, producing no error or warning output for that input.

After such an import has been accepted, it must take effect for the remainder of the REPL session: subsequent REPL inputs may use the syntax enabled by that global language import. In particular, after `import language.experimental.captureChecking`, later inputs may use capture-checking syntax, and after `import language.experimental.pureFunctions`, later inputs may use the pure-function arrow syntax.

problem_statement:
Separation checking import vs. compiler option are inconsistent
## Compiler version

3.nightly


## Minimized Code

The following program fails when separation checking is enabled with language imports:

```scala
import language.experimental.captureChecking
import language.experimental.separationChecking
import caps.*
import scala.reflect.ClassTag

class Arr[T: ClassTag](n: Int) extends Mutable:
  private val elems: Array[T]^ = new Array[T](n)
  def get(i: Int): T = elems(i)
  update def update(i: Int, x: T): Unit = elems(i) = x
```

## Output

Compiling that file normally reports:

```scala
Read-only method get accesses exclusive capability `Arr.this.elems`;
method get should be declared an update method to allow this.
```

However, compiled with the respective language options:
```bash
scalac -language:experimental.captureChecking -language:experimental.separationChecking Arr.scala
```
it succeeds!

## Expectation

Enabling capture checking and separation checking via language imports should give the same typing behavior as enabling them with the corresponding -language options.

## Further minimization

The behavior also depends on whether the array field type is inferred or written explicitly.

With language imports:

```scala
import language.experimental.captureChecking
import language.experimental.separationChecking
import caps.*
import scala.reflect.ClassTag

class Arr[T: ClassTag](n: Int) extends Mutable:
  private val elems = new Array[T](n)
  def apply(i: Int): T = elems(i)
  update def update(i: Int, x: T): Unit = elems(i) = x
```

this fails with:

```text
Read-only method apply accesses exclusive capability `Arr.this.elems`;
method apply should be declared an update method to allow this.
```

But with an explicit field type:

```scala
import language.experimental.captureChecking
import language.experimental.separationChecking
import caps.*
import scala.reflect.ClassTag

class Arr[T: ClassTag](n: Int) extends Mutable:
  private val elems: Array[T] = new Array[T](n)
  def apply(i: Int): T = elems(i)
  update def update(i: Int, x: T): Unit = elems(i) = x
```

the same code compiles.

With command-line flags, the behavior is the opposite and appears more sensible:

```scala
import caps.*
import scala.reflect.ClassTag

class Arr[T: ClassTag](n: Int) extends Mutable:
  private val elems = new Array[T](n)
  def apply(i: Int): T = elems(i)
  update def update(i: Int, x: T): Unit = elems(i) = x
```

compiled with

```bash
scalac -language:experimental.captureChecking -language:experimental.separationChecking Arr.scala
```

compiles successfully.

But this variant:

```scala
import caps.*
import scala.reflect.ClassTag

class Arr[T: ClassTag](n: Int) extends Mutable:
  private val elems: Array[T] = new Array[T](n)
  def apply(i: Int): T = elems(i)
  update def update(i: Int, x: T): Unit = elems(i) = x
```

fails with:

```text
Cannot call update method update of Arr.this.elems
since its capture set {Arr.this.elems} is read-only.
```

So the current matrix is:

- imports + inferred field type: fail
- imports + explicit field type: success
- flags + inferred field type: success
- flags + explicit field type: fail

This suggests that enabling the features by import does not just differ from `-language:` flags in one corner case. It seems to produce a different interpretation of the field type.

accept an optional, human-readable timeout reason:

- `withTimeout(length: Int, unit: TimeUnit, reason: Option[String])` returns a
  future that completes with the original future's value when that future
  completes within the given bound, and otherwise fails with a
  `TimeoutException`. When a reason is provided and the timeout elapses, an
  error-level log entry containing that reason is emitted through the Metals
  logger before the timeout failure is propagated.
- `onTimeout(length: Int, unit: TimeUnit, reason: Option[String])(action: => Unit)`
  behaves like `withTimeout` and additionally runs the supplied `action`
  exactly once when the future times out — after logging the reason when one is
  provided — and still fails with the `TimeoutException`. When the future
  completes before the timeout, the action is not run.

Observable behavior requirements:

- When the wrapped future completes successfully, the returned future completes
  with the same value and no timeout reason is logged.
- When the wrapped future times out without a provided reason (`None`), the
  returned future fails with a `TimeoutException` and no timeout-reason message
  is logged.

contract_addendum:
The `Future` timeout enrichment used across Metals (`withTimeout` / `onTimeout`
in `scala.meta.internal.metals.MetalsEnrichments`) provides overloads that
accept an optional, human-readable timeout reason:

- `withTimeout(length: Int, unit: TimeUnit, reason: Option[String])` returns a
  future that completes with the original future's value when that future
  completes within the given bound, and otherwise fails with a
  `TimeoutException`. When a reason is provided and the timeout elapses, an
  error-level log entry containing that reason is emitted through the Metals
  logger before the timeout failure is propagated.
- `onTimeout(length: Int, unit: TimeUnit, reason: Option[String])(action: => Unit)`
  behaves like `withTimeout` and additionally runs the supplied `action`
  exactly once when the future times out — after logging the reason when one is
  provided — and still fails with the `TimeoutException`. When the future
  completes before the timeout, the action is not run.

Observable behavior requirements:

- When the wrapped future completes successfully, the returned future completes
  with the same value and no timeout reason is logged.
- When the wrapped future times out without a provided reason (`None`), the
  returned future fails with a `TimeoutException` and no timeout-reason message
  is logged.

+  private val enrichmentsClass =
+    Class.forName(
+      "scala.meta.internal.metals.MetalsEnrichments$XtensionScalaFuture"
+    )
+
+  private val optionClass = Class.forName("scala.Option")
+
+  /** Reflectively create the enriched future wrapper for `future`. */
+  private def enrich(future: Future[_]): AnyRef = {
+    val ctor = enrichmentsClass.getConstructors.head
+    ctor.newInstance(future)
+  }
+
+  private def describe(m: Method): String =
+    m.getParameterTypes.toList.map(_.getSimpleName).mkString("(", ", ", ")")
+
+  private def findReasonOverload(name: String): Option[Method] =
+    enrichmentsClass.getMethods
+      .filter(_.getName == name)
+      .find { m =>
+        val p = m.getParameterTypes.toList
+        // instance method: (length: Int, unit: TimeUnit, reason: Option[String], ec)
+        p.length >= 4 &&
+        p(0) == classOf[Int] &&
+        p(1) == classOf[TimeUnit] &&
+        p(2).isAssignableFrom(optionClass) &&
+        classOf[ExecutionContext].isAssignableFrom(p(p.length - 1))
+      }
+
+  private def requireReasonOverload(name: String): Method = {
+    val overload = findReasonOverload(name)
+    assert(
+      overload.isDefined,
+      s"Expected a '$name' overload accepting an Option[String] reason, " +
+        "but only found: " +
+        enrichmentsClass.getMethods
+          .filter(_.getName == name)
+          .map(describe)
+          .mkString(" "),
+    )
+    overload.get
+  }
+
+  /** A never-completing future so `withTimeout` always times out. */
+  private def neverCompleting[A]: Future[A] = Promise[A]().future
+
+  private def awaitResult[A](f: Future[A]): Try[A] =
+    Try(Await.result(f, Duration(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)))
+
+  /**
+   * Runs `body` while capturing everything that is logged through the Metals
+   * logger as (level name, message text) pairs, so tests can assert both the
+   * logged message and its severity.
+   */
+  private def withCapturedMetalsLog[A](
+      body: => A
+  ): (A, List[(String, String)]) = {
+    val buffer =
+      java.util.Collections.synchronizedList(new java.util.ArrayList[(String, String)]())
+    val handler = new scribe.handler.LogHandler {
+      override def log(record: scribe.LogRecord): Unit = {
+        val text = record.messages.asInstanceOf[scala.Seq[scribe.message.LoggableMessage]]
+          .map((m: scribe.message.LoggableMessage) => String.valueOf(m.value))
+          .mkString(" ")
+        buffer.add((record.level.name, text))
+        ()
+      }
+    }
+    val root = scribe.Logger.root
+    val previousHandlers = root.handlers
+    root.clearHandlers().withHandler(handler).replace()
+    try {
+      val result = body
+      (result, {
+        import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters._
+        buffer.asScala.toList
+      })
+    } finally {
+      root.clearHandlers()
+      previousHandlers.foreach(h => root.withHandler(h))
+      root.replace()
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def callWithTimeout(
+      method: Method,
+      future: Future[_],
+      length: Int,
+      reason: Option[String],
+  ): Future[_] = {
+    val instance = enrich(future)
+    method
+      .invoke(instance, Int.box(length), TimeUnit.SECONDS, reason, ec)
+      .asInstanceOf[Future[_]]
+  }
+
+  test("withTimeout logs the reason when the future times out") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("withTimeout")
+    val reason = "connecting to the build server"
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val timed = callWithTimeout(method, neverCompleting[Unit], 1, Some(reason))
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isFailure && result.failed.get.isInstanceOf[TimeoutException],
+      s"Expected the future to time out, got: $result",
+    )
+    val reasonLogs = logs.filter { case (_, text) => text.contains(reason) }
+    assert(
+      reasonLogs.nonEmpty,
+      s"Expected the Metals logger to contain the timeout reason '$reason', " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("onTimeout logs the reason when the future times out") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("onTimeout")
+    val reason = "waiting for a response to the shutdown request"
+    val noOp: () => Unit = () => ()
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val instance = enrich(neverCompleting[Unit])
+      val timed = method
+        .invoke(
+          instance,
+          Int.box(1),
+          TimeUnit.SECONDS,
+          Some(reason),
+          noOp,
+          ec,
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[Future[_]]
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isFailure && result.failed.get.isInstanceOf[TimeoutException],
+      s"Expected the future to time out, got: $result",
+    )
+    val reasonLogs = logs.filter { case (_, text) => text.contains(reason) }
+    assert(
+      reasonLogs.nonEmpty,
+      s"Expected the Metals logger to contain the timeout reason '$reason', " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("onTimeout runs the supplied action exactly once on timeout") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("onTimeout")
+    val counter = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger(0)
+    val action: () => Unit = () => { counter.incrementAndGet(); () }
+    val (result, _) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val instance = enrich(neverCompleting[Unit])
+      val timed = method
+        .invoke(
+          instance,
+          Int.box(1),
+          TimeUnit.SECONDS,
+          None,
+          action,
+          ec,
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[Future[_]]
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isFailure && result.failed.get.isInstanceOf[TimeoutException],
+      s"Expected the future to time out, got: $result",
+    )
+    assertEquals(
+      counter.get(),
+      1,
+      "Expected the onTimeout action to run exactly once on timeout",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("onTimeout does not run the action when the future completes") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("onTimeout")
+    val counter = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger(0)
+    val action: () => Unit = () => { counter.incrementAndGet(); () }
+    val (result, _) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val instance = enrich(Future.successful(()))
+      val timed = method
+        .invoke(
+          instance,
+          Int.box(30),
+          TimeUnit.SECONDS,
+          None,
+          action,
+          ec,
+        )
+        .asInstanceOf[Future[_]]
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isSuccess,
+      s"Expected the future to complete successfully, got: $result",
+    )
+    assertEquals(
+      counter.get(),
+      0,
+      "Expected the onTimeout action not to run when the future completes",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("withTimeout logs the timeout reason at error level") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("withTimeout")
+    val reason = "initializing the workspace"
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val timed = callWithTimeout(method, neverCompleting[Unit], 1, Some(reason))
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isFailure && result.failed.get.isInstanceOf[TimeoutException],
+      s"Expected the future to time out, got: $result",
+    )
+    val reasonLogs = logs.filter { case (_, text) => text.contains(reason) }
+    assert(
+      reasonLogs.nonEmpty,
+      s"Expected the Metals logger to contain the timeout reason '$reason', " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+    assert(
+      reasonLogs.exists { case (level, _) => level.equalsIgnoreCase("error") },
+      s"Expected the timeout reason '$reason' to be logged at error level, " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("withTimeout completes with the original value before the timeout") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("withTimeout")
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val timed = callWithTimeout(method, Future.successful(42), 30, Some("unused"))
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assertEquals(
+      result.toOption,
+      Some(42),
+      s"Expected the future to complete with its original value, got: $result",
+    )
+    assert(
+      !logs.exists { case (_, text) => text.toLowerCase.contains("timeout") },
+      s"Expected nothing about a timeout to be logged on success, " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("withTimeout does not log a reason when the future completes") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("withTimeout")
+    val reason = "completing successfully"
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val completed = callWithTimeout(method, Future.successful(()), 30, Some(reason))
+      awaitResult(completed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isSuccess,
+      s"Expected the future to complete successfully, got: $result",
+    )
+    assert(
+      !logs.exists { case (_, text) => text.contains(reason) },
+      s"Expected no timeout reason to be logged on success, " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+
+  test("withTimeout without a reason does not log a timeout message") {
+    val method = requireReasonOverload("withTimeout")
+    val (result, logs) = withCapturedMetalsLog {
+      val timed = callWithTimeout(method, neverCompleting[Unit], 1, None)
+      awaitResult(timed)
+    }
+    assert(
+      result.isFailure && result.failed.get.isInstanceOf[TimeoutException],
+      s"Expected the future to time out, got: $result",
+    )
+    assert(
+      !logs.exists { case (_, text) => text.toLowerCase.contains("timeout while") },
+      s"Expected no timeout-reason message when no reason is provided, " +
+        s"but the captured logs were: $logs",
+    )
+  }
+}
