+module Companion.Tests.RequestCaptureTests
+
+#nowarn "3261"
+#nowarn "3264"
+#nowarn "3559"
+#nowarn "1182"
+
+// The addendum deliberately leaves production symbol names unspecified.  These tests discover
+// the public capture and observation operations by their HTTP signatures, then use a test-owned
+// transformer to retain the exact request instance from a real FSI Run.  Every body shape is
+// sent twice against the recorder — once plain, once with the capture installed — and the two
+// received recordings are compared byte for byte, so a capture that reads a nested part's
+// headers (materialising a Content-Length into that part) fails the comparison.
+
+open System
+open System.Collections.Generic
+open System.IO
+open System.Net.Http
+open System.Reflection
+open System.Text
+open System.Threading.Tasks
+open Microsoft.FSharp.Reflection
+open Expecto
+open Companion.Tests.TestServer
+
+type RunProbe =
+    static let seen = ResizeArray<HttpRequestMessage>()
+    static member Record(message: HttpRequestMessage) =
+        lock seen (fun () -> seen.Add message)
+        message
+    static member Clear() = lock seen (fun () -> seen.Clear())
+    static member Take() = lock seen (fun () -> List.ofSeq seen)
+
+type private Observation = ObsNoBody | ObsCaptured of byte[] | ObsNotCaptured of string
+
+type private UnknownLengthContent() =
+    inherit HttpContent()
+    override _.SerializeToStreamAsync(stream, _) =
+        let bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes "unknown-length"
+        stream.WriteAsync(bytes, 0, bytes.Length)
+    override _.SerializeToStream(stream, _, _) =
+        let bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes "unknown-length"
+        stream.Write(bytes, 0, bytes.Length)
+    override _.TryComputeLength(length: byref<int64>) = length <- 0L; false
+
+type private ThrowingContent() =
+    inherit HttpContent()
+    override _.SerializeToStreamAsync(_, _) = raise (InvalidOperationException "unreadable")
+    override _.SerializeToStream(_, _, _) = raise (InvalidOperationException "unreadable")
+    override _.TryComputeLength(length: byref<int64>) = length <- 4L; true
+
+/// A capture probe: every asynchronous read faults, so the capture's `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`
+/// always fails and must be declined. `AllowNextSyncSend` then lets exactly the synchronous
+/// serialization (the send itself) write the payload — a failed capture must never break a
+/// Run that would otherwise have succeeded.
+type private ReadOnceThrowingContent() =
+    inherit HttpContent()
+    let mutable allowSyncSend = false
+    member _.AllowNextSyncSend() = allowSyncSend <- true
+    override _.SerializeToStreamAsync(_, _) =
+        Task.FromException(InvalidOperationException "unreadable")
+    override _.SerializeToStream(stream, _, _) =
+        if not allowSyncSend then
+            raise (InvalidOperationException "unreadable")
+        let bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes "recovered"
+        stream.Write(bytes, 0, bytes.Length)
+    override _.TryComputeLength(length: byref<int64>) = length <- 9L; true
+
+let private utf8 (s: string) = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes s
+
+let private types () =
+    AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()
+    |> Array.filter (fun a -> a.GetName().Name = "Companion")
+    |> Array.collect (fun a ->
+        try a.GetTypes()
+        with
+        | :? ReflectionTypeLoadException as e -> e.Types |> Array.choose (fun t -> if isNull t then None else Some t)
+        | _ -> [||])
+
+let private methods () =
+    types ()
+    |> Array.collect (fun t ->
+        try t.GetMethods(BindingFlags.Static ||| BindingFlags.Public ||| BindingFlags.NonPublic)
+        with _ -> [||])
+
+let private oneMessageArg (m: MethodInfo) =
+    try m.GetParameters() |> Array.map (fun p -> p.ParameterType) = [| typeof<HttpRequestMessage> |]
+    with _ -> false
+
+let private decode (value: obj) =
+    let case, fields = FSharpValue.GetUnionFields(value, value.GetType())
+    match case.Name, fields with
+    | "NoBody", [||] -> ObsNoBody
+    | "Captured", [| bytes |] ->
+        let bytes = bytes :?> (byte[] | null)
+        if isNull bytes then failtest "captured body must not be null" else ObsCaptured bytes
+    | "NotCaptured", [| reason |] ->
+        let reason = reason :?> (string | null)
+        if isNull reason then failtest "decline reason must not be null" else ObsNotCaptured reason
+    | shape -> failtestf "unsupported body observation: %A" shape
+
+/// Wraps a `use` binding so it can appear as one expression inside a test's computation
+/// expression (Expecto's { } builder rejects a bare parenthesised `use` group).
+let private captureParen (f: unit -> 'a) : 'a = f ()
+
+/// Outer None: no observer exists in the companion. Inner None: the contract's safe lookup miss.
+let private lookup (message: HttpRequestMessage) : Observation option option =
+    methods ()
+    |> Array.filter (fun m ->
+        oneMessageArg m
+        && m.ReturnType.IsGenericType
+        && m.ReturnType.GetGenericTypeDefinition() = typedefof<option<_>>)
+    |> Array.tryPick (fun m ->
+        try
+            match m.Invoke(null, [| box message |]) with
+            | null -> Some None
+            | value ->
+                let case, fields = FSharpValue.GetUnionFields(value, value.GetType())
+                if case.Name = "Some" && fields.Length = 1 then
+                    let body = fields.[0]
+                    if isNull body then None else Some(Some(decode body))
+                elif case.Name = "None" then Some None
+                else None
+        with _ -> None)
+
+let private requireLookup message =
+    match lookup message with
+    | Some result -> result
+    | None -> failtest "no public request-body observation operation was found"
+
+/// Applies the production capture to `message` and returns the entry it stored.  The accepted
+/// operation must return the very same instance, so the send itself is untouched by it.
+let private capture (message: HttpRequestMessage) : Observation =
+    methods ()
+    |> Array.filter (fun m -> oneMessageArg m && m.ReturnType = typeof<HttpRequestMessage>)
+    |> Array.tryPick (fun m ->
+        try
+            let returned = m.Invoke(null, [| box message |]) :?> (HttpRequestMessage | null)
+            if not (isNull returned) && Object.ReferenceEquals(returned, message) then
+                match lookup message with
+                | Some(Some body) -> Some body
+                | _ -> None
+            else None
+        with _ -> None)
+    |> Option.defaultWith (fun () -> failtest "no working request capture operation was found")
+
+/// The temporary file behind the "body file" shape, created once for the suite.
+let private uploadFilePath : string =
+    let path = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "capture-upload-" + Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".bin")
+    File.WriteAllBytes(path, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes "from-file")
+    path
+
+let private streamedReasonText =
+    "streamed body — not captured, so that the upload is unchanged"
+
+let private capturedBody (expected: byte[]) = function
+    | ObsCaptured actual -> Expect.equal actual expected "captured body"
+    | other -> failtestf "expected captured bytes, got %A" other
+
+let private noBodyEntry = function
+    | ObsNoBody -> ()
+    | other -> failtestf "expected no body, got %A" other
+
+let private declinedReason = function
+    | ObsNotCaptured reason ->
+        Expect.isFalse (String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace reason) "declined bodies have a written reason"
+        reason
+    | other -> failtestf "expected a declined capture, got %A" other
+
+let private overCapReason body = declinedReason body
+
+let private streamedDecline name body =
+    let reason = declinedReason body
+    Expect.equal reason streamedReasonText (name + " states the streamed reason")
+
+let private sendOnce (server: TestServer) (makeMessage: string -> HttpRequestMessage) =
+    use client = new HttpClient()
+    use message = makeMessage (server.BaseUrl + "/probe")
+    use response = client.Send(message)
+    Expect.equal (int response.StatusCode) 200 "local server response"
+
+/// Sends one body shape twice against the recorder — once plain, once with the capture
+/// installed — and asserts the server received byte-identical payloads and headers both times.
+/// Both requests are independently constructed, so the comparison catches any header the
+/// capture materialises into a sent instance (including a nested multipart part's
+/// Content-Length, whose appearance grows the payload on the wire).  Returns the entry stored
+/// for a third, capture-only instance of the same shape.
+let private wireUnchanged (makeMessage: string -> HttpRequestMessage) : Observation =
+    let payloads = ResizeArray<byte[]>()
+    let combinedHeaders = ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>()
+    use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/probe", recordingFullHandler payloads combinedHeaders ])
+    sendOnce server makeMessage
+
+    captureParen (fun () ->
+        use captured = makeMessage (server.BaseUrl + "/probe")
+        capture captured |> ignore
+        sendOnce server (fun _ -> captured))
+
+    Expect.equal payloads.Count 2 "plain and captured sends should each hit the server"
+    Expect.equal payloads.[1] payloads.[0] "the capture must not change the bytes the server receives"
+    Expect.equal (List.ofSeq combinedHeaders.[1]) (List.ofSeq combinedHeaders.[0]) "the capture must not change the headers the server receives"
+
+    use probe = makeMessage "http://example.invalid/"
+    capture probe
+
+let private recorderSource =
+    String.concat "\n"
+        [ "let __fsHttpStudioTestRecorder (m: System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage) ="
+          "    try"
+          "        System.AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()"
+          "        |> Array.collect (fun a -> try a.GetTypes() with _ -> [||])"
+          "        |> Array.tryPick (fun t ->"
+          "            if t.Name <> \"RunProbe\" then None"
+          "            else"
+          "                let x = t.GetMethod \"Record\""
+          "                if isNull x then None else Some x)"
+          "        |> function"
+          "            | Some x -> x.Invoke(null, [| box m |]) :?> System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage"
+          "            | None -> m"
+          "    with _ -> m" ]
+
+let private runAndRecord (server: TestServer) =
+    RunProbe.Clear()
+    let source =
+        String.concat "\n"
+            [ "#r \"nuget: FsHttp, 15.0.3\""
+              "open FsHttp"
+              recorderSource
+              "http {"
+              (sprintf "    GET \"%s/probe\"" server.BaseUrl)
+              "    config_transformHttpRequestMessage __fsHttpStudioTestRecorder"
+              "}"
+              "" ]
+    match Companion.BlockRunner.runInProcessDirect source 0 None 0 with
+    | Companion.BlockRunner.Ok _ -> RunProbe.Take()
+    | other -> failtestf "instrumented Run should complete, got %A" other
+
+[<NoComparison; NoEquality>]
+type private Shape =
+    { Name: string
+      Expected: byte[] option
+      Make: string -> HttpRequestMessage }
+
+let private shapes : Shape list =
+    [ { Name = "byte array with an explicit content type"
+        Expected = Some(utf8 "binary-payload")
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            let c = new ByteArrayContent(utf8 "binary-payload")
+            c.Headers.ContentType <- System.Net.Http.Headers.MediaTypeHeaderValue("application/octet-stream")
+            m.Content <- c
+            m }
+      { Name = "get"
+        Expected = None
+        Make = fun url -> new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url) }
+      { Name = "json"
+        Expected = Some(utf8 """{"kind":"json"}""")
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            m.Content <- new StringContent("""{"kind":"json"}""", Encoding.UTF8, "application/json")
+            m }
+      { Name = "binary"
+        Expected = Some [| 0uy; 1uy; 2uy; 255uy |]
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            m.Content <- new ByteArrayContent [| 0uy; 1uy; 2uy; 255uy |]
+            m }
+      { Name = "form"
+        Expected = Some(utf8 "a=one&b=two")
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            m.Content <- new FormUrlEncodedContent([ KeyValuePair("a", "one"); KeyValuePair("b", "two") ])
+            m }
+      { Name = "text multipart"
+        Expected = Some(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes "--test-boundary\r\nContent-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=field\r\n\r\nhello\r\n--test-boundary--\r\n")
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            let mp = new MultipartFormDataContent("test-boundary")
+            mp.Add(new StringContent("hello"), "field")
+            m.Content <- mp
+            m }
+      { Name = "stream multipart"
+        Expected = None
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            let mp = new MultipartFormDataContent("test-boundary")
+            mp.Add(new StringContent("meta"), "field")
+            mp.Add(new StreamContent(new MemoryStream(utf8 "file-bytes")), "file", "f.bin")
+            m.Content <- mp
+            m }
+      { Name = "body stream"
+        Expected = None
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            m.Content <- new StreamContent(new MemoryStream(utf8 "from-stream"))
+            m }
+      { Name = "body file"
+        Expected = None
+        Make = fun url ->
+            let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+            m.Content <- new StreamContent(File.OpenRead uploadFilePath)
+            m } ]
+
+[<Tests>]
+let tests =
+    testList "RequestCapture"
+        [ test "an actual Run captures the exact request instance retained by a test transformer" {
+              let received = ResizeArray<byte[]>()
+              let headers = ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>()
+              use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/probe", recordingFullHandler received headers ])
+              let messages = runAndRecord server
+              Expect.equal received.Count 1 "the instrumented Run reaches the local server once"
+              let found =
+                  messages
+                  |> List.exists (fun message ->
+                      match requireLookup message with
+                      | Some ObsNoBody -> true
+                      | _ -> false)
+              Expect.isTrue found "the installed capture stored the exact Run message seen by test support"
+          }
+
+          test "every body shape reaches the server byte-identically, with or without capture" {
+              for shape in shapes do
+                  let body = wireUnchanged shape.Make
+                  match shape.Expected with
+                  | Some expected -> capturedBody expected body
+                  | None when shape.Name = "get" -> noBodyEntry body
+                  | None -> streamedDecline shape.Name body
+          }
+
+          test "the cap stores the exact boundary and the exact over-cap reason, and the send stays complete" {
+              let atCap = Array.create 1_048_576 42uy
+              use atMessage = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "http://example.invalid/at")
+              atMessage.Content <- new ByteArrayContent(atCap)
+              capture atMessage |> capturedBody atCap
+
+              let received = ResizeArray<byte[]>()
+              let headers = ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>()
+              use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/probe", recordingFullHandler received headers ])
+              let over = Array.create 1_048_577 43uy
+              use overMessage = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, server.BaseUrl + "/probe")
+              overMessage.Content <- new ByteArrayContent(over)
+              let reason = overCapReason (capture overMessage)
+              Expect.equal reason "body too large to show (1.0 MB)" "over-cap reason"
+              sendOnce server (fun _ -> overMessage)
+              Expect.equal received.Count 1 "the over-cap body reaches the server once"
+              Expect.equal received.[0] over "the over-cap body reaches the server in full"
+          }
+
+          test "two requests correlate by requestMessage identity, and a miss is safe" {
+              use first = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "http://example.invalid/first")
+              use second = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "http://example.invalid/second")
+              first.Content <- new StringContent("first")
+              second.Content <- new StringContent("second")
+              capture first |> ignore
+              capture second |> ignore
+              requireLookup first
+              |> Option.defaultWith (fun () -> failtest "first missing")
+              |> capturedBody (utf8 "first")
+              requireLookup second
+              |> Option.defaultWith (fun () -> failtest "second missing")
+              |> capturedBody (utf8 "second")
+              use missed = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "http://example.invalid/miss")
+              match requireLookup missed with
+              | None -> ()
+              | Some other -> failtestf "a lookup miss must be None, got %A" other
+          }
+
+          test "unknown length declines in its own words, and the send is unchanged by the capture" {
+              let received = ResizeArray<byte[]>()
+              let headers = ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>()
+              use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/probe", recordingFullHandler received headers ])
+              sendOnce server (fun url ->
+                  let m = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
+                  m.Content <- new UnknownLengthContent()
+                  m)
+              captureParen (fun () ->
+                  use captured = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, server.BaseUrl + "/probe")
+                  captured.Content <- new UnknownLengthContent()
+                  let reason = declinedReason (capture captured)
+                  Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "streamed body") "unknown length is not streamed"
+                  Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "body too large") "unknown length is not oversized"
+                  sendOnce server (fun _ -> captured))
+              Expect.equal received.Count 2 "plain and captured sends should each hit the server"
+              Expect.equal received.[1] received.[0] "unknown-length bytes are unchanged by the capture"
+              Expect.equal (List.ofSeq headers.[1]) (List.ofSeq headers.[0]) "unknown-length headers are unchanged by the capture"
+              Expect.equal received.[0] (utf8 "unknown-length") "the unknown-length body arrives in full"
+          }
+
+          test "a read failure declines in its own words, and the throw cannot reach the send" {
+              use declined = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "http://example.invalid/unreadable")
+              declined.Content <- new ThrowingContent()
+              let reason = declinedReason (capture declined)
+              Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "streamed body") "unreadable is not streamed"
+              Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "body too large") "unreadable is not oversized"
+
+              let received = ResizeArray<byte[]>()
+              let headers = ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>()
+              use server = new TestServer(Map [ "/probe", recordingFullHandler received headers ])
+              use client = new HttpClient()
+              use message = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, server.BaseUrl + "/probe")
+              let content = new ReadOnceThrowingContent()
+              message.Content <- content
+              let reason =
+                  match capture message with
+                  | ObsNotCaptured reason -> reason
+                  | other -> failtestf "a failed read must be declined, got %A" other
+              Expect.isFalse (String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace reason) "declined bodies have a written reason"
+              Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "streamed body") "failed read is not streamed"
+              Expect.isFalse (reason.Contains "body too large") "failed read is not oversized"
+              content.AllowNextSyncSend()
+              use response = client.Send(message)
+              Expect.equal (int response.StatusCode) 200 "the send after a failed capture completes"
+              Expect.equal received.Count 1 "the recovered send reaches the server once"
+              Expect.equal received.[0] (utf8 "recovered") "the send after a failed capture arrives in full"
+          } ]

--- a/tests/companion.Tests/TestServer.fs
+++ b/tests/companion.Tests/TestServer.fs
@@ -140,3 +140,16 @@ let streamingBytesHandler (contentType: string) (bytes: byte[]) (ctx: HttpListen
         off <- off + n
 
     ctx.Response.OutputStream.Close()
+
+/// Test-only request recorder for capture wire-identity assertions: stores each received
+/// request's payload plus the combined request/content headers, then answers `200 OK`.
+let recordingFullHandler (payloads: ResizeArray<byte[]>) (headers: ResizeArray<ResizeArray<string>>) (ctx: HttpListenerContext) =
+    use ms = new IO.MemoryStream()
+    ctx.Request.InputStream.CopyTo ms
+    let bytes = ms.ToArray()
+    let headerPairs = ResizeArray<string>()
+    for key in ctx.Request.Headers.AllKeys do
+        if isNull (box key) then headerPairs.Add "" else headerPairs.Add(sprintf "%O: %s" key ctx.Request.Headers.[key])
+    lock payloads (fun () -> payloads.Add bytes)
+    lock headers (fun () -> headers.Add headerPairs)
+    textHandler 200 "ok" ctx
FAIL_TO_PASS: RequestCapture.the cap stores the exact boundary and the exact over-cap reason, and the send stays complete

RequestCapture.unknown length declines in its own words, and the send is unchanged by the capture
RequestCapture.a read failure declines in its own words, and the throw cannot reach the send
RequestCapture.every body shape reaches the server byte-identically, with or without capture
RequestCapture.an actual Run captures the exact request instance retained by a test transformer

problem_statement:
Companion: read the request off requestMessage and put it on the wire
## Parent

Sub-issue of #99. Full spec: docs/spec/0012-request-as-sent.md, Implementation Decisions 1-3, 9-10, Testing Decisions Seam 1 (test 6).

## What to build

`extractResponse` reads the method, URL, and headers off `Response.requestMessage` (a BCL `HttpRequestMessage`) instead of anything derived from source text: method via `Method.ToString()`, URL via `RequestUri.AbsoluteUri` (not `ToString()`, which decodes percent-escapes), headers from `requestMessage.Headers` plus `requestMessage.Content.Headers` when present, joined and deduped the same way response headers already are. The request body comes from the `CapturedBody` correlated in #199, looked up by the same `requestMessage` instance.

`RunOutcome.Ok`'s five-field tuple becomes two records — `RequestData` (method, url, headers, body) and `ResponseData` (status, reason, headers, contentType, bodyBase64, requestMs) — since it is about to carry ten-plus fields between this ticket and #98. `outcomeToWire` and `wireToOutcome` both grow a `request` object on the `ok` envelope, with `bodyState` one of `"none"`, `"captured"`, `"notCaptured"`, and `bodyBase64`/`bodyReason` populated only for the matching state. Both wire directions — `RequestHandler`'s response to the host, and the `--worker` child's frame — go through these same two functions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RequestData` and `ResponseData` record types replace the `Ok` tuple in `RunOutcome`.
- [ ] For a computed URL with a query string, the extracted URL preserves percent-escaping (e.g. `?q=one%20two`, not `?q=one two`) — the defect this spec exists to fix.
- [ ] Request headers include ones the HTTP stack added (e.g. `Accept-Encoding`), not only ones FsHttp/the script set.
- [ ] A request with a captured body, a streamed/uncaptured body, and no body each round-trip through `outcomeToWire` then `wireToOutcome` with the correct `bodyState` and matching payload.
- [ ] `requestMessage` being null never occurs on a successful Run in the test coverage (per the spec's own measurement, this is not expected, but the mapping code does not assume it silently).

## Blocked by

#199 (needs `CapturedBody` and the correlation table).

### Additional contract requirements

- The wire mapping must be exercised only through shipped behavior — for example, an outcome
  that crosses the worker child-to-parent frame — not by calling internal serialization or
  body-mapping helpers directly. An implementation is not required to make those helpers
  visible outside the shipped module.
- A request with no body, an in-memory (captured) body, and a streamed body each round-trip
  across the worker frame with their documented body state: a captured body keeps its bytes,
  and a streamed body reports its uncaptured state with the streamed-body reason.
- No behavior is specified for a capture-table lookup that misses, and no additional
  uncaptured-reason literal is required beyond the documented ones.
- Tests must not require any particular handling of an unrecognized body state value on the
  wire, such as throwing rather than mapping it to a known state.

index 958037f..300370a 100644
--- a/docs/spec/0012-request-as-sent.md
+++ b/docs/spec/0012-request-as-sent.md
@@ -234,8 +234,14 @@ request. So the capture stores into a
 the `requestMessage` it already holds. Exact, and the weak table cannot leak.
 
 A lookup that misses yields the "not captured" state of Decision 8 rather than an error. The method,
-URL, and headers do not depend on the capture at all, so a miss degrades to a Request section with
-no body — never to a broken status line.
+URL, and headers do not depend on the capture at all, so a miss degrades to a Request section that
+shows no body — never to a broken status line.
+
+The content of the `requestMessage` decides which blank state a miss degrades to, not the miss
+itself. A message with no content sent no body, so "no body" is true of it. A message with content
+did send a body, so a miss there is the "not captured" state, and it carries the fifth reason of
+Decision 8. A Request section that shows "no body" for a POST states something false about a real
+body.
 
 ### 8. The body is a three-state value, not a string
 
@@ -249,16 +255,18 @@ type CapturedBody =
     | NotCaptured of reason: string
 ```
 
-`reason` is one of four written strings, and it is shown to the user:
+`reason` is one of five written strings, and it is shown to the user:
 
 - `"streamed body — not captured, so that the upload is unchanged"`
 - `"body too large to show (%s)"`, with the size rendered by the existing `humanSize`.
 - `"body length unknown — not captured, so that the send is unchanged"`, for the absent
   `Content-Length` of Decision 6.
 - `"body could not be read, so it is not shown"`, for a content that throws on read.
+- `"body was not captured, so it is not shown"`, for the missed lookup of Decision 7. The capture
+  never ran, so the companion knows nothing about this body beyond the fact that it was sent.
 
-The last two reasons each name their own condition. One string for all four conditions would tell a
-user that a body was streamed when it was not, and the viewer would state something that is false.
+The last three reasons each name their own condition. One string for all five conditions would tell
+a user that a body was streamed when it was not, and the viewer would state something that is false.
 
 The capture must not throw. It runs inside the user's send, so an exception from an exotic
 `HttpContent` would fail a Run that would otherwise succeed. A failed capture costs the body display
diff --git a/src/companion/BlockRunner.fs b/src/companion/BlockRunner.fs
index 8c174e1..6481990 100644
--- a/src/companion/BlockRunner.fs
+++ b/src/companion/BlockRunner.fs
@@ -24,20 +24,31 @@ open FSharp.Compiler.Diagnostics
 open FSharp.Compiler.Interactive.Shell
 open Companion.BlockLocator
 open Companion.Envelope
+open Companion.RequestCapture
 
 type Diagnostic = { Message: string; Range: BlockRange }
 
+/// The request that was actually sent, read off `Response.requestMessage` plus the body
+/// capture (docs/spec/0012-request-as-sent.md, Decisions 1 and 9).
+type RequestData =
+    { Method: string
+      Url: string
+      Headers: (string * string) list
+      Body: CapturedBody }
+
+/// The response half of a successful Run. `RequestMs` is the invocation bracket only: the
+/// single `EvalExpressionNonThrowing` that sends the request
+/// (docs/spec/0004-run-path-robustness.md, Decision 7). It is not the host-side total.
+type ResponseData =
+    { Status: int
+      Reason: string
+      Headers: (string * string) list
+      ContentType: string

+
+              // 13.3.0 conflicts with the loaded pin, so these Runs route to a fresh worker.
+              // Their outcomes must cross the child-to-parent frame the worker emits.
+              let noBody = sourceFor "13.3.0" (sprintf "    GET \"%s/fast\"" server.BaseUrl)

+              let captured =

+              | other -> failtestf "worker POST expected ok, got %A" other

problem_statement:
Assert the absent-parseFailed compatibility rule
## Parent

Sub-issue of #101.

## What to build

The host must read an absent `parseFailed` property as `false`. `Companion.locate` implements the rule today. The decode sits in Fable interop (`json?parseFailed`), which `tests/host.Tests` cannot reach. The rule therefore ships unasserted.

The spec asks for the assertion. Testing item 12 of `docs/spec/0014-explain-missing-lenses.md` states: "An absent `parseFailed` property decodes to `false`. This is Decision 3's compatibility rule." The spec files the assertion under Seam 3, and Seam 3 drives `Protocol.fs`.

Split the decode in two. `Companion.locate` keeps the interop lookup, which reads the property off the response object. A pure function in `Protocol.fs` decides the flag from what the lookup found. `tests/host.Tests` drives the pure function.

The polarity is the reason that the rule matters. Decision 3 states that a companion which does not send the property must not light the syntax-error lens on each response. The rule protects one case: an old companion that talks to a new host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Protocol.fs` declares a pure function that decides `parseFailed` from an absent or a present value, with no Fable or VSCode interop.
- [ ] `Companion.locate` calls that function, and holds the interop lookup alone.
- [ ] `host.Tests` covers an absent value (`false`), a present `false` (`false`), and a present `true` (`true`).
- [ ] `dotnet build FsHttp.Studio.slnx` succeeds, and `dotnet test tests/host.Tests` passes.

## Notes

#219 shipped the wire and left this gap. #220 moves `State` and `statusText` into `Protocol.fs`. This ticket is a separate move, because #220 does not touch the decode.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

### Additional contract requirements

## Test-facing contract addition

The host's protocol module (`Protocol.fs`) exposes a pure helper named
`parseFailedOrDefault` that decides the parse-failed flag a `blocks` response carries.

- Signature: it takes a `bool option` and returns a `bool`. `None` represents a
  response in which the `parseFailed` property is absent, and `Some value` represents a
  response in which the property is present.
- Semantics: an absent value (`None`) decides `false`; a present `false` decides
  `false`; a present `true` decides `true`.
- The helper is pure and uses no Fable or VSCode interop, so it can be driven directly
  from the host test suite.

problem_statement:
TADA_FlagCoordinates: add flag if state/county/etc. metadata does not match coordinate location
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**

Flag data where the lat/long assigned to monitoring sites is NOT in the state and country included in metadata. This is available for WQX submissions as part of the QAQC service. It is the only piece of the WQX QAQC service not replicated in TADA (see WQXValidationService.Rmd.)

**New features and/or edits should include all the following work:**

-   [x] Create or edit the function/code.

-   [x] Document all code using line/inline and/or multi-line/block comments
    to describe what is does.

-   [x] Create or edit tests in tests/testthat folder to help prevent and/or 
    troubleshoot potential future issues.

-   [x] Create or edit the function documentation. Include working
    examples.

-   [x] Update or add the new functionality to the appropriate vignette
    (or create new one).

-   [ ] If function/code edits made as part of this issue impact other
    functions in the package or functionality in the shiny app, ensure
    those are updated as well.
    
-   [ ] Run TADA_UpdateAllRefs(), TADA_UpdateExampleData(), styler::style_pkg(),
    devtools::document(), and devtools::check() and address any new notes or 
    issues before creating a pull request.    

-   [x] Run more robust check for releases: devtools::check(manual = TRUE, 
    remote = TRUE, incoming = TRUE)

### Additional contract requirements

# Coordinate metadata checking

`TADA_FlagCoordinates()` accepts an optional `check_location_metadata` logical
argument, which defaults to `FALSE`. With the default, coordinate flagging
retains its existing behavior and does not require location-metadata fields.

When `check_location_metadata = TRUE`, input must contain `StateCode` and
`CountyCode` as well as the coordinate fields. Missing required fields and a
non-logical option value are errors.

For coordinates that can be associated with location metadata, non-missing
state and county values are compared with the associated values. State codes
compare as two-digit, zero-padded codes and county codes as three-digit,
zero-padded codes, so numerically equivalent unpadded or numeric inputs compare
equally. Missing metadata is not itself a mismatch, and coordinates with no
association receive no metadata-comparison flag.

`CountryCode`, if present, remains ordinary input metadata and is not compared.
Metadata checking preserves the usual coordinate-result columns and row order.
A state disagreement produces `Coordinate_StateMismatch`; otherwise a county
disagreement produces `Coordinate_CountyMismatch`. When another coordinate
flag already exists, the metadata flag is appended using `; `; otherwise it
replaces `Pass` in `TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag`.

diff --git a/tests/testthat/test-ResultFlagsIndependent.R b/tests/testthat/test-ResultFlagsIndependent.R
index dcb809d4..f1b9fe02 100644
--- a/tests/testthat/test-ResultFlagsIndependent.R
+++ b/tests/testthat/test-ResultFlagsIndependent.R
@@ -362,3 +362,239 @@ test_that("TADA_FlagAboveThreshold treats threshold equality as Pass", {
   res <- TADA_FlagAboveThreshold(dat)
   expect_equal(res$TADA.ResultValueAboveUpperThreshold.Flag, "Pass")
 })
+
+# The matching state and county are discovered from observable results, so these
+# checks do not prescribe a particular boundary-data provider.
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates compares state and county metadata", {
+  state_candidates <- sprintf("%02d", 1:56)
+  metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = rep(40.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = rep(-100.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    CountryCode = rep("CA", length(state_candidates)),
+    StateCode = state_candidates,
+    CountyCode = NA_character_
+  )
+
+  state_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(metadata, check_location_metadata = TRUE)
+  state_match <- state_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag == "Pass"
+  expect_equal(sum(state_match), 1L)
+  expect_true(any(state_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag == "Coordinate_StateMismatch"))
+
+  matching_state <- state_candidates[state_match]
+  normalized_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+      CountryCode = "CA",
+      StateCode = as.integer(matching_state),
+      CountyCode = NA_character_
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_equal(normalized_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, "Pass")
+  expect_equal(normalized_out$CountryCode, "CA")
+
+  # At least one of these distinct counties cannot be the resolved county.
+  # The coordinate is deliberately imprecise to also verify flag appending.
+  county_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = c(40.1, 40.1),
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = c(-100.1234, -100.1234),
+      StateCode = rep(as.integer(matching_state), 2),
+      CountyCode = c("001", "002")
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  county_flags <- county_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag
+  expect_false(any(grepl("Coordinate_StateMismatch", county_flags, fixed = TRUE)))
+  expect_true(any(
+    county_flags == "Imprecise_lessthan3decimaldigits; Coordinate_CountyMismatch"
+  ))
+})
+
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates keeps metadata checking opt-in and validates it", {
+  metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+    CountryCode = "CA",
+    StateCode = "99",
+    CountyCode = "999"
+  )
+
+  unchecked <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(metadata)
+  expect_equal(unchecked$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, "Pass")
+  expect_equal(unchecked$CountryCode, metadata$CountryCode)
+  expect_error(
+    TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+      dplyr::select(metadata, -StateCode),
+      check_location_metadata = TRUE
+    )
+  )
+  expect_error(TADA_FlagCoordinates(metadata, check_location_metadata = "TRUE"))
+})
+
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates normalizes county codes and preserves shape", {
+  state_candidates <- sprintf("%02d", 1:56)
+  state_metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = rep(40.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = rep(-100.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    StateCode = state_candidates,
+    CountyCode = NA_character_
+  )
+  matching_state <- state_candidates[
+    TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+      state_metadata,
+      check_location_metadata = TRUE
+    )$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag == "Pass"
+  ]
+
+  # Searching the complete valid county-code range derives the matching county
+  # from the documented behavior rather than embedding geographic ground truth.
+  county_candidates <- sprintf("%03d", 1:999)
+  county_metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = rep(40.1234, length(county_candidates)),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = rep(-100.1234, length(county_candidates)),
+    StateCode = rep(as.numeric(matching_state), length(county_candidates)),
+    CountyCode = county_candidates
+  )
+  county_flags <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    county_metadata,
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag
+  expect_false(any(grepl("Coordinate_StateMismatch", county_flags, fixed = TRUE)))
+  expect_equal(sum(county_flags == "Pass"), 1L)
+  expect_equal(sum(county_flags == "Coordinate_CountyMismatch"), 998L)
+
+  matching_county <- county_candidates[county_flags == "Pass"]
+  unpadded_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+      StateCode = as.numeric(matching_state),
+      CountyCode = as.numeric(matching_county)
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_equal(unpadded_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, "Pass")
+
+  mismatching_county <- county_candidates[
+    county_flags == "Coordinate_CountyMismatch"
+  ][1]
+  preserve_metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    row_marker = c("first", "second"),
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = c(40.1234, 40.1234),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = c(-100.1234, -100.1234),
+    StateCode = c(NA_character_, "99"),
+    CountyCode = c(mismatching_county, mismatching_county)
+  )
+  baseline_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(preserve_metadata)
+  preserve_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    preserve_metadata,
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+
+  # Missing state metadata is not itself a state mismatch; a supplied county
+  # is still compared. Metadata checking neither adds columns beyond the usual
+  # coordinate result nor changes row order.
+  expect_equal(
+    preserve_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag,
+    c("Coordinate_CountyMismatch", "Coordinate_StateMismatch")
+  )
+  expect_equal(names(preserve_out), names(baseline_out))
+  expect_equal(preserve_out$row_marker, baseline_out$row_marker)
+
+  precedence_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+      StateCode = "99",
+      CountyCode = mismatching_county
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_equal(precedence_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, "Coordinate_StateMismatch")
+  expect_equal(precedence_out$StateCode, "99")
+  expect_equal(precedence_out$CountyCode, mismatching_county)
+})
+
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates leaves unassociated coordinates unflagged", {
+  outside_metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = c(9.1234, 9.1234, 9.1234),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = c(-180.1234, -180.1234, -180.1234),
+    StateCode = c("36", "99", NA_character_),
+    CountyCode = c("007", "999", NA_character_)
+  )
+  outside_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    outside_metadata,
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_equal(outside_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, rep("Pass", 3))
+})
+
+# The default call must run without StateCode, CountyCode, or CountryCode
+# present, while opting into checking still requires both metadata fields.
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates only requires metadata when checking", {
+  coordinates_only <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234
+  )
+
+  default_out <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(coordinates_only)
+  expect_equal(default_out$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag, "Pass")
+  expect_error(
+    TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+      dplyr::tibble(
+        TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1234,
+        TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+        StateCode = "99"
+      ),
+      check_location_metadata = TRUE
+    )
+  )
+})
+
+# Metadata flags are appended to an existing coordinate flag for either
+# mismatch kind. The matching state is derived from observable results.
+test_that("TADA_FlagCoordinates appends both metadata flags", {
+  state_candidates <- sprintf("%02d", 1:56)
+  state_metadata <- dplyr::tibble(
+    TADA.LatitudeMeasure = rep(40.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    TADA.LongitudeMeasure = rep(-100.1234, length(state_candidates)),
+    StateCode = state_candidates,
+    CountyCode = NA_character_
+  )
+  matching_state <- state_candidates[
+    TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+      state_metadata,
+      check_location_metadata = TRUE
+    )$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag == "Pass"
+  ]
+
+  state_append <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = 40.1,
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = -100.1234,
+      StateCode = "99",
+      CountyCode = NA_character_
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_equal(
+    state_append$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag,
+    "Imprecise_lessthan3decimaldigits; Coordinate_StateMismatch"
+  )
+
+  county_append <- TADA_FlagCoordinates(
+    dplyr::tibble(
+      TADA.LatitudeMeasure = c(40.1, 40.1),
+      TADA.LongitudeMeasure = c(-100.1234, -100.1234),
+      StateCode = rep(as.integer(matching_state), 2),
+      CountyCode = c("001", "002")
+    ),
+    check_location_metadata = TRUE
+  )
+  expect_true(any(
+    county_append$TADA.SuspectCoordinates.Flag ==
+      "Imprecise_lessthan3decimaldigits; Coordinate_CountyMismatch"
+  ))
+})

### Additional contract requirements

The package must compile successfully, without errors, under its existing package
manifest and declared dependency versions (Swift tools 5.10, swift-collections from
1.0.5, Swift 6.2 compiler) with the `MemberImportVisibility` upcoming feature
enabled, as configured in the package manifest. In particular, building the
`AsyncKit` library target must not fail with
`[#MemberImportVisibility]` "not available due to missing import of defining
module" errors in `EventLoopConnectionPool`, and every use of the connection
pool's internal collections storage (initialization, iteration, removal, and
subscripting) must see the declarations of the modules that define them.

Because this failure occurs while building the library itself, a successful fix
allows the package's entire existing test suite to compile, and all of the
package's existing test cases then run and pass.

At runtime, the public `EventLoopConnectionPool` behavior must remain unchanged:

- `requestConnection()` opens new connections up to the `maxConnections` limit;
  requests beyond the limit wait until a connection is released, and a waiting
  request is fulfilled with a released connection (connections are returned to
  the pool for reuse rather than closed).
- `close()` closes the pool's open connections, fails every queued connection
  request with `ConnectionPoolError.shutdown`, and causes all subsequent
  connection requests to fail with `ConnectionPoolError.shutdown`.

contract_addendum:
The package must compile successfully, without errors, under its existing package
manifest and declared dependency versions (Swift tools 5.10, swift-collections from
1.0.5, Swift 6.2 compiler) with the `MemberImportVisibility` upcoming feature
enabled, as configured in the package manifest. In particular, building the
`AsyncKit` library target must not fail with
`[#MemberImportVisibility]` "not available due to missing import of defining
module" errors in `EventLoopConnectionPool`, and every use of the connection
pool's internal collections storage (initialization, iteration, removal, and
subscripting) must see the declarations of the modules that define them.

Because this failure occurs while building the library itself, a successful fix
allows the package's entire existing test suite to compile, and all of the
package's existing test cases then run and pass.

At runtime, the public `EventLoopConnectionPool` behavior must remain unchanged:

- `requestConnection()` opens new connections up to the `maxConnections` limit;
  requests beyond the limit wait until a connection is released, and a waiting
  request is fulfilled with a released connection (connections are returned to
  the pool for reuse rather than closed).
- `close()` closes the pool's open connections, fails every queued connection
  request with `ConnectionPoolError.shutdown`, and causes all subsequent
  connection requests to fail with `ConnectionPoolError.shutdown`.

+import Atomics
+import AsyncKit
+import Logging
+import NIOCore
+import NIOPosix
+import XCTest
+
+// Regression tests for the reported build-time failure of the
+// `EventLoopConnectionPool` build path (missing defining-module visibility of the
+// pool's internal collections storage). At runtime, these tests exercise the
+// storage-backed behaviors that the failed build path contains: capacity-limited
+// connection reuse, FIFO waiters, and waiter failure on close.
+final class ConnectionPoolBuildRegressionTests: XCTestCase {
+    var group: (any EventLoopGroup)!
+    var eventLoop: any EventLoop { self.group.any() }
+
+    override func setUpWithError() throws {
+        try super.setUpWithError()
+        self.group = MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup(numberOfThreads: 1)
+    }
+
+    override func tearDownWithError() throws {
+        try self.group.syncShutdownGracefully()
+        self.group = nil
+        try super.tearDownWithError()
+    }
+
+    func testPoolCapacityAndReuse() throws {
+        let source = BuildRegressionDatabase()
+        let pool = EventLoopConnectionPool(
+            source: source,
+            maxConnections: 2,
+            on: self.eventLoop
+        )
+        defer { try! pool.close().wait() }
+
+        let connA = try pool.requestConnection().wait()
+        let connB = try pool.requestConnection().wait()
+        XCTAssertFalse(connA.isClosed)
+        XCTAssertFalse(connB.isClosed)
+        XCTAssertEqual(source.connectionsCreated.load(ordering: .relaxed), 2)
+
+        // The pool is exhausted, so a third request must wait; releasing a
+        // connection must service the waiting request, reusing the released
+        // connection.
+        let futureC = pool.requestConnection()
+        pool.releaseConnection(connB)
+        XCTAssert(try futureC.wait() === connB)
+
+        pool.releaseConnection(connA)
+        pool.releaseConnection(connB)
+    }
+
+    func testPoolCloseFailsWaiters() throws {
+        let source = BuildRegressionDatabase()
+        let pool = EventLoopConnectionPool(
+            source: source,
+            maxConnections: 1,
+            on: self.eventLoop
+        )
+
+        let conn = try pool.requestConnection().wait()
+        let waiter = pool.requestConnection()
+        try pool.close().wait()
+
+        // Requests queued in the waitlist must fail when the pool closes.
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try waiter.wait()) {
+            XCTAssertEqual($0 as? ConnectionPoolError, .shutdown)
+        }
+
+        // New requests after shutdown must also fail.
+        XCTAssertThrowsError(try pool.requestConnection().wait()) {
+            XCTAssertEqual($0 as? ConnectionPoolError, .shutdown)
+        }
+
+        // Release the held connection after close; closing it must not crash.
+        pool.releaseConnection(conn)
+    }
+}
+
+private final class BuildRegressionDatabase: ConnectionPoolSource {
+    let connectionsCreated = ManagedAtomic(0)
+
+    func makeConnection(logger: Logger, on eventLoop: any EventLoop) -> EventLoopFuture<BuildRegressionConnection> {
+        self.connectionsCreated.wrappingIncrement(by: 1, ordering: .relaxed)
+        return eventLoop.makeSucceededFuture(BuildRegressionConnection(on: eventLoop))
+    }
+}
+
+private final class BuildRegressionConnection: ConnectionPoolItem {
+    let eventLoop: any EventLoop
+    var isClosed = false
+
+    init(on eventLoop: any EventLoop) {
+        self.eventLoop = eventLoop
+    }
+
+    func close() -> EventLoopFuture<Void> {
+        self.isClosed = true
+        return self.eventLoop.makeSucceededFuture(())
+    }
+}

problem_statement:
Block specific user
Users should have a feature to block specific users. Once blocked, the blocked user cannot follow the user, and the user will no longer see statuses from the blocked user on their timelines, including private, local, global, category, and hashtag feeds.

### Additional contract requirements

## Block specific users

This addendum defines the public API behavior for blocking accounts. All paths below are relative to `/api/v1` unless stated otherwise. A `:name` path parameter identifies an account and accepts either its normal name or its `@`-prefixed form.

### Block and unblock operations

- `POST /users/:name/block` creates a block from the authenticated account to the named account. Its JSON body must be an object with an optional `reason` string; `{}` is valid when no reason is supplied.
- `POST /users/:name/unblock` removes the authenticated account's block of the named account. It has no request body.
- Both operations return HTTP 200 with the normal relationship representation. That representation includes a boolean `blocked` field; it is true after a successful block and false after a successful unblock.
- Blocking an account that is already blocked and unblocking an account that is not blocked are successful, idempotent operations. A repeated block does not create a duplicate entry in the account's blocked-account list.
- A missing target account produces HTTP 404. Requests without an authenticated user produce HTTP 401.

Blocking ends an existing follow from the authenticated account to the blocked account. A Follow activity from a blocked account delivered to the shared ActivityPub inbox (`POST /shared/inbox`, without the `/api/v1` prefix) is acknowledged but creates neither an approved nor a pending follow toward the account that blocked it.

### Timeline behavior

For an authenticated account, statuses associated with accounts it has blocked are excluded from its home, public (unfiltered and local-only), category, and hashtag timelines. Statuses authored by a blocked account, reblogs of statuses authored by a blocked account, and reblogs made by a blocked account are all associated with it. Removing a reblog made by a blocked account does not remove the reblogged original status authored by an account that is not blocked; the original also remains visible to other accounts and anonymous users. A block removes matching entries already present in the blocking account's home timeline when the block is created, and matching new entries are not added thereafter. The block does not alter what other accounts or anonymous users can view on the public, category, or hashtag timelines.

### Blocked-account list

`GET /user-blocked-users` requires authentication and returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object wrapping the paginated collection of the blocks created by the authenticated account. The object carries:

- a `data` array with one entry per block created by the authenticated account;
- an integer `page` for the returned page number, an integer `size` for the page size, and an integer `total` for the overall number of blocks created by the authenticated account.

Each entry in `data` carries:

- an `id` string identifying the block;
- a `blockedUser` object identifying the blocked account, including its `id`, `userName`, and `name` members;
- an optional `reason` string holding the reason supplied when the block was created;
- `createdAt` and `updatedAt` timestamps for the block, encoded as ISO 8601 date-time strings (the same timestamp encoding used by the rest of the API).

Blocks created by other accounts are never included. An account with no blocks receives an empty `data` array and a `total` of `0`. Unauthenticated requests receive HTTP 401.

+//

+
+import Vapor
+import Fluent
+
+extension UserBlockedUsersController: RouteCollection {
+    
+    @_documentation(visibility: private)
+    static let uri: PathComponent = .constant("user-blocked-users")
+
+    func boot(routes: RoutesBuilder) throws {
+        let domainsGroup = routes
+            .grouped("api")
+            .grouped("v1")
+            .grouped(UserBlockedUsersController.uri)
+            .grouped(UserAuthenticator())
+            .grouped(UserPayload.guardMiddleware())
+
+        domainsGroup
+            .grouped(EventHandlerMiddleware(.userBlockedUsersList))
+            .grouped(CacheControlMiddleware(.noStore))
+            .get(use: list)
+    }
+}
+
+/// Controls basic operations for user blocked users.
+///
+/// > Important: Base controller URL: `/api/v1/user-blocked-users`.
+struct UserBlockedUsersController {
+
+    /// List of user's blocked users.
+    ///
+    /// The endpoint returns a list of all user's blocked users added to the system.
+    ///
+    /// Optional query params:
+    /// - `page` - number of page to return
+    /// - `size` - limit amount of returned entities on one page (default: 10)
+    ///
+    /// > Important: Endpoint URL: `/api/v1/user-blocked-users`.
+    ///
+    /// **CURL request:**
+    ///
+    /// ```bash
+    /// curl "https://example.com/api/v1/user-blocked-users" \
+    /// -X GET \
+    /// -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    /// -H "Authorization: Bearer [ACCESS_TOKEN]" \
+    /// ```
+    ///
+    /// **Example response body:**
+    ///
+    /// ```json
+    /// {
+    ///     "data": [
+    ///         {
+    ///             "id": "7267938074834522113",
+    ///             "blockedUser": { ... },
+    ///             "reason": "This is a porn website.",
+    ///             "createdAt": "2023-08-16T15:13:08.607Z",
+    ///             "updatedAt": "2024-02-09T05:12:23.479Z"
+    ///         },
+    ///         {
+    ///             "id": "7332804261530576897",
+    ///             "blockedUser": { ... },
+    ///             "reason": "Domain with spam",
+    ///             "createdAt": "2024-02-07T10:25:36.538Z",
+    ///             "updatedAt": "2024-02-07T10:25:36.538Z"
+    ///         }
+    ///     ],
+    ///     "page": 1,
+    ///     "size": 2,
+    ///     "total": 176
+    /// }
+    /// ```
+    ///
+    /// - Parameters:
+    ///   - request: The Vapor request to the endpoint.
+    ///
+    /// - Returns: List of paginable blocked domains.
+    @Sendable
+    func list(request: Request) async throws -> PaginableResultDto<UserBlockedUserDto> {
+        let baseImagesPath = request.application.services.storageService.getBaseImagesPath(on: request.executionContext)
+        let baseAddress = request.application.settings.cached?.baseAddress ?? ""
+
+        let page: Int = request.query["page"] ?? 0
+        let size: Int = request.query["size"] ?? 10
+        
+        let authorizationPayloadId = try request.requireUserId()
+        let blockedUsersFromDatabaseQuery = UserBlockedUser.query(on: request.db)
+            .filter(\.$user.$id == authorizationPayloadId)
+            .with(\.$blockedUser)
+
+        let blockedUsersFromDatabase = try await blockedUsersFromDatabaseQuery
+            .sort(\.$createdAt, .ascending)
+            .paginate(PageRequest(page: page, per: size))
+        
+        let blockedUserDtos = blockedUsersFromDatabase.items.map { blockedUser in
+            UserBlockedUserDto(from: blockedUser, baseImagesPath: baseImagesPath, baseAddress: baseAddress)
+        }
+
+        return PaginableResultDto(
+            data: blockedUserDtos,
+            page: blockedUsersFromDatabase.metadata.page,
+            size: blockedUsersFromDatabase.metadata.per,
+            total: blockedUsersFromDatabase.metadata.total
+        )
+    }
+}

+    /// Block specific user.
+    ///
+    /// An endpoint to block a user's account.
+    ///
+    /// > Important: Endpoint URL: `/api/v1/users/:userName/block`.
+    ///
+    /// **CURL request:**
+    ///
+    /// ```bash
+    /// curl "https://example.com/api/v1/users/@johndoe/block" \
+    /// -X POST \
+    /// -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    /// -H "Authorization: Bearer [ACCESS_TOKEN]" \
+    /// ```
+    ///
+    /// **Example request body:**
+    ///
+    /// ```json
+    /// {
+    ///     "reason": "This is a porn account."
+    /// }
+    /// ```
+    ///
+    /// - Parameters:
+    ///   - request: The Vapor request to the endpoint.
+    ///
+    /// - Returns: HTTP status code.
+    ///
+    /// - Throws: `EntityNotFoundError.userNotFound` if user not exists.
+    /// - Throws: `UserError.userNameIsRequired` if user name not specified.
+    @Sendable
+    func block(request: Request) async throws -> RelationshipDto {
+        let usersService = request.application.services.usersService
+        let followsService = request.application.services.followsService
+        let timelineService = request.application.services.timelineService
+        let userBlockRequestDto = try request.content.decode(UserBlockRequestDto.self)
+        
+        guard let userName = request.parameters.get("name") else {
+            throw UserError.userNameIsRequired
+        }
+        
+        let userNameNormalized = userName.deletingPrefix("@").uppercased()
+        guard let blockedUser = try await usersService.get(userName: userNameNormalized, on: request.db) else {
+            throw EntityNotFoundError.userNotFound
+        }
+
+        let authorizationPayloadId = try request.requireUserId()
+        guard let authorizationPayloadUser = try await usersService.get(id: authorizationPayloadId, on: request.db) else {
+            throw EntityNotFoundError.userNotFound
+        }
+        
+        let userBlockedUser = try await UserBlockedUser.query(on: request.db)
+            .filter(\.$user.$id == authorizationPayloadId)
+            .filter(\.$blockedUser.$id == blockedUser.requireID())
+            .first()
+        
+        if userBlockedUser == nil {
+            // Create a new block user if not exists.
+            let newUserBlockedId = request.application.services.snowflakeService.generate()
+            let newUserBlockedUser = try UserBlockedUser(id: newUserBlockedId,
+                                                         userId: authorizationPayloadId,
+                                                         blockedUserId: blockedUser.requireID(),
+                                                         reason: userBlockRequestDto.reason)
+            
+            try await newUserBlockedUser.save(on: request.db)
+        }
+        
+        // Delete follow from local database.
+        let followId = try await followsService.unfollow(sourceId: authorizationPayloadId,
+                                                         targetId: blockedUser.requireID(),
+                                                         on: request.executionContext)
+        
+        // If user follows blocked user.
+        if let followId {
+            try await usersService.updateFollowCount(for: authorizationPayloadId, on: request.db)
+            try await usersService.updateFollowCount(for: blockedUser.requireID(), on: request.db)
+            
+            // If target user is from remote server, notify remote server about unfollow (in background job).
+            if blockedUser.isLocal == false {
+                guard let privateKey = authorizationPayloadUser.privateKey else {
+                    throw ActivityPubError.privateKeyNotExists(authorizationPayloadUser.activityPubProfile)
+                }
+                
+                try await informRemote(on: request,
+                                       type: .unfollow,
+                                       source: authorizationPayloadUser.activityPubProfile,
+                                       target: blockedUser.activityPubProfile,
+                                       sharedInbox: blockedUser.userInbox,
+                                       withId: followId,
+                                       privateKey: privateKey)
+            }
+        }
+        
+        // We have to delete all user statuses from the user timeline.
+        try await timelineService.removeStatusesFromHomeTimeline(forUserId: authorizationPayloadId,
+                                                                 byUserId: blockedUser.requireID(),
+                                                                 on: request.executionContext)
+        
+        // We have to delete all muted user reblogs from the user timeline.
+        try await timelineService.removeReblogsFromTimeline(forUserId: authorizationPayloadId,
+                                                            byUserId: blockedUser.requireID(),
+                                                            on: request.executionContext)
+        
+        return try await self.relationship(sourceId: authorizationPayloadId, targetUser: blockedUser, on: request)
+    }
+

+        guard let userName = request.parameters.get("name") else {

+        }
+        
+        let userNameNormalized = userName.deletingPrefix("@").uppercased()
+        guard let blockedUser = try await usersService.get(userName: userNameNormalized, on: request.db) else {
+            throw EntityNotFoundError.userNotFound
+        }
+        
+        let authorizationPayloadId = try request.requireUserId()
+        let userBlockedUser = try await UserBlockedUser.query(on: request.db)
+            .filter(\.$user.$id == authorizationPayloadId)
+            .filter(\.$blockedUser.$id == blockedUser.requireID())
+            .first()
+        
+        if let userBlockedUser {
+            try await userBlockedUser.delete(on: request.db)
+        }
+        
+        return try await self.relationship(sourceId: authorizationPayloadId, targetUser: blockedUser, on: request)
+    }

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+//
+//  https://mczachurski.dev
+//  Copyright © 2026 Marcin Czachurski and the repository contributors.
+//  Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
+//
+
+import Vapor
+import Fluent
+import ActivityPubKit
+
+extension Application.Services {
+    struct UserBlockedUsersServiceKey: StorageKey {
+        typealias Value = UserBlockedUsersServiceType
+    }
+
+    var userBlockedUsersService: UserBlockedUsersServiceType {
+        get {
+            self.application.storage[UserBlockedUsersServiceKey.self] ?? UserBlockedUsersService()
+        }
+        nonmutating set {
+            self.application.storage[UserBlockedUsersServiceKey.self] = newValue
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+@_documentation(visibility: private)
+protocol UserBlockedUsersServiceType: Sendable {
+    /// Checks whether the given domain (host from URL) is blocked by the user.
+    /// - Parameters:
+    ///   - userId: Signed in user.
+    ///   - blockedUserId:Blocked user.
+    ///   - database: Database to perform the query on.
+    /// - Returns: True if the user is blocked by the signed in user.
+    /// - Throws: Database errors.
+    func exists(userId: Int64, blockedUserId: Int64, on database: Database) async throws -> Bool
+    
+    /// Returns list od blocked user Id's.
+    /// - Parameters:
+    ///   - userId: Signed in user.
+    ///   - database: Database to perform the query on.
+    /// - Returns: List of user ids which are blocked by signed in user.
+    /// - Throws: Database errors.
+    func blockedUsers(forUserId userId: Int64, on database: Database) async throws -> [Int64]
+}
+
+/// A service for managing domains blocked by the user.
+final class UserBlockedUsersService: UserBlockedUsersServiceType {
+    public func exists(userId: Int64, blockedUserId: Int64, on database: Database) async throws -> Bool {
+        let count = try await UserBlockedUser.query(on: database)
+            .filter(\.$user.$id == userId)
+            .filter(\.$blockedUser.$id == blockedUserId)
+            .count()
+
+        return count > 0
+    }
+    
+    public func blockedUsers(forUserId userId: Int64, on database: Database) async throws -> [Int64] {
+        let userBlocedUsers = try await UserBlockedUser.query(on: database)
+            .filter(\.$user.$id == userId)
+            .field(\.$blockedUser.$id)
+            .all()
+        
+        return userBlocedUsers.map({ $0.$blockedUser.id })
+    }
+}
+

### Description

Support for Flutter 3.44 and Dart 3.12

### Requirements

- [ ] All CI/CD checks are passing.
- [ ] There is no drop in the test coverage percentage.

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Additional contract requirements

Compatibility requirements for Flutter 3.44 / Dart 3.12 support:

- The root `pubspec.yaml` and the standalone package manifests under
  `tool/spdx_license` (`tool/spdx_license/pubspec.yaml` and
  `tool/spdx_license/hooks/pubspec.yaml`) must each declare a Dart SDK
  environment constraint that admits Dart `3.12.0`, expressed as an
  explicit version range whose minimum (lower bound) version is `3.12.0`
  or later within the Dart 3 line, and whose range remains bounded to the
  Dart 3 line (it must not admit Dart `4.0.0` or later). Any standard
  constraint form that satisfies these properties is acceptable (for
  example `^3.12.0` or `>=3.12.0 <4.0.0`); the formatting or indentation
  of the `environment` section does not matter.
- Continuous integration configuration under `.github/workflows/` must
  provision toolchains consistent with the upgrade:
  - Workflows that set up a Dart SDK toolchain must declare Dart versions
    of `3.12.0` or newer within the Dart 3 line. This applies to
    `bump_templates.yaml`, `pub_publish.yaml`, and `spdx_license.yaml`;
    every Dart toolchain entry declared in those workflows must meet the
    requirement, and additional compatible Dart toolchain entries are
    acceptable.
  - Workflows that set up a Flutter toolchain must request the Flutter
    `3.44` release line (for example `3.44.0` or `3.44.x`). This applies
    to `spdx_license_bot.yaml` and `very_good_cli.yaml`; every Flutter
    toolchain entry declared in those workflows must meet the requirement,
    and additional compatible Flutter toolchain entries are acceptable.

problem_statement:
feat: support --(no-)workspace flag for monorepo packages
### Description

To add support for [Pub Workspaces](https://dart.dev/tools/pub/workspaces) in our templates, we need to add a boolean `workspace` flag (can have a `ws` alias) to add the necessary configuration for the package to look up its parent workspace. 

This is the configuration the flag should wrap:

```yaml
environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.0
resolution: workspace # new configuration to wrap in pubspec.yaml
```

To add the package to the workspace, there will be another issue created in the CLI project. The scope of this is just adding the configuration for the templates.

### Requirements

- [ ] All CI/CD checks are passing.
- [ ] There is no drop in the test coverage percentage.

### Additional Context

https://github.com/VeryGoodOpenSource/very_good_cli/issues/1635

### Additional contract requirements

# Contract Addendum

This addendum clarifies the observable CLI behavior of the workspace
scaffolding feature beyond the base problem statement. It prescribes no
implementation mechanism and no internal naming choices, and it deliberately
leaves open how the option value reaches the generated templates.

## Affected commands

The workspace option applies to exactly the following seven
`very_good create` scaffold subcommands:

- `app_ui_package`
- `dart_cli`
- `dart_package`
- `flame_game`
- `flutter_app`
- `flutter_package`
- `flutter_plugin`

No other `create` subcommand (for example `docs_site`) is required to accept
a workspace option.

## Option behavior

- Each listed subcommand exposes a boolean `workspace` option.
- The option is negatable: both `--workspace` and `--no-workspace` must be
  accepted.
- When the option is omitted, workspace mode is off (equivalent to
  `--no-workspace`).
- The option is discoverable from each listed command's usage output. The
  exact help wording and description sentence are not prescribed and need
  not match any particular text.
- The base problem statement describes the `ws` alias as optional, so
  supporting `--ws` is permitted but is **not required**. An implementation
  must not be rejected for omitting the alias, and the alias need not be
  rejected either.

## Generated output

- When workspace mode is enabled, the generated project's `pubspec.yaml`
  carries the workspace resolution configuration shown in the base problem
  statement (`resolution: workspace`, alongside the environment SDK
  constraint).
- When workspace mode is disabled (including when the option is omitted),
  that configuration is absent from the generated `pubspec.yaml`.

## Explicitly not required

- No MCP (Model Context Protocol) behavior is part of this feature; neither
  tool-schema changes nor argument forwarding for the workspace option are
  required.
- Registering the generated package in a parent workspace is out of scope;
  only the per-package configuration above is in scope.
- The internal mechanism used to deliver the option value to the templates
  is an implementation detail and is deliberately not part of this contract.

problem_statement:
[Bug] Copyright header check enforces hardcoded year "2024"
### Describe the Bug
The Gradle `spotlessKotlinCheck` task enforces that copyright headers contain the hardcoded year "2024". Any other year (e.g. 2026) causes the build to fail.

Where does the problem occur:
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] YAML format
- [ ] Suppression output
- [x] Gradle build / Spotless convention plugin (`vulnlog.common-convention`)

### Steps to Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Modify any file's copyright header year to `2026` (e.g. `// Copyright 2026 the Vulnlog contributors`)
2. Run `./gradlew check`

### Expected Behavior
The copyright header check should accept any valid year, not just "2024". A header like `// Copyright 2026 the Vulnlog contributors` should pass without violations.

### Actual Behavior
The build fails with a Spotless format violation:
```
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

* What went wrong:
Execution failed for task ':lib:spotlessKotlinCheck' (registered by plugin 'vulnlog.common-convention').
> The following files had format violations:
      src/test/kotlin/dev/vulnlog/lib/parse/suppression/cargoaudit/CargoAuditSuppressionWriterTest.kt
          @@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
          -//Â·CopyrightÂ·2026Â·theÂ·VulnlogÂ·contributors
          +//Â·CopyrightÂ·2024Â·theÂ·VulnlogÂ·contributors
           //Â·SPDX-License-Identifier:Â·Apache-2.0
           packageÂ·dev.vulnlog.lib.parse.suppression.cargoaudit
           
  Run './gradlew spotlessApply' to fix all violations.

* Try:
> Run with --stacktrace option to get the stack trace.
> Run with --info or --debug option to get more log output.
> Run with --scan to get full insights from a Build Scan (powered by Develocity).
> Get more help at https://help.gradle.org.

BUILD FAILED in 16s
```

### Additional contract requirements

## Copyright header year handling

The Kotlin formatting convention must recognize a copyright header whose first line is `// Copyright <year> the Vulnlog contributors`, where `<year>` is a four-digit decimal calendar year from `1000` through `9999`, inclusive. Formatting such a source file must normalize the copyright line to the year-independent form `// Copyright the Vulnlog contributors`; it must not replace the supplied year with a fixed numeric year. The SPDX identifier line remains `// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` and must be preserved unchanged by formatting.

diff --git a/modules/lib/src/test/kotlin/dev/vulnlog/lib/core/LicenseHeaderConventionTest.kt b/modules/lib/src/test/kotlin/dev/vulnlog/lib/core/LicenseHeaderConventionTest.kt
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..941c701
--- /dev/null
+++ b/modules/lib/src/test/kotlin/dev/vulnlog/lib/core/LicenseHeaderConventionTest.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+// Copyright 2024 the Vulnlog contributors
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+package dev.vulnlog.lib.core
+
+import io.kotest.assertions.withClue
+import io.kotest.core.spec.style.FunSpec
+import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
+import java.nio.file.Files
+import java.nio.file.Path
+
+class LicenseHeaderConventionTest :
+    FunSpec({
+        listOf(1000, 2026, 2027, 9999).forEach { year ->
+            test("spotless normalizes copyright year $year without pinning a year") {
+                val probe = moduleDirectory.resolve("src/test/kotlin/dev/vulnlog/lib/core/LicenseHeaderProbe$year.kt")
+                Files.createDirectories(probe.parent)
+                Files.writeString(
+                    probe,
+                    """
+                    // Copyright $year the Vulnlog contributors
+                    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+                    package dev.vulnlog.lib.core
+
+                    class LicenseHeaderProbe$year
+                    """.trimIndent() + "\n",
+                )
+
+                try {
+                    val result = runSpotlessApply()
+                    withClue({ "spotlessApply did not complete:\n${result.output}" }) {
+                        result.exitCode shouldBe 0
+                    }
+                    withClue({ "Spotless retained a fixed year for $year:\n${Files.readString(probe)}" }) {
+                        Files.readAllLines(probe).take(2) shouldBe NORMALIZED_COPYRIGHT_HEADER
+                    }
+                } finally {
+                    Files.deleteIfExists(probe)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    })
+
+private val NORMALIZED_COPYRIGHT_HEADER =
+    listOf(
+        "// Copyright the Vulnlog contributors",
+        "// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0",
+    )
+
+private val moduleDirectory: Path = Path.of(System.getProperty("user.dir"))
+private val projectDirectory: Path = moduleDirectory.parent.parent
+
+private data class GradleResult(
+    val exitCode: Int,
+    val output: String,
+)
+
+private fun runSpotlessApply(): GradleResult {
+    val process =
+        ProcessBuilder(
+            projectDirectory.resolve("gradlew").toString(),
+            ":lib:spotlessApply",
+            "--console=plain",
+            "--no-configuration-cache",
+        ).directory(projectDirectory.toFile())
+            .redirectErrorStream(true)
+            .start()
+    val output = process.inputStream.bufferedReader().readText()
+    return GradleResult(process.waitFor(), output)
+}

problem_statement:
Allow for multiple cadence and acceleration thresholds in detectEventBouts
I propose enhancing `detectEventBouts` to support vector inputs for `ebout.th.cad` and `ebout.th.acc`, enabling the calculation of multiple intensity definitions within a single execution (e.g., might be interpreted as bouts of moderate-intensity walking or vigorous-intensity walking).

### Additional contract requirements

Additional observable requirements for `detectEventBouts`:

- `ebout.th.cad` and `ebout.th.acc` may each be supplied either as a single number or as a numeric vector of length one or larger. Passing single numbers is unchanged behavior and must produce exactly the same results and summary variable names as before.
- When either threshold is supplied as a vector with more than one value, bout summaries are calculated for every combination of a cadence threshold and an acceleration threshold (all pairwise combinations of the two vectors, including when only one of them has multiple values), and this is done for each bout duration in `ebout.dur`.
- The summary variable names identify the threshold combination they belong to by embedding the individual values, e.g. names in the form `_cad<cadence threshold><condition>acc<acceleration threshold>` such as `ExtFunEvent_totdur_B1M100%_cad30ANDacc100`. Each combination therefore gets its own dedicated set of summary variables, and the bout metrics reported for one threshold combination differ from those of another combination whenever the combinations select different bouts.
- Vector thresholds are supported with both `ebout.condition = "AND"` and `ebout.condition = "OR"`, with the same combination logic in either case.
- For every threshold combination and bout duration, the same set of bout measures as for a single threshold is reported: total time in bouts, number of bouts, and mean bout duration.

 To control the criteria for bout detection, include in your `myfun` object the items:
 
 - `ebout.dur` a numeric vector of length 1 or larger with the minimum bout duration(s) of interest, e.g. `ebout.dur = c(1, 5, 10)`.
-- `ebout.th.cad` a single number being the minimum cadence value in steps per minute, e.g. `ebout.th.cad = 30`.
