+- `ebout.th.cad` a numeric vector of length 1 or larger being the minimum cadence value in steps per minute, e.g. `ebout.th.cad = 30`.
+- `ebout.th.acc` a numeric vector of length 1 or larger being the minimum acceleration value in steps per minute, e.g. `ebout.th.acc = 50`.
 - `ebout.criter` a single number as a fraction of 1 being the faction of a bout for which the inclusion criteria need to be met identical to `boutcriter` in the context of physical activity bouts, e.g. `ebout.criter = 0.8`.
 - `ebout.condition` whether cadence and acceleration condition are both required (`ebout.condition = "AND"`) or either of the conditions is required (`ebout.condition = "OR"`). If both cadence and acc need to meet a thresholds then fill in `"AND"`. If it also acceptable if only one of the thresholds is met then fill in `"OR"`. If you do not want cadence or acceleration to be used in the equation then simply set `ebout.th.cad = 0` or `ebout.th.acc = 0`.

+
+# Helper functions: every metric assertion below locates each summary variable

+metric_value = function(eventBouts, measure, boutdur, cad, acc, condition) {
+  varname = paste0("ExtFunEvent_", measure, "_B", boutdur, "M100%_cad",
+                   cad, condition, "acc", acc, "__anyRandomText")
+  slot = which(eventBouts$ds_names == varname)

+               info = paste("expected exactly one summary variable named", varname))
+  as.numeric(eventBouts$daysummary)[slot]
+}
+
+# expect the (totdur, number, meandur) metrics of one bout duration and one
+# cadence/acceleration threshold combination, looked up by their names
+expect_metrics_for_combination = function(eventBouts, boutdur, cad, acc,
+                                          condition, expected) {
+  expect_equal(c(metric_value(eventBouts, "totdur", boutdur, cad, acc, condition),

+                 metric_value(eventBouts, "meandur", boutdur, cad, acc, condition)),

                ebout.criter = 1,

+  
+  # create dummy test data: 6 events that each keep one constant cadence and
+  # acceleration level so that every cadence/acceleration threshold
+  # combination selects a different subset of bouts
+  ws3 = 5
+  zero_gap = rep(0, 60/ws3) # one minute of zeros to separate the bouts
+  bout_cadence = c(200, 400, 200, 400, 100, 200)
+  bout_acceleration = c(300, 300, 800, 800, 300, 50)
+  bout_minutes = c(12, 8, 5, 11, 7, 5)

+  varnum = zero_gap

+    varnum_event = c(varnum_event, rep(bout_cadence[bout] * (ws3/60), epochs), zero_gap)

+  }
+  daysummary = matrix("", 1, 50)
+  fi = 1
+  di = 1
+  ds_names = ""
+  myfun = list(ilevels = c(0, 50, 100),
+               clevels = c(0, 30, 50),
+               qlevels = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
+               ebout.dur = c(1, 5, 10),
+               ebout.th.cad = c(150, 350),
+               ebout.th.acc = c(100, 500),
+               ebout.criter = 1,
+               ebout.condition = "AND")
+
+  # run function

+  
+  # bout metrics are calculated for every combination of the cadence and
+  # acceleration thresholds: 3 bout durations x 2 cadence thresholds x
+  # 2 acceleration thresholds x 3 bout metrics = 36 summary variables
+  expect_equal(eventBouts$fi - 1, 36)
+  
+  # every threshold combination yields its own bout metrics, looked up by its
+  # identifying summary variable name, because each combination selects a
+  # different subset of bouts; thresholds (cad, acc):
+  # (150, 100) -> bouts of 12, 8, 5, 11 min -> 36 min in 4 bouts, mean 9 min
+  # (150, 500) -> bouts of 5, 11 min        -> 16 min in 2 bouts, mean 8 min
+  # (350, 100) -> bouts of 8, 11 min        -> 19 min in 2 bouts, mean 9.5 min
+  # (350, 500) -> bout of 11 min            -> 11 min in 1 bout,  mean 11 min
+  # bouts of 1 minute: all bouts that meet the thresholds qualify

+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 1, cad = 350, acc = 100,

+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 1, cad = 350, acc = 500,

+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(36, 4, 9))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 5, cad = 150, acc = 500,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(16, 2, 8))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 5, cad = 350, acc = 100,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(19, 2, 9.5))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 5, cad = 350, acc = 500,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(11, 1, 11))
+  # bouts of 10 minutes: only the 12-minute and 11-minute bouts qualify for
+  # the looser thresholds and only the 11-minute bout for the stricter thresholds
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 10, cad = 150, acc = 100,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(23, 2, 11.5))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 10, cad = 150, acc = 500,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(11, 1, 11))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 10, cad = 350, acc = 100,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(11, 1, 11))
+  expect_metrics_for_combination(eventBouts, boutdur = 10, cad = 350, acc = 500,
+                                 condition = "AND", expected = c(11, 1, 11))
+})
+
+test_that("Detect bouts in events with multiple thresholds and OR condition", {
+  skip_on_cran()
+  
+  # create dummy test data: 5 events of which two meet only the acceleration
+  # threshold, one meets only the cadence threshold, one meets both and one
+  # meets neither, so that every combination also differs under OR
+  ws3 = 5
+  zero_gap = rep(0, 60/ws3) # one minute of zeros to separate the bouts
+  bout_cadence = c(100, 100, 200, 200, 400)
+  bout_acceleration = c(50, 300, 50, 300, 800)
+  bout_minutes = c(4, 5, 8, 7, 9)
+  varnum_event = zero_gap
+  varnum = zero_gap

problem_statement:
Reparse warning should be suppressed for typedefs around _pointers_ to structs/unions
As part of https://github.com/well-typed/hs-bindgen/issues/707 we fixed `processTypedef` so that something like

```c
#define MyInt int

typedef struct { MyInt x; } foo;
```

would not result in a reparse error: [HIDDEN]. However, if we make this a _pointer_ to a struct instead:

```c
#define MyInt int

typedef struct { MyInt x; } * foo;
```

the reparse error re-appears. 

We do still generate the right output, because we do still re-parse the field, but the error is a bit confusing.

NOTE: We should allow for an arbitary number of pointer levels.

diff --git a/hs-bindgen/CHANGELOG.md b/hs-bindgen/CHANGELOG.md
index a21294d5fd..755aeb87bb 100644
--- a/hs-bindgen/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/hs-bindgen/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -161,8 +161,15 @@
   referenced by global variables. For example, `struct { int x; } var;` was
   previously supported but `struct { int x; } * var;` or `struct { int x; }
   var[];` would cause a panic. See [PR #2017][pr-2017].
+* Prevent confusing info-level messages for reparse errors involving
+  declarations that contain nested declarations. For example, for a nested
+  declaration such as `typedef struct { MyInt x; } * foo;` where `MyInt` is a
+  macro type, a message would be traced that the `foo` could not be reparsed,
+  even though the struct field `x` is still reparsed successfully. See [issue
+  #1382][is-1382] and [PR #2021][pr-2021].

problem_statement:
`entryToLoc` should return `NonEmpty`
An empty list of locations may result in trace messages without location information; not a huge deal (esp after #1579), but not quite ideal either.

### Additional contract requirements

`entryToLoc` must return a location representation whose type guarantees that at least one C source location is present. The concrete non-empty representation is not prescribed. This guarantee applies to every declaration-index entry, including external declarations and declarations with conflicting source locations.

When declaration-index locations are used in diagnostics, conversion to the diagnostic location format must preserve at least one source location. In particular, selection diagnostics for external declarations and for unusable transitive dependencies caused by conflicts must not have empty location information.

problem_statement:
Rename data type remnant from parse predicate times
We still have a data type `ParseNotAttempted` with a single constructor `DeclarationUnavailable`.

We should rename/refactor and clarify.

### Additional contract requirements

## Additional details

The data type describing why parsing was not attempted, and its single
"declaration unavailable" constructor, are remnants of the old parse-predicate
design. This task replaces that wrapper entirely with a dedicated "unavailable"
classification of the parse result.

### Required observable behavior

- When hs-bindgen encounters a declaration that libclang reports as
  `CXAvailability_Unavailable` (for example, a declaration annotated with the C
  `unavailable` attribute), it does not attempt to parse that declaration and
  instead records an *unavailable* parse result for it. The unavailable parse
  result carries no additional payload: there is only a single way for a
  declaration to be unavailable, so nothing is — or needs to be — stored about
  the reason beyond the fact that the declaration is unavailable.

- The unavailable classification is preserved by the subsequent frontend
  passes (in particular the AST-simplification pass): a declaration classified
  as unavailable after parsing remains classified as unavailable afterwards.

- An unavailable declaration is unusable and is therefore never selected and
  never generates bindings.

- If a user selection predicate explicitly selects an unavailable declaration,
  hs-bindgen reports an informative, user-facing *Warning*-level trace that
  explains that the declaration could not be selected because it is
  unavailable; processing then continues and the run does not fail.

- Any trace message, log line, or other output that describes an unavailable
  declaration must describe it in terms of the declaration being unavailable
  (in the C availability sense, i.e. the declaration is present but marked as
  unavailable on this platform), not in terms of parsing "not being attempted".

### Required terminology

- The concept is called "unavailable": all user-visible and internal
  terminology uses the "unavailable declaration" vocabulary (matching Clang's
  availability attribute) rather than the obsolete "parse not attempted"
  vocabulary.

- The removed indirection is gone entirely: no type, constructor, field, or
  helper retains the obsolete "not attempted" naming, retains the removed
  payload, nor reconstitutes a one-case reason wrapper around the unavailable
  classification.

problem_statement:
Hash the auth-cache key (M1: raw session tokens as ETS keys in a public table)
Follow-up from the 2026-05-19 security audit (Medium). Tracked publicly because the finding has been disclosed on a public PR branch since May; no new exposure.

**Problem:** `auth_cache_tab` stores raw session tokens as ETS keys in a `public` table. asobi is single-tenant so there's no untrusted Lua, but raw tokens are still exposed to: anyone with observer/hot-code-load/debugger access, and anyone who can trigger a crash dump (heap/binaries land in the dump).

**Fix:** [HIDDEN] so a dump/observer read never yields a usable token. One-line change, high payoff.

Part of the H1-H3 audit follow-up (Highs shipped in #167).

### Additional contract requirements

## Clarifications on the intended auth-cache behavior

The fix for the raw-session-token exposure covers the whole cache, not only
resolution. The following behavior is part of the public contract and is
exercised by the test suite:

### Token key derivation

- Every row stored in the auth cache's ETS table is keyed by the SHA-256
  digest of the raw token bytes (`crypto:hash(sha256, Token)`), never by the
  raw token itself.
- This keying applies uniformly to every cache operation:
  - storing positive entries (`put_positive/2`),
  - storing negative entries (`put_negative/1`) — negative entries receive
    the same raw-key protection as positive ones,
  - resolving tokens (`resolve_token/1`, both cache hits and the miss path
    that populates the cache), and
  - invalidating tokens (`invalidate/1`).
- Observable consequences:
  - The raw token binary never appears as a key in the cache table, for
    either positive or negative entries, at any point (including after
    `resolve_token/1` calls).
  - A direct `ets:lookup` on the cache table using the raw token finds no
    entry; a direct `ets:lookup` using `crypto:hash(sha256, Token)` finds
    exactly the cached row `{Key, Value, ExpiresAt}`.
  - Tokens still resolve through the derived key exactly as before;
    invalidation still removes the entry; TTL and negative-TTL behavior is
    unchanged.

problem_statement_base:
Hash the auth-cache key (M1: raw session tokens as ETS keys in a public table)
Follow-up from the 2026-05-19 security audit (Medium). Tracked publicly because the finding has been disclosed on a public PR branch since May; no new exposure.

**Problem:** `auth_cache_tab` stores raw session tokens as ETS keys in a `public` table. asobi is single-tenant so there's no untrusted Lua, but raw tokens are still exposed to: anyone with observer/hot-code-load/debugger access, and anyone who can trigger a crash dump (heap/binaries land in the dump).

**Fix:** [HIDDEN] so a dump/observer read never yields a usable token. One-line change, high payoff.

Part of the H1-H3 audit follow-up (Highs shipped in #167).
contract_addendum:
## Clarifications on the intended auth-cache behavior

The fix for the raw-session-token exposure covers the whole cache, not only
resolution. The following behavior is part of the public contract and is
exercised by the test suite:

### Token key derivation

- Every row stored in the auth cache's ETS table is keyed by the SHA-256
  digest of the raw token bytes (`crypto:hash(sha256, Token)`), never by the
  raw token itself.
- This keying applies uniformly to every cache operation:
  - storing positive entries (`put_positive/2`),
  - storing negative entries (`put_negative/1`) — negative entries receive
    the same raw-key protection as positive ones,
  - resolving tokens (`resolve_token/1`, both cache hits and the miss path
    that populates the cache), and
  - invalidating tokens (`invalidate/1`).
- Observable consequences:
  - The raw token binary never appears as a key in the cache table, for
    either positive or negative entries, at any point (including after
    `resolve_token/1` calls).
  - A direct `ets:lookup` on the cache table using the raw token finds no
    entry; a direct `ets:lookup` using `crypto:hash(sha256, Token)` finds
    exactly the cached row `{Key, Value, ExpiresAt}`.
  - Tokens still resolve through the derived key exactly as before;
    invalidation still removes the entry; TTL and negative-TTL behavior is
    unchanged.

### Cached player data minimization

- `put_positive/2` does not store the supplied player map verbatim. Only the
  fields the authentication path consumes are kept: `id`, and `banned_at`
  when the map contains it. Every other key supplied in the player map
  (including `username` and, critically, `hashed_password`) is dropped before
  the entry is stored.
- Observable consequences:
  - No cached row ever contains a `hashed_password` key.
  - `resolve_token/1` returns only the projected map on a cached positive
    hit: `{ok, #{id => Id}}` when the supplied map had no `banned_at` key,
    or `{ok, #{id => Id, banned_at => BannedAt}}` when it did.
  - Banned-player handling is unchanged: a cached player with a non-`nil`
    `banned_at` still resolves to `{error, banned}`, and one with `banned_at`
    `nil` (or absent) still resolves to `{ok, _}`.

@@ -183,10 +193,26 @@ insert(Token, Value, ExpiresAt) ->

-            ets:insert(?TABLE, {Token, Value, ExpiresAt}),

+-doc """
+Derive the ETS key from a token.

+The token itself is never stored - only its SHA-256. A crash dump,
+`observer`, or a hot-loaded debugger reading the table yields hashes, not

problem_statement:
game.zone.spawn returns true for an unknown template_id (issue #246's root cause for 'hard to find')
Follow-up from architecture-guardian review of widgrensit/asobi_lua#107 (fixing #246).

`asobi_zone:spawn_entity/4` is a cast; when the target zone's spawner returns `{error, unknown_template}` (template not registered), `asobi_zone`'s cast handler drops it on the floor with no log or telemetry (`[HIDDEN]` as of this writing). Meanwhile `asobi_lua_api:fun_zone_spawn/1` returns `[true]` to the Lua caller unconditionally on every successful *call* (not successful *spawn*).

This is exactly why #246 "took so long to find" per the reporter's own writeup: `game.zone.spawn("cube", x, y)` returning `true` gives zero signal that nothing was actually spawned - and it's not just a Lua/asobi_lua problem, since `asobi_zone:spawn_entity/4` is core `asobi` and any `asobi_world` implementation (not just Lua) hits this same silent-drop.

Ask: at minimum, log + emit `[asobi, error]` telemetry on the `unknown_template` branch in `asobi_zone`'s cast handler, so an unresolvable template_id is observable server-side even though the cast API can't return synchronous failure to the caller.

problem_statement:
Sweep: other schemas with unbounded jsonb metadata (follow-up to #169)
The #169/#170 security review noted that #169 fixed player metadata but the same unbounded-`jsonb`-metadata pattern recurs across the schema layer. A `grep` for `name = metadata, type = jsonb` (and the `value`/`data` jsonb columns) turns up these schemas:

- `asobi_leaderboard_entry`
- `asobi_store_listing`
- `asobi_item_def`
- `asobi_player_item`
- `asobi_transaction`
- `asobi_tournament`
- `asobi_group`
- `asobi_player_stats`
- `asobi_match_record`
- `asobi_chat_message`

**The discriminator that decides which matter:** is the field writable from client-supplied input through a changeset cast? A field the server always sets (e.g. `asobi_transaction`, `asobi_match_record`, computed `asobi_player_stats`) is not an attacker lever and needs no cap. A field a client can populate via a `PUT`/`POST` body is #169 all over again.

**Likely client-writable, check first:**
- `asobi_group` — players create/update groups; if `metadata` is in the update cast, it's uncapped and directly reachable.
- `asobi_chat_message` — if message metadata is client-supplied.

**Almost certainly server-only (verify, then skip):** `asobi_transaction`, `asobi_match_record`, `asobi_item_def`, `asobi_store_listing`, `asobi_leaderboard_entry`.

For each client-writable one, add [HIDDEN] in the changeset, mirroring `asobi_player`. [HIDDEN]

Not urgent — #169 closed the one the audit named — but the pattern is fleet-wide and worth one deliberate pass.

problem_statement_base:
Sweep: other schemas with unbounded jsonb metadata (follow-up to #169)
The #169/#170 security review noted that #169 fixed player metadata but the same unbounded-`jsonb`-metadata pattern recurs across the schema layer. A `grep` for `name = metadata, type = jsonb` (and the `value`/`data` jsonb columns) turns up these schemas:

- `asobi_leaderboard_entry`
- `asobi_store_listing`
- `asobi_item_def`
- `asobi_player_item`
- `asobi_transaction`
- `asobi_tournament`
- `asobi_group`
- `asobi_player_stats`
- `asobi_match_record`
- `asobi_chat_message`

**The discriminator that decides which matter:** is the field writable from client-supplied input through a changeset cast? A field the server always sets (e.g. `asobi_transaction`, `asobi_match_record`, computed `asobi_player_stats`) is not an attacker lever and needs no cap. A field a client can populate via a `PUT`/`POST` body is #169 all over again.

**Likely client-writable, check first:**
- `asobi_group` — players create/update groups; if `metadata` is in the update cast, it's uncapped and directly reachable.
- `asobi_chat_message` — if message metadata is client-supplied.

**Almost certainly server-only (verify, then skip):** `asobi_transaction`, `asobi_match_record`, `asobi_item_def`, `asobi_store_listing`, `asobi_leaderboard_entry`.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1993c00
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/asobi_jsonb.erl
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+-module(asobi_jsonb).
+-moduledoc """
+Size-bound checks for values headed into an unbounded `jsonb` column.
+
+A `jsonb` column has no server-side size limit of its own, so any field a
+client can populate through a changeset cast is a lever for an oversized
+payload unless something checks it first (asobi#169, asobi#216). This is
+the one place that idiom lives, shared by every schema and controller that
+needs it rather than a per-call-site copy.
+""".
+
+-export([within_limit/2, check/2, default_metadata_bytes/0]).
+
+-spec within_limit(dynamic(), non_neg_integer()) -> boolean().
+within_limit(Value, MaxBytes) ->
+    check(Value, MaxBytes) =:= ok.
+
+%% A caller that reports a specific reason to a client or a log wants
+%% "too big" and "not valid JSON at all" told apart - shrinking a payload
+%% doesn't fix the latter. within_limit/2 collapses both into `false` for
+%% callers (a size-only gate ahead of an insert) that don't need the
+%% distinction.
+-spec check(dynamic(), non_neg_integer()) -> ok | too_large | not_encodable.
+check(Value, MaxBytes) ->
+    try iolist_size(json:encode(Value)) of
+        Size when Size =< MaxBytes -> ok;
+        _ -> too_large
+    catch
+        _:_ -> not_encodable
+    end.
+
+%% The shared ceiling for a "metadata annotation" field (as opposed to a
+%% bulk-data field like cloud-save/storage values, which set their own,
+%% larger limit) - one place so every schema that adopts this idiom agrees
+%% by default rather than each declaring its own copy of the same number.
+-spec default_metadata_bytes() -> non_neg_integer().
+default_metadata_bytes() -> 16384.

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+-module(asobi_group_tests).
+
+-include_lib("eunit/include/eunit.hrl").
+-include_lib("kura/include/kura.hrl").
+
+valid_changeset_test() ->
+    CS = asobi_group:changeset(#{}, #{
+        ~"name" => ~"raid team", ~"creator_id" => asobi_id:generate()
+    }),
+    ?assert(CS#kura_changeset.valid).
+
+%% asobi#216: metadata is unbounded jsonb and changeset/2 casts it - the
+%% same lever #169 closed for asobi_player, applied here. The boundary
+%% value below encodes to exactly the shared ceiling, so the changeset
+%% accepts it only if the schema's cap matches the shared helper's
+%% ceiling and treatment of the limit.
+metadata_within_limit_passes_test() ->
+    MaxBytes = asobi_jsonb:default_metadata_bytes(),
+    Boundary = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", MaxBytes - 11)},
+    ?assertEqual(MaxBytes, iolist_size(json:encode(Boundary))),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(Boundary, MaxBytes)),
+    ?assertEqual(true, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Boundary, MaxBytes)),
+    CS = asobi_group:changeset(#{}, #{
+        ~"name" => ~"raid team", ~"creator_id" => asobi_id:generate(), ~"metadata" => Boundary
+    }),
+    ?assert(CS#kura_changeset.valid).
+
+metadata_over_limit_is_rejected_test() ->
+    Big = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", 20000)},
+    MaxBytes = asobi_jsonb:default_metadata_bytes(),
+    ?assertEqual(too_large, asobi_jsonb:check(Big, MaxBytes)),
+    ?assertEqual(false, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Big, MaxBytes)),
+    CS = asobi_group:changeset(#{}, #{
+        ~"name" => ~"raid team", ~"creator_id" => asobi_id:generate(), ~"metadata" => Big
+    }),
+    ?assertNot(CS#kura_changeset.valid).
+
+metadata_absent_is_not_checked_test() ->
+    CS = asobi_group:changeset(#{}, #{
+        ~"name" => ~"raid team", ~"creator_id" => asobi_id:generate()
+    }),
+    ?assert(CS#kura_changeset.valid).
+
+%% A small-but-unencodable value must fail for the right reason, not be
+%% misreported as oversized - shrinking it wouldn't fix the actual problem.
+metadata_not_encodable_is_rejected_test() ->
+    Bad = #{~"blob" => {tuple, ~"json:encode/1 can't serialize this"}},
+    MaxBytes = asobi_jsonb:default_metadata_bytes(),
+    ?assertEqual(not_encodable, asobi_jsonb:check(Bad, MaxBytes)),
+    ?assertEqual(false, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Bad, MaxBytes)),
+    CS = asobi_group:changeset(#{}, #{
+        ~"name" => ~"raid team", ~"creator_id" => asobi_id:generate(), ~"metadata" => Bad
+    }),
+    ?assertNot(CS#kura_changeset.valid),
+    ?assertEqual(
+        [~"is not encodable"], proplists:get_all_values(metadata, CS#kura_changeset.errors)
+    ).
+
+%% Unit coverage for the shared encode-and-measure-size guard and its shared
+%% byte ceiling. Distinct oversized vs. non-encodable outcomes are
+%% contractual; the ceiling and the three-valued check/2 contract are
+%% published and apply to every capped jsonb field.
+jsonb_default_metadata_bytes_is_the_shared_ceiling_test() ->
+    ?assertEqual(16384, asobi_jsonb:default_metadata_bytes()).
+
+jsonb_check_encodable_under_limit_is_ok_test() ->
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(#{~"tag" => ~"eu"}, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_check_exactly_at_the_limit_is_ok_test() ->
+    %% Encodes to exactly 16384 bytes; the ceiling is inclusive.
+    Exact = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", 16373)},
+    ?assertEqual(16384, iolist_size(json:encode(Exact))),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(Exact, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_check_one_over_the_limit_is_too_large_test() ->
+    Over = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", 16374)},
+    ?assertEqual(16385, iolist_size(json:encode(Over))),
+    ?assertEqual(too_large, asobi_jsonb:check(Over, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_check_measures_encoded_byte_size_not_term_size_test() ->
+    %% A UTF-8 binary is measured by its JSON-encoded byte size.
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(#{~"blob" => ~"caf\x{E9}"}, 16)),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(#{~"k" => ~"v"}, 9)),
+    ?assertEqual(too_large, asobi_jsonb:check(#{~"k" => ~"v"}, 8)).
+
+jsonb_check_non_encodable_value_is_not_too_large_test() ->
+    %% A small value that cannot be encoded at all must never be misreported
+    %% as oversized: shrinking it would not fix the actual problem.
+    Bad = #{~"blob" => {tuple, ~"json:encode/1 can't serialize this"}},
+    ?assertEqual(not_encodable, asobi_jsonb:check(Bad, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_check_honours_caller_supplied_limit_test() ->
+    %% Encodes to 9 bytes; a caller that sets its own limit is honoured.
+    Value = #{~"k" => ~"v"},
+    ?assertEqual(9, iolist_size(json:encode(Value))),
+    ?assertEqual(too_large, asobi_jsonb:check(Value, 8)),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_jsonb:check(Value, 9)).
+
+jsonb_within_limit_true_when_check_is_ok_test() ->
+    ?assertEqual(true, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(#{~"tag" => ~"eu"}, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_within_limit_true_at_the_limit_test() ->
+    Exact = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", 16373)},
+    ?assertEqual(true, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Exact, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_within_limit_false_when_too_large_test() ->
+    Over = #{~"blob" => binary:copy(~"x", 16374)},
+    ?assertEqual(false, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Over, 16384)).
+
+jsonb_within_limit_false_when_not_encodable_test() ->
+    Bad = #{~"blob" => {tuple, ~"json:encode/1 can't serialize this"}},
+    ?assertEqual(false, asobi_jsonb:within_limit(Bad, 16384)).

problem_statement:
asobi_world_server crashes the whole world on any ensure_zone failure (place_player/4, restore_entities/3, move_player zone-crossing)
Found during architecture-guardian review of #257 (which fixed the *silent-drop* half of `ensure_zone` error handling in the `spawn_at` cast clause).

Three other call sites in `asobi_world_server.erl` hard-match `ensure_zone/2`'s result instead of handling `{error, _}`:

```erlang
{ok, ZonePid} = asobi_zone_manager:ensure_zone(ZMPid, Coords)
```

- `place_player/4` (called on every player join)
- `restore_entities/3` (load-recovery path)
- the zone-crossing branch inside `move_player` (called whenever a player crosses a zone boundary)

`asobi_zone_manager:ensure_zone/2` returns `{error, max_zones_reached}` when the world hits its configured zone-capacity limit (`asobi_zone_manager.erl:258`, `max_active_zones`). If that fires on any of these three paths, the `{ok, ZonePid} = ...` pattern match fails with a `badmatch`, which crashes the entire `asobi_world_server` gen_statem - taking down **every player in that world instance**, not just the one join/move/recovery attempt.

This is strictly worse than the "spawn something, hear nothing" pattern #247/#249/#251 chased down: those drop one spawn silently; this is "one player's zone crossing kills the whole world." Under normal MMO load - many concurrent players spread across zones, a world approaching its zone budget - a single unlucky zone-crossing at the capacity boundary is a full-world outage.

Fix shape: [HIDDEN]

Not fixed in #257 - out of that PR's stated scope (#251 only covered the two spawn-drop paths), filing separately per house convention.

### Additional contract requirements

Asobi world servers can be configured with a limited zone capacity via the world's zone manager. When the zone manager cannot provide a zone (for example, by reporting `{error, max_zones_reached}` when the configured zone-capacity limit is reached), the world server must handle every zone-provisioning failure gracefully instead of crashing the whole world server process, taking down every player in that world instance.

The observable contract on each zone-provisioning failure path is:

- **Player join**: when the zone manager cannot provide the player's spawn zone, `asobi_world_server:join` on the running world must reply `{error, zone_unavailable}` and must not crash. The player must not be registered: the world's reported player count and player list must not include them. Afterwards the world must remain fully usable, with no sticky state left by the failed join; in particular, once the zone manager can provide the zone again, retrying the same join succeeds and the player then appears in the world's player list normally.

- **Zone-crossing move**: when a `move_player` cast crosses a zone boundary and the zone manager cannot provide the destination zone, the world server must not crash and the crossing must be a no-op from the client's perspective: the player stays registered in the world and remains an entity of the zone they occupied before the move; a failed crossing must never leave a player without zone membership. This resilience also covers a transient provisioning failure that strikes at any point during the processing of a single crossing (for example, capacity reached for just one zone request): the world must not crash and must not lose the player.

- **Snapshot recovery**: when a world boots with persistence enabled and the snapshot store returns recovered entities for a zone that the zone manager cannot provide, the world's boot must not crash: the world must still reach `status` `running`, and the entities for the unavailable zone are skipped rather than aborting the recovery of the world.

On every failure path above, the world server process must remain alive and responsive (its other players, state queries, and subsequent operations keep working normally).

+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun(_Ref, _Coords) ->
+        {error, max_zones_reached}
+    end),
+    try
+        ?assertEqual({error, zone_unavailable}, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1")),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(player_count, asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid)))
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager)
+    end,
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% The rejection must not leave sticky state behind: once the zone manager
+%% can provide the zone again, the same join succeeds and registers the
+%% player. Arm a controller that reports capacity reached for one zone
+%% request and then serves requests normally; expect one clean rejection,
+%% then a successful retry.
+join_recovers_when_zone_capacity_frees_up() ->
+    Ctx = start_world(),
+    Pid = maps:get(world_pid, Ctx),
+    Counter = counters:new(1, []),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun(Ref, Coords) ->
+        case counters:get(Counter, 1) of
+            0 ->
+                counters:add(Counter, 1, 1),
+                {error, max_zones_reached};
+            _ ->
+                meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords])
+        end
+    end),
+    try
+        ?assertEqual({error, zone_unavailable}, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1")),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1")),
+        Info = asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid),
+        ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, Info)),
+        ?assert(lists:member(~"p1", maps:get(players, Info)))
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager)
+    end,
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% Same capacity failure, reached via a zone-crossing move instead of a
+%% join. The crossing must be an observable no-op: the world stays healthy,
+%% the player stays registered, and they remain an entity of their ORIGINAL
+%% zone - a failed crossing must not leave them without zone membership.
+move_zone_unavailable_is_a_noop() ->
+    Ctx = start_world(),
+    Pid = maps:get(world_pid, Ctx),
+    ZMPid = asobi_world_instance:get_child(maps:get(instance_pid, Ctx), asobi_zone_manager),
+    %% asobi_test_world_game:spawn_position/2 always returns {100.0, 100.0},
+    %% which is zone {1,1} at zone_size = 100 (see ?BASE_CONFIG).
+    ok = asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1"),
+    timer:sleep(20),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun
+        (_Ref, {0, 0}) -> {error, max_zones_reached};
+        (Ref, Coords) -> meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords])
+    end),
+    try
+        %% {0.0, 0.0} is zone {0,0} - a real zone-crossing, mocked to fail.
+        asobi_world_server:move_player(Pid, ~"p1", {0.0, 0.0}),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid))),
+        {ok, OldZonePid} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(ZMPid, {1, 1}),
+        ?assertMatch(#{~"p1" := _}, asobi_zone:get_entities(OldZonePid))
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager)
+    end,
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% A transient zone-manager failure that hits partway through a crossing -
+%% after the destination zone was already provisioned once for the move -
+%% must be survived the same way: no crash, no lost player, and the player
+%% keeps an observable zone membership instead of being stranded zoneless.
+%% Arm a controller that serves the first request for the destination zone
+%% normally and then reports capacity reached for the crossing's later
+%% re-provisioning of that same zone within the same move operation.
+move_zone_unavailable_survives_transient_zone_failure() ->
+    Ctx = start_world(),
+    Pid = maps:get(world_pid, Ctx),
+    ZMPid = asobi_world_instance:get_child(maps:get(instance_pid, Ctx), asobi_zone_manager),
+    ok = asobi_world_server:join(Pid, ~"p1"),
+    timer:sleep(20),
+    FailAt = counters:new(1, []),
+    counters:put(FailAt, 1, 0),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun(Ref, Coords) ->
+        case counters:get(FailAt, 1) of
+            0 ->
+                meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords]);
+            _ ->
+                {error, max_zones_reached}
+        end
+    end),
+    %% Fake the meck dynamic call context so the one-shot touch below is
+    %% dispatched to the REAL ensure_zone/2 (meck:passthrough/1 is normally
+    %% only callable from inside an expectation).
+    RealEnsure = fun() ->
+        put('$meck_call', {asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone}),
+        meck:passthrough([ZMPid, {0, 0}])
+    end,
+    try
+        %% Touch the destination zone {0,0} once through the real zone
+        %% manager, and only THEN arm the failure: the crossing's own first
+        %% destination request (however many internal look-ups the move
+        %% performs) must succeed, and every later re-provisioning inside the
+        %% same crossing fails.
+        {ok, _} = RealEnsure(),
+        counters:put(FailAt, 1, 1),
+        asobi_world_server:move_player(Pid, ~"p1", {0.0, 0.0}),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid))),
+        {ok, OldZonePid} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(ZMPid, {1, 1}),
+        ?assertMatch(#{~"p1" := _}, asobi_zone:get_entities(OldZonePid))
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager)
+    end,
+    stop_world(Ctx).
+
+%% World-boot snapshot recovery must skip a zone that the zone manager
+%% cannot provide rather than crashing the world's boot, and must continue
+%% recovering the remaining zones afterwards: the recovered entity of an
+%% available zone must be present in that zone once the world is running.
+restore_entities_skips_unavailable_zone() ->
+    Snapshot = #{
+        {0, 0} => #{
+            zone_state => #{}, entities => #{~"e1" => #{x => 0.0, y => 0.0}}, spawner_state => #{}
+        },
+        {1, 1} => #{
+            zone_state => #{}, entities => #{~"e2" => #{x => 1.0, y => 1.0}}, spawner_state => #{}
+        }
+    },
+    ServedSnapshots = counters:new(1, [atomics]),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_snapshotter, [passthrough]),
+    %% Per-zone snapshot lookups (each restored zone's own lazy restore path)
+    %% must also find nothing, or the meckless fallback would hit the DB.
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_snapshotter, load_snapshot, fun(_WorldId, _Coords) ->
+        {error, not_found}
+    end),
+    %% The snapshot is handed only to the first world that boots while this
+    %% expectation is installed; any later persistent-world boot (e.g. from
+    %% another test in the same VM) sees an empty store instead.
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_snapshotter, load_snapshots, fun(_WorldId) ->
+        try counters:add(ServedSnapshots, 1, 1) of
+            ok ->
+                case counters:get(ServedSnapshots, 1) of
+                    1 ->
+                        {ok, Snapshot};
+                    _ ->
+                        {ok, #{}}
+                end
+        catch
+            _:_ ->
+                {ok, #{}}
+        end
+    end),
+    meck:new(asobi_zone_manager, [passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_zone_manager, ensure_zone, fun
+        (_Ref, {0, 0}) -> {error, max_zones_reached};
+        (Ref, Coords) -> meck:passthrough([Ref, Coords])
+    end),
+    try
+        Ctx = start_world(#{persistence => true}),
+        Pid = maps:get(world_pid, Ctx),
+        ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+        Info = asobi_world_server:get_info(Pid),
+        ?assertEqual(running, maps:get(status, Info)),
+        ZMPid = asobi_world_instance:get_child(maps:get(instance_pid, Ctx), asobi_zone_manager),
+        %% The available zone's recovered entity must have been restored into
+        %% zone {1,1} (proves recovery continued past the skipped zone), while
+        %% nothing of the unavailable zone {0,0} was restored (proves it was
+        %% actually skipped rather than restored or aborting the boot).
+        {ok, GoodZonePid} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(ZMPid, {1, 1}),
+        ?assertMatch(#{~"e2" := _}, asobi_zone:get_entities(GoodZonePid)),
+        {ok, SkippedZonePid} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(ZMPid, {0, 0}),
+        ?assertEqual(false, maps:is_key(~"e1", asobi_zone:get_entities(SkippedZonePid))),
+        stop_world(Ctx)
+    after
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_manager),
+        meck:unload(asobi_zone_snapshotter)
+    end.
+

     Ctx = start_world(),
     Pid = maps:get(world_pid, Ctx),

contract_addendum:
The engine must satisfy the following observable behavior. During a zone
crossing in which the crossing player's destination zone is brought into
existence by the crossing itself (lazy zone creation):

- The crossing player must keep receiving zone state from the zone they
  walked into, including their own entity and every entity of players
  already next to them there (their interest ring covers those positions).
- Any already-connected player whose interest ring covers the destination
  zone (for example a stationary neighbour one zone away with view radius 1)
  must keep receiving the crossing player's entity after the crossing.
- A second player who walks into the same destination zone afterwards must
  receive, and be received by, the players already there, including their own
  entity.
- Entity state other than position (fields a game script attached to the
  entity) must survive the crossing.

The delivery mechanism is not prescribed: no particular subscription call
count, monitor or message-internal bookkeeping, or zone-manager return-shape
beyond the documented `{ok, ZonePid}` contract is required; the assertions
observe delivered entity state and subscriber counts only.

Separately, re-subscribing an already-subscribed player to a zone (as
crossings and reconnects do legitimately) must leave exactly one working
subscription for that player: unsubscribing once removes it entirely, a
re-subscribe under a new session pid moves delivery to the new pid, and the
stale session's death must not evict the live subscription.

+%% A live, pg-registered stand-in for a player session, so player-pid lookups
+%% resolve to a real process. Forwards every asobi_message it receives to
+%% Owner tagged with PlayerId, so the test asserts on actual message delivery
+%% (what a websocket client would receive), never on zone internals.
+fake_session(PlayerId, Owner) ->
+    Pid = spawn(fun Loop() ->
+        receive
+            stop ->
+                ok;
+            Msg ->
+                Owner ! {PlayerId, Msg},
+                Loop()
+        end
+    end),
+    ok = pg:join(nova_scope, {player, PlayerId}, Pid),
+    Pid.
+
+%% Wait until PlayerId's forwarded messages include some zone payload whose
+%% EntityId state satisfies Check, or give up after Timeout ms. Presence-only
+%% assertions pass fun is_map/1 as Check; field assertions observe only the
+%% delivered state a websocket client would decode, never zone internals.
+received_entity(PlayerId, EntityId, Check, Timeout) ->
+    receive
+        {PlayerId, {asobi_message, Msg}} ->
+            case entity_state(Msg, EntityId) of
+                {ok, State} ->
+                    case Check(State) of
+                        true -> true;
+                        false -> received_entity(PlayerId, EntityId, Check, Timeout)
+                    end;
+                false ->
+                    received_entity(PlayerId, EntityId, Check, Timeout)
+            end
+    after Timeout -> false
+    end.
+
+%% Extract EntityId's state from any delivered zone payload: the decoded op
+%% list of a subscribe snapshot (atom keys on raw entities) and the
+%% already-encoded tick payload (string keys after JSON decoding) alike, so
+%% field assertions observe only what a websocket client would receive.
+entity_state(Ops, EntityId) when is_list(Ops) ->
+    lists:foldl(
+        fun
+            (#{<<"id">> := Id, <<"op">> := <<"r">>}, _Acc) when Id =:= EntityId ->
+                false;
+            (#{<<"id">> := Id} = Op, _Acc) when Id =:= EntityId, map_size(Op) > 2 ->
+                {ok, normalize_entity(maps:remove(~"op", Op))};
+            (_, Acc) ->
+                Acc
+        end,
+        false,
+        Ops
+    );
+entity_state(Payload, EntityId) when is_binary(Payload) ->
+    try
+        Decoded = json:decode(Payload),
+        Updates = maps:get(~"updates", maps:get(~"payload", Decoded, #{}), []),
+        entity_state(Updates, EntityId)
+    catch
+        _:_ -> false
+    end;
+entity_state({_ZoneDelta, _TickN, Ops}, EntityId) ->
+    entity_state(Ops, EntityId);
+entity_state({_ZoneDeltaRaw, Payload}, EntityId) ->
+    entity_state(Payload, EntityId);
+entity_state(_Other, _EntityId) ->
+    false.
+
+%% Normalize one delivered entity to plain atom keys (dropping JSON's string
+%% keys and proto-internal op/id fields) so Check funs match raw and decoded
+%% payloads the same way. Unknown keys are dropped rather than invented.
+normalize_entity(Map) when is_map(Map) ->
+    maps:fold(
+        fun
+            (K, V, Acc) when is_binary(K) ->
+                try binary_to_existing_atom(K, utf8) of
+                    A -> Acc#{A => V}
+                catch
+                    error:badarg -> Acc
+                end;
+            (K, V, Acc) when is_atom(K), K =/= id ->
+                Acc#{K => V};
+            (_, _, Acc) ->
+                Acc
+        end,
+        #{},
+        Map
+    );
+normalize_entity(Other) ->
+    Other.
+
+%% Regression for the zone-crossing blackout: when a player crosses one zone
+%% boundary and that crossing brings the destination zone into existence for
+%% the first time (lazy_zones), the destination must contribute state to
+%% everyone whose interest ring covers it - black-box message delivery, no
+%% zone internals. This is the reproduction's report directly: the crossing
+%% player must receive the destination zone's entity state (their own entity,
+%% plus whoever is already there), and an already-connected player whose
+%% interest ring already covered the destination zone must receive the
+%% crossing player.
+crossing_into_lazily_created_zone_delivers_both_ways() ->
+    AnyState = fun(S) -> is_map(S) end,
+    HeraldB = fun(S) -> maps:get(herald, S, undefined) =:= ~"herald_b" end,
+    Ctx =
+        #{world_pid := Pid, zone_mgr := Mgr} = start_world(#{
+            lazy_zones => true, grid_size => 5
+        }),
+    Ada = ~"xfade_ada",
+    Bob = ~"xfade_bob",
+    Cara = ~"xfade_cara",
+    AdaPid = fake_session(Ada, self()),
+    BobPid = fake_session(Bob, self()),
+    CaraPid = fake_session(Cara, self()),
+    try
+        ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, Cara)),
+        %% Ada joins and stays put in zone {1,1}; with view_radius=1 her ring
+        %% already covers {2,1}, but {2,1} does not exist yet.
+        ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, Ada)),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        ?assertEqual(not_loaded, asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {2, 1})),
+        {ok, Z11} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {1, 1}),
+        %% A game script marks Ada's {1,1} entity with non-position state; it
+        %% is part of what the crossing player must receive on arrival.
+        asobi_zone:add_entity(Z11, Ada, #{
+            x => 100.0, y => 100.0, type => ~"player", herald => ~"herald_a"
+        }),
+
+        %% Bob joins in {1,1} and crosses one zone east into {2,1} - the
+        %% crossing is what brings {2,1} into existence. x=225 clears {1,1}'s
+        %% rehome margin (edge at 200 + 15% of 100).
+        ?assertEqual(ok, asobi_world_server:join(Pid, Bob)),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        asobi_zone:player_input(Z11, Bob, #{
+            ~"action" => ~"move", ~"x" => 225.0, ~"y" => 100.0
+        }),
+        timer:sleep(150),
+        ?assertMatch({ok, _}, asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {2, 1})),
+        %% The crossing player must receive the destination zone's entity
+        %% state - most centrally his own entity, which the blackout drops.
+        ?assert(received_entity(Bob, Bob, AnyState, 500)),
+        %% Ada, standing still in {1,1} with a ring that covers {2,1} the
+        %% whole time, must receive the crossing player after the crossing.
+        ?assert(received_entity(Ada, Bob, AnyState, 500)),
+
+        %% A second player (Cara) walks into Bob's same, already-created
+        %% destination zone {2,1} - the "two players next to each other each
+        %% holding exactly one entity" case from the report. Whatever her
+        %% entity fields, she must be delivered to and receive the players
+        %% already in {2,1}, including her own entity there.
+        asobi_zone:player_input(Z11, Cara, #{
+            ~"action" => ~"move", ~"x" => 230.0, ~"y" => 100.0
+        }),
+        timer:sleep(200),
+        %% {2,1} is still Bob's (and now Cara's) destination - no new zone
+        %% east of it was created, so she walked into the SAME zone.
+        ?assertMatch({ok, _}, asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {2, 1})),
+        ?assertEqual(not_loaded, asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {3, 1})),
+        %% All four deliveries between the pair now standing in {2,1}: Bob
+        %% receives Cara (and still his own) from the zone he walked into,
+        %% and the entrant Cara receives both Bob and her own entity there
+        %% from the zone she walked into - in the blackout each of them sees
+        %% nothing but themselves.
+        ?assert(received_entity(Bob, Bob, AnyState, 500)),
+        ?assert(received_entity(Bob, Cara, AnyState, 500)),
+        ?assert(received_entity(Cara, Bob, AnyState, 500)),
+        ?assert(received_entity(Cara, Cara, AnyState, 500)),
+
+        %% Non-position entity state must survive a crossing. Cara's {1,1}
+        %% entity is empty per the game's join placement, so mark Bob's own
+        %% {2,1} entity with a non-position field the game attached, then hop
+        %% him one zone east. The field must show up on the delivered
+        %% post-crossing entity - no bare, zone-default ghost arrives.
+        {ok, Z21} = asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {2, 1}),
+        asobi_zone:add_entity(Z21, Bob, #{
+            x => 225.0, y => 100.0, type => ~"player", herald => ~"herald_b"
+        }),
+        timer:sleep(20),
+        asobi_zone:player_input(Z21, Bob, #{
+            ~"action" => ~"move", ~"x" => 325.0, ~"y" => 100.0
+        }),
+        timer:sleep(150),
+        ?assertMatch({ok, _}, asobi_zone_manager:get_zone(Mgr, {3, 1})),
+        %% Bob receives his own post-crossing entity with the marker intact.
+        ?assert(received_entity(Bob, Bob, HeraldB, 500))
+    after
+        exit(AdaPid, kill),
+        exit(BobPid, kill),
+        exit(CaraPid, kill),
+        stop_world(Ctx)
+    end.

+    Old = spawn(fun Loop() ->

+    timer:sleep(10),
+    ?assertEqual(1, asobi_zone:get_subscriber_count(Pid)),

+    asobi_zone:subscribe(Pid, {~"p1", self()}),

+    after 500 ->

problem_statement:
find_player_pid/1's self() fallback subscribes the world server as a player's session
## Context

Follow-up from #275 (zone-crossing blackout). The fix there added `backfill_zone_subscribers/4`, which deliberately resolves player pids via `pg:get_members(?PG_SCOPE, {player, PlayerId})` directly instead of `find_player_pid/1`, because that helper falls back to `self()` when a player has no live pg registration:

[HIDDEN]

That fallback exists for "the player currently acting" call sites (join, move), where the caller is always the live session driving the request. But `place_player/4` and `handle_move/4`'s crossing branch still call `find_player_pid/1` for the acting player - and a `player_zones` entry outlives disconnection (kept around for reconnect, per the `{reconnect_state := RS}` clause in `asobi_world_server`). If a disconnected-but-reconnectable player's session dies mid-flight and somehow re-triggers one of these paths before reconnecting, `find_player_pid/1` would return the world server's own pid and subscribe it to a zone as that player's "session":

- the zone starts monitoring and streaming `zone_delta` to the world server, silently swallowed by the catch-all `running(info, {asobi_message, _}, _)` clause - an unbounded per-tick message flow into a `gen_statem` for a player who will never see it;
- `asobi_zone`'s DOWN handler filters subscribers by pid, so if more than one player id ever shared the world-server pid this way, killing the world server would evict all of them together (not a realistic path today, but a landmine).

## Proposed fix

[HIDDEN] rather than relying on an implicit "it's always the current caller" invariant.

## Scope

Out of scope for #275's fix - that PR only closes the gap for `backfill_zone_subscribers/4` (a genuinely new caller resolving *other* players' pids, where the invariant never held). This ticket is about tightening the pre-existing acting-player call sites so the invariant doesn't quietly break under some future caller that isn't guaranteed to be live.

### Additional contract requirements

The world server and world chat must never substitute a caller's own pid (in
production, the world server's process) for a player that has no live
pg-registered session. Concretely, all of the following are observable:

- When the world chat learns that a player joined, left, or changed zone and
  that player has no live registered session, the calling process is not
  enrolled in any of that player's world, zone, or proximity chat channels,
  and any channel membership the calling process already holds is left
  untouched (the absent player is never treated as the caller).
- A world-server join for a player with no live registered session succeeds
  without subscribing the world server (or any other non-session process) to
  that player's zone as the player's session.
- A zone-crossing move for a player whose world entry survives its session in
  a reconnect grace window still moves the player's entity, but subscribes
  nothing on that player's behalf: neither the origin nor the destination
  zone gains a subscriber, and the calling process receives no zone-delta
  messages streamed as that player.
- `reconnect/2` for a player with no live registered session returns
  `{error, no_live_session}` (rather than succeeding or raising an error) and
  does not consume that player's pending reconnect/grace state: once a live
  session is registered for the player, a subsequent `reconnect/2` succeeds.

problem_statement:
asobi_match_server's find_player_pid/1 has the same self()-fallback landmine as #277
## Context

#277 hardened `asobi_world_server:find_player_pid/1` (and the parallel copy in `asobi_world_chat.erl`) so a player with no live pg registration for `{player, PlayerId}` resolves to `undefined` instead of silently falling back to `self()` - avoiding a monitor/subscribe/message-send that would otherwise target the calling process's own pid instead of a real session.

`asobi_match_server.erl` has its own independent copy of the same helper:

```erlang
-spec find_player_pid(binary()) -> pid().
find_player_pid(PlayerId) ->
    case pg:get_members(?PG_SCOPE, {player, PlayerId}) of
        [Pid | _] -> Pid;
        [] -> self()
    end.
```

Used at two call sites, both structurally identical to what #277 fixed in `asobi_world_server`:

- Match join (`:513-517`): `SessionPid = find_player_pid(PlayerId)`, then `erlang:monitor(process, SessionPid)` - a match server monitoring itself if the joining player has no live session, meaning reconnect-grace / disconnect handling for that player silently never fires (the monitor can never produce a real DOWN).
- Match reconnect (`:884-892`): same pattern, `NewSessionPid = find_player_pid(PlayerId)` then `erlang:monitor(process, NewSessionPid)`.

## Proposed fix

Same shape as #277/#278:
1. `find_player_pid/1` returns `pid() | undefined` instead of falling back to `self()`.
2. The join-path monitor call: on `undefined`, [HIDDEN] rather than crashing on `monitor(process, undefined)`.
3. The reconnect-path monitor call: on `undefined`, reject the reconnect with a new error atom (mirroring `{error, no_live_session}`) [HIDDEN], rather than crashing.
4. [HIDDEN]

## Scope

Out of scope for #277/#278 - those only touched `asobi_world_server` and `asobi_world_chat` (both reachable from the same join/crossing code path). `asobi_match_server` is a structurally independent subsystem (matches, not worlds/zones) with its own copy of the helper; fixing it is a separate, self-contained change.

### Additional contract requirements

## Missing live-session behavior in asobi_match_server

When a match operation needs the pid of a player's live session and that player
has no process currently registered for it (no live session), the match server
must not substitute its own pid (or any other process) as that player's
session, and it must not set up a monitor on a process the player does not own.
The observable requirements are:

- **Join with no live session.** `asobi_match_server:join/2` (and `join/3`)
  succeeds (returns `ok`) and the joining player is retained on the match
  roster, exactly as if a session had been present. The match server stays
  alive and responsive, and `get_info/1` reports the player as joined. No
  substitute pid is recorded for the player and no monitor is created against
  the match server itself, so the match does not later mistake its own
  lifecycle for that player's session ending.

- **Reconnect with no live session.** `asobi_match_server:reconnect/2` for a
  player who is in the match but currently has no live session fails cleanly by
  returning the error tuple `{error, no_live_session}`. It must not crash the
  match server and must not silently monitor the match server's own pid.

- **Failed reconnect leaves reconnect grace intact.** A reconnect rejected
  because there is no live session does not consume or clear the player's
  outstanding reconnect-grace entry. If a genuine session for that player
  registers afterwards, a subsequent `reconnect/2` succeeds (returns `ok`) and
  the player remains in the match.

These are observable-behavior contracts expressed only through the public
`join/2,3`, `reconnect/2`, and `get_info/1` surface; they do not depend on the
server's internal state representation.

problem_statement:
asobi_match_server crashes if a player session dies while match is in waiting state
## Context

Found during review of #280 (find_player_pid/1 self()-fallback fix). `asobi_match_server` monitors player sessions from `handle_join/4`, which runs in both the `waiting` state (before `min_players` is reached) and while `running`. But only `running/3` has an `info`/`'DOWN'` clause - `waiting/3` has no `info` clause and no catch-all.

If a player's session dies (WS drop, crash) while the match is still `waiting` for more players to join, the resulting `'DOWN'` message has no matching clause in `waiting/3` and the match server crashes with `function_clause`, taking down every player already in the lobby with it.

Confirmed empirically: join a live session while `waiting`, kill it -> `function_clause ... asobi_match_server.erl:212 (waiting/3)`.

This is a common mobile scenario: a player joins a lobby, then backgrounds the app or loses signal before the match fills.

## Secondary, lower-severity instance

`paused/3` ends in a catch-all, so a session dying while paused is silently swallowed - no grace started, no leave, the player stays pinned in the roster forever. With no reconnect policy configured, the match can then never empty and never shut down.

`asobi_world_server` doesn't have this asymmetry because it rejects joins outside its `loading`/ready state, so `running` is its only monitor-creating state and its single `'DOWN'` handler is complete by construction. `asobi_match_server` has a real lobby (`waiting`) state that accepts joins, so it needs its own `'DOWN'` handling there.

[HIDDEN]

Found by the asobi-architecture-guardian agent during review of PR #280.

### Additional contract requirements

The match server must handle player session death and reconnect requests
not only while a match is running, but also while it is still waiting for
players and while it is paused.

Observable requirements:

- If a joined player's session dies while the match is still waiting for
  players, the match server must not crash. The dead player is treated as
  having left (removed from the roster), the match keeps waiting, and the
  remaining players stay in the lobby.
- If a joined player's session dies while the match is paused and no
  reconnect policy is configured, the player leaves immediately, exactly
  as when the match is running without a policy; in particular, when this
  was the last player the match shuts down as empty.
- If a joined player's session dies while the match is paused and a
  reconnect policy is configured, that player's reconnect grace period
  starts, as it would while running. The player remains in the roster
  during grace, the match stays paused and alive, and if the match is
  later resumed without a reconnect, the grace expiry removes the player
  from the roster.
- A synchronous reconnect request for a joined player (for example
  `asobi_match_server:reconnect(Pid, PlayerId)` or, equivalently, a
  `{reconnect, PlayerId}` call) issued while the match is paused, with a
  reconnect policy configured and that player in an active grace period,
  must receive a reply within a bounded time (it must not hang) and must
  be accepted (reply `ok`), even before the match is resumed. After a
  successful such reconnect the match remains paused and the player
  remains in the roster.
- A synchronous reconnect request issued while the match is still waiting,
  when the match has no reconnect policy configured, must receive the
  reply `{error, no_reconnect_policy}` within a bounded time. It must not
  crash or terminate the match server with `function_clause` (or any other
  error) and must not hang. After handling such a request, the match
  server process remains alive and the match stays in the waiting state
  with its joined players intact.

 waiting(cast, {broadcast_event, Event, Payload}, State) ->
     broadcast_match_event(Event, Payload, State),
     keep_state_and_data;
+%% asobi#285: the match hasn't started yet, so no reconnect_state grace
+%% applies pre-match-start - a session dying while still gathering players
+%% is a leave, same as running's no-reconnect-policy branch. Without this
+%% clause the DOWN message hit no clause here and crashed the match server,
+%% taking every player already in the lobby down with it.
+waiting(info, {'DOWN', _MonRef, process, DownPid, _Reason}, State) when is_pid(DownPid) ->
+    case find_player_by_pid(DownPid, State) of
+        {ok, PlayerId} -> handle_leave(PlayerId, State);
+        none -> keep_state_and_data
+    end;
+%% asobi#285: without this clause a reconnect/2 call while still waiting hit
+%% no clause and crashed the match server (waiting/3 has no catch-all) -
+%% handle_reconnect_call/3 already replies {error, no_reconnect_policy} or
+%% {error, not_in_match} correctly for this state, it was just unreachable.
+waiting({call, From}, {reconnect, PlayerId}, State) when is_binary(PlayerId) ->
+    handle_reconnect_call(From, PlayerId, State);
 waiting(cast, cancel, State) ->
     {stop, {shutdown, cancelled}, State}.
 
@@ -427,6 +443,14 @@ paused({call, From}, resume, State) ->
     {next_state, running, State, [{reply, From, ok}]};

     {keep_state_and_data, [{reply, From, {error, already_paused}}]};
+%% asobi#285: without this clause a reconnect/2 call while paused fell
+%% through to the catch-all below, which never replies - the caller's
+%% gen_statem:call/2 (default timeout infinity) would hang forever. Needed
+%% now that a session DOWN while paused starts real grace (see the 'DOWN'
+%% clauses below): a player in grace during a pause must be able to
+%% reconnect before resume/1 is called.
+paused({call, From}, {reconnect, PlayerId}, State) when is_binary(PlayerId) ->
+    handle_reconnect_call(From, PlayerId, State);
 paused(cast, cancel, State) ->
     {next_state, finished, State#{result => #{status => ~"cancelled"}}};
 paused(cast, {leave, PlayerId}, State) ->
@@ -453,6 +477,30 @@ paused(
 paused(info, {vote_vetoed, VoteId, _Template}, State) ->
     Active = maps:remove(VoteId, maps:get(active_votes, State, #{})),
     {keep_state, State#{active_votes => Active}};
+%% asobi#285: mirrors running's pair of 'DOWN' clauses. Without these, a
+%% session dying while paused fell through to the catch-all below and was
+%% silently swallowed - no grace started, no leave, the player stuck in the
+%% roster forever (and, with no reconnect policy, the match could then never
+%% empty and never shut down).

+    info, {'DOWN', _MonRef, process, DownPid, _Reason}, #{reconnect_state := undefined} = State
+) when is_pid(DownPid) ->

+        none -> keep_state_and_data
+    end;
+paused(info, {'DOWN', _MonRef, process, DownPid, _Reason}, #{reconnect_state := RS} = State) when
+    is_pid(DownPid)
+->
+    case find_player_by_pid(DownPid, State) of

+        none ->

+        {'DOWN', Ref, process, Pid, {shutdown, empty}} -> ok
+    after 2000 ->
+        ?assert(false)
+    end.
+
+%% Regression for widgrensit/asobi#285: with a reconnect policy active, a
+%% session DOWN while paused must start reconnect grace exactly like
+%% running's with-policy branch - not be swallowed by the catch-all.
+%%
+%% paused/3, unlike running/3, still ends in a catch-all, so "player still
+%% counted right after the kill" is not proof grace actually started - the
+%% catch-all silently dropping the DOWN produces the identical observation.
+%% tick_reconnect/2 only runs from running's tick handler, so grace can't
+%% progress while paused; resume/1 and let the (short) grace period expire
+%% instead - that only happens if asobi_reconnect:disconnect/3 genuinely
+%% populated grace state, which only the fixed with-policy clause does.
+paused_down_starts_grace() ->
+    Pid = start_match(#{
+        min_players => 1,
+        max_players => 2,
+        reconnect => #{
+            grace_period => 100,
+            during_grace => idle,
+            on_reconnect => resume,
+            on_expire => remove,
+            pause_match => false,
+            max_offline_total => infinity
+        }
+    }),
+    SessionPid = fake_session(~"p285_paused_policy"),
+    ok = asobi_match_server:join(Pid, ~"p285_paused_policy"),
+    timer:sleep(50),
+    ok = asobi_match_server:pause(Pid),
+    ?assertMatch(#{status := paused}, asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid)),
+
+    exit(SessionPid, kill),
+    timer:sleep(50),
+    %% Grace active - player still counted, match server alive.
+    ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+    Info = asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid),
+    ?assertEqual(paused, maps:get(status, Info)),
+    ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, Info)),
+
+    ok = asobi_match_server:resume(Pid),
+    timer:sleep(500),
+    ?assertEqual(0, maps:get(player_count, asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid))),
+    stop(Pid).
+
+%% Regression for widgrensit/asobi#285: paused/3 had no {call, reconnect}
+%% clause, so calling reconnect/2 while paused fell through to the
+%% catch-all, which never replies - gen_statem:call/2 defaults to timeout
+%% infinity, so the caller would hang forever. Calls gen_statem:call/3
+%% directly with a bounded timeout so a regression fails fast here instead
+%% of hanging the whole test run.
+reconnect_while_paused_succeeds() ->
+    Pid = start_match(#{
+        min_players => 1,
+        max_players => 2,
+        reconnect => #{
+            grace_period => 30_000,
+            during_grace => idle,
+            on_reconnect => resume,
+            on_expire => remove,
+            pause_match => false,
+            max_offline_total => infinity
+        }
+    }),
+    PlayerId = ~"p285_reconnect_paused",
+    SessionPid1 = fake_session(PlayerId),
+    ok = asobi_match_server:join(Pid, PlayerId),
+    timer:sleep(50),
+    ok = asobi_match_server:pause(Pid),
+    exit(SessionPid1, kill),
+    timer:sleep(100),
+    %% Grace active (see paused_down_starts_grace/0) - a real session
+    %% arriving now must be able to reconnect before resume/1 is called.
+    _SessionPid2 = fake_session(PlayerId),
+    ?assertEqual(ok, gen_statem:call(Pid, {reconnect, PlayerId}, 2000)),
+    ?assertMatch(#{status := paused}, asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid)),
+    ?assertEqual(1, maps:get(player_count, asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid))),
+    stop(Pid).
+
+%% Regression for widgrensit/asobi#285: waiting/3 had no {call, reconnect}
+%% clause and no catch-all, so calling reconnect/2 while still gathering
+%% players crashed the match server with function_clause. Bounded timeout
+%% for the same reason as reconnect_while_paused_succeeds/0. After the
+%% call the lobby must be untouched: still waiting, same players.
+reconnect_while_waiting_does_not_crash() ->
+    Pid = start_match(#{min_players => 3, max_players => 4}),
+    PlayerId = ~"p285_reconnect_waiting",
+    ok = asobi_match_server:join(Pid, PlayerId),
+    ok = asobi_match_server:join(Pid, ~"p285_reconnect_waiting_2"),
+    ?assertEqual(
+        {error, no_reconnect_policy}, gen_statem:call(Pid, {reconnect, PlayerId}, 2000)
+    ),
+    ?assert(is_process_alive(Pid)),
+    Info = asobi_match_server:get_info(Pid),
+    ?assertEqual(waiting, maps:get(status, Info)),
+    ?assertEqual(2, maps:get(player_count, Info)),
+    ?assertEqual(
+        lists:sort([PlayerId, ~"p285_reconnect_waiting_2"]),
+        lists:sort(maps:get(players, Info))
+    ),
+    stop(Pid).
+
 %% --- Helpers ---
 
 fake_session(PlayerId) ->

contract_addendum:
When a player's subscription to a zone ends, the departure must mirror the
arrival:

- Subscribing to a zone hands the new subscriber the zone's full contents as
  add operations; unsubscribing must hand the departing subscriber a removal
  (`r`) operation for every entity that zone holds at unsubscription time, so
  the departing client drops those entities instead of keeping a frozen copy
  that is never updated again.
- This applies equally when the unsubscription is caused indirectly — for
  example when a player's movement carries them so far that a zone falls
  entirely outside their interest ring. Occupants of that zone who never
  moved must still be actively removed from the departing player's client.
- Unsubscribing a player who is not (or no longer) subscribed to the zone
  remains a pure no-op: no departure notification is emitted for a
  subscription that does not exist.

problem_statement:
asobi_matchmaker: inline join loop not exception-isolated, loses queued tickets on match failure
## Context

Found during review of #289 (fix for #285). `asobi_matchmaker:spawn_match/6` (`src/matches/asobi_matchmaker.erl:413`) runs its player-join fan-out inline in the matchmaker `gen_server`'s tick handling, joining players sequentially via `asobi_match_server:join/2` with `_ =` discarding the result (not catching an exit). The sibling `spawn_world/6` path wraps its equivalent fan-out in `spawn(fun() -> try ... catch ... end end)` for isolation; `spawn_match/6` does not.

If the newly-created match server exits mid-loop (e.g. `{shutdown, empty}` if a joining player's session is already dead - exactly the scenario #285/#289 made a clean, correct exit instead of a crash), the exit propagates into the matchmaker `gen_server`'s `join/2` call, which restarts the matchmaker and drops every ticket queued in that mode (`tickets => #{}` reset on restart).

Note: #289 strictly *narrows* the blast radius here rather than causing it - pre-#285, a `waiting`-state `'DOWN'` crashed the match server outright, which produced the same matchmaker-restart-and-drop-tickets failure. #289 makes the match server's exit clean and predictable, but the matchmaker's lack of isolation around the join loop is a separate, pre-existing defect.

## Proposed fix

Wrap the join fan-out in `spawn_match/6` the same way `spawn_world/6` does - isolate it so a single match server's exit during fan-out doesn't propagate into and restart the matchmaker `gen_server`.

Found by the asobi-architecture-guardian agent during review of PR #289 (fix for #285).

### Additional contract requirements

## Additional observable contract for the matchmaker join fan-out

When the join fan-out for a newly formed match fails because the freshly spawned
match server exits while players are being joined (for example when a joining
player's session is already gone), the following externally observable behaviour
is required:

- The matchmaker `gen_server` must keep running. Its state must not be reset by a
  restart, so tickets that were still queued in other modes remain queued and
  remain retrievable by their owner.

- Every player of the failed match must receive, via `asobi_presence:send/2`,
  the message `{match_event, matchmaker_failed, #{reason => <<"match_start_failed">>}}`.
  The failure reason must be exactly the binary `<<"match_start_failed">>`.

Found during review of #289 (fix for #285). `asobi_matchmaker:spawn_match/6` (`src/matches/asobi_matchmaker.erl:413`) runs its player-join fan-out inline in the matchmaker `gen_server`'s tick handling, joining players sequentially via `asobi_match_server:join/2` with `_ =` discarding the result (not catching an exit). The sibling `spawn_world/6` path wraps its equivalent fan-out in `spawn(fun() -> try ... catch ... end end)` for isolation; `spawn_match/6` does not.

If the newly-created match server exits mid-loop (e.g. `{shutdown, empty}` if a joining player's session is already dead - exactly the scenario #285/#289 made a clean, correct exit instead of a crash), the exit propagates into the matchmaker `gen_server`'s `join/2` call, which restarts the matchmaker and drops every ticket queued in that mode (`tickets => #{}` reset on restart).

Note: #289 strictly *narrows* the blast radius here rather than causing it - pre-#285, a `waiting`-state `'DOWN'` crashed the match server outright, which produced the same matchmaker-restart-and-drop-tickets failure. #289 makes the match server's exit clean and predictable, but the matchmaker's lack of isolation around the join loop is a separate, pre-existing defect.

## Proposed fix

Wrap the join fan-out in `spawn_match/6` the same way `spawn_world/6` does - isolate it so a single match server's exit during fan-out doesn't propagate into and restart the matchmaker `gen_server`.

contract_addendum:
## Additional observable contract for the matchmaker join fan-out

When the join fan-out for a newly formed match fails because the freshly spawned
match server exits while players are being joined (for example when a joining
player's session is already gone), the following externally observable behaviour
is required:

- The matchmaker `gen_server` must keep running. Its state must not be reset by a
  restart, so tickets that were still queued in other modes remain queued and
  remain retrievable by their owner.

- Every player of the failed match must receive, via `asobi_presence:send/2`,
  the message `{match_event, matchmaker_failed, #{reason => <<"match_start_failed">>}}`.
  The failure reason must be exactly the binary `<<"match_start_failed">>`.

diff --git a/test/asobi_matchmaker_isolation_tests.erl b/test/asobi_matchmaker_isolation_tests.erl
new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/asobi_matchmaker_isolation_tests.erl
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+-module(asobi_matchmaker_isolation_tests).
+
+-include_lib("eunit/include/eunit.hrl").
+
+%% Regression coverage for the matchmaker's exception isolation: an exit from
+%% the freshly spawned match server while the match-join fan-out runs must
+%% neither kill/restart the matchmaker gen_server nor drop the tickets still
+%% queued in other modes.
+
+setup() ->
+    {ok, _} = application:ensure_all_started(telemetry),
+    meck:new(asobi_presence, [non_strict, no_link, passthrough]),
+    meck:expect(asobi_presence, send, fun(_PlayerId, _Msg) -> ok end),
+    meck:new(asobi_match_sup, [non_strict, no_link, passthrough]),
+    ok.
+
+cleanup(_) ->
+    catch meck:unload(asobi_match_sup),
+    catch meck:unload(asobi_presence),
+    application:unset_env(asobi, matchmaker),
+    application:unset_env(asobi, game_modes),
+    ok.
+
+matchmaker_isolation_test_() ->
+    {setup, fun setup/0, fun cleanup/1,
+        {timeout, 30, fun exit_does_not_restart_matchmaker_or_drop_tickets/0}}.
+
+%% Drives the real matchmaker through its public API: two players fill a
+%% two-player match whose match server dies on the second join, while an
+%% unrelated ticket stays queued in another mode. The failure must stay inside
+%% the matchmaker's tick handling: the gen_server keeps running with its state
+%% intact and the surviving ticket is still queued.
+exit_does_not_restart_matchmaker_or_drop_tickets() ->
+    application:set_env(asobi, matchmaker, #{tick_interval => 100}),
+    application:set_env(asobi, game_modes, #{
+        ~"iso_fill" => #{module => asobi_fake_game, match_size => 2},
+        ~"iso_hold" => #{module => asobi_fake_game, match_size => 5}
+    }),
+    {ok, MatchPid} = fake_match_server(),
+    meck:expect(asobi_match_sup, start_match, fun(_Config) -> {ok, MatchPid} end),
+    {ok, Pid} = asobi_matchmaker:start_link(),
+    unlink(Pid),
+    Monitor = monitor(process, Pid),
+    {ok, Ticket1, _} = asobi_matchmaker:add(~"iso_p1", #{mode => ~"iso_fill"}),
+    {ok, Ticket2, _} = asobi_matchmaker:add(~"iso_p2", #{mode => ~"iso_fill"}),
+    {ok, HeldTicket, _} = asobi_matchmaker:add(~"iso_hold_p", #{mode => ~"iso_hold"}),
+    StateBefore = sys:get_state(Pid, 5000),
+    try
+        ?assertEqual(3, maps:size(maps:get(tickets, StateBefore))),
+        %% Force the tick - the normal deadline-reply path, before a second
+        %% timer fires.
+        Pid ! tick,
+        %% The second join makes the match server exit without replying. An
+        %% un-isolated fan-out takes the matchmaker down with it.
+        receive
+            {'DOWN', Monitor, process, Pid, Reason} ->
+                ?assertEqual(
+                    {no_matchmaker_exit, Reason}, {no_matchmaker_exit, matchmaker_survived}
+                )
+        after 5000 ->
+            ok
+        end,
+        %% The matchmaker still answers; same state (its tickets were not reset
+        %% by a restart), with the two matched tickets consumed by the tick.
+        StateAfter = sys:get_state(Pid, 5000),
+        ?assertEqual(1, maps:size(maps:get(tickets, StateAfter))),
+        %% The matched group's tickets left the queue via the spawn path ...
+        ?assertEqual({error, not_found}, asobi_matchmaker:get_ticket(Ticket1)),
+        ?assertEqual({error, not_found}, asobi_matchmaker:get_ticket(Ticket2)),
+        %% ... not via a restart - the surviving ticket it carried into the
+        %% tick is still queued and owned.
+        {ok, Held} = asobi_matchmaker:get_ticket(~"iso_hold_p", HeldTicket),
+        ?assertEqual(~"iso_hold", maps:get(mode, Held)),
+        %% Both players of the failed match are told the match could not start.
+        ?assert(match_failed_notified(~"iso_p1")),
+        ?assert(match_failed_notified(~"iso_p2"))
+    after
+        demonitor(Monitor, [flush]),
+        catch meck:unload(asobi_match_sup),
+        catch gen_server:stop(Pid)
+    end.
+
+match_failed_notified(PlayerId) ->
+    meck:called(asobi_presence, send, [
+        PlayerId, {match_event, matchmaker_failed, #{reason => ~"match_start_failed"}}
+    ]).
+
+%% Minimal stand-in for a match server: replies to get_info, replies ok to the
+%% first join, then exits mid fan-out on the second - the `{shutdown, empty}'
+%% style exit a dead player session produces in the real match server.
+fake_match_server() ->
+    Pid = spawn(fun() -> fake_loop() end),
+    {ok, Pid}.
+
+fake_loop() ->
+    receive
+        {'$gen_call', From, get_info} ->
+            gen_statem:reply(From, #{match_id => ~"iso-match-1"}),
+            fake_loop();
+        {'$gen_call', From, {join, ~"iso_p1", _Ctx}} ->
+            gen_statem:reply(From, ok),
+            fake_loop();
+        {'$gen_call', _From, {join, _PlayerId, _Ctx}} ->
+            exit({shutdown, empty})
+    end.
FAIL_TO_PASS: asobi_matchmaker_isolation_tests:exit_does_not_restart_matchmaker_or_drop_tickets
